The <s>Tathāgata</s>, through great compassion, for the deliverance of beings, dwells in this world having taken up the body consisting of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), which is unbearable even for a moment, like a red-hot iron ball. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, is one whose equanimity-mind is well-cultivated; relinquishing that equanimity-mind, he always practices the mind of great compassion. Therefore he is worthy of worship.

body.text: tathāgataḥ sujanānāṃ sujanatamaḥ | kasmāt | ātmano mahāhitaṃ prāpayati parāṃśca mahāhitaṃ prāpayati | svaparahitakṛddhi sujanaḥ | tathāgataḥ sattvānāṃ cittaparijñāne paramakuśalaḥ yathoktaṃ sūtre- ahaṃ sattvaparamārthasya suvijñaḥ kṛpāvān hitakārī ityādi | kiñca buddhasya bhagavato vīryādiguṇaskandhāḥ santi | yathā upāliḥ śatagāthābhistathāgataṃ stutavān | tādṛśaguṇasamanvitatvāt abhivandyaḥ | tathāgatasya guṇāḥ svayamuktāḥ | yathoktamekottarāgame tathāgatavarge- svayamāha- ahaṃ puruṣasārathiḥ puruṣāvataṃsaḥ puruṣahastī śramaṇānāṃ paramo brāhmaṇānāmapyuttamaḥ āryāṇāmadhipo 'pramattacārī, na sukhaduḥkhanuyāyī mama kāya iti |
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is the best among the good. Why? He brings himself to great benefit and brings others to great benefit. One who creates benefit for self and others is indeed a good person. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is supremely skilled in knowing the minds of beings, as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'I am one who thoroughly knows the ultimate nature of beings, compassionate, and a benefactor,' and so forth. Furthermore, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, possesses aggregate-qualities such as vigor and the rest. As <s>Upāli</s> praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> in a hundred verses. Because of being endowed with such qualities, he is worthy of veneration. The qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> have been declared by himself. As stated in the <s>Ekottarāgama</s>, in the section on the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he himself said: 'I am the charioteer of persons, the ornament of persons, the elephant among persons, supreme among <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics), foremost even among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the lord of the <s>Āryas</s> (Noble Ones), one who conducts himself with diligence, not one who follows pleasure and pain — this is my body.'

body.text: (pṛ) tathāgataḥ kasmāt ātmānaṃ ātmabhāvañca praśaṃsati | ātmapraśaṃsanaṃ hi sammūḍhalakṣaṇam | (u) bhagavān na khyātilābhamākāṃkṣate | parārthamevātmabhāvaṃ stauti | tathāgatasya nāstyātmamatiḥ | parahitārthamevātmānaṃ stautītyanavadyam | bahubhiralpairvā pratyayairātmanaḥ praśaṃsā bhavati | tathāgatasya guṇānāmanto na vaktuṃ śakyate | ato na sammūḍhalakṣaṇe patati | ātmana auddhalyābhāvāt | yathā vyavadāna sūtre śāriputrastathāgatasyābhimukhaṃ tathāgataguṇān stauti | ato 'bhivandyaḥ | alpecchatātuṣṭyādayo 'pramāṇaguṇā stathāgatakāye vartante | kasmāt | tathāgatena sarvaguṇānāṃ sañcitatvāt | ityādibhiḥ pratyayairabhivandyastathāgataḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why does the <s>Tathāgata</s> praise himself and his own state? Self-praise is a mark of delusion. (Answer) The Blessed One does not desire fame or gain. He praises his own state only for the benefit of others. The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not have self-regard. Because he praises himself only for the benefit of others, it is blameless. Self-praise arises from many or few conditions. The end of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities cannot be expressed. Therefore it does not fall into the mark of delusion, because there is no haughtiness in him. Just as in the <s>Vyavadāna Sūtra</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s> praises the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> to his face. Therefore he is worthy of veneration. Immeasurable qualities such as few desires, contentment, and the rest exist in the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Why? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s> has accumulated all qualities. For these and other reasons, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is worthy of veneration.

body.text: trividhārakṣāvargaḥ pañcamaḥ
body.translated_text: This is the fifth chapter, the Chapter on the Threefold Non-Guardedness.

body.text: 6 dharmaratnādhikāre tridhākalyāṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 6. Chapter on Threefold Goodness, in the Section on the Jewel of <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: (pṛ) bhavatā pūrvamuktaṃ- dharmo 'bhivandyaḥ iti | kena guṇenābhivandyaḥ | (u) tathāgataḥ svayaṃ pravacanaṃ praśaṃsati- mayā bhāṣito dharma ādau madhye 'vasāne ca kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātamanulomakaṃ brahmacaryamiti | ādau madhye 'vasāne ca kalyāṇamiti | jinaśāsanamakālikaṃ kalyāṇañca bālye yauvane vārdhakye ca kalyāṇam | praveśe prayoge niryāṇe ca kalyāṇam | ādāvakuśalaṃ śamayati | madhye puṇyavipākaṃ hāpayati | avasāne sarvaṃ hāpayati | idaṃ tridhā kalyāṇamityucyate | tathāgato nityaṃ kālatraye saddharmamupadiśati | na tīrthikā ivāsaddharmaṃ vyāmiśrayati | ādau madhye 'vasāne ca sarvadā viduṣāṃ kamanīyam, kālatraye sarvadā gabhīram | nānyasūtravat rādau mahat madhye sūkṣmamavasāne sūkṣmataram | ityādipratyayaiḥ tridhā kalyāṇam |
body.translated_text: (Question) You have previously said: 'The <s>Dharma</s> is worthy of veneration.' By what quality is it worthy of veneration? (Answer) The <s>Tathāgata</s> himself praises his own teaching: 'The <s>Dharma</s> spoken by me is good in the beginning, in the middle, and in the end; good in meaning, good in expression, complete, perfect, pure, stainless, conducive to the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>).' 'Good in the beginning, in the middle, and in the end' means: the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) is timely and good — good in youth, in adulthood, and in old age. Good at the stage of entry, at the stage of practice, and at the stage of completion. In the beginning, it pacifies the unwholesome. In the middle, it removes the fruit of merit. In the end, it removes everything. This is called threefold goodness. The <s>Tathāgata</s> always teaches the true <s>Dharma</s> in all three periods of time. He does not adulterate it with false doctrine as the <s>Tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) do. In the beginning, in the middle, and in the end — always pleasing to the wise, always profound at all three times. Not like other <s>sūtras</s> that are great at the beginning, subtle in the middle, and subtler still at the end. For these and other reasons, it is threefold good.

body.text: svarthamiti | jinaśāsanasyārthaḥ paramahitakaraḥ | aihikalābhasya āmuṣmikalābhasya lokottaramārgalābhasya ca prāpakam | nādhidevatāprārthanārūpabāhyagranthasamānam |
body.translated_text: 'Good in meaning' means: the meaning of the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) produces the highest benefit. It leads to the gain of this life, the gain of the next life, and the gain of the supramundane path. It is not like the external texts which are merely in the form of prayers to deities.

body.text: suvyañjanamiti | prādeśikaprākṛtabhāṣayā samyagarthaṃ prakāśayatīti suvyañjanam | kasmāt | bhāṣaṇaphalaṃ hyarthaprakāśanam | ato bhāṣitāni arthanayaṃ vivecayantīti suvyañjanam | jinaśāsanaṃ yathāvadācaraṇayopadiṣṭam | na tu paṭhanāya | ataḥ prādeśikabhāṣayā mārgaṃ prāpayatīti suvyañjanam | na bāhyatīrthakagranthavat kevalaṃ japārhaṃ bhavati | [tadyathā] yo duṣṭaḥ śabdaḥ yo vā duṣṭasvaraḥ śabdaḥ sa yajamānaṃ hinasti iti | paramārthavacanakuśalatvādvā svartham | lokasatyavacanakuśalatvāt suvyañjanam |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'well-articulated' (<s>suvyañjana</s>): it clearly reveals the meaning through regional vernacular language — thus it is well-articulated. Why? Because the fruit of speech is the illumination of meaning. Therefore, what is spoken discriminates the method of meaning — thus it is well-articulated. The teaching of the <s>Jina</s> is instructed for proper practice, not merely for recitation. Therefore, because it leads one to the path through regional language, it is well-articulated. It is not like the texts of the external <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretics), which are fit merely for chanting — [for example:] 'Whatever word is corrupted, or whatever word has corrupted accent, that injures the sacrificer.' Or, because of skill in ultimate speech, it is well-articulated in its own meaning. Because of skill in conventional speech, it is well-articulated.

body.text: kevalamiti | tathāgataḥ saddharmaṃ kevalamupadiśati | na tu prāgvṛttavastuprapañcaṃ karoti | nāpi dharmamadharmañca saṃkīryopadiśati | nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇārthatvāt kevalam | kevalaṃ tathāgata upadiśatīti vā kevalam | (pṛ) śrāvakanikāyasūtraṃ śrāvakabhāṣitam | santi kānicana anyāni sūtrāṇi ca deva[putra]bhāṣitāni | kasmāducyate kevalaṃ tathāgata upadiśatīti | (u) dharmasyāsya mūlaṃ tathāgatasambhūtam | śrāvakadevaputrādibhiḥ sarvaistathāgatādavavādaḥ
body.translated_text: Regarding 'exclusive' (<s>kevala</s>): the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the true <s>Dharma</s> exclusively. He does not elaborate on past events and circumstances, nor does he teach by mixing <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> together. Because it is for the purpose of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>), it is exclusive. Or, because only the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches it, it is exclusive. (Objection:) The <s>sūtras</s> of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> school are spoken by <s>Śrāvakas</s>. There are also certain other <s>sūtras</s> spoken by <s>devaputras</s> (celestial beings). Why then is it said that only the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches it? (Reply:) The root of this <s>Dharma</s> originates from the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>devaputras</s>, and all others, the instruction was received from the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

body.text: prāptaḥ | yathoktaṃ vinaye- dharmo nāma yat buddhabhāṣitaṃ, śrāvakabhāṣitaṃ nirmitabhāṣitaṃ devabhāṣitaṃ vā saṃkṣipya yāni loke subhāṣitāni tāni sarvāṇi buddhabhāṣitāni | tasmātkevaladharma ityākhyāyate |
body.translated_text: — received. As stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>: '<s>Dharma</s> means whatever is spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>, spoken by <s>Śrāvakas</s>, spoken by emanations, or spoken by <s>devas</s> — in brief, whatever is well-spoken in the world, all of that is spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>.' Therefore it is called the exclusive <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: paripūrṇamiti | tathāgatabhāṣito dharmo na kiñcidvīyate | yathā rūdrakasūtra uktaṃ paripūrṇalakṣaṇam | jinaśāsane nānyasūtrāṇyapekṣya siddhirbhavati | yathā vyākaraṇasūtre pañcasūtrāṇyapekṣyaiva siddhirbhavati | na tathā jinaśāsane | ekasyāmeva gāthāyāmarthaḥ paripūrṇaḥ | yathābhāṣata-
body.translated_text: Regarding 'complete' (<s>paripūrṇa</s>): the <s>Dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> lacks nothing whatsoever. As stated in the <s>Raudra-sūtra</s>, [it has] the characteristic of completeness. In the teaching of the <s>Jina</s>, accomplishment does not depend on other <s>sūtras</s> — unlike in the grammar <s>sūtras</s>, where accomplishment depends on five [supplementary] <s>sūtras</s>. It is not so in the teaching of the <s>Jina</s>: in a single verse alone, the meaning is complete. As he declared:

body.text:
sarvapāpasyākaraṇaṃ kaśalasyopasampadā |
svacittaparyavadapanametabduddhānuśāsanam || iti |
body.translated_text:
The non-commission of all evil, the accumulation of the wholesome,
the purification of one's own mind — this is the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: tasmātparipūrṇam |
body.translated_text: Therefore it is complete.

body.text: pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātamiti | dvidhā pariśuddhatvāt pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātam | vacanapariśuddhatvāt pariśuddham | arthapariśuddhatvāt paryavadātam | tathāgatāt śrutastu samyagarthe nikṣiptaṃ yathārthaṃ vacanaṃ bhavati | samyagvacane ca nikṣipto yathāvacanamartho bhavati | na tīrthikānāmiva yathāsūtraṃ gṛhyate | jinaśāsane dharma āśrīyate na puruṣaḥ | dharmo 'pi nītārthasūtraṃ niśritya nirdiśyate | na neyārthasūtraṃ niśritya | ayaṃ paryavadātadharma ucyate [yo] na sūtramātrānuyāyī bhavati | santi ca jinaśāsanasya tisro dharmamudrāḥ- sarvamanātmā, sarve saṃskṛtadharmāḥ kṣaṇikā anityāḥ- śāntaṃ nirodho nirvāṇam iti | imā stisro dharmamudrāḥ sarvairapi vādibhirna śakyāḥ khaṇḍayitum | paramārthikatvācca pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātam |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'pure and immaculate' (<s>pariśuddha</s>, <s>paryavadāta</s>): because of twofold purity, it is pure and immaculate. Because of purity of speech, it is pure (<s>pariśuddha</s>). Because of purity of meaning, it is immaculate (<s>paryavadāta</s>). What is heard from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, when placed in correct meaning, becomes speech that accords with reality. And when placed in correct speech, the meaning accords with the words. It is not grasped literally as with the <s>tīrthikas</s>. In the teaching of the <s>Jina</s>, one relies on the <s>Dharma</s>, not on the person. The <s>Dharma</s> too is taught relying on <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning (<s>nītārthasūtra</s>), not on <s>sūtras</s> of provisional meaning (<s>neyārthasūtra</s>). This immaculate <s>Dharma</s> is said to be [that which] does not merely follow the <s>sūtra</s> text. And the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> has three <s>Dharma</s>-seals (<s>dharmamudrā</s>): all [phenomena] are without self (<s>anātman</s>), all conditioned <s>dharmas</s> are momentary and impermanent, and the cessation that is peace is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. These three <s>Dharma</s>-seals cannot be refuted even by all disputants. And because of being ultimate, it is pure and immaculate.

body.text: brahmacaryamiti | āryāṣṭāṅgikamārgo brahmacaryam | nirvāṇākhyamidamayaṃ mārgaḥ prāpayatīti brahmacaryam |
body.translated_text: Regarding '<s>brahmacarya</s>' (the holy life): the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>) is the holy life. Because this path leads to that which is called <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, it is the holy life.

body.text: īdṛśaguṇasampannatvāddharmaratnamabhibandyam ||
body.translated_text: Because of being endowed with such qualities, the Jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> is worthy of devotion.

body.text: dharmaratnādhikāre tridhākalyāṇavargaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: In the section on the Jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>, this is the sixth chapter: the Chapter on the Threefold Auspiciousness (<s>tridhākalyāṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 7 dharmaguṇaskandhavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 7. Chapter on the Aggregates of <s>Dharma</s>-Qualities (<s>dharmaguṇaskandhavarga</s>)

body.text: atha tathāgataḥ svayaṃ svadharmaṃ stauti- mama dharmo nirodho nirvāṇagāmī samyak sambodhijanaka aupanāyika iti |
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself praises his own <s>Dharma</s>: 'My <s>Dharma</s> is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, producing perfect awakening (<s>samyak sambodhi</s>), and leading one onward (<s>aupanāyika</s>).'

body.text: rāgadveṣādīn kleśāgnīna nirodhayatīti nirodhaḥ | yathā aśubhabhāvanā kāmāgniṃ nirodhayati | yathā vā maitrībhāvanā vyāpādaṃ nirodhayati | na tīrthikānāmiva āhārādiprahāṇānnirodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Because it extinguishes the fires of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) such as passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and others, it is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). Just as meditation on the impure (<s>aśubhabhāvanā</s>) extinguishes the fire of desire. And just as the cultivation of loving-kindness (<s>maitrībhāvanā</s>) extinguishes ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>). It is not cessation through the abandoning of food and such, as with the <s>tīrthikas</s>.

body.text: nirvāṇa[gāmī]ti | tathāgatadharmo 'tyantanirvāṇagāmī | na tīrthikānāmiva bhavāṅge sthitvā dhyānasamādhiṣvāsañjayati | buddhāgama ucyate sarve saṃskṛtāḥ sādīnavā nāniśaṃsāsthānam iti | na tu yathā brāhmaṇāḥ brahmalokādīn praśaṃsanti | atastathāgatadharmo nirvāṇagāmī |
body.translated_text: 'Leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>': the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> leads ultimately to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. It is not like the <s>tīrthikas</s>' [teaching], which, remaining in the limbs of existence (<s>bhavāṅga</s>), becomes attached to <s>dhyānas</s> and <s>samādhis</s>. The <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching declares that all conditioned things are disadvantageous and not a place of benefit. It is not like the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who praise the <s>Brahma</s>-world and similar [realms]. Therefore the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> leads to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: samyaksambodhijanaka iti | tathāgatasya san dharmo nirvāṇāya bhavati ityataḥ samyaksambodhijanakaḥ | tathāgatadharme 'sti tattvajñānaṃ phalam | yathā śrutamayaprajñātaścintāmayī prajñā bhavati | tato bhāvanāmayī prajñā bhavati | ato buddhadharmaḥ samyaksambodhijanaka ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'producing perfect awakening' (<s>samyaksambodhijanaka</s>): the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is for the purpose of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — therefore it produces perfect awakening. In the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, there is the fruit of knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>). Just as from wisdom born of learning (<s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>) arises wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>), and from that arises wisdom born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>). Therefore the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is said to produce perfect awakening.

body.text: aupanāyika iti | buddhadharmaḥ pūrvamātmanaḥ kalyāṇaṃ sādhayati | paścāt parān saddharme sthāpayatīti aupanāyikaḥ |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'leading one onward' (<s>aupanāyika</s>): the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> first accomplishes one's own welfare, and afterwards establishes others in the true <s>Dharma</s> — thus it is leading one onward.

body.text: buddha dharmaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ- svākhyāto [bhagavatā] sāndṛṣṭikaḥ akālikaḥ aupanāyika ehipaśyakaḥ pratyātmaṃ vedayitavyo vijñaiḥ | svākhyāta iti | tathāgato dharmān yathādharmalakṣaṇamupadiśati | akuśaladharmān akuśalalakṣaṇāniti upadiśati | kuśalān kuśalalakṣaṇāniti | ataḥ svākhyātaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is sixfold: well-proclaimed by the Blessed One (<s>svākhyāta</s>), visible here and now (<s>sāndṛṣṭika</s>), timeless (<s>akālika</s>), leading one onward (<s>aupanāyika</s>), inviting one to come and see (<s>ehipaśyaka</s>), and to be individually experienced by the wise (<s>pratyātmaṃ vedayitavyo vijñaiḥ</s>). Regarding 'well-proclaimed' (<s>svākhyāta</s>): the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches <s>dharmas</s> according to their true characteristics. He teaches unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> as having unwholesome characteristics, and wholesome ones as having wholesome characteristics. Therefore it is well-proclaimed.

body.text: sāndṛṣṭika iti | buddhadharmo dṛṣṭa eva loke vipākaṃ prāpayati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- prātarvinītaḥ sāyaṃ mārgamanuprāpnoti | sāyamupadiṣṭaḥ prātarmārgamanuprāpnoti iti | sāndṛṣṭikaṃ yathā sāndṛṣṭikaśrāmaṇyaphalasūtra uktam | sāndṛṣṭikāḥ khalu khyātipūjāsatkāradhyānasamādhyabhijñādīnāṃ lābhāḥ iti | buddhadharmo 'rthanayayuktaḥ | ataḥ sāndṛṣṭikaṃ pūjāsatkāraṃ prāpayan aurdhvavipākaṃ nirvāṇaśca prāpayati | tīrthikadharmāṇāmarthanayābhāvāt sāndṛṣṭikavipākaeva nāsti | kiṃpunaraurdhvalaukikaṃ nirvāṇamiti sāndṛṣṭika ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'visible here and now' (<s>sāndṛṣṭika</s>): the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> yields its fruits in this very visible world. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One instructed in the morning attains the path by evening; one instructed in the evening attains the path by morning.' The visible [fruit] is as stated in the <s>Sāndṛṣṭikaśrāmaṇyaphala-sūtra</s> (the Sūtra on the Visible Fruits of the Ascetic Life): 'Visible indeed are the gains of renown, honor, respect, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, <s>abhijñā</s> (supernormal knowledges), and the rest.' The <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is endowed with the method of meaning. Therefore, yielding visible results such as honor and respect, it also yields results in higher [existences] and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Since the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>tīrthikas</s> lack the method of meaning, they do not even have visible results — how much less supramundane <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? Thus it is called 'visible here and now.'

body.text: akālika iti | buddhadharmo na kañcana divasaṃ māsaṃ vatsaraṃ nakṣatraṃ vāpekṣya mārgo bhāvyate | asmin divase māse vatsare va mārgo na bhāvyata iti | na brāhmaṇadharmavat vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnīnādadhīta grīṣme rājanya ityādi | punarudite juhoti anudite juhoti | yathā paśyāmaḥ pañca dhānyāni kālamapekṣyopyante | tathā buddhadharmo 'pi bhaviṣyatīti kaścit vadet | ata āha akālika iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre buddhadharmaḥ svācāraścaryāsthitiniṣādanaśayaneṣvakālika iti |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'timeless' (<s>akālika</s>): the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> does not require any particular day, month, year, or constellation for the path to be cultivated. [There is no restriction that] 'on this day, in this month, or in this year, the path should not be cultivated.' It is not like the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>dharma</s>, [which prescribes:] 'In spring, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> kindles the fires; in summer, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>,' and so forth. Furthermore, [the Vedic injunctions say:] 'One offers oblations when the sun has risen; one offers when it has not risen.' Just as we see that the five grains ripen by depending on the seasons — someone might say that the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> would be similar. Therefore it is declared 'timeless.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is timeless in one's conduct, practice, abiding, sitting, and lying down.'

body.text: aupanāuyika iti | samyak caryayā sattvān vimuktimupanayatīti aupanāyikaḥ |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'leading one onward' (<s>aupanāyika</s>): through right practice, it leads beings to liberation — thus it is leading one onward.

body.text: ehipaśyaka iti | baddhadharmaḥ svakāyena sākṣātkartavyo bhaviṣyati na parānuvartanena | yathāvocadbhagavān- mā bhikṣavaḥ kevalaṃ mama pravacanādhimuktikā bhavata | svayameva parīkṣadhvam ayaṃ dharma ācāritavyaḥ ayamanācaritavya iti | na yathā tīrthikā vadanti svaśiṣyān- praśnaprativacanaṃ mā kurudhvam | yathāvat śucisnātā bhavata, mā malinābhirucikāḥ | badhiramūkavat mama vacanamātramanusarata iti | ata āha ehipaśyaka iti |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'inviting one to come and see' (<s>ehipaśyaka</s>): the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is to be directly realized by one's own body, not by following others. As the Blessed One declared: 'O monks, do not be merely convinced by my teaching through faith alone. Examine for yourselves — this <s>Dharma</s> is to be practiced, and this is not to be practiced.' It is not like the <s>tīrthikas</s> who tell their disciples: 'Do not engage in questioning and answering. Be properly bathed and clean; do not be fond of filthiness. Like the deaf and mute, merely follow my words.' Therefore it is declared 'inviting one to come and see.'

body.text: pratyātmaṃ vedayitavyo vijñairiti | buddhadharmo vijñānāmadhimuktikānāñca hitakaraḥ | upavāsādau paramamugdhāḥ śraddadhante vijñaiḥ sukhaṃ na vedyata iti | kleśasamūhananasamyak jñānādibhirdharmai rvijño mucyate | āhārabharite 'pi svadehe cittaikāgratāvīryarāgadveṣasapīḍanādīni
body.translated_text: Regarding 'to be individually experienced by the wise' (<s>pratyātmaṃ vedayitavyo vijñaiḥ</s>): the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> benefits the wise and those of deep conviction. In matters like fasting and the rest, even the most deluded have faith — it is not [something] happily experienced by the wise. Through <s>dharmas</s> such as the right knowledge that destroys the aggregation of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), the wise person is liberated. Even in a body that has been well fed, one-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>), vigor, and the torments of passion and hatred —

body.text: vijño dṛṣṭa eva vedayate | yathā kaścit rogānmuktaḥ adhyātmaṃ pravivekaṃ vedayate | yathā vā śītalakṣaṇaṃ vedayate jalapāyī | kecit sadoṣaṃ dharmaṃ vadanti yathā khakkaṭalakṣaṇā pṛthivī iti | kiṃ khakkaṭalakṣaṇam ityasya spṛṣṭvā vedayitavyam iti prativacanaṃ na vindate | yathā jātyandho nīlapītalohitāvadātān na vyavahartuṃ śaknoti | [tathā] yo buddhadharmarasasyāpratilābhī, na sa buddhadharmasya paramārthaṃ vyavahartuṃ śankoti | upaśamātmakatvāt |
body.translated_text: — the wise person experiences [these] directly in this very life. Just as someone freed from illness internally experiences well-being. And just as one who drinks water experiences its coolness. Some speak of the <s>Dharma</s> as having faults, saying, for example, 'the earth has the characteristic of hardness.' [If asked,] 'What is the characteristic of hardness?' — the answer 'it must be experienced by touch' is not forthcoming. Just as one born blind cannot distinguish blue, yellow, red, and white, so too one who has not obtained the taste of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> cannot properly discuss the ultimate meaning of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> — because it is of the nature of peace (<s>upaśama</s>).

body.text: atha buddhadharma adhyātmamadhigantavyaḥ na dhanādivat svayamadhigamya parasmai pradātavyaḥ | yathā pārāyaṇa sūtre bhagavānāha- nāhaṃ [bhikṣava] ucchetsyāmi vaḥ kāṃkṣām | mama dharmamadhigacchantaḥ svayamucchetsyatha kāṃkṣām | iti | nāyaṃ dharmaḥ paragāmī san upalabhyate, tejaḥ saṃkramādivat | pṛthagjanā avidyāparvatapraticchannā na śraddhadhanta imaṃ dharmam | yathā aciravata śrāmaṇeramupādāya mahāparvatadṛṣṭāntamavocat | ata āha pratyātmaṃ vedayitavyo vijñairiti |
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is to be realized internally — it cannot be attained by oneself and then given to another, like wealth and such things. As stated in the <s>Pārāyaṇa-sūtra</s>, the Blessed One said: 'O monks, I shall not cut through your doubts. Realizing my <s>Dharma</s>, you yourselves will cut through your doubts.' This <s>Dharma</s> is not obtained by being transferred to another, like the transference of radiance and so forth. Ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), covered by the mountain of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), do not have faith in this <s>Dharma</s>. As was said with reference to the novice <s>Aciravata</s>, using the simile of the great mountain. Therefore it is declared: 'to be individually experienced by the wise.'

body.text: buddhadharmo gahanaḥ | vivriyamāṇaḥ san sulabho bhavati | santrasyatāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ māyāmapanayati | gahana iti buddhadharmasya gahanatvam | kāraṇajñānāt | laukikā hi bahavo dṛṣṭaphalaṃ paśryanto na jānanti tatkāraṇam | ato vadanti īśvarādīni mithyākāraṇāni | dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo durbodhaḥ, gabhīratvāt | uttānacetanā laukikā buddhadharme na gabhīrasaṃjñāṃ kurvanti | na pratibudhyante pratītyasamutpādadharmam | tṛṇamapi hetupratyayaiḥ sañcitaṃ parīkṣayituḥ tallakṣaṇaṃ gabhīraṃ vivartate | yathā bhagavatā bhāṣitaḥ pratītyasamutpādadharmo gahanaṃ vastu | [tathā] tṛṣṇāyāḥ kṣayo viyogo nirodho nirvāṇam, idaṃ padaṃ durdarśam |
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is profound (<s>gahana</s>). When it is disclosed, it becomes easy to understand. For frightened gods and humans, it removes delusion. 'Profound' — the profundity of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> is because of the knowledge of causes. For many worldly people, seeing the visible fruits, do not know their causes. Therefore they speak of false causes such as <s>Īśvara</s> (a creator God) and others. The twelvefold dependent origination (<s>dvādaśāṅga pratītyasamutpāda</s>) is difficult to comprehend, because of its profundity. Worldly beings with shallow understanding do not form the notion of profundity regarding the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>. They do not awaken to the <s>dharma</s> of dependent origination. Even a blade of grass, when examined as assembled from causes and conditions, its characteristic unfolds as profound. As the Blessed One declared: 'The <s>dharma</s> of dependent origination is a profound matter.' [Likewise:] 'The cessation of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), separation, extinction — <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — this state is difficult to perceive.'

body.text: (pṛ) yadi pratītyasamutpādo gabhīraḥ | kuta ānanda uttānaka saṃjñāmutpāditavān | (u) kecidvā dino vadanti- nedaṃ vacanaṃ yuktam | ānando mahān śrāvako dharmalakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī kathaṃ vadiṣyati pratītyasamutpādadharma uttānaka iti | sāmānyalakṣaṇena pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyata uttānakasaṃjñotpadyate | kasmāt | na hi sa karmakleśān suvivicya paśyati | āditaḥ śikṣitasya vastunaḥ paryantaṃ labdhavato [vā] uttānakasaṃjñotpadyate | yathā pratilabdhābhisambodhaḥ
body.translated_text: (Objection:) If dependent origination is profound, how did <s>Ānanda</s> generate the notion that it is straightforward? (Reply:) Some say: 'This statement is not proper. <s>Ānanda</s>, being a great <s>Śrāvaka</s> who understood the characteristics of <s>Dharma</s>, how could he say that the <s>dharma</s> of dependent origination is straightforward?' When one views dependent origination by its general characteristics, the notion of it being straightforward arises. Why? Because he does not discriminate well between <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (defilements). For one who has been trained from the beginning and has reached the end of that matter, the notion of it being straightforward arises. Just as one who has attained awakening —

body.text: punaḥ prāthamikavākyamīkṣate | kecit punaḥ gabhīradharme 'niṣpannacetanāḥ santa uttānakasaṃjñāmutpādayanti | kecittu sattvā uttānakasaṃjñāmutpādayanti | tathāgatena dharmasya svākhyātatvāt |
body.translated_text: — again looks at the preliminary words. But some beings, having immature understanding in the profound <s>Dharma</s>, generate the notion that it is straightforward. Yet certain beings generate the notion that it is straightforward because of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s quality of having well-proclaimed the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha buddhadharmaḥ śūnyatā [deśanaḥ] | śūnyateyaṃ gabhīrā | tathāgate nānāhetupratyayadṛṣṭāntairarthaṃ prakāśayati sati subodhā bhavati | bālā api jānanti yathā sudā ya śrāmaṇerādayaḥ | buddhadharmaḥ sāravān sarvapravacaneṣu tattvārthaḥ pradhāno bhavati | na yathā bhāratarāmāyaṇādīni tattvārthaṃ vinā kevalākhyānarūpāṇi | yathā vā rāghabrāhmaṇa āha- bhagavān bhikṣūn arthadharme paramārthadharme yogaṃ śikṣāpayati yadutāsravakṣaye | iti |
body.translated_text: Now, the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> is [a teaching of] <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). This <s>śūnyatā</s> is profound. When the <s>Tathāgata</s> illuminates its meaning through various causes, conditions, and examples, it becomes easy to comprehend. Even the unlearned can understand it, such as young <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> (novice monks) and the like. The teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> has substance — in all [his] discourses, the meaning of reality (<s>tattvārtha</s>) is primary. Not like the <s>Bhārata</s>, <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, and others, which are merely in the form of narratives without the meaning of reality. As the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Rāgha</s> said: 'The Blessed One trains the monks in the practice of the <s>Dharma</s> of meaning and the <s>Dharma</s> of ultimate meaning, namely, in the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements).'

body.text: buddhadharmaḥ sarvalokānāmarthāyopadiṣṭaḥ, na brāhmaṇā iva brāhmaṇadharmaṃ vadanta ātmana eva bodhimanuprāpnuvanti; nānyeṣām buddhadharmaḥ satkāryaḥ | pañcakāmeṣu ātmārāmā devamanuṣyā api śraddhadhante; ityādibhiḥ pratyayairdharmo 'bhivandyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> has been taught for the benefit of all beings, not like the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who, teaching the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-<s>dharma</s>, attain awakening only for themselves and not for others. The teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> is effective. Even gods and humans who delight in themselves amidst the five sense-pleasures place their faith [in it]. For these and other reasons, the <s>Dharma</s> is worthy of veneration.

body.text: dharmaguṇaskandhavargaḥ saptamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the seventh chapter, the Chapter on the Aggregate-Qualities of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: 8 dvādaśāṅgapravacanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 8. Chapter on the Twelve Divisions of the Teaching (<s>Dvādaśāṅga-pravacana</s>)

body.text: atha tathāgataśāsanaṃ dvādaśadhā vibhaktam- sūtraṃ, geyaṃ, vyākaraṇaṃ, gāthā, udānaṃ, nidānaṃ, apadānaṃ, itivṛttakaṃ, jātakaṃ, vaipulyaṃ, adbhutadharma upadeśaśceti |
body.translated_text: Now, the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is divided into twelve [parts]: <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>nidāna</s>, <s>apadāna</s>, <s>itivṛttaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharma</s>, and <s>upadeśa</s>.

body.text: sūtraṃ svakaṇṭhoktaṃ pravacanam |
body.translated_text: <s>Sūtra</s> is the teaching spoken in the [<s>Tathāgata</s>'s] own voice.

body.text: geyaṃ gāthayoddiṣṭaṃ sūtraṃ gāthābhāṣitaṃ [tathāgata]śrāvakabhāṣitaṃ vā | (pṛ) kasya hetorgāthayā sūtroddeśaḥ | (u) arthasya dārḍhyacikīrṣayā | yathā rajjunibaddhāni kusumāni dṛḍhāni bhavanti | puruṣāṇāṃ saṃpraharṣaṇāya śabdālaṅkārecchayā ca | yathā alaṅkaraṇāya puṣpāṇi vikīryante mālā vā dhriyate | gāthānibaddho 'rthaḥ saṃkṣiptaḥ sugamo bhavati | kecit sattvā gadyavacanādhimuktikāḥ | kecittu gāthādhimuktikāḥ | pūrvaṃ kaṇṭhoktasya dharmasya paścādgāthayopadiṣṭasyārthaḥ spaṣṭapratītaḥ śraddhādārḍhyakṛdbhavati | gāthānibaddho 'rthaḥ sāsakti kramaśaḥ supāṭhyo bhavati | ato gāthāmāha |
body.translated_text: <s>Geya</s> is a <s>sūtra</s> introduced by a <s>gāthā</s> (verse) — spoken in verse, spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> or by [his] <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples). (Question) For what reason is the <s>sūtra</s> introduced by a <s>gāthā</s>? (Answer) Out of the desire to strengthen the meaning. Just as flowers bound by a string become firm. For the delight of persons, and out of the desire for verbal ornamentation. Just as flowers are scattered or garlands are worn for adornment. The meaning bound in <s>gāthā</s> is concise and easy to understand. Some beings are inclined toward prose. Others are inclined toward verse. The meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> previously spoken in [prose] voice, when subsequently taught in verse, becomes clearly understood and strengthens faith. The meaning bound in <s>gāthā</s> is easy to recite gradually in sequence. Therefore he speaks in <s>gāthā</s>.

body.text: kecidāhu- śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ na kāvyapratirūpayā gāthayā racayitavyamiti | tadayuktam | gāthayā racayitavyameva | kasmāt | bhagavatā arthānāṃ gāthayā bhāṣitatvāt | yathāha sūtram- sarve lokāḥ supraṇītavacananirūktikā mama pravrajitāḥ | iti | tasmādgāthā supraṇītavacanā bhavati |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'The teaching of the Master should not be composed in <s>gāthā</s> resembling poetry.' That is not correct. It should indeed be composed in <s>gāthā</s>. Why? Because the Blessed One has himself spoken meanings in verse. As the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'All the world, having gone forth as my renunciants, are skilled in well-spoken words and etymology.' Therefore <s>gāthā</s> consists of well-spoken words.

body.text: vyākaraṇam | arthavibhaṅgasūtrāṇi vyākaraṇamityucyante | yat sūtramaprativacanamavibhaṅgaṃ yathā catuḥpratisaṃ vidādisūtram tat sūtramityucyate sapraśnaprativacanaṃ sūtrantuyathocyate- catvāraḥ pudgalāḥ | [katame catvāraḥ] | tamastamaḥparāyaṇaḥ, tamojyotiḥparāyaṇaḥ, jyotirjyotiḥparāyaṇaḥ, jyotistamaḥparāyaṇaḥ | tamastamaḥparāyaṇaḥ katamaḥ | yathā kaścit daridro vividhānyakuśalakarmāṇi kṛtvā durgatau patati | ityādi sūtraṃ vyākaraṇam | (pṛ) kasya hetorbhagavānupadiśati apraśnaprativacanamavibhaṅgañca sūtram | (u) kānicana sūtrāṇi gabhīragurvarthanayāni | teṣāṃ sūtrāṇāmartho 'bhidharme vivicya vaktavya ityato 'vibhaṅgamupadiśati |
body.translated_text: <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (explanation): <s>sūtras</s> that analyze meanings are called <s>vyākaraṇa</s>. A <s>sūtra</s> that has no question-and-answer and no analysis, such as the <s>sūtra</s> on the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) and the like, is simply called a <s>sūtra</s>. A <s>sūtra</s> with questions and answers is called [<s>vyākaraṇa</s>], as when it is said: 'There are four types of persons. Which four? One going from darkness to darkness, one going from darkness to light, one going from light to light, one going from light to darkness. Which is the one going from darkness to darkness? Such as a poor person who, having done various unwholesome deeds, falls into a lower realm.' Such a <s>sūtra</s> with analysis is <s>vyākaraṇa</s>. (Question) For what reason does the Blessed One teach <s>sūtras</s> without questions, answers, and analysis? (Answer) Certain <s>sūtras</s> have meanings that are deep and weighty in import. The meaning of those <s>sūtras</s> is to be discussed in the <s>Abhidharma</s> in detail — therefore he teaches them without analysis.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- tathāgatabhāṣitāni sarvāṇi sūtrāṇi sārthavibhaṅgāni | kintu saṅgīti kārā gabhīrasūtrārthān saṅgṛhyābhidharme prākṣipan | yathā bāhyābhyantarasaṃyojanikaḥ puruṣaḥ sadā rātrāvarthaṃ vibhajate | ityanena hetunā ayamarthaḥ saṃyojanaskandhe niveśitavya iti |
body.translated_text: Some say: All the <s>sūtras</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> are with analysis of meaning. But the compilers of the council (<s>saṅgītikāras</s>) extracted the meanings of the profound <s>sūtras</s> and placed them in the <s>Abhidharma</s>. Just as a person who ties together inner and outer matters always analyzes meanings at night. For this reason, the saying: 'This meaning should be placed in the aggregate of fetters (<s>saṃyojanaskandha</s>).'

body.text: gāthā- dvitīyamaṅgaṃ geyamityucyate | geyameva gāthā | dvividhā gāthā | gāthā ca ślokaḥ | ślokaśca dvividhaḥ kleśabhāgīyo 'kleśabhāgīya iti | akleśabhāgīya geya ucyamāno gāthetyucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Gāthā</s> (verse): The second division is called <s>geya</s>. <s>Geya</s> itself is <s>gāthā</s>. <s>Gāthā</s> is of two kinds: <s>gāthā</s> and <s>śloka</s> (verse). <s>Śloka</s> too is of two kinds: that which pertains to defilements and that which does not pertain to defilements. The <s>geya</s> that does not pertain to defilements is called <s>gāthā</s>.

body.text: dvividhāṃ gāthāṃ vihāyānyat gāthārahitaṃ sūtram udānamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Setting aside the two kinds of <s>gāthā</s>, the remaining <s>sūtra</s> devoid of <s>gāthā</s> is called <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance).

body.text: nidānaṃ sūtranidānam | kasmāt | tathāgatairāryaiścopadiśyamānāni sūtrāṇi avaśyaṃ sanidānāni bhavanti | tāni sūtranidānāni kadācit sūtra eva vartante anyatra vā vartante | tasmānnidānamityākhyā |
body.translated_text: <s>Nidāna</s> (introduction): This is the introduction (<s>nidāna</s>) of a <s>sūtra</s>. Why? Because <s>sūtras</s> taught by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and <s>Āryas</s> (Noble Ones) necessarily have introductions. Those <s>sūtra</s>-introductions sometimes occur within the <s>sūtra</s> itself and sometimes occur elsewhere. Therefore the designation <s>nidāna</s>.

body.text: apadānam- paurvāparyakramakathanamidam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- viduṣāṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ sakramaṃ sārthaṃ savibhaṅgamavikṣepakam | iti | idamapadānam |
body.translated_text: <s>Apadāna</s> (narrative): This is the orderly narration of prior and subsequent events. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The speech of the wise is sequential, meaningful, analytical, and non-distracting.' This is <s>apadāna</s>.

body.text: itivṛttakam- idaṃ sūtrasya nidānaṃ bhavati, sūtrasyānantarañca bhavati | yadi dvitayamidaṃ sūtrasyātītādhvavṛttikaṃ bhavati | tat itivṛttakamityucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Itivṛttaka</s> (historical account): This serves as the <s>nidāna</s> of a <s>sūtra</s>, and also as what follows a <s>sūtra</s>. When both of these relate to events of the past, it is called <s>itivṛttaka</s>.

body.text: jātakam- pratyutpannaṃ vastūṇadāya tadatītavastuvarṇanam | tathāgato 'nāgataṃ vastu kathayannapi atītaṃ pratyutpannamupādāyaiva kathayatītyataḥ pṛthaṅ nocyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Jātaka</s> (birth story): Taking a present event as the occasion, it describes a past event. Although the <s>Tathāgata</s> also narrates future events, he narrates them by taking the past and present as the basis — therefore [future narratives] are not separately designated.

body.text: vaipulyam- bhagavato vipula upadeśo vaipulyam | kecinna śraddadhante yanmahāmunaya upaśamābhiratā na vikṣepavighāte suprītikā laukikasaṃbhinnapralāpānnirviṇṇāḥ samulluñchitendriyagrāmārāmāśca santo na vipulopadeśāyābhirocanta iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- mārgasya pratilābhī puruṣo dvau māsāvatītya ekamakṣaramuccārayati | iti | tadvyāvartānayocyate asti vaipulyasūtraṃ parārthāya | yathoktaṃ- tathāgato vaipulyataḥ saṃkṣepataśca dvidhā dharmamupadiśati | tatra vaipulyaṃ saṃkṣepāt prakṛṣṭam iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Vaipulya</s> (extensive discourse): The extensive teaching of the Blessed One is <s>vaipulya</s>. Some do not believe this, [arguing] that great sages who delight in tranquility are not pleased with the disturbance of dispersion; that, being disgusted with worldly idle chatter, and being those whose aggregate-garden of faculties has been uprooted, they do not take delight in extensive teaching. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A person who has attained the path, after two months have passed, utters a single syllable.' To counter this [view], it is said: there is <s>vaipulya sūtra</s> for the benefit of others. As stated: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in two ways — extensively and concisely. Therein, the extensive is superior to the concise.'

body.text: adbhutadharmaḥ- adbhutasūtram | yathāha kalpānte bhūtāni vikṛtavṛttāni, devakāyā mahāpramāṇāḥ pṛthivī ca samprakampante | iti | kecinna śraddadhanta īdṛśāni vastūni | ata ucyata idamadbhutasūtram | karmavipākadharmāṇāmacintyaśakterdarśanāt |
body.translated_text: <s>Adbhutadharma</s> (marvelous events): This is the <s>sūtra</s> of marvels. As it says: 'At the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), beings behave strangely; the bodies of gods are of great measure; and the earth trembles.' Some do not believe in such things. Therefore it is said: 'This is the <s>sūtra</s> of marvels' — because the power of the ripening of <s>karma</s> is inconceivable.

body.text: upadeśaḥ- mahākātyāyanādayo mahājñānino bhagavadbhāṣitaṃ suvistṛtaṃ vyabhajanta | kecinna śraddadhante nedaṃ buddhabhāṣitamiti | tadarthaṃ bhagavānāha- asti śāstrātmakasūtram iti | sūtrasya śāstrapratirūpatvādarthaḥ sugamo bhavati |
body.translated_text: <s>Upadeśa</s> (instruction): <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> and other great knowledgeable ones analyzed in detail what the Blessed One had spoken. Some do not believe [this], [saying]: 'This is not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>.' For this reason, the Blessed One said: 'There exists a <s>sūtra</s> that has the character of a <s>śāstra</s> (treatise).' Because the <s>sūtra</s> has the form of a treatise, its meaning becomes easy to understand.

body.text: imāni dvādaśāṅgāni sūtrāṇi śāstuḥpravacanam | dharmaratnamīdṛśaguṇasampannamityato 'bhivandyam ||
body.translated_text: These twelve divisions of the <s>sūtras</s> are the teaching of the Master. Because the jewel of <s>Dharma</s> is endowed with such qualities, it is worthy of veneration.

body.text: dvādaśāṅgapravacanavargo 'ṣṭamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the eighth chapter, the Chapter on the Twelve Divisions of the Teaching.

body.text: 9 saṅgharatnādhikāre ādyaviśuddhivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 9. Chapter on the Initial Purity, in the Section on the Jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s>

body.text: (pṛ) bhavatā pūrvamuktam- saṅgho 'bhivandya iti | kasmādabhivandyaḥ | (u) tathāgataḥ sarvatna saṅghaṃ praśaṃsati- saṅgharatnamidaṃ śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaviśuddham,
body.translated_text: (Question) You have previously said: 'The <s>Saṅgha</s> is worthy of veneration.' Why is it worthy of veneration? (Answer) The <s>Tathāgata</s> everywhere praises the <s>Saṅgha</s>: 'This jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s> is purified in the aggregate of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), the aggregate of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), the aggregate of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the aggregate of <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), and the aggregate of <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (knowledge and vision of liberation),

body.text: āhvanīyaṃ, prahvanīyaṃ dakṣiṇeyamañjalikaraṇīyamanuttaraṃ puṇyakṣetraṃ dāyakānāṃ hitakaram iti |
body.translated_text: worthy of invitation, worthy of homage, worthy of offerings, worthy of the <s>añjali</s> (gesture of reverence), the unsurpassed field of merit, and beneficial to donors.'

body.text: śīlaskandhaviśuddhamiti | tathāgata śrāvakasaṅghaḥ aneḍakaṃ śīlaṃ dhārayan yāvadalpāparādhe 'pi paramatrāsaśaṅkī bhavati | jinaurasāḥ puṇyavipākāya na devamanuṣyādiṣūtpadyante | narakādibhyo 'pyabhītāḥ śīlaṃ saprayatnaṃ dhārayantaḥ kevalaṃ saddharmābhiratā bhavanti | kasmādviśuddhaṃ śīlam | viśuddhaśīladhāraṇañca na kālaparicchinnam | na brāhmaṇānāmiva ṣāṇmāsikaṃ śīladhāraṇam | [apitu] dīrgharātraṃ yāvadantamupādīyate | ato viśuddham | viśuddhaṃ śīlamantadvayavimuktaṃ pañcakāmaguṇavimuktaṃ duḥkhakāyavisuktañca dadhate | ata āryāṇāṃ kāntaśīlā bhavanti | tacchīlaṃ vijñānāñca priyaṃ bhavati | cittaṃ viśuddhamityataḥ śīlamapi viśuddham | praśamitādhyāśayadoṣā na kevalaṃ śīlaṃ rakṣanti | paralokādapi bibhyanti | ataḥ saṅgharatnaṃ śīlaskandhaviśuddham |
body.translated_text: 'Purified in the aggregate of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct)': The <s>Saṅgha</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples), maintaining unblemished <s>śīla</s>, is trembling with utmost fear even at the slightest transgression. The sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) are not reborn among gods, humans, and the like for the ripening of merit. Fearless even of the hells and the like, they maintain <s>śīla</s> with effort, solely delighting in the true <s>Dharma</s>. Why is their <s>śīla</s> purified? Because the maintenance of purified <s>śīla</s> is not limited by time — not like the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who maintain <s>śīla</s> for [only] six months. Rather, it is taken up for the long duration, until the end. Therefore it is purified. They maintain purified <s>śīla</s> that is free from both extremes, free from the five strands of sensual pleasure, and free from the body of suffering. Therefore the <s>Āryas</s> (Noble Ones) have lovely <s>śīla</s>. That <s>śīla</s> is also pleasing to consciousness. Because the mind is purified, <s>śīla</s> too is purified. They do not merely guard <s>śīla</s> with pacified inner defects — they also fear the next world. Therefore the jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s> is purified in the aggregate of <s>śīla</s>.

body.text: samādhiskandhaviśuddhamiti | yaḥ samādhistattvajñānamutpādayati sa viśuddha ityucyate |
body.translated_text: 'Purified in the aggregate of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration)': The <s>samādhi</s> that generates knowledge of reality is called purified.

body.text: prajñāskandhaviśuddhamiti | prajñā kleśān kṣapayatītyato viśuddhā |
body.translated_text: 'Purified in the aggregate of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)': <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) is purified because it destroys the defilements.

body.text: vimuktiviśuddhamiti | yā sarvakleśānāṃ kṣayaṃ prāpayati na kevalaṃ vighnayati | ato vimuktirviśuddhā |
body.translated_text: 'Purified in <s>vimukti</s> (liberation)': That which brings about the complete destruction of all defilements, not merely obstructing them — therefore <s>vimukti</s> is purified.

body.text: vimuktijñānadarśanaviśuddhamiti | kṣīṇakleśānāṃ jñānaṃ bhavati yaduta kṣīṇā me jātiriti | nākṣīṇakleśānām | idaṃ vimuktijñānadarśanaṃ viśuddham |
body.translated_text: 'Purified in <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (knowledge and vision of liberation)': For those whose defilements are destroyed, there arises the knowledge: 'My births are exhausted.' Not for those whose defilements are not destroyed. This knowledge and vision of liberation is purified.

body.text: āhvanīyaṃ prahvanīyaṃ dakṣiṇeyamañjalikaraṇīyamiti | īdṛśaguṇasampannatvāt āhvanīyaṃ prahvanīyaṃ dakṣiṇeyamañjalikaraṇīyam |
body.translated_text: 'Worthy of invitation, worthy of homage, worthy of offerings, worthy of the <s>añjali</s> (gesture of reverence)': Because of being endowed with such qualities, [the <s>Saṅgha</s>] is worthy of invitation, worthy of homage, worthy of offerings, and worthy of the <s>añjali</s>.

body.text: anuttaraṃ
body.translated_text: 'The unsurpassed field of merit': By the merit planted therein, one obtains immeasurable ripening. That [merit]

body.text: puṇyakṣetramiti | tatra ropitena puṇyena apramāṇavipākaṃ pratilabhate | tat yāvannirvāṇañca na kṣīyate |
body.translated_text: is not exhausted until <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: dāyakānāṃ hitakaramiti | dāyakānāṃ guṇān vardhayati | yathā aṣṭāṅgasamanvitaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Beneficial to donors': It increases the virtues of donors. Just as a field endowed with eight factors

body.text: kṣetraṃ pañcavidhadhānyānyatiśayena saṃvardhayati na vināśaṃ gamayati | tathā saṅghakṣetramapi aṣṭāṅgasamanvitamityato dāyakānāṃ guṇān vardhayati | ato 'bhivandyam ||
body.translated_text: causes the five kinds of grain to grow abundantly and does not bring about their destruction — so too the field of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, being endowed with eight factors, increases the virtues of donors. Therefore it is worthy of veneration.

body.text: saṅgharatnādhikāre ādyaviśuddhivargo navamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the ninth chapter, the Chapter on Initial Purity in the Section on the Jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

body.text: 10 āryavibhāgavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 10. Chapter on the Classification of the <s>Āryas</s> (Noble Ones)

body.text: pṛ
body.translated_text: (Question) By what <s>dharma</s> is it designated as <s>Saṅgha</s>? (Answer) Because the four types of practice and the four types of practitioners are purified in qualities such as <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and the rest — therefore it is designated as <s>Saṅgha</s>.

body.text: kena dharmeṇa saṅgha ityākhyāyate | (u) caturvidhāḥ pratipattayañcaturvidhāḥ pratipannakāḥ śīlasamādhiprajñādiguṇāśca pariśuddhā ityataḥ saṅgha ityākhyāyate |

caturvidhāḥ pratipattayaḥsrotaāpatti sakṛdāgipratipattianāgāmipratipatti arhatpratipattayaḥ | caturvidhāḥ phalasthitāḥ srotaāpannasakṛdāgāmyanāgāmyarhantaḥ | srotaāpattipratipattau trayaḥ pudgalāḥ śraddhānusāripratipannako dharmānusāripratipannako 'nimittānusāripratipannaka iti | śraddhānusāripratipannaka iti | yo 'labdhānātmaśūnyatājñāno bhagavacchāsane śraddadhāno bhagavadvacanamanusṛtya pratipanno bhavati | sa śraddānusāripratipannaka ityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre ahamasmin vastuni śraddhayā pratipannaḥ | iti | labdhe tu tattvajñāne na śraddhāmātramanusṛtya pratipadyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- nāsti kārako nāsti śraddhālurityādi prajānan uttamapudgalo bhavati | iti | ato jñāyate alabdhatattvajñānaḥ śraddhānusāripratipannaka iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo dharme kṣāntisukhaṃ prajñayā bhāvayati sa śraddhāpratipannakaḥ [yaḥ] pṛthagjanabhūmimatikrāntaḥ srotaāpattiphalañca nālabhata | atrāntare jīvitāntaṃ nālabhata | sa śraddhāpratipannakaḥ | iti | ayaṃ śrutacintāmayaprajñāyāṃ sthito dharmaṇāṃ kṣāntikāmasukhacittaṃ samyak bhāvayan anātmaśūnyatājñānamalabhamāno 'pi laukikaṃ dharmakṣāntyābhāsacittamutpādayati | ayaṃ svayamāgata iti atikrāntapṛthagjanabhūmiritityucyate | kasmāditi paścādvakṣyate | yaḥ śraddhādi pañcendriyavirahitaḥ sa
body.translated_text: There are four types of practitioners: the practitioner of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattipratipatti</s>), the practitioner of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmipratipatti</s>), the practitioner of non-returning (<s>anāgāmipratipatti</s>), and the practitioner of <s>Arhat</s>-ship (<s>arhatpratipatti</s>). There are four types of fruit-abiders: the stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>), the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), and the <s>Arhat</s>. In the practice of stream-entry, there are three types of persons: the faith-follower practitioner (<s>śraddhānusāripratipannaka</s>), the <s>Dharma</s>-follower practitioner (<s>dharmānusāripratipannaka</s>), and the signless-follower practitioner (<s>animittānusāripratipannaka</s>). The faith-follower practitioner: one who has not yet obtained the knowledge of the emptiness of self (<s>anātmaśūnyatājñāna</s>), who has faith in the Blessed One's teaching and practices by following the Blessed One's words — he is called a faith-follower practitioner. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'I practice in this matter through faith.' But when the knowledge of reality is attained, one does not practice merely by following faith. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There is no doer, there is no one of faith' — one who knows such things becomes the highest type of person. From this it is known that the faith-follower practitioner is one who has not obtained the knowledge of reality. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who cultivates through wisdom the bliss of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) in the <s>dharmas</s> — he is a faith-practitioner. One who has transcended the stage of an ordinary being (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) but has not yet attained the fruit of stream-entry, and in the interval has not met the end of life — he is a faith-practitioner.' This one, established in the wisdom born of learning and reflection, while properly cultivating the mind of patience-bliss toward <s>dharmas</s>, even though not attaining the knowledge of the emptiness of self, produces a worldly mental state that resembles the appearance of patience toward <s>dharmas</s>. He is called 'one who has come by himself' — meaning one who has transcended the stage of the ordinary being. Why this is so will be explained later. One who is devoid of the five faculties beginning with faith

body.text: bāhyapṛthagjaneṣuvartate | sa krameṇa uṣmādidharmeṣu sthitau bhāvanāmayīṃ prajñāṃ labhamāno 'pi maulanāmnaiva śraddhānusārītyucyate | dharmapratipannakabhāvānugāmitvāt | asmāt sūtrāt vaktavyamavaśyaṃ srotaāpattiphalaṃ lapsyata iti | na vaktavyaṃ jīvitānte na lapsyata iti | kasmāt | śraddhāpratipannakasyāsya viprakṛṣṭatvāt | yathogreṇa saṅghe nimantrite devatā upasaṃgamyārocayanti- amuko 'rhan amuko 'rhatpratipannako yāvadamukaḥ śrotaāpannaḥ amukaḥ srotaāpattipratipannaka iti | yadyayaṃ pañcadaśacittakṣaṇavartī nārocanaṃ labdhuṃ śakyate | iti jñātavyaṃ srotaāpattipratipannakaḥ sannikṛṣṭo viprakṛṣṭaśca | ayaṃ śraddhāpratipannaka ityucyate |
body.translated_text: remains among the external ordinary beings. He, gradually becoming established in the <s>dharmas</s> beginning with the warmth (<s>uṣman</s>), even while obtaining the wisdom born of meditation, is still called by the original name 'faith-follower' — because he follows the path of the <s>Dharma</s>-practitioner. From this <s>sūtra</s> it must be said that he will certainly attain the fruit of stream-entry. It cannot be said that he will not attain it at the end of his life. Why? Because this faith-practitioner may be at a distant [stage]. For example, when <s>Ugra</s> invited the <s>Saṅgha</s>, deities approached and announced: 'Such-and-such is an <s>Arhat</s>, such-and-such is an <s>Arhat</s>-practitioner, down to such-and-such is a stream-enterer, such-and-such is a stream-entry practitioner.' If this [practitioner] were only in the fifteen mind-moments, the announcement could not be obtained. Thus it should be known that the stream-entry practitioner may be either near or far. This one is called the faith-practitioner.

body.text: dharmānusāripratipannaka iti | ayaṃ labdhānātmajñāna ūṣmamūrdhakṣāntyagradharmeṣusthito dharmamanusṛtya pratipadyate yadanātmaśūnyādi | ayaṃ dharmapratipannaka ityucyate | imau dvau pratipannakau satyadarśanamārgamavatārya nirodhasatyaṃ paśyata ityato 'nimittapratipannaka ityucyate | ime trayaḥ pudgalāḥ srotaāpattipratipannakā bhavanti | laukikamārge saṃyojanaprahāṇāt phalatrayapratipanna iti na prathāṃ labhante | idaṃ paścādvakṣyate |
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s>-follower practitioner: this one, having obtained the knowledge of selflessness (<s>anātmajñāna</s>), established in the <s>dharmas</s> of warmth (<s>uṣman</s>), summit (<s>mūrdhan</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), and supreme <s>dharmas</s> (<s>agradharma</s>), practices by following the <s>Dharma</s> — namely the emptiness of self and so forth. He is called a <s>Dharma</s>-practitioner. These two practitioners, having entered the path of truth-seeing (<s>satyadarśana</s>), see the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) — therefore they are called signless practitioners (<s>animittapratipannaka</s>). These three persons are stream-entry practitioners. Because the fetters are abandoned on the mundane path, they do not become renowned as practitioners of the three [higher] fruits. This will be explained later.

body.text: srotaāpanna iti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā sūtram- satkāyadṛṣṭidṛṣṭivicikitsāśīlavrataparāmarśānāṃ trayāṇāṃ sayojānanāṃ parikṣayāt srotaāpanno bhavati avinipātadharmā niyataḥ sambodhiparāyaṇaḥ saptakṛtbhavaparama iti | (pṛ) yaḥ srotaāpannaḥ sa satyadarśanaprahīṇakleśo 'tyantaparikṣīṇāpramāṇaduḥkhaḥ pṛthivīsama iti aupamyasūtramāha | kasmāducyate kevalaṃ trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ parikṣayāditi | (u) idamuttaratra vakṣyate yaduta satyadṛṣṭikṣayādanye kṣīṇā iti | avinipātadharmeti | idamapi paścādvakṣyate karmaskandhe | niyataḥ sambodhiparāyaṇa iti | dharmasrotasyavataran niyataṃ nirvāṇamanuprāpnoti | yathā gaṅghaughavartī dāruskandho vināṣṭapratyayān
body.translated_text: The stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>): as the Blessed One stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Through the complete destruction of the three fetters — the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and clinging to rites and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) — one becomes a stream-enterer, one of the nature of not falling into a lower realm, certain, destined for awakening, with at most seven more births.' (Objection:) The stream-enterer, through the destruction of the defilements abandoned by truth-seeing, has completely destroyed immeasurable suffering and is like the earth — so says the <s>sūtra</s> of comparisons (<s>aupamyasūtra</s>). Why then is it said 'merely through the destruction of the three fetters'? (Reply:) This will be stated later — namely, that through the destruction of the view of truth, the others are [also] destroyed. 'Of the nature of not falling [into a lower realm]' — this too will be explained later in the section on <s>karma</s>. 'Certain, destined for awakening' — having entered the stream of <s>Dharma</s>, one certainly attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Just as a log of wood in the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, barring obstructing conditions

body.text: niyataṃ mahāsamudramanuprāpnoti | saptakṛdbhavaparama iti | sa saptasu adhvasvanāsravajñānaṃ paripācayati | yathā [garbhaḥ] kalalādinā saptasu dineṣu pariṇamati | yathā ca navanītādi saptadinaparamaṃ sevamānasya dhruvā glānirapi jarjaritā bhavati | yathā ca jñātisambandhaḥ saptasantānān yāti | yathā ca saptaphaṇasarpadaṣṭaḥ pudgalakāyaścaturbhūtabalāt saptapadāni gacchati nāṣṭamaṃ viṣabalādgacchati | yathā ca śāṭhyadharmaḥ saptādhvaparamo yāti | yathā vā saptadinepvatīteṣu kalpāgniḥ śāmyati | evaṃ saptajanmasu sañcitānāsravaprajñāgninā kleśāḥ kṣīyante | dharmasya saptabhavāḥ syuḥ | srotaāpanno 'sminnadhvani nirvāṇe 'vatarati | dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ saptaparamaṃ vā yāti | ayaṃ srotaāpanna ityucyate |
body.translated_text: certainly reaches the great ocean. 'With at most seven more births' — he ripens the undefiled knowledge (<s>anāsravajñāna</s>) in seven existences. Just as an embryo develops through the stages beginning with <s>kalala</s> in seven days. And just as one who consumes butter and similar foods for a maximum of seven days — even a chronic illness becomes weakened. And just as kinship relations extend through seven generations. And just as a person bitten by a seven-hooded serpent walks seven steps by the power of the four elements but does not walk an eighth, due to the power of the poison. And just as the quality of deceitfulness extends through at most seven existences. And just as the fire at the end of the aeon subsides after seven days. So too, the defilements are destroyed by the fire of the undefiled wisdom accumulated over seven births. The <s>Dharma</s> [practitioner] may have seven existences. The stream-enterer enters <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in this existence, or goes to the second, third, or at most the seventh. This one is called the stream-enterer.

body.text: sakṛdāgāmipratipannaka iti | bhāvanāheyasaṃyojanasya navaskandhā bhavanti | ya ekaṃ dvau vā prahāya trīn caturaḥ pañca vā yāti | sa sakṛdāgā mipratipannakaḥ |
body.translated_text: The once-returner practitioner (<s>sakṛdāgāmipratipannaka</s>): the fetters to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>) have nine degrees. One who has abandoned one or two [degrees] and goes through three, four, or five — he is a once-returner practitioner.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- ekenānāvaraṇamārgeṇa prajahāti iti | tadayuktam | bhagavatoktam apramāṇacittaiḥ prajahāti | yathā vāśījaṭā iti aupamyasūtra uktam | sakṛdāgāmipratipannakaḥ kulaṃkula ityapi ākhyāyate | sa dve vā trīṇi vā kulāni sandhāvati saṃsarati | dṛṣṭa eva vā kāye nirvāṇe 'vatarati | ayaṃ sakṛdāgāmipratipannakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'He abandons [them] by a single unobstructed path.' That is incorrect. The Blessed One said: 'He abandons them by means of immeasurable mental states.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s> of comparisons: 'Just as the knots of a bamboo [are cut one by one].' The once-returner practitioner is also called <s>Kulaṃkula</s> (family-to-family). He wanders and transmigrates through two or three families, or enters <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in this very body. This is the once-returner practitioner.

body.text: sakṛdāgāmī imaṃ lokaṃ sakṛdāgatya duḥkhasyāntaṃ karoti | sa bhāvanāparikṣīṇatanusaṃyojanaḥ |
body.translated_text: The once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>): having returned to this world once more, he makes an end of suffering. His fetters have been thinned through cultivation.

body.text: saṃyojanānāṃ tanutve sthitaḥ sakṛdāgāmītyucyate | ayaṃ sakṛdāgāmī ihaiva vā janmani duḥkhasyāntaṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: Established in the thinning of the fetters, he is called the once-returner. This once-returner makes an end of suffering in this very birth or [the next].

body.text: anāgāmipratipannaka iti | yaḥ parikṣīṇasaptamāṣṭamasaṃyojanaskandhaḥ so 'nāgāmipratipannakaḥ | parikṣīṇāṣṭamasaṃyojano 'yamekabījī anāgāmipratipannakaḥ | sa ihaiva vā janmani duḥkhasyāntaṃ karoti | atyantaparikṣīṇakāmāvacaranava saṃyojanaskandho 'nāgāmī | anāgāmino 'ṣṭaprabhedāḥ- yaduta antarā parinirvāyī, upapadyaparinirvāyī, anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī, sābhīsaṃskāraparinirvāyī, ūrdhvasrotaḥ akaniṣṭhagāmī, ārūpyāyatanagāmī, parāvṛttajanmā, dṛṣṭadharmanirvāyī iti | uttamamadhyādhamendriyatvāt prabhedāḥ |
body.translated_text: The non-returner practitioner (<s>anāgāmipratipannaka</s>): one whose seventh and eighth degrees of fetter-aggregates have been completely destroyed is a non-returner practitioner. One whose eighth [degree of] fetter is completely destroyed is called <s>Ekabījin</s> (one-seeder), a non-returner practitioner. He makes an end of suffering in this very birth. One whose nine degrees of fetters belonging to the desire-realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) have been completely destroyed is a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>). The non-returner has eight subdivisions: one who attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>), one who attains it upon rebirth (<s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>), one who attains it without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>), one who attains it with effort (<s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>), one who goes upstream to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (<s>ūrdhvasrotas akaniṣṭhagāmin</s>), one who goes to the formless realm (<s>ārūpyāyatanagāmin</s>), one who reverses birth (<s>parāvṛttajanman</s>), and one who attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmaparinirvāyin</s>). The subdivisions arise from the distinction of superior, middling, and inferior faculties.

body.text: antarāparinirvāyyapi uttamamadhyādhamendriyatvena tridhābhidyate | kaścidanāgāmī bhavānnirvidyate, alpanīvaraṇo na dṛṣṭe nirvāṇamanuprāpnoti | so 'ntarāparinirvāti |
body.translated_text: The one who attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state is also threefold, according to superior, middling, and inferior faculties. A certain non-returner, becoming disenchanted with existence and having few hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), does not attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the present life. He attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state.

body.text: upapadyaparinirvāyī tridhā bhidyate upapadyanirvāyī, sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī, anabhisaṃskaraparinirvāyīti | upapadyaparinirvāyīti | ya utpadyamāna eva bhavānnirvidya parinirvāti | sa upapadyaparinirvāyī | indriyataikṣṇyāt | kaścidutpannaḥ san anāsravamārgeṣu prakṛtyā sthito 'bhisaṃskāramaprayujya parinirvāti | so 'nabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī | madhyamendriyatvāt | kaścidutpannaḥ san kāyopādāne 'tibhīrurabhisaṃskāramārgaṃ prayujya parinirvāti | sa sābhisaṃskāra parinirvāyī | indriyamāndyāt |
body.translated_text: The one who attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth is threefold: one who attains it upon rebirth, one who attains it with effort, and one who attains it without effort. The one who attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth: one who, at the very moment of being reborn, becomes disenchanted with existence and attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> — he is one who attains it upon rebirth, because of the sharpness of his faculties. A certain one, having been reborn, naturally established in the undefiled paths, attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> without applying effort — he is one who attains it without effort, because of middling faculties. A certain one, having been reborn, greatly fearful of the appropriation of a body, attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> by applying the path of effort — he is one who attains it with effort, because of the dullness of his faculties.

body.text: ūrdhvastrotā [akaniṣṭhagā]myapi trividhaḥ | ya ekasmādāyatanāt cyuto 'parasminnāyatana utpadya parinirvāti | sa tīkṣṇendriyaḥ | yo dvayostriṣu vāyataneṣu utpadya [parinirvāti] sa madhyamendriyaḥ | yaḥ sarvasmādāyatanāccyutaḥ sarvāyataneṣūtpadya parinirvāti | sa mṛdvindriyaḥ | prathamadhyānāt [yo] bṛhatphaladevagāmī sa nistīrṇo nāma | prāptabṛhatphalo yadi śuddhāvāsa utpadyate | sa na punarārūpyāyatanaṃ gacchati | prajñādhimuktatvāt [ārūpyago] ya ārūpyāyatanaṃ gacchati | sa naiva śuddhāvāsa utpadyate | samādhyadhimuktatvāt |
body.translated_text: The one who goes upstream to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> is also threefold. One who, having died in one realm, is reborn in another realm and attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> — he has sharp faculties. One who is reborn in two or three realms and attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> — he has middling faculties. One who, having died in every realm, is reborn in all realms and attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> — he has dull faculties. From the first <s>dhyāna</s>, one who goes to the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods is called 'one who has crossed over.' If, having reached <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, he is reborn in the Pure Abodes (<s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>), he does not further go to the formless realm — because of his inclination toward wisdom. One who goes to the formless realm does not arise in the Pure Abodes — because of his inclination toward <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: parāvṛttajanmeti | yaḥ pūrvabhave srotaāpattiphalasakṛdāgāmiphalaprāptaḥ paścātpravṛttakāyena anāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti | sa na rūpārūpyadhātāvavatarati |
body.translated_text: 'One who reverses birth' (<s>parāvṛttajanman</s>): one who in a previous existence attained the fruit of stream-entry or once-returning, and then with a subsequently arisen body attains the fruit of non-returning — he does not descend into the form or formless realms.

body.text: dṛṣṭadharmaparinirvāyī ti paramatīkṣṇendriyo dṛṣṭa eva kāye nirvāṇaṃ prāpnoti |
body.translated_text: 'One who attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the present life' (<s>dṛṣṭadharmaparinirvāyin</s>): one with supremely sharp faculties attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in this very body.

body.text: atha pudgalo dvividhaḥ śraddhāvimukto dṛṣṭiprāpta iti | indriyabhedāt pudgaladvaividhyam | mṛdvindriyaḥ śaikṣo bhāvanāmārge sthitaḥ śraddhāvimuktaḥ | tīkṣṇastu dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person is twofold: 'liberated through faith' (<s>śraddhāvimukta</s>) and 'attainer of views' (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>). The twofold division of persons is due to the distinction of faculties. One of dull faculties who is a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), established on the path of cultivation, is liberated through faith. One of sharp faculties is an attainer of views.

body.text: yo 'nāgāmi avikalāṣṭavimokṣaḥ sa kāyasākṣī | ime sarve arhatphalapratipannakāḥ saṃyojanaprahāṇasāmyāt |
body.translated_text: A non-returner who possesses the complete eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>) is a body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>). All of these are practitioners of the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>-ship, because of the equal abandonment of fetters.

body.text: yaḥ parikṣīṇasarvakleśaḥ so 'rhana | navavidho 'rhana- parihāṇalakṣaṇaḥ, anurakṣaṇalakṣaṇaḥ mṛtalakṣaṇaḥ, sthitalakṣaṇaḥ, prativedhanalakṣaṇaḥ, akopyalakṣaṇaḥ, prajñāvimuktalakṣaṇaḥ, ubhayatobhāgavimuktalakṣaṇaḥ, aparihāṇalakṣaṇa iti | śraddhendriyādiprāptyā arhantaḥ prabhinnāḥ |
body.translated_text: One whose defilements are completely destroyed is an <s>Arhat</s>. The <s>Arhat</s> is of nine kinds: the one characterized by decline (<s>parihāṇalakṣaṇa</s>), the one characterized by guarding (<s>anurakṣaṇalakṣaṇa</s>), the one characterized by death (<s>mṛtalakṣaṇa</s>), the one characterized by stability (<s>sthitalakṣaṇa</s>), the one characterized by penetration (<s>prativedhanalakṣaṇa</s>), the one characterized by unshakeability (<s>akopyalakṣaṇa</s>), the one characterized by liberation through wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>), the one characterized by liberation in both ways (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>), and the one characterized by non-decline (<s>aparihāṇalakṣaṇa</s>). The <s>Arhats</s> are differentiated by their attainment of faculties beginning with the faith-faculty.

body.text: paramamṛdvindriyaḥ parihāṇalakṣaṇaḥ, samādheḥ parihāṇaduṣṭaḥ | samādhiparihāṇyā anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ nābhimukhībhavati | anurakṣaṇalakṣaṇa iti kiñcidviśiṣṭendriyatvāt yaḥ samādhimanurakṣati sa na parihīyate | arakṣaṃstu parihīyate | pūrvaparihāṇalakṣaṇastu [samādhiṃ] rakṣannapi tataḥ parihīyate || mṛtalakṣaṇaḥ tato 'pi kiñcidviśiṣṭendriyo bhaveṣu paramaṃ nirviṇṇaḥ | sa na samādhiṃ labdhavānityato 'nāsravajñānasyābhimukhībhāvo durlabhaḥ | labdhvāpi prītirvinaśyati | ato maraṇārthī bhavati || sthitalakṣaṇa iti yaḥ samādhiṃ labdhvā na parākramate na ca parihīyate sa sthitalakṣaṇaḥ | purve trayaḥ samādhiparihāṇabhāge vartante | sthitalakṣaṇastu samādhisthitibhāge vartate || prativedhalakṣaṇa iti | yaḥ samādhiṃ labdhvā bhūyo 'dhikamabhivardhayati | sa samādhyabhivardhanabhāge vartate || akopyalakṣaṇa iti | yaḥ samādhiṃ labdhvā nānāpratyayairna vikṣepayati | sa samādhiprativedhabhāge vartate | paramatīkṣṇaprajñatvāt | samādhisamāpattisthitivyutthānalakṣaṇānāṃ sugṛhītatvādakopyo bhavati | nirodhasamāpattimupādāya dvividhaḥ pudgalaḥ- tatsamādhyalābhī prajñāvimuktaḥ, tatsamādhilābhī tu ubhayatobhāgavimukta iti || aparihāṇalakṣaṇa iti | yaḥ kṛtāt kṣayaguṇādaparihīṇaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhagavānāha- yo bhikṣavo macchrāvakaḥ śayane paryaṅke vā ahamahamikayā pratilabdhāt [āsrava]kṣayānna parihīyate | iti | evaṃ navavidhā aśaikṣāḥ | pūrvoktā aṣṭādaśa śaikṣā navāśaikṣāśca [militvā] saptaviṃśati [pudgalāḥ] laukikaṃ sarvapuṇyakṣetram | te saṅghe samanvitāḥ | ato 'bhivandyaṃ [saṅgharatnam] ||
body.translated_text: One with supremely soft faculties has the characteristic of decline (<s>parihāṇa</s>), being corrupted by decline from <s>samādhi</s>. Through decline from <s>samādhi</s>, undefiled knowledge does not come to the fore. The one with the characteristic of guarding (<s>anurakṣaṇa</s>), having somewhat superior faculties, guards his <s>samādhi</s> and does not decline; but without guarding, he declines. The one with the former characteristic of decline, even while guarding his <s>samādhi</s>, declines from it. The one with the characteristic of death-seeking (<s>mṛta</s>), having yet somewhat superior faculties, is supremely disgusted with existences. He has not attained <s>samādhi</s>, and therefore the coming-to-the-fore of undefiled knowledge is difficult to obtain; even having attained it, his delight perishes — therefore he becomes desirous of death. The one with the characteristic of stability (<s>sthita</s>), having attained <s>samādhi</s>, neither advances further nor declines — he has the characteristic of stability. The former three abide in the portion of decline from <s>samādhi</s>, while the one with the characteristic of stability abides in the portion of stability of <s>samādhi</s>. The one with the characteristic of penetration (<s>prativedha</s>), having attained <s>samādhi</s>, further increases and develops it. He abides in the portion of growth of <s>samādhi</s>. The one with the characteristic of unshakeability (<s>akopya</s>), having attained <s>samādhi</s>, is not distracted by various conditions. He abides in the portion of penetration of <s>samādhi</s>, because of having supremely sharp wisdom. Because the characteristics of attainment, abiding, and emergence from <s>samādhi</s> are well grasped, he is unshakeable. With reference to the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), there are two types of persons: one who has not attained that <s>samādhi</s> is liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>), while one who has attained that <s>samādhi</s> is liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>). The one with the characteristic of non-decline (<s>aparihāṇa</s>) has not declined from the attained quality of destruction. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Blessed One said: O monks, that disciple of mine who, whether on a bed or couch, through self-assertion, does not decline from the attained destruction of defilements.' Thus there are nine types of non-learners (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). The eighteen learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) mentioned earlier and the nine non-learners, combined, make twenty-seven persons who constitute the worldly field of merit. They are comprised in the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Therefore the Jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s> is worthy of veneration.

body.text: āryavibhāgavargo nāma daśamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the tenth chapter, named the Chapter on the Classification of Noble Ones (<s>āryavibhāgavarga</s>).

body.text: 11 puṇyakṣetravargaḥ
body.translated_text: 11. Chapter on the Field of Merit (<s>puṇyakṣetravarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) kasmādāryāste puṇyakṣetramityucyante | (u) lobhakrodhādīnāṃ kleśānāṃ parikṣīṇatvāt puṇyakṣetramityucyate | yathā tṛṇānāhataḥ subijāṅkura ityucyate | ato vītarāgāṇāṃ dānaṃ mahāhitavipākaprāpakam | śūnyatācittā ityataśca puṇyakṣetramityucyante | kasmāt | śūnyalakṣaṇatvāt sarve rāgadveṣādayaḥ kleśā anutpannā nākuśalaṃ karmotpādayanti | āryā akṛtakadharmalābhina iti puṇyakṣetraṃ bhavanti | tairlabdhvā dhyānasamādhayaḥ sarve pariśuddhāḥ mahālpaiḥ kleśairviśaṃyuktatvāt | saumanasyadaurmanasyayornirākṛtattvācca puṇyakṣetram | pañca
body.translated_text: (Question) Why are the Noble Ones called a 'field of merit' (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>)? (Answer) Because defilements such as greed, anger, and others have been completely exhausted, they are called a field of merit — just as a field unobstructed by weeds is said to produce good sprouts. Therefore, giving to those free from passion yields results of great benefit. They are also called a field of merit because their minds abide in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). Why? Because, having the characteristic of emptiness, all defilements such as passion and hatred are unborn and do not produce unwholesome karma. The Noble Ones, having attained qualities without artifice, become a field of merit. Having attained the <s>dhyānas</s> and <s>samādhis</s>, all are purified, being disjoined from even the subtlest defilements. And because elation and dejection have been eliminated, they are a field of merit. Having abandoned the five —

body.text: cetokhilāni prahāya pratilabdhaviśuddhacittatvācca puṇyakṣetram | aṣṭakṣetraguṇasamanvitvāt saptavidha samādhipariṣkāraiḥ surakṣitatvāt saptāsrava sannirodhitvāt āsravairaduṣṭam | śīlādisaptapariśuddhadharmasampannatvāt alpecchāsantuṣṭyādyaṣṭaguṇasamanvitatvāt | tat pāraṃ santīrya ākāṃkṣāvitaraṇavyavasāyitvācca puṇyakṣetram | uktaṃ ca sūtre prasthānacitamātra eva kuśaladharmamācaritumabhilaṣati | kiṃ punarbahvarthaṃ prayogam | iti | te āryāḥ sadā kuśaladharmānācarantītyataḥ puṇyakṣetram | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre yasmāddāyakād gṛhapateḥ śīlavato bhikṣuḥ satkāramādāya apramāṇasamādhimupasampadya viharati | sa dāyakto gṛhapatirapramāṇaṃ puṇyaṃ labhata iti | saṅghe santi kecidapramāṇasamādhisamāpannāḥ, kecidanimittasamādhisamāpannāḥ, kecidacalasamādhisamāpannāḥ | tena dānapatirapramāṇavipākaṃ labhate ato 'pi puṇyakṣetram | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- trayāṇāṃ sannipātānmahataḥ puṇyasya pratilābhaḥ | śraddhā deyaṃ puṇyakṣetramiti | santi ca saṅghe bahavo bhadantāḥ | bhadanteṣu śraddhācittaṃ bāḍhamutpadyate | saṅghasya dānaṃ navapratyayasaṃyuktamityato mahāphalaprāpakam | saṅghadānasya pratigrahītā pariśuddha ityatastaddānamapi avaśyaṃ pariśuddham |
body.translated_text: — mental barrennesses (<s>cetokhila</s>) and having attained purified consciousness, they are a field of merit. Being endowed with the eight field-qualities, being well guarded by the seven kinds of <s>samādhi</s>-purification, and having suppressed the seven outflows (<s>āsrava</s>), they are uncorrupted by outflows. Being endowed with the seven purified qualities beginning with moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and being endowed with the eight qualities beginning with few desires and contentment — having crossed to the far shore, because of their resolve to cross over aspirations and deliberations, they are a field of merit. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'From the very moment of setting forth, one aspires to practice wholesome qualities — how much more so with great effort applied toward many goals.' The Noble Ones always practice wholesome qualities, and therefore they are a field of merit. Furthermore, as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'When a monk of moral conduct, having received an offering from a donor-householder, enters into and abides in the immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>, that donor-householder obtains immeasurable merit.' In the <s>Saṅgha</s>, some have attained the immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>, some have attained the signless <s>samādhi</s>, and some have attained the unshakeable <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore the donor obtains results of immeasurable extent — hence it is a field of merit. Furthermore, as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'From the conjunction of three factors, great merit is obtained: faith, the gift, and the field of merit.' In the <s>Saṅgha</s> there are many venerable ones. Toward venerable ones, a mind of faith powerfully arises. Giving to the <s>Saṅgha</s> is connected with nine conditions, and therefore yields great results. The recipient of a gift to the <s>Saṅgha</s> is pure, and therefore that gift is also necessarily pure.

body.text: dānañcāṣṭavidham | (1) pariśuddhacitto 'lpaṃ deyavastu bhinnaśīlasyālpaśo dadāti | (2) pariśuddhacitto 'lpaṃ deyaṃ bhinnaśīlasya bahuśo dadāti | (3) pariśuddhacitto deyamalpaṃ dhṛtaśīlasyālpaśo dadāti | (4) pariśuddhacitto 'lpaṃ deyaṃ dhṛtaśīlasya bahuśo dadāti | (5) pariśuddhacitto bahuśo ['lpaśo vā] dadāti tathā deyaṃ caturvidham | saṅghasya dānamavaśyaṃ dve trīṇi vā prasādhayet | sarve sujanāḥ saṅghamupādāya
body.translated_text: Giving is of eight kinds: (1) one of pure mind gives a small gift-object to one of broken morality on few occasions; (2) one of pure mind gives a small gift to one of broken morality on many occasions; (3) one of pure mind gives a small gift to one of maintained morality on few occasions; (4) one of pure mind gives a small gift to one of maintained morality on many occasions; (5) one of pure mind gives on many occasions [or few occasions] — thus the gift is fourfold.
