A gift to the <s>Saṅgha</s> necessarily accomplishes two or three [of these conditions]. All good people, relying on the <s>Saṅgha</s> —

body.text: guṇān vardhante | yatheṣṭaṃ bodhaye pariṇamanti | saṅghasya dīyamānaṃ sarvaṃ vimuktiṃ prāpayiṣyati | naiva ca saṃsāre pātayati | saṅghasya dīyamānaṃ sarvaṃ cittaprasādhanāya bhavati | yadyekasmin puruṣe utpannā śraddhā cittaṃ kadācit pariśodhayet kadācidvā prakampeta | saṅghe tu [samutpannā] śraddhā cittaṃ pariśodhayedeva | na punaḥ prakampeta | kasmiṃścidutpannaḥ snehaḥ cittaṃ na gurukuryāt na pracīyeta | saṅghe tūtpannā bhaktiḥ cittaṃ gurukuryāt apramāṇālambanatvāt cittaṃ pracīyeta | saṅghagaṇitānāṃ sarveṣāṃ pudgalānāṃ dadyāt | cittamahimnā vipāko 'pi mahān bhavati | ityādibhiḥ pratyayaiḥ āryapudgalāḥ puṇyakṣetramityākhyāyante | ato 'bhivandyam ||
body.translated_text: — increase their virtues. They may dedicate them to enlightenment as they wish. What is given to the <s>Saṅgha</s> will bring everything to liberation. It does not at all cause one to fall into <s>saṃsāra</s>. What is given to the <s>Saṅgha</s> all serves to purify the mind. If faith arises toward one individual person, the mind may sometimes be purified and sometimes waver. But faith arisen toward the <s>Saṅgha</s> will surely purify the mind and will not waver again. Affection arisen toward some individual may not make the mind weighty nor cause it to grow. But devotion arisen toward the <s>Saṅgha</s> makes the mind weighty, and because the object is immeasurable, the mind grows. If one gives to all the individual persons counted within the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the ripened result is also great due to the greatness of the mind. By these and other conditions, noble persons are declared to be a field of merit. Therefore it is worthy of veneration.

body.text: puṇyakṣetravargaḥ ekādaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the eleventh chapter, the Chapter on the Field of Merit (<s>puṇyakṣetravarga</s>).

body.text: 12 maṅgalavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 12. Chapter on Auspiciousness (<s>maṅgalavarga</s>)

body.text: ratnatrayamidaṃ guṇasampannamityataḥ sūtrasyādāvuktam, idaṃ ratnatrayaṃ sarvasya lokasya prathamaṃ maṅgalam | yathoktaṃ maṅgalagāthāyām- buddho dharmaśca saṅgaśca etanmaṅgalamuttamam iti | atha kānicitsūtrāṇi maṅgalādīni śaikṣāṇāmāyuryaśaḥprasaravardhanāni iti sūtrakartāro 'bhiprayanti | yathā athetyādipadaṃ sūtrārambhagatamiti | na tanmaṅgalalakṣaṇamiti paścādvakṣyate | uttamamaṅgalaprārthinā idaṃ ratnatrayameva śaraṇīkartavyam | yathoktaṃ maṅgalagāthāyām-
body.translated_text: Because this <s>Ratnatraya</s> (Three Jewels) is endowed with qualities, it was stated at the beginning of the treatise that this <s>Ratnatraya</s> is the foremost auspiciousness (<s>maṅgala</s>) of the entire world. As declared in the Verse on Auspiciousness: '<s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> — this is the supreme auspiciousness.' Now, certain <s>sūtras</s> beginning with auspiciousness increase the lifespan and fame of learners — so the authors of <s>sūtras</s> intend. Just as the word 'atha' and similar words are placed at the commencement of <s>sūtras</s> — that is not the mark of auspiciousness, as will be explained later. One who desires the supreme auspiciousness should take refuge in this <s>Ratnatraya</s> alone. As declared in the Verse on Auspiciousness:

children.translated_text: Among gods and humans, the Teacher, the unsurpassed Guide,
the greatly wise, the Fully Awakened One — this is the supreme auspiciousness.
One whose mind of faith is well established in the <s>Buddha</s> and does not waver,
endowed with pure moral conduct — this is the supreme auspiciousness.

body.text:
asevanā ca bālānāṃ paṇḍitānāñca sevanā |
pūjā ca pūjanīyānāmetanmaṅgalamuttamam ||iti |
body.translated_text:
Not associating with fools, associating with the wise,
worshipping those worthy of worship — this is the supreme auspiciousness.

body.text: ato 'bhivandyaṃ ratnatrayam | uttamamaṅgalatvānmayā sūtrādāvuktam ||
body.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Ratnatraya</s> is worthy of veneration. Because it is the supreme auspiciousness, it was stated by me at the beginning of the treatise.

body.text: maṅgalavargo dvādaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twelfth chapter, the Chapter on Auspiciousness (<s>maṅgalavarga</s>).

body.text: 13 śāstrasthāpanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 13. Chapter on Establishing the Teaching (<s>śāstrasthāpanavarga</s>)

body.text: adhunā lokānāṃ hitakaro jinadharmo jijñāsyate | bhagavato mahākaruṇācittena sarvalokānāṃ hitakaratvāt taddharmo 'pāryantikabādha ityucyate | tadyathā kecit brāhmaṇānāmeva mokṣaśāstramupadiśanti | bhagavadupadiṣṭaṃ śāstrantu cāturvargīyāṇāṃ sattvānāmātiryagjantūnāñca santārakaṃ bhavati iti nāsti pāryantikabādhā |
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), which is beneficial to the world, is to be investigated. Because the Blessed One, with his mind of great compassion, is beneficial to all worlds, his <s>Dharma</s> is said to be without any limiting obstruction. For example, some teach the <s>śāstra</s> of liberation only for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. But the <s>śāstra</s> taught by the Blessed One is able to ferry across beings of all four castes and even animals — thus there is no limiting obstruction.

body.text: (pṛ) na kartavyo buddhapravacanavicāraḥ | kasmāt | yadi bhagavatā svayameva vicāritam | kimasti vicārāya | yadi bhagavatā na vicāritam | anye 'pi na vicārayituṃ śaknuyuḥ | kasmāt | sarvajñābhiprāyo hi duravagāhaḥ | kimarthamidamuktamiti na jñāyate | bhagavadabhisandhimajānatāmupadiṣṭaṃ vṛtheti tat ātmanaḥ kleśāyaiva bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dvau puruṣau bhagavantaṃ nindataḥ eko 'śraddhādveṣābhyāṃ nindati, aparastadupadiṣṭe saśraddho 'pi satyasamādānāsamarthaḥ | saiva buddhanindā | vidvānapi buddhābhisandhimanavabudhya buddhabhāṣitaṃ na vicārayituṃ śaknoti | kiṃ punastadalābhī buddhābhisandheḥ kathāsamprayogaṃ cikīrṣati | kasmāt | yathā parapravādasūtre bhagavatā pratipattyarthamidamuktam | sarve bhikṣavo nānāvidhāḥ parapravādino nālabhanta tathāgatāśayam | yathā ca sthaviramahākātyāyano bhikṣūnavocat | yathā ca kaścit mahāntaṃ vṛkṣaṃ chitvā atikramyaiva mūlamatikramyaiva skandhaṃ śākhāpalāśāni paryeṣayanti | tathā yūyamapi tathāgatamatikramyasmānartha pṛcchatha, iti | yadi mahākātyāyana evārthavivecane śākhāpalāśānyudāharati | kiṃ punaranye buddhapravacanaṃ pratipadyeran | kiñca bhagavān śariputramapṛcchat ke śaikṣāḥ ke ca sāṅkhyā iti | evaṃ triḥ pṛṣṭo nottaramavādīt | tathāgatamūlāḥ sarvadharmāḥ | tathāgata eva pratipadyate nānye | iti ānanda stathāgatamāmantyāha- abhisambodhisamadhigamāt pratilabdhe mārge hitaṃ bhavatītyatadapi yujyate | kasmāt | dvābhyāṃ pratyayābhyāṃ samyak dṛṣṭirbhavati parato ghoṣāt yoniśaśca
body.translated_text: (Objection) Investigation of the <s>Buddha</s>'s word should not be undertaken. Why? If it was already investigated by the Blessed One himself, what need is there for investigation? If it was not investigated by the Blessed One, then others too would be unable to investigate it. Why? Because the intent of the Omniscient One is unfathomable. Why this was said cannot be known. For those who do not understand the Blessed One's intent, what is taught is futile, and that only serves to increase one's own defilements. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Two persons disparage the Blessed One — one disparages through faithlessness and hatred, the other, though faithful in what was taught, is unable to put the truth into practice. That itself is disparagement of the <s>Buddha</s>.' Even a learned person, not understanding the <s>Buddha</s>'s intent, cannot properly investigate the <s>Buddha</s>'s word. How much less one who has not attained it, yet wishes to engage in discussion of the <s>Buddha</s>'s intent? Why? As in the <s>Parapravādasūtra</s>, the Blessed One spoke for the purpose of practice: 'O monks, the various disputants of other schools cannot attain the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s intent.' And as the Elder <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> said to the monks: 'Just as someone, having felled a great tree, passing beyond the root and passing beyond the trunk, searches among the branches and leaves — so too you, passing beyond the <s>Tathāgata</s>, ask us for the meaning.' If even <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, in distinguishing the meaning, cites branches and leaves as an illustration, how much less could others comprehend the <s>Buddha</s>'s word? Furthermore, the Blessed One asked <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Who are the learners and who are the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>?' Though asked three times, he gave no answer. 'All <s>dharmas</s> are rooted in the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Only the <s>Tathāgata</s> comprehends them, not others.' Thus <s>Ānanda</s>, addressing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, said: 'From the attainment of full awakening, the benefit of the path is complete' — this too is fitting. Why? Right view arises from two conditions: hearing from others (<s>parato ghoṣa</s>) and wise attention (<s>yoniśas</s>) —

body.text: manaskārāt | bhagavānānandamavocat- abhisambodhimātrānmārgalābhahitaṃ sampannaṃ bhavati | iti | yathā cāha bhagavān- yadi mayā kasyacit dharma upadiṣṭaḥ so 'pratilabdhamadabhisandhitvāt kalahāyate | iti |
body.translated_text: — attention. The Blessed One said to <s>Ānanda</s>: 'From the mere attainment of full awakening, the benefit of gaining the path is accomplished.' And as the Blessed One declared: 'If I have taught a <s>dharma</s> to someone, he who has not attained my intent quarrels about it.'

body.text: adhunā vādinaḥ pṛthak pṛthagabhiniviṣṭāḥ | kecidvadanti santi atītānāgatadharmā iti | kecidvadanti na santi iti | ato jñātavyameva vādinaḥ tathāgatamapratipadyamānā yathārutamanuvartamānāḥ kalahāyanta iti | yathā ānandaḥ samādhyarthaṃ sarvāṇyupādānāni duḥkhamityavocat | tadā bhagavān bhikṣūnabravīt- bhāvayathemamartha nānandopamitākāram iti |
body.translated_text: Now, the disputants are each established in different views. Some say: 'Past and future <s>dharmas</s> exist.' Others say: 'They do not exist.' Therefore it should be understood that disputants, not comprehending the <s>Tathāgata</s>, following the literal words, quarrel. Just as <s>Ānanda</s>, for the purpose of <s>samādhi</s>, said: 'All attachments (<s>upādāna</s>) are suffering.' At that time, the Blessed One told the monks: 'Cultivate this meaning — <s>Ānanda</s> has spoken it not as a mere simile.'

body.text: sarve vādina āhuḥ- arhan agradakṣiṇīya iti | bhikṣavo 'jñātvā tathāgatamupetyāprākṣuḥ | bhagavānavocat- mama śāsane agrapravrajito 'gradakṣiṇīya iti | [evam] annapāne sthūlavastunyeva na jānanti [yathāvat] kaḥ punarvādastathāgatenabhisandhāya bhāṣite sūkṣmadharme | ityādinā hetunā na kartavyo vicāraḥ |
body.translated_text: All disputants say: 'An <s>Arhat</s> is the foremost worthy of offerings.' The monks, not understanding, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> and asked. The Blessed One said: 'In my teaching, the first to go forth is the foremost worthy of offerings.' [Thus] they do not even understand gross matters such as food and drink — how much less could there be discourse about the subtle <s>Dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> with hidden intent? By these and other reasons, investigation should not be undertaken [— so the objection claims].

body.text: atrocyate | na yuktamidam | kasmāt | kāraṇasattvāt parāmisandhirjñātuṃ śakyate | yathoktaṃ gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: This is not correct. Why? Because through reasoning, the hidden intent can be understood. As declared in the verse:

body.text:
jānanti vaktuḥ sandhānaṃ [paramaṃ] yatparāyaṇam |
jānantyapi ca vaktuśca vivakṣā yasya vastunaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
They know the speaker's intention, [the supreme] goal;
and knowing the speaker's wish regarding which subject matter — thus it is said.

body.text: tatrāsti dvidhā mārga āryamārgo laukikamārga iti | idaṃ paścādvakṣyate | anena mārgeṇa vakturāśayo jñāyate | atha parapravāda sūtre 'pi bhagavān saṃśrāvayati sma | [ārya]kātyāyanādibhirmahāvādibhirbhagavadāśayaḥ pratilabdha ityato bhagavān sādhupraśaśaṃsa |
body.translated_text: Therein there is a twofold path: the Noble Path (<s>āryamārga</s>) and the worldly path (<s>laukikamārga</s>). This will be explained later. By this method, the speaker's intention is known. Now, in the <s>Parapravādasūtra</s> as well, the Blessed One proclaimed: 'The Blessed One's intent was obtained by the great disputants beginning with the Noble <s>Kātyāyana</s>' — therefore the Blessed One praised them as 'excellent.'

body.text: udāyibhikṣudharmadinnādibhibhikṣuṇībhiḥ kṛtaṃ bhagavacchāsanaṃ bhagavān śrutvā [tadeva punaḥ] śrāvayati sma |
body.translated_text: The teaching of the Blessed One that was formulated by the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> such as <s>Udāyi bhikṣu</s>, <s>Dharmadinnā</s>, and others — having heard it, the Blessed One [himself again] proclaimed it.

body.text: gabhīraṃ tathāgataśāsanaṃ vivṛṇvatā śāstraṃ viracyate | avivaraṇe santiṣṭhet | evamanyaḥ "tathāgatamūlāḥ sarvadharmā" ityādi praśnaḥ sarvaḥ pratyuktaḥ | kiñca śāstraṃ viracayitavyam | kasmāt | śāstre viracitte hi arthaḥ sugamaḥ syāt | dharmaśca cirasthitikaḥ syāt | bhagavāṃśca śāstrapraṇayanaṃ saṃśrāvayati sma | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhagavānavocadbhikṣūn- yathāpraṇītaṃ śāstraṃ samyagdhārayata | iti | ataḥ sūtrādarthamādāya śāstraṃ nikāyānta rātmanā pṛthak sthāpyate | ataḥ śāstraṃ racayitavyam |
body.translated_text: When elucidating the profound teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, a treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) is composed. One should remain firm in the elucidation. Thus every other question such as 'All <s>dharmas</s> are rooted in the <s>Tathāgata</s>' and so forth has been answered. Furthermore, a treatise should be composed. Why? Because when a treatise is composed, the meaning becomes easily accessible, the <s>Dharma</s> would endure for a long time, and the Blessed One himself proclaimed the composition of treatises. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Blessed One said to the monks: Properly maintain the treatise as it has been composed.' Therefore, taking the meaning from the <s>sūtras</s>, a treatise is separately established by oneself apart from the <s>nikāyas</s>. Therefore a treatise should be composed.

body.text: kiñca bhagavān nānāsattvānāṃ santaraṇīyānāṃ kṛte lokādīni śāstramukhānyuktavān | yathā svātyādayo 'pratipadyamānā bhrāntamatayo 'bhūvan | svātyādayo bhikṣava āhuḥ- tadevedaṃ vijñānaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati | ananyaditi |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the Blessed One, for the sake of the various beings to be ferried across, taught the treatise-approaches (<s>śāstramukha</s>) beginning with the worldly. Just as <s>Svāti</s> and others, not comprehending, became those of confused views. The monks <s>Svāti</s> and others said: 'This very consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) runs on and transmigrates; it is nothing other [than the same one].'

body.text: bhagavānevamādinā nānādharmamupadiṣṭavān | vinā śāstraṃ kathamarthaḥ pratipadyeta | ityādibhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ śāstraṃ viracayitavyam ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One taught the various <s>dharmas</s> in this and other ways. Without a treatise, how could the meaning be comprehended? For these and other reasons, a treatise should be composed.

body.text: śāstrasthāpanavargastrayodaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the thirteenth chapter, the Chapter on Establishing the Teaching (<s>śāstrasthāpanavarga</s>).

body.text: 14 śāstramukhavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 14. Chapter on the Approaches of the Teaching (<s>śāstramukhavarga</s>)

body.text: lokamukhaṃ paramārthamukhamiti dvimukhaṃ | lokamukhataḥ astyātmā ityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: There are two approaches (<s>mukha</s>): the worldly approach (<s>lokamukha</s>) and the ultimate approach (<s>paramārthamukha</s>). From the worldly approach, it is said that the self (<s>ātman</s>) exists. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
ātmā hi ātmano nāthaḥ ko nu nāthaḥ paro bhavet |
ātmanaiva kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ ātmanaiva viśudhyate |
ātmanaiva kṛtaṃ pāpamātmanā saṃkliśyate || iti |

kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- śāśvataṃ manovijñānam | iti | āha ca- dīrgharātraṃ bhāvitacitto mṛta ūrdhvajanmabhāk bhavati | iti | kiñcāha kārakaḥ karma karoti, kārakaḥ svayamanubhavati | iti | amukaḥ sattvo 'trotpadyate ityādi sarvaṃ lokamukhenoktam, paramārthamukhatastūcyate sarvaṃ śūnyamasat iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre eṣu pañcasu skandheṣu nāstyātmā vā ātmīyaṃ vā | cittañca samīraṇajvalanavat pratikṣaṇavināśi | asti karma asti karmaphalam, kārakastu nopalabhyate | iti | yathā bhagavān āha- skandhānāṃ santatyāsti saṃsāra iti |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) is eternal.' And it says: 'One whose mind has been long cultivated, upon death, becomes a recipient of higher birth.' Furthermore it says: 'The doer (<s>kāraka</s>) performs action (<s>karma</s>); the doer himself experiences [its result].' 'Such-and-such a being is born here' — and so forth, all is spoken from the worldly approach. But from the ultimate approach (<s>paramārthamukha</s>), it is said that all is empty and non-existent. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'In these five <s>skandhas</s> there is neither self (<s>ātman</s>) nor anything belonging to self (<s>ātmīya</s>). And consciousness (<s>citta</s>), like wind-blown fire, is perishing every moment. There is <s>karma</s> and there is the fruit of <s>karma</s>, but no doer is apprehended.' As the Blessed One said: 'Through the continuity of the <s>skandhas</s>, there is <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

body.text: (2) anyadasti dvividhaṃ śāstramukham vyavahāramukhamāryamukham iti | vyavahāramukhamiti | vyavahārata ucyamānam, [yathā] candraḥ kṣīyata iti | vastutastu candro na kṣīyate | [yathā vā] mṛgā ramāteti snuṣāṃ māteti vadanti | na vastutaḥ sā mātā | yathoktaṃ sūtre- jihvā rasaṃ vijānāti iti | jihvāvijñānaṃ rasaṃ vijānāti na tu jihvā | yathā śaktipratihataṃ puruṣaṃ prati vadanti puruṣo 'yaṃ duḥkhaṃ vijānātīti | vijñānantu duḥkhaṃ vijānāti, na tu puruṣaḥ | yathā vā daridraḥ puruṣaḥ prabhuriti vyapadiśyate | buddho 'pi puruṣavaśāt prabhuriti khyāpayati | kiñca bhagavān tīrthikānākārayati brāhmaṇāniti śramaṇāniti ca | kṣatriyabrāhmaṇādaya iva buddho 'pi vyavahārataḥ pūjyo bhavati | ekameva yathā bhājanaṃ deśavaśāt vibhinnanāmakam, buddho 'pi nāmānuyāti | yathā bhagavānāha- ahaṃ vaiśālīṃ paścimā [valoka]mavalokayāmīti | evamādivacanaṃ vyavahāramanuvartata iti vyavahāramukhamityucyate |
body.translated_text: (2) There is another twofold approach of the teaching: the conventional approach (<s>vyavahāramukha</s>) and the noble approach (<s>āryamukha</s>). The conventional approach: that which is stated through convention — [for example,] 'the moon wanes.' But in reality, the moon does not wane. [Or as when] they call a daughter-in-law 'mother,' saying 'the deer delights.' In reality she is not the mother. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The tongue cognizes taste.' [But actually] it is tongue-consciousness (<s>jihvāvijñāna</s>) that cognizes taste, not the tongue. Just as when a man is struck by a spear, they say of him: 'This man cognizes suffering.' But it is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) that cognizes suffering, not the man. Or just as a poor man is designated as 'lord' (<s>prabhu</s>). The <s>Buddha</s> too, on account of personhood, proclaims [things as] 'lord.' Furthermore, the Blessed One addresses the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist sectarians) as '<s>brāhmaṇas</s>' and '<s>śramaṇas</s>.' Just as <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and others, the <s>Buddha</s> too is conventionally worthy of worship. Just as one and the same vessel has different names depending on the region, the <s>Buddha</s> too follows names. As the Blessed One said: 'I look back at <s>Vaiśālī</s> with a final glance.' Such and other words follow convention — therefore it is called the conventional approach.

body.text: āryamukhamiti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- pratītyasamutpannaṃ vijñānaṃ cakṣurādīnāmindriyāṇāṃ mūlaṃ mahāsamudravat | yathāha sūtram- skandhāyatanadhātūnāṃ pratyayāḥ sāmagrīmātram na kārakaḥ nāpi vedakaḥ iti | sarvaṃ duḥkhamiti cāha | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yat laukikā vadanti sukhamiti [tat] āryā duḥkhaṃ vadanti | yat āryā duḥkhaṃ vadanti [tat]laukikāḥ sukhaṃ vadanti | iti | abhidheyāḥ śūnyā animittā ityādi ca | tat āryamukhamityucyate |
body.translated_text: The noble approach (<s>āryamukha</s>): as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Consciousness arising from conditions (<s>pratītyasamutpanna vijñāna</s>) is the root of the sense-faculties beginning with the eye, like a great ocean.' As the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'The conditions of the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> are merely an assemblage (<s>sāmagrī</s>) — there is no doer, nor is there an experiencer.' And it says: 'All is suffering.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'What worldly people call happiness, the Noble Ones call suffering. What the Noble Ones call suffering, worldly people call happiness.' And 'the expressible things are empty, signless (<s>animitta</s>),' and so forth. That is called the noble approach.

body.text: (3) traikālika śāstramukham | yatra rūpamityākhyāyate tatra yadatītaṃ yadanāgataṃ vartamānam sarvaṃ tat rūpamityucyate | idaṃ laukikaṃ śāstramukham |
body.translated_text: (3) The temporal approach (<s>traikālika śāstramukha</s>) of the teaching: wherever form (<s>rūpa</s>) is described — that which is past, that which is future, and that which is present — all of that is called form. This is the worldly approach of the teaching.

body.text: (4) asti cediti śāstramukham | [yathā] sparśo 'sti cet, so 'vaśyaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamupādāya bhavati | na tu sarvaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ sparśasya hetūkriyate | tṛṣṇasti cet avaśyaṃ sā vedanāmupādāyaṃ bhavati | na tu sarvā vedanā tṛṣṇāyā hetūkriyate | kadācit samagraheturucyate yathā sparśapratyayā vedanā iti | kadācidasamagra heturucyate yathā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā iti | na tūcyate avidyeti | kadācidanyathocyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- prītamanasaḥ kāyaḥ praśrabhyate | aprītasyāpi tribhirdhyānaiḥkāyaḥ praśrabhyate | praśrabdha[kāyaḥ] sukhaṃ vedayate | iti ca caturbhirdhyānaiḥ prasrabdhimānapi na sukhaṃ vedayate | itīdamanyathā vacanam |
body.translated_text: (4) The conditional approach (<s>asti cet śāstramukha</s>) of the teaching: [for example,] if contact (<s>sparśa</s>) exists, it necessarily arises depending on the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>). But not all six sense-bases serve as causes of contact. If craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) exists, it necessarily arises depending on feeling (<s>vedanā</s>). But not all feeling serves as the cause of craving. Sometimes a complete cause is stated, as in 'Feeling is conditioned by contact.' Sometimes an incomplete cause is stated, as in 'Craving is conditioned by feeling' — ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is not mentioned. Sometimes it is stated otherwise. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one of joyful mind, the body becomes tranquil.' Yet even without joy, through the three <s>dhyānas</s>, the body becomes tranquil. '[One with] a tranquil body experiences happiness.' Yet even with tranquility through the four <s>dhyānas</s>, one does not experience [sensory] happiness. This is an example of alternative statement.

body.text: (5) utsargo 'pavāda iti dvividhaṃ śāstramukham | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yaścai- tyavandanāya pādāvutkṣipati sa āyuṣo 'nte deveṣūtpadyate iti | ayamutsargaḥ | sūtrāntaramāha- anantaryasya kartā na deveṣūtpadyata iti | ayamapavādaḥ | uktañca sūtre- kāmānāmanubhavitā nāpāpakaṃ karoti iti | ayamutsargaḥ | srotaāpannaḥ puruṣaḥ kāmānupabhuñjāno 'pi na durgatipatanīyaṃ karma karoti iti | ayamapavādaḥ | api coktaṃ sūtre- cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpañca cakṣurvijñānamutpadyate iti | ayamutsargaḥ | yadi tadaiva sarvāṇi rūpāṇi pratītya cakṣurvijñānamutpadyata
body.translated_text: (5) There is a twofold approach of the teaching: general rule (<s>utsarga</s>) and exception (<s>apavāda</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who lifts his feet to worship a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), at the end of life is reborn among the gods.' This is the general rule. Another <s>sūtra</s> says: 'One who has committed an act of immediate retribution (<s>ānantarya</s>) is not reborn among the gods.' This is the exception. And it is stated in a <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who enjoys sense-pleasures (<s>kāma</s>) does not commit evil.' This is the general rule. 'A stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>), even while enjoying sense-pleasures, does not perform <s>karma</s> that leads to lower rebirths.' This is the exception. Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Depending on the eye and form, eye-consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) arises.' This is the general rule. If one were to say that at that very moment eye-consciousness arises depending on all forms

body.text: iti vadet | tadayuktam | atha coktaṃ sūtre- śrotraṃ pratītya śabdañca śrotravijñānamutpadyate na cakṣurvijñānam | iti | ayamapavādaḥ | utsargo 'pavādaśca sarvaḥ sayuktiko na dharmalakṣaṇavilomakaḥ |
body.translated_text: — that would be incorrect. Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Depending on the ear and sound, ear-consciousness (<s>śrotravijñāna</s>) arises, not eye-consciousness.' This is the exception. Both general rule and exception are logically consistent and do not contradict the characteristics of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: (6) aparamasti dvividhaṃ śāstramukham- viniścitamaviniścitamiti | viniścitam- yathocyate- buddhaḥ sarvajñaḥ puruṣa iti | bhagavato bhāṣitaḥ paramārtho dharmaḥ | bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ samyagācāraśīlā iti | kiñcāha- sarve saṃskṛtadharmā anityā duḥkhāḥ śūnyā anātmānaḥ [teṣāṃ]nirodho nirvāṇam ityādi mukhaṃ viniścitam | aviniścitam- yadyucyate mriyamāṇo jāyata iti | tadaviniścitam | satyāṃ tṛṣṇāyāṃ jāyate | tṛṣṇākṣaye nirudhyate | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- samāhitasya tattvajñānamutpadyata iti | idamapi aviniścitam | āryāṇāṃ samādhilābhināṃ tattvajñānamutpadyate | na tu tīrthikānāṃ labdhasamādhikānāmapi | yathāha sūtram- yadabhilaṣitaṃ tallabhyate iti | idamapi aviniścitam | kadācittu na labhyate | yadāha- ṣaḍāyatanaṃ sparśajanakam iti | idamapi aviniścitam | kiñcijjanakaṃ kiñcinna janakam | evamādyaviniścitamukham |
body.translated_text: (6) There is yet another twofold approach of the teaching: the determinate (<s>viniścita</s>) and the indeterminate (<s>aviniścita</s>). The determinate: as it is said, 'The <s>Buddha</s> is an omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>) person.' 'The ultimate <s>Dharma</s> has been taught by the Blessed One.' 'The disciples of the Blessed One are of right conduct.' Furthermore it says: 'All conditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>saṃskṛtadharma</s>) are impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self; their cessation is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>' — and so forth. This approach is determinate. Indeterminate: if it is said, 'The dying one is reborn' — that is indeterminate. When craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) exists, one is reborn; when craving is destroyed, one ceases. Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one in <s>samādhi</s>, knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) arises.' This too is indeterminate. For Noble Ones who have attained <s>samādhi</s>, knowledge of reality arises; but not for <s>tīrthikas</s> who have also attained <s>samādhi</s>. As the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'What is desired is obtained.' This too is indeterminate — sometimes it is not obtained. When it says: 'The six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) give rise to contact' — this too is indeterminate; some give rise and some do not. Such is the indeterminate approach.

body.text: (7) atha kṛtakākṛtakaśāstramukham | yathocyate- adbhuta mūlikā surabhipuṣpañca na vātarogapratikūlam iti | āha- kovidārapuṣpaṃ vātarogapratikūlam iti | ādyasya manuṣyapuṣpatvāt na vātarogapratikūlamityucyate | dvitīyasya divyapuṣpatvāt vātarogapratikūlamityucyate | kiñca vadanti tisro vedanā- duḥkhā vedanā sukhā vedanā aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā iti | sūtrāntaramāha- vidyamānāḥ sarvā vedanā duḥkhamiti | trividhaṃ duḥkhaṃ- duḥkha- duḥkhaṃ, vipariṇāmaduḥkhaṃ saṃskāra duḥkhamiti | tadarthamāha- vidyamānāḥ sarvā vedanā duḥkhamiti | āha ca- duḥkhamidaṃ trividhaṃ navaṃ purāṇaṃ madhyamiti | aciravedanāyāṃ sukham | ciranirvede duḥkham | madhyame upekṣā |
body.translated_text: (7) Now the approach of the teaching regarding the made and unmade (<s>kṛtaka-akṛtaka</s>): as it is said, 'A wondrous root-medicine and a fragrant flower are not harmful to wind-disease (<s>vātaroga</s>).' It says: '<s>Kovidāra</s> flowers are harmful to wind-disease.' The first, being human flowers, is said to be not harmful to wind-disease. The second, being divine flowers, is said to be harmful to wind-disease. Furthermore, they say there are three feelings (<s>vedanā</s>): painful feeling, pleasant feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Another <s>sūtra</s> says: 'All existing feelings are suffering.' There is threefold suffering: the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkha-duḥkha</s>), the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkha</s>), and the suffering of formations (<s>saṃskāraduḥkha</s>). For this purpose it says: 'All existing feelings are suffering.' And it says: 'This suffering is threefold — new, old, and middle.' In a brief feeling, there is happiness; in prolonged discomfort, there is suffering; in the middle, there is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).

body.text: kiñcāha- abhisambuddhatvāt parivrāṭ iti | anabhisambuddho 'ṣi parivrāṭ bhavati | evamādilakṣaṇānāṃ hetuta ākhyā bhavati |
body.translated_text: Furthermore it says: 'Because of being fully awakened (<s>abhisambuddha</s>), one is a <s>parivrāṭ</s> (wandering ascetic).' One who is not fully awakened is also a <s>parivrāṭ</s>. Thus the designations of such characteristics arise from their causes.

body.text: (8) pratyāsattiḥ śāstramukham | yathā bhagavānavocabhdikṣūn- prajahata prapañcam, tadā nirvāṇaṃ labhadhve iti | alabdhe 'pi pratyāsattyā labhadhve ityucyate |
body.translated_text: (8) Proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>) is an approach of the teaching. As the Blessed One said to the monks: 'Abandon proliferations (<s>prapañca</s>); then you will obtain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' Even though it is not yet obtained, due to proximity it is said 'you will obtain.'

body.text: (9) lakṣaṇasāmyaṃ śāstramukham | yathā ekavastukathane anyadapi vastu samalakṣaṇamuktaṃ bhavati | yathā cāha bhagavān- laghuparivṛttaṃ cittam | tadā anye 'pi caittadharmā uktā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: (9) Similarity of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇasāmya</s>) is an approach of the teaching. When speaking of one thing, another thing of similar characteristics is also implied. As the Blessed One said: 'The mind (<s>citta</s>) turns quickly.' Then other mental factors (<s>caittadharma</s>) are also understood as stated.

body.text: (10) bhūyo 'nuvartanaṃ śāstramukham | yathā bhagavānā ha- ya udayavyayalakṣaṇadṛṣṭidvayaṃ na prajānāti sa sarvaḥ sarāgī bhavati | yastu prajānāti sa vītarāgo bhavati | iti | srotaāpanna udayavyayalakṣaṇadvitayadṛṣṭiṃ jānannapi sarāgo bhavati | tatprajānānāṃ bhūyastvena paraṃ vītarāgā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: (10) Following the majority (<s>bhūyo'nuvartana</s>) is an approach of the teaching. As the Blessed One said: 'One who does not understand the dual view of the characteristics of arising and ceasing — all such persons have attachment (<s>sarāga</s>). But one who understands is free from attachment (<s>vītarāga</s>).' A stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>), even while knowing the dual view of the characteristics of arising and ceasing, still has attachment. But in the majority of cases, those who understand become free from attachment.

body.text: (11) kāraṇe kāryopacāraḥ śāstramukham | yathocyate- annadānaṃ prayacchati pañca guṇān- āyuḥ varṇaṃ balaṃ sukhaṃ pratibhānam iti | vastutastu nāyurādīn pañca guṇān prayacchati | api tu taddhetūn prayacchati | kiñcāhuḥ kārṣāpaṇamadyata iti | kārṣāpaṇaṃ nādanīyam | api tu kārṣāpaṇamupādāya labdhamadyate ityataḥ kārṣāpaṇamadyata ityucyate | yathāha sūtram- strīpuruṣau malam iti | na vastuto malam | āsaṅgādikleśamalahetutvāt | malamityucyate | kiñcāha- pañca viṣayāḥ kāmā iti | na vastutaḥ kāmāḥ | kāmajanakatvāt | kāmā ityucyante | sukhakāraṇaṃ sukhamityucyate | yathā vadanti- upacitadharmāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sukha iti | duḥkhakāraṇaṃ duḥkhamityucyate | yathā vadanti- mūḍhaiḥ saha saṃvāso duḥkhamiti | yathā vadanti sukho 'gniḥ duḥkho 'gniriti | āhuśca- āyurheturāyuriti | yathoktaṃ gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: (11) Figurative designation of effect for cause (<s>kāraṇe kāryopacāra</s>) is an approach of the teaching. As it is said: 'The gift of food bestows five qualities: life-span (<s>āyus</s>), complexion (<s>varṇa</s>), strength (<s>bala</s>), happiness (<s>sukha</s>), and eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>).' But in reality, it does not bestow these five qualities; rather, it bestows their causes. Furthermore they say: 'One eats a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin).' A coin is not edible; but because by means of a coin one obtains what is eaten, it is said 'one eats a coin.' As the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'Men and women are impurity.' They are not actually impurity, but because they are causes of defilement-impurities such as attachment, they are called impurity. Furthermore it says: 'The five sense-objects are <s>kāmas</s> (desires).' They are not actually desires, but because they give rise to desire, they are called desires. The cause of happiness is called happiness — just as they say of a man endowed with <s>dharma</s>: 'This man is happiness.' The cause of suffering is called suffering — just as they say: 'Cohabitation with fools is suffering.' Just as they say: 'The fire is pleasant,' or 'the fire is unpleasant.' And they say: 'The cause of longevity is longevity.' As stated in the verse:

body.text:
janmopakaraṇasampacca bāhyaṃ jīvitamasti hi |
dhanahārī yathā nṝṇāṃ jīvitāpahṛducyate || iti |
body.translated_text:
And the instruments of birth are external life indeed;
just as a thief of wealth is said to be a robber of life for people. Thus it is said.

body.text: āhuścāsravaheturāsrava iti | yathāha saptāsravasūtram- tatra dvau vastuta āsravau, amyāni pacca vastūni āsravakāraṇāni |
body.translated_text: They also say that the cause of outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) is itself called an outflow. As the <s>Saptāsravasūtra</s> (Sūtra on Seven Outflows) states: 'Therein, two are outflows in the real sense, and the remaining five are causes of outflows.'

body.text: kārye kāraṇopacāraścāsti | yathā bhagavānāha- mayā pūrvakarmānubhavitavyamiti | karmaphalamanubhavitavyamityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: And there is the figurative use of cause for effect. As the Blessed One said: 'The <s>karma</s> of my past lives must be experienced by me' — the meaning is that the fruit of <s>karma</s> must be experienced.

body.text: evamādīni bahūni śāstramukhāni parijñātavyāni ||
body.translated_text: Thus many such entrances to the <s>śāstra</s> are to be fully comprehended.

body.text: śāstramukhavargaścaturdaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the fourteenth chapter, the Chapter on Entrances to the Treatise (<s>śāstramukhavarga</s>).

body.text: 15 śāstrapraśaṃsāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 15. Chapter on the Praise of the Treatise (<s>śāstrapraśaṃsāvarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramidamabhyasitavyam kasmāt | śāstramabhyasan puruṣadharmajñānaṃ labhate | yathoktaṃ sūsre- dvau puruṣau staḥ jño 'jñaśca | yaḥ skandhadhātvāyatanadvādaśanidānakāraṇakāryādidharmavivekākuśalaḥ so 'jñaḥ | yastu kuśalaḥ, sa jña iti | śāstre cāsmin skandhadhātvāyatanādīni samyagvivicyante | ata idaṃ śāstramupādāya puruṣadharmajñānaṃ labhyate | itīdamabhyasitavyam |
body.translated_text: Why should this <s>śāstra</s> be studied? By studying the <s>śāstra</s>, one obtains the knowledge of human <s>dharma</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are two types of persons — the knower and the ignorant. One who is unskilled in the discrimination of <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the twelve <s>nidānas</s> (links of dependent origination), cause and effect, and so forth — he is the ignorant one. But one who is skilled — he is the knower.' And in this <s>śāstra</s>, the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and so forth are properly analyzed. Therefore, by taking up this <s>śāstra</s>, one obtains the knowledge of human <s>dharma</s>. Thus it should be studied.

body.text: etacchāstrābhyāsādaprākṛto bhavati | prākṛto 'prākṛta iti dvau puruṣau staḥ | yathā vadanti- kaścinmuṇḍitakeśaśmaśruko dharmapaṭaṃ paridadhānaḥ parigṛhītabuddheryāpatho 'pi bhagavacchāsanād dūrībhūtaḥ | śraddhendriyādyasamanvāgamāt | yastu śraddhendriyādisamanvāgataḥ sa gṛhastho 'pi aprākṛta ityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- caturvidhāḥ puruṣāḥ kaścit saṅghasyeryāpathe 'vatīrṇaḥ na saṅghagaṇitaḥ | kaścit saṅghagaṇito na saṅghasyeryāpathe 'vatīrṇaḥ | kaścit saṅgheryāpathe saṅghagaṇanāyāñcāvatīrṇaḥ | kaścinna saṅgheryāpathe 'vatīrṇo nāpi saṅghagaṇanāyām | ādyaḥ pravrajitaḥ prākṛtaḥ | anantaro gṛhastha āryaḥ | tṛtīyaḥ pravrajitaḥ āryaḥ | caturtho gṛhastha prākṛtaḥ | iti | anena hetunā śraddhendriyādivirahito na saṅghagaṇānāyāmavatarati | ataḥ śradvendriyādīnāṃ kṛta udyogaḥ kāryaḥ | śraddhendriyalipsunā bhagavacchāsanaṃ śrutvā uddiṣṭaṃ prātimokṣamādāya yathāvaccaritavyam | ato 'bhyasitavyamidaṃ buddhadharmaśāstram |
body.translated_text: Through the study of this <s>śāstra</s>, one becomes a person of distinction (<s>aprākṛta</s>). There are two types of persons — the ordinary (<s>prākṛta</s>) and the distinguished (<s>aprākṛta</s>). As they say: 'A certain one, with shaved hair and beard, wearing the robe of <s>Dharma</s>, having adopted the deportment of the awakened ones, is yet far from the Blessed One's teaching — because he lacks the faculties beginning with faith (<s>śraddhendriya</s>). But one who possesses the faculties beginning with faith, even though a householder, is called a person of distinction.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four types of persons: a certain one has entered the deportment of the <s>Saṅgha</s> but is not counted among the <s>Saṅgha</s>. A certain one is counted among the <s>Saṅgha</s> but has not entered the deportment of the <s>Saṅgha</s>. A certain one has entered the deportment of the <s>Saṅgha</s> and is also counted among the <s>Saṅgha</s>. A certain one has neither entered the deportment of the <s>Saṅgha</s> nor is counted among the <s>Saṅgha</s>.' The first is an ordinary renunciant. The second is a noble householder. The third is a noble renunciant. The fourth is an ordinary householder. For this reason, one who lacks the faculties beginning with faith does not enter the reckoning of the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Therefore effort must be made to cultivate the faculties beginning with faith. One who desires the faith-faculty, having heard the teaching of the Blessed One and having taken up the prescribed <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of discipline), should practice accordingly. Therefore this <s>śāstra</s> of the <s>Buddhadharma</s> should be studied.

body.text: kiñcānena śāstreṇa dvividhaṃ hitaṃ bhavati ātmahitaṃ parahitamiti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- caturvidhāḥ puruṣāḥ | kaścidātmahitāya pratipanno na parahitāya | kaścit parahitāya pratipanno nātmahitāya | kaścidātmahitāya ca pratipannaḥ parahitāya ca | kaścinnaivātmahitāya
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through this <s>śāstra</s>, twofold benefit arises — benefit for oneself (<s>ātmahita</s>) and benefit for others (<s>parahita</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four types of persons: a certain one is devoted to self-benefit but not to the benefit of others. A certain one is devoted to the benefit of others but not to self-benefit. A certain one is devoted to both self-benefit and the benefit of others. A certain one is devoted neither to self-benefit

body.text: pratipanno na parahitāya iti | ya ātmanā śīlādīn sampādayati na parān śīlādiṣu sthāpayati | sa ātmahitāya pratipannaḥ | evaṃ caturdhā | yat kaścidātmahitāya pratipanno 'pi pareṣāñca dānādimahāphalaṃ sampādayati | tadapi parahitam | tatra buddhānusmṛte rnedaṃ hitamucyate | yadi kaścit parasya dharmopadeśāya pratipannaḥ | tat parahitam | sa ātmanā dharmacaryāmanuvartamāno 'pi parārthamupadeśāt ātmano 'pi hitamanuprāpnoti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- parasyadharmamupadiśan pañcavidhaṃ hitaṃ labhate iti | tatra buddhānusmṛterapi nedamucyate | tatra pravacanamātrasyottamaṃ hitaṃ bhavati yadyathoktamācarata āsravāḥ kṣīyante iti | ato dharmasya prakktā parahitāya pratipannaḥ | sa sahitatvācca puruṣeṣūttamaḥ | tadyathā raseṣu maṇḍam |
body.translated_text: nor to the benefit of others.' One who himself cultivates moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and other virtues but does not establish others in moral conduct and the rest — he is devoted to self-benefit. And so it is fourfold. But a certain one, even while devoted to self-benefit, enables others to accomplish the great fruit of giving (<s>dāna</s>) and so forth — that too is benefit for others. In that case, this benefit is not spoken of from the perspective of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>). If a certain one is devoted to teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to others — that is benefit for others. He, while following the practice of <s>Dharma</s> himself, also obtains benefit for himself through teaching others. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to others obtains fivefold benefit.' In that context, this is not spoken of from the perspective of <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> either. Therein, the supreme benefit lies in the proclamation alone — namely, 'if one practices as taught, the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) are destroyed.' Therefore, the proclaimer of <s>Dharma</s> is devoted to the benefit of others. And because of possessing both [benefits], he is the foremost among persons — just as cream is [the foremost] among flavors.

body.text: atha sa puruṣa idānīṃ jyotiṣi sthitaḥ paścādapi jyotiḥ parāyaṇo bhavati | laukikāḥ sarve bhūyasā tamastamaḥ parāyaṇāḥ jyotiṣo jyotiḥ parāyaṇā vā | yaḥ kaścid buddhaśāsanamācarati sa tamaso jyotiḥ parāyaṇaḥ jyotiṣo jyotiḥ parāyaṇo vā bhavati | kasmāt | dānādīnācaran na [tādṛśaṃ] hitaṃ vindate yādṛśaṃ buddhadharmaṃ śṛṇvan [vindate] | yaścālpa[mapi] buddhapravacanaṃ śṛṇoti sa prativedhajñānalābhī san sarvakleśān bhaṅktvā apramāṇahitaṃ prasavati | yaktoktaṃ sūtre- catvāraḥ pudgalāḥ- tamastamaḥparāyaṇaḥ tamojyotiḥparāyaṇaḥ jyotirjyotiḥ parāyaṇaḥ jyotistamaḥparāyaṇaḥ iti | kiñca caturvidhāḥ parāyaṇāḥ anussrotogāmī pratisrotogāmī sthitātmā, tīrṇaḥ pāraṅgata iti | yaścittaikāgryeṇa bhagavaddharmaṃ śṛṇoti sa eva pañca nīvaraṇāni prahāya saptabodhyaṅgāni bhāvayati | ataḥ sa pratiruddhasaṃsārasrotāḥ pratīkūla ityucyate | sa ca sthitātmā pāraṅgataśca bhavati |
body.translated_text: Now, that person stands in light, and hereafter too he is one who is bound for light. All worldly beings are for the most part either those who go from darkness to darkness, or those who go from light to light. Whoever practices the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching goes from darkness to light, or from light to light. Why? One who practices giving (<s>dāna</s>) and other virtues does not obtain such benefit as one who listens to the <s>Buddhadharma</s> obtains. And one who hears even a little of the <s>Buddha</s>'s discourse, having obtained the knowledge of penetration (<s>prativedhajñāna</s>), destroys all defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) and brings forth immeasurable benefit. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four persons — one who goes from darkness to darkness, one who goes from darkness to light, one who goes from light to light, and one who goes from light to darkness.' Furthermore, there are four kinds of dispositions: one who goes with the current (<s>anusrotogāmin</s>), one who goes against the current (<s>pratisrotogāmin</s>), one who stands firm (<s>sthitātman</s>), and one who has crossed over and reached the far shore (<s>tīrṇa pāraṅgata</s>). One who, with one-pointed concentration, listens to the <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One — he alone abandons the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) and cultivates the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>). Therefore he is called one who goes against the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And he becomes one who stands firm and one who has reached the far shore.

body.text: punaścaturvidhāḥ puruṣāḥ- sadābhavanimagnaḥ kañcit kālaṃ bhavānnirgatya punarnimagnaḥ, bhavanirgamaparīkṣakaḥ bhavapāraṅgata iti | yo nirvāṇagāmiśraddhādiguṇānnotpādayati | sa sadā bhavanimagnaḥ | kaścit laukikaśraddhādīnutpādya na dṛḍhayati panaḥ parihīyate | sa kañcit kālaṃ nirgatya punarnimagnaḥ | yaḥ śraddhādīnutpādya śubhāśubhaṃ vivecayati sa nirgamaparīkṣakaḥ | yaḥ nirvāṇagāmiśraddhādīnupasampādya bhāvayati sa pāraṅgataḥ | yo bhagavaddharmasya samyagarthaṃ vetti sa naiva sadā nimagno bhavati | sa muhūrtaṃ parihīno 'pi nātyantaṃ parihīyate |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, there are four types of persons: one who is perpetually submerged in existence, one who emerges from existence for a time but sinks again, one who examines how to emerge from existence, and one who has reached the far shore of existence. One who does not produce virtuous qualities such as faith directed toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — he is perpetually submerged in existence. A certain one who produces worldly faith and other virtues but does not strengthen them and regresses — he emerges for a time but sinks again. One who produces faith and other virtues and discriminates between wholesome and unwholesome — he is the examiner of emergence. One who, having fully cultivated the virtuous qualities such as faith directed toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, develops them — he has reached the far shore. One who correctly understands the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One is never perpetually submerged in existence. Even if he regresses for a moment, he does not regress completely.

body.text: sa ca guṇābhāvayitetyucyate yaḥ kāyena śīlaṃ manasā prajñāṃ ca bhāvayati sa kiñcid duṣkarma kurvannapi durgatau patati | yastu bhāvayati kāyena śīlaṃ manasā prajñāṃ sa bahu duṣkarma kurvannapi na durgatau patati | kāyasya bhāvayitā śrutaprajñābhyāṃ kāyavedanācaittān bhāvayati | kāyaṃ bhāvayan krameṇa śīlasamādhiprajñāskandhānutpādya karmāṇi prajahāti | karmaṇāṃ prahāṇāt saṃsāro 'pi nirudhyate | - uktañca sūtre caturvidhāḥ puruṣāḥ- kecit agambhīratīkṣṇānuyāḥ, kecit atīkṣṇagambhīrānuśayāḥ, kecidgambhīratīkṣṇānuśayā, kecidagambhīrātīkṣṇānuśayāḥ | ādyaḥ adhimātrānuśayaḥ kāle kāla āgacchati | samanantaro yo mṛdumadhyānuśayaḥ sa sadāgatya cittaniviṣṭo bhavati | tṛtīyo yo 'dhimātrānuśayaḥ so 'pi āgatya cittaniviṣṭaḥ | caturtho yo mṛdumadhyānuśayaḥ sa kaśmiṃñcitkāla āgacchati | sa yadi bhagavataḥ śāsane samyacchāsraṃ śṛṇoti | sa tīkṣṇagabhīrākhyadvividhānanuśayān prajahāti |
body.translated_text: He is called a cultivator of virtues who cultivates moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) with the body and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) with the mind. Even if he commits some unwholesome action, he falls into a lower realm [only briefly]. But one who cultivates moral conduct with the body and wisdom with the mind — even if he commits much unwholesome action, he does not fall into a lower realm. The cultivator of the body, through learning and wisdom, cultivates the body, feelings, and mental factors. Cultivating the body, he progressively produces the aggregates of moral conduct, concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom, and abandons <s>karmas</s>. Through the abandonment of <s>karmas</s>, <s>saṃsāra</s> too ceases. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four types of persons: some have tendencies that are neither deep nor sharp, some have sharp but not deep tendencies, some have both deep and sharp tendencies, and some have neither deep nor sharp tendencies.' The first, who has intense tendencies (<s>adhimātrānuśaya</s>), comes from time to time. The next, who has mild and middling tendencies, always comes and remains fixed in mind. The third, who has intense tendencies, also comes and remains fixed in mind. The fourth, who has mild and middling tendencies, comes only occasionally. If he correctly hears the <s>śāstra</s> in the teaching of the Blessed One, he abandons both kinds of tendencies known as sharp and deep.

body.text: bhagavaddharmasya samyagarthaṃ yo vetti | tasya nātmavyābādhā na paravyābādhā bhavati | tīrthikāḥśīlamātradhāriṇaḥ svakāyameva vyābādhante | nāsti puṇyapāpaṃ [nāsti] karmaphalamiti mithyādṛṣṭau yaḥ patati saparāneva vyābādhate | yaddānamācarati sa ātmānamapi vyābādhate parānapi vyābādhate | yathādhvare bahavaḥ paśavo hanyante | yastu bhagavaddharmasyārthaṃ vetti | sa hitameva kurvan nātmānaṃ byābādhate | nāpi parān | yathā dhyānasamādhimaitrīkaruṇānāṃ lābhī | ato 'bhyasitavyamidaṃ bhagavacchāsanaśāstram |
body.translated_text: One who correctly understands the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One — for him there is neither self-affliction nor affliction of others. The <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretical teachers), who merely observe moral conduct, afflict only their own bodies. One who holds the wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) that there is no merit or sin, that there is no fruit of <s>karma</s> — he afflicts others. One who practices giving in that manner afflicts both himself and others — just as in a sacrifice (<s>adhvara</s>), many animals are slaughtered. But one who understands the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One, performing only what is beneficial, afflicts neither himself nor others — just as one who obtains the <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>samādhis</s>, loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). Therefore this <s>śāstra</s> on the teaching of the Blessed One should be studied.

body.text: etacchāsrābhyāsī samyagarthaveditvāt kathyo bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre kathāsamprayogeṇa [pudgalo] veditavyo yadi vā kathyo yadi vākathya iti | yo viduṣāṃ dharmaṃ pṛṣṭhaḥ sthānāsthāne na santiṣṭhati | parikalpe na santiṣṭhati | pratipadāyāṃ na santiṣṭhati | ayamakathyo bhavati | tadviparītaḥ kathya iti | viduṣāṃ dharme na tiṣṭhatīti | vādī samyak prajñānenārthagatiṃ jñātvā paścātprayogamādatte | so 'syājñatvāt na grāhyaḥ | yathā nāthaputrādayaḥ svayaṃ vadanti asmākaṃ śāstā āptaḥ tadvacanamevānuvartāmaha iti | sthānāsthāne na santiṣṭhatīti | hetuprayoge na tiṣṭhati | tīrthikādīnāṃ dvidhā hetuḥ sādhāraṇahetuḥ viśeṣaheturiti | pareṇa sādhāraṇahetāvukte asādhāraṇahetunā prativadanti | asādhāraṇahetāvukte sādhāraṇahetunā prativadanti | evaṃ dvividhahetāvapi na tiṣṭhanti | parikalpe na santiṣṭhati iti | dṛṣṭānte na
body.translated_text: One who studies this <s>śāstra</s>, because he correctly understands the meaning, becomes fit for discourse. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'By the mode of discourse, a person is to be known — whether he is fit for discourse or unfit for discourse.' One who, when questioned about the <s>Dharma</s> by the learned, does not stand firm on proper and improper grounds, does not stand firm in his thesis, and does not stand firm in the method of practice — he is unfit for discourse. One who is the opposite is fit for discourse. 'Does not stand firm in the <s>Dharma</s> of the learned' means: a debater, having correctly known the meaning through wisdom, thereafter undertakes the method [of argument]. Because of his ignorance, he is not to be accepted — just as <s>Nāthaputra</s> (Jain Mahāvīra) and others who themselves say: 'Our teacher is an authority; we merely follow his words.' 'Does not stand firm on proper and improper grounds' means: he does not stand firm in the method of reasoning. The <s>tīrthikas</s> and others have two kinds of reasoning — general reasoning (<s>sādhāraṇahetu</s>) and specific reasoning (<s>viśeṣahetu</s>). When the opponent states a general reason, they respond with a specific reason. When the opponent states a specific reason, they respond with a general reason. Thus they do not stand firm in either type of reasoning. 'Does not stand firm in his thesis' means: he does not stand firm in his example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>).

body.text: tiṣṭhati | pratipadāyāṃ na santiṣṭhatīti | vādapaddhatau na tiṣṭhati | yathā ha- mā paruṣavacanamuccāraya | mā tyaja pratijñārtham | yatnenopāyaṃ śikṣaya saṃvillābhāya | ātmano vā mānasikī tuṣṭhiḥ āryapravacanadharmaḥ iti | tatra yo bhagavaddharma samyak jñātvā pravakti sa kathyo bhavati | nānye |
body.translated_text: 'Does not stand firm in the method of practice' means: he does not stand firm in the method of debate. As it is said: 'Do not utter harsh words. Do not abandon the object of your thesis. Learn skillful means with diligence for the attainment of consensus. Self-satisfaction of the mind is the <s>Dharma</s> of the noble discourse.' Therein, one who correctly knows the <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One and then expounds it — he is fit for discourse. Others are not.

body.text: akathya iti | ya [ekāṃśa]vyākaraṇīyaṃ praśnaṃ nai[kāṃśena] vyākaroti | vibhajya vyākaraṇīyaṃ praśnaṃ na vibhajya vyākaroti | pratipṛcchāvyākaraṇīyaṃ praśnaṃ na patipṛcchya vyākaroti sthapanīyaṃ praśnaṃ na sthapayitvā vyākaroti | tadviparītaḥ kathyaḥ | ekāṃśa vyākaraṇīyaḥ praśna iti | [tatra] eka eva heturasti | [tena] yathā buddho bhagavān [tathā] loke nāsti tatsama itīdṛśamanumānaṃ bhavati | vibhajyavyākaraṇīyaḥ praśna iti | punarasti kāraṇaṃ [vibhajya vyākaraṇasya] | yathā mṛtasantānādayaḥ [punarutpatsyant] iti | paripṛcchāvyākaraṇīyaḥ praśna iti | yathā kaścitpṛcchati | anyaḥ punaḥ paripṛcchaya vyākaroti | sthapanīyaḥ praśna iti yo dharmo 'bhūtarūpaḥ kintu prajñaptisan | sa dharmaḥ kimekaḥ uta nānā, kiṃ śāśvataḥ utāśāśvata ityādi yadi kaścit pṛcchati | nāyamartho vyākaraṇīyaḥ | bhagavacchāsanasya vettā kevalaṃ tat vetti | tasmādabhyasitavyamidaṃ bhagavacchāsanaśāsram |
body.translated_text: 'Unfit for discourse' means: one who does not answer a question requiring a categorical answer (<s>ekāṃśavyākaraṇīya</s>) categorically; does not answer a question requiring an analytical answer (<s>vibhajyavyākaraṇīya</s>) analytically; does not answer a question requiring a counter-question (<s>pratipṛcchāvyākaraṇīya</s>) with a counter-question; does not set aside a question to be set aside (<s>sthāpanīya</s>). One who is the opposite is fit for discourse. A question requiring a categorical answer: therein only one reason exists, [and therefore] such an inference as 'As the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, there is no equal in the world' is made. A question requiring an analytical answer: there is further a reason [to answer analytically], as in the case of 'those in the continuity of the dead will be reborn again.' A question requiring a counter-question: as when someone asks and another answers by posing a counter-question. A question to be set aside: a <s>dharma</s> that has no real existence but is a mere designation — whether that <s>dharma</s> is one or many, whether it is eternal or non-eternal, and so forth — if someone asks such a question, this matter is not to be answered. Only one who knows the teaching of the Blessed One understands this. Therefore this <s>śāstra</s> on the teaching of the Blessed One should be studied.

body.text: kiñca santi caturvidhāḥ puruṣāḥ- sāvadyaḥ badyabahulaḥ alpāvadyaḥ anavadya iti | sāvadya iti yasya kevalamakuśalaṃ naiko 'pi kuśaladharmo 'sti | vadyabahula iti | yasyākuśalaṃ bahu kuśalamalpam | alpavadya iti | yasya kuśalaṃ bahu akuśalamalpam |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, there are four types of persons: one who is blameworthy (<s>sāvadya</s>), one who is predominantly blameworthy (<s>vadyabahula</s>), one who has little blame (<s>alpāvadya</s>), and one who is blameless (<s>anavadya</s>). 'Blameworthy' means one who has only unwholesome qualities and not a single wholesome <s>dharma</s>. 'Predominantly blameworthy' means one who has much unwholesome and little wholesome. 'Of little blame' means one who has much wholesome and little unwholesome.

body.text: anavadya iti | yasya kuśaladharmamātraṃ nākuśalam | bhagavacchāsanasya samyagarthavedī dvaividhyaṃ bhajate alpavadyo 'navadya iti |
body.translated_text: 'Blameless' means one who has only wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and nothing unwholesome. One who correctly understands the meaning of the teaching of the Blessed One partakes of twofold [status] — one of little blame and one who is blameless.

body.text: atha yo bhagavacchāsanasyārthaṃ vetti | tasya duḥkhavedanā parimitā | sa hi nirvāṇamavaśyaṃ prāpsyati ||
body.translated_text: Now, one who understands the meaning of the Blessed One's teaching — his experience of suffering is limited. He will certainly attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: śāstrapraśaṃsāvargaḥ pañcadaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the fifteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Praise of the Treatise (<s>śāstrapraśaṃsāvarga</s>).

body.text: 16 caturdharmavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 16. Chapter on the Four <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>caturdharmavarga</s>)

body.text: athaitacchāsrābhyāsī uttamaṃ saṅgrahadharmaṃ vindate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- catvāri saṅgrahavastūni- dānaṃ priyavacanamarthacaryā samānārthatā iti | dānam annavastrādīnām | dhanadānena saṃgṛhītāḥ sattvāḥ punarvikampyā bhavanti | priyavacanam yathāpriprāyaṃ bhāṣaṇam | idamapi duṣṭameva | tasyābhiprāyasya [svīyatayā] grahaṇāt | arthacarcā parārthaṃ hitākāṃkṣaṇam | yat sahetupratyayamanyasya kāryasiddhiṃ karoti | idamapi prakampyaṃ bhavati | samānārthatā | yathā śoke mode ca [pareṇa] sahaikībhavanam | iyaṃ samānārthatā | idaṃ kadācitprakampyam | yadi kaścit dharmadānapriyavacanārthacaryāsamānārthatābhiḥ sattvān saṅgṛhṇāti | tadā te sattvā na prakampyā bhavanti | dharmeṇa saṅgraho yadutaitacchāstrābhyāsaḥ | ato yatnena śikṣitavyam |
body.translated_text: Now, one who studies this treatise obtains the supreme <s>dharma</s> of gathering (<s>saṅgrahadharma</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four means of gathering (<s>saṅgrahavastu</s>): giving (<s>dāna</s>), kind speech (<s>priyavacana</s>), beneficial conduct (<s>arthacaryā</s>), and impartiality (<s>samānārthatā</s>).' Giving is of food, clothing, and the like. Beings gathered through the giving of wealth may later waver. Kind speech is speaking according to one's wishes. This too is defective, because one accepts [another's] intention as one's own. Beneficial conduct is the wish for the welfare of others — that which brings about the accomplishment of another's purpose through proper causes and conditions. This too may be shaken. Impartiality means sharing alike with others in grief and joy. This is impartiality. This may sometimes be shaken. If someone gathers beings through <s>Dharma</s>-giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and impartiality, then those beings cannot be shaken. Gathering through <s>Dharma</s> means the study of this very treatise. Therefore one should learn it with diligence.

body.text: etacchāstramabhyasan uttamaṃ śaraṇaṃ labhate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dharmapratiśaraṇena bhavitavyam na pudgalapratiśaraṇeneti | yadyapi kaścidevaṃ vadet mayā bhagavataḥ sammukhāt śrutaṃ bhadantaśca sammukhādvā pūrvānte śrutamiti | tasyāśraddheyatvāt na tadvavacanamādeyam | yadvacanantu sūtre 'vatīrṇaṃ dharmalakṣaṇāviruddhaṃ vinayānuloimitañca tatpunarādeyaṃ syāt iti | sūtre 'vatīrṇamiti yat nītārthasūtre 'vatīrṇam | nītārthasūtrañca yasyārthagatirdharmalakṣaṇāviruddhā | dharmalakṣaṇañca yadvinayānulomakam | vinayaśca saṃvaraḥ | tadyathā kaścit saṃskṛtadharmāḥ śāśvatāḥ
body.translated_text: One who studies this treatise obtains the supreme refuge. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One should take <s>Dharma</s> as one's refuge, not persons.' Even if someone were to say: 'I heard this directly from the Blessed One,' or 'The Elder heard it directly, or it was heard in the past' — because of its unreliability, his words should not be accepted. But whatever speech is found in the <s>sūtras</s>, is not contradicted by the marks of <s>Dharma</s>, and accords with the <s>Vinaya</s> — that should be accepted. 'Found in the <s>sūtras</s>' means found in <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning (<s>nītārthasūtra</s>). A <s>sūtra</s> of definitive meaning is one whose purport is not contradicted by the marks of <s>Dharma</s>. The marks of <s>Dharma</s> are what accords with the <s>Vinaya</s>. And the <s>Vinaya</s> is moral restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). For example, when someone contemplates that conditioned <s>dharmas</s> are permanent,

body.text: sukhāḥ sātmāna iti bhāvayati | sa na kāmādīn prajahāti | anityā duḥkhā anātmāna iti yo bhāvayati | sa kāmādīn prajahāti | anityatādijñānameva dharmalakṣaṇam dharmo 'yaṃ śaraṇīkartavyo na pudgalāḥ |
body.translated_text: pleasant, and possessed of self — he does not abandon desires and the rest. But one who contemplates them as impermanent, suffering, and without self — he abandons desires and the rest. The knowledge of impermanence and so forth is itself the mark of <s>Dharma</s>. This <s>Dharma</s> should be taken as refuge, not persons.

body.text: dharmapratiśaraṇaṃ vadatā sarve dharmāḥ saṅgṛhītā bhavanti | ataḥ punarucyate nitārthasūtrapratiśaraṇena bhavitavyaṃ na neyārthasūtrapratiśaraṇeneti | nītārthasūtrameva tṛtīyaṃ pratiśaraṇam | yaducyate arthapratiśaraṇena bhavitavyaṃ na vyañjanapratiśareṇa iti | yo 'yaṃ vyañjanārthaḥ sūtre 'vatīrṇo dharmalakṣaṇāvirodhī vinayānulomakaśca tatpratiśaraṇena bhavitavyam | jñānapratiśaraṇena bhavitavyaṃ na vijñānapratiśaraṇena iti | [vijñānaṃ] yat rūpādivijñānam | yathoktaṃ sūtre vijānātīti vijñānam | iti | jñānaṃ nāma yathābhūtadharmābhisamayaḥ | yathoktaṃ- rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti jñānam | śūnyataiva yathābhūtam | ato yadvijñānapratilabdham, na tatpratiśaraṇena bhavitavyam | yā jñānapratiśaraṇatā saiva śūnyatāpratiśaraṇatā | tāmuttamapratiśaraṇatāṃ prativedhitukāmena idaṃ śāstramabhyasitavyam |
body.translated_text: By declaring <s>Dharma</s> as the refuge, all <s>dharmas</s> are encompassed. Therefore it is further said: 'One should take <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning (<s>nītārthasūtra</s>) as one's refuge, not <s>sūtras</s> of provisional meaning (<s>neyārthasūtra</s>).' The <s>sūtra</s> of definitive meaning is itself the third refuge. When it is said: 'One should take the meaning (<s>artha</s>) as one's refuge, not the letter (<s>vyañjana</s>)' — whatever meaning of the letter is found in the <s>sūtras</s>, is not contradicted by the marks of <s>Dharma</s>, and accords with the <s>Vinaya</s> — that should be taken as refuge. 'One should take knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) as one's refuge, not consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).' Consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the consciousness of form and so forth. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'It cognizes, therefore it is called consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).' Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the realization of <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are (<s>yathābhūtadharmābhisamaya</s>). As stated: 'One who truly knows form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — that is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).' Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) alone is reality as it truly is. Therefore, what is obtained through consciousness should not be taken as refuge. The taking of knowledge as refuge is itself the taking of emptiness as refuge. One who wishes to penetrate that supreme refuge should study this treatise.

body.text: uktañca sūtre- catvāri devamanuṣyāṇāṃ cakrāṇi śubhavardhakāni | pratirūpadeśavāsaḥ satparuṣopāśrayaḥ ātmanaḥ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ pūrve ca kṛtapuṇyatā | iti | pratirūpadeśavāso nāma yat pañcadūṣaṇavivikto madhyadeśaḥ | satpuruṣopāśrayo yat buddhādhvani janmanā saṅgamaḥ | pūrve ca kṛtapuṇyatā nāma yat bādhiryamūkatādyabhāvaḥ | ātmanaḥ samyak praṇidhānaṃ nāma samyak darśanamidam | samyak darśanañcāvaśryaṃbhagavacchāsanaśravaṇādutpadyate ityata idaṃ samyacchāsanaśāstramabhyasitavyam |
body.translated_text: It is also stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four wheels (<s>cakra</s>) that increase the virtue of gods and humans: dwelling in a suitable place (<s>pratirūpadeśavāsa</s>), reliance on good persons (<s>satpuruṣopāśraya</s>), proper self-determination (<s>ātmanaḥ samyakpraṇidhāna</s>), and having previously accumulated merit (<s>pūrve kṛtapuṇyatā</s>).' Dwelling in a suitable place means the middle country free from the five corruptions. Reliance on good persons means being born during the time of a <s>Buddha</s>'s dispensation. Having previously accumulated merit means the absence of deafness, muteness, and the like. Proper self-determination means right view. And right view necessarily arises from hearing the Blessed One's teaching — therefore this treatise of right teaching should be studied.

body.text: asya śāstrasyādhyetā cāsminnevāyuṣi satyaprativedhākhyaṃ mahāsārārthaṃ labhate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- catvāraḥ sāradharmāḥ vacanasāraḥ samādhisāro darśanasāro vimuktisāra iti |
body.translated_text: The student of this treatise, in this very lifetime, obtains the great essential benefit called the penetration of truth (<s>satyaprativedha</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four essential <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sāradharma</s>): the essence of speech (<s>vacanasāra</s>), the essence of concentration (<s>samādhisāra</s>), the essence of vision (<s>darśanasāra</s>), and the essence of liberation (<s>vimuktisāra</s>).'

body.text: vacanasāra iti | sarve saṃskṛtā anityā duḥkhāḥ, sarve anātmānaḥ śāntaṃ nirodho nirvāṇamiti yadvacanam | ayaṃ vacanasāraḥ śrutamayaprajñāparipūraṇamityākhyāyate | imamupādāya pratilabdhaḥ samādhiścintāmayaprajñāparipūraṇamityucyate | imaṃ samādhimupādāya saṃskṛtadharmā anityā duḥkhāḥ ityādi bhāvanā samyagdarśanaprāpiṇī bhāvanāmayaprajñāparipūraṇamityucyate | prajñātrittayapratilabdhaṃ phalaṃ vimuktisāra ityākhyāyate |
body.translated_text: The essence of speech (<s>vacanasāra</s>) is the statement: 'All conditioned things are impermanent and suffering; all are without self; cessation is peace — <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' This is the essence of speech, and it is called the fulfillment of wisdom born of learning (<s>śrutamayaprajñā</s>). The <s>samādhi</s> obtained on the basis of this is called the fulfillment of wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayaprajñā</s>). On the basis of this <s>samādhi</s>, the contemplation that conditioned <s>dharmas</s> are impermanent, suffering, and so forth, which leads to right view, is called the fulfillment of wisdom born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayaprajñā</s>). The fruit obtained through the threefold wisdom (<s>prajñātraya</s>) is called the essence of liberation (<s>vimuktisāra</s>).

body.text: atha yaḥ śṛṇoti bhagavacchāsanasya samyacchāsram, sa mahāntamarthaṃ labhate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- catvāro mahārthadharmāḥ satpuruṣasaṃsevā, saddharmaśravaṇaṃ, yoniśo manaskāraḥ dharmānudharmapratipattiriti | yaḥ satpuruṣamupāste sa saddharmaṃ śṛṇoti | asya saddharmasya satpuruṣavartitvāt | śrutasaddharmā san yoniśo manaskāramutpādya anityādinā dharmān samyagbhāvayati | anayā bhāvanayā dharmānudharmaṃ pratipadyate yadutānāsravaṃ darśanam |
body.translated_text: Now, one who hears the true teaching of the Blessed One's dispensation obtains great benefit. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four <s>dharmas</s> of great benefit (<s>mahārthadharma</s>): association with good persons (<s>satpuruṣasaṃsevā</s>), hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharmaśravaṇa</s>), wise attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>), and practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānudharmapratipatti</s>).' One who attends upon good persons hears the true <s>Dharma</s>, because the true <s>Dharma</s> abides among good persons. Having heard the true <s>Dharma</s>, one generates wise attention and rightly contemplates <s>dharmas</s> as impermanent and so forth. Through this contemplation, one practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> — that is, undefiled insight (<s>anāsrava darśana</s>).

body.text: etacchāstraṃ śṛṇvataścatvāri guṇādhiṣṭhānāni bhavanti- prajñādhiṣṭhānaṃ, satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ, tyāgādhiṣṭhānaṃ, upaśamādhiṣṭhānamiti | dharmaśravaṇātprajñā bhavatīti prajñādhiṣṭhānam | anayā prajñayā paramārthaśūnyatāṃ paśyatīti satyādhiṣṭhānam | śūnyatādarśanena kleśānāṃ viyogaṃ labhata iti tyāgādhiṣṭhānam | kleśānāṃ kṣayācittamupaśāmyatīdamupaśamādhiṣṭhānam |
body.translated_text: One who hears this treatise acquires four bases of virtue (<s>guṇādhiṣṭhāna</s>): the basis of wisdom (<s>prajñādhiṣṭhāna</s>), the basis of truth (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), the basis of relinquishment (<s>tyāgādhiṣṭhāna</s>), and the basis of tranquility (<s>upaśamādhiṣṭhāna</s>). The basis of wisdom: through hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, wisdom arises. The basis of truth: through this wisdom, one sees the ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>). The basis of relinquishment: through seeing emptiness, one obtains separation from defilements (<s>kleśa</s>). The basis of tranquility: through the destruction of defilements, the mind becomes tranquil.

body.text: kiñca bhagavacchāsanasya samyacchāstraṃ śrutavataścatvāri nirvāṇagāmini kuśalamūlāni aṅkurībhavanti yaduta ūṣmadharmo mūrdhadharmaḥ kṣāntidharmo laukikāgradharma iti | anityādyākāreṇa pañcaskandhān bhāvayato 'varaṃ mṛdu nirvāṇagāmi kuśalamūlaṃ cittasyoṣmakaramutpadyate | ayamūṣmadharma ityucyate | uṣmadharmasaṃvardhitaṃ madhyaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ mūrdhadharma ityākhyāyate | mūrdhadharmasaṃvardhitamuttamaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ kṣāntidharma ityucyate | kṣāntisaṃvardhitamuttamottamaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ laukikāgradharma ityabhidhīyate |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, for one who has heard the true teaching of the Blessed One's dispensation, four wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> sprout forth — namely, the <s>dharma</s> of warmth (<s>uṣmadharma</s>), the <s>dharma</s> of the summit (<s>mūrdhadharma</s>), the <s>dharma</s> of patience (<s>kṣāntidharma</s>), and the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>). When one contemplates the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) with the aspect of impermanence and so forth, the lowest and softest wholesome root that warms the mind toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s> arises — this is called the <s>dharma</s> of warmth. The middling wholesome root nurtured by the <s>dharma</s> of warmth is called the <s>dharma</s> of the summit. The superior wholesome root nurtured by the <s>dharma</s> of the summit is called the <s>dharma</s> of patience. The supremely superior wholesome root nurtured by patience is called the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: santi ca catvāri kuśalamūlāni- hānabhāgīyaṃ, sthitibhāgīyaṃ, viśeṣabhāgīyaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyamiti | dhyānasamādhipūjanavandanastotrādikuśalamūlānāṃ hānaṃ hānabhāgīyam | dhyānasamādhyādikuśalamūlānāṃ pratilābhaḥ sthitibhāgīyam | śravaṇacintanādibhya utpannāni
body.translated_text: There are also four kinds of wholesome roots: that pertaining to decline (<s>hānabhāgīya</s>), that pertaining to stability (<s>sthitibhāgīya</s>), that pertaining to distinction (<s>viśeṣabhāgīya</s>), and that pertaining to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). The decline of wholesome roots such as <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, worship, prostration, hymns, and the like is the portion pertaining to decline. The attainment of wholesome roots such as <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, and the like is the portion pertaining to stability. [Those] arising from hearing, reflection, and so forth —

body.text: kuśalamūlāni viśeṣabhāgīyam | anāsravaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyam | yastathāgatasya dharmaṃ śṛṇoti sa hānabhāgīyaṃ visaṃyujya trīṇi kuśalamūlāni pratilabhate ||
body.translated_text: — are wholesome roots pertaining to distinction. Undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) wholesome roots pertain to penetration. One who hears the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, being separated from the portion pertaining to decline, obtains the [remaining] three wholesome roots.

body.text: caturdharmavargaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the sixteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Four <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>caturdharmavarga</s>).

body.text: 17 catussatyavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 17. Chapter on the Four Noble Truths (<s>catussatyavarga</s>)

body.text: atha yastāthāgatadharmaṃ śṛṇoti sa catussatyāni savibhaṅgāni samprajānāti duḥkhasatyaṃ, samudayasatyaṃ, nirodhasatyaṃ mārgasatyamiti | duḥkhasatyamiti yat traidhātukam, kāmadhātuḥ avīcinarakāt yāvatparanirmitavaśavartino devān | rūpadhātuḥ ābrahmalokāt ācākaniṣṭhāt devalokāt | ārūpyadhātuścatvāri arūpadhyānāni |
body.translated_text: Now, one who hears the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully comprehends the Four Noble Truths (<s>catussatya</s>) with their subdivisions: the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), the truth of the origin (<s>samudayasatya</s>), the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>), and the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>). The truth of suffering is the triple world (<s>traidhātuka</s>): the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), from <s>Avīci</s> hell up to the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods; the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), from <s>Brahmaloka</s> up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven; and the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>), which comprises the four formless absorptions (<s>arūpadhyāna</s>).

body.text: santi ca catasro vijñānasthitayo rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārā iti | tīrthikāḥ kecidvadanti vijñānam ātmopagā sthitiriti | ato bhagavānāha catu [skandho]pagā vijñānasthitayaḥ iti | santi ca catasro jātayaḥ- aṇḍajo jarāyujaḥ saṃsvedeja aupapāduka iti | devā nārakāḥ sarva aupapādukāḥ | pretā ubhayathā jarāyujā aupapādukāśca | anye catasṛṣu jātiṣu [antarbhūtāḥ] | catvāra āhārāḥ- kavaḍīkāra āhāraḥ audārikaḥ sūkṣmo vā | odanādiraudārika ityucyate | ghṛtatailagandhabāṣpapānādayaḥ sūkṣmāḥ | sparśāhāraḥ śītoṣṇavātādiḥ | manaḥsañcetanāhāro yat kadācit puruṣāḥ sañcetanāpraṇidhānena jīvati | vijñānāhāraḥ antarābhavikanārakārūpyā nirodhasamāpattipraviṣṭhāḥ satvā adṛṣṭavijñānā api vijñānapratilambhe vartanta ityato vijñānāhārā ityucyante |
body.translated_text: There are four stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>): form (<s>rūpa</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Certain non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthika</s>) say: 'Consciousness is [like] a self; its station is a support for the self.' Therefore the Blessed One said: 'The stations of consciousness rest upon the four aggregates (<s>skandha</s>).' There are also four kinds of birth (<s>jāti</s>): egg-born (<s>aṇḍaja</s>), womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>), moisture-born (<s>saṃsvedaja</s>), and spontaneously born (<s>aupapāduka</s>). Gods and hell-beings are all spontaneously born. Hungry ghosts (<s>preta</s>) are of both kinds — womb-born and spontaneously born. The rest are included in the four kinds of birth. There are four kinds of nutriment (<s>āhāra</s>): material food (<s>kavaḍīkāra āhāra</s>), whether coarse or subtle — rice and the like are called coarse, while ghee, oil, fragrance, vapor, drinks, and the like are subtle; contact as nutriment (<s>sparśāhāra</s>), such as cold, heat, wind, and so forth; mental volition as nutriment (<s>manaḥsañcetanāhāra</s>), whereby a person sometimes lives by volition and resolve; and consciousness as nutriment (<s>vijñānāhāra</s>) — intermediate-state beings, hell-beings, formless-realm beings, and those who have entered the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), though they have no manifest consciousness, continue to exist through the obtaining of consciousness — therefore they are called sustained by consciousness as nutriment.

body.text: ṣaṅgatayaḥ- uttamapāpaṃ narakam | madhyamapāpāstiryañcaḥ | adhamapāpāḥ pretāḥ | uttamapuṇyā devagatiḥ | madhyamapuṇyā manuṣyagatiḥ | adhamapuṇyā asuragatiḥ | kiñca ṣaṭ [bhūta]prakārāḥ- pṛthivyaptejovāvyākāśavijñānānīti | caturbhirmahābhūtaiḥ parivṛtaṃ vijñānamadhyakamākāśaṃ
body.translated_text: There are six destinies (<s>gati</s>): the supreme evil [destiny] is hell (<s>naraka</s>); the middling evil [destiny] is [rebirth as] animals (<s>tiryañc</s>); the lesser evil [destiny] is [rebirth as] hungry ghosts (<s>preta</s>); the supreme meritorious [destiny] is the divine realm (<s>devagati</s>); the middling meritorious [destiny] is the human realm (<s>manuṣyagati</s>); the lesser meritorious [destiny] is the <s>Asura</s> realm. Furthermore, there are six kinds of elements (<s>bhūta</s>): earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), water (<s>ap</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), wind (<s>vāyu</s>), space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Consciousness surrounded by the four great elements, with space as the central [element],

body.text: puruṣa iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | ṣaṭ sparśāyatanāni cakṣurādīni ṣaḍindriyāṇi vijñānasaṅgatāni sparśāyatanamityākhyāyante |
body.translated_text: is reckoned as a 'person' (<s>puruṣa</s>). The six bases of contact (<s>sparśāyatana</s>) — the six sense faculties beginning with the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) — when conjoined with consciousness, are called bases of contact.

body.text: saptavijñānasthitayaḥ | āsu sthitiṣu viparyayabalāt vijñānaṃ sābhirāmaṃ tiṣṭhati |
body.translated_text: There are seven stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>). In these stations, consciousness abides with delight due to the power of false views (<s>viparyaya</s>).

body.text: aṣṭau lokadharmāḥ- lābho 'lābho yaśo 'yaśo nindā praśaṃsā sukhaṃ duḥkhamiti | puruṣā loke sthitā avaśyabhimānupādadate | ityato lokadharmā ityucyante |
body.translated_text: There are eight worldly conditions (<s>lokadharmāḥ</s>): gain (<s>lābha</s>) and loss (<s>alābha</s>), fame (<s>yaśas</s>) and infamy (<s>ayaśas</s>), blame (<s>nindā</s>) and praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and pain (<s>duḥkha</s>). Persons dwelling in the world inevitably take up pride (<s>abhimāna</s>). Therefore they are called worldly conditions.

body.text: nava sattvāvāsāḥ | sattvāḥ sarve viṣayabalādeṣu vasanti |
body.translated_text: There are nine abodes of beings (<s>sattvāvāsa</s>). All beings dwell in these by the power of sense-objects.

body.text: sarve ca dharmāḥ pañcadhā vikalpyante- pañca skandhāḥ dvādaśāyatanāni aṣṭādaśa dhātavo dvādaśa nidānāni dvāviṃśatirindriyāṇi iti | cakṣurvijñaptirūpaṃ rūpaskandhaḥ | tatpratītyoptannaṃ vijñānaṃ yatpurovartirūpagrāhakaṃ sa vijñānaskandhaḥ | yat cittaṃ strī puruṣaḥ śatrubandhurityādisaṃjñāṃ janayati | sa saṃjñāskandhaḥ | śatrurbandhurmadhyastha iti yat puruṣaṃ vikalpayati tat tisro vedanā janayati | ayaṃ vedanāskandhaḥ | āsu tisṛṣu vedanāsu yat trividhāḥ kleśā utpadyante | sa saṃskāraskandhaḥ | eṣāṃ pravṛttyā kāyopādānānyupādatta iti pañcopādānaskandhā ityucyante |
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are classified in five ways: the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), the twelve sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), the eighteen elements (<s>dhātu</s>), the twelve links of dependent origination (<s>nidāna</s>), and the twenty-two faculties (<s>indriya</s>). Visual cognition of form is the form aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>). The consciousness arisen dependent upon it, which grasps the form presented before it, is the consciousness aggregate (<s>vijñānaskandha</s>). That which generates the mind's designation of 'woman,' 'man,' 'enemy,' 'kinsman,' and so forth is the perception aggregate (<s>saṃjñāskandha</s>). That which classifies a person as 'enemy,' 'kinsman,' or 'neutral' generates three kinds of feeling — this is the feeling aggregate (<s>vedanāskandha</s>). In these three feelings, the three kinds of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) that arise constitute the formations aggregate (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>). Through the activity of these, one appropriates the bases of the body — therefore they are called the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>).

body.text: caturbhiḥ pratyayai vijñānamutpadyate yaduta hetupratyayaḥ samanantarapratyaya ālambanapratyayo
body.translated_text: Consciousness arises from four conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>): the causal condition (<s>hetupratyaya</s>), the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), the object condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>),

body.text: 'dhipatipratyayaśceti | karma hetupratyayaḥ | vijñānaṃ samanantarapratyayaḥ | vijñānasamanantaraṃ vijñānasya jāyamānatvāt | rūpamālambanapratyayaḥ | cakṣu[rādi]radhipatipratyayaḥ | tatra vijñānaṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate yat cakṣuḥrūpaṃ yāvanmano dharmān | imāni dvādaśāyatanāni bhavanti | tatra vijñānayojanayā aṣṭādaśa dhātavo bhavanti | cakṣurdhātuḥ rūpadhātuścakṣuvijñānadhātuḥ ityādi |
