You say: 'Because the seeing of ultimate wisdom is opposed to wrong inclination, that itself is the abandonment of desire-and-passion.' But wrong inclination is the cultivation of what is unreal. Therefore it is said that the abandonment of desire-and-passion through wisdom is the abandonment of form. But ultimate wisdom is the contemplation of impermanence. As for what you say — 'In dreams, what is existent is seen' — that is incorrect. Just as in a dream, [one sees oneself] falling from a wall — one does not actually fall. Therefore there exists knowledge of the non-existent. But it is not the case that wherever knowledge operates, that constitutes the mark of existence.

body.text: daśasu vādeṣu ādyasattālakṣaṇavarga ekonaviṃśaḥ
body.translated_text: Among the ten debates, this is the nineteenth chapter, the first chapter on the Characteristic of Existence (<s>sattālakṣaṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 20 asattālakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: 20. The Characteristic of Non-Existence (<s>asattālakṣaṇa</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) yadi nāstīdaṃ sallakṣaṇam | skandhadhātvāyatanasaṅgṛhītairdharmaiḥ bhavitavyamastīti | (u) tadapi na yuktam | kasmāt | ayaṃ vādī vadati- skandhadhātvāyatanasaṅgṛhītaṃ vastu pṛthagjanadharmo na dharmalakṣaṇānugatam | tathā cet tathatādayo 'saṃskṛtadharmā api santaḥ syuḥ | iti kecidvadeyuḥ | vastutastu asantaste | ato jñāyate skandhadhātvāyatanasaṅgṛhītā dharmā na sallakṣaṇā iti |
body.translated_text: (Objection) If this is not a characteristic of existence, then one must accept that <s>dharmas</s> comprised in the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) exist. (Reply) That too is not correct. Why? This disputant says that things comprised in the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases are a worldling's conception (<s>pṛthagjanadharma</s>) and do not accord with the marks of <s>Dharma</s>. If that were so, then <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and other unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>asaṃskṛtadharma</s>) would also exist — so some might say. But in reality, they do not exist. Therefore it is known that <s>dharmas</s> comprised in the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases do not have the characteristic of existence.

body.text: (pṛ) yat puruṣasya pratyakṣajñānādinā astyupalabhyamiti śraddhā bhavati tatsallakṣaṇam | (u) tadapi na sallakṣaṇam | ayaṃ śraddheyadharmo niyatavikalparūpo noalapabhyavacanaḥ | āha ca sūtram- jñānapratiśaraṇena bhavitavyaṃ na vijñānapratiśaraṇena iti | svabhāvalabdhatvāt rūpādayo viṣayā nopalambhanīyā iti paścādvakṣyate | ime 'sallakṣaṇāḥ santo [vastuto] nāpohyante | astitayopalambhalakṣaṇaṃ kathaṃ sthāpyeta | (pṛ) bhāvadharmayogādastītyucyate | (u) bhāvaśca paścāddūṣayiṣyate | nahyasti bhāve bhāvaḥ | kathaṃ bhāvadharmayogādastīti |
body.translated_text: (Objection) That which a person believes to be apprehended through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣajñāna</s>) and other [means of knowledge] — that is the characteristic of existence. (Reply) That too is not a characteristic of existence. This trustworthy <s>dharma</s> has the nature of determined conceptualization and is not to be stated as 'apprehended.' As the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'One should take knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) as one's refuge, not consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).' Because they are obtained through their own nature, objects such as form and the rest are not to be apprehended — this will be explained later. These, having the characteristic of non-existence, are [in reality] not negated. How then could the characteristic of apprehension as 'existence' be established? (Objection) Because of the connection with the quality of being (<s>bhāvadharma</s>), it is said to 'exist.' (Reply) 'Being' (<s>bhāva</s>) too will be refuted later. For indeed there is no 'being' in being. How then could it be said to 'exist' because of a connection with the quality of being?

body.text: pratītyasamutpannatvāddhāvalakṣaṇaṃ niyatavikalparūpaṃ nopalabhyavacanam | lokasatyamātrato 'sti na paramārthataḥ |
body.translated_text: Because they are dependently originated (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), the characteristic of being has the nature of determined conceptualization and is not to be stated as 'apprehended.' It exists only from the standpoint of conventional truth (<s>lokasatya</s>), not from the standpoint of ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadi lokasatyato 'sti | tadā punarvaktavyaṃ lokasatyato 'tīto 'nāgataśca kimasti uta nāsti iti | (u) nāsti | kasmāt | ye rūpādayaḥ skandhā vartamānādhvagatāḥ, te sakāritrā upalabhyajñānadarśanāḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- rūpyata iti rūpalakṣaṇam iti | yadvartamānādhvagataṃ tat rūpyate nātītamanāgataṃ vā | tathā vedanādayo 'pi | ato jñāyate vartamānamātre santi pañca skandhāḥ | nādhvadvaye santi | atha yo dharmaḥ kāritravihīnaḥ sa svalakṣaṇavihīnaḥ | yadyatīto vahnirna dahati | na sa vahnirityākhyāyate | tathā vijñānamapi, yadyatītaṃ na vijānāti na tadvijñānamityucyate | yannirhetukaṃ tadastīti na yujyate | atīto dharmo nirhetukaḥ, so 'stīti na yujyate | atha prākṛtāḥ santo dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ | yathā asti pṛthivī, santi bījasalilādayaḥ pratyayāḥ, tadā aṅkurādikamutpadyate | patralekhinīpuruṣakāreṣu satsu sidhyatyakṣaram | dvayordharmayoḥ samavāye vijñānamutpadyate | anāgate 'dhvani aṅkurākṣaravijñānādīnāṃ kāraṇāni asamavetāni | kathaṃ santīti labhyante | ato 'dhvadvayamasatsyāt |
body.translated_text: (Objection) If it exists from the standpoint of conventional truth, then it must further be asked: from the standpoint of conventional truth, do the past and future exist or not? (Reply) They do not exist. Why? The aggregates such as form and the rest belonging to the present time-period have causal efficacy (<s>kāritra</s>) and are apprehended through knowledge and vision. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'That which is formed — that is the characteristic of form.' What belongs to the present time-period is formed, not what is past or future. Likewise for feeling and the rest. Therefore it is known that the five aggregates exist only in the present moment — they do not exist in the two [other] time-periods. Now, a <s>dharma</s> that lacks causal efficacy lacks its own characteristic. If past fire does not burn, it is not called fire. Likewise, consciousness — if past, it does not cognize, and therefore it is not called consciousness. What is without cause cannot be said to exist — a past <s>dharma</s> is without cause, and therefore cannot be said to exist. Now, natural <s>dharmas</s> that exist are dependently originated. Just as when earth exists and seeds, water, and other conditions are present, then sprouts and the rest arise. When leaves, stylus, and human effort are present, letters are produced. From the conjunction of two <s>dharmas</s>, consciousness arises. In the future time-period, the causes of sprouts, letters, consciousness, and the like have not yet conjoined. How can they be obtained as existing? Therefore the two time-periods [past and future] would be non-existent.

body.text: atha yadyanāgatadharmo 'sti | tadā nityaḥ syāt | anāgatādvartamānaṃ pratyanuprāpteḥ | yathā kuṭītaḥ kuṭīmanuprāpnoti | tadā nānityaḥ syāt | na caitatsambhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- cakṣurvijñānamutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati | nirudhyamānaṃ na kvacidgacchati | iti | ato 'tītānāgatadharmau na kalpayitavyau | atha yadyanāgataṃ sat cakṣū rūpaṃ paśyati tadā sakāritraṃ syāt | tathātītamapi | na tu vastuto yujyate | ato jñāyate atītānāgatadharmo 'sanniti | [yadi]atītānāgatarūpamasti, tadā sapratighaṃ sāvaraṇañca syāt | na vastuto yujyate | ato nāsti | atha yadi ghaṭādayaḥ padārthāḥ anāgatāḥ santi | tadā kulālādayaḥ savyāpārā na bhaveyuḥ | dṛśyante tu savyāpārāḥ | ato nāstyanāgataḥ | kiñca bhagavānāhasaṃskṛtadharmā utpādavyayasthityanyathātvai strilakṣaṇā upalabhyante iti | utpāda iti yo dharmaḥ
body.translated_text: Now, if a future <s>dharma</s> exists, then it would be permanent — because it would arrive at the present from the future. Just as one goes from one house to another house — then it would not be impermanent. But this is not possible. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Eye-consciousness, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go anywhere.' Therefore, past and future <s>dharmas</s> should not be postulated. Now, if the future eye, being existent, sees form, then it would have causal efficacy — and likewise the past. But this is not [the case] in reality. Therefore it is known that past and future <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent. If past and future form exists, then it would have resistance (<s>sapratigha</s>) and be obstructive (<s>sāvaraṇa</s>). This is not [the case] in reality. Therefore it does not exist. Now, if things such as pots and the like exist in the future, then potters and the like would have no work to do. But they are seen to have work. Therefore the future does not exist. Furthermore, the Blessed One said: 'Conditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>saṃskṛtadharma</s>) are apprehended with three characteristics: arising (<s>utpāda</s>), passing away (<s>vyaya</s>), and change while persisting (<s>sthityanyathātva</s>).' 'Arising' means a <s>dharma</s> which

body.text: pūrvamabhūtvā idānīṃ savyāpāro dṛśyate | vyaya iti kṛtaḥ punarasan bhavati | sthityanyathātvam iti santatyā sthite vikaro 'nyathātvam | imāni trīṇi saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni vartamānagatāni nātītānāgatāni ||
body.translated_text: previously did not exist and now is seen with causal efficacy. 'Passing away' means what was produced again becomes non-existent. 'Change while persisting' (<s>sthityanyathātva</s>) means transformation while persisting in continuity. These three characteristics of the conditioned belong to the present — not to the past or future.

body.text: asattālakṣaṇavargo viṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twentieth chapter, the Chapter on the Characteristic of Non-Existence (<s>asattālakṣaṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 21 adhva dvayasattāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 21. Chapter on the Existence of the Two Time-Periods (<s>adhvadvayasattāvarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) vastusadatīmanāgatam | kasmāt | yo dharmo 'sti tatra cittaṃ bhavati | yathā vartamānadharmo 'saṃskṛtadharmāśca | bhagavān rūpalakṣaṇamuktvā punarāha- atītamanāgatañca rūpamiti | apicāha- yatkiñcana rūpamādhyātmikaṃ bāhyaṃ vā audārikaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vā atītamanāgataṃ pratyutpannaṃ vā [sarva]mabhisaṃkṣipya rūpaskandha iti | kiñcāha- [rūpa]manityamatītamanāgatam, kaḥ punarvādaḥ pratyutpannaṃ iti | anityaṃ hi saṃskṛtalakṣaṇam | ato 'stīti vaktavyam | dṛṣṭe jñānāt jñānamutpadyate iti paribhāvitatvāt | yathā śāleḥ śālirbhavati | ato 'tītamastīti syāt | yadi nāstyatītaṃ, phalaṃ nirhetukaṃ syāt | uktañca sūtre- yadatītaṃ vastusat hitakaraṃ tadbhagavānupadiśati | iti | kiñcāha- atītamanāgataṃ sarvamanātmānaṃ bhāvayet | iti | anāgatālambanaṃ manovijñānaṃ atītaṃ mana āśrayate | yadātītaṃ vijñānamasat, kimāśrayet | atītakarmata anāgataṃ phalamiti jñānaṃ samyagdṛṣṭiḥ | tathāgatasya daśabalānyatītānāgatakarmāṇi janayanti | tathāgataḥ svayameva vadati- yasya nāstyatītaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpakarma sa puruṣo naiva durgatau patiṣyati iti | sāsravacittavartināṃ śaikṣāṇāṃ śraddhādinyanāsravendriyāṇi na syuḥ | āryāścānāgataṃ vastu na vyavasthayā
body.translated_text: (Objection) Past and future things exist as real entities (<s>vastusat</s>). Why? Because wherever a <s>dharma</s> exists, consciousness (<s>citta</s>) arises with respect to it — just as with present <s>dharmas</s> and unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>asaṃskṛtadharma</s>). The Blessed One, having stated the characteristic of form (<s>rūpalakṣaṇa</s>), further said: 'Past and future are also form.' Furthermore, he said: 'Whatever form, whether internal or external, gross or subtle, past, future, or present — [all] of it, taken together, is the form aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>).' Furthermore, he said: '[Form] is impermanent — past and future; what need to speak of the present?' For impermanence is the characteristic of the conditioned. Therefore it must be said that [past and future] exist. Because knowledge arises from [previous] knowledge in what has been seen — this has been established. Just as from rice comes rice. Therefore, the past exists. If the past did not exist, the fruit would be without a cause. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whatever is past, existing as a real entity and beneficial — that the Blessed One teaches.' Furthermore he says: 'One should contemplate all that is past and future as without self.' Mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) that takes a future object as its support depends on a past mind (<s>manas</s>). If past consciousness were non-existent, what would it depend on? The knowledge that 'from past <s>karma</s> comes future fruit' is right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). The ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> generate [knowledge of] past and future <s>karmas</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> himself says: 'One who has no past evil <s>karma</s> — that person will never fall into a lower destiny.' For learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) who dwell in consciousness with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>), the undefiled faculties (<s>anāsravendriya</s>) beginning with faith would not exist [if past were non-existent]. And the Noble Ones would not, by established convention, predict a future entity

body.text: vyākuryaḥ | smṛtiryadi nāsti atītānāgatayoḥ tadā puruṣo nānusmaretpañcaviṣayān | kasmāt | nahi manovijñānaṃ dṛṣṭe pañca viṣayān prajānāti | kiñcāṣṭādaśa manaupavicārā atītālambanā ityucyante | yadyatītamanāgataṃ nāsti, tadā arhan na kīrtayet- ahaṃ dhyānasamādhimupasampanna iti | nahi samādhisthito vacanaṃ vakti | caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu adhicittamadhivedanañca bhāvanā na bhavet | kutaḥ | nahi pratyutpanne 'tītaṃ bhāvayatīti labhyate | catvāri samyak pradhānāni ca nābhyasyet | kutaḥ | nahyanāgatādhvagatā akuśalā dharmāḥ santi | tathānyāni trīṇyapi | yadyatītamanāgataṃ nāsti, tadā tathāgato 'san syāt | dīrghamalpakālaṃ vā śīlābhyāsaśca na syādityato na yujyate ||
body.translated_text: . If memory (<s>smṛti</s>) does not exist with respect to the past and future, then a person would not recollect the five sense-objects. Why? Because mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) does not cognize the five sense-objects in direct perception. Furthermore, the eighteen mental investigations (<s>manaupavicāra</s>) are said to have past objects as their support. If the past and future do not exist, then an <s>Arhat</s> would not proclaim: 'I have attained <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>' — for one established in <s>samādhi</s> does not utter words. In the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the cultivation of higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) and higher feeling (<s>adhivedana</s>) would not occur. Why? Because it is not possible to say 'one cultivates the past in the present.' The four right efforts (<s>samyakpradhāna</s>) also could not be practiced. Why? Because unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to the future time-period would not exist — and likewise for the other three. If the past and future do not exist, then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be non-existent. And the practice of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) for a long or short period would not exist — therefore [the non-existence of past and future] is untenable.

body.text: adhvadvayasattāvarga ekaviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-first chapter, the Chapter on the Existence of the Two Time-Periods (<s>adhvadvayasattāvarga</s>).

body.text: 22 adhvadvayanāstitāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 22. Chapter on the Non-Existence of the Two Time-Periods (<s>adhvadvayanāstitāvarga</s>)

body.text: atrocyate | atītamanāgatañca nāsti | bhavatā yadyapyuktaṃ sati dharme cittamutpadyata iti | tatpūrvameva pratyuktam | asan dharmo 'pi cittamutpādayatīti | yaducyate bhavatā- rūpalakṣaṇena rūpasaṃjñayā [atītaṃ] rūpaṃ lakṣyata iti | tadapi na yuktam | yadatītamanāgatam, tadrūpaṃ na syāt | rūpaṇābhāvāt | anityalakṣaṇamityapi na vaktavyam | bhagavān sattvānāṃ kevalamithyāsaṃjñāvikalpānuvartanāttannāma vyavaharati | bhavānāha- jñānāt jñānaṃ bhavatīti | hetuḥ phalasya hetukriyāṃ kṛtvā nirudhyate |yathā bījamaṅkurasya hetuṃ kṛtvā nirudhyate | bhagavānapyāha- asyotpādādidamutpadyata iti | bhavatoktaṃ- yat vastu sat hitakaraṃ tadbhagavānupadiśatīti | bhagavaduktaṃ vastvidaṃ prakṛtitaḥ pratyutpannakāle 'nuktamapyasti | yadi matam- atītaṃ niruddhamiti | tadā nāstīti jñāyate | bhavānāha- sarvamanātma
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: The past and future do not exist. Although you have said 'when a <s>dharma</s> exists, consciousness arises' — this has already been answered previously: 'Even a non-existent <s>dharma</s> gives rise to consciousness.' As to your statement that 'the past form is characterized by the characteristic of form and by the designation of form' — that too is not correct. What is past and future would not be form, because the act of forming (<s>rūpaṇa</s>) does not exist [for them]. Nor should it be said that the characteristic of impermanence [applies to them]. The Blessed One uses those names merely in conformity with the false conceptions and designations of beings. You have said: 'From knowledge, knowledge arises.' [But] the cause, having performed its causal function for the effect, ceases. Just as a seed, having performed its causal function for the sprout, ceases. The Blessed One too said: 'From the arising of this, that arises.' You have said: 'What exists as a real entity and is beneficial — that the Blessed One teaches.' [But] this entity spoken by the Blessed One, by its own nature, even when not spoken of in the present time, still exists. If you think 'the past has ceased' — then it is known to be non-existent. You have said: 'One should contemplate all as without self

body.text: bhāvayet iti | yasmātsattvā atītānanāgatān dharmān sātmano manyante tasmāt bhagavānevamavocat | bhavatoktam [iti jñānaṃ] samyak dṛṣṭiriti | yasmāt kāyo 'yaṃ karmasamutpādakaḥ | tacca karma phalasya hetuṃ kṛtvā niruddham | paścācca tatphalaṃ punarātmanānubhūyate | tasmāduktam- asti phalamiti | tathāgataśāsane asti vā nāsti vā iti sarvamupāya ityucyate | puṇyapāpakarmapratyayatvapradarśanārtham, natu paramārthataḥ | yathā pratītyāsti sattva ityucyate | tathātītamanāgatamapi | atītaṃ mana āśrayata itīdamapi upāyāśrayaṇam | na tu yathā puruṣeṇa bhittyādyāśrīyate | cittasyotpādo nātmani niśrayata iti ca viśadam | pūrvacittamupādāyānantaracittamutpadyate | tathā karmabalamapi | tathāgataḥ prajānāti- karmaniruddhamapi phalasya hetuṃ karotīti | na vadati ekāntataḥ prajānāmīti | yatharṇapatnasthamakṣaram | tathā pāpakarmāpi | anena kāyena karma kriyate | tasya ca karmaṇo nirodhe 'pi vipāko na praṇaśyati |
body.translated_text: .' Because beings conceive past and future <s>dharmas</s> as having a self, therefore the Blessed One spoke thus. You have said '[this] knowledge is right view.' Because this body is the producer of <s>karma</s>, and that <s>karma</s>, having performed its causal function for the fruit, has ceased, and afterwards that fruit is experienced by oneself — therefore it is said: 'The fruit exists.' In the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, whether something 'exists' or 'does not exist' — all of this is called skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), for the purpose of demonstrating the conditionality of meritorious and sinful <s>karma</s>, not in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthataḥ</s>). Just as it is said conventionally (<s>pratītya</s>) that a 'being' exists — so too with the past and future. That 'the mind depends on the past' — this too is a dependence on skillful means. It is not like a person leaning against a wall and so forth. And it is clear that the arising of consciousness does not depend on a self. Depending on the preceding consciousness, the immediately subsequent consciousness arises — and likewise the power of <s>karma</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> knows: 'Even though <s>karma</s> has ceased, it still serves as a cause for the fruit.' He does not say: 'I know [it] absolutely.' Just as the syllable stored in a debt-bond — so too with sinful <s>karma</s>. <s>Karma</s> is performed by this body, and even upon the cessation of that <s>karma</s>, the ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) does not perish.

body.text: bhavānāha- śraddhādīnyanāsravendriyāṇi na syuriti | yadi śaikṣo 'nāsravendriyaṃ labdhavān | pratyutpannasthameva labdhavān | atītaṃ niruddhamanāgatañcāprāptam | [pratyutpannantu] samanvāgatamityato nāstīti na vaktuṃ śakyate | bhavānāha- āryā anāgataṃ na vyākuryuriti | āryajñānabalena hi tathā | asantaṃ dharmamapi vyākurvanti | yathā atītaṃ dharmaṃ niruddhamapi smṛtibalātprajānāti | bhavānāha- nānusmaretpañca viṣayāniti | prākṛto jano mohādabhūtasmṛtyā pūrvagṛhītaṃ niyatalakṣaṇaṃ paścānniruddhamapi utpadyamāna[mivā]nusmarati | smṛtidharmaśca tathaiva syāt | na tu śaśaśṛṅgādisamānā syāt | aṣṭādaśamaupavicārāḥ punarevam | pratyutpannagṛhītaṃ rūpaṃ niruddhātītamapi tatsmṛtiranuvartate | bhavānāha- na kīrtayet- ahaṃ dhyānasamādhiṃ labdhavāniti | taṃ samādhiṃ [pūrvaṃ] pratyutpanne 'labhata | anusmaraṇabalādvadati- ahaṃ labdhavāniti | bhavān bravīti- adhicittamadhivedanañca bhāvanā na bhavet iti | cittaṃ dvidhākṣaṇikamānubandhikamiti | pratyutpannaṃ cittaṃ prayujyānubandhikaṃ cittaṃ bhāvayati | na tvanusmṛto vartate | bhavānavocat- catvāri samyakpradhānāni nābhyasyediti | anāgatākuśaladharmāṇāṃ nidānamapasārayati | anāgatakuśaladharmāṇāṃ nidānamutpādayati | bhavānāha- tadā tathāgato 'san syāditi | tathāgataḥ parinirvṛtalakṣaṇaḥ | [atīte] 'dhvani dṛṣṭo 'pi [pratyutpanne]
body.translated_text: You have said: 'The undefiled faculties (<s>anāsravendriya</s>) beginning with faith would not exist.' If a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) has obtained the undefiled faculty, he has obtained it as existing in the present. The past has ceased and the future has not yet been reached. [But the present] is possessed (<s>samanvāgata</s>) — therefore it cannot be said to be non-existent. You have said: 'The Noble Ones would not predict the future.' By the power of noble knowledge (<s>āryajñāna</s>), indeed, they predict even a non-existent <s>dharma</s>. Just as one cognizes a past <s>dharma</s> that has already ceased, by the power of memory (<s>smṛti</s>). You have said: 'One would not recollect the five sense-objects.' An ordinary person (<s>prākṛta jana</s>), through delusion, by false memory (<s>abhūtasmṛti</s>), recollects what was previously grasped with definite characteristics — even though it has subsequently ceased — as if it were arising [again]. And the nature of memory is just like that. But it should not be equated with [the non-existence of things like] a hare's horn and so forth. The eighteen mental investigations are likewise: even though the form grasped in the present has ceased and become past, the memory of it continues. You have said: 'He would not proclaim: I have attained <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>.' He obtained that <s>samādhi</s> [previously] when it was present. By the power of recollection, he says: 'I have obtained it.' You say: 'The cultivation of higher mind and higher feeling would not occur.' Consciousness (<s>citta</s>) is twofold: momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) and continuous (<s>ānubandhika</s>). Applying present consciousness, one cultivates continuous consciousness. But what is recollected does not [still] exist. You have said: 'The four right efforts could not be practiced.' One removes the causes (<s>nidāna</s>) of future unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; one generates the causes of future wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. You have said: 'Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be non-existent.' The <s>Tathāgata</s> has the characteristic of having attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. Even though [he was] seen in the past time-period, in the present

body.text: asti nāstīti na parigṛhyate | sa parinirvāya pāragataḥ khalu | sattvāśca śaraṇīkurvanti yathā laukikāḥ pitarāvārādhayanti | uktañca bhavatā- sūdīrghamalpakālaṃ vā śīlābhyāsaśca na syāditi | na hi kālataḥ śīlaṃ viśiṣyate | kasmāt | na hi kālo dravyam | dharmāṇāmutpattivyayasamavāyamātraṃ kālo 'stītyucyate | tasmādbhavatoktā hetavaḥ sarve 'yuktāḥ ||
body.translated_text: it is not grasped whether he exists or does not exist. He, having attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, has indeed gone beyond. And beings take refuge [in him] just as worldly people honor their parents. You have also said: 'The practice of moral conduct for a long or short period would not exist.' But moral conduct is not distinguished by time. Why? Because time is not a substance (<s>dravya</s>). Time is said to exist merely as the conjunction of the arising and ceasing of <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore all the reasons stated by you are untenable.

body.text: adhvadvayanāstitāvargo dvāviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-second chapter, the Chapter on the Non-Existence of the Two Time-Periods (<s>adhvadvayanāstitāvarga</s>).

body.text: 23 sarvadharmasadasattāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 23. Chapter on the Existence and Non-Existence of All <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmasadasattāvarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- kecidvadanti sarve dharmāḥ santīti | kecidvadanti- sarve dharmā na santīti |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Some say: 'All <s>dharmas</s> exist.' Others say: 'All <s>dharmas</s> do not exist.'

body.text: (pṛ) kena kāraṇena astīti vadanti | kena kāraṇena nāstīti | (u) astīti | bhagavānāha- sarvaṃ sarvamiti brāhmaṇa yāvadeva dvādaśāyatanāni | sarvamasti [brāhmaṇa] iti | pṛthivyādīni dravyāṇi saṃkhyādayo guṇāḥ utkṣepaṇāvakṣepaṇādikaṃ karma | sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyādayo dharmāḥ | mūlaprakṛtyādayaḥ | loke ca śaśaviṣāṇakūrmaromāhipādalavaṇagandhavāyurūpādayo na santi | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā sūtre-
body.translated_text: (Question) For what reason do they say 'they exist'? For what reason do they say 'they do not exist'? (Answer) [They say] 'they exist': The Blessed One said: 'All, all — O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, just so far as the twelve sense-bases (<s>dvādaśāyatana</s>). All exists, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' Substances (<s>dravya</s>) such as earth and the rest; qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) such as number and the rest; <s>karma</s> such as lifting up, putting down, and so forth; <s>dharmas</s> such as universality (<s>sāmānya</s>), particularity (<s>viśeṣa</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and the rest; the root-nature (<s>mūlaprakṛti</s>) and the rest. In the world, however, [things like] a hare's horn, a tortoise's hair, a snake's feet, the smell of salt, the form of wind, and the like do not exist. As the Blessed One stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: ākāśe [ca] padaṃ nāsti śramaṇo nāsti bāhyataḥ |
children.translated_text: In space there is no path, and there is no <s>śramaṇa</s> outside [the teaching];
The world delights in proliferations (<s>prapañca</s>); the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are free from proliferations — thus it is said.

body.text: anubhavavaśāddharmāḥ santītyucyante | yathā dravyādayaḥ ṣaṭpadārthāssanti aulūkyānām | pañcaviṃśatitattvāni santi sāṃkhyānām | ṣoḍaśa padārthāḥ santi nayasomānām |
body.translated_text: Based on experience, <s>dharmas</s> are said to exist. Just as the six categories (<s>padārtha</s>) — substance and the rest — exist for the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> (<s>Aulūkya</s>); the twenty-five principles (<s>tattva</s>) exist for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>; the sixteen categories exist for the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (<s>Nayasoma</s>).

body.text: yadi vastusādhanī yuktirasti | tadā astītyucyate | yathā dvādaśāyatanāni | bhagavataḥ śāsana upāyatayā sarvamastīti vā sarvaṃ nāstīti vocyate | na tu paramārthataḥ | kasmāt | astīti vyavasthāyāṃ śāśvatāntapātaḥ | nāstīti vyavasthāyāmucchedāntapātaḥ | anayorantayorvarjanamevāryā madhyamā patipat ||
body.translated_text: If there is a valid reasoning (<s>yukti</s>) that establishes a real entity — then it is said to exist, just as the twelve sense-bases. In the teaching of the Blessed One, 'all exists' or 'all does not exist' is spoken as a skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), not in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthataḥ</s>). Why? Because in the position of 'it exists,' there is the fall into the extreme of eternalism (<s>śāśvatānta</s>). In the position of 'it does not exist,' there is the fall into the extreme of annihilationism (<s>ucchedānta</s>). The avoidance of both these extremes is itself the noble Middle Way (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>).

body.text: sarvadharmasadasattāvargastrayoviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-third chapter, the Chapter on the Existence and Non-Existence of All <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmasadasattāvarga</s>).

body.text: 24 antarābhavāstitāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 24. Chapter on the Existence of Intermediate Existence (<s>antarābhavāstitāvarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- kecidvadanti- astyantarābhava iti | kecidvadanti nāstīti | (pṛ) kena kāraṇenāstīti vadanti | kena kāraṇena nāstīti | (u) astyantarābhavaḥ | āśvalāyanasūtre hi bhagavānāha- yadā pitarau sannipatitau bhavataḥ | gandharvaśca pratyupasthito bhavati iti | ato jñāyate astyantarābhava iti | vatsasūtrañcāha- yasmin samaye sattva imaṃ kāyaṃ nikṣipati punaścittotpādanakāyamanupādāno bhavati | asminnantarāle [bhavaṃ] upādānapratyayaṃ vadāmi | ayamantarā bhava iti | saptasatpuruṣeṣu astyantarāparinirvāyī | uktañcasūtre- vyavakīrṇaṃ karmābhisaṃskṛtya vyavakīrṇaṃ kāyamupādāya vyavakīrṇe loka utpadyate | jñātavyamastyantarābhava iti | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- catvāro bhavāḥ pūrvakālabhavo maraṇabhavo 'ntarābhava upapattibhava iti | āha ca- saptabhavāḥ- pañcagatayaḥ
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Some say: 'Intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) exists.' Others say: 'It does not exist.' (Question) For what reason do they say it exists? For what reason do they say it does not exist? (Answer) Intermediate existence exists. For in the <s>Āśvalāyanasūtra</s>, the Blessed One said: 'When the parents have come together and the <s>gandharva</s> is present' — from this it is known that intermediate existence exists. The <s>Vatsasūtra</s> also says: 'At the time when a being lays down this body and again takes up a mind-produced body without clinging — in this interval, I declare there is existence conditioned by clinging (<s>upādānapratyaya</s>). This is the intermediate existence.' Among the seven types of noble persons, there is one who attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>). And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Having fashioned a mixed <s>karma</s>, having taken up a mixed body, one is born in a mixed world. It should be known that intermediate existence exists.' Furthermore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four kinds of existence (<s>bhava</s>): prior existence (<s>pūrvakālabhava</s>), death-existence (<s>maraṇabhava</s>), intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), and birth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>).' And it says: 'There are seven existences: the five destinies (<s>gati</s>)

body.text: karmabhavo 'ntarābhava iti | āha ca- yamarājo 'ntarābhave pāpinaḥ santarjya vyatyastaṃ pātayanti | iti | tathāgato 'ntarābhavamupādāya sattvānāṃ pūrvanivāsaṃ prajānāti ayaṃ sattvo 'smin upapattisthāna utpadyate sa sattvastasminnupapattisthāna iti | uktañca sūtre- divyena cakṣuṣā paśyati sattvān cyavamānānupapadyamānāṃśceti | kiñcāha- sattvo [antarā]bhavasantatyā asmāllokātparalokaṃ saṅkrāmati | iti | laukikā api astyantarābhava iti śraddhadhānā vadantimriyamāṇasya sūkṣmāṇi catvāri mahābhūtāni asmādbhavāt [bhavāntaraṃ] krāmanti iti | satyantarābhave paralokaḥ | asatyantarābhave nāsti paralokaḥ | yadi nāstyantarābhavaḥ, imaṃ kāyaṃ visṛjya parakāyamanupādānasyāntarā vyucchedaḥ syāt | ato jñāyate 'styantarābhava iti ||
body.translated_text: , <s>karma</s>-existence (<s>karmabhava</s>), and intermediate existence.' And it says: 'King <s>Yama</s>, having threatened sinners in the intermediate state, casts them down headlong.' The <s>Tathāgata</s>, taking intermediate existence into account, cognizes the previous abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>) of beings: 'This being is born in such-and-such a place of rebirth; that being [is born] in such-and-such a place of rebirth.' And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'With the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>), one sees beings dying and being reborn.' Furthermore it says: 'A being, through the continuity of intermediate existence, transmigrates from this world to the next world.' Even worldly people, having faith that intermediate existence exists, say: 'The subtle four great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) of a dying person transmigrate from this existence [to another existence].' If intermediate existence exists, then the next world exists. If intermediate existence does not exist, then the next world does not exist. If intermediate existence does not exist, then having relinquished this body and not yet having taken up the next body, there would be annihilation in the interval. Therefore it is known that intermediate existence exists.

body.text: antarābhavāstitāvargaścaturviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-fourth chapter, the Chapter on the Existence of Intermediate Existence (<s>antarābhavāstitāvarga</s>).

body.text: 25 antarābhavanāstitāvarga
body.translated_text: 25. Chapter on the Non-Existence of Intermediate Existence (<s>antarābhavanāstitāvarga</s>)

body.text: kecidvadanti- nāstyantarābhava iti | yadyapyuktaṃ bhavatā- āśvalāyanasūtra uktam astyantarābhava iti | tanna yuktam | kasmāt | yadyāryā na jānanti- ayaṃ kaḥ kuta āgata iti | tadā nāstyantarābhavaḥ | yadyasti kasmānna jānanti | bhavānāha- vatsasūtra uktamiti | idamayuktam | kutaḥ | sūtre 'smin praśno 'nyaḥ prativacanañcānyat | anena brāhmaṇena kalpitam- anyaḥ kāyo 'nyo jīva iti | ata evaṃ prativakti- santyantarābhave pañcaskandhā iti | bhavānāha- astyantarāparinirvāyīti | sa kāmarūpadhātvorantarā kāyamupādāya tatra parinirvṛta iti antarāparinirvāyī | kasmāt | yathoktaṃ sūtre- kaścinmriyamāṇaḥ kutra gacchati kutrotpadyate kutra tiṣṭhati itīdamekārthakam | bhavānāha- vyavakīrṇaṃ kāyamupādāya vyavakīrṇe loka utpadyata iti | kāyamupādāyeti vacanaṃ loka utpadyata iti cedamekārthakam | catvāro bhavāḥ sapta bhavā iti ca bhavaduktaṃ sūtramayuktam | dharmalakṣaṇānanugamāt | bhavaduktaṃ yamarājasantarjanamupapattibhave bhavati nāntarābhave | bhavānāha- tathāgato 'ntarābhavamupādāya
body.translated_text: Some say: 'Intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) does not exist.' Even though you have cited the <s>Āśvalāyanasūtra</s> as stating that intermediate existence exists, that is not valid. Why? If the Noble Ones do not know 'Who is this? Where did he come from?' — then intermediate existence does not exist. If it does exist, why do they not know? You have cited the <s>Vatsasūtra</s>. This is not valid. Why? In that <s>sūtra</s>, the question is one thing and the answer is another. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> conceived: 'The body is one thing and the soul (<s>jīva</s>) is another.' Therefore the reply was given thus: 'In the intermediate state there are five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>).' You have cited the intermediate-state <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> attainer (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>). He, having taken up a body in the interval between the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) and the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> there — therefore he is called 'one who attains <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state.' Why? As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A certain dying person — where does he go? Where is he reborn? Where does he abide?' — this all has a single meaning. You have cited: 'Having taken up a mixed body, one is born in a mixed world.' The statement 'having taken up a body' and 'one is born in a world' have a single meaning. The <s>sūtras</s> you have cited about 'four kinds of existence' and 'seven kinds of existence' are not valid, because they do not accord with the marks of <s>Dharma</s>. Your citation that 'King <s>Yama</s> threatens [sinners]' — that occurs in birth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>), not in intermediate existence. You have said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, taking intermediate existence into account,

body.text: pūrvanivāsaṃ prajānātīti | tadayuktam | āryajñānabalaṃ hi tat | asantamanāgatamapi smṛtyā prajānāti | bhavānāha- divyena cakṣuṣā paśyati mriyamāṇānupapadyamānāniti | utpitsuḥ sa upapadyamāna ityucyate | maraṇonmukhaśca cyavamānaḥ | natvantarābhavagataḥ | bhavānāha- sattvo bhavasantatyā asmāllokātparalokaṃ saṅkrāmatīti | paralokāstitvapradarśanāya tādṛśaṃ vacanaṃ na tvantarābhavāstitvaprakāśanāya | bhavānāha- mriyamāṇasya sūkṣmāṇi catvāri mahābhūtāni bhavāntaraṃ krāmantīti | kaukikānāmupalabhyamaśraddheyam | na taddheturupayujyate | bhavānāha- yadi nāstyantarābhavaḥ antarāvyucchedaḥ syāditi | karmabalādayamatrotpadyate yathā atītamanāgatamananuvṛttamapi saṃsmarati | ato nāstyantarābhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: cognizes previous abodes.' That is not valid. For that is the power of noble knowledge (<s>āryajñānabala</s>). Even what is non-existent and future, he cognizes through memory. You have said: 'With the divine eye, one sees beings dying and being reborn.' One who is about to be reborn is called 'one being reborn' (<s>upapadyamāna</s>). And one facing death is called 'one falling away' (<s>cyavamāna</s>) — but not one who has gone to intermediate existence. You have said: 'A being transmigrates from this world to the next through the continuity of existence.' Such a statement is for the purpose of demonstrating the existence of the next world, not for demonstrating the existence of intermediate existence. You have said: 'The subtle four great elements of a dying person transmigrate to another existence.' What is apprehended by ordinary people is unreliable. That reason is not applicable. You have said: 'If intermediate existence does not exist, there would be annihilation in the interval.' By the power of <s>karma</s>, this one is born there — just as one remembers things past and future even without continuity. Therefore, intermediate existence does not exist.

body.text: pūrvanivāsajñāna uktaṃ jānāti ayaṃ puruṣo 'smiṃlloke mṛtastasmiṃlloka utpadyata iti na tūktam antarābhave tiṣṭhatīti | tathāgata āha- trividhaṃ karma dṛṣṭavipākamupapattivipākamūrdhvavipākamiti | na tvāha- antarābhavavipākaṃ karmeti | yadyantarābhave sparśo 'sti | sa evopapattibhava ityucyate | yadi na spṛśati, sparśavihīnaḥ | sparśavihīnatvādvedanādayo 'pi na santi | tādṛśaṃ punaḥ kutrāsti | yaḥ sattvo 'ntarābhavarūpamupādatte sa evopapattiṃ vedayate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yadimaṃ kāyaṃ nikṣipan kāyāntaramupādatte tadahaṃ vadāmi upapattiriti | yadi na kāyamupādatte | tadā nāstyantarābhavaḥ | yadyantarābhave cyutiḥ | upapattireva sā | kutaḥ | pūrvamutpadyannasya paścādavaśyaṃ cyuteḥ | yadi nāsti cyutiḥ | nityo bhavet | karmabalāccopapattiriti kimantarābhavena | yadyantarābhava karmataḥ siddhaḥ | sa evopapattibhavaḥ | yathocyate- karmapratyayā jātiriti | yanna karmataḥ siddham | kena bhavo 'sti | tatprativaktavyam |
body.translated_text: In the knowledge of previous abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsajñāna</s>), it is said: 'He knows that this person died in this world and was reborn in that world' — but it is not said 'he abides in intermediate existence.' The <s>Tathāgata</s> said: 'There are three kinds of <s>karma</s>: <s>karma</s> with result visible in this life (<s>dṛṣṭavipāka</s>), <s>karma</s> with result in the next rebirth (<s>upapattivipāka</s>), and <s>karma</s> with result in subsequent lives (<s>ūrdhvavipāka</s>).' But he did not say: '<s>Karma</s> with result in intermediate existence.' If there is contact (<s>sparśa</s>) in intermediate existence, then that itself is called birth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>). If there is no contact, then it is devoid of contact. Being devoid of contact, feeling and the rest also do not exist. Where then does such a thing exist? The being that takes up the form of intermediate existence is itself experiencing rebirth-existence. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'When one lays down this body and takes up another body — that I declare to be rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>).' If one does not take up a body, then there is no intermediate existence. If there is passing away (<s>cyuti</s>) in intermediate existence, that itself is rebirth-existence. Why? Because one who was previously reborn must subsequently pass away. If there is no passing away, it would be permanent. And since rebirth occurs by the power of <s>karma</s>, what need is there for intermediate existence? If intermediate existence is established through <s>karma</s>, then it is itself rebirth-existence. As it is said: 'Conditioned by <s>karma</s>, birth arises.' If it is not established through <s>karma</s>, through what does it exist? That must be answered.

body.text: ucyate | upapattiviśeṣamevāntarābhavaṃ vadāmaḥ | ato nāsti yathoktadoṣaḥ | antarābhava utpannasyāpyasya upapattibhavāntarayogo bhavati | yataḥ kalale vijñānamupasaṅkrāmati | ayamantarābhava ityucyate |
body.translated_text: It is replied: We call intermediate existence a special type of rebirth-existence (<s>upapattiviśeṣa</s>). Therefore the faults you have stated do not apply. Even for one born in intermediate existence, there is a connection with rebirth-existence. Because consciousness enters the embryonic stage (<s>kalala</s>) — this is called intermediate existence.

body.text: atra dūṣaṇamāha | karmabalādupasaṅkrāmati | kimantarābhavavikalpena | cittaṃ na kutracidupasaṅkrāmati | karmapratyayāttu asmiṃlloke niruddhaṃ tatrotpadyate | nahi pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate cittaṃ santatyotpadyata iti | yathā pāde viddhasya śirasi vedanānubhūyate | na tatra pāde sthitaṃ
body.translated_text: Here a refutation is stated: By the power of <s>karma</s>, consciousness enters [the embryo]. What need is there for the conception of intermediate existence? Consciousness does not transmigrate from anywhere. Rather, conditioned by <s>karma</s>, what has ceased in this world arises there. For it is not directly perceived that consciousness arises in a continuum. Just as when the foot is pierced, pain is experienced in the head — the consciousness established in the foot

body.text: vijñānaṃ bhavapratyayaṃ śirasi saṅkrāmati | ato sannikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭapratyayagaṇasāmagrya tu citatutpadyate | ato 'styantarābhava iti na kalpanā kāryā ||
body.translated_text: does not transmigrate to the head because of the condition of existence. Rather, consciousness arises through the aggregation of proximate and distant conditions. Therefore, the supposition that 'intermediate existence exists' need not be made.

body.text: antarābhavanāstitvavargaḥ pañcaviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-fifth chapter, the Chapter on the Non-Existence of Intermediate Existence (<s>antarābhavanāstitvavarga</s>).

body.text: 26 anupūrvavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 26. Chapter on Sequential [Realization] (<s>anupūrvavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha | kecidvadanti caturṇāṃ satyānāmanupūrveṇābhisamaya iti | kecidvadanti ekakṣaṇeneti | (pṛ) kena kāraṇenocyate anupūrveṇābhisamayaḥ, kena kāraṇena ekakṣaṇenābhisamaya iti | (u) anupūrveṇābhisamayaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre lokasya samudayaṃ paśyato nāstitādṛṣṭirna bhavati | lokasya nirodhaṃ paśyato 'stitādṛṣṭirna bhavati iti | ato jñātavyaṃ nirodhasamudayayorlakṣaṇaṃ pratyekaṃ pṛthagiti | yaḥ prajānāti- yatsamudayalakṣaṇaṃ tatsarvaṃ nirodhalakṣaṇamiti | tasya virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dharmacakṣurbhavati | āha ca-
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Some say: 'The realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) of the Four Noble Truths is sequential.' Others say: 'It occurs in a single moment.' (Question) For what reason is sequential realization asserted? For what reason is single-moment realization asserted? (Answer) Sequential realization: As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one who sees the arising of the world, the view of non-existence (<s>nāstitādṛṣṭi</s>) does not occur. For one who sees the cessation of the world, the view of existence (<s>astitādṛṣṭi</s>) does not occur.' From this it should be known that the characteristics of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) and arising (<s>samudaya</s>) are individually distinct. One who understands: 'Whatever has the characteristic of arising, all of that has the characteristic of cessation' — for him the stainless, immaculate <s>Dharma</s>-eye (<s>dharmacakṣus</s>) arises. And it is said:

children.text: anupūrveṇa medhāvī stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: The wise one, gradually, little by little, moment by moment,
should blow away the impurities of the self, like a goldsmith [removes impurities] of silver.

body.text: āsravakṣayasūtramāha jānataḥ paśyataḥ āsravāṇāṃ kṣayo bhavati iti | pratipattupratidinaṃ kṣīyamāṇaṃ svayamajānato 'pi sadā bhāvitatvāt āsravāṇāṃ kṣayo bhavati |
body.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> on the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣayasūtra</s>) says: 'For one who knows and sees, the destruction of the outflows occurs.' Even for a practitioner who day by day is diminishing [outflows] without knowing it himself, because of constant cultivation, the destruction of the outflows occurs.

body.text: bhagavānāha satyeṣu udapadyata cakṣuḥ jñānaṃ vidyā prajñā iti | kāmadhātukaduḥkhe dvau [kṣaṇau] rūpārūpyadhātaka [duḥkhe] ca dvau | tathā samudāyadāvapi | sūtre ca bhagavān kaṇṭhata āha anupūrveṇa satyābhisamaya iti | yathā puruṣaḥ śreṇimāruhya uparyārohati | ityādisūtrāt jñāyate catussatyāni naikakālikāni iti | kleśānāñca catussatyeṣu caturdhā mithyācārā bhavanti yaduta nāsti dukhaṃ, nāsti samudayaḥ, nāsti nirodhaḥ, nāsti mārgaḥ iti | anāsravajñānasyāpi anupūrveṇa caturdhā samyagācārāḥ syuḥ | yogī ca cittaṃ samādhāya idaṃ duḥkhaṃ ayaṃ duḥkhanirodha iyaṃ duḥkhanigāminī patipat iti vikalpayet | yadyekasmin citte syāt kathamevamanupūrveṇa samādhivikalpo bhavet | ato jñāyate anupūrveṇābhisamayo naikakṣaṇeneti |
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'With respect to the truths, the eye, knowledge, understanding, and wisdom arose.' In the suffering of the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), [there are] two moments; in the suffering of the form and formless realms (<s>rūpārūpyadhātu</s>), also two; and likewise for the origin and the rest. And in the <s>sūtra</s>, the Blessed One explicitly says: 'The realization of the truths is sequential.' Just as a person ascends a staircase, climbing upward — from such <s>sūtras</s> it is known that the Four Noble Truths are not [realized] simultaneously. And there are four kinds of wrong conduct with respect to the Four Noble Truths: 'There is no suffering; there is no origin; there is no cessation; there is no path.' The undefiled knowledge (<s>anāsravajñāna</s>) would also have four kinds of right conduct sequentially. A <s>yogin</s>, having composed his mind in <s>samādhi</s>, would discriminate: 'This is suffering; this is the cessation of suffering; this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' If this occurred in a single moment of mind, how could such sequential discrimination in <s>samādhi</s> occur? Therefore it is known that realization is sequential, not in a single moment.

body.text: anupūrvavargaḥ ṣaḍviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-sixth chapter, the Chapter on Sequential [Realization] (<s>anupūrvavarga</s>).

body.text: 27 ekakṣaṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 27. Chapter on Single-Moment [Realization] (<s>ekakṣaṇavarga</s>)

body.text: kecidāhuḥ caturṇāṃ satyānāmabhisamayo nānupūrveṇeti | bhavānāha lokasya samudayaṃ paśyato nastitādṛṣṭirna bhavati | lokasya nirodhaṃ paśyato astitādṛṣṭirna bhavatīti | tadā svamataṃ vinaśyet | tathā cet ṣoḍaśabhiḥ cittakṣaṇaiḥ dvādaśabhirākāraiśca mārgo labhyata iti na syāt | bhavatoktaṃ yatsamudayalakṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ tannirodhalakṣaṇamiti prajānato dharmacakṣurbhavatīti | tathā cet cittadvayena mārgalābhaḥ syāt- adyaṃ samudayacittaṃ dvitīyaṃ nirodhacittaṃ iti | na tvaitadyuktam | bhavānāha anupūrveṇa medhāvī stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe | ....nirdhamenmalamātmana iti [anenāpi] na syāt ṣoḍaśamātraiścittakṣaṇairiti | bhavatoktaṃ āsravakṣayasūtramāha rūpādīn jānataḥ paśyataḥ āsravānāṃ kṣayo bhavatīti | evañcāpramāṇacittāni syuḥ na tu ṣoḍaśacittamātrāṇi | bhavatoktaṃ- cakṣurjñānaṃ vidyā prajñeti | bhagavān svayaṃ bravīti caturṣu satyeṣu jñānaṃ cakṣurvidyā prajñodapadyateti na bravīti anupūrveṇa ṣoḍaśacittakṣaṇāni bhavantīti |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'The realization of the Four Noble Truths is not sequential.' You have said: 'For one who sees the arising of the world, the view of non-existence does not occur. For one who sees the cessation of the world, the view of existence does not occur.' If so, your own position would be destroyed. And if so, the attainment of the path through sixteen mind-moments and twelve aspects would not hold. Your statement that 'one who understands that whatever has the characteristic of arising, all has the characteristic of cessation — for him the <s>Dharma</s>-eye arises' — if so, the attainment of the path would occur through two mind-moments: the first being the mind of arising (<s>samudayacitta</s>) and the second being the mind of cessation (<s>nirodhacitta</s>). But that is not valid. You have cited: 'The wise one, gradually, little by little, moment by moment... should blow away the impurities of the self' — from this too, [the realization] through merely sixteen mind-moments would not follow. Your citation of the <s>āsravakṣayasūtra</s> that 'for one who knows and sees form and so forth, the destruction of the outflows occurs' — in that case, there would be immeasurable mind-moments, not merely sixteen. Your citation that 'the eye, knowledge, understanding, and wisdom [arose]' — the Blessed One himself says: 'With respect to the four truths, the eye, knowledge, understanding, and wisdom arose.' He does not say: 'Sequentially, there are sixteen mind-moments.'

body.text: bhavatoktaṃ bhagavān kaṇṭhenāha- anupūrveṇa satyabhisamayaḥ śreṇyārohaṇavat iti | nādhītamidaṃ sūtramasmābhiḥ | sattve 'pi nirākartavyameva | dharmalakṣaṇānanugamāt | bhavatoktaṃ caturdhā mithyācārā bhavantīti | pañcaskandhādāvapi mithyācārāḥ syuḥ | yān mithyācārānanusṛtya sarvaṃ jñānamutpadyeta | evaṃ ca ṣoḍaśabhireva cittakṣaṇairmārgalābha iti na syāt | bhavānāha samādhyā vikalpayediti | rūpādāvapi tathā vikalpayet | ato na ṣoḍaśaiva cittakṣaṇāḥ syuḥ |
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'the Blessed One explicitly says: the realization of the truths is sequential, like ascending a staircase' — we have not studied this <s>sūtra</s>. Even if it exists, it should be rejected, because it does not accord with the marks of <s>Dharma</s>. Your statement about 'four kinds of wrong conduct' — there would also be wrong conducts with respect to the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) and so forth. Following those wrong conducts, all knowledge would arise. Thus, the attainment of the path through merely sixteen mind-moments would not hold. You have said 'one should discriminate in <s>samādhi</s>.' One would also discriminate with respect to form and the rest in the same way. Therefore, there would not be merely sixteen mind-moments.

body.text: yogino
body.translated_text: For the <s>yogin</s>, there are not multiple truths but only one truth — namely, the seeing of the cessation of suffering, called the initial awakening (<s>ādyābhisambodhi</s>). Because visible <s>dharmas</s> and the rest are dependently originated (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), the <s>yogin</s>, through the sequential <s>dharmas</s> of warmth (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and the rest, sees the truth in the form of the final cessation-truth. Through seeing the truth of cessation, the attainment of the path is declared.

body.text: na [nānā]satyāni bhavanti kintu ekameva satyaṃ bhavati yaduta duḥkhanirodhadarśanamādyābhisambodhi nāmakam | dṛśyadharmādīnāṃ pratītyasamutpannatvāt yogī ūṣmagatādidharmānupūrveṇa caramanirodhasatyarūpaṃ satyaṃ paśyati | nirodhasatyadarśanānmārgalābhaityākhyāyate |
ekakṣaṇa saptaviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-seventh chapter, [the Chapter on] Single-Moment [Realization] (<s>ekakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: 28 parihāṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 28. Chapter on Decline (<s>parihāṇavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- kecidvadanti arhan parihīyate | kecidvadanti na parihīyata iti | (pṛ) kena kāraṇena parihīyate kena kāraṇena na parihīyate | (u) parihīyata iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- pañca hetavaḥ pañca pratyayāḥ samayavimuktasyārhataḥ parihāṇāya saṃvartante | katame pañca | karmaprasṛto bhavati | bhāṣyaprasṛto bhavati | adhikaraṇaprasṛto bhavati | dīrghacārikāyogamanuyukto bhavati | dīrgheṇa rogajātena spṛṣṭo bhavati | iti | āha ca sūtram dvividho 'rhan parihāṇalakṣaṇo 'parihāṇalakṣaṇa iti | api coktaṃ sūtre yadyamuko bhikṣuḥ vimuktimukhāt parihīyate tadidaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate iti | api coktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Some say: 'An <s>Arhat</s> declines.' Others say: 'He does not decline.' (Question) For what reason does he decline? For what reason does he not decline? (Answer) He declines. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Five causes and five conditions conduce to the decline of an <s>Arhat</s> liberated by occasion (<s>samayavimukta</s>). What are the five? He is engaged in <s>karma</s>; he is engaged in talk; he is engaged in disputes; he is engaged in lengthy travels; he is afflicted by long illness.' And the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'There are two kinds of <s>Arhat</s>: one with the characteristic of decline (<s>parihāṇalakṣaṇa</s>) and one with the characteristic of non-decline (<s>aparihāṇalakṣaṇa</s>).' Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'If a certain monk declines from the gateway of liberation (<s>vimuktimukha</s>) — this situation is found.' And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
kumbhopamaṃ kāyamidaṃ viditvā nagaropamaṃ cittamidaṃ sthāpayet |
yudhyeta māraṃ prajñāyudhena jitañca rakṣedaniveśanaḥ syāt || iti |
body.translated_text:
Having known this body to be like a pot, having established this mind like a fortress,
one should fight <s>Māra</s> with the weapon of wisdom; one should guard what is won and be without attachment.

body.text: aparihīnasya jitarakṣaṇaṃ na syāt | jñānañca dvividhaṃ- kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānamiti | kṣayajñānavān na punarutpadyate | kimanutpādajñānena | udāyino yā nirodhasamāpatti durlabhā | sa eva parihāṇahetuḥ | sa parihīno 'pi rūpadhātāva(vu)dapadyata ityādibhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ jñātavyaṃ parihīyata iti |
body.translated_text: For one who has not declined, there would be no need to 'guard what is won.' Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is twofold: the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>). One who possesses the knowledge of destruction does not arise again. What then is the need for the knowledge of non-arising? The cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) of <s>Udāyin</s> is difficult to obtain — that itself is a cause of decline. Even though he has declined, he is reborn in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>). By these and other reasons, it should be known that [an <s>Arhat</s>] declines.

body.text: parihāṇavarga aṣṭāviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-eighth chapter, the Chapter on Decline (<s>parihāṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 29 aparihāṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 29. Chapter on Non-Decline (<s>aparihāṇavarga</s>)

body.text: kecidvadanti āryamārgānna parihīyate dhyānasamādheḥ paraṃ parihīyata iti | (pṛ) tathā cet arhan dvividho na syāt | asti khalu parihāṇalakṣaṇaḥ | sarveṣāmarhatāṃ dhyānasamādhibhyaḥ parihāṇamastyeva | (u) dhyānasamādhiparihīṇasya vaśitābalamasti na tu sarveṣāmarhatām | (pṛ) na yujyate | yathā gaudhiko bhikṣuḥ ṣaḍvāraṃ [cetovimukteḥ] parihīṇaḥ asinā ātmānaṃ jaghāna | yadi dhyānasamādheḥ prahīṇaḥ, nātmānaṃ hanyāt | tathāgatāśāsane hi vimuktiḥ pradhānā na samādhiḥ | (u) sa imaṃ dhyānasamādhimavalambyārhanmārgaṃ spṛśet | tasmāt samādheḥ cyutasyānāsravaṃ cyavate na tu anāsravātparihīyate | kasmāt | yathāha gāthā-
body.translated_text: Some say: 'From the noble path one does not decline, but from <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> one may decline.' (Objection) If that is so, the <s>Arhat</s> would not be twofold. Indeed, there is one with the characteristic of decline (<s>parihāṇalakṣaṇa</s>). For all <s>Arhats</s>, there certainly is decline from <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>. (Reply) One who has declined from <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> possesses mastery and power, but this does not apply to all <s>Arhats</s>. (Objection) This is not correct. Just as the monk <s>Gaudhika</s>, having declined from mental liberation (<s>cetovimukti</s>) six times, killed himself with a sword. If he had [merely] declined from <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>, he would not have killed himself. For in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, liberation (<s>vimukti</s>) is paramount, not <s>samādhi</s>. (Reply) He, relying on this <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>, would have attained the path of <s>Arhat</s>-ship. Therefore, when he fell from <s>samādhi</s>, the undefiled [knowledge] also fell — but he did not decline from the undefiled [path itself]. Why? As the verse states —

body.text:
kṣīṇaṃ purāṇaṃ na navo 'sti sambhavo viraktacittā āyatike bhave ca |
te kṣīṇabījā aviruḍhacchandā nirvānti dhīrā yathāyaṃ pradīpaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
The old is destroyed, there is no new arising;
their minds are dispassionate toward future existence.
With seeds destroyed and desires unarisen,
the steadfast ones are extinguished like this lamp.

body.text: kiñcāha-
body.translated_text: Furthermore it is said —

body.text:
śailo yathā caikaghano vātena na samīryate |
evaṃ nindāpraśaṃsāsu na samiñjanti paṇḍitāḥ | iti |
body.translated_text:
Just as a solid mass of rock is not moved by the wind,
so the wise are not shaken by blame and praise.

body.text: api coktaṃ sūtre- tṛṣṇā tṛṣṇājananītyādi | tṛṣṇāmūlamarhato 'tyantamunmūlitam | kutaḥ pravarteta saṃyojanam | āha ca- āryo 'tyantaparikṣīṇāntaḥ kṛtakaraṇīya iti | kiñcāha- āryasya kṣīyamāṇaḥ samudayo na punarbhavati | pradalitaṃ vijñānaṃ na [punaḥ] bhavati
body.translated_text: Furthermore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Craving begets craving,' and so forth. The root of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) has been completely uprooted in the <s>Arhat</s>. Whence would fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) arise? And it is said: 'The Noble One has completely exhausted [the defilements] within; his task is done.' Furthermore it is said: 'For the Noble One, the arising (<s>samudaya</s>) that is being destroyed does not arise again. The shattered consciousness does not

body.text: ityādi | uktañca sūtre- avidyāpratyayāḥ kāmadveṣamohāḥ pravartante | arhato 'tyantaparikṣīṇāvidyā | [tasya] kathaṃ saṃyojanāni pravartante | iti | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- ye śaikṣā nirvāṇamārgaṃ paryeṣante | ahaṃ vadāmi tairapramattairbhavitavyamiti | yeṣāmāsravāḥ kṣīṇāḥ na teṣāṃ punarāsravā bhavanti | ato nāsti parihāṇiḥ | kiñcāha- vidvāna kuśalabhāvanaḥ kuśalavāk kuśalakāyakarmāntaḥ karaṇīyānna cyavata iti | api cāha-
body.translated_text: arise again,' and so forth. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), desire, hatred, and delusion operate. The <s>Arhat</s>'s ignorance is completely exhausted. How then would fetters operate for him?' Furthermore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Those who are learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) seek the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. I say they must be heedful. Those whose outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) are destroyed — for them, outflows do not arise again.' Therefore there is no decline. Furthermore it is said: 'The wise one who cultivates the wholesome, with wholesome speech and wholesome bodily action, does not fall from what is to be done.' And it is also said —

body.text:
apramādarato bhikṣuḥ pramāde bhayakovidaḥ |
abhavyaḥ parihāṇāya nirvāṇasyaiva santike || iti |
body.translated_text:
The monk who delights in heedfulness, who is skilled in seeing danger in heedlessness,
is incapable of decline — he is in the very presence of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: uktañca sūtre-
body.translated_text: And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.translated_text: Wild animals take shelter in the forest; birds take shelter in the sky;
The <s>Dharma</s> is devoted to seclusion; good persons rest in tranquility.

body.text: trīṇi nidānāni saṃyojanānāṃ samutpādāya aprahīṇacchandarāgaḥ, chandarāgasthānīyasyopasthānaṃ, tatra mithyāmanaskārasamutpādaḥ | arhataḥ chandarāgaḥ prahīṇaḥ | chandarāgasthānīyasyo [pasthitā]vapi na mithyāmanaskāraḥ samudyate | ataḥ saṃyojanāni notpādayati | āha ca- dharmān mithyābhāvayato bhikṣostraya āsravāḥ prādurbhavanti iti | arhan punarna mithyābhāvayatīti na ta āsravāḥ prādurbhavanti iti | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- ya āryaprajñayā prajānāti na sa parihīyate | yathā srotaāpattiphalamaparihīṇam iti | kīñcārhan tisro vedanāḥ samyak prajānāti [tāsā]mutpādalakṣaṇaṃ nirodhalakṣaṇamāsvādalakṣaṇaṃ mārgalakṣaṇaṃ nissaraṇalakṣaṇañcetyato notpādayati saṃyojanam | kiñcāha- yo bhikṣuḥ śīlasamādhiprajñākhyai stribhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sa na parihīyate | iti | arhata utpannaṃ saṃyojanaṃ prahīṇam | anāgatañca notpādayati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- satyavihārī āryo naiva parihīyata iti | arhan
body.translated_text: There are three causes for the arising of fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>): desire-and-passion (<s>chandarāga</s>) not yet abandoned, the presentation of objects occupying the place of desire-and-passion, and the arising of unwise attention (<s>mithyāmanaskāra</s>) toward those [objects]. For the <s>Arhat</s>, desire-and-passion has been abandoned. Even though objects occupying the place of desire-and-passion present themselves, unwise attention does not arise. Therefore he does not produce fetters. And it is said: 'For a monk who cultivates <s>dharmas</s> wrongly, three outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) manifest.' But the <s>Arhat</s> does not cultivate wrongly — therefore those outflows do not manifest in him. Furthermore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who knows through noble wisdom (<s>āryaprajñā</s>) does not decline — just as the fruit of stream-entry is without decline.' Furthermore, the <s>Arhat</s> rightly knows the three feelings (<s>vedanā</s>) — their characteristic of arising, their characteristic of cessation, their characteristic of relishing, their characteristic as the path, and their characteristic as the escape — and therefore does not produce fetters. Furthermore it is said: 'A monk who is endowed with three <s>dharmas</s>, namely moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), does not decline.' For the <s>Arhat</s>, the arisen fetter has been abandoned, and he does not produce future [fetters]. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Noble One who abides in truth never declines.' The <s>Arhat</s>

body.text: sākṣātkṛtacatussatyaḥ kṣīṇāsrava ityataḥ satyavihārītyucyate | kiñcāha- saptabodhyaṅgāni aparihāṇīyā dharmā iti | arhataḥ saptabodhyaṅgasampannatvāt na parihāṇirbhavati | kiñcārhan akopyāṃ [ceto]vimuktiṃ sākṣātkṛtatvān ityato na parihīyate | arhan tathāgataśāsane sāramarthaṃ pratilabdhavān yadutākopyā cetovimuktiḥ | kasyacit karacchedavat tatsmaraṇe 'smaraṇe ca sadā karacchedo 'styeva | tathā arhataḥ prahīṇaṃ saṃyojanam | tatsamaraṇe 'smaraṇe ca sadā prahāṇamastyeva | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- śraddhādināmindriyāṇāṃ tīkṣṇatvāt arhan bhavati iti | tīkṣṇendriyaḥ kadāpi na parihīyate | anuttamatṛṣṇāprahāṇadharmakuśalasyārhataścittaṃ samyagvimucyate 'tyantaṃ kṣīyate | tadyathā dahano 'dagdhaṃ dahati dagdhvā ca napunastatra pratyāvartate | evaṃ bhikṣuḥ ekā daśabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgata ityato na kadāpi parihīyate |
body.translated_text: has directly realized the Four Noble Truths and has destroyed the outflows — therefore he is called 'one who abides in truth.' Furthermore it is said: 'The seven factors of awakening (<s>saptabodhyaṅga</s>) are <s>dharmas</s> that prevent decline.' Because the <s>Arhat</s> is endowed with the seven factors of awakening, there is no decline. Furthermore, because the <s>Arhat</s> has directly realized the unshakeable mental liberation (<s>akopyā cetovimukti</s>), he does not decline. The <s>Arhat</s> has obtained the essential meaning in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — namely, the unshakeable mental liberation. Just as for someone whose hand has been cut off, whether he remembers or does not remember it, the hand is always cut off. Likewise, for the <s>Arhat</s>, the fetter has been abandoned — whether he remembers or does not remember it, the abandonment always remains. Furthermore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Because of the sharpness of the faculties beginning with faith, one becomes an <s>Arhat</s>.' One of sharp faculties never declines. The mind of the <s>Arhat</s>, who is skilled in the <s>dharma</s> of the supreme abandonment of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), is rightly liberated and completely destroyed [of defilements]. Just as fire burns what is unburnt and, having burnt it, does not return to it again. Thus, because a monk is endowed with ten <s>dharmas</s>, he never declines.

body.text: (pṛ) dvividho 'rhan iti bhavatodāhṛtasūtramāha- asti aparihāṇa[lakṣaṇa] iti | (u) idaṃ sāmānyata uktam | śaikṣerapramattairbhavitavyamiti arhantamanapekṣya, na tu viśeṣata uktam aparihāṇalakṣaṇo 'stīti | bhagavanāha gāthām-
body.translated_text: (Objection) You have cited a <s>sūtra</s> [stating that] there are two kinds of <s>Arhat</s>, which says: 'There exists one with the characteristic of non-decline.' (Reply) This was stated in general terms — namely, [the injunction] that learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) must be heedful, said without specific reference to the <s>Arhat</s>. It is not stated specifically that 'there exists one with the characteristic of non-decline.' The Blessed One spoke a verse —

body.text:
jinaścet punarutpannaḥ syāt ucyate na tu so jinaḥ
jino bhūtvā na jāyet tātvikaḥ sa jino mataḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
If one who has conquered were to be reborn, he would be called not a true conqueror;
one who, having conquered, is not born again — he is regarded as the true conqueror (<s>jina</s>).

body.text: yo 'rhan punaḥ kleśānutpādayati na sa jino bhavet | arhataḥ kṣīṇajātitvāt na punaḥ kāyo vedyate | bhavataḥ sūtraṃ yadyapyāha- arhan parihāṇadharmā punaḥ parihīyeta iti | tathā cet aparihāṇadharmāpi syāt | yo bhikṣustathendriyāṇi karoti yathā notpadyate, so 'rhan bhavati | ato na parihīyate |
body.translated_text: The <s>Arhat</s> who again produces defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) would not be a conqueror (<s>jina</s>). Because the <s>Arhat</s>'s birth is destroyed, he does not again experience a body. Even though your <s>sūtra</s> says: 'An <s>Arhat</s> with the characteristic of decline may again decline' — if that is so, there would also be one with the characteristic of non-decline. A monk who makes his faculties such that [defilements] do not arise becomes an <s>Arhat</s>. Therefore he does not decline.

body.text: aparihāṇavarga ekonatriṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the twenty-ninth chapter, the Chapter on Non-Decline (<s>aparihāṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 30 cittasvabhāvavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 30. Chapter on the Nature of Mind (<s>cittasvabhāvavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- kecidvadanti cittaṃ prakṛtipariśuddhamāgantukamalairapariśuddhamiti | kecidvadanti na tatheti |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Some say: 'The mind is pure by nature (<s>prakṛtipariśuddha</s>) and impure due to adventitious defilements (<s>āgantukamala</s>).' Others say: 'It is not so.'

body.text: (pṛ) kena kāraṇena vadanti prakṛtipariśuddhamiti | kena kāraṇena vadanti na tatheti | (u) na tatheti | na cittaṃ prakṛtipariśuddhamāgantukamalaipariśuddham | kutaḥ | kleśā hi sadā cittena saha saṃprayogajāḥ | nāgantukalakṣaṇāḥ | cittañca trividham- kuśalamakuśalamavyākṛtamiti | kuśalamavyākṛtañca cittamamalam | akuśalacittaṃ prakṛtito 'pariśuddham | nāgantukatayā | idañca cittaṃ pratikṣaṇamutpannavināśi kleśānapekṣam | yaḥ kleśaḥ sahajo bhavati na sa āgantuka ityucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) For what reason do they say it is pure by nature? For what reason do they say it is not so? (Reply) 'It is not so' — the mind is not pure by nature and impure due to adventitious defilements. Why? Because defilements are always produced in conjunction (<s>saṃprayoga</s>) with the mind. They do not have the characteristic of being adventitious. And the mind is threefold: wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). The wholesome and indeterminate mind is without defilement. The unwholesome mind is impure by nature — not through adventitious [factors]. And this mind, arising and perishing at every moment (<s>pratikṣaṇam</s>), does not depend on defilements. A defilement that is innate (<s>sahaja</s>) is not called 'adventitious.'

body.text: (pṛ) cittaṃ rūpādimātramanubhūya tato nimittaṃ gṛhṇāti | nimittajāḥ kleśāḥ cittasya malaṃ kurvanti | ataḥ prakṛtipariśuddhamityucyate | (u) na yuktamidam | cittamidaṃ tatkāla eva niruddhaṃ na malanimittavat bhavati | cittaṃ tatkāla eva vinaṣṭaṃ kena malena lipyate | (pṛ) na pratikṣaṇavināśi cittamityata evaṃ vadāmi | [kintu] santanyamānaṃ cittamityato malinamiti vadāmi | (u) cittasantāno 'yaṃ lokasatyato 'sti na paramārthataḥ | [paramārthatastu] ayamanirvācyaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Objection) The mind, having experienced mere objects such as form and the rest, then grasps their marks (<s>nimitta</s>). The defilements born from marks defile the mind. Therefore it is said to be 'pure by nature.' (Reply) This is not correct. This mind has ceased at that very moment and does not possess the mark of defilement. The mind has perished at that very moment — by what defilement is it stained? (Objection) I say this because the mind does not perish at every moment. [Rather,] I say the mind is defiled because it is continuous (<s>santanyamāna</s>). (Reply) This continuity of mind exists only from the standpoint of conventional truth (<s>lokasatya</s>), not from the standpoint of ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>). [In the ultimate sense,] this is inexpressible (<s>anirvācya</s>).

body.text: lokasatyato 'pi santi bahavo doṣāḥ | cittamutpannavināśi | anutpannasyānabhinirvṛttasya kathaṃ santatiḥ | ato na cittaṃ prakṛtitaḥ pariśuddhamāgantukamalaipariśuddhakam | kintu tathāgataḥ cittaṃ nityaṃ sthāyīti vadatāṃ sattvānāṃ kṛta āha āgantukamalakliṣṭaṃ sat cittamapariśuddhamiti | kiñca kusīdasattvā ye śṛṇvanti cittaṃ prakṛtito 'pariśuddhamiti | te vadeyuḥ prakṛtiḥ na pratikāryeti | na te cittavyavadānamārabheran ityataḥ tathāgata āha prakṛtipariśuddhamiti ||
body.translated_text: Even from the standpoint of conventional truth, there are many faults. The mind arises and perishes [at every moment]. How can there be continuity for what has not arisen and not been produced? Therefore the mind is not pure by nature and impure through adventitious defilements. Rather, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the sake of beings who say that the mind is permanent and enduring, said: 'The mind, being defiled by adventitious defilements, is impure.' Furthermore, lazy beings (<s>kusīdasattva</s>) who hear that 'the mind is impure by nature' would say: 'Nature cannot be counteracted.' They would not undertake the purification of the mind. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> said 'it is pure by nature.'

body.text: cittasvabhāvavargastriṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the thirtieth chapter, the Chapter on the Nature of Mind (<s>cittasvabhāvavarga</s>).

body.text: 31 samprayogāsamprayogavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 31. Chapter on Association and Dissociation (<s>samprayogāsamprayogavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- kecidvadanti anuśayāścittasamprayuktā iti | kecidvadanti cittaviprayuktā iti |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Some say: 'The latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) are associated with the mind (<s>cittasamprayukta</s>).' Others say: 'They are dissociated from the mind (<s>cittaviprayukta</s>).'

body.text: (pṛ) kena kāraṇena vadanti cittasaṃprayuktā iti | kena kāraṇena vadanti cittaviprayuktā iti | (u) cittasamprayuktā iti | [idaṃ] paścādanuśayavarge vakṣyate | chandarāgādiḥ kleśānāṃ karma | tacca karma anuśayaiḥ samprayuktam | bhavatāṃ śāsane yadyapyucyate cittaviprayukto 'nuśayaḥ cittasamprayuktasaṃyojanaparyavasthānasya hetuṃ karotīti | na yuktamidam | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre- avidyāyoniśomanaskāramithyāsaṅkalpādibhyo rāgādīni saṃyojanani prādurbhavanti iti | na tu sūtramāha- anuyādutpadyata iti | yadyapi bhavatāṃ śāsana uktaṃ- cirābhyastasaṃyojanaparyavasthāpako 'nuśayo nāma iti | na yuktamidam | kasmāt | kāyikavacikādi karmāpi cirābhyastalakṣaṇam | tadapi anuśayābhāsaḥ cittaviprayuktasaṃskāraḥ syāt | na vastuto yujyate | yujyata iti cet sarve 'pi dharmāḥ pratyutpanna hetorupadyeran nātītahetoḥ | tathā ca na karmajo vipākaḥ syāt | manovijñānañca manaso jātaṃ na syāt | anuśayānāmeṣāṃ kṣaṇikatvāt kathaṃ punaste janakahetavaḥ syuḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) For what reason do they say they are associated with the mind? For what reason do they say they are dissociated from the mind? (Reply) 'Associated with the mind' — this will be explained later in the chapter on latent tendencies. Desire-and-passion (<s>chandarāga</s>) and the rest constitute the action of defilements. And that action is associated with latent tendencies. Although in your teaching it is said that 'a latent tendency dissociated from mind produces the cause of fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) and afflictions (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) that are associated with mind' — this is not correct. Why? Because it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'From ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), unwise attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>), wrong resolve (<s>mithyāsaṅkalpa</s>), and the rest, fetters such as passion (<s>rāga</s>) and others arise.' But the <s>sūtra</s> does not say: 'From latent tendencies they arise.' Although in your teaching it is said: 'That which causes the operation of fetters and afflictions long practiced is called a latent tendency' — this is not correct. Why? Because bodily, verbal, and other <s>karmas</s> also have the characteristic of being long practiced. They too would be semblances of latent tendencies and would be formations dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>). This is not correct in reality. If you say it is correct — then all <s>dharmas</s> too would arise from a present cause and not from a past cause. And in that case, there would be no ripened fruit (<s>vipāka</s>) born of <s>karma</s>. And mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) born of mind would not exist. Since these latent tendencies are momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), how could they be generative causes?

body.text: (pṛ) sahalakṣaṇo janakahetuḥ | (u) tadapi na yuktam | hetuphalayorayaugapadyāt | tacca paścāt pradīpadṛṣṭānte vakṣyate | ato na vaktavyamanuśayāścittaviprayuktā iti ||
body.translated_text: (Objection) The generative cause has the characteristic of co-existence (<s>sahalakṣaṇa</s>). (Reply) That too is not correct — because of the non-simultaneity of cause and effect. This will be explained later in the illustration of the lamp. Therefore it should not be said that the latent tendencies are dissociated from mind.

body.text: samprayogasamprayogavarga ekatriṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the thirty-first chapter, the Chapter on Association and Dissociation (<s>samprayogāsamprayogavarga</s>).

body.text: 32 atītakarmavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 32. Chapter on Past <s>Karma</s> (<s>atītakarmavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- kāśyapīyā vadanti ananubhūtavipākaṃ karma atīte 'dhvani asti | anyadatīte nāsti iti | ucyate | tatkarma yadi vinaṣṭaṃ tadā [tat] atītamatītameva | yadi avinaṣṭam | tadā nityaṃ bhavet | vinaṣṭamiti atītasya nāmāntaram | tadā vinaṣṭaṃ sat punarvinaśyet | tatkarma vipākasya hetukṛtyaṃ kṛtvā niruddham | vipākaḥ punarūrdhvajanmavartī | yathoktaṃ sūtre- asmin satīdamutpadyata iti | yathā payo nirodhe daghno hetukṛtyaṃ karoti | kimatītakarmavikalpena | yuktamiti yadi matam | anyo hetāvasti doṣaḥ | kathaṃ vinā kāraṇaṃ vijñānamutpadyate | yathā payaso 'bhāve kiṃ dadhi bhavati | cāturbhautikakāyavā gādīnāmabhāve karma kimāśritya bhavet | ityevamādayaḥ | yanmayā pūrvamukto 'tītasya doṣaḥ | sa idaṃ pratibrūyāt ||
body.translated_text: The treatise says: The <s>Kāśyapīyas</s> say: '<s>Karma</s> whose ripening has not yet been experienced exists in the past time-period. Other past [things] do not exist.' It is replied: If that <s>karma</s> has been destroyed, then it is past and nothing but past. If it has not been destroyed, then it would be permanent. 'Destroyed' is another name for 'past.' Then, being destroyed, it would again be destroyed. That <s>karma</s>, having performed its causal function for the ripening (<s>vipāka</s>), has ceased. The ripening further belongs to a subsequent birth. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'When this exists, that arises.' Just as milk, upon ceasing, performs the causal function for curds. What need is there for speculating about past <s>karma</s>? If you think this is correct — there is another fault regarding the cause. How does consciousness arise without a cause? Just as in the absence of milk, how can there be curds? And in the absence of a body composed of the four elements (<s>cāturbhautikakāya</s>), wind, and the rest, upon what would <s>karma</s> depend? And so forth. The fault regarding the past that I have previously stated — he should reply to that.

body.text: atītakarmavargo dvāviṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the thirty-second chapter, the Chapter on Past <s>Karma</s> (<s>atītakarmavarga</s>).

body.text: 33 ratnadvayavivādavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 33. Chapter on the Dispute Regarding the Two Jewels (<s>ratnadvayavivādavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- mahīśāsakā vadanti tathāgata saṅghavartī iti | ucyate | yadi mataṃ tathāgataḥ catasṛṣu pariṣatsu antargataḥ yaduta sattvapariṣat prāṇipariṣat manuṣyapariṣat āryapariṣat iti | tadā na doṣaḥ | yadi mataṃ tathāgataḥ śrāvakapariṣadi antargata iti | tadāsti doṣaḥ | dharmaṃ śrutvā saṃvillābhinaḥ śrāvakā ityucyante | tathāgatastu vibhinnalakṣaṇa ityatastatra nāntargataḥ |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: The <s>Mahīśāsakas</s> say that the <s>Tathāgata</s> dwells within the <s>Saṅgha</s>. It is replied: If the view is that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is included within the four assemblies (<s>pariṣad</s>) — namely, the assembly of beings (<s>sattvapariṣad</s>), the assembly of living creatures (<s>prāṇipariṣad</s>), the assembly of humans (<s>manuṣyapariṣad</s>), and the assembly of Noble Ones (<s>āryapariṣad</s>) — then there is no fault. But if the view is that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is included within the assembly of disciples (<s>śrāvakapariṣad</s>), then there is a fault. Those who, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, gain understanding are called disciples (<s>śrāvaka</s>). But the <s>Tathāgata</s> has a distinct characteristic — therefore he is not included therein.

body.text: (pṛ) saṅghārāmāgragasya tathāgatasya dāyakaḥ puruṣaḥ saṅghadāyaka ityucyate | (u) dānamidaṃ keṣāṃ saṅghasambandhi | sūtramidaṃ kiñcidbhraṣṭam | idaṃ vaktavyaṃ syāt buddhasaṅghasambandhīti |
body.translated_text: (Objection) A person who gives to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who stands at the head of the monastery (<s>saṅghārāma</s>), is called a giver to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. (Reply) This gift — to whom does it pertain as related to the <s>Saṅgha</s>? This <s>sūtra</s> is somewhat corrupted. It should be stated as 'related to the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'

body.text: (pṛ) bhagavān gautamīmavocat- imaṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghe dehi | tadā ahamapi pūjito bhaviṣyāmi saṅgho 'pi ca | iti | (u) ahaṃ pūjito bhaviṣyāmīti saṅghapūjābhiprāyeṇa bhagavānavocat | yathoktaṃ sūtre yo rogaprekṣī sa māṃ paśyati | iti | (pṛ) kecidāryaguṇasamanvitāḥ śāriputrādayaḥ saṅghāntargatāḥ, lakṣaṇasāmyāt bhagavānapyevam | (u) yadi lakṣaṇasāmyāditi | sarve pṛthagjanāḥ asatvākhyāśca saṅghapraviṣṭāḥ syuḥ | na yujyato vastutaḥ | ato jñāyate na bhagavān saṅgāntargata iti | kiñca bhagavān na saṅghakarmapraviṣṭaḥ nāpi anyasaṅghavastusamaḥ | ratnatrayaviśeṣāt na bhagavān saṅghāntargataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Objection) The Blessed One said to <s>Gautamī</s>: 'Give this robe to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Then I too will be worshipped, and the <s>Saṅgha</s> as well.'
