body.text: yat cittaṃ vyagraṃ muharmuhurālambhakaṃ sa vitarkaḥ | samāhitacittasyāpyasti audārikatā sūkṣmatā | [tatra yat] audārikaṃ sa vitarkaḥ | sūkṣmasamādhānābhāvādaudārikaṃ cittamityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhagavānāha- savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ prathamadhyānamupasampadya viharāmīti | ataḥ prathamadhyānamasūkṣmasamāhitamiti savitarkaṃ bhavati | yā cittasya vyagratā kiñcitsūkṣmatā sa vicāraḥ | imau dvau traidhātukau | cittasyaudārikasūkṣmalakṣaṇatvāt | vyagraṃ vikṣiptaṃ cittaṃ vitarkavicārau bhavataḥ | tallakṣaṇatvāt sarvatra syātām | apratyakṣaṃ vastu anumityā jñāyate | evaṃ syānnaivaṃ syādityabhyūho vitarkaḥ | ato 'pratyakṣavastuno 'nuvitarkaḥ samyagvitarko vā mithyāvitarko vā iti taṃ kathayāmaḥ | nirvikalpānuvitarkaḥ samyak dṛṣṭirityākhyāyate | ayaṃ tridhājñātaḥ | mithyāvitarko viparītamanaskāraḥ yadanitye nityamityādiḥ | samyagvitarkaḥ yadapratilabdhaṃ tattvajñānamanumitilakṣaṇena jñānena labdhvā yogī nirvedhabhāgīyakuśalamūle vartate | iyaṃ kṣāntirityucyate | evamanyamārgeṇānuyāyi anumitijñānaṃ samyagvitarkaḥ | tatra yat saṃzñānusmaraṇavikalpāpoḍhaṃ tat pratyakṣamityucyate | tasminneva vitarke anena hetunā evaṃ bhavati anena hetunā naivaṃ bhavati iti cintanā vicāraṇā vā sa vicāraḥ |
body.translated_text: That which is the mind's agitation, grasping objects from moment to moment — that is applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>). Even in a concentrated mind there is grossness and subtlety. Therein, what is gross is applied thought. Because of the absence of subtle concentration, the mind is called 'gross.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Blessed One said: I enter and abide in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, which is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought.' Therefore the first <s>dhyāna</s>, being not subtly concentrated, has applied thought. That which is a slight subtlety of the mind's agitation is sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>). These two exist throughout the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>), because the mind has the characteristics of grossness and subtlety. The agitated and distracted mind has [both] applied and sustained thought, because it possesses their characteristics — they would exist everywhere. An imperceptible thing is known by inference. 'It may be thus, it may not be thus' — such deliberation is applied thought. Therefore, regarding an imperceptible thing, investigation (<s>anuvitarka</s>) is either right applied thought or wrong applied thought — so we explain it. Non-conceptual investigation is designated as right view (<s>samyag dṛṣṭi</s>). This is known to be threefold. Wrong applied thought is perverted attention, such as [perceiving] permanence in what is impermanent, and so forth. Right applied thought is when, having obtained the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) that was not previously attained, through inferential knowledge, the <s>yogin</s> abides in the wholesome roots conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīyakuśalamūla</s>). This is called 'acceptance' (<s>kṣānti</s>). In this way, inferential knowledge that follows another path is right applied thought. Therein, that which is free from conceptual proliferation of designation and recollection is called 'direct perception' (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). In that very applied thought, 'by this reason it is thus, by this reason it is not thus' — such deliberation and examination is sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- vitarkavicārāvekāgratāntargatāviti | kathamidam | (u) maivam | kasmāt | uktaṃ khalu bhavadbhirghaṇṭātāḍanadṛṣṭāntaḥ | ādyaśabda[samo] vitarkaḥ | anyaśabda[samo] vicāraḥ | taraṅgadṛṣṭāntaśca [uktaḥ] | ya audārikaḥ [tatsamo] vitarkaḥ | yaḥ sūkṣmaḥ [tatsamo] vicāraḥ | kāladeśabhedānna cittaikāgratā syāt | nirvikalpakatvātpañca vijñānāni na savitarkavicāralakṣaṇāni bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: 'Applied and sustained thought are included within one-pointedness of mind.' How is this? (Answer) Not so. Why? For you have stated the analogy of striking a bell. The first sound is like applied thought; the subsequent sound is like sustained thought. And the analogy of waves has been stated: what is gross is like applied thought; what is subtle is like sustained thought. Because of the distinction of time and place, there would not be one-pointedness of mind. Because the five consciousnesses are non-conceptual, they do not have the characteristics of applied and sustained thought.

body.text: vitarkavicāravargo dvinavatitamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the ninety-second chapter, the Chapter on Applied and Sustained Thought (<s>vitarkavicāravarga</s>).

body.text: 93 anyacaitasikavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 93. Chapter on Other Mental Factors (<s>anyacaitasikavarga</s>)

body.text: yat kuśalasyānācaraṇaṃ mithyācaraṇaṃ vā sa pramādaḥ | na pramādākhyo 'nya ekadharmo 'sti | tasmin samaye cittasamudācāraḥ pramādaḥ ityucyate | tadviparīto 'pramādaḥ | yaḥ kuśalaścittasamudācāro 'pramādādanyaḥ so 'pi dharmāntaram | akuśalānugataṃ cittaṃ pramādaḥ | kuśalānugatantu apramādaḥ |
body.translated_text: The non-practice of what is wholesome, or wrong practice — that is heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). There is no single separate <s>dharma</s> called 'heedlessness.' At that time, the mental activity is called 'heedlessness.' Its opposite is heedfulness (<s>apramāda</s>). Whatever wholesome mental activity other than heedfulness — that too is a distinct <s>dharma</s>. The mind accompanied by the unwholesome is heedlessness; accompanied by the wholesome is heedfulness.

body.text: kuśalamūlamiti alobho 'dveṣo 'mohaḥ | yoniśomanaskārāśiraskānāsaktiralobhaḥ | maitrīkaruṇāśiraskaḥ krodhānutpādo 'dveṣaḥ | samyadgarśanaśirasko 'bhrānto 'viparyayaḥ amohaḥ | alobho nāma nāstyekaṃ dharmāntaram |
body.translated_text: Wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) are: non-greed (<s>alobha</s>), non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>), and non-delusion (<s>amoha</s>). Non-attachment headed by proper attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>) is non-greed. The non-arising of anger headed by loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) is non-hatred. Being unconfused and non-perverted, headed by right view (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), is non-delusion. As for non-greed — there is no single separate <s>dharma</s> [called thus].

body.text: kecidāhuḥ lobhābhāvo 'lobha iti | na yuktamidam | kasmāt | lobhābhāvo 'bhāvadharmaḥ | kathamabhāvo dharmasya hetuḥ | adveṣāmohāvapyevam | tatrāyāṇāmakuśalamūlānāṃ viparītāni trīṇi kuśalamūlānyucyante | madamānādayo 'pyakuśalamūlāni syuḥ | saṃkṣepatastrīṇyevākuśalamūlānyuktāni | vakṣyante cākuśalavarge |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'The absence of greed is non-greed.' This is not valid. Why? The absence of greed is a non-existent <s>dharma</s>. How can non-existence be the cause of a <s>dharma</s>? Non-hatred and non-delusion are likewise. Therein, the opposites of these unwholesome roots are called the three wholesome roots. Intoxication (<s>mada</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and the rest would also be unwholesome roots. In brief, only three unwholesome roots have been stated. They will be explained in the Chapter on the Unwholesome.

body.text: avyākṛtamūlamiti | kecidvadanti- catvāryavyākṛtamūlāni- tṛṣṇā dṛṣṭiḥ mānamavidyeti | [anye] kecidāhuḥ trīṇi tṛṣṇā avidyā prajñā iti | naitadbhagavatoktam | avyākṛtānugaṃ cittaṃ yaddhetujaṃ sa heturavyākṛtamūlaṃ bhavati | kāyavākkarmaṇī prāyo 'vyākṛtānuge iti cittamutpadyate | avyākṛtacittamavyākṛtamūlamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Regarding indeterminate roots (<s>avyākṛtamūla</s>): some say there are four indeterminate roots — craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Others say there are three — craving, ignorance, and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). This was not stated by the Blessed One. Whatever mind accompanied by the indeterminate is born from a cause — that cause is the indeterminate root. Bodily and verbal actions are for the most part accompanied by the indeterminate — thus the mind that arises [in those contexts] is called the indeterminate root.

body.text: cittasamācaraṇakāle yat kāyaścittaṃ dauṣṭhalyavigataṃ praśāntaṃ bhavati | tasmin samaye praśrabdhirityucyate |
body.translated_text: At the time of the mind's activity, when the body and mind become free from restlessness (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) and tranquil — at that time it is called tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>).

body.text: nānāvastuṣu citta [samācaraṇa]kāle upekṣetyucyate | yat vedanāsu anabhijñā cittasamācaraṇaṃ sopekṣā | dhyāneṣu yat sukhaduḥkhaviviktaṃ vimuktiparāyaṇaṃ cittasamācaraṇaṃ sopekṣā | saptabodhyaṅgeṣu alīnamakampasamatādi yaccittasamācaraṇaṃ sopekṣā | prītidaurmanasyavinirmuktaṃ samatādipratilabdhaṃ cittamupekṣā | caturṣu apramāṇeṣu vairamaitravigataṃ cittamupekṣā | evaṃ nānādharmāṇāṃ virodhāccaitasikānāṃ viśeṣo 'pramāṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: At the time of the mind's activity toward various objects, it is called equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). That which is the mind's activity without awareness regarding feelings is equanimity. In the <s>dhyānas</s>, the mind's activity that is separated from pleasure and suffering and directed toward liberation is equanimity. Among the seven limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the mind's activity that is the equilibrium of neither sinking nor being agitated, and the like, is equanimity. The mind that is freed from joy and mental displeasure, having attained equilibrium and the rest, is equanimity. Among the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the mind free from hostility and [partial] friendliness is equanimity. Thus, because various <s>dharmas</s> are opposed [to each other], the distinctions among mental factors are immeasurable.

body.text: anyacaitasikavargastrinavatitamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the ninety-third chapter, the Chapter on Other Mental Factors (<s>anyacaitasikavarga</s>).

body.text: 94 viprayuktasaṃskāravargaḥ
body.translated_text: 94. Chapter on Formations Disjoined from Mind (<s>viprayuktasaṃskāravarga</s>)

body.text: cittaviprayuktasaṃskārāḥ yaduta prāptiḥ, aprāptiḥ asaṃjñisamāpattiḥ nirodhasamāpattiḥ āsaṃjñikaṃ jīvitendriyaṃ jātiḥ vyayaḥ sthitiḥ anyathātvaṃ jarā maraṇaṃ nāmakāyaḥ padakāyo vyañjanakāyaḥ pṛthagjanatvaṃ ityādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Formations disjoined from mind (<s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>) are: attainment (<s>prāpti</s>), non-attainment (<s>aprāpti</s>), the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>), the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), the state of non-perception (<s>āsaṃjñika</s>), the life faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>), birth (<s>jāti</s>), decay (<s>vyaya</s>), duration (<s>sthiti</s>), alteration (<s>anyathātva</s>), aging (<s>jarā</s>), death (<s>maraṇa</s>), the collection of names (<s>nāmakāya</s>), the collection of words (<s>padakāya</s>), the collection of syllables (<s>vyañjanakāya</s>), the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjanatva</s>), and so forth.

body.text: prāptiriti | sattvānāṃ kṛte dharmāṇāṃ samanvāgamaḥ prāptiḥ | pratyutpannādhvani pañcaskandhasamanvāgataḥ sattvaḥ prāpta ityucyate | atītādhvani yāni kuśalākuśalakarmāṇi ananubhūtavipākāni | taddharmasamanvāgataḥ sattvaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- kuśaladharmasamanvāgato 'kuśaladharmasamanvāgataśca pudgala iti | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- atītakuśalākuśalakāyavākkarmasamanvāgataḥ | yathā pravrajitaḥ atītaśīlasaṃvarasamanvāgata iti | kathamidam | (u) sarveṣāṃ samanvāgamaḥ | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre yaḥ puṇyaṃ pāpañca karoti | tasya tadvidyamānameva | tat dvayaṃ tatkāyamanupatati rūpānupāticchāyāvat iti | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- mṛtasya puṇyaṃ na praṇaśyati yaduta phalaprāpakameva | yadasamanvāgataṃ puṇyapāpaṃ karma na tatphalaprāpakam | tāni karmāṇi naśyanti | iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Prāpti</s> (acquisition): the coming-together of <s>dharmas</s> for the sake of beings is <s>prāpti</s>. In the present time-period (<s>pratyutpannādhvan</s>), a being who is endowed with the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) is said to have 'acquired.' In the past time-period (<s>atītādhvan</s>), whatever wholesome and unwholesome <s>karmas</s> whose ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) has not been experienced — a being endowed with those <s>dharmas</s> [is also said to have acquired them]. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>pudgala</s> (person) is endowed with wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and endowed with unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' (Question) Some say: one is endowed with past wholesome and unwholesome bodily and verbal <s>karmas</s>. For example, one who has gone forth (<s>pravrajita</s>) is said to be endowed with the past moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>). How is this? (Answer) There is acquisition (<s>samanvāgama</s>) of all. Why? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whoever performs merit and sin — those [merit and sin] exist for him. Those two follow his body, like a shadow that follows a form.' Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The merit of one who has died does not perish — namely, that which leads to the obtaining of the fruit. That merit or sin which is not acquired (<s>asamanvāgata</s>) does not lead to the obtaining of the fruit. Those <s>karmas</s> perish.'

body.text: (pṛ) atītasaṃvarasya na samanvāgamaḥ syāt | kasmāt | bhavatoktam atītadharmo niruddhaḥ | anāgato 'vidyamāna iti | pratyutpannaśca na sadā kuśalacittavattve
body.translated_text: (Question) There should be no acquisition of past restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). Why? You have stated that a past <s>dharma</s> has ceased, and a future one is non-existent. And the present [mind] is not always capable of being endowed with a wholesome mind

body.text: kṣamaḥ | kathaṃ śīlasaṃvarasamanvāgataḥ syāt | (u) puruṣaḥ pratyutpannena saṃvareṇa samanvāgato nātītena | yathā pratyutpannakliṣṭāt kliṣṭam, tathā pratyutpannaśīlāt śīlaṃ bhavati | nātītāt | [yaḥ] pūrvaṃ svīkṛtyāparityaktavān [saḥ] atītasamanvāgata ityucyate |
body.translated_text: . How would one be endowed with moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>)? (Answer) A person is endowed with present restraint, not with past [restraint]. Just as from a presently defiled [mind] comes what is defiled, so from present morality comes morality — not from what is past. One who formerly accepted [the restraint] and has not relinquished it is said to be 'endowed with what is past.'

body.text: (pṛ) ābhidharmikā āhuḥ sattvā anāgatādhvanīnakuśalākuśalacittasamanvāgatā iti | tatkathamidam | (u) na samanvāgatāḥ | kasmāt | akṛtābhyāgamāt | ato 'nāgatāsamanvāgamaḥ prāptirityucyate | na cāsti prāptyākhyaḥ pṛthakcittaviprayuktadharmaḥ | tadviparitāprāptirapi nāsti pṛthakcittaviprayuktadharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> (Abhidharma scholars) say that beings are endowed with future unwholesome and wholesome minds. How is this? (Answer) They are not endowed [with them]. Why? Because what has not been done has not [yet] arrived. Therefore, non-acquisition of the future is called <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition) [by them]. But there is no separate <s>dharma</s> dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta</s>) called '<s>prāpti</s>.' The opposite — <s>aprāpti</s> (non-acquisition) — is also not a separate <s>dharma</s> dissociated from mind.

body.text: asaṃjñisamāpattirityayaṃ samāpattidharmo nāsti | kasmāt | na hi nirudhyante pṛthagjanānāṃ cittacaitasikadharmā iti paścādvakṣyate | cittacaitasikānāṃ sūkṣmatayā duravabodhāt asaṃjñīti nāma | āsaṃjñikamapyevam | nirodhasamāpattiriti | cittanirodhe samudācārābhāvānnirodhasamāpattiriti nāma | sa ca nāsti dharmāntaram | nirvāṇavat | jīvitendriyamiti | karmapratyayaḥ pañcaskandhasantāno jīvitamityucyate | jīvitañca karmaṇo mūlamiti jīvitendriyamityucyate | jātiriti | pañcaskandhānāṃ pratyutpannādhvā jātiḥ | pratyutpannādhvaparityāgo vyayaḥ | santanyamānatvaṃ sthitiḥ | sthitipariṇāmo 'nyathātvam | na santi pṛthakjātivyayādayo dharmāḥ | bhagavataḥ śāsanaṃ gabhīraṃ yatpratyayānāṃ sāmagryā dharmā
body.translated_text: '<s>Asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>' (attainment of non-perception): this <s>dharma</s> of attainment does not exist. Why? Because the mind and mental factors of ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) do not cease — this will be stated later. Because of the subtlety and difficulty of understanding mind and mental factors, it is called '<s>asaṃjñī</s>' (non-perception). The same applies to '<s>āsaṃjñika</s>' (the realm of non-perception). '<s>Nirodhasamāpatti</s>' (attainment of cessation): in the cessation of mind, because of the absence of activity, it is called '<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>.' But that is not a separate <s>dharma</s> — like <s>nirvāṇa</s>. '<s>Jīvitendriya</s>' (life faculty): the continuum of the five <s>skandhas</s> conditioned by <s>karma</s> is called 'life' (<s>jīvita</s>). And life, being the root of <s>karma</s>, is called '<s>jīvitendriya</s>' (life faculty). '<s>Jāti</s>' (birth): the present time-period of the five <s>skandhas</s> is <s>jāti</s>. The relinquishing of the present time-period is <s>vyaya</s> (decay). The state of being continued is <s>sthiti</s> (duration). The transformation of duration is <s>anyathātva</s> (alteration). There are no separate <s>dharmas</s> such as birth, decay, and so forth. The teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is profound — that <s>dharmas</s> arise from the totality of conditions

body.text: utpadyanta iti | ato nāsti kaściddharmo dharmāntarasyotpādakaḥ | uktaṃ hi- cakṣūrūpādayaścakṣurvijñānasya pratyayā iti | na tatroktaṃ jātirastīti | ato nāsti jātirityanavadyam |
body.translated_text: . Therefore there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that produces another <s>dharma</s>. For it is stated: 'The eye, form, and so forth are the conditions of eye-consciousness.' It is not stated there that '<s>jāti</s> (birth) exists.' Therefore, [saying] there is no <s>jāti</s> is blameless.

body.text: kiñca vadanti jātyādayo dharmā ekakālīnā iti | ya ekakālīnaḥ sa niruddha eva | tatra jātyādayaḥ kimarthā iti vicārayitavyam | dvādaśanidāne ca bhagavān svayamāha jāterartham | yā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmin tasmin [sattvanikāye] jātiḥ skandhānāṃ pratilābhaḥ....... [sā jātiḥ] iti | ataḥ pratyutpannādhvani skandhānāmādyalābho jātiḥ | āha ca- skandhānāṃ cyutirantahāṇirmaraṇamiti | āha ca- skandhānāṃ jīrṇatā bhugnatā jareti | [ato] na pṛthak sto jarāmaraṇadharmau |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, they say that <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>jāti</s> and the rest are simultaneous. What is simultaneous has already ceased. Therefore, what purpose do <s>jāti</s> and the rest serve? This must be examined. And in the twelve-fold chain of dependent origination (<s>dvādaśanidāna</s>), the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself stated the meaning of <s>jāti</s>: 'The birth of those various beings in those various classes of beings — the obtaining of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) ... that is <s>jāti</s>.' Therefore, in the present time-period, the initial obtaining of the <s>skandhas</s> is <s>jāti</s>. And he said: 'The falling away of the <s>skandhas</s>, their final destruction — that is <s>maraṇa</s> (death).' And he said: 'The aging, the bending of the <s>skandhas</s> — that is <s>jarā</s> (old age).' Therefore old age and death are not separate <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: nāmakāya iti | vyañjanebhya utpannaṃ nāma yathā vadanti devadatta iti | yathāvyañjanamarthasādhanaṃ padam | vyañjanāni akṣarāṇi | kecidāhuḥ- nāmapadavyañjanakāyāścitaviprayuktasaṃskārā iti | tadayuktam | dharmā ime vāksvabhāvā dharmāyatanasaṃgṛhītāḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Nāmakāya</s>' (word-body): a name (<s>nāma</s>) arises from syllables (<s>vyañjana</s>), such as when they say '<s>Devadatta</s>.' A <s>pada</s> (word/phrase) is that which accomplishes meaning according to its syllables. <s>Vyañjanas</s> are letters (<s>akṣara</s>). Some say that name-bodies, phrase-bodies, and syllable-bodies are <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta</s>). This is incorrect. These <s>dharmas</s> have the nature of speech (<s>vāk</s>) and are included in the <s>dharmāyatana</s> (mental sense-base).

body.text: (pṛ) asti pṛthakagjanatvaṃ nāma cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra iti | [kecidvadanti] | kathamidam | (u) na pṛthagjanatvaṃ puthagjanādanyat | yadyasti tadanyat | anye ghaṭatvādayo
body.translated_text: (Question) 'There exists a separate [dharma called] <s>pṛthagjanatva</s> (the state of being an ordinary person), which is a <s>saṃskāra</s> dissociated from mind' — [some say]. How is this? (Answer) <s>Pṛthagjanatva</s> is not other than the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). If it were other [than him],

body.text: 'pyanubhūyeran | saṃkhyāpariṇāmaikatvapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvādayo dharmāḥ pṛthak syuḥ | tīrthikānāṃ hi sūtreṣūktaṃ- anyo ghaṭo 'nyat ghaṭatvam | ghaṭatvaṃ pratītya jñāyate 'yaṃ ghaṭa iti | rūpamanyat rūpatvamanyat iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | tattvaṃ tatsvabhāvaḥ | yadi bravīṣi pṛthagjanatvamanyaditi | tadā rūpaṃ svabhāvaṃ vinā syāt, rūpatvāpekṣitvāt | tattu na yujyate | ato gabhīramananuvicintya vavīṣi- asti pṛthagjanatvaṃ pṛthagiti |
body.translated_text: then other [universals] such as 'pot-ness' (<s>ghaṭatva</s>) and so forth would also be experienced [as separate entities]. [Properties such as] number, transformation, unity, plurality, conjunction, disjunction, priority, posteriority, and so forth would be separate <s>dharmas</s>. For in the <s>sūtras</s> of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist philosophers) it is stated: 'The pot is one thing, pot-ness is another. Depending on pot-ness, it is known that this is a pot. Form is one thing, form-ness is another.' This is incorrect. Why? The essence (<s>tattva</s>) [of a thing] is its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). If you say that <s>pṛthagjanatva</s> is something other [than the person], then form would exist without its own nature, since it would depend on form-ness. But that is untenable. Therefore, without deeply reflecting on the profound [teaching], you speak [superficially] saying 'there exists <s>pṛthagjanatva</s> as a separate [entity].'

body.text: ābhidharmikāstīrthikagranthānabhyasyābhidharmaśāstramāracayanto vadanti santi pṛthakagjanatvādayo dharmāḥ pṛthagiti | anya ābhidharmikā api vadanti | santi pṛthak tathatābhūtakoṭipratītyasamutpādādayo 'saṃskṛtadharmā iti | ato gabhīramimaṃ nayamanuvicintyamā rutamanuvartadhvam ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s>, having studied the texts of the <s>tīrthikas</s>, compose the <s>Abhidharmaśāstra</s> and say that <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>pṛthagjanatva</s> and the rest exist separately. Other <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> too say: 'There exist separately unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>asaṃskṛtadharma</s>) such as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (reality-limit), <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and so forth.' Therefore, having deeply reflected on this profound method, do not follow mere hearsay.

body.text: viprayuktasaṃskāravargaścaturnavatitamaḥ
body.translated_text: This is the ninety-fourth chapter: the chapter on <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) dissociated [from mind] (<s>viprayuktasaṃskāra</s>).

body.text: iti
body.translated_text: Thus the section on the Truth of Suffering (<s>duḥkhasatyaskandha</s>) is completed.

body.text: duḥkhasatyaskandhaḥ samāptaḥ ||

atha samudayasatyaskandhaḥ
95 samudayasatyaskandhe karmādhikāre karmalakṣaṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text:
Now the section on the Truth of Origination (<s>samudayasatyaskandha</s>).
95. In the section on the Truth of Origination, in the topic of <s>karma</s>: the chapter on the definition of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: śāstramāha- duḥkhasatyaṃ parisamāpya samudayasatyamidānīṃ vakṣyata iti | tatra karma kleśāśca samudayasatyam | trividhaṃ karma kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ mānasikamiti | kāyena kṛtaṃ karma kāyikam | tat trividhaṃ akuśalaṃ prāṇātipātādi | kuśalaṃ caityavandanādi | avyākṛtaṃ tṛṇacchedādi |
body.translated_text: The <s>śāstra</s> states: Having completed the Truth of Suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), the Truth of Origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>) will now be explained. Therein, <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) constitute the Truth of Origination. <s>Karma</s> is threefold: bodily (<s>kāyika</s>), verbal (<s>vācika</s>), and mental (<s>mānasika</s>). Action performed by the body is bodily <s>karma</s>. That is threefold: unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>) — such as taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>) and so forth; wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) — such as worshipping a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) and so forth; indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — such as cutting grass and so forth.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi kāyena kṛtaṃ kāyikam | tadā ghaṭādidravyamapi kāyikaṃ karma syāt | kāyena kṛtatvāt | (u) ghaṭādi kāyikakarmaṇaḥ phalam na kāyikaṃ karma | hetuphalayorbhedāt | (pṛ) na syātkāyikaṃ karma | kasmāt | kāyaspandanakṛtaṃ kāyikaṃ karma | saṃskṛtadharmāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvāt na syātspandanam | (u) idaṃ kṣaṇikavarge pratyuktaṃ yadekasmin dharma utpadyamāne 'nyasyāpacaya upacayo vā [tat] kāyikaṃ karmeti | (pṛ) tathā cet kāya eva kāyikaṃ karma bhavet | anyatrotpadyamānatvāt | na tu kāyena kṛtaṃ kāyikaṃ karma | (u) kāyaḥ karmakriyāyāḥ sādhanam | kāye 'nyatrotpadyamāne puṇyapāpasamudayaḥ karma | ato na kāya eva karma | (pṛ) puṇyapāpasamudayo 'vijñaptiḥ | kāyavijñaptiḥ katham | (u) kāye 'nyatrotpadyamāne kriyamāṇā vijñaptiḥ kāyavijñaptirbhavati | (pṛ) kāyavijñaptiḥ kuśalā vākuśalā vā | kāyastu na tathā | ato na kāyavijñaptiḥ syāt | (u) cittabalāt kāye 'nyatrotpadyamāne karma samudeti | atastatsamudayo yadi vā kuśalo [yadi vā] akuśalaḥ na tu sākṣātkāyikaḥ | tathā vācikakarmāpi | na tu tat sākṣācchabdavyavahāra[rūpam] |
body.translated_text: (Question) If what is done by the body is bodily [karma], then even substances such as pots and the like would be bodily <s>karma</s>, being done by the body. (Answer) A pot and the like are the fruit of bodily <s>karma</s>, not bodily <s>karma</s> [itself] — because of the distinction between cause and fruit. (Question) There should be no bodily <s>karma</s>. Why? Bodily <s>karma</s> is that which is done by the movement (<s>spandana</s>) of the body. Since conditioned <s>dharmas</s> are momentary, there should be no movement. (Answer) This was answered in the chapter on momentariness — namely, that when one <s>dharma</s> arises and there is the decrease or increase of another, that is bodily <s>karma</s>. (Question) If so, bodily <s>karma</s> would be the body itself, since it arises elsewhere [at a different location]. It would not be [karma] done by the body. (Answer) The body is the instrument of the activity of <s>karma</s>. When the body arises at another [location], the accumulation of merit and sin is <s>karma</s>. Therefore <s>karma</s> is not the body itself. (Question) The accumulation of merit and sin is <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action). How is there bodily <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action)? (Answer) When the body arises at another [location], the <s>vijñapti</s> (manifestation) that is being produced is bodily <s>vijñapti</s>. (Question) Bodily <s>vijñapti</s> is either wholesome or unwholesome. But the body is not thus [wholesome or unwholesome]. Therefore there should be no bodily <s>vijñapti</s>. (Answer) Through the force of the mind, when the body arises at another [location], <s>karma</s> accumulates. Therefore, whether that accumulation is wholesome or unwholesome, it is not directly bodily. Similarly with verbal <s>karma</s> as well — it is not directly in the form of speech-activity

body.text: cittabalāt śabdavyavahārasamuditaṃ karma kuśalamakuśalaṃ vācikaṃ karmetyucyate | evaṃ mānasaṃ karmāpi | ya imaṃ sattvaṃ hanmīti adhyavasitacitto bhavati | tasya tasmin samaye pāpaṃ samudeti | evaṃ puṇyamapi |
body.translated_text: . Through the force of the mind, <s>karma</s> that accumulates together with speech-activity — whether wholesome or unwholesome — is called verbal <s>karma</s>. Similarly with mental <s>karma</s> as well. When one resolves with the thought 'I shall kill this being,' at that time sin accumulates for him. Similarly with merit as well.

body.text: (pṛ) yathā kāyavāgbhyāṃ pṛthagasti karma | [tathā] mano 'pi mānasakarmaṇo 'nyadeva | (u) tat dvidhā bhavati mana eva mānasaṃ karma manasa utpannaṃ vā mānasaṃ karma iti | sattvaṃ hanmīti yadadhyavasitaṃ manaḥ tadakuśalaṃ mana eva manasaṃ karma | tatkarma pāpasañcayarūpaṃ kāyikavācikakarmātiśāyakam | yadi cittamanadhyavasitam | tadā manaḥ karmaṇo 'nyat |
body.translated_text: (Question) Just as there is <s>karma</s> separate from body and speech, so too the mind should be something different from mental <s>karma</s>. (Answer) That is twofold: either the mind itself is mental <s>karma</s>, or what arises from the mind is mental <s>karma</s>. The mind that has resolved 'I shall kill the being' — that unwholesome mind itself is mental <s>karma</s>. That <s>karma</s>, being in the form of an accumulation of sin, surpasses bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>. If the mind has not [thus] resolved, then the mind is other than the <s>karma</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) vijñaptilakṣaṇaṃ jñātam | vijñaptita utpanno 'nyaḥkarmasamudayaḥ | kiṃ [tasya] lakṣaṇam | (u) tadavijñaptireva | (pṛ) kiṃ kevalamasti kāyikavācikāvijñaptireva na mānasikāvijñaptiḥ | (u) maivam | kasmāt | nahyasti tatra kāraṇaṃ kevalaṃ kāyikavācikāvijñaptirevāsti na mānasikāvijñaptiriti | sūtre coktaṃ dvidhā karma- cetanā vā cetayitvā vā [karme]ti | cetanā mānasaṃ karma | cetayitvā [karma] trividham- cetanāsañcitaṃ karma kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmeti | tatra mānasaṃ karma gurutaramiti paścādvakṣyate | gurutarakarmasañcitamavijñaptyākhyaṃ sadā santānena pravartate | ato jñāyate mānasikakarmaṇo 'pi avijñaptirastīti ||
body.translated_text: (Question) The definition of <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action) has been understood. The other accumulation of <s>karma</s> that arises from <s>vijñapti</s> — what is its definition? (Answer) That is precisely <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action). (Question) Does there exist only bodily and verbal <s>avijñapti</s>, and not mental <s>avijñapti</s>? (Answer) It should not be so. Why? For there is no reason [to hold that] only bodily and verbal <s>avijñapti</s> exists and not mental <s>avijñapti</s>. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Karma</s> is twofold: <s>cetanā</s> (volition) or [action done] after having willed.' <s>Cetanā</s> is mental <s>karma</s>. [Action done] 'after having willed' is threefold: <s>karma</s> accumulated by volition is bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>. Therein, mental <s>karma</s> is the weightier — this will be stated later. The <s>avijñapti</s> accumulated from the weightier <s>karma</s> always proceeds in the continuum. Therefore it is known that mental <s>karma</s> too has <s>avijñapti</s>.

body.text:
samudayasatyaskandhe karmādhikāre
karmalakṣaṇavargaḥ pañcanavatitamaḥ |
body.translated_text:
In the section on the Truth of Origination, in the topic of <s>karma</s>:
the chapter on the definition of <s>karma</s>, the ninety-fifth.

body.text: 96 avijñaptivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 96. Chapter on <s>Avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action).

body.text: (pṛ) ko 'vijñaptidharmaḥ | (u) cittaṃ pratītyotpadyamānaṃ puṇyapāpaṃ middhamūrchādikāle 'pi yannityaṃ pravartate | sāvijñaptiḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: (Question) What is the <s>dharma</s> of <s>avijñapti</s>? (Answer) Merit and sin that arise depending on the mind, which always continue even during sleep, fainting, and so forth — that is <s>avijñapti</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
ārāmaropā vanaropā ye janāḥ setukārakāḥ |
prapāñcaivodapānañca ye dadanti upāśrayam |
teṣāṃ divā ca rātriñca sadā puṇyaṃ pravartate || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Those people who plant gardens and groves, who build bridges,
who give drinking-water, wells, and shelters —
for them, day and night, merit always continues.'

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- vijñaptikarma pratyakṣamupalabhyate | yāni cīvaradānacaityavandanahananahiṃsādīni tāni bhaveyuḥ | avijñaptistu anupalabhyamānatvāt nāstītyayamarthaḥ spaṣṭaṃ syāditi | (u) yadi nāstyavijñaptiḥ | tadā prāṇātipātaviratyādidharmo nāsti | (pṛ) viratirnāmākaraṇam | akaraṇamabhāvadharmaḥ | yathā puruṣasyābhāṣaṇakāle nāstibhāṣaṇadharmaḥ | rūpasyādarśanakāle 'pi nāstyadarśanadharmaḥ | (u) prāṇātipātaviratyādinā svarga utpadyate | yadi viratirabhāvadharmaḥ | kathaṃ hetuḥ syāt | (pṛ) na viratyā svarga utpadyate, kintu kuśalacittena | (u) maivam | uktaṃ hi sūtre- vīryavān puruṣa āyurvaśāt bahupuṇyaṃ prasavati | puṇyabahutvācciraṃ svargasukhaṃ vindata iti | yadi kuśalacittamātreṇa, kimarthaṃ bahupuṇyo bhavati | na hyayaṃ kuśalacitto bhavituṃ kṣamate | āha ca vanādiropasya divā rātriñca sadā puṇyaṃ pravardhata iti | śīlaṃ dhruvamiti coktam | yadi nāstyavijñaptiḥ | kathaṃ vaktavyaṃ syāt puṇyaṃ sadā pravardhate, śīlaṃ dhruvamiti ca | na ca vijñaptiḥ prāṇātipātakriyaiva | prāṇātipātānantaraṃ dharmo bhavati | tadūrdhvaṃ prāṇātipātapāpaṃ labhate | yathā hantuṃ kañcana prerayati | hananakālamanu prerako hananapāpaṃ labhate | ato jñāyate 'styavijñaptiriti | manaśca na śīlasaṃvaraḥ | kasmāt | yadi kaścidakuśalāvyākṛtacittasthaḥ, yadi vācittaḥ | so 'pi śīladhārītyucyate | ato jñāyate tasmin samaye 'styavijñaptiriti | evamakuśala saṃvaro 'pi |
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: '<s>Vijñaptikarma</s> (manifest action) is directly perceived. Those such as the giving of robes, worshipping <s>caityas</s>, binding, harming, and the like — those would exist. But <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest [action]), being unperceivable, does not exist — this meaning should be clear.' (Answer) If <s>avijñapti</s> does not exist, then the <s>dharma</s> of abstaining from taking life (<s>prāṇātipātavirati</s>) and the like does not exist. (Question) Abstinence (<s>virati</s>) is merely non-action. Non-action is a <s>dharma</s> of non-existence. Just as at the time when a person is not speaking, there is no <s>dharma</s> of speaking. At the time of not seeing form, there is no <s>dharma</s> of non-seeing. (Answer) Through abstaining from taking life and the like, heaven is produced. If abstinence is a <s>dharma</s> of non-existence, how could it be a cause? (Question) Heaven is not produced through abstinence, but through a wholesome mind (<s>kuśalacitta</s>). (Answer) That is not so. For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A person endowed with vigor, by the power of long life, generates much merit. Because of the abundance of merit, he obtains heavenly happiness for a long time.' If it were merely through a wholesome mind, why would he have abundant merit? For he is not able to be continuously wholesome-minded. And it says: 'For one who plants trees and the like, day and night, merit continually increases.' And it is said: 'Moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) is firm.' If <s>avijñapti</s> does not exist, how could it be said that 'merit continually increases' and 'moral conduct is firm'? And <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action) is not merely the act of taking life. After taking life, there is a <s>dharma</s> [that persists]. After that, one obtains the sin of taking life. Just as one who incites another to kill — at the time of the killing, the inciter obtains the sin of killing. From this it is known that <s>avijñapti</s> exists. And mind (<s>manas</s>) is not the moral restraint of <s>śīla</s> (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>). Why? If someone abides in an unwholesome or indeterminate state of mind, or is even without mind — he too is called 'a keeper of <s>śīla</s>.' From this it is known that at that time <s>avijñapti</s> exists. Likewise with the unwholesome restraint (<s>akuśala saṃvara</s>) as well.

body.text: (pṛ) jñātaṃ vināpi cittamastyavijñaptidharma iti | idānīṃ kimidaṃ rūpaṃ kiṃ vā cittaviprayuktasaṃskāraḥ | (u) sa saṃskāraskandhasaṅgṛhītaḥ | kasmāt | yasmādabhisaṃskaraṇalakṣaṇaḥ saṃskāraḥ | avijñaptirapi abhisaṃskaraṇalakṣaṇā | rūpañca rūpaṇālakṣaṇam nābhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is known that even apart from mind, the <s>dharma</s> of <s>avijñapti</s> exists. Now, is this form (<s>rūpa</s>), or is it a formation dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>)? (Answer) It is comprised in the formations aggregate (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>). Why? Because formations have the characteristic of conditioning (<s>abhisaṃskaraṇalakṣaṇa</s>). <s>Avijñapti</s> too has the characteristic of conditioning. But form has the characteristic of being affected (<s>rūpaṇālakṣaṇa</s>), not the characteristic of conditioning.

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktaṃ ṣaṭ cetanākāyāḥ saṃskāraskandha iti | na cittaviprayuktasaṃskārā iti | (u) pratipāditamidaṃ pūrvaṃ yadasti puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ cittaviprayuktamiti | (pṛ) avijñaptiryadi rūpalakṣaṇā | ko doṣaḥ | (u) rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāḥ pañca dharmā na puṇyapāpasvabhāvāḥ | ato na rūpasvabhāvāvijñaptiḥ | bhagavānāha- rūpaṇālakṣaṇaṃ rūpamiti | avijñaptau rūpaṇālakṣaṇānupalambhānna rūpasvabhāvatā |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The six groups of volition (<s>ṣaṭ cetanākāyāḥ</s>) are the formations aggregate' — not formations dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>). (Answer) It has been established previously that there exists merit and demerit dissociated from mind. (Question) If <s>avijñapti</s> has the nature of form (<s>rūpalakṣaṇā</s>), what fault is there? (Answer) The five — form, sound, smell, taste, and tangible — are <s>dharmas</s> that do not have the essential nature of merit and demerit. Therefore <s>avijñapti</s> does not have the essential nature of form. The Blessed One said: 'Form has the characteristic of being affected (<s>rūpaṇālakṣaṇa</s>).' Since the characteristic of being affected is not found in <s>avijñapti</s>, it does not have the essential nature of form.

body.text: (pṛ) avijñaptiḥ kāyikavācikakarmasvabhāvā | kāyikavācikakarma ca rūpameva | (u) avijñaptiḥ kāyikavācikakarmeti nāmamātram | na vastutaḥ kāyavāgbhyāṃ kriyate | kāyañca vācañca pratītya mānasikakarmaṇotpannatvātkāyikavācikamānasikakarmasvabhāvetyucyate | athavā manasa utpannaivāvijñaptiḥ | iyamavijñaptiḥ kathaṃ rūpasvabhāvā | ārūpye 'pyastyavijñaptiḥ | ārūpye kathaṃ rūpaṃ bhaviṣyati | (pṛ) kāḥ kriyā avijñaptimutpādayanti | (u) śubhāśubhakarmakriyābhya utpadyate 'vijñaptiḥ | nāvyākṛtābhyaḥ | alpabalatvāt | (pṛ) kadā kriyābhyo 'vijñaptirutpadyate | (u) dvitīyacittādutpadyate | yat kuśalākuśalānugāmi cittaṃ prabalaṃ bhavati | tat ciraṃ tiṣṭhati | yaccittaṃ durbalaṃ na tacciraṃ tiṣṭhati | yathā ekadinasamāttaṃ śīlamekadinaṃ tiṣṭhati | ādehapātasamāttaṃ śīlantu ādehapātaṃ tiṣṭhati ||
body.translated_text: (Question) <s>Avijñapti</s> has the essential nature of bodily and vocal <s>karma</s>. And bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> is indeed form. (Answer) That <s>avijñapti</s> is bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> is a mere name. In reality it is not produced by body and speech. Because it is produced by mental <s>karma</s> (<s>mānasikakarma</s>) depending on body and speech, it is called 'having the essential nature of bodily, vocal, and mental <s>karma</s>.' Or rather, <s>avijñapti</s> arises from mind alone. How then does this <s>avijñapti</s> have the essential nature of form? Even in the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>), <s>avijñapti</s> exists. How could form exist in the formless realm? (Question) What actions produce <s>avijñapti</s>? (Answer) <s>Avijñapti</s> arises from wholesome and unwholesome actions of <s>karma</s> — not from indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) ones, because of their weak force. (Question) When does <s>avijñapti</s> arise from actions? (Answer) It arises from the second moment of mind onward. Whatever mind follows the wholesome or unwholesome [impulse] and is powerful — that persists for a long time. Whatever mind is weak — that does not persist for a long time. Just as moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) undertaken for one day lasts for one day; moral conduct undertaken until the dissolution of the body lasts until the dissolution of the body.

body.text: avijñaptivargaḥ ṣaṇṇavatitamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the ninety-sixth chapter, the Chapter on <s>Avijñapti</s> (Non-Manifest Action) (<s>avijñaptivarga</s>).

body.text: 97 hetvahetuvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 97. Chapter on Intentional and Unintentional [Action] (<s>hetvahetuvarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- hetukṛtaṃ karma ahetukṛtaṃ karmeti | katamo hetuḥ ahetuśca | (u) jñānapūrvakaṃ kṛtaṃ [karma] hetukṛtam | tadviparītamahetukṛtam | (pṛ) [tarhi] yadahetukṛtaṃ na tat karma bhavati | (u) astīdaṃ karma | kintu yaccittahetukṛtaṃ karma tatsavipākam | citte 'dhyavasīyakṛtaṃ karma hetu [kṛta]m, anadhyavasīyakṛtaṃ karmāhetu [kṛtam] | yathā yodhājīvavyavahāro 'hetukaḥ | ayodhājīvavyavahārastu hetuḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- tava doṣān gaṇayiṣyāmi | yadi yodhājīvo vyavaharasi na tadā gaṇayiṣyāmīti yāvat tridhā pṛcchati | yadyakaraṇacittapūrvakaṃ karoti- yathā kaścidviharan pādanikṣepaṇena kīṭaṃ hanti | so 'hetuḥ | ahetukakarmāsañcitamiti na vipākajanakam |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Karma</s> done with intention (<s>hetukṛta</s>) and <s>karma</s> done without intention (<s>ahetukṛta</s>).' What is intention (<s>hetu</s>) and what is non-intention (<s>ahetu</s>)? (Answer) What is done preceded by knowledge is intentionally done. What is contrary to that is unintentionally done. (Question) Then that which is done without intention would not be <s>karma</s>. (Answer) This is indeed <s>karma</s>. But <s>karma</s> done with mental intention (<s>cittahetu</s>) yields ripening (<s>savipāka</s>). <s>Karma</s> done with deliberation (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) of mind is intentional [<s>karma</s>]; <s>karma</s> done without deliberation is unintentional [<s>karma</s>]. Just as the livelihood of a soldier (<s>yodhājīva</s>) is unintentional. But the livelihood of a non-soldier is intentional. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'I will count your faults. If you engage in the livelihood of a soldier, I will not count [them]' — thus he asks three times. If one acts preceded by the intention of not-doing — just as someone while walking kills an insect by stepping on it — that is unintentional. Unintentional <s>karma</s> is unaccumulated (<s>asañcita</s>) — it does not produce ripening.

body.text: karmāṇi caturvidhāni- kṛtānupacitaṃ, upacittākṛtaṃ, kṛtopacitaṃ akṛtānupacitam iti | kṛtānupacitamiti- yathā hananādikarma kṛtvā paścāccittaṃ paritapati | dānādikarma kṛtvā ca cittaṃ paritapati | karmakriyācittamutpādya na punaḥ smarati | tat kṛtānupacitam | upacitākṛtamiti- yat anyaṃ hananādi kārayitvā pramuditacitto bhavati | anyaṃ dānādi kārayitvā ca pramuditacitto bhavati | kṛtopacitamiti- yat hananādi pāpaṃ kṛtvā dānādipuṇyaṃ kṛtvā ca pramuditacitto bhavati | akṛtānupacitamiti- na ca karoti nāpi muditacitto bhavati | tatra kṛtopacitakarmaṇo 'sti vipākavedanā | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yat karma kṛtamupacitaṃ tasya karmaṇo 'vaśyamasti vipākapratisaṃvedanā iti | ataḥ kṛtopacitakarmaṇo dṛṣṭadharme vā vipāko vedyate | upapattau vā vipāko vedyate | āyatyāṃ vā vipāko vedyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Karmas</s> are fourfold: done but not accumulated (<s>kṛtānupacita</s>), accumulated but not done (<s>upacitākṛta</s>), done and accumulated (<s>kṛtopacita</s>), and neither done nor accumulated (<s>akṛtānupacita</s>). 'Done but not accumulated' means: having performed <s>karma</s> such as killing and the like, the mind afterwards feels remorse; and having performed <s>karma</s> such as giving and the like, the mind feels remorse; having generated the mind of <s>karma</s>-action, one does not remember it again — that is 'done but not accumulated.' 'Accumulated but not done' means: having caused another to kill and the like, one becomes joyful-minded; and having caused another to give and the like, one becomes joyful-minded. 'Done and accumulated' means: having committed sin such as killing and the like, and having performed merit such as giving and the like, one becomes joyful-minded. 'Neither done nor accumulated' means: one neither does it nor becomes joyful-minded. Therein, <s>karma</s> that is done and accumulated has ripened fruition (<s>vipākavedanā</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whatever <s>karma</s> is done and accumulated — for that <s>karma</s>, there is necessarily the experience of ripening.' Therefore, <s>karma</s> that is done and accumulated — its ripening is experienced either in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharma</s>), or in the next birth (<s>upapatti</s>), or in future [lives] (<s>āyati</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadi hetukṛtopacitakarmaṇo 'vaśyamasti vipākapratisaṃvedanā tadā nāsti vimuktiḥ | (u) karma hetukṛtamapi tattvajñānalābhino na punarupacīyate | yathā dagghabījaṃ na punaḥ prarohati | lavaṇapalavarge bhagavānāha- ekatyaḥ(śca) puruṣo [bhāvitakāyo]
body.translated_text: (Question) If <s>karma</s> that is intentionally done and accumulated necessarily has the experience of ripening, then there is no liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). (Answer) Even <s>karma</s> that is intentionally done — for one who has obtained the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), it is no longer accumulated. Just as a burnt seed does not sprout again. In the chapter on the lump of salt (<s>lavaṇapalavarga</s>), the Blessed One said: 'A certain person [with a cultivated body]

body.text: narakavedanīyaṃ karma karoti | tasya tādṛśamevālpamātrakaṃ dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ bhavati | iti | (pṛ) yadi gurupāpakaṃ karma alpamātrakaṃ [dṛṣṭadharma]vedanīyaṃ prajñāyate | kasmānnātyantaṃ kṣayameti | (u) yastattvajñānaṃ na bhāvayati sa pāpakarmaṇo 'nuśayaṃ labhate | ato 'lpako dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyo vipāko bhavati | (pṛ) [tarhi] bhāvitatattvajñāno 'rhannapi akuśalavipākaṃ vedayate | (u) paramakuśaladharmamabhyasannakuśalaṃ pratihanti | ato yo janmaśatasahasreṣu śīlādi kuśalamupacinoti | na tasyākuśalaṃ karmodeti | yathā buddhānāṃ sarvajñānāṃ puruṣāṇām | nānyeṣāmevaṃ sāmarthyam | ato 'kuśalakarma labhante | ato 'rhan bhāvitatattvajñāno 'pi pūrvakarmavaśādakuśalavipākaṃ vedayate ca | (pṛ) uktaṃ sūtre 'pi- bhagavānapavādādyakuśalakarmavipākaṃ vedayata iti | (u) bhagavān sarvajño nākuśalakarmavipākaḥ | samucchinna sarvākuśalamū[la]tvāt | kintvapramāṇarddhyupāyenopadarśayati acintyaṃ buddhavastviti | yathoktamekottarāgame acintyāni pañcavastūnīti |
body.translated_text: commits <s>karma</s> that would be experienced in hell. For him, that very same [<s>karma</s>] becomes merely slight, to be experienced in the present life.' (Question) If even grave sinful <s>karma</s> becomes merely slight and experienced in the present life, why does it not come to complete exhaustion? (Answer) One who does not cultivate the knowledge of reality obtains the latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) of sinful <s>karma</s>. Therefore the ripening to be experienced in the present life is slight. (Question) Then even an <s>Arhat</s> who has cultivated the knowledge of reality would experience the ripening of unwholesome [<s>karma</s>]. (Answer) One who practices the supreme wholesome <s>dharmas</s> counteracts the unwholesome. Therefore, one who accumulates wholesome [<s>karma</s>] such as moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and the like over a hundred thousand births — for him, unwholesome <s>karma</s> does not arise. Just as for the <s>Buddhas</s>, persons of omniscience — but others do not have such capacity. Therefore they obtain unwholesome <s>karma</s>. Therefore even an <s>Arhat</s> who has cultivated the knowledge of reality experiences the ripening of unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] due to prior <s>karma</s>. (Question) It is also stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Blessed One experienced the ripening of unwholesome <s>karma</s> such as slander and the like.' (Answer) The Blessed One, being omniscient, does not [actually experience] the ripening of unwholesome <s>karma</s> — because all roots of the unwholesome have been utterly eradicated. But through immeasurable power of supernatural means, he demonstrates [this] — 'the matter of the <s>Buddha</s> is inconceivable.' As stated in the <s>Ekottarāgama</s>: 'There are five inconceivable matters.'

body.text: karma dvividham- niyatavipākamaniyatavipākamiti | niyatavipākaṃ karma bahu vā alpaṃ vā avaśyavedanīyavipākam | aniyatavipākaṃ karmeti atyantaparikṣīyamāṇam | (pṛ) kiṃ niyatavipākaṃ karmaṃ kimaniyatavipākam | (u) yāni sūtroktāni tāni niyatavipākakarmāṇi | (pṛ) kiṃ pañcānantaryāṇyeva niyatavipākakarmāṇi | kimanyānyapi santi | (u) anyeṣāṃ karmaṇāmasti niyatavipākatābhāgaḥ | kintu na pradarśitaḥ | viṣayagauravādvā niyatavipākatā | yathā bhagavati tacchrāvake vā satkāraḥ athavālpamātrānindā | cittagauravādvā niyatavipākatā | yathā gambhīraghanaparyavasthānena krimikīṭān hanti | idaṃ puruṣahananādapi gurutaram | evamādi | anyāni karmāṇyaniyatavipākāni santi | (pṛ) yadi pañcānantaryapāpakāni tanūbhavantīti | kasmādatyantaṃ na kṣīyante | (u) na te pāpadharmāstasmin samaye 'tyantaṃ kṣīyante | yathā srotaāpannaḥ kausīdyaprāpto 'pi nāṣṭayonīḥ prāpnoti |
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is twofold: with fixed ripening (<s>niyatavipāka</s>) and with unfixed ripening (<s>aniyatavipāka</s>). <s>Karma</s> with fixed ripening — whether great or small — necessarily has a ripening to be experienced. <s>Karma</s> with unfixed ripening is that which is ultimately exhaustible. (Question) Which <s>karma</s> has fixed ripening and which has unfixed ripening? (Answer) Those stated in the <s>sūtras</s> are <s>karmas</s> with fixed ripening. (Question) Are only the five heinous crimes (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) <s>karmas</s> with fixed ripening? Or are there others as well? (Answer) Other <s>karmas</s> too have a share of fixed ripening. But they have not been [specifically] demonstrated. Fixed ripening may be due to the gravity of the object (<s>viṣaya</s>) — just as honoring the Blessed One or his disciples, or even slight criticism [of them]. Or fixed ripening may be due to the gravity of the mind (<s>citta</s>) — just as one who kills worms and insects with deep, intense affliction (<s>gambhīraghanaparyavasthāna</s>) — this is graver than killing a person. And so forth. Other <s>karmas</s> have unfixed ripening. (Question) If the sins of the five heinous crimes become attenuated, why are they not completely exhausted? (Answer) Those sinful <s>dharmas</s> are not completely exhausted at that time. Just as a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>), even when afflicted by laziness, does not reach the eight [lower] destinies.

body.text: sāragauravātpañcānantaryāṇi nātyantaṃ kṣīyante | yathā rājadharme gurupātakī daṇḍya eva na kṣantavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Because of the gravity of their essential nature, the five heinous crimes are not completely exhausted. Just as in the law of the king, one guilty of a grave offense must be punished and cannot be pardoned.

body.text: hetvahetuvargaḥ saptanavatitamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the ninety-seventh chapter, the Chapter on Intentional and Unintentional [Action] (<s>hetvahetuvarga</s>).

body.text: 98 gurulaghupāpavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 98. Chapter on Heavy and Light Sin (<s>gurulaghupāpavarga</s>)

body.text: sūtra uktam- asti gurulaghupāpaṃ karmeti | katamadgurulaghu | (u) yatkarmāvīcinarakavedanīyaprāpakaṃ tat karma gurupāpakamityucyate | (pṛ) kāni karmāṇi tadvipākaprāpakāni | (u) yatsaṅghabhedanakarma tenāvaśyaṃ tadvipākaṃ vedayate | kasmāt | trīṇi ratnāni prativibhinnāni | saṅgharatnaṃ buddharatnādvyatiriktam | dharmaratnabhedo 'pi [gurupāpam] | adhimātra mithyādṛṣṭijātastatkarmābhinirvartayati | buddhe paramīrṣyāvyāpādābhyāṃ tatkarma karoti | ciropacitākuśalasvabhāvaḥ svalābhalobhāttatkarma karoti | dharmo dharma iti [yat] tannāstīti tasmin vadati kuśaladharmāṇāmacaritāro bahavaḥ sattvāḥ pratihanyanta ityato bhavati gurutaraṃ pāpam |
body.translated_text: It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There is heavy and light sinful <s>karma</s>.' What is heavy and what is light? (Answer) Whatever <s>karma</s> brings about the experience of the <s>Avīci</s> hell — that <s>karma</s> is called 'heavy sin.' (Question) What <s>karmas</s> bring about that ripening? (Answer) The <s>karma</s> of splitting the <s>Saṅgha</s> (<s>saṅghabhedana</s>) — by that, one necessarily experiences that ripening. Why? Because the Three Jewels (<s>triratna</s>) are separate [from each other] — the Jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s> is distinct from the Jewel of the <s>Buddha</s>. Splitting the Jewel of <s>Dharma</s> is also [heavy sin]. One born with extreme wrong views (<s>adhimātra mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) brings about that <s>karma</s>. Through supreme envy and malice toward the <s>Buddha</s>, one commits that <s>karma</s>. One whose unwholesome nature has been long accumulated, through greed for personal gain, commits that <s>karma</s>. When one says 'There is no <s>Dharma</s>' regarding what is truly <s>Dharma</s>, many beings who practice wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are obstructed — therefore it becomes very heavy sin.

body.text: (pṛ) kiṃ saṅghabhedamātramavīcau vipākaprāpakam | kimanyadapyasti | (u) anyadapyasti karma | nāsti pāpaṃ nāsti puṇyaṃ nāsti mātāpitṛsajjānānāṃ satkāravipāka iti yadvacanaṃ tadādimithyādṛṣṭirapi tadvipākaprāpiṇī | anyaṃ mithyādṛṣṭau pātayan bahūn sattvānakuśalāni kārayaṃśca tadvipākaṃ vedayate | īdṛśamithyādṛṣṭisūtrāṇi racayanti yathā pūraṇādayo mithyādṛṣṭināmācāryāḥ samyagdṛṣṭivihiṃsayā bahūnāṃ sattvānāmakuśalāya hetupratyayaṃ prakāśayanti | āryāṇāmapavādo 'pi tadvipākaprāpakaḥ | yathā vadanti caturaśītivarṣasahastrāṇi ekanindako duḥkhamanubhavati | yathā coktaṃ dharmapade-
body.translated_text: (Question) Is the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s> alone what brings about ripening in <s>Avīci</s>? Or are there other [sins] as well? (Answer) There are other <s>karmas</s> too. The statement 'There is no sin, there is no merit, there is no ripening of honoring parents and virtuous persons' — that initial wrong view (<s>ādimithyādṛṣṭi</s>) also brings about that ripening. One who causes others to fall into wrong views and causes many beings to commit unwholesome acts experiences that ripening. Those of such wrong views compose <s>sūtras</s>, just as <s>Pūraṇa</s> and other teachers of wrong views — they reveal causes and conditions for the unwholesome of many beings through the destruction of right view. Slandering the Noble Ones (<s>ārya</s>) also brings about that ripening. As they say: 'For eighty-four thousand years, one who slanders [a Noble One] experiences suffering.' As stated in the <s>Dharmapada</s>:

children.translated_text: A noble person who lives by <s>Dharma</s> should train by that <s>Dharma</s>;
one of weak faculties, devoted to sin, perverts that teaching.
Just as the plucking of thorns injures one's own body,
he falls into hell indeed, head downward and feet upward.

body.text:
śataṃ sahasrāṇāṃ nirarbudānāṃ ṣaṭ triṃśacca pañca ca arbudānām
yadāryagarhī nirayamupaiti vācaṃ manaḥ praṇidhāya pāpakam | iti |
body.translated_text:
A hundred thousand <s>nirarbuda</s> [hells] and thirty-six and five <s>arbuda</s> [hells] —
when one who reviles the Noble Ones enters hell, having directed speech and mind toward evil. Thus it is said.

body.text: prāṇātipātādi yadviṣayagurukaṃ cittagurukaṃ tatpāpamapi avīcinarakapātakam | guruviparītaṃ laghu yaduta tapanapratapanādiṣu hīnanarakeṣu tīryakṣu preteṣu devamanuṣyeṣu cākuśalavipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayate | tallaghupāpakamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Killing living beings and the rest — whatever is grave in terms of its object-domain and grave in terms of the mind — that sin too causes one to fall into the <s>Avīci</s> hell. The opposite of grave is light — namely, in the hells of <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, and the rest, in the lower hells, among animals, hungry ghosts, and among gods and humans, one experiences the ripening of unwholesome [karma]. That is called 'light sin.'

body.text: gurulaghupāpavargo 'ṣṭanavatitamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the ninety-eighth chapter, the Chapter on Heavy and Light Sin (<s>gurulaghupāpavarga</s>).

body.text: 99 mahālpārthakakarmavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 99. Chapter on Karma of Great and Small Fruit (<s>mahālpārthakakarmavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktaṃ mahālpārthakaṃ karmeti | kiṃ tanmahārthakaṃ karma | (u) yena karmaṇā anuttarasamyaksambodhimadhigacchati | tanmahattamārthakaṃ karma | tato 'varakarmaṇā pratyekabuddhamārgaṃ vindate | tato 'varakarmaṇā śrāvakamārgaṃ labhate | tato 'varakarmaṇā bhavāgra 'śītimahākalpasāhasrāṇyāyurvipākaṃ labhate | idaṃ saṃsāre mahattamavipākaṃ karma | tato 'varakarmaṇā ākiñcanyāyatane ṣaṣṭikalpasahasrāṇyāyurvindate | evaṃ krameṇa yāvadbrahmalokaṃ kalpārdhamāyurvindate | tato 'varakāmadhātau paranirmitadeveṣu divyagaṇanayā ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇyanubhavati | yāvaccaturmahārājikeṣu divyagaṇanayā pañcavarṣaśatāni [vipākaṃ] vedayate | evaṃ manuṣyeṣu caturmahārājikānāmadhaḥ pratyekaṃ karmavaśādvipākaṃ vedayate | evaṃ tiryakpretanarakeṣvapyasti alpalābhaṃ karma |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Karma is of great and small fruit.' What is karma of great fruit? (Answer) The <s>karma</s> by which one attains unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s>) — that is <s>karma</s> of the greatest fruit. By <s>karma</s> inferior to that, one obtains the path of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. By <s>karma</s> inferior to that, one obtains the path of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. By <s>karma</s> inferior to that, one obtains at the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) a lifespan-ripening of eighty thousand great <s>kalpas</s>. This is the <s>karma</s> of greatest ripening in <s>saṃsāra</s>. By <s>karma</s> inferior to that, at the base of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), one obtains a lifespan of sixty thousand <s>kalpas</s>. Thus progressively, down to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, one obtains a lifespan of half a <s>kalpa</s>. Inferior to that, in the desire realm, among the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, by divine reckoning one experiences sixty thousand years. Down to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, by divine reckoning one experiences five hundred years [of ripening]. Likewise among humans, below the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, individually according to the power of <s>karma</s>, one experiences ripening. Likewise among animals, hungry ghosts, and hell-beings too, there is <s>karma</s> of small gain.

body.text: kīdṛśāni karmāṇi anuttarasamyaksambodhyādīn prāpayanti | (u) dānādiṣaṭpāramitāsampadanuttarasamyaksambodhiṃ prāpayati | tataḥ kuśalakarmakrameṇa jaghanyapravṛttaṃ pratyekabuddhabodhiṃ prāpayati | [tato 'pi] jaghanyapravṛttaṃ śrāvakabodhiṃ prāpayati | adhimātreṣu caturapramāṇacitteṣu viharan bhavagra utpadyate | tato jaghanyabhūteṣu caturapramāṇacitteṣu viharannavarabhūmāvutpadyate |
body.translated_text: What kinds of <s>karmas</s> lead to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s>) and the rest? (Answer) The accomplishment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) beginning with generosity (<s>dāna</s>) leads to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Then, by the gradation of wholesome <s>karma</s>, the most inferior leads to the awakening of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. [Still more] inferior leads to the awakening of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. Dwelling in the four immeasurable minds (<s>caturapramāṇacitta</s>) of the highest degree, one is reborn at the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). Then, dwelling in the four immeasurable minds of inferior degree, one is reborn in a lower plane.

body.text: tato jaghanyabhūteṣu caturapramāṇacitteṣu viharan śīlasamādhipratyayavaśācca rūpadhātāvutpadyate | dānaśīlakuśalābhyāsapratyayena kāmadhātāvutpadyate | dānādikarmaṇāṃ puṇyakṣetrotkarṣanikarṣamanusṛtyāsti viśeṣaḥ | yat buddhakṣetra ācaraṇaṃ tadatyuttamam | yatpratyekabuddhakṣetra ācaraṇaṃ tat tato nyūnam |
body.translated_text: Then, dwelling in the four immeasurable minds of inferior degree, through the condition of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), one is reborn in the form realm. Through the condition of habitual practice of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and wholesome [action], one is reborn in the desire realm. There is differentiation among the <s>karmas</s> of generosity and the rest according to the superiority or inferiority of the field of merit (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>). Practice in the field of a <s>Buddha</s> is the most supreme. Practice in the field of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> is inferior to that.

body.text: (pṛ) puṇyakṣetraṃ kiṃ bodhyotkṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ vā prahāṇena | (u) atyantaśūnyatākhyaṃ dharmalakṣaṇaṃ yā bodhiḥ prāpayati | sā prahāṇādutkarṣati | kasmāt | yathā bhagavān bodhyā śrāvakebhyo 'tiricyate na prahāṇena | yathoktaṃ saṃyuktapiṭake-
body.translated_text: (Question) Is a field of merit (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>) superior because of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), or because of abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>)? (Answer) The <s>dharma</s>-characteristic called 'ultimate emptiness' (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>) — that which leads to awakening — that is superior to abandonment. Why? Just as the Blessed One surpasses the <s>Śrāvakas</s> because of awakening, not because of abandonment. As stated in the <s>Saṃyuktapiṭaka</s>:

children.translated_text: Were one to purify a monastic ground equal to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,
that would be comparable to the purification of a shrine to the Teacher, [mere as] the palm of one's hand.

body.text: sarvajñajñānañca prahāṇārtham | ato yadbodhisattvānāṃ saṃsāre dīrghakālāvāsaḥ sa samyak prahāṇārthaḥ | samyak prahāṇamiti yat svasaṃyojanaprahāṇaṃ sattvaprahāṇañca | tāni saṃyojanāni ca kramaśo bodhipraheyāni | ato jñāyate bodhyā puṇyakṣetraṃ prahāṇādutkṛṣṭamiti |
body.translated_text: And the knowledge of the omniscient (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>) is for the purpose of abandonment. Therefore, the long abiding of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in <s>saṃsāra</s> is for the purpose of right abandonment. 'Right abandonment' means the abandonment of one's own fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) and the [liberation of] beings. Those fetters are to be abandoned progressively through awakening. Therefore it is known that the field of merit is superior because of awakening rather than because of abandonment.

body.text: (pṛ) yastīkṣṇendriyaḥ srotaāpannaḥ yaśca mṛdvindriyaḥ sakṛdāgāmī | atayo puṇyakṣetrayoḥ ka utkṛṣṭaḥ | (u) tīkṣṇendriya utkṛṣṭo na mṛdvindriyaḥ | (pṛ) tadvacana mayuktam | yathoktaṃ sūtre srotaāpannaśatasatkāro naikasakṛdāgāmisatkārakalpa iti | āha ca- dandhānāṃ hiṃsayā kāmarāgakalahacittaṃ prarohati | iti | ato vītarāgasya dānaṃ bahupuṇyāni prāpayet | sakṛdāgāmī ca trīṇi viṣāṇi tanūkaroti | na srotaāpannaḥ | kasmāducyata utkṛṣṭa iti | (u) tatsūtraṃ neyārthakam | kenedaṃ jñāyate | tasminneva sūtra uktaṃ- tiraścāṃ dānaṃ śataguṇaṃ hitaṃ prāpayati iti | vastutastu pārāvatapakṣyādīnāṃ dānena pratilabdho vipākaḥ tīrthikānāṃ pañcābhijñānāṃ dānamatiśete | atastatsūtraṃ cintyārthakam | sūtraṃ tat bahunā hetunāha- nissaraṇārthā prajñā iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Between a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) with sharp faculties and a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) with dull faculties — which of these two fields of merit is superior? (Answer) The one with sharp faculties is superior, not the one with dull faculties. (Question) That statement is untenable. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The honor given to a hundred stream-enterers is not equal to the honor given to a single once-returner.' And it says: 'In those who are slow, through harm, there arises a mind of desire-and-passion and quarrel.' Therefore the gift to one free from passion would produce much merit. And the once-returner has attenuated the three poisons, but the stream-enterer has not. Why then is [the stream-enterer] called superior? (Answer) That <s>sūtra</s> has a provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>). How is this known? In that very <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'A gift to animals yields a hundredfold benefit.' But in reality, the ripening obtained from a gift to pigeons and the like is surpassed by a gift to <s>tīrthikas</s> endowed with the five superknowledges (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>). Therefore that <s>sūtra</s> has a meaning that requires reflection. That <s>sūtra</s> states for many reasons: 'Wisdom has the purpose of going forth (<s>nissaraṇa</s>).'

body.text: srotaāpannaśca prajñābalena kāmān vedayamāno 'pi puṇyakṣetramityucyate | na tu prahīṇarāgaḥ prākṛto yāvadbhavāgraniyamalābhī [puṇyakṣetram] | bahuśrutajñānaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyagatameva prakṛṣṭaṃ na bhavāgraniyato 'nirvedhabhāgīyagataḥ | maitreyabodhisattvo 'pratilabdhabuddhatvo 'pi arhatāṃ satkāryaḥ | śūnyatākāramātrabodhicittotpādako 'rhatāṃ satkāryaḥ | tadyathā ekaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ pātracīvaramādāya arhantamanucarati | asmin śrāmaṇere utpannānuttara [bodhi]citte tu arhanneva tatpātracīvaramādāya svayamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā tamanugacchati | tadyathā dṛṣṭānte vistareṇoktam | ato jñāyate prajñayā puṇyakṣetramutkṛṣṭaṃ bhavatīti ||
body.translated_text: And a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>), even while experiencing sensual pleasures, is called a 'field of merit' by the power of wisdom. But an ordinary being who has abandoned passion, up to one who has obtained the attainment of the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), is not [called] a field of merit. Learning and knowledge that have entered the penetrative stage (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) alone are excellent — not one who is fixed at the summit of existence without having entered the penetrative stage. <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even without having attained <s>Buddhahood</s>, is worthy of honor by <s>Arhats</s>. One who has generated the <s>bodhicitta</s> (aspiration to awakening) with [the realization of] merely the aspect of emptiness (<s>śūnyatākāramātra</s>) is worthy of honor by <s>Arhats</s>. For example, a certain novice (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>), taking the bowl and robe, follows an <s>Arhat</s>. When in that novice the unsurpassed <s>bodhicitta</s> has arisen, the <s>Arhat</s> himself takes his bowl and robe, puts on his own upper robe, and follows him. As stated in the example at length. Therefore it is known that the field of merit becomes superior through wisdom.

body.text: mahālpārthakakarmavarga ekonaśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the ninety-ninth chapter, the Chapter on Karma of Great and Small Fruit (<s>mahālpārthakakarmavarga</s>).

body.text: 100 trividhakarmavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 100. Chapter on the Three Kinds of Karma (<s>trividhakarmavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- trividhaṃ karma kuśalamakuśalamavyākṛtamiti | kiṃ kuśalaṃ karma | (u) yat karma pareṣāṃ priyaṃ prayacchati tat kuśalam | (pṛ) kiṃ priyam | (u) pareṣāṃ yat sukhaprāpakaṃ tat priyam | kuśalamityapyucyate puṇyamityapyucyate | (pṛ) yat pareṣāṃ sukhaprāpakaṃ tat puṇyam | yat pareṣāṃ duḥkhaprāpakaṃ tena pāpena bhavitavyam | yathā āñjanauṣadhaśalyavedhāḥ pareṣāṃ duḥkhajanakāḥ pāpāḥ syuḥ | (u) āñjanauṣadhaśalyavedhāḥ sukhapradatvādapāpāḥ | (pṛ) sukhapradaṃ tat puṇyamiti | yathā paradāragamanaṃ tat tasya sukhajanakaṃ tat puṇyakaramapi syāt | (u) abrahmacaryaṃ niyamenākuśalam | yat parānukuśaladharme pravartayati tat duḥkhāya bhavati na sukhāya | sukhaṃ nāma yadihāmutra ca sukham | na tvaihikamalpasukham | yat pretyāmutra mahāduḥkhaṃ vindate |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Karma</s> is of three kinds: wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>).' What is wholesome <s>karma</s>? (Answer) That <s>karma</s> which gives what is pleasing to others is wholesome. (Question) What is 'pleasing'? (Answer) That which brings happiness to others is pleasing. It is also called 'wholesome' and also called 'merit' (<s>puṇya</s>). (Question) If that which brings happiness to others is merit, then that which brings suffering to others should be sin (<s>pāpa</s>). Just as applying collyrium, administering medicine, and piercing with a surgical instrument bring suffering to others — these would be sinful. (Answer) Applying collyrium, administering medicine, and piercing with a surgical instrument are not sinful because they bestow happiness. (Question) If that which bestows happiness is merit, then adultery (<s>paradāragamana</s>) — since it generates happiness for that person — would also be meritorious. (Answer) Sexual misconduct (<s>abrahmacārya</s>) is invariably unwholesome. That which causes another to engage in unwholesome <s>dharma</s> brings suffering, not happiness. 'Happiness' means that which is happiness both here and hereafter — not merely a small happiness in this life, when one obtains great suffering in the next life.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidannapānapratyayaṃ pareṣāṃ sukhamutpādayanti | tadannapānaṃ kadācidajīryamāṇaṃ sat puruṣasya maraṇaṃ prāpayati | tadannadāyakaḥ kiṃ pāpaṃ labheta kiṃ vā puṇyam | (u) sa sādhucitto 'nnaṃ prayacchati na duṣṭacittaḥ | ataḥ puṇyamātraṃ labhate na pāpam | (pṛ) paradāragamanamapyevaṃ syāt | kevalaṃ sukhārthatvātpuṇyamapi labheta | (u) idaṃ pūrvameva pratyuktaṃ yadabrahmacaryaṃ niyamena akuśalamiti | mahāduḥkhajanakatvāt | annapānadāne tvasti
body.translated_text: (Question) Certain people produce happiness for others by means of food and drink. That food and drink sometimes, not being digested, brings about the death of a person. Does the giver of that food obtain sin or merit? (Answer) He gives the food with a good intention, not with a malicious intention. Therefore he obtains merit only, not sin. (Question) Adultery too would be the same — being solely for the sake of happiness, one might obtain merit. (Answer) This has already been refuted before — that sexual misconduct (<s>abrahmacārya</s>) is invariably unwholesome, because it produces great suffering. But in the giving of food and drink there is

body.text: puṇyaguṇabhāgaḥ | kasmāt | nahyavaśyamannalābhī mriyate | sattvāḥ kāmakliṣṭāḥ kāmamaithunamanubhavanti | tat sarvathāpuṇyahetuḥ | kathaṃ puṇyaṃ labheran | (pṛ) kecit prāṇihiṃsayā bahū nāmupakurvanti | yathā corāṇāṃ nigrahe rāṣṭraṃ nirīti bhavati | krūrapaśumāraṇe janānāṃ hitaṃ bhavati | evamādiprāṇihiṃsayā kiṃ puṇyaṃ labhyeta | kecitsteyapratyayaṃ pitarau poṣayanti | maithunapratyayaṃ priyaputraṃ janayanti | mṛṣāvādapratyayañca kasyacijjīvītaṃ pradadanti | pāruṣyavacanapratyayaṃ pareṣāṃ hitaṃ bhavati | idaṃ sarvaṃ daśākuśalasaṅgṛhītam | kathamanena puṇyaṃ labheran | (u) te puṇyaṃ pāpañca labhante | parānugrahātpuṇyaṃ labhante paropaghātātpāpam | (pṛ) cikitsāpi parasyādau duḥkhapradā paścātsukhaṃ prāpayati | kasmātpāpamalabdhvā puṇyamātraṃ labhate | (u) cikitsāyāṃ kuśalacittena kṛtāyāṃ nāstyakuśalāśayaḥ | yat karma kuśalākuśalahetusamuddhitaṃ, tataḥ puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ vyāmiśraṃ labhate |
body.translated_text: a share of meritorious quality. Why? Because the recipient of food does not invariably die. Beings, afflicted by desire, experience sexual intercourse. That is in every way a non-meritorious cause. How could they obtain merit? (Question) Certain people, through harming living beings, benefit many. For example, in the suppression of robbers, the kingdom becomes free from calamity. In the killing of a ferocious animal, it becomes beneficial for people. In such cases of harming living beings, would merit be obtained? Some maintain a household through theft. Through sexual intercourse, they beget a beloved son. Through false speech, they save someone's life. Through harsh speech, it becomes beneficial for others. All of this is included in the ten unwholesome [actions]. How could they obtain merit through these? (Answer) They obtain both merit and sin. They obtain merit from benefiting others. They obtain sin from harming others. (Question) Medical treatment too initially causes suffering to others and later brings happiness. Why does one obtain merit only and not sin? (Answer) In medical treatment performed with a wholesome intention, there is no unwholesome disposition. Whatever <s>karma</s> arises from both wholesome and unwholesome motives — from that one obtains a mixture of merit and sin.

body.text: codayati | hiṃsādayaḥ sarve puṇyaprāpakāḥ | kasmāt | hiṃsāpratyayamabhīṣṭaṃ labhate | yathā rājñāścoranigrahe puṇyaṃ labhyate | puṇyapratyayañca yadabhīpsitaṃ tallabhyate | iti prāṇātipātāt kathaṃ puṇyaṃ na bhavati | hiṃsāṃ kurvan yaśo labhate | yaśaḥ puruṣasya kāmyaṃ bhavati | puruṣasya kāmyaṃ puṇyaphalakam | hiṃsayā ca prītisukhaṃ labhate | prītisukhamapi puṇyaphalavipākam | āha ca ca sūtram- yo yuddhe hanyate sa svarga utpadyata iti | yathāha gāthā- mriyamāṇañca saṅgrāme patiṃ barayatepsarāḥ iti | kiñcāha-
body.translated_text: An objection is raised: All acts of killing and the rest produce merit. Why? Through killing, one obtains what is desired. Just as a king obtains merit from suppressing robbers. And through the condition of merit, one obtains what is desired. Therefore, from killing living beings, how is there no merit? One who kills gains fame. Fame is desired by a person. What is desired by a person has the ripening of merit. And through killing, one obtains joyful happiness. Joyful happiness too is a ripening of merit. And the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'He who is killed in battle is born in heaven.' As the verse says: 'A celestial <s>apsaras</s> escorts the lord who dies in battle.' Furthermore it says:

body.text:
sudhanatve 'pi puruṣaścoraṃ purata āgatam
hanyādeva na vai pāpaṃ āhantā vindate tu tat || iti
body.translated_text:
'Even a good man, when a thief comes before him,
should certainly kill — there is no sin; the slayer obtains that [merit].' Thus it is said.

body.text: dharmasūtramāha- catvāro varṇāḥ brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ | eṣāṃ pṛthak santi svadharmāḥ | brāhmaṇasya ṣaḍdharmāḥ kṣatriyasya catvāro vaiśyasya trayaḥ śūdrasyaikaḥ | ṣaḍ dharmā iti yajanamārvijya madhyayatamadhyāpanaṃ dānaṃ pratigrahaḥ | catvāro dharmā iti yajanaṃ nārtvijyaṃ, parato vedādhyayanaṃ nādhyāpanaṃ, dānaṃ na pratigrahaḥ prajāpālanam | trayo dharmā iti yajanaṃ nārtvijyaṃ, adhyayanaṃ nādhyāpanaṃ dānaṃ na pratigrahaḥ | eko dharma iti trayāṇāmuttamavarṇānāṃ
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharmasūtra</s> says: 'There are four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes): <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>. Each of these has its own <s>dharmas</s>. A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has six <s>dharmas</s>; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> has four; a <s>Vaiśya</s> has three; a <s>Śūdra</s> has one. The six <s>dharmas</s> are: performing sacrifice, officiating as a priest, study, teaching, giving gifts, and receiving gifts. The four <s>dharmas</s> are: performing sacrifice but not officiating as a priest, studying the <s>Vedas</s> from others but not teaching, giving gifts but not receiving gifts, and ruling the people. The three <s>dharmas</s> are: performing sacrifice but not officiating as a priest, studying but not teaching, giving gifts but not receiving gifts. The one <s>dharma</s> is:

body.text: śūśrūṣā | kṣatriyasya prajāpālanāya prāṇivadhe puṇyameva na pāpam | veda uktam- prāṇivadhaḥ puṇyaprāpakaḥ yaduta vaidikamantreṇa hatāḥ paśavaḥ svarga utpadyanta iti | vedāśca loke śraddheyā bhavanti | kiñcāha yadvastuto martavyaṃ taddhanane nāsti pāpam- yathā pañcābhijña ṛṣirmantreṇa puruṣaṃ hanti | na vaktavyamṛṣeḥ pāpamastīti | [anṛṣe]ḥ pāpiṣṭhasya kathametatsidhyati | ato jñāyate prāṇivadho na pāpaprāpaka iti | kaścitkadāciccittabalena prāṇinaṃ hatvā puṇyaṃ labhate | prāṇadānena tu pāpaṃ labhate | yadi kuśalacittena sukhalipsayā prāṇinaṃ hanti | kathaṃ tasya pāpaṃ bhavati | yathā sūnakādayaḥ | paśupālānāṃ gavājadāne 'pi pāpam | evamadattādānādiṣvapi puṇyaguṇo 'sti |
body.translated_text: service to the three upper <s>varṇas</s>. For a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, in the killing of living beings for the protection of the people, there is merit only, not sin. The <s>Vedas</s> say: 'The killing of living beings produces merit — namely, animals killed by Vedic mantras are born in heaven.' And the <s>Vedas</s> are trusted in the world. Furthermore it says: whatever is destined by nature to die — in its killing there is no sin. Just as a <s>ṛṣi</s> endowed with the five superknowledges (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>) kills a person by a mantra. It should not be said that the <s>ṛṣi</s> has sin. [But if even for the] non-<s>ṛṣi</s>, a most sinful one — how can this be established? Therefore it is known that the killing of living beings does not produce sin. Someone, at a certain time, through the power of mind, having killed a living being, obtains merit. But through the gift of life, one obtains sin. If with a wholesome intention and a desire for happiness one kills a living being, how can there be sin for him? Just as with butchers and the rest. Even for herders, in the giving of cattle and goats, there is sin. Likewise, in the taking of what is not given and the rest too, there is a share of meritorious quality.

body.text: atrocyate | yaduktaṃ bhavatā prāṇivadhenābhīpsitalābhādasti puṇyaguṇa iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | puṇyaguṇādhīnatayā hi abhīpsitalābhaḥ | abhīpsitapratyayaḥ prāṇivadhalābha iti kasmādyuktam | pūrvādhvakṛtāviśuddhapuṇyatvāt | yathoktaṃ sūtre- cauryaharaṇavadhahiṃsāpratilabdhadhano 'nyasya dānaṃ prayojayati | tat daurmanasyaparidevanenāpariśuddhaṃ dānamiti | evamādidānamapariśuddhamityucyate | avaśyamaśubhapratyayādhīnāṃ vipākavedanāṃ prāpayati | tasya puruṣasya pūrvādhvani puṇyamasti prāṇātipātakarmapratyayo 'pyasti | tasmādidānīṃ kāyo hananahetukaṃ vipākaṃ vedayate | kecitsattvā api pratyarpaṇīyajīvitadhanā ityato vadhahiṃsayā yadabhīpsitaṃ tallabhate | na ca tathā sarve sattvāḥ | [ataḥ] prāṇivadhenopabhogyaṃ labhate | yathā loka āhuḥ- ayaṃ puruṣo 'lpapuṇyo bahukurvannapi na vindata iti | yaśaḥprītisukheṣvapyevaṃ syāt | puṇyaguṇapratyayena yaśaḥkāyabalasukhāni labhate | puṇyasya kevalamapariśuddhatvāt vadhena [upabhogyaṃ] labhate | (pṛ) siṃhavyāghrādilabdhaṃ kāyabalaṃ sarvaṃ pāpajam | yakṣarākṣasādilabdhaṃ kāyabalasukhamapi pāpajam | (u) idaṃ pūrvameva pratyuktam | aviśuddhapuṇyatvātpāpapratyayena labhate |
body.translated_text: Here we reply: Your statement that 'through the killing of living beings, because one obtains what is desired, there is the quality of merit' — that is untenable. Why? Because the obtaining of what is desired depends on the quality of merit. That the obtaining of what is desired has killing of living beings as its condition — why would that be valid? Because the merit from past lives is impure. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who, through theft, robbery, killing, and violence, obtains wealth and then causes another to give — that gift is impure, [accompanied by] mental anguish and lamentation.' Thus, gifts and the like are said to be impure. One necessarily experiences the ripened result of feeling that depends on unwholesome conditions. That person has merit from past lives, and also has the karmic condition of taking life. Therefore, now his body experiences the ripened result caused by killing. Certain beings have lives and wealth that must be repaid — therefore, through killing and violence, one obtains what is desired. But not all beings are like that. [Therefore] through killing beings, one obtains what is to be enjoyed. Just as in the world, people say: 'This person has little merit — even though he labors much, he does not find [reward].' The same would apply to fame, joy, and happiness. Through the condition of meritorious quality, one obtains fame, bodily strength, and happiness. It is merely because the merit is impure that through killing one obtains [what is to be enjoyed].

body.text: yadbravīṣi sūtra uktaṃ- yo yuddhe hanyate sa svarga utpadyata iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | sūtramidamanena mithyāpralāpena mūḍhān protsāhayati sauryamutpādayitum | kenedaṃ jñāyate | avaśyaṃ puṇyādhīnaṃ puṇyamutpadyate pāpādhīnaṃ pāpam | tatrātyantamasati puṇyahetau kena puṇyaṃ labheta | yadāha bhavān- caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ pṛthak santi svadharmāḥ | kṣatriyasya
body.translated_text: (Question) Your statement that 'it is said in the <s>sūtra</s> that one who is killed in battle is reborn in heaven' — that is untenable. Why? That <s>sūtra</s>, through such false speech, encourages the deluded to generate courage. How is this known? Necessarily, merit arises dependent on merit; sin arises dependent on sin. In that case, in the complete absence of a cause of merit, how could one obtain merit? (Answer) As you have said: 'For the four castes (<s>varṇa</s>), there are separate duties (<s>svadharma</s>). For the <s>kṣatriya</s>,
