body.text: caturthadhyānasaṅgṛhītaṃ kuśalaṃ karma rūpadhātuvedanīyavipākam | caturārūpyasamādhisaṅgṛhītamārūpyavedanīyavipākam | anyadvikṣiptacittasamutpāditaṃ karma kāmadhātuvedanīyavipākam | iti | (pṛ) kathaṃ tatra samutpāditaṃ kuśalaṃ karma kāmadhātuvedanīyavipākaṃ bhavet | (u) yathāsmin loke samāhitacittasamutpāditakuśalakarmaṇastatra vipākaṃ vedayate | tathā tatra vikṣiptacittasamutpāditakuśalakarmaṇo 'smin loke vipākaṃ vedayate | yathā ca rūpārūpyadhātusamutpāditākuśalakarmaṇaḥ kāmadhātau vipākaṃ vedayate | tathā tatra samutpāditakuśalakarmaṇo 'pi |
body.translated_text: Wholesome <s>karma</s> comprised in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> has ripening to be experienced in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>). [<s>Karma</s>] comprised in the four formless concentrations (<s>ārūpyasamādhi</s>) has ripening to be experienced in the formless [realm]. Other <s>karma</s> produced by a distracted mind has ripening to be experienced in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). (Question) How could wholesome <s>karma</s> produced there [in the higher realms] have ripening to be experienced in the desire realm? (Answer) Just as one who, in this world, produces wholesome <s>karma</s> with a concentrated mind experiences its ripening there [in the higher realms] — so too, one who produces wholesome <s>karma</s> with a distracted mind there [in the higher realms] experiences its ripening in this world. And just as one who produces unwholesome <s>karma</s> in the form and formless realms experiences its ripening in the desire realm — so too with wholesome <s>karma</s> produced there.

body.text: (pṛ) yo rūpārūpyadhātugataḥ na sa utpādayati kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalaṃ karma | (u) tatra nāstyayaṃ hetuḥ yat kāmadhātugato rūpārūpya[pratisaṃyuktaṃ] kuśalaṃ karmaiva samutpādayati na rūpārūpyadhātugataḥ kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalaṃ karma samutpādayati iti | ucyate ca yuṣmābhiḥ kāmadhātugataḥ kāmadhātukamavyākṛtaṃ cittaṃ samutpādayatīti | yadyavyākṛtaṃ cittaṃ samutpādayati | kasmānna kucalaṃ cittam | sūtre bhagavān hastakadevaputrametadavocat- cittaviharaṇe audārikavedanāsaṃjñāṃ manasikuru iti | audārikasaṃjñā kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ cittameva | ayaṃ kuśalacittena yat dharmaṃ śṛṇoti buddhaṃ pūjayati tat sarvaṃ kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ cittam | tathā no cet audārikasaṃjñeti nākhyā syāt | tatrānusmṛtiprārthanā puṇyavastu | yathāha bhagavān triṣu vastuṣu atṛpto 'smin loke āyuṣo 'nte 'navataptadeveṣūpapatsye yaduta tathāgataṃ paśyāmi dharmaṃ śṛṇomi saṅghaṃ satkaromīti | [tatra] anusmṛtiprārthanā puṇyavastu kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ cittam | tatrāsti buddhānusmṛtiḥ na puṇyavastu | ato jñeyaṃ kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamastīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) One who is in the form and formless realms does not produce wholesome <s>karma</s> connected with the desire realm. (Answer) There is no reason for this — [namely,] that one in the desire realm produces only wholesome <s>karma</s> connected with the form and formless [realms], but one in the form and formless realms does not produce wholesome <s>karma</s> connected with the desire realm. And you yourselves say: 'One in the desire realm produces indeterminate mind (<s>avyākṛta citta</s>) of the desire realm.' If one produces indeterminate mind, why not wholesome mind? In the <s>sūtra</s>, the Blessed One said to the divine son <s>Hastaka</s>: 'In the meditation on mind (<s>cittaviharaṇa</s>), attend to the perception of gross feelings.' The gross perception is mind connected with the desire realm itself. When this [divine being] with a wholesome mind hears the <s>Dharma</s> and worships the <s>Buddha</s> — all of that is mind connected with the desire realm. If it were not so, the designation 'gross perception' would not apply. Therein, recollection and aspiration are a basis of merit (<s>puṇyavastu</s>). As the Blessed One said: 'Insatiable with respect to three things, at the end of life in this world, I shall be reborn among the <s>Anavatagta</s> gods — namely, seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and honoring the <s>Saṅgha</s>.' Therein, recollection and aspiration are a basis of merit — [which is] mind connected with the desire realm. Therein there is recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, [which is] a basis of merit. Therefore it should be known that wholesome [<s>karma</s>] connected with the desire realm exists [even in the higher realms].

body.text: pratisaṃyuktamakarmavargastrayuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and third chapter, the Chapter on <s>Karma</s> Connected with [Specific Realms] (<s>pratisaṃyuktamakarmavarga</s>).

body.text: 104 trividhakarmavipākavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 104. Chapter on the Three Kinds of Karmic Ripening (<s>trividhakarmavipākavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtre bhagavānāha- trividhaṃ karma dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyavipākaṃ, upapadyavedanīyavipākaṃ ūrdhvavedanīyavipākamiti | kimidam | yadetatkāyābhisaṃskṛtaṃ karma etatkāya eva
body.translated_text: (Question) The Blessed One said in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Karma</s> is of three kinds: that whose ripening is to be experienced in this very life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmavedanīya</s>), that whose ripening is to be experienced upon [the next] rebirth (<s>upapadyavedanīya</s>), and that whose ripening is to be experienced in subsequent [lives] (<s>ūrdhvavedanīya</s>).' What is this? Whatever <s>karma</s> is fashioned by this body — [when] that is experienced in this very body,

body.text: vedyate | tad dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyavipākam | yadetallokābhisaṃskṛtaṃ karma samanantaralokamatītya vedyate tadūrdhvavedanīyavipākam | [yat] samanantaralokātītaṃ tadūrdhvamityucyate | (pṛ) antarābhavikakarmavipākaḥ kasmin sthāne vedyate | (u) sthānadvaye vedyate | samanantarāntarābhavikaṃ karma upapadyavipākasthāne vedyate | upapattiviśeṣasyaivāntarābhavatvāt | anyāntarābhavikaṃ karma ūrdhvavipākasthāne vedyate | (pṛ) kimetāni trīṇi karmāṇi niyatavipākāni niyatakālāni ca | (u) kecidāhuḥ- niyatavipākānīti | dṛṣṭavipākaṃ karmāvaśyaṃ dṛṣṭa eva vedanīyavipākam | tathānyat dvayamapi | sato 'pīdṛśavacanasyārtho na yujyate | kasmāt | tathā cet pañcānantaryāṇi niyatavipākānīti na syāt | ṣaṭ pādābhidharme tūktaṃ pañcānantaryāṇi niyatavipākānīti | lavaṇapalopamasūtre punaruktam- aniyatavipākānīti yatkiñcanāsti narakavedanīyavipākam | ihaikatyaḥ pudgalaḥ bhāvitakāyo bhavati | bhavitaśīlo bhāvitacitto bhāvitaprajño bhavati | tasya tatkarma dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ bhavati | tasmāttrividhakarmaṇāṃ niyatakālatayā bhāvyam | dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyavipākaṃ karma nāvaśyaṃ dṛṣṭadharma eva vedyate | vedyate cet dṛṣṭadharma eva vedanīyaṃ syāt nānyatra | evamanyat dvayamapi |
body.translated_text: that is <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in this very life. Whatever <s>karma</s> is fashioned in this world — [when] that is experienced immediately after passing beyond this world, that is <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced subsequently. That which has passed beyond the immediately following world — that is called 'subsequent.' (Question) Where is the ripening of <s>karma</s> done in the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) experienced? (Answer) It is experienced in two places. <s>Karma</s> of the immediately following intermediate existence is experienced in the place of ripening upon rebirth — because the intermediate existence is itself a specific [form of] rebirth. Other intermediate-existence <s>karma</s> is experienced in the place of subsequent ripening. (Question) Are these three <s>karmas</s> fixed in their ripening and fixed in their time? (Answer) Some say: 'They are fixed in their ripening.' <s>Karma</s> whose ripening is to be seen [in this life] necessarily has its ripening to be experienced in this very life. Likewise with the other two as well. Even though such a statement exists, its meaning is not valid. Why? If so, the statement that 'the five heinous crimes (<s>ānantarya</s>) have fixed ripening' would not hold. But in the <s>Ṣaṭpādābhidharma</s> it is stated that 'the five heinous crimes have fixed ripening.' Furthermore, in the <s>Lavaṇapalopama Sūtra</s> it is stated: 'They have unfixed ripening — whatever <s>karma</s> has ripening to be experienced in hell. Herein a certain person has a cultivated body, cultivated moral conduct, cultivated mind, and cultivated wisdom. For him, that <s>karma</s> has ripening to be experienced in this very life.' Therefore, the three kinds of <s>karma</s> should be understood as fixed in their time. <s>Karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in this very life is not necessarily experienced in this very life. If it is experienced, it would be experienced in this very life only, not elsewhere. Likewise with the other two as well.

body.text: (pṛ) kena karmaṇā dṛṣṭadharme vipākaṃ vedayate | (u) kecidāhuḥ- vyādhyarthakarmaṇo dṛṣṭadharma eva vipākaṃ vedayate | yathā tathāgata āryeṣu mātāpitrādiṣu samutpāditaṃ yat kuśalamakuśalaṃ karma tat dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyavipākam | yadanarthaguru tadupapadyavedanīyavipākam | yathā pañcānantaryādīni | yadartha guru ca tadūrdhvavedanīyavipākam | yathā cakravartinaḥ karma bodhisattvasya vā karma | kecidāhuḥ- trividhakarmaṇāmeṣāṃ yathāpraṇidhānaṃ vipākaṃ vedayata iti | yat karma praṇidadhāti ihaivādhvani vedayeyamiti | tat dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam | yathā mallikādevī svānnabhāgadānena praṇidadhāti dṛṣṭa evādhvani rājamahiṣī bhaveyamiti | evamanyat karmadvayamapi | yathākarmaparipākaṃ pūrvaṃ vedayate | (pṛ) atītaṃ karma kathaṃ paripacyate | (u) gurutvalakṣaṇasampadeva paripāka ityucyate | (pṛ) yasmin kṣaṇe karmotpadyate tatsamanantarakṣaṇa eva kiṃ vipāko vedyate | (u) na | krameṇaiva vedyate | yathā bījātkrameṇāṅkuraḥ prarohati | karmāpi tathā |
body.translated_text: (Question) By what <s>karma</s> does one experience ripening in this very life? (Answer) Some say: '<s>Karma</s> done for the sake of healing illness has its ripening experienced in this very life.' Also, wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> produced toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Noble Ones, parents, and the like — that has ripening to be experienced in this very life. That whose object is grave has ripening to be experienced upon rebirth — such as the five heinous crimes (<s>ānantarya</s>) and the like. That whose intention is grave has ripening to be experienced subsequently — such as the <s>karma</s> of a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>) or the <s>karma</s> of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Some say: 'The ripening of each of these three kinds of <s>karma</s> is experienced according to one's aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>).' Whatever <s>karma</s> one resolves 'May I experience [its fruit] in this very life' — that has ripening to be experienced in this life. Just as Queen <s>Mallikā</s>, through the gift of a portion of her own food, resolved: 'May I become a chief queen in this very life.' Likewise with the other two kinds of <s>karma</s> as well. One experiences [ripening] first according to the maturation of <s>karma</s>. (Question) How does past <s>karma</s> mature? (Answer) The very possession of the characteristic of gravity is called 'maturation.' (Question) In the very moment when <s>karma</s> arises, is its ripening experienced in the immediately subsequent moment? (Answer) No. It is experienced only sequentially. Just as from a seed, a sprout grows forth gradually — <s>karma</s> too is likewise.

body.text: yo garbhamadhyastho ye ca middhonmattādayaḥ te karma sañcinvanti na vā (u) te sacetanāścet karmopacinvanti | kintu na [te cetanā] sampannāḥ | (pṛ) yo 'syāṃ bhūmau vītarāgaḥ sa pṛthivīkarma karoti na vā | (u) sātmacittāḥ sarve 'pi tat karmopacinvanti | ātmacittavigatāstu nopacinvanti | (pṛ) arhannapi vandanakarmābhyasyati | tatkarma kasmānnopacinoti | (u) yasmāt sattvacittaḥ tasmāt karmāṇyupacinoti | arhannātmacittavihīna ityataḥ karmāṇi nopacinoti | arhannanāsravacittaḥ | yo 'nāsravacittaḥ na sa karmāṇyupacinoti | uktañca sūtre- prahīṇapuṇyapāpakarmako 'rhanniti sa nopacinoti puṇyakarmāṇi apuṇyakarmāṇyāneñjyakarmāṇi ca | ato vedanāparyavasannaṃ karmeti na nūtnaṃ karmābhisaṃskaroti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Does one who is in the midst of the womb, or those who are in torpor, madness, and the like — do they accumulate <s>karma</s> or not? (Answer) If they are sentient, they accumulate <s>karma</s>. However, they are not [fully] endowed [with intention]. (Question) Does one who is free from passion for this plane produce <s>karma</s> of this earth or not? (Answer) All those who possess self-consciousness (<s>ātmacitta</s>) accumulate that <s>karma</s>. But those devoid of self-consciousness do not accumulate it. (Question) An <s>Arhat</s> too practices the <s>karma</s> of salutation. Why does he not accumulate that <s>karma</s>? (Answer) Because one who has a mind of [clinging to] being (<s>sattvacitta</s>) accumulates <s>karmas</s>. An <s>Arhat</s>, being devoid of a mind of self-consciousness, therefore does not accumulate <s>karmas</s>. An <s>Arhat</s> has a mind free from outflows (<s>anāsravacitta</s>). One who has a mind free from outflows does not accumulate <s>karmas</s>. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'An <s>Arhat</s> has abandoned the <s>karmas</s> of merit and sin.' He does not accumulate meritorious <s>karmas</s>, demeritorious <s>karmas</s>, or imperturbable <s>karmas</s> (<s>āneñjyakarma</s>). Therefore, since <s>karma</s> ends in feeling, he does not fashion new <s>karma</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) śaikṣāḥ karmāṇyupacinvanti na vā | (u) nopacinvanti | kasmāt | sūtre hyuktaṃ- sa karmāṇi vidhvasya na sañcinoti nopacinoti niruddhaṃ na tathā bhavati ityādi | ābhidhārmikā vadanti- śaikṣāḥ sāsmimānatvātkarmāṇyapyupacinvanti | nairātmyajñānabalena paraṃ nāvaśyaṃ vedayante vipākamiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Do <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners) accumulate <s>karmas</s> or not? (Answer) They do not accumulate them. Why? Because it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'He destroys <s>karmas</s>, does not accumulate them, does not store them up — what has ceased does not recur' and so forth. The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say: '<s>Śaikṣas</s>, because of still having the conceit "I am" (<s>asmimāna</s>), also accumulate <s>karmas</s>. But through the power of the knowledge of non-self (<s>nairātmyajñāna</s>), they do not necessarily experience the subsequent ripening.'

body.text: (pṛ) imāni karmāṇi kasmin dhātāvabhisaṃskriyante | (u) sarvatra triṣvapi dhātuṣu (pṛ) aniyataṃ karma kimasti kiṃ vā nāsti | (u) asti | yat karma dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyavipākaṃ vā upapadyavedanīyavipākaṃ vā tadūrdhvavedanīyavipākaṃ vā bhavati | tada niyatamityucyate | evaṃ karmāṇi bahūni |
body.translated_text: (Question) In which realm are these <s>karmas</s> fashioned? (Answer) In all three realms. (Question) Does indeterminate <s>karma</s> (<s>aniyatakarma</s>) exist or not? (Answer) It exists. Whatever <s>karma</s> has ripening to be experienced in this very life, or ripening to be experienced upon rebirth, or ripening to be experienced subsequently — that is called 'determinate.' Such <s>karmas</s> are many.

body.text: (pṛ) ya imāni trīṇi karmāṇi prajānāti | tasya ka upakāro bhavati | (u) ya imāni trividhakarmāṇi vivecayati sa samyagdṛṣṭimutpādayati | kasmāt | paśyāmaḥ khalu kecidakuśalacāriṇo 'pi prabhūtaṃ sukhamanubhavati | kuśalacāriṇo duḥkham | udāsīnasya kadācinmithyādṛṣṭirbhavet yaduta kuśalasyākuśalasya vā nāsti vipāka iti | yasteṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ vibhāgaṃ prajānāti | tasya samyagdṛṣṭirbhavati | yathoktaṃ gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: (Question) For one who understands these three kinds of <s>karma</s>, what benefit is there? (Answer) One who discriminates these three kinds of <s>karma</s> generates right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). Why? We observe that some who practice unwholesome deeds also experience abundant happiness, while those who practice wholesome deeds [experience] suffering. For an indifferent person, wrong view might sometimes arise — namely, 'There is no ripening of the wholesome or the unwholesome.' One who understands the division of those <s>karmas</s> — for him, right view arises. As stated in the verse:

children.text: pāpo 'pi paśyati bhadrāṇi yāvatpāpaṃ na pacyate |
children.translated_text: Even a sinner sees good things as long as the sin has not ripened;

children.text: yadā ca pacyate pāpamatha pāpo pāpāni paśyati ||
children.translated_text: but when the sin ripens, then the sinner sees evil things.

children.text: bhadro 'pi paśyati pāpāni yāvadbhadraṃ na pacyate |
children.translated_text: Even a good person sees evil things as long as the good has not ripened;

children.text: yadā ca pacyate bhadramatha bhadro bhadrāṇi paśyati ||
children.translated_text: but when the good ripens, then the good person sees good things.

body.text: mahākarmavibhaṅgasūtramāha- avirataprāṇivadho 'pi svarga utpadyate | yaḥ pūrvādhvani puṇyavān san āyuṣo 'nte prabalakuśalacittamutpādayati iti | evaṃ prajānan samyagdṛṣṭimutpādayati | ata eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ prajānīyāt ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahākarmavibhaṅga Sūtra</s> says: 'Even one who does not abstain from taking life is reborn in heaven — one who was meritorious in past lives, at the end of his lifespan, generates a powerful wholesome mind.' Thus, understanding this, one generates right view. Therefore one should understand the characteristics of these three kinds of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: trividhakarmavipākavargaścaturuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and fourth chapter, the Chapter on the Three Kinds of Karmic Ripening (<s>trividhakarmavipākavarga</s>).

body.text: 105 trividhakarmavipākavedanāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 105. Chapter on the Feeling of the Three Kinds of Karmic Ripening (<s>trividhakarmavipākavedanāvarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtre bhagavānāha- trividhaṃ karma sukhavipākaṃ, duḥkhavipākamaduḥkhāsukhavipākamiti | kimidam | (u) kuśalaṃ karma sukhavipākaprāpakam | akuśalaṃ karma duḥkhavipākaprāpakam | aneñjyaṃ karma aduḥkhāsukhavipākam | tatkarma nāvaśyaṃ niyatavedanam | yadi vedanā bhavati | tadā sukhavipākaṃ vedayate | na duḥkhavipākam ityādi | tathānyat dvayamapi | (pṛ) tāni karmāṇi rūpavipākaprāpakānyapi bhavanti | kasmāduktaṃ [sukhādi]vedanāmātram | (u) vipākeṣu vedanā pradhānā | vedanaiva vastuto vipākaḥ | rūpādi tu tatsādhanam | vedanāpratyayeṣu vedaneti vyavahāraḥ | yathocyate agnirduḥkhamagniḥ sukhamiti | hetau phalopacāraḥ yathānnasya dātā pañcārthānāṃ dāteti | yathā cānnaṃ dhanam ityādi | (pṛ) kāmadhātumārabhya yāvattṛtīyadhyānaṃ kimaduḥkhāsukhavedanāvipāko labhyate | (u) labhyetaiva vedanā | (pṛ) kasya karmaṇo vipāko 'yam | (u) avarakuśalakarmaṇo vipākaḥ | uttamakuśalakarmaṇastu sukhavedanāvipākaḥ | (pṛ) tathā cetkasmāccaturthadhyāna ārūpyasamāpattau [aduḥkhāsukhavedanāvipāka] ucyate | (u) svabhūmikaḥ saḥ | kasmāt | tatrāyameva vipāko 'sti | na punarvipākāntaram | sūpaśāntatvāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) The Blessed One said in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Karma</s> is of three kinds: that with pleasant ripening, that with painful ripening, and that with neither-painful-nor-pleasant ripening.' What is this? (Answer) Wholesome <s>karma</s> leads to pleasant ripening. Unwholesome <s>karma</s> leads to painful ripening. Imperturbable <s>karma</s> (<s>āneñjyakarma</s>) [leads to] neither-painful-nor-pleasant ripening. That <s>karma</s> does not necessarily have a fixed [type of] feeling [as its result]. If there is feeling, then one experiences pleasant ripening, not painful ripening — and so forth. Likewise with the other two as well. (Question) Those <s>karmas</s> also lead to ripening as form. Why is only feeling mentioned? (Answer) Among ripenings, feeling is predominant. Feeling alone is in reality the ripening. Form and the rest are merely its instruments. In the conditions for feeling, the designation 'feeling' is used. As it is said: 'Fire is suffering; fire is happiness.' The effect is figuratively applied to the cause — just as 'the giver of food is the giver of five things.' And just as 'food is wealth' and so forth. (Question) From the desire realm up to the third <s>dhyāna</s>, is the ripening of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling obtained? (Answer) That feeling is indeed obtained. (Question) Of which <s>karma</s> is this the ripening? (Answer) It is the ripening of inferior wholesome <s>karma</s>. But the ripening of supreme wholesome <s>karma</s> is pleasant feeling. (Question) If so, why is it said that in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and the formless attainments, there is ripening of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? (Answer) That is specific to those planes. Why? Because there, only this ripening exists and no other ripening — due to [those planes'] extreme tranquility.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- daurmanasyaṃ na vipāka iti | kathamidam | (u) kasmānna bhavati | (pṛ) daurmanasyaṃ saṃjñāvikalpamātrādutpadyate | [karma]
body.translated_text: Some say: 'Displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is not [karmic] ripening.' What does this mean? (Answer) Why would it not be? (Question) Displeasure arises merely from conceptual discrimination (<s>saṃjñāvikalpa</s>). [Karmic]

body.text: vipākasya saṃjñāvikalpatvā bhāvāt | yadi daurmanasyaṃ vipākaḥ | tadā laghuḥ syāt vipākaḥ | ato na vipākaḥ | daurmanasyaṃ vitarāgāṇāṃ vyāvartate | na vipāko vītarāgāṇāṃ vyāvartate | ato daurmanasyaṃ na vipākaḥ syāt | ucyate | daurmanasyaṃ saṃjñāvikalpādutpadyata ityato na vipākaḥ | sukhantu vipāka iti bravīṣi | dvividhaṃ sukham- sukhaṃ saumanasyañceti | tatra saumanasyamapi saṃjñāvikalpādutpadyata iti na vipākaḥ syāt | bhavānāha vipākastarhi laghuḥ syāditi | daurmanasyamidaṃ duḥkhāt duḥkhataradoṣaḥ | kasmāt | taddhi mūḍhānāṃ vidyate | na tu jñāninām | ato duḥśśodhaṃ paramasantāpakarañca | kiñca catuśśatakaparīkṣāyāmuktam-
body.translated_text: ripening does not have the nature of conceptual discrimination. If displeasure were ripening, then the ripening would be light. Therefore it is not ripening. Displeasure ceases for those free from passion. But [karmic] ripening does not cease for those free from passion. Therefore displeasure would not be ripening. (Answer) [Your argument is:] 'Displeasure arises from conceptual discrimination, therefore it is not ripening.' But you say that happiness is ripening. Happiness is of two kinds: bodily happiness (<s>sukha</s>) and mental happiness (<s>saumanasya</s>). Therein, mental happiness too arises from conceptual discrimination — so it too would not be ripening. You have said: 'Then ripening would be light.' This displeasure is a more painful fault than [bodily] suffering. Why? Because it exists for the deluded, not for the wise. Therefore it is difficult to purify and produces extreme distress. Furthermore, in the <s>Catuśśatakaparīkṣā</s> it is stated:

body.text: agryāṇāṃ mānasaṃ duḥkhamitareṣāṃ śarīrajam iti |
body.translated_text: For those of the highest [attainment], suffering is mental; for the rest, it is bodily. Thus it is said.

body.text: tacca daurmanasyaṃ jñānapraheyaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhamapi pariharati | daurmanasya triṣvadhvasu kleśaṃ janayati yaduta pūrvamahaṃ duḥkhī idānīṃ duḥkhī āyatyāñca duḥkhīti | daurmanasyaṃ kleśānāṃ pratiṣṭhāyatanam | yathā sūtre kleśāyatanatvenāṣṭādaśa manaupavicārā bhavanti | pañcavijñānānāṃ kleśājanakatvāt | uktañca sūtre- daurmanasyaṃ dviśalyarūpamiti | gurutaraduḥkhavedanābhūtatvāt | yathā kaścidekatra gurutaradviśalyaviddho duḥkhamadhikataraṃ pratisaṃvedayate | yathā ca rogī kaścit [roga]duḥkhābhihataḥ punaḥ kāyacittapīḍanayātyadhikadaurmanasyopāyāso bhavati | ato duḥkhādadhikataraṃ [daurmanasyam] | mūḍhā nityadaurmanasyāḥ | kasmāt | te hi priyavirahavipriyasamāgamaprārthitālabhādimattvāt nityadaurmanasyapīḍitāḥ |
body.translated_text: That displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is to be abandoned by knowledge. It also averts bodily happiness and suffering. Displeasure generates defilements in the three time-periods — namely: 'Previously I was suffering, now I am suffering, and in the future I shall be suffering.' Displeasure is the base of establishment for defilements. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, the eighteen mental investigations (<s>manaupavicāra</s>) function as bases of defilements. Because the five consciousnesses do not generate defilements. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Displeasure has the form of a double dart (<s>dviśalya</s>).' Because it is a more intense painful feeling. Just as someone pierced by a more intense double dart in one place experiences more intense suffering. And just as a sick person, stricken by the suffering of [his] disease, again through the affliction of body and mind has excessively intense displeasure and despair. Therefore [displeasure] is more intense than [bodily] suffering. The deluded are constantly subject to displeasure. Why? Because, possessing separation from the beloved, union with the hateful, not obtaining what is desired, and the like, they are constantly afflicted by displeasure.

body.text: taddaurmanasyaṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate ekaṃ saumanasyādutpadyate | dvitīyaṃ daurmanasyāt | tadā priyavastu praṇaśyati tadā saumanasyajaṃ [daurmanasyam] | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhagavān
body.translated_text: That displeasure arises from two causes: the first arises from elation (<s>saumanasya</s>); the second arises from displeasure itself. When a beloved object perishes, then [there arises] displeasure born from elation. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Blessed One

body.text: prasenajitaṃ rājānamapṛcchat- api tvaṃ [mahārāja] kāśīkosaleṣu priyo 'si iti | uktañca- devā rūpāsaktā rūpakāmāḥ rūpe vinaṣṭe daurmanasyajātā bhavanti | iti | idaṃ saumanasyādutpannam | daurmanasyādutpannamiti yat vipriyavastusamutpannam | īrṣyādibhyo 'pi samutpadyate | avītarāgasya īrṣyādisaṃyojanāni sadā cittaṃ pīḍayanti | yathoktam- īrṣyāmātsarya bahulā devā iti | bahavaśca sattvā daurmanasyakaraṃ parān sampīḍayantaḥ sadaurmanasyasampīḍanavipākaṃ labhante | yathoktam- yathābījaṃ phalaṃ pravartata iti | ato jñāyate daurmanasyaṃ karmavipāka iti |
body.translated_text: asked King <s>Prasenajit</s>: "Are you, O great king, beloved in <s>Kāśī</s> and <s>Kosala</s>?"' And it is said: 'Gods, attached to form, desiring form — when form is destroyed, they become subject to displeasure.' This is [displeasure] arisen from elation. That which is 'arisen from displeasure' means that which arises from an unpleasant object. It also arises from jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and the like. For one who is not free from passion, the fetters of jealousy and the like constantly afflict the mind. As stated: 'The gods are abundant in jealousy and avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>).' And many beings, afflicting others so as to produce displeasure, obtain the ripening of being afflicted with displeasure [themselves]. As stated: 'The fruit proceeds according to the seed.' Therefore it is known that displeasure is a ripening of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhavatā- vītarāgāṇāṃ vyāvṛttatvānna vipāka iti | tadayuktam | srota āpanno 'vītarāgo 'pi vyāvṛttanarakādivipākaḥ | narakādivipāko na vipāka iti kiṃ sambhavet | ato na sambhavati vītarāgāṇāṃ vyāvṛttamavipāka iti |
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'for those free from passion, because [suffering] has been averted, there is no ripening' — that is untenable. A stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>), though not free from passion, has averted the ripening of rebirth in hells and the like. Would the ripening of hells and the like then not be a ripening? That is not possible. Therefore it is not possible [to maintain] that for those free from passion, what has been averted is not a ripening.

body.text: (pṛ) aduḥkhāsukhaṃ karma āneñjyam | tat karma kuśalaṃ satsukhavedanīyavipākaṃ syāt | kasmādaduḥkhāsukhavedanīyavipākam | (u) vedaneyamāneñjyeti vastutaḥ sukham | upaśamarūpatvādaduḥkhāsukhetyucyate | uktañca sūtre- sukhavedanāyāṃ rāgo 'nuśaya iti | yatra rāgaḥ tadvedanāyāṃ [so ']nuśayaḥ | iti jñāyata idaṃ sukhamiti ||
body.translated_text: (Question) <s>Karma</s> that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant is imperturbable (<s>āneñjya</s>). That <s>karma</s>, being wholesome, should have a ripening experienced as pleasant feeling. Why then does it have a ripening experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? (Answer) That feeling is in reality pleasant when it is imperturbable (<s>āneñjya</s>). Because it has the nature of tranquility, it is called 'neither-painful-nor-pleasant.' And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'In pleasant feeling, passion becomes latent (<s>anuśaya</s>).' Where there is passion, that is latent in feeling. Therefore it is known that this is pleasant.

body.text: trividhakarmavipākavedanāvargaḥ pañcottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-fifth chapter, the Chapter on the Three Kinds of Karma and the Feeling of Ripening (<s>trividhakarmavipākavedanāvarga</s>).

body.text: 106 trividhāvaraṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 106. Chapter on the Three Obstructions (<s>trividhāvaraṇavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktaṃ- trīṇyāvaraṇāni karmāvaraṇaṃ kleśāvaraṇaṃ vipākāvaraṇamiti | kānīmāni | (u) karmāṇi kleśā vipākāśca vimuktimārgamāvṛṇvantīti āvaraṇāni | (pṛ) kimityāvṛṇvanti | (u) dānaśīlakuśalābhyāsastriṣu bhaveṣu parivartayatīti sa mārgamāvṛṇoti | samāpattivedanīyaṃ karmāpyāvaraṇam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo 'yaṃ puruṣo nitayaṃ samāpattau vedanīyavipākaṃ karmopacinoti na sa supade 'vatarati iti | idaṃ karmāvaraṇam | yat kasyacitkleśā ghanāstīvrāścittagatāḥ tat kleśāvaraṇam | yat kasyacit kleśā anivāryāḥ tadyathā ṣaṇḍādīnāṃ kāmaḥ | tadapi kleśāvaraṇam | yannarakādau pāpākuśalopapattyāyatane yathopapattyāyanañca na mārgaṃ bhāvayati | tat vipākāvaraṇam |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are three obstructions (<s>āvaraṇa</s>): the obstruction of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>), the obstruction of defilements (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>), and the obstruction of ripening (<s>vipākāvaraṇa</s>).' What are these? (Answer) <s>Karmas</s>, defilements, and ripenings obstruct the path of liberation — therefore they are called obstructions. (Question) How do they obstruct? (Answer) Through the habitual practice of wholesome [actions] such as generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), one revolves in the three existences — thus one obstructs the path. <s>Karma</s> whose ripening is experienced in the attainment [of meditative states] is also an obstruction. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A person who always accumulates <s>karma</s> whose ripening is experienced in the attainment — he does not enter the good path.' This is the obstruction of <s>karma</s>. When someone's defilements are dense, intense, and pervade the mind — that is the obstruction of defilements. When someone's defilements are irresistible — just as the desire of eunuchs (<s>ṣaṇḍa</s>) and the like — that too is the obstruction of defilements. When, in hell and the like, in the place of birth (<s>upapattyāyatana</s>) characterized by sinful unwholesome [karma], depending on the place of birth, one does not cultivate the path — that is the obstruction of ripening.

body.text: (pṛ) kecit pūrvaṃ vidyāvihīnebhyaḥ pūrvapuruṣebhyo na prajānanti idaṃ kuśalamiti | tadā te na dadanti yat sa yadi matto dānaṃ labdhvā akuśalāni karoti tadā ahaṃ bhāgī syāmiti | yathā brāhmaṇādayaḥ parivrājakāḥ | ataḥ parivrājako na dadyāt | nūtnakarmaṇā mārgapratibandhāt | (u) na yuktamidam | nānyakṛtasya puṇyaṃ pāpamātmano bhāgo bhavati | kasmāt | pratyayānāṃ puṇyapāpavattve bahūnyavadyāni santi | kimiti | yathā sattvo vadhasya pratyayaḥ | yadi nāsti sattvaḥ | kasya vadhaḥ syāt | tathā ca mṛtena pāpinā bhāvyam | yathā ca ghanikaścauryasya pratyayaḥ | sūrūpaṃ kāmamithyācārasya pratyayaḥ | parapuruṣā mṛṣāvādādīnāṃ pratyayāḥ | kūṭamānādayaḥ kuhanāyāḥ pratyayāḥ iti kretāraḥ pāpinaḥ syuḥ | pratigrahītā dānasya pratyaya iti puṇyabhāk syāt | ye kūpataṭākādyupabhoktāraḥ te sarve puṇyabhājaḥ syuḥ | tathā ca svasya puṇyaṃ na syāt | na tat vastuto yujyate | ataḥ pratyayānāṃ na syātpuṇyapāpavattā |
body.translated_text: (Question) Certain people, not understanding from their predecessors who were devoid of learning, do not know 'this is wholesome.' At that time they do not give, [thinking]: 'If he, having received a gift from me, commits unwholesome deeds, then I would have a share [in that sin].' Just as <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and other wandering ascetics (<s>parivrājaka</s>) [think]. Therefore the wandering ascetic should not give. Through new <s>karma</s>, the path is obstructed. (Answer) This is not valid. The merit or sin done by another does not become one's own share. Why? If merit and sin belonged to conditions [i.e., to the facilitators], there would be many faults. How so? Just as a being is the condition for killing — if there were no being, whose killing would there be? Then the one killed would have to be sinful. Just as a goldsmith is the condition for theft; a beautiful form is the condition for sexual misconduct; other persons are the conditions for false speech and the like; false weights and measures and the like are the conditions for deceit — then buyers would be sinful. The recipient is the condition of a gift — then he would partake of merit. All those who enjoy wells, ponds, and the like would partake of merit. And then one's own merit would not exist. That is not valid in reality. Therefore merit and sin do not belong to conditions.

body.text: atha yadi
body.translated_text: Moreover, if

body.text: pratigrahītuḥ svapuṇyabhāgaḥ kṣīyamāṇaḥ syāt | tadā na kaścidanyasmāt dānaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt | kasmāt | svapuṇyabhāgenānnapānayoḥ krīyamāṇatvāt | dātā ca pāpabahulo 'lpapuṇyaḥ syāt | kasmāt | kiyatkuśalaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ kuryuriti | bhūyasā te trividhaviṣakaluṣitacittāḥ pañcakāmaguṇāsaktā na vyavasyanti kuśalabhāvanām | ato dātā pāpabahulo 'lpapuṇyaḥ syāt | brāhmaṇādaya ātmānaṃ sujanabhāvitadharmacaya iti kīrtayanto na samyak paśyanti samāpatticittasamādhānāni dharmān | ye dhyānasamāpattivinirmuktāḥ te cittadurvineyāḥ | ato dātā avītarāgāya dadan pāpabāhulyaṃ labheta | janāḥ pitṝn pūjayantaḥ putrabhāryābandhūn samārādhayantaḥ [yadi] jñātvā vijānanti sarve pāpaṃ prāpayeyuriti | tadā na ko 'pi puṇyabhāk syāt | na tu vastutastathā yujyate | ataḥ puṇyaṃ pāpañca na pratyayagatam | śīlādidharmopi pareṣāṃ hitakaraḥ | prāṇātipātavirataḥ sarveṣāṃ jīvitaṃ prayacchati | śīladhārī tadā mahāpāpabhāgaṃ labheta | prāṇātipātaviratyā purovartijano jīvitalabdho yadakuśalaṃ karoti | tat śīlavato bhāgaḥ syāt | ataḥ puṇyārthī punaḥ prāṇinaṃ hanyāt, na śīlaṃ dhārayet |
body.translated_text: the recipient's own share of merit were to be diminished [by receiving], then no one would accept a gift from another. Why? Because one's own share of merit would be spent in exchange for food and drink. And the giver would have much sin and little merit. Why? How much wholesome [action] would the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> perform? For the most part, their minds are defiled by the three poisons, attached to the five strands of sensual pleasure — they do not endeavor in the cultivation of the wholesome. Therefore the giver would have much sin and little merit. <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and others, proclaiming themselves as 'those of good birth who have accumulated <s>dharma</s>,' do not correctly perceive the <s>dharmas</s> of concentration and <s>samādhi</s> of mind. Those who are free from <s>dhyāna</s> and attainment — their minds are difficult to train. Therefore the giver, giving to one who is not free from passion, would obtain an abundance of sin. If people, honoring parents, satisfying sons, wives, and relatives — [if] knowing this, they understand that all would produce sin — then no one would partake of merit. But in reality it is not so. Therefore merit and sin do not belong to conditions. <s>Dharmas</s> such as moral conduct and the like also benefit others. One who abstains from taking life gives life to all. Then the upholder of moral conduct would obtain a great share of sin. Through the abstainer's abstention from taking life, the people in front of him, having obtained their lives, commit whatever unwholesome [actions] — that would be the share of the upholder of moral conduct. Therefore one who desires merit should rather kill beings, and not uphold moral conduct.

body.text: kiñca kaściddharmamupadiśati | tena paraḥ puṇyamabhyasyati | puṇyābhyāsapratyayaṃ paścātprabhūtaghanaṃ labhate | prabhūtaghanena pramatto bhavati | pramattaḥ san pāpāni karoti | teṣāṃ pāpānāṃ dharmabhāṇako bhāgī syāt | dānapratyayaṃ paro ghaniko bhavati | ghanikatvahetoḥ kṛtānāṃ pāpānāmapi dātā bhāgī syāt | tathā ca brāhmaṇā na dānaṃ pratigṛhṇīyuḥ | nāpi prayaccheyuḥ | idānīntu brāhmaṇāḥ kevalaṃ pratigṛhṇanti na prayacchanti | ato jñāyate sa duṣṭaḥ panthā iti |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, someone teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. Through that, another practices merit. As a condition of practicing merit, he later obtains abundant wealth. Through abundant wealth, he becomes heedless. Being heedless, he commits sins. The <s>Dharma</s>-preacher would have a share of those sins. As a condition of a gift, another becomes a goldsmith. The giver would also have a share of the sins committed because of being a goldsmith. And then <s>brāhmaṇas</s> would neither accept gifts nor give them. But now, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> only accept and do not give. Therefore it is known that that is a wrong path.

body.text: yathā ca rājāno yathādharmaṃ prajāḥ pālayantaḥ pāpino 'pi syuḥ | yadi putraḥ pāpaṃ karoti | tadā pitarau bhāginau syātām | tadā na putramutpādayetām | vaidyaścikitsamāno 'pi pāpabhāk syāt | taccikitsālabdhajīvitena pāpakaraṇāt | deve varṣati pañcasasyānyāyatāni prarohanti | tadā devaḥ pāpabhāk syāt | duṣṭasattvānāṃ poṣaṇaparitrāṇakaratvāt | annadātāpi pāpabhāg syāt | bhokturannamajīrṇaṃ kadācinmaraṇāya bhavet | avītarāga āsvādābhiniviṣṭa ityato dātā pāpī syāt | tathā ca dātā, tvadannaṃ bhuktvā nākuśalaṃ kariṣyāmīti bhoktāraṃ sadā pratijñāpya paścāddāsyati | tathā no cet dāturubhayaṃ naśyet |
body.translated_text: Just as kings, ruling their subjects according to <s>dharma</s>, would also be sinful. If a son commits sin, then the parents would have a share. Then one should not beget a son. A physician practicing medicine would also partake of sin — because the one whose life was saved by the treatment commits sin. When the god rains, the five crops and weeds grow abundantly. Then the god would partake of sin — because of nourishing and protecting evil beings. The giver of food would also partake of sin — because the food of the eater, sometimes not being digested, may cause death. [Or because] one who is not free from passion is engrossed in relishing [food] — therefore the giver would be sinful. And then the giver, having always made the eater promise: 'Having eaten your food, I shall not commit unwholesome [deeds]' — only afterward would he give. If not, both [merit and sin] would be lost for the giver.

body.text: (pṛ) nanu sūtre 'pyuktam- yadi bhikṣurdānapaterannaṃ bhuktvā cīvarañca paridhāyāpramāṇasamādhimupasampadya viharati tatpratyayāt sa dānapatirapramāṇapuṇyaṃ prasūta iti | tatpratyayena puṇyalābhī cet kathaṃ na pāpabhāk bhavati | (u) yadi sa bhikṣurdānapaterannaṃ bhuktvā cīvarañca paridhāyāpramāṇasamādhimupasampadya viharati | tadā dānapaterdānapuṇyaṃ svata evādhikaṃ vardhate | na tu tatsamādheḥ puṇyabhāk bhavati | yathā kṣetrasya sāravattvādāyaphalaṃ bahu bhavati | bandhye 'lpam | evaṃ puṇyakṣetrasya sāravattve dānavipāko mahān | vandhye puṇyamalpam | na tu pratigrahītuḥ puṇye pāpe vā dātā bhāgaṃ labhate | ato na tatpuṇyapāpapratyayena dātā puṇyapāpabhāk bhavati | sa yadyapi pratyayo bhavati | tathāpi svaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ vā svakṛtatrividhakarmāpekṣya bhavati |
body.translated_text: (Question) But it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'If a monk, having eaten the food of a donor and having put on his robes, attains and dwells in the immeasurable <s>samādhi</s> — through that condition, that donor produces immeasurable merit.' If through that condition one obtains merit, how can one not partake of sin? (Answer) If that monk, having eaten the food of the donor and having put on his robes, attains and dwells in the immeasurable <s>samādhi</s> — then the merit of the donor's gift itself increases greatly. But he does not partake of the merit of that <s>samādhi</s>. Just as because of the richness of a field, the crop-yield is abundant; in a barren [field], it is little. So too, because of the richness of the field of merit (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>), the ripening of the gift is great; in a barren [field], the merit is small. But the giver does not partake of the merit or sin of the recipient. Therefore the giver does not partake of merit or sin through the condition of [the recipient's] merit or sin. Even though he is a condition, nevertheless one's own merit or sin exists in dependence on one's own threefold <s>karma</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) avītarāgasya cittaṃ na svavaśavarti, avaśyaṃ kāmāsaktam | ataḥ pravrajito na dānamācaret [tasya] | (u) tathā cet pravrajinaḥ śīlādin dhṛtvā sapuṇyo bhavatīdamupekṣitaṃ syāt | na vastutastatsambhavati | ato dānamapi nopekṣyam | tribhavānāṃ kṛte kebalaṃ nācaret | nirvāṇāya paramācaret | kintu kleśānakuśalakarmāṇi ca varjayet | kasmāt | tāni hi karmāṇi hetukāla eva vāryāṇi | phalakāle na kathamapi śakyate [vārayitum] | ato buddhā [bhagavanto] hetukāla eva vinayāya dharmamupadiśanti | na tu yamarājavat phalakāle 'parādhamanyathayeyuḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) The mind of one who is not free from passion is not under one's own control — it is necessarily attached to sensual pleasures. Therefore a renunciant should not practice giving [to such a one]. (Answer) If that were so, then the fact that renunciants, having upheld moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and the like, become endowed with merit — that would be disregarded. But in reality that is not tenable. Therefore giving too should not be disregarded. One should practice [giving] solely for the sake of the three existences — but not at all; one should practice it supremely for the sake of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. But one should avoid defilements and unwholesome <s>karmas</s>. Why? Because those <s>karmas</s> are to be prevented at the time of the cause. At the time of the fruit, they cannot be prevented in any way. Therefore the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, teach the <s>Dharma</s> for discipline at the time of the cause — but they do not, like <s>Yamarāja</s> (the King of Death), alter offenses at the time of the fruit.

body.text: (pṛ) triṣvāvaraṇeṣu kiṃ gurutaram | (u) kecidāhuḥ- vipākāvaraṇaṃ gurutaramiti | anyathayitumaśakyatvāt | [anye] kecidāhuḥ- pudgalānusaraṇataḥ sarvaṃ gurutaram | (pṛ) kiṃ nivartyaṃ bhavati | (u) sarvaṃ hāpayituṃ śakyam | yannivartyaṃ na tadāvaraṇamityucyate ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Among the three obstructions, which is the most severe? (Answer) Some say: 'The obstruction of ripening (<s>vipākāvaraṇa</s>) is the most severe' — because it cannot be altered. Others say: 'According to the individual person, any [of the three] may be the most severe.' (Question) Can [the obstructions] be removed? (Answer) All can be eliminated. What can be removed is not called an 'obstruction.'

body.text: trividhāvaraṇavargaḥ ṣaḍuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-sixth chapter, the Chapter on the Three Obstructions (<s>trividhāvaraṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 107 catuḥkarmavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 107. Chapter on the Four Kinds of Karma (<s>catuḥkarmavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtre bhagavatoktam- catvārīmāni karmāṇi | [katamāni] | asti karma kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavipākam | asti karma śuklaṃ śuklavipākam | asti karma kṛṣṇaśuklaṃ kṛṣṇaśuklavipākam | asti karma akṛṣṇamaśuklamakṛṣṇāśuklavipākam | karma karmakṣayāya saṃvartata iti | kāni tāni | (u) asti karma kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavipākamiti | yena karmaṇā savyābādhye loke yathāvaivartinaraka upapadyate | anyatra ca savyābādhye 'kuśala vipākāyatane samupapadyate yadi vā tiryañca ekatyāḥ pretā vā | etadviparītaṃ dvitīyaṃ karma | yena karmaṇā avyābādhye loka upapadyate yathā rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ kāmadhātau ca devā manuṣyā ekatyāḥ | kṛṣṇaśuklavyāmiśraṃ karma tṛtīyam | yena karmaṇā samutpadyate savyābādhye 'vyābādhye ca loke yadi vā tiryañcaḥ pretā devā manuṣyā ekatyāḥ | caturthamanāsravaṃ karma trīṇi karmāṇi kṣapayati |
body.translated_text: (Question) The Blessed One stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four kinds of <s>karma</s>. What are they? There is <s>karma</s> that is black with black ripening. There is <s>karma</s> that is white with white ripening. There is <s>karma</s> that is black-and-white with black-and-white ripening. There is <s>karma</s> that is neither black nor white, with neither-black-nor-white ripening — <s>karma</s> that leads to the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>.' What are these? (Answer) 'There is <s>karma</s> that is black with black ripening' — that is the <s>karma</s> by which one is reborn in a world with affliction, such as the <s>Avaivartika</s> hell and elsewhere in unwholesome realms of ripening with affliction, whether as animals, certain hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>), or [the like]. The second <s>karma</s> is the opposite of this — the <s>karma</s> by which one is reborn in a world without affliction, such as the form and formless realms (<s>rūpārūpyadhātu</s>), and certain gods and humans in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). The third <s>karma</s> is a mixture of black and white — the <s>karma</s> by which one is reborn in a world both with and without affliction, whether as animals, hungry ghosts, gods, or certain humans. The fourth is undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>karma</s>, which exhausts the [other] three <s>karmas</s>.

body.text: yat karmalokadvayavigarhitaṃ iha vigarhitamamutra ca vigarhitam | tat pāpaṃ karma puruṣaḥ kṛtvā tamasi patitaḥ san na yaśaḥ śrutavān bhavatīti kṛṣṇamityucyate | iha duḥkhamamutra duḥkhamityadhvadvaye 'pi duḥkhaviṣamiti kṛṣṇam | (pṛ) idaṃ karma kimiti savyābādhyalokajanakam | (u) nimittakrameṇākuśalaṃ kṛtvā na cittaṃ paritapati | antarāle cākuśalavyāvartakaṃ kuśalaṃ nāsti | idaṃ karma savyābādhyalokajanakam | mithyādṛṣṭicittena hi kriyante 'kuśalāni | akuśalakriyā ca gurujaneṣu yanmātāpitṛṣu anyeṣu sajjaneṣu ca | sattvānāmahitaṃ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi kṛpāṃ karoti | yathā sattvān hanti samastaṃ taddhanaṃ vāpaharati | kārāgāre vā badhvā punarāhāramapi niṣedhayati | gurutaraṃ vā tāḍayati | tena na bhavati sukhāntaramapi | evamādi karma ekāntasavyābādhyalokajanakam |
body.translated_text: That <s>karma</s> which is despised in both worlds — despised here and despised hereafter — a person who has committed that sinful <s>karma</s>, having fallen into darkness, does not become one of fame and learning — therefore it is called 'black.' Here there is suffering and hereafter there is suffering — because in both courses of time there is the poison of suffering, it is 'black.' (Question) Why does this <s>karma</s> generate a world with affliction? (Answer) Having committed the unwholesome in the course of signs (<s>nimittakrama</s>), the mind does not feel remorse. And in the interval, there is no wholesome [<s>karma</s>] to counteract the unwholesome. This <s>karma</s> generates a world with affliction. For unwholesome actions are committed with a mind of wrong views. And the unwholesome action is [directed] toward elders, namely toward parents and other virtuous persons. Having done what is harmful to beings, one does not generate even the slightest compassion. Just as one who kills beings and steals all their wealth, or imprisons them and further denies them food, or beats them even more severely — for him there is not even a modicum of happiness. Such and similar <s>karma</s> is exclusively the generator of a world with affliction.

body.text: śuklaṃ śuklavipākaṃ karmeti | yaḥ kaścidekāntataḥ kuśalānyupacinoti | akuśalavāṃśca na bhavati | tatkarmadvayātiśayabalaṃ mahattamam | nānyattadatiśete | na kṛṣṇavipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayataḥ śuklavipākasya prasaṅgo 'sti | nāpi śuklavipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayataḥ kṛṣṇavipākasya prasaṅgaḥ | kasmāt | sarve sattvāḥ kuśalamakuśalañcopacinvanti | karmabalasya parasparamāvaraṇatvānna yugapatpratisaṃvedayante | yathā dvayormallayo balīyānagre vinipātayati [durbalam] | tṛtīyaṃ karma durbalaṃ kuśalākuśalavyāmiśratvāt tadvipākaṃ yugapatpratisaṃvedayate | anyonyaṃ spardhitvāt |
body.translated_text: 'White <s>karma</s> with white ripening' — whoever accumulates the wholesome exclusively, and does not have an unwholesome share — that <s>karma</s> of surpassing strength of the two is the greatest. Nothing else surpasses it. There is no occasion for white ripening when experiencing black ripening, nor for black ripening when experiencing white ripening. Why? All beings accumulate both the wholesome and the unwholesome. Because the power of <s>karma</s> mutually obstructs, they are not experienced simultaneously. Just as between two wrestlers, the stronger one first defeats the weaker one. The third <s>karma</s> is weak — because it is a mixture of wholesome and unwholesome, its ripening is experienced simultaneously, because they compete with each other.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- yadakuśalaṃ karma durgatau vipākapratisaṃvedakaṃ tadādyaṃ karma | yadrūpadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalaṃ tat dvitīyaṃ karma | yat kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu vyāmiśravipākapratisaṃvedakaṃ tat tṛtīyaṃ karma | anāvaraṇamārge saptadaśaśaikṣacetanā caturthaṃ karma iti | kathamayamarthaḥ syāt | (u) bhagavān svayamavocadeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ lakṣaṇam | yaduta ekatyaḥ savyābādhyaṃ kāyasaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti, savyābādhyaṃ vāksaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti, savyābādhyaṃ manaḥ saṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti | sa savyābādhyaṃ kāyasaṃskāramabhisaṃskṛtya savyābādhyaṃ vāksaṃskāramabhisaṃskṛtya savyābādhyaṃ manaḥsaṃskāramabhisaṃskṛtya savyābādhye loke utpadyate | tatra savyābādhye loka utpannaṃ santaṃ savyābādhyāḥ sparśāḥ spṛśanti iti | ato jñāyate yat sattvānāṃ kṛṣṇaduḥkhalokotpādakaṃ tadādyaṃ karmeti | rūpārūpyadhātvostu ekāntasukhavedanaiva | kāmadhātukadevamanuṣyā apyekāntasukhavedinaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- sukhināṃ manuṣyāṇāmapi santi ṣaṭ sparśā iti | devamanuṣyairanubhūyamānā viṣayā yena amanorūpā na bhavanti tat dvitīyaṃ karma | kṛṣṇaśuklavyāmiśrasamudācaraṇaṃ tṛtīyaṃ karma | sarvāṇyanāsravakarmāṇi karmāṇāṃ kṣayāya saṃvartante | mitho virodhāt | na saptadaśaśaikṣacetanāmātraṃ caturthaṃ karma |
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: 'The unwholesome <s>karma</s> that produces the experience of ripening in the lower destinies is the first <s>karma</s>. The wholesome <s>karma</s> connected with the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) is the second <s>karma</s>. The <s>karma</s> connected with the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) that produces the experience of mixed ripening among gods and humans is the third <s>karma</s>. On the unobstructed path (<s>ānāvaraṇamārga</s>), the seventeen <s>śaikṣa</s> (trainee) volitions constitute the fourth <s>karma</s>.' How should this meaning be [understood]? (Answer) The Blessed One himself stated the characteristics of these <s>karmas</s> — namely: 'A certain one conditions bodily formations with affliction, conditions vocal formations with affliction, conditions mental formations with affliction. Having conditioned bodily formations with affliction, having conditioned vocal formations with affliction, having conditioned mental formations with affliction, one is reborn in a world with affliction. Having been reborn in a world with affliction, contacts with affliction touch him.' From this it is known that whatever generates a world of black suffering for beings — that is the first <s>karma</s>. In the form and formless realms, there is exclusively pleasant feeling only. Certain gods and humans of the desire realm too experience exclusively pleasant feeling. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Even for humans who are happy, there are six [kinds of] contacts.' The sense objects experienced by gods and humans that are not displeasing — that is the second <s>karma</s>. The third <s>karma</s> is the mixed practice of black and white. All undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>karmas</s> lead to the exhaustion of <s>karmas</s> — because of their mutual opposition. It is not merely the seventeen <s>śaikṣa</s> volitions that constitute the fourth <s>karma</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) anāsravaṃ vastutaḥ śuklam | kasmādaśuklamityucyate | (u) tat śuklalakṣaṇādbhinnam | na dvitīyaśuklakarmasamānam | asmādatiśayitamaśuklasya, tadanapekṣatvāt | yathā rājñaścakravartinaḥ suviśuddhātikrāntadevamānuṣacakṣuḥ sampat | vastutastu tanmānuṣameva cakṣuḥ | anyapuruṣātiśāyitvādatimānuṣamityucyate | tathā tatkarmāpi anyaśuklakarmātiśāyitvādaśuklamityucyate | kecidāhuḥ- akṛṣṇaṃ śuklavipākaṃ karmeti vaktavyamiti | tattvaduṣṭam | nirvāṇañca na śuklam | atastatkarmāśuklamiti vācyam | vaktavyañcākṛṣṇamaśuklamiti | kasmāt | nirvāṇaṃ hyadharmaḥ | nirvāṇārthatvāttatkarmākṛṣṇamaśuklam | loke ślādhyataraṃ sāsravaṃ kuśalaṃ karma śuklamityucyate | caturthaṃ karma tatkarma vyāvartayatīti aśuklam | tasya karmaṇo 'kṛṣṇalakṣaṇatvādaśuklalakṣaṇatāpi prāpyate | vipākasya śuklatvātkarma śuklamityākhyāyate | idaṃ karma tvavipākamityato na śuklamityākhyāyate ||
body.translated_text: (Question) The undefiled is in reality white. Why is it called 'non-white'? (Answer) It is different from the characteristic of white. It is not the same as the second white <s>karma</s>. It surpasses [ordinary] 'non-white,' because it is independent of it. Just as the king <s>Cakravartin</s> has supremely pure vision surpassing that of gods and humans. In reality, that is indeed a human eye. Because it surpasses that of other persons, it is called 'superhuman.' Likewise, that <s>karma</s> too, because it surpasses other white <s>karmas</s>, is called 'non-white.' Some say: 'It should be said that it is non-black and has white ripening.' That is incorrect. <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not white. Therefore that <s>karma</s> should be called 'non-white.' And it should be said to be 'non-black and non-white.' Why? Because <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is a non-existent <s>dharma</s>. Because it aims at <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, that <s>karma</s> is neither black nor white. In the world, the more praiseworthy defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>) wholesome <s>karma</s> is called 'white.' The fourth <s>karma</s> counteracts that <s>karma</s> — therefore it is 'non-white.' Because that <s>karma</s> has the characteristic of being non-black, it also obtains the characteristic of being non-white. Because the ripening is white, <s>karma</s> is designated as 'white.' But this <s>karma</s> is without ripening — therefore it is not designated as 'white.'

body.text: catuḥkarmavargaḥ saptotaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-seventh chapter, the Chapter on the Four Kinds of <s>Karma</s> (<s>catuḥkarmavarga</s>).

body.text: 108 pañcānantaryavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 108. Chapter on the Five Heinous Crimes (<s>pañcānantaryavarga</s>)

body.text: eta
body.translated_text: It is called '<s>ānantarya</s>' (immediately-effective) because the ripening is experienced immediately after the [dissolution of the]

body.text: tkāyasamanantaraṃ vipāko vedyata ityānantaryamityucyate | yadi dṛṣṭa eva dharme vedyate tadā savyābādhavipāko laghurbhavati | tasya gurutvātkrameṇa kṣipraṃ vā avaivartike narake patati | trīṇyānantaryāṇi puṇyakṣetraguṇagauravādānantaryāṇītyucyante yaduta saṅghabhedaḥ tathāgataśarīre duṣṭacittena lohitotpādanamarhadvadhaḥ | mātṛpitṛvadha ānantaryamakṛtajñatvāt | tadānantaryaṃ manuṣyagatāveva sambhavati | nānyagatiṣu | manuṣyāṇāmeva vivekajñānavattvāt | (pṛ) anyeṣāmāryajanānāṃ vadha ānantaryaṃ labhate na vā | (u) āryajanānāṃ vadhitā prāyo narake patati | yastvarhantaṃ hanti so 'vaśyaṃ narake patet | yastathāgataṃ tāḍayati na tu lohitamutpādayati sa gurutaraṃ pāpaṃ labhate | icchayā bhagavatyāghātāt |
body.translated_text: body. If it is experienced in this very present life, then the ripening with affliction would be light. Because of its gravity, one quickly falls in sequence into the <s>Avaivartika</s> hell. Three of the heinous crimes are called '<s>ānantarya</s>' because of the gravity of the virtues of the merit-field (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>) — namely, splitting the <s>Saṅgha</s>, drawing blood from the body of a <s>Tathāgata</s> with malicious intent, and killing an <s>Arhat</s>. The killing of one's mother and father is a heinous crime because of ingratitude. These heinous crimes occur only in the human destiny — not in other destinies — because only humans possess the knowledge of discrimination. (Question) Does the killing of other Noble Ones (<s>ārya</s>) also constitute a heinous crime, or not? (Answer) The killer of Noble Ones generally falls into hell. But one who kills an <s>Arhat</s> necessarily falls into hell. One who strikes a <s>Tathāgata</s> but does not draw blood obtains extremely grave sin — because of the intentional assault upon the Blessed One.

body.text: (pṛ) yadyekamānantaryaṃ karoti | tadā narake patati | yadi dve trīṇi vā karoti | tadā ekasminneva kāye vipākavedanā kṣīyate na vā | (u) pāpānāṃ prācuryāt sa ciraṃ gurutaraduḥkhānyanubhavati | tataścyutaḥ punastatraiva jāyate | (pṛ) saṅghabhede kathaṃ gurutaraṃ bhavati [pāpam] | (u) yadyadharmamadharmato jñātvā imaṃ dharmaṃ dharmato jānāti | evaṃmanaskāro gurutaro bhavati | yadyadharmaṃ dharmamiti vadati dharmañcādharmamiti | nedaṃ pūrvavat | yat kaścit buddhātsaṅghaṃ prabhidya ātmānaṃ praśaṃsati mahān śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ pūjya iti | idamapi gurutaram | (pṛ) yaḥ prākṛtajanabhedyaḥ, nāyamāryaḥ | [tadbhedaḥ] kimiti gurutaraṃ pāpam | (u) saddharmasya vighnitatvādguru gurutaraṃ pāpam |
body.translated_text: (Question) If one commits a single heinous crime, one falls into hell. If one commits two or three — does the experience of ripened fruition [of all of them] come to an end in a single body, or not? (Answer) Because of the abundance of sins, one experiences severe suffering for a long time. Having passed away from there, one is reborn in that very same [hell] again. (Question) How does sin become graver in the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>? (Answer) When one who knows a non-<s>dharma</s> to be a non-<s>dharma</s> [then proclaims]: 'This <s>dharma</s> is truly <s>dharma</s>' — such a mental attitude becomes graver. When one calls a non-<s>dharma</s> '<s>dharma</s>' and <s>dharma</s> 'non-<s>dharma</s>' — this is not like the previous [case]. When someone, having split the <s>Saṅgha</s> away from the <s>Buddha</s>, praises himself [saying] 'I am a great Teacher, worthy of honor by gods and humans' — this too is graver. (Question) One who is split away by an ordinary person — he is not a Noble One. How is that splitting an extremely grave sin? (Answer) Because the True <s>Dharma</s> is obstructed, the sin is extremely grave.

body.text: (pṛ) saṅghadharmabhedaḥ kadā bhavati | (u) dharme 'cirapratiṣṭhite naikāmapi rātrimativāhayati sma | brahmādayo devāḥ śāliputrādimahāśrāvakāḥ punaḥ [saṅghaṃ] samīcakruḥ | kecidāhuḥ imāni pañca bhikṣuśatāni pūrvādhvani parān vighnayantaḥ kuśalamūlamārgalabdhāstatpratyayamidānīṃ tadvipākaṃ vindanta iti | prākṛtā laghucalacittatvātsubhedyāḥ | yo laukikānātmaśūnyatāmātraṃ labdhavān tasya cittamevābhedyam | kaḥ punarvādo 'nāsravaṃ [cittam] | cittagatāmidhyātvāt saṅghabhedapratyayaṃ karoti | ataḥ puṇyārthī san tyajedabhidhyām ||
body.translated_text: (Question) When does the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s> occur? (Answer) When the <s>Dharma</s> had not long been established, it did not last even a single night. <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods, and great <s>Śrāvakas</s> such as <s>Śāriputra</s> and others, again reunited [the <s>Saṅgha</s>]. Some say: 'These five hundred monks, in past lives, while obstructing others, obtained the roots of the wholesome on the path. As a result of that condition, they now experience that ripening.' Ordinary persons, being of fickle and easily swayed minds, are easily split. One who has obtained merely the worldly [realization of] emptiness of self — his mind alone is unsplittable. What more need be said of the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) mind? Because of a mental perversion, one creates the condition for the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Therefore, one who desires merit should abandon covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>).

body.text: pañcānantaryavargo 'ṣṭottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-eighth chapter, the Chapter on the Five Heinous Crimes (<s>pañcānantaryavarga</s>).

body.text: 109 pañcaśīlavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 109. Chapter on the Five Precepts (<s>pañcaśīlavarga</s>)

body.text: bhagavānāha- upāsakasya pañcaśīlānīti | (pṛ) kecidvadanti- samādānasamanvitastu śīlasaṃvaraṃ labhate iti | kathamidam | (u) samāttabahvalpatvavaśātsaṃvaraṃ labhate nāvaśyaṃ pañcamātrāṇi gṛhṇāti | (pṛ) āptiviratyādayaḥ kasmānna śīlam | kevalaṃ prāṇātipātaviratyādaya ucyante | (u) saparibāratvāt | (pṛ) kasmānnocyate kāmacāravarjanam | kāmamithyācāraviratiḥ kevalamucyate | (u) avadātavasanānāmāvasathe lokavyavahārasya sadā duṣparihāratvāt | svabhāryāgamanañca nāvaśyaṃ durgatiṣu pātayati | yathā srotaāpannādayo 'pīmaṃ dharmamācaranti | ato noktaṃ kāmacāravarjanam |
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'For a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), there are five precepts (<s>pañcaśīla</s>).' (Question) Some say: 'One who has undertaken [the precepts] with a formal vow obtains the moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>).' How is this? (Answer) According to the extent of what is undertaken, whether many or few, one obtains the restraint — one does not necessarily take all five. (Question) Why are [acts such as] non-stealing and the like not [included as] precepts? Only abstention from taking life (<s>prāṇātipātavirati</s>) and the rest are stated. (Answer) Because they are accompanied by subsidiary [precepts]. (Question) Why is the avoidance of sexual conduct in general (<s>kāmacāravarjana</s>) not stated? Only the abstention from sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāravirati</s>) is stated. (Answer) Because, for householders in white robes living in their dwellings, it is always difficult to completely avoid worldly conduct. And sexual relations with one's own wife do not necessarily cause rebirth in the lower destinies. Just as even stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) and the rest practice this <s>dharma</s>. Therefore, avoidance of sexual conduct in general is not stated.

body.text: (pṛ) paiśunyādiviratiḥ kasmānna śīlam | (u) vastvidamatisūkṣmaṃ duṣparipālam | paiśunyādirmṛṣāvādasyāṅgam | yadi mṛṣocyate tadā sāmānyataḥ [paiśunya]muktameva | (pṛ) kiṃ madyapānaṃ prakṛtisāvadyam | (u) na | kasmāt | madyapānasya sattvāvyābādhātkevalaṃ pāpahetuḥ | yo madyaṃ pibati so 'kuśaladvāramapāvṛṇoti | ato madyapānaṃ yaḥ śāsti sa pāpāṅgaṃ labhate | samādhyādikuśaladharmāṇāṃ vighnakṛttvāt | yathā taruṣaṇḍo 'vaśyaṃ bhittyāvaraṇārthaḥ | evamime catvāro dharmāḥ prakṛtisāvadyāḥ | tadviratayaḥ prakṛtipuṇyāni | tatpālanāyaitanmadya [saṃvara]śīlaṃ yojyate ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is abstention from slander (<s>paiśunya</s>) and the rest not a precept? (Answer) In reality, this matter is extremely subtle and difficult to maintain. Slander and the rest are part of false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>). If false speech is [covered], then generally slander [and the rest] are already included. (Question) Is the drinking of intoxicants (<s>madyapāna</s>) wrong by its own nature (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>)? (Answer) No. Why? Because the drinking of intoxicants does not harm beings. It is merely a cause of sin. One who drinks intoxicants opens the door to the unwholesome. Therefore, one who forbids the drinking of intoxicants eliminates a constituent of sin — because it obstructs wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) and the like. Just as a grove of trees necessarily needs the protection of a wall. Thus, these four <s>dharmas</s> are wrong by their own nature (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>). Abstaining from them constitutes merit by one's own nature (<s>prakṛtipuṇya</s>). For their protection, this precept of [abstaining from] intoxicants is conjoined.

body.text: pañcaśīlavargo navottaraśatatamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-ninth chapter, the Chapter on the Five Precepts (<s>pañcaśīlavarga</s>).

body.text: 110 ṣaṭkarmavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 110. Chapter on the Six Kinds of <s>Karma</s> (<s>ṣaṭkarmavarga</s>)

body.text: ṣaḍvidhaṃ karma- naraka[vedanīya]vipākaṃ karma, tiryagyoni[vedanīya]vipākaṃ karma, preta[vedanīya]vipākaṃ karma, manuṣya[vedanīya]vipākaṃ karma, deva[vedanīya]vipākaṃ karma, asamādhivedanīyavipākaṃ karma iti | (pṛ) kānīmāni | (u) narakavedanīyavipākaṃ karmeti
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is sixfold: <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in hell, <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in the animal realm, <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in the hungry ghost realm, <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in the human realm, <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in the divine realm, and <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced as non-concentration (<s>asamādhi</s>). (Question) What are these? (Answer) <s>Karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in hell —

body.text: yathā ṣaṭpādābhidharme lokaprajñaptau vistṛtam | prāṇātipātapāpena narakaṃ bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yaḥ prāṇātipātanirataḥ sa naraka utpadyate | yo manuṣyeṣu bhavati so 'lpāyurvindate | iti | evaṃ yāvanmithyādṛṣṭi [vaktavyam] |
body.translated_text: as is elaborated in the <s>Ṣaṭpādābhidharma</s> and the <s>Lokaprajñapti</s>. Through the sin of taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), one is [reborn in] hell. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who delights in taking life is reborn in hell. If one is [reborn] among humans, one obtains a short lifespan.' Likewise, up to wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) should be stated.

body.text: (pṛ) jānīma eva daśākuśalakarmapathairnarakavipākaṃ vindate | tiryakpretamanuṣyagatirvotpadyata iti | bhavāṃstu kevalamāha narakeṣu manuṣyeṣu votpadyata iti | idānīṃ viśiṣya vaktavyaṃ kiṃ karma narakavipākamātravedakamiti | (u) tadeva pāpakarma gurutaraṃ sat narakavipākavedakam | yadyalpaṃ laghu tadā tiryagādivipākavedakam | yaḥ sampannatrividhamithyācāraḥ tasya narakaṃ bhavati | asampannānyakarmaṇaḥ tiryagādayo bhavanti | ataśca gurutarapāpakriyāyāṃ narakaṃ bhavati | śīlabhedinā dṛṣṭibhedinā ca kṛtamakuśalaṃ karma narakāya bhavati | cittabhedacaryābhedākuśale 'dhicitto yastatkṛtamakuśalaṃ karma narakāya bhavati | yo 'kuśalaṃ karma kṛtvā akuśalasyānucaro bhavati | tasya narakaṃ bhavati | āryeṣu yo 'kuśalaṃ karma karoti | tasya narakaṃ bhavati | akuśalaṃ karma kurvato 'kuśalaṃ karmopacīyate | yathā kaścidakuśalaṃ karma kṛtvā paścātprīyā praśaṃsan na parityaktumicchati | tasya narakaṃ bhavati | yo vidveṣavyāpādacittena pāpakaṃ karoti | tasya narakaṃ bhavati | yo ghanārthaṃ [pāpaṃ] karoti | sa vipākāntaraṃ vedayate | mithyādṛṣṭicittenākuśalaṃ karma kurvato narakaṃ bhavati | śīladūṣiṇā kṛtaṃ pāpakarma narakāya bhavati | ahrīkeṇāpatrapeṇa kṛtaṃ pāpakarma narakāya bhavatti | akuśalasvabhāvena janena kṛtaṃ pāpakarma narakāya bhavati | tadyathā klinnā bhūmiralpavṛṣṭāpi kardamaṃ sādhayati | sadākuśala karmacāriṇā kṛtamakuśalaṃ karma narakāya bhavati | yaḥ sambhramakāraṇaṃ vinā [sasaṃbhrama]makuśalaṃ karma karoti | tasya narakaṃ bhavati | yo 'nātmaśūnyatāṅgamanyatrābhiniveśānna labhate | tena kṛta pāpakarma narakāya bhavati | yaḥ kāyena śīlaṃ manasā ca prajñāṃ nābhyasyati | tena kṛtamakuśalaṃ karma narakāya bhavati | prākṛtena kṛtamakuśalaṃ karma narakāya bhavati | kasmāt | na hyayaṃ prajānāti skandhadhātvāyatanadvādaśanidānādīni | ajñānādakāryaṃ kuryāt | kāryañca na kuryāt | avācyaṃ vadet | vācyañca na vadet | ananusmaraṇīyamanusmaret | anusmaraṇīyañca
body.translated_text: (Question) We know indeed that through the ten unwholesome courses of action (<s>daśākuśalakarmapatha</s>), one obtains the ripening of hell, or is reborn in the animal, hungry ghost, or human destinies. But you merely say 'one is reborn in the hells or among humans.' Now, it must be stated specifically: what <s>karma</s> produces ripening in the hells alone? (Answer) That same sinful <s>karma</s>, when it is more grave, produces ripening to be experienced in hell. If it is slight and light, then it produces ripening to be experienced as an animal and the like. One who is endowed with the complete threefold wrong conduct — for him, there is hell. For one whose other <s>karmas</s> are incomplete — for him, there are animal [rebirths] and the like. Therefore, in the doing of graver sinful actions, there is hell. Unwholesome <s>karma</s> done by one who violates moral conduct (<s>śīlabhedin</s>) and one who violates right views (<s>dṛṣṭibhedin</s>) leads to hell. One who is intent upon the unwholesome through the splitting of mind and the splitting of conduct — unwholesome <s>karma</s> done by such a one leads to hell. One who, having done unwholesome <s>karma</s>, becomes a follower of the unwholesome — for him, there is hell. One who commits unwholesome <s>karma</s> against the Noble Ones (<s>ārya</s>) — for him, there is hell. For one committing unwholesome <s>karma</s>, unwholesome <s>karma</s> accumulates. Just as someone, having done unwholesome <s>karma</s>, afterwards delights in it, praises it, and does not wish to abandon it — for him, there is hell. One who commits sin with a mind of hatred and malice (<s>vidveṣavyāpāda</s>) — for him, there is hell. One who commits sin for the sake of dense [material gain] — he experiences a different ripening. One who commits unwholesome <s>karma</s> with a mind of wrong views — for him, there is hell. Sinful <s>karma</s> done by one who corrupts moral conduct — that leads to hell. Sinful <s>karma</s> done by one who is shameless (<s>ahrīka</s>) and without moral dread (<s>anapatrapa</s>) — that leads to hell. Sinful <s>karma</s> done by a person of unwholesome nature — that leads to hell. Just as moist ground, even with little rain, produces mud. Unwholesome <s>karma</s> done by one who always practices unwholesome actions leads to hell. One who commits agitated unwholesome <s>karma</s> without cause for agitation — for him, there is hell. One who, due to attachment elsewhere, does not obtain the factor of non-self and emptiness (<s>anātmaśūnyatāṅga</s>) — sinful <s>karma</s> done by him leads to hell. One who does not practice moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) with the body nor wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) with the mind — unwholesome <s>karma</s> done by him leads to hell. Unwholesome <s>karma</s> done by an ordinary person (<s>prākṛta</s>) leads to hell. Why? Because such a person does not understand the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), the twelve links of dependent origination (<s>dvādaśanidāna</s>), and the like. Through ignorance, he would do what should not be done, and not do what should be done; he would say what should not be said, and not say what should be said; he would recollect what should not be recollected, and

body.text: nānusmaret | tena kṛtaṃ pāpamalpamapi narakāya bhavati | yo na paśyatyakuśalasyādīnavam | sa gurukaṃ pāpakarma kṛtvā narakavipākaṃ vedayate | yaḥ pāpaṃ kṛtvā na kuśalaṃ pratiśrayate | tasya narakaṃ bhavati | yathādhamarṇo na rājānaṃ śaraṇīkaroti | tadottamarṇo 'vakāśabhāgbhavati | yasya kuśalaṃ karma durbalam | tena kṛtamalpamapi pāpaṃ narakāya bhavati | yathā kasyacitkāye pācanaśaktiralpā | sa duṣparipācanamāhāraṃ bhuṅktvā na paripaktuṃ śaknoti | akuśalakarmavyāmiśramakuśalamātramācarato narakaṃ bhavati | yathā kaściccauryaṃ kṛtvā laghutaraṃ gurutaraṃ vā badhyate | yaḥ sarvakuśalamūlaviviktaḥ yathā hastinā yudhyamānaḥ [tasya] hastaṃ na parirakṣati | tatpuruṣakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ narakāya bhavati | yo hīnadharmamācaran hīnācāryācchikṣāṃ samādatte | tena kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ narakāya bhavati | yathā daridro 'dharmaṇa āhriyate | yo 'kuśalaṃ sadā vardhayati adhamarṇasyeva vṛddhim | tadyathā saunakaputravyādhādayaḥ | teṣāṃ karma narakāya bhavati | gaṇḍasyāntaḥ srāvavat pāpasya mrakṣaṇe narakaṃ bhavati | yo dīrghakālaṃ cittagatamakuśalaṃ na sahasā niyacchati | tasya narakaṃ bhavati | yathā cikitsāyai dattaṃ viṣameva puruṣaṃ hanti | yaḥ svayamakuśalaṃ kṛtvā parānapi śāsti | tena bahūnāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhopāyāsadvārasyoddhāṭanānnarakaṃ bhavati | yathā rāṣṭrapālā bahavo vijñāḥ pūrṇādivadakuśalamithyācāramācarantonyānyapi bahūn śikṣayanti | yacca kṛtaṃ karma bhūyasā sattvānāṃ byābādhāya bhavati yathā vanadāhādi | bahūnāṃ śāsanaṃ yena adharme te patanti | yathā kedāravyādhādayaḥ | yo 'kuśalakarmaṇā jīvati yathā corāmātyasūnikavyādhādayaḥ | atyantaśīladūṣiṇā kṛtaṃ pāpakarma narakāya bhavati | yadāmaraṇaṃ na tyajanti tadatyantamityucyate | yathāha gāthā-
body.translated_text: would not recollect what should be recollected. Therefore sinful <s>karma</s> done by him, even if slight, leads to hell. One who does not see the danger of the unwholesome — having done grave sinful <s>karma</s>, he experiences the ripening of hell. One who, having committed sin, does not take refuge in the wholesome — for him, there is hell. Just as a debtor who does not seek refuge with the king — the creditor obtains the opportunity [to punish]. One whose wholesome <s>karma</s> is weak — sinful <s>karma</s> done by him, even if slight, leads to hell. Just as someone whose digestive power is weak, having eaten food difficult to digest, is unable to digest it. One who practices mere unwholesome <s>karma</s> mixed with unwholesome — for him, there is hell. Just as someone who commits theft is bound [punished], whether it be lighter or more grave. One who is completely severed from wholesome roots — just as one who fights with an elephant does not protect his hand — sinful <s>karma</s> done by such a person leads to hell. One who practices inferior <s>dharmas</s> and takes up training from an inferior teacher — sin committed by him leads to hell. Just as a poor person is oppressed by injustice. One who constantly increases the unwholesome, like the interest of a debtor — such as the sons of butchers, hunters, and the like — their <s>karma</s> leads to hell. Like the festering within a boil, concealing one's sin leads to hell. One who for a long time does not immediately restrain the unwholesome that has entered the mind — for him, there is hell. Just as medicine given [too late] becomes poison that kills the person. One who, having committed unwholesome <s>karma</s> himself, also instructs others [in it] — because of opening the door of suffering and distress for many beings, for him there is hell. Just as many learned ministers, practicing unwholesome wrong conduct like <s>Pūraṇa</s> and others, also teach many others. And whatever <s>karma</s> is done that harms a great number of beings, such as setting fire to forests and the like. And one who instructs many in <s>adharma</s> so that they fall into it — such as field-hunters and the like. One who lives by unwholesome <s>karma</s> — such as thieves, corrupt ministers, slaughterers, hunters, and the like. Sinful <s>karma</s> done by one who is an extreme violator of moral conduct leads to hell. That which is not abandoned until death is called 'extreme.' As the verse says:

body.text:
yasyātyantadauḥśīlyaṃ māluḥsālamivātatā |
karoti sa tathātmānaṃ yathainaṃ icchanti dviṣaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
One whose extreme immorality spreads like a <s>mālu</s> vine upon a <s>śāla</s> tree —
he makes himself such that his enemies would wish [upon him].

body.text: avastu kupyati | anena kopena yatpāpaṃ karoti | tannarakāya bhavati | yastu savastu kupyasti | tatkṛtaṃ pāpaṃ na tādṛśaṃ bhavati | yo dveṣeṇa karma karoti | asya gurusaṃyojanatvānnarakaṃ bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dveṣaḥ pāpīyānapi sunigraha iti | yo 'kuśalacittasvabhāvaḥ tasya narakaṃ bhavati | yat hetupratyayaiḥ pāpaṃ karma karoti tadaṇīyo bhavati | yaḥ pramādāya vyutsṛṣṭaḥ tena kṛtamaśubhaṃ karma narakāya bhavati | yo vijñaiḥ paripālito bhavati sa deveṣūtpadyate | vāsavayakṣe āyuṣo 'nte mriyamāṇe śāriputraḥ tadantikamāgataḥ | so 'kuśalendriyeṇa śāliputramabhisabhīkṣya nānyathābhūt | purata āgataṃ mandamāhūya punaraucchvasat |
body.translated_text: One who becomes angry without cause — sinful <s>karma</s> done through that anger leads to hell. But one who becomes angry with cause — the sin done by him is not so [grave]. One who does <s>karma</s> through hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) — because of the gravity of that fetter, for him there is hell. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Hatred, though worse, is easy to overcome.' One whose nature is an unwholesome mind — for him, there is hell. <s>Karma</s> that is sinful done through causes and conditions is punishable. One who has been abandoned to heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) — unwholesome <s>karma</s> done by him leads to hell. One who is cared for by the wise is born among the gods. When the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Vāsava</s> was dying at the end of his life, <s>Śāriputra</s> came to his side. He, with unwholesome faculties, having gazed at <s>Śāriputra</s>, was not otherwise [transformed]. Calling forth a dullard who came before him, he revived again.

body.text: śāriputraprabhāsvaramāhātmyamavalokyācintayat ayaṃ mahātmā na hantavya iti viśuddhacittena saptakṛtvaḥ śāriputramūrdhvamadho vyavālokayat | anenaiva hetunā saptakṛtvo deveṣūdapadyata | saptakṛtvo manuṣyeṣu codapadyata | atha pratyekabuddhamārgamalabhata | yathā cāṅgulimālaḥ pāpakaṃ karma bahukṛtvā mātara[mapi]hantumaicchat | bhagavān tatkuśalābhijñatvāt tasya vimuktiṃ prāpayati sma | yathā ca kaściddānapati ragnighādaviṣānnabhojanairmadhye [gṛhaṃ] hantumaicchat | bhagavān tatkuśalābhijñatvāt tasya vimuktiṃ prāpayat | evamādayaḥ puruṣāḥ akuśalakarmakā api na narake patanti | ata uktaṃ yaḥ pramādāya vyusṛṣṭaḥ tena kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ karma narakāya bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: Having beheld the radiant majesty of <s>Śāriputra</s>, he thought: 'This great being should not be harmed.' With a purified mind, seven times he looked up and down at <s>Śāriputra</s>. By this very cause, he was reborn seven times among the gods and seven times among humans. Then he attained the path of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Just as <s>Aṅgulimāla</s>, having done much sinful <s>karma</s>, even wished to kill his own mother — the Blessed One, knowing his wholesome potential, caused him to attain liberation. And just as a certain householder wished to kill [people] in his own house through fire, poison, and poisoned food — the Blessed One, knowing his wholesome potential, caused him to attain liberation. Such persons, even though of unwholesome <s>karma</s>, do not fall into hell. Therefore it is said: 'One who has been abandoned to heedlessness — sinful <s>karma</s> done by him leads to hell.'

body.text: yaḥ samucchinnakuśalamūlo devadattādivatpunaracikitsyo bhavati | tadyathā kaścidrogī dṛṣṭamaraṇanimittaḥ | tena kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ narakāya bhavati | yaḥ kuśalaṃ kartumagaṇayan mriyamāṇo durutpādakuśalacitto bhavati | sa cittaparitāpānnarake patati | yo mriyamāṇo mithyādṛṣṭi cittamutpādayati | sa pūrvākuśalahetukaṃ mithyādṛṣṭi pratyayañca narake patati | evaṃ bahūni karmāṇi narakavipākāya bhavanti | ābhidharmikā vadanti- sarvāṇyakuśalāni narakanidānānīti | ebhyo 'kuśalebhyo 'nyaistiryagādiṣūtpadyante | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantryāvocat- yān sattvān paśyatha kāyikamithyācārān vācikamithyācārān mānasikamithyācārān tān jānīta narakaprekṣakāniti |
body.translated_text: One whose wholesome roots are completely cut off, like <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, becomes incurable. Just as a certain sick person who has the sign of death [appearing] — sinful <s>karma</s> done by him leads to hell. One who, disregarding the doing of the wholesome and dying, has a mind in which it is difficult to produce wholesome [thoughts] — he falls into hell because of mental anguish. One who, while dying, generates a mind of wrong view — he falls into hell because of the cause of prior unwholesome [karma] and the condition of wrong view. Thus there are many <s>karmas</s> that lead to the ripening of hell. The <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: 'All unwholesome [karmas] are causes for hell.' By other unwholesome [karmas] apart from these, one is reborn among animals and the like.
