As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: The Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Those beings whom you see practicing bodily wrong conduct, verbal wrong conduct, and mental wrong conduct — know them to be destined for hell.'

body.text: (pṛ) narakavipākaṃ karmādhigatam | kiṃ punastiryagvipākaṃ karma | (u) yaḥ kuśalavyāmiśramakuśalaṃ karma karoti | sa tataḥ tiryakṣu patati | anuśayasaṃyojanautkaṭyācca tiryakṣu patati | yathā kāmarāgautkaṭyāccaṭakapārāvatacakravākādiṣūtpadyate | dveṣautkaṭayātsarpavṛścikādiṣūtpadyate | mohautkaṭyāt varāhādiṣūtpadyate | madautkaṭyāt siṃhavyāghraśvāpadādiṣūtpadyate | auddhatyacāñcalyautkaṭyānmarkaṭādiṣūtpadyate | īrṣyāmātsaryautkaṭyāt śvādiṣūtpadyate | evamādīnāmanyeṣāmapi kleśānāmautkaṭyānnānātiryakṣūtpadyate | yaḥ kaściddānabhāgī bhavati | sa tiryakṣūtpanno 'pi sukhamanubhavati | suvarṇapakṣagaruḍahastyaśvādayaḥ | vācikakarmaṇo vipāko bhūyasā tiryakṣu patanam | yathā kaścitkarmavipākamajñātvā śraddhayā ca nānāvākkarma tathā karoti yathā vadanti ayaṃ puruṣo markaṭavadaticapala iti | sa markaṭeṣūtpadyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>karma</s> leading to the ripening of hell has been stated. What then is the <s>karma</s> leading to the ripening of an animal rebirth? (Answer) One who performs unwholesome <s>karma</s> mixed with wholesome — he thereby falls among animals. And through the intensity of latent defilements and fetters (<s>anuśayasaṃyojana</s>), one falls among animals. Just as through the intensity of sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>), one is reborn among sparrows, pigeons, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, and the like. Through the intensity of hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), one is reborn among serpents, scorpions, and the like. Through the intensity of delusion (<s>moha</s>), one is reborn among boars and the like. Through the intensity of pride (<s>mada</s>), one is reborn among lions, tigers, wild beasts, and the like. Through the intensity of restlessness and agitation (<s>auddhatyacāñcalya</s>), one is reborn among monkeys and the like. Through the intensity of jealousy and avarice (<s>īrṣyāmātsarya</s>), one is reborn among dogs and the like. Likewise, through the intensity of various other defilements, one is reborn among various animals. One who has a share of giving (<s>dāna</s>), even when born among animals, experiences happiness — such as golden-winged <s>Garuḍas</s>, elephants, horses, and the like. The ripening of verbal <s>karma</s> is for the most part a fall among animals. Just as someone, not understanding the ripening of <s>karma</s> and through faith, performs various verbal <s>karma</s> as they say: 'This person is as fickle as a monkey.' He is reborn among monkeys.

body.text: yadvadanti vāyasavadāhāralolupaḥ | śvabukkavadbhāṣate | ajavarāhavaddhāvati | gardabhavacchabdāyate | uṣṭravat yāti | hastivadātmānamunnamayati | mattabalīvardavadaśubhayati | caṭakavadyabhati | viḍālavatsārajyati | śṛgālavadvañcayati | kṛṣṇorabhravajjaḍo bhavati | govat droṇabahulo bhavati | evamādyakuśalaṃ vācikaṃ karma kṛtvā yathākarma vipākaṃ vedayate | sattvāḥ sukhalobhānnānāpraṇidhānyutpādayati | tadyathā kāmasukharāge sati pakṣiṣūtpadyate | yo nāgagaruḍādīnāṃ śaktibalaṃ śrutvā praṇidadhāti sa tatrotpadyate | uktañca sūtre- yo nibiḍasthāne mriyamāṇaḥ praṇidadhāti vipulaṃ sthānaṃ labha iti | sa pakṣiṣūtpadyate | yaḥ paritarṣito mriyate sa jalārthitayā jaleṣūtpadyate | kṣudhito mriyamāṇo 'nnarāgārdvacaḥ kuṭyāmutpadyate |
body.translated_text: As they say: 'He is as greedy for food as a crow.' 'He speaks like a dog-barker.' 'He runs like a goat or pig.' 'He makes noise like a donkey.' 'He walks like a camel.' 'He raises himself up like an elephant.' 'He disgraces like a mad bull.' 'He mates like a sparrow.' 'He creeps like a cat.' 'He deceives like a jackal.' 'He is as dull as a black ram.' 'He is as herd-minded as a cow.' Having done such unwholesome verbal <s>karma</s>, one experiences ripening according to the <s>karma</s>. Beings, through greed for pleasure, generate various aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). When there is attachment to sensual pleasure, one is reborn among birds. One who, having heard of the power and strength of <s>nāgas</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, and the like, aspires [to be like them] — he is reborn there. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One dying in a confined place aspires: "May I obtain a spacious place." He is reborn among birds.' One who dies parched [with thirst] — through craving for water, he is reborn in waters. One dying hungry — through craving for food, he is reborn among worms in a privy.

body.text: vyomāhāt laghu karmāṇi kurvan vyāmiśrakuśalatvāt makṣikālīkṣākṛmikīṭādiṣūtpadyate | yaḥ parānupadiśan asaddharme pātayati so 'vidvatpada utpadyate | andho jāyate | mṛtvā ca śave kṛmirbhavati | vyāmiśrakarmācaraṇācca tiryakṣūtpadyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- tiryañco nānācittavaśānnānākārānanuprāpnuvanti iti | yastṛṇamadyām iti karma karoti | yathā kaścinmithyā vadati ahaṃ mantrānadhyemīti | yo vā idamannamattvā tṛṇamadbhīti prakaṭayati | atha vā vadati mṛdaṃ bhakṣayāmītyeyamādi | yaśca kaścidvākpārūṣyeṇādhikṣipati | kiṃ tṛṇamanattvā mṛdaṃ bhakṣayasīti | so 'bhilāpavaśāttṛṇamṛdādibhakṣakeṣūpapattiṃ vedayate | aviśuddhadānāmācāran tṛṇādibhakṣakeṣu vipākaṃ vedayate | ya ṛṇamādāya na pratyarpayati | sa gavājakṛṣṇamṛgāśvagardabhādiṣu patitvā ṛṇarātrīryāpayati | evamādikarmaṇā tiryakṣu patati |
body.translated_text: One who makes light promises and performs light <s>karmas</s> — because of mixed wholesomeness, he is reborn among flies, lice, worms, insects, and the like. One who teaches others and causes them to fall into the wrong <s>dharma</s> — he is reborn in a state of ignorance, born blind, and after death becomes a worm in a corpse. And through the practice of mixed <s>karma</s>, one is reborn among animals. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Animals, due to their various mental dispositions, attain various forms.' One who performs the <s>karma</s> of 'I shall eat grass' — just as someone falsely says 'I study the <s>mantras</s>,' or one who proclaims 'Having eaten this food, I shall eat grass,' or else says 'I eat earth' — these and the like. And whoever reviles with harsh speech: 'Why do you not eat grass but eat earth?' — through the power of such utterances, he experiences rebirth among grass-eaters, earth-eaters, and the like. One who practices impure giving also experiences ripening among grass-eaters and the like. One who takes a debt and does not repay it — having fallen among cows, donkeys, black deer, horses, mules, and the like, he passes his nights [of debt]. Through such <s>karmas</s>, one falls among animals.

body.text: (pṛ) tiryadvipākaṃ karma parijñātam | kena karmaṇā preteṣu patati | (u) annapānādiṣu sañjātamatsaralobhacittaḥ san preteṣu patati | (pṛ) yadi kaścitsvadravyaṃ na dadāti | kasmātsa pāpabhāgbhavati | (u) ayaṃ kadaryo yadi kaścidyācanāṃ karoti | sāpekṣatvāttasmai kupyati | anenāvadyena preteṣūtpadyate | sa kṛpaṇaḥ yācanāṃ kurvati kasmiṃścit nāstīti vadan anṛtavāditvātpreteṣu patati | sa cirātkadaryasaṃyojanāmabhyasyati | parasya hitalābhaṃ dṛṣṭvā īrṣyāsūyācittamutpādayati | ataḥ preteṣu patati | kadaryo 'yaṃ dānacāriṇaṃ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ dānapatiṃ dvipyati | yācako 'yaṃ lābhābhyāsānmatto 'vaśyaṃ yāceteti | cirādārabhya kadaryacittavāsanayā na svayaṃ dadāti paramapi niṣedhati | yatkiñcidasti vihāre saṅghadravyaṃ yajñe ca brāhmaṇadravyam |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>karma</s> with animal ripening has been understood. By what <s>karma</s> does one fall among the hungry ghosts (<s>preta</s>)? (Answer) One who has generated a mind of avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>) and greed (<s>lobha</s>) regarding food, drink, and the like falls among the hungry ghosts. (Question) If someone does not give his own property, why does he become a partaker of sin? (Answer) This miser, if someone makes a request, becomes angry toward him because of his clinging — by this fault, he is reborn among the hungry ghosts. The wretched one, when someone makes a request, says 'There is nothing' — by being a speaker of falsehood, he falls among the hungry ghosts. He habitually cultivates for a long time the fetter of miserliness. Seeing another obtain what is beneficial, he generates a mind of jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and malice (<s>asūyā</s>). Therefore he falls among the hungry ghosts. This miser, seeing another who practices generosity, despises that patron of gifts [thinking]: 'This beggar, intoxicated by habitual gain, will certainly keep begging.' Having long cultivated the habitual tendency (<s>vāsanā</s>) of a miserly mind, he neither gives himself nor prevents others [from giving]. Whatever monastic property of the <s>Saṅgha</s> exists in a monastery, or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> property at a sacrifice —

body.text: tat kaścit svayaṃ kevalamabhilaṣati na parasya dātumicchati | ataḥ preteṣu patati | yaḥ parasyānnapānamapaharati nāśayati vā | sa niraśanasthāna utpadyate | yo dānapuṇyavigataḥ sa tadupapattyāyatane vipākālābhī tato yācakādhikṣepakarmaṇo duḥkhaṃ tatraivānubhavati | ayaṃ kṛpaṇaḥ kṣuttṛṣṇārditaṃ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nirdayacitto bhavati | ato yatrotpadyate tatra sadā kṣuttṛṣṇāmanubhavati | yathā dayayā deveṣūtpadyate | tathā dveṣopanāhābhyāṃ durgatāvutpadyate | bandhuparivārapriyajaneṣu supratiṣṭhite deśe ca paramāsaktatvātkaliṅgādipreteṣūtpadyate, rāgatṛṣṇāpratyayatvāt | evamādi yathā vistṛtaṃ karmavipākasūtre |
body.translated_text: that, someone desires solely for himself and does not wish to give to others. Therefore he falls among the hungry ghosts. One who steals or destroys another's food and drink is reborn in a place without food. One who is devoid of the merit of giving, being one who does not obtain ripening in that place of rebirth — from the <s>karma</s> of disparaging beggars, he experiences suffering right there. This wretched one, seeing another afflicted by hunger and thirst, has a merciless mind. Therefore, wherever he is reborn, he constantly experiences hunger and thirst. Just as through compassion one is reborn among the gods, so through hatred and resentment one is reborn in a lower destiny. One who is supremely attached to relatives, retinue, beloved ones, and to a well-established region is reborn among the <s>Kaliṅga</s> and other hungry ghosts, because of the condition of passion and craving. Such and more is detailed in the <s>Karmavipāka Sūtra</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) parijñātāni trīṇi durgativipākāni | kena karmaṇā deveṣūtpadyate | (u) yo dānasaṃvarakuśalādikarmābhyasyati | sa uttamaḥ san deveṣūtpadyate | adhamaḥ san manuṣyeṣūtpadyate | yaśca tīkṣṇendriyaḥ sa manuṣyeṣūtpadyate | manuṣyadharmamācaratīti manuṣyaḥ | vyāmiśrakuśalakarmaṇā ca manuṣyeṣūtpadyate | tatkarma [trividha]muttamaṃ madhyamamadhamamiti | ekāgratānaikāgratā viśuddhamaviśuddhamityādi | kenedaṃ jñāyate | manuṣyāṇāṃ nānāvibhāgaśreṇīnāṃ vaiṣamyāt | yathoktaṃ sūtre- prāṇātipātyalpāyuṣko bhavati | caurye daridraḥ | kāmamithyācāre hīnāsatkulaḥ | mṛṣāvāde sadā paribhāṣyate | paiśunye kulapāṃsulaḥ | pāruṣye sadā paruṣaśabdaṃ śṛṇoti | saṃmbhinnapralāpe janānāmaśraddheyaḥ | rāgerṣyāyāṃ kāmacārabahulaḥ | krodhe duḥkhabhāvabhūyiṣṭhaḥ | mithyādṛṣṭau mohabahulaḥ | māne 'varajanmā | ātmana unmāne kharvaḥ | īrṣyāyāmate[ja]svī | mātsarye dāridryapīḍitaḥ | dveṣe virūpī bhavati | parapīḍāyāṃ vyādhibahulaḥ | vyāmiśracittena dāne 'madhurarasābhilāṣī | akāladāne na yatheṣṭabhāk | paścāttāpavimatau paryantabhūmau jāyate | aviśuddhadānacaryāyāṃ duḥkhato vipākalābhī bhavati | amārgeṇa kāmacaryāyāmapuruṣākāraṃ labhate | manuṣyeṣu evamādīni saṅkīrṇānyakuśalakarmāṇi | tadviparītāni tu kuśalakarmāṇi | yathā prāṇātipātaviratirdīrghāyuṣyaprāpiṇītyādi | manuṣyagatāvevamādi nānāvaiṣamyamastītyato jñāyate vyāmiśrakarmavipāko 'yamiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) The three ripenings [leading to rebirth] in the lower destinies have been understood. By what <s>karma</s> is one reborn among the gods? (Answer) One who habitually practices the wholesome <s>karmas</s> of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), and the like — being superior, is reborn among the gods; being inferior, is reborn among humans. And one who has sharp faculties is reborn among humans. One who practices the human <s>dharma</s> is called a human (<s>manuṣya</s>). And through mixed wholesome <s>karma</s>, one is reborn among humans. That <s>karma</s> is of three kinds: superior, middling, and inferior. One-pointed [concentration] and non-one-pointed, pure and impure, and so forth. How is this known? Because of the inequality among the various categories and ranks of human beings. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who kills living beings has a short lifespan. Through theft, one is poor. Through sexual misconduct, one is born in a low and impure family. Through false speech, one is always disparaged. Through slander, one is the disgrace of the family. Through harsh speech, one always hears harsh words. Through idle chatter, one is not believed by people. Through passionate jealousy, one is predominantly given to sensual indulgence. Through anger, one is predominantly of a nature of suffering. Through wrong view, one is predominantly deluded. Through pride, one has a low birth. Through self-exaltation, one is dwarfish. Through jealousy, one is devoid of brilliance. Through avarice, one is afflicted by poverty. Through hatred, one is ugly. Through harming others, one is predominantly afflicted by disease. Through giving with a mixed mind, one does not relish sweet tastes. Through giving at an improper time, one does not enjoy as desired. Through hesitant and doubtful [giving], one is born in a borderland. Through impure practice of giving, one obtains ripening with suffering. Through sexual conduct by a wrong path, one obtains a non-masculine form.' Among humans, such and other mixed unwholesome <s>karmas</s> [exist]. The opposite of those are wholesome <s>karmas</s> — just as abstention from killing leads to long life, and so forth. Among human rebirths, such various inequalities exist — therefore it is known that this is the ripening of mixed <s>karma</s>.

body.text: praṇidhānena hi manuṣyeṣu jāyate | kecidapramādaratā api na kāmabahulā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: Through aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), one is reborn among humans. Some who delight in non-heedlessness are not predominantly given to sensual pleasures.

body.text: ye prajñāsvadhimuktikā manuṣyadehapraṇidhānaṃ kurvanti | te manuṣyeṣūtpadyante | yaḥ pitroḥ pūjyānāñca satkāre svabhiruciko bhavati | brāhmaṇaśramaṇādīnāmapi satkāravit tatkarmakriyātuṣṭaśca puṇyaṃ samyagabhyasyati | so 'pi manuṣyeṣūtpadyate | manuṣyeṣu ca yo viśuddhakarmapratyayaḥ sa uttara[kuruṣū]tpadyate | yaśca kṣetragṛhakuṭīṣvātmīyaviśeṣeṣu dviṣyati | sa uttarāsūtpadyate | yaḥ śuklakarma samyagācaran parānapīḍayitvā dhanamādatte dānāya nābhiṣvaṅgāya | svayañca śīlamācaran na pūrvāparaparivāreṣu śīlaṃ bhedayati | sa uttarakuruṣūtpadyate | tataḥ kiñcidūnakuśalo godānīya utpadyate | tato 'pi kiñcidūnaśca ayathāvat (?) pūrvavideha utpadyate |
body.translated_text: Those who are inclined toward wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) make the aspiration for a human body. They are reborn among humans. One who delights in honoring parents and those worthy of respect, who also knows how to honor <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, ascetics, and the like, who is content with the performance of those <s>karmas</s> and properly practices merit — he too is reborn among humans. And among humans, one whose <s>karma</s>-condition is pure is reborn in <s>Uttarakuru</s>. And one who despises [attachment to] fields, houses, and dwellings as one's own special [possessions] is reborn in the northern [continent]. One who properly practices pure <s>karma</s>, who takes wealth without harming others, for the purpose of giving and not for the purpose of attachment, who himself practices moral conduct and does not cause the breach of moral conduct among those in his retinue, before or after — he is reborn in <s>Uttarakuru</s>. One somewhat inferior in wholesome [karma] to that is reborn in <s>Godānīya</s>. One still somewhat inferior to that, and not fully [accomplished], is reborn in <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.

body.text: devavipākaṃ karmeti | atiśuddhadānaśīlatvāt deveṣūtpadyate | yaḥ prajñāṅgaṃ labdhvā saṃyojanāni samucchedayati | sa deveṣūtpadyate | vyāmiśrakarmavaśācca viśiṣyate | manuṣyeṣūktavat praṇidhānahetunā ca viśrutadeveṣu sukhavedanāpratyayaṃ kṛtakuśalakarmakāḥ sarve tatra janmagatiṃ praṇidadhati | yathoktaṃ- aṣṭapuṇyasargasthāne yaḥ karuṇāmuditopekṣāsu viharati sa utpadyate brahmaloke yāvadbhavāgram | atra dhyānasamāpatterviśiṣṭarūpatvāt vipāko 'pi viśiṣyate | yasya styānamiddhauddhatyādīni na samyak prahīṇāni | so 'nābhāsvaradehaprabho bhavati | yasya samyak prahīṇāni sa viśuddhataraprabho bhavati | atyuttamakuśalakarmavipāko deveṣūtpadyate | amīpsitānāṃ yathāmanaskārameva pratilābhāt | yo viviktarūpairarūpyasamādhimupasampadya viharati | sa ārūpyasthāna utpadyate | evamādi devavipākaṃ karmākhyāyate |
body.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> with divine ripening: Through extremely pure generosity and moral conduct, one is reborn among the gods. One who, having obtained the component of wisdom (<s>prajñāṅga</s>), eradicates the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) — he is reborn among the gods. And through the power of mixed <s>karma</s>, there is differentiation. As stated regarding humans, through the cause of aspiration, those who have performed wholesome <s>karma</s> that is a condition for pleasant feeling among the renowned gods — all of them make the aspiration for rebirth there. As stated: 'One who dwells in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) — compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity — at the eight places where merit is generated, is reborn in the <s>Brahmaloka</s> up to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>).' Here, because of the superiority of the form of <s>dhyāna</s> and attainment, the ripening too is differentiated. One whose torpor (<s>styāna</s>), drowsiness (<s>middha</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), and the like are not properly abandoned — he does not have the radiance of an <s>Ābhāsvara</s> body. One whose [hindrances] are properly abandoned has a purer radiance. The ripening of supremely excellent wholesome <s>karma</s> [leads to] rebirth among the gods — because of obtaining what is desired exactly according to one's mental intention. One who, having entered the distinguished formless (<s>ārūpya</s>) concentration in the form of detachment, abides — he is reborn in the formless realm. Such and more is what is called '<s>karma</s> with divine ripening.'

body.text: aniyatavipākaṃ karmeti | yadavaraṃ kuśalamakuśalaṃ karma | idaṃ karma narakeṣu preteṣu tiryakṣu deveṣu manuṣyeṣu vā vedyate | (pṛ) anyāsu catasṛṣu gatiṣu kuśalakarmavipāko vedayituṃ śakyate | narake katham | (u) kaścinnarakānmuhūrtaṃ nivartate | yathā [kaści]darcirnarakādvimukto dūrato vanaṣaṇḍaṃ dṛṣṭvā muditacitta āśu tasmin vane praviśati | śītavātakampite tasmin vane [yāvat] asitomarāṇi na patanti | tasmin samaye muhūrtaṃ sukhī bhavati | athavā kṣāranadīṃ dṛṣṭvā idaṃ prasannasalilamiti drutagati pradhāvya muhūrtaṃ sukhabhāgbhavati | evaṃ narake 'pi kuśalakarmaṇo vipākabhāgo 'sti | idamaniyataṃ karmetyucyate ||
body.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> with indeterminate ripening: Whatever inferior wholesome or unwholesome <s>karma</s> — this <s>karma</s> is experienced in hells, among hungry ghosts, among animals, among gods, or among humans. (Question) In the other four destinies, the ripening of wholesome <s>karma</s> can be experienced. But how [is it experienced] in hell? (Answer) Someone returns from hell for a moment. Just as someone freed from the blazing fire hell, seeing a forest-grove from a distance, with a joyful mind quickly enters that forest. In that forest shaken by cold wind, as long as sword-leaf [trees] do not fall, at that time he is happy for a moment. Or, seeing a caustic river, [thinking] 'This is clear water,' running quickly, he is happy for a moment. Thus even in hell, there is a share of the ripening of wholesome <s>karma</s>. This is called 'indeterminate <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: ṣaṭkarmavargo daśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and tenth chapter, the Chapter on the Six Kinds of Karma (<s>ṣaṭkarmavarga</s>).

body.text: 111 saptākuśalasaṃvaravargaḥ
body.translated_text: 111. Chapter on the Seven Unwholesome Restraints (<s>saptākuśalasaṃvaravarga</s>)

body.text: saptākuśalasaṃvarāḥ yaduta hiṃsāsteyakāmamithyācārapaiśunyapāruṣyamṛṣāvādasambhinnapralāpāḥ | ya eṣāṃ saptānāṃ vastunāṃ samagro vā asamagro bhavati | so 'kuśalasaṃvara ityucyate | (pṛ) ko 'kuśalasaṃvarasamanvāgataḥ | (u) hiṃsākuśalasamanvāgato yaduta saunikavyādhādayaḥ | steyasamanvāgato yaduta corādayaḥ | kāmamithyācārasamanvāgato yadutāmārgamaithunacāriṇo gaṇikādayaḥ | mṛṣāvādāmanvāgatā gāyakanaṭaputrādayaḥ | paiśunyasamanvāgato dūṣaṇaparivādānandī rāṣṭravṛttyādisandhilipidūṣaṇādhyetā ca | pāruṣyasamanvitā narakapālādayaḥ pāruṣyopajīvyādayaśca | sambhinnapralāpasamanvitāḥ śabdasandarbhayogena janahāsyakarādayaḥ | kecidāhuḥ- rājānaḥ pratipakṣiṇo rājñaḥ śāsanāvasare etadakuśalasaṃvarasamanvitā iti | tadayuktam | yaḥ pāpasantatiṃ kṛtvā na viramati | sa khalu etadakuśalasaṃvarasamanvita ityucyate | na tathā rājādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The seven unwholesome restraints (<s>akuśalasaṃvara</s>) are: killing (<s>hiṃsā</s>), theft (<s>steya</s>), sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>), slander (<s>paiśunya</s>), harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), and idle chatter (<s>sambhinnapralāpa</s>). One who possesses all or some of these seven things is called one endowed with unwholesome restraint. (Question) Who is endowed with unwholesome restraint? (Answer) One endowed with killing — such as butchers, hunters, and the like. One endowed with theft — such as robbers and the like. One endowed with sexual misconduct — such as those who practice intercourse by a wrong path, courtesans, and the like. Those endowed with false speech — such as singers, actors, and the like. One endowed with slander — such as one who delights in defamation and abuse, and one who studies [the art of] forging state documents and the like. Those endowed with harsh speech — such as hell-wardens and the like, and those who live by harshness. Those endowed with idle chatter — such as those who make people laugh through the art of arranging words. Some say: 'Kings who, at the command of a rival king, are endowed with this unwholesome restraint.' That is not valid. Only one who, having made a continuity of sin, does not desist — he alone is said to be endowed with this unwholesome restraint. Kings and the like are not like that.

body.text: (pṛ) ayamakuśalasaṃvara iti kathaṃ labhyate | (u) yasmin kāle pāpakarmācarati | tadā labhyate | (pṛ) kiṃ vadhitasattvāt saṃvaramimaṃ labhate kiṃ vā sarvasattvebhyaḥ | (u) sarvasattvebhyaḥ | yathā kaścit śīladhārī sarvasattvebhyaḥ śīlasaṃvaraṃ labhate | tathā akuśalasaṃvaramapi | prāṇātipātānuvartinaḥ vadhapāpasaṅgṛhītākuśalasaṃvarasaṅgṛhītarūpadvividhāvijñaptilābhe anyasattvebhyo 'kuśalasaṃvarasaṅgṛhītāpi labhyate | (pṛ) ayamakuśalasaṃvaraḥ kiyatkālaṃ samanvito bhavati | (u) yāvadupekṣācittaṃ na pratilabhyate | tāvatsadā samanvito bhavati | (pṛ) yo 'varamṛducittādakuśalasaṃvaraṃ pratilabhate | yo vā lobhādicitāt pratilabhate | sa sadā etatsamanvito bhavati | punaḥ kiṃ pratilabhate | (u) yathācittaṃ yathākleśapratyayañca punaretadakuśalasaṃvaraṃ pratilabhate | pratikṣaṇaṃ sadā pratilabhate | sarvasattveṣūtpannaḥ saptavidho bhavati | saptavidho 'yamuttamamadhyādhama iti ekaviṃśatidhā bhavati | evaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvasattvabhūmiṣu pratilabhate |
body.translated_text: (Question) How is this unwholesome restraint obtained? (Answer) At the time when one performs sinful <s>karma</s>, at that time it is obtained. (Question) Does one obtain this restraint from the being that was killed, or from all beings? (Answer) From all beings. Just as one who upholds moral conduct obtains the wholesome restraint of moral conduct from all beings, so too with the unwholesome restraint. For one who follows the course of taking life, upon obtaining the twofold <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest form) comprised in the unwholesome restraint of killing-sin, from other beings too the [unwholesome restraint] comprised in the unwholesome restraint is obtained. (Question) For how long is one endowed with this unwholesome restraint? (Answer) As long as one does not obtain a mind of equanimity, one is always endowed with it. (Question) Does one who obtains unwholesome restraint from an inferior, mild mind, or one who obtains it from a mind of greed and the like — is he always endowed with it? And does he obtain it again? (Answer) According to the mind and according to the defilement-condition, one obtains this unwholesome restraint again. One obtains it at every moment, constantly. [The restraint] arisen toward all beings is sevenfold. This sevenfold [restraint], being superior, middling, and inferior, becomes twenty-one-fold. Thus, at every moment, it is obtained on all planes of all beings.

body.text: (pṛ) akuśalasaṃvaramimaṃ kadā tyajati | (u) kuśalasaṃvarasamādānakāle tyajati | maraṇakāle 'pi tyajati | adyaprabhṛti na punaḥ karomīti yadādhyāśayamutpādayati | tasmin kāle 'pi tyajati | abhidharmikā āhuḥ- indriyaparāvṛtto tyajatīti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | aśaktā api samanvāgamaṃ labhante | vinaye 'pyuktam | yo bhikṣuḥ parāvṛttendriyaḥ na sa vinaṣṭasaṃvaro bhavati iti | ato jñāyate nendriyaparāvṛttyā tyajatīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) When does one abandon this unwholesome restraint? (Answer) At the time of undertaking the wholesome restraint, one abandons it. At the time of death too, one abandons it. When one generates the intention 'From this day forth I shall not do it again' — at that time too, one abandons it. The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say: 'One who has undergone a transformation of faculties abandons it.' That is not valid. Why? Because even those who are incapable still possess [the restraint]. And it is stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>: 'A monk whose faculties have been transformed — he has not lost his restraint.' Therefore it is known that one does not abandon it through the transformation of faculties.

body.text: (pṛ) pañcasu gatiṣu kasyāṃ gatau sattvā akuśalasaṃvarasamanvitā bhavanti | (u) manuṣyā eva samanvitā nānyagatisthāḥ | kecidāhuḥ- [tathā nocet] siṃhavyāghrādayaḥ sadā duṣkarmaṇopajīvino 'pi samanvitāḥ syuriti ||
body.translated_text: (Question) In which of the five destinies are beings endowed with the unwholesome restraint? (Answer) Only humans are endowed with it, not those in other destinies. Some say: 'If it were not so, then lions, tigers, and the like, who always live by evil deeds, would also be endowed [with it].'

body.text: saptākuśalasaṃvaravarga ekādaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and eleventh chapter, the Chapter on the Seven Unwholesome Restraints (<s>saptākuśalasaṃvaravarga</s>).

body.text: 112 saptakuśalasaṃvaravargaḥ
body.translated_text: 112. Chapter on the Seven Wholesome Restraints (<s>saptakuśalasaṃvaravarga</s>)

body.text: sapta kuśalasaṃvarāḥ prāṇātipātaviratiryāvatsambhinnapralāpaviratiḥ | (pṛ) asattvākhyebhya imaṃ kuśalasaṃvaraṃ labhate na vā | (u) labhate | kevalaṃ sattvamupādāya bhavati | kuśalasaṃvaro 'yaṃ trividhaḥ- śīlasaṃvaro dhyānasaṃvaraḥ samādhisaṃvara iti | (pṛ) kasmānnocyate 'nāsrasaṃvaraḥ | (u) anāsravasaṃvaro 'ntyadvaye saṅgṛhīta ityataḥ pṛthaṅ nocyate | ābhidharmikā āhuḥ- asti punaḥ prahāṇasaṃvaro yaduta kāmadhātuvīta[rāgaḥ] tasmin kāle kuśalasaṃvaraṃ labhate | śīlabhedādyakuśalaṃ prajahātīti prahāṇam iti | vastutastu sarve saṃvarāstiṣu saṅgṛhītāḥ |
body.translated_text: The seven wholesome restraints (<s>kuśalasaṃvara</s>) are: abstention from taking life up to abstention from idle chatter. (Question) Does one obtain this wholesome restraint from non-sentient beings or not? (Answer) One obtains it. However, it exists only with reference to sentient beings. This wholesome restraint is of three kinds: the restraint of moral conduct (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>), the restraint of <s>dhyāna</s> (<s>dhyānasaṃvara</s>), and the restraint of concentration (<s>samādhisaṃvara</s>). (Question) Why is the outflow-free restraint (<s>anāsravasaṃvara</s>) not mentioned? (Answer) Because the outflow-free restraint is included in the latter two, it is not mentioned separately. The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say: 'There is also a restraint of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasaṃvara</s>) — namely, one who is free from passion for the desire realm. At that time, one obtains the wholesome restraint. Through the breaking of moral conduct and such, one abandons the unwholesome — this is called "abandonment."' But in reality, all restraints are included in the [above] three.

body.text: (pṛ) tīrthikā imaṃ śīlasaṃvaraṃ labhante na vā | (u) labhante | teṣāmapi akuśalacittebhyo viratāvadhicittatvāt | ācāryaḥ śīlamupadiśati adyaprabhṛti prāṇātipātādipāpaṃ mā kuryā iti | (pṛ) anyāsu gatiṣu imaṃ śīlasavaraṃ labhante na vā | (u) uktaṃ hi sūtre- nāgādayo 'pi dinamekaṃ śīlamupādadate | iti | ato jñāyate bhavediti | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- aśaktādināṃ na śīlasaṃvaro 'stīti | kathamidam | (u) ayaṃ śīlasaṃvaraścittabhūmijaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) Do the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) obtain this moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>) or not? (Answer) They do obtain it. Because even for them, there exists a mind of determination to abstain from unwholesome minds. The teacher instructs in moral conduct: 'From today onward, do not commit sins such as killing and the rest.' (Question) Do those in other destinies (<s>gati</s>) obtain this moral restraint or not? (Answer) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Even <s>nāgas</s> and the like undertake moral conduct for a single day.' Therefore it is known that it is possible. (Question) Certain people say: 'Those who are impotent (<s>aśakta</s>) and the like do not have moral restraint.' How is this? (Answer) This moral restraint is born of the mental ground (<s>cittabhūmi</s>).

body.text: aśaktādīnāmapi kuśalacittamasti | kuto na labhante | kuto na śṛṇvanti bhikṣukriyām | atigahanasaṃyojanānuśayānāmeṣāṃ durlabhamārgatvāt | tādṛśāḥ puruṣā na bhikṣumadhye vartate(nte) nāpi bhikṣuṇīmadhye | ato na śṛṇvanti | teṣu cānye pratiṣiddhāḥ yathā kāṇādayaḥ | te 'pi kuśalasaṃvarasyāsyārhāḥ | (pṛ) asti ca pratiṣedho vinaye pātakinīcavṛttikabhikṣuṇīdūṣakādayo na bhikṣucaryāṃ śṛṇvanti iti | teṣāmapi kiṃ kuśalasaṃvaro 'sti | (u) sa yadyavadātavasano bhavati | kadācitkuśalasaṃvaraṃ labhate | yathā te dānadayādisaddharmacaryābhyāse na pratiṣiddhāḥ | evaṃ laukikaśīlasaṃvaravattve ko doṣaḥ | kevalaṃ duṣkarmadūṣitatvāt te pratihatāryamārgāśca bhavanti | ato na pravrajyāṃ śṛṇvanti |
body.translated_text: Even those who are impotent and the like have wholesome mind. Why would they not obtain it? [The question is:] Why do they not receive the monastic ordination (<s>bhikṣukriyā</s>)? Because for those with extremely dense fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) and latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), the path is difficult to attain. Such persons do not dwell among monks nor among nuns. Therefore they do not receive [ordination]. Among them, others are prohibited [from ordination], such as the one-eyed and the like. They too are worthy of this wholesome restraint. (Question) There is also a prohibition in the <s>Vinaya</s> that those who have committed grave offenses (<s>pātakin</s>), those of base conduct, and those who have corrupted nuns do not receive the monastic training. Do even they have wholesome restraint? (Answer) If such a person wears white garments [i.e., lives as a layperson], at some time he may obtain wholesome restraint. Just as they are not prohibited from practicing the good <s>dharmas</s> of generosity, compassion, and the like — likewise, what fault is there in having worldly moral restraint? Only because of being defiled by evil <s>karma</s>, they have the noble path obstructed. Therefore they do not receive the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) kiṃ vadhyādisattvebhyaḥ kiṃ kuśalasaṃvaraṃ labhate kiṃ vā sarvasattvebhyaḥ | (u) sarvasattvānāṃ sāmantāllabhate | tathā no cet saṃvaraḥ prādeśikaḥ syāt | prādeśiko vikalaḥ syāt | ayaṃ tu saṃvara upacīyamāno 'pacīyamāno nirgranthaputradharmasamaśca yaduta śatayojaneṣvantaḥ prāṇātipātādibhyo viratiḥ iti | tādṛśadoṣavattvātsaṃvaro na prādeśiko bhavati | ya āha asya puruṣasya vadhādviramāmi na tasya puruṣasyeti | na sa imaṃ śīlasaṃvaraṃ labhate | ābhidharmikāḥ āhuḥ- prādeśike 'pi dānacaryākaruṇācittādau puṇyaguṇo 'sti | tathā śīlamapi bhavet | yathaikamapi śīladhāraṇaṃ śīlapuṇyaṃ prasūte | tathaikasattve saṃvaraṃ labheta iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Does one obtain wholesome restraint with respect to those beings who are to be killed and the like, or with respect to all beings? (Answer) One obtains it universally with respect to all beings. If it were not so, the restraint would be partial (<s>prādeśika</s>). What is partial would be incomplete. But this restraint, whether increasing or decreasing, would be the same as the doctrine of the <s>Nirgrantha</s> sons (Jains) — namely, 'abstention from killing and the like within a hundred <s>yojanas</s>.' Because of having such a fault, the restraint should not be partial. One who says: 'I abstain from killing this person but not that person' — he does not obtain this moral restraint. The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say: 'Even in partial [restraint], the quality of merit exists in the practice of giving, compassion-mind, and the like. Likewise with moral conduct as well. Just as even the observance of a single moral precept produces the merit of moral conduct — so too, one could obtain restraint with respect to even a single being.'

body.text: (pṛ) śīlasaṃvaro 'yaṃ dvividhaḥ yāvajjīvaka ekadināhorātraka iti | yāvajjīvaka iti yat bhikṣorūpāsakasya vā | ekāhorātraka iti yathā ekāhorātramaṣṭaśīlānyupādatte | kathamidam | (u) aniyatamidam | ekāhorātraṃ vā ekadinamātraṃ vā ekarātrimātraṃ vā ardhadinamātraṃ vā ardharātraṃ vā yathaśakti kālaṃ svīkaroti | pravrajyālabdhasya tu yāvajjīvamātraṃ bhavati | ya āha- āhamekamāsamātraṃ māsadvitayamātraṃ vā ekavatsaramātraṃ vā [śīlaṃ samādada iti] | na sa pravrajyālabdha ityucyate | tathā pañcaśīlānyapi | (pṛ) yaḥ kuśalasaṃvaraṃ labhate sa punaḥ saṃvarādbhraśyati na vā | (u) na bhraśyati | kevalamakuśaladharmeṇa saṃvaramimaṃ dūṣayati | (pṛ) kiṃ pratyutpannasattvebhyaḥ śīlasaṃvaraṃ labhate kiṃ vā traikālikasattvebhyaḥ | (u) traikālikasattvebhyo labdhasyaḥ | yathā
body.translated_text: (Question) This moral restraint is of two kinds: lifelong (<s>yāvajjīvaka</s>) and for a single day-and-night (<s>ekadināhorātraka</s>). 'Lifelong' refers to that of a monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>) or a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>). 'For a single day-and-night' refers to when one undertakes the eight precepts (<s>aṣṭaśīla</s>) for one day-and-night. How is this? (Answer) This is not fixed. One undertakes it for one day-and-night, or for a single day only, or for a single night only, or for half a day only, or for half a night only — accepting the time according to one's ability. But for one who has obtained the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), it is lifelong. One who says: 'I undertake [moral conduct] for one month only, or for two months only, or for one year only' — he is not called one who has obtained the going-forth. The same applies to the five precepts (<s>pañcaśīla</s>). (Question) Does one who has obtained wholesome restraint later fall away from the restraint or not? (Answer) One does not fall away. One merely corrupts this restraint through unwholesome <s>dharma</s>. (Question) Does one obtain moral restraint with respect to beings existing in the present only, or with respect to beings of the three time-periods? (Answer) One who has obtained it with respect to beings of the three time-periods — just as

body.text: kaścidatītān pūjyān pūjayitvāpi puṇyaguṇo bhavati | tathā saṃvaro 'pi | ataḥ sarve buddhāḥ samānaikaśīlaskandhāḥ |
body.translated_text: someone who worships the venerable ones of the past also has the quality of merit. So too with restraint. Therefore all <s>Buddhas</s> share the same single aggregate of moral conduct (<s>śīlaskandha</s>).

body.text: apramāṇo 'yaṃ saṃvaraḥ | yathaikasya sattvasya saptavidha utpadyate | alobhādikuśalamūlebhya utpadyate | uttamamadhyādhamacittebhyaścotpadyata iti bahuvidho bhavati | yathaikasya puruṣasya tathā sarvasattvānāṃ samantādapi pratikṣaṇaṃ sadā pratilābhādapramāṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: This restraint is immeasurable. Just as for a single being, it arises in seven kinds — it arises from the wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) of non-greed and the like, and it arises from minds of superior, middling, and inferior [quality] — thus it is of many kinds. Just as for a single person, so too universally for all beings — because of obtaining [restraint] at every moment at all times, it is immeasurable.

body.text: (pṛ) śīlasaṃvaraḥ kadā labhyaḥ | (u) kaściddinamekaṃ śīlamupādatte | ayamādyasaṃvaraḥ | tasminneva dine upāsakaśīlamupādatte | ayaṃ dvitīyasaṃvaraḥ | tasminneva dine pravrajya śrāmaṇyaṃ karoti | ayaṃ tṛtīyasaṃvaraḥ | tasminneva dine samagraśīlamupādatte | ayaṃ caturthaḥ saṃvaraḥ | tasminneva dine dhyānasamāpattiṃ labhate | ayaṃ pañcamaḥ saṃvaraḥ | tasminneva dina ārūpyasamādhiṃ labhate | ayaṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ saṃvaraḥ | tasminneva dine 'nāsrava[saṃvaraṃ] labhate | ayaṃ saptamaḥ saṃvaraḥ | mārgaphalalābhamanusaran punaḥ saṃvaraṃ labhate | labdhamūlo na naśyati | pratyuta viśiṣṭa ityākhyāṃ gṛhṇāti | evaṃ puṇyaguṇo 'bhivardhate | yasmādayaṃ śīlasaṃvaraḥ sarvasattveṣu sadā pratikṣaṇaṃ labhyate | tasmāducyate catvāro ratnākarā nārhanti ṣoḍaśīṃ kalāṃ dinamekaṃ saṃvarasyeti |
body.translated_text: (Question) When is moral restraint obtained? (Answer) Someone undertakes moral conduct for a single day — this is the first restraint. On that very day, he undertakes the precepts of a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>) — this is the second restraint. On that very day, going forth, he becomes a novice (<s>śrāmaṇya</s>) — this is the third restraint. On that very day, he undertakes the complete precepts — this is the fourth restraint. On that very day, he obtains <s>dhyāna</s> and meditative attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>) — this is the fifth restraint. On that very day, he obtains formless concentration (<s>ārūpyasamādhi</s>) — this is the sixth restraint. On that very day, he obtains the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) [restraint] — this is the seventh restraint. Following the attainment of the fruit of the path, he further obtains restraint. What has been obtained at the root does not perish. Rather, it acquires the designation 'distinguished.' Thus the quality of merit increases. Because this moral restraint is obtained at every moment with respect to all beings at all times, therefore it is said: 'The four treasure-mines are not worth a sixteenth fraction of a single day of restraint.'

body.text: dhyānasaṃvaro 'nāsravasaṃvaraśca yathācittaṃ samudācarati | śīlasaṃvaro na yathācitta[mātraṃ] samudācarati | (pṛ) kecidvadanti- samādhipraviṣṭasyāsti dhyānasaṃvaraḥ | na samādhivyutthitasyeti | kathamidam | (u) samādhivyutthitasya sadāsti | labdhatattvo 'yaṃ na karoti śīlabhedanaviruddhamakuśalam | akuśalaṃ kadāpyakurvadbhiḥ kuśalacittaprakarṣapravṛttaiḥ sadā bhavitavyam | (pṛ) yadyārūpye dhyānasya śīlabhedakatā nāsti | kasya virodhāt kuśalasaṃvara ityākhyā | (u) dharmatā īdṛśī syāt | [yat] āryā maharṣayaḥ sarve kuśalasaṃvaralābhina iti | yadi śīlabhedanavirodhādeva te saṃvaravantaḥ | tadā sampīḍanīyasattvebhya eva kuśalasaṃvaro labhyeta ityayamasti doṣaḥ | ato na yujyate |
body.translated_text: The restraint of <s>dhyāna</s> and the undefiled restraint (<s>anāsravasaṃvara</s>) operate according to [their respective] minds. Moral restraint does not operate according to mind alone. (Question) Certain people say: 'For one who has entered <s>samādhi</s>, there exists the restraint of <s>dhyāna</s>, but not for one who has emerged from <s>samādhi</s>.' How is this? (Answer) For one who has emerged from <s>samādhi</s>, it always exists. One who has obtained its reality (<s>tattva</s>) does not commit the unwholesome that violates moral conduct. For those who never commit the unwholesome, there must always be a mind operating with the excellence of the wholesome. (Question) If in the formless [realm] there is no violation of the moral conduct of <s>dhyāna</s>, in opposition to what is the designation 'wholesome restraint' [given]? (Answer) Such is the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>) — that all Noble Ones and great seers (<s>maharṣi</s>) are possessors of wholesome restraint. If one were [said to be] a restraint-possessor merely in opposition to the violation of moral conduct, then one would obtain wholesome restraint only with respect to beings who can be afflicted — and this is a fault. Therefore that is not valid.

body.text: saptakuśalasaṃvaravargo dvādaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-twelfth chapter, the Chapter on the Seven Wholesome Restraints (<s>saptakuśalasaṃvaravarga</s>).

body.text: 113 aṣṭāṅgopavāsaśīla vargaḥ
body.translated_text: 113. Chapter on the Eight-Factored Fasting Observance (<s>aṣṭāṅgopavāsaśīlavarga</s>)

body.text: aṣṭāṅga upavāsa upāsakasyocyate | sa kuśalacetasā śīlabhedādvirata upavasatīti upavasathaḥ | (pṛ) kasmāt aṣṭa viratayo mukhyata ucyante | (u) aṣṭāvetā dvāraṃ bhavanti | ebhiraṣṭadharmaiḥ sarvākuśalebhyo viramati | tatra catvāri dravyato 'kuśalāni | surāpānaṃ sarvākuśalānāṃ mūlam | anyāni trīṇi pramādakāraṇāni | pañcākuśalebhyo viratiḥ puruṣasya puṇyakāraṇam | tribhyo 'nyebhyo viratirmārgakāraṇam | avadātavasanānāṃ kuśaladharmo bhūyasā hīnaḥ mārgasya kāraṇatāmātraṃ karoti | ata ebhiraṣṭabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatāni pañca yānāni |
body.translated_text: The eight-factored observance (<s>aṣṭāṅga upavāsa</s>) is taught for the lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>). He, with a wholesome mind, abstaining from the violation of moral conduct, observes the fast — hence it is called 'observance' (<s>upavasatha</s>). (Question) Why are the eight abstentions stated as the principal ones? (Answer) These eight serve as the gateway. Through these eight <s>dharmas</s>, one abstains from all unwholesome [actions]. Among them, four are unwholesome by their substance (<s>dravyatas</s>). The drinking of liquor (<s>surāpāna</s>) is the root of all unwholesome [actions]. The other three are causes of heedlessness. Abstention from the five unwholesome [actions] is the cause of merit for a person. Abstention from the other three is the cause of the path. For white-clad [laypeople], the wholesome <s>dharma</s> is for the most part inferior; it merely functions as a cause of the path. Therefore, through being endowed with these eight <s>dharmas</s>, there are five vehicles.

body.text: (pṛ) kimetānyaṣṭopavāsāṅgāni sahopādeyāni kiṃ vā pṛthak | (u) yathābalaṃ dhartuṃ śakyate | kecidāhuḥ- eme dharmā ekamupavāsadinaṃ rātriñca bhavanti iti | tadayuktam | bahvalpaṃ śīlaṃ yathā [balaṃ] upādāya ardhadinaṃ vā yāvadekaṃ māsaṃ vā sambhavatīti ko doṣo 'sti | kecidāhuḥ- avaśyamanyasmādupādatta iti | ayamapyaniyamaḥ | asatyanyasmin manasā smaran vācā vadati- ahamaṣṭaśīlāni dhārayāmīti | śīlasya pañca śaucāni- (1) daśakuśala[karma]pathācāraṇam | (2) pūrvāntāparāntayo duḥkha[saṃjñā] | (3) akuśalacittena na kasyacidupaghātaḥ | (4) smṛtvā saṃvararakṣaṇam | (5) nirvāṇapravaṇatā | ya idṛśopavāsasamarthaḥ tasya catvāro mahāratnākarā naikāmapi kalāmarhanti | denāvāmindrasya puṇyavipāko 'pi nārhati | śakro gāthāmavocat | bhagavān taṃ vigarhya [avocat]- yaḥkṣīṇāsravaḥ tena hīyaṃ gāthā vaktavyā | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: (Question) Are these eight factors of the observance to be undertaken together or separately? (Answer) They can be maintained according to one's ability. Some say: 'These <s>dharmas</s> are for one day of observance and one night.' That is not valid. What fault is there if moral conduct, whether much or little, can be undertaken according to one's ability for half a day, or up to a single month? Some say: 'One must necessarily undertake them from another [person].' This too is not a fixed rule. When another [teacher] is not present, remembering with the mind and speaking with the voice, one says: 'I shall maintain the eight precepts.' The five purities (<s>śaucāni</s>) of moral conduct are: (1) the practice of the ten wholesome action-paths (<s>daśakuśalakarmapatha</s>); (2) the perception of suffering regarding past and future [lives]; (3) not harming anyone with an unwholesome mind; (4) guarding the restraint through mindfulness; (5) inclination toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. For one who is capable of such an observance, the four great treasure-mines are not worth even a single fraction [of its merit]. Even the merit-ripening of [the god] <s>Indra</s> is not equal [to it]. <s>Śakra</s> spoke a verse. The Blessed One rebuked him, [saying]: 'One who has destroyed the outflows (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>) — by him this verse should be spoken.' As stated:

body.text:
māse ṣaḍupāvāsārddha aṣṭāṅgeṣu prapannakaḥ |
sa pumān puṇyamāpnoti mayā ca sadṛśo bhavet || iti |
body.translated_text:
'One who observes the fast on six [days] per month, established in the eight factors —
that person obtains merit and becomes equal to me.' Thus it is said.

body.text: yo dinamupavasati sa upavāsapuṇyamupabhuñjānaḥ śakratulyo bhavati | imamupavāsadharmamupādāturnirvāṇaphalaṃ syāt | ataḥ kṣīṇāsraveṇa sā gāthā vaktavyeti |
body.translated_text: One who observes the fast for a day, enjoying the merit of the observance, becomes equal to <s>Śakra</s>. For one who undertakes this observance-<s>dharma</s>, the fruit would be <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore the verse should be spoken by one who has destroyed the outflows.

body.text: upavāsadharmasamādāne sunibaddhāḥ śṛṅkhalāḥ sarvā mocayitavyāḥ | sarvākuśalapratyayo 'pi prahātavyaḥ | idaṃ śaucamityucyate | (pṛ) āryaścaka vartī rājā upavāsadharmasamādānamabhilaṣati [cet] kastaṃ samādāpayati | (u) bhadantā brahmā devā bhagaddraṣṭārastaṃ śāsayitvā grāhayeyuḥ ||
body.translated_text: In undertaking the observance-<s>dharma</s>, all bonds and chains that are firmly bound are to be released. All conditions of the unwholesome are also to be abandoned. This is called 'purity' (<s>śauca</s>). (Question) If a noble wheel-turning king (<s>cakravartin rāja</s>) desires to undertake the observance-<s>dharma</s>, who will administer it to him? (Answer) Venerable elders, <s>Brahmā</s>, gods, and those who see the blessed [truth] — having instructed him, they would make him undertake it.

body.text: aṣṭāṅgopavāsaśīlavargasrayodaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-thirteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Eight-Factored Fasting Observance (<s>aṣṭāṅgopavāsaśīlavarga</s>).

body.text: 114 aṣṭavidhavādavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 114. Chapter on the Eight Kinds of Speech (<s>aṣṭavidhavādavarga</s>)

body.text: aṣṭavidhavādeṣu catvāro 'śuddhāḥ catvāraḥ śuddhāḥ | catvāro 'śuddhā iti | yo vadati dṛṣṭvā nādrākṣamiti | adṛṣṭvā vadati adrākṣamiti | adṛṣṭvā adrākṣamiti van [vyavahāre] pṛṣṭo vadati nādrākṣamiti | dṛṣṭvā nādrākṣamiti brūvan pṛṣṭo vadati- adrākṣamiti | evaṃ vastuviparyāsena cittaviparyāsādaśuddhāḥ | catvāraḥ śuddhā iti | dṛṣṭvā vadati adrākṣamiti | adṛṣṭvā vadati nādrākṣamiti | dṛṣṭvā nādrākṣamiti brūvan pṛṣṭho vadati nādrākṣamiti | adṛṣṭvā adrākṣamiti bruvan pṛṣṭho vadati adrākṣamiti | evaṃ vastutattvena cittatattvāt śuddhāḥ | śrutibuddhijñāneṣvapi |
body.translated_text: Among the eight kinds of speech, four are impure and four are pure. The four impure are: one who, having seen, says 'I did not see'; one who, not having seen, says 'I saw'; one who, not having seen, saying 'I did not see,' when questioned in [legal] proceedings says 'I did not see'; one who, having seen, saying 'I did not see,' when questioned says 'I saw.' Thus, through the reversal of the object and the reversal of the mind, they are impure. The four pure are: one who, having seen, says 'I saw'; one who, not having seen, says 'I did not see'; one who, having seen, saying 'I did not see,' when questioned says 'I did not see'; one who, not having seen, saying 'I saw,' when questioned says 'I saw.' Thus, through the truth of the object and the truth of the mind, they are pure. The same applies to hearing, cognition, and knowledge as well.

body.text: (pṛ) dṛṣṭiśrutibuddhijñānānāṃ ko bhedaḥ | (u) trividhāḥ śraddhāḥ | dṛṣṭiḥ pratyutpanne śraddhā | śrutirāptavacane śraddhā | jñānamanumitijñānam | buddhistrividhaśraddhāvivecanī prajñā | imāstrividhāḥ prajñāḥ kadācitsatyā bhavanti | kadācidviparīttāḥ | uttamapuruṣā aśuddhavādamakṛtvā śuddhavādamātraṃ kurvanti | ato 'varajanaiḥ prayujyamāno 'śuddha ityucyate | uttamajanaiḥ prayujyamānastu śuddha iti | kecidāhuḥ- arthasyāsya samyagabhijñātāraḥ uttamā bhavanti | na mārgamātralābhina [uttamāḥ] | ataḥ prākṛtā api śuddhavādina iti ||
body.translated_text: (Question) What is the difference between seeing (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), hearing (<s>śruti</s>), cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>)? (Answer) There are three kinds of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). Seeing is faith in what is present. Hearing is faith in the word of a trustworthy authority (<s>āpta</s>). Knowledge is inferential knowledge (<s>anumitijñāna</s>). Cognition is the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that discriminates the three kinds of faith. These three kinds of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) are sometimes true and sometimes perverted. Superior persons, not engaging in impure speech, engage only in pure speech. Therefore, when employed by inferior persons, it is called 'impure'; when employed by superior persons, it is called 'pure.' Some say: 'Those who correctly understand the meaning of this are superior — not merely those who have obtained the path. Therefore even ordinary persons can be speakers of pure speech.'

body.text: aṣṭhavidhavādavargaścaturdaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-fourteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Eight Kinds of Speech (<s>aṣṭavidhavādavarga</s>).

body.text: 115 navakarmavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 115. Chapter on the Nine Kinds of Karma (<s>navakarmavarga</s>)

body.text: navavidhaṃ karma- kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ karma trividhaṃ vijñaptiravijñaptirnavijñapti nāvijñaptiriti | rūpadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ karmāpyevam | ārūpyadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ dvividhañcānāsravaṃ karma |
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is of nine kinds: <s>karma</s> connected with the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) is threefold — manifest (<s>vijñapti</s>), non-manifest (<s>avijñapti</s>), and neither-manifest-nor-non-manifest (<s>na vijñapti nāvijñapti</s>). <s>Karma</s> connected with the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) is likewise. <s>Karma</s> connected with the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>) is twofold, plus undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>karma</s>.

body.text: kāyavāgbhyāṃ kṛtaṃ karma vijñaptiḥ | vijñaptimupādāya [yaḥ] puṇyapāpasañcayaḥ sadānuyāyī | ayaṃ cittaviprayuktadharmo 'vijñaptirityucyate | cittamātrajāvijñaptirapyasti | navijñapti nāvijñaptiriti mana eva | manaśca cetanaiva | cetanā ca karmetyucyate | tasmādyanmanasā praṇidhāya paścātkāya[kṛtaṃ] tanmānasaṃ karmāpi cetanetyucyate | cetanayā cintayitvā kāya[kṛta]mityataḥ karmetyucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> performed by body and speech is <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action). Depending on <s>vijñapti</s>, the accumulation of merit and demerit that constantly follows — this <s>dharma</s> dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayuktadharma</s>) is called <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action). There is also <s>avijñapti</s> that arises from mind alone. What is neither <s>vijñapti</s> nor <s>avijñapti</s> is mind (<s>manas</s>) itself. And mind is volition (<s>cetanā</s>) itself. And volition is called '<s>karma</s>.' Therefore, what one first resolves mentally and afterward performs bodily — that is also called mental <s>karma</s>, i.e., volition. Because one has deliberated through volition and then performed it bodily — therefore it is called '<s>karma</s>.'

body.text: (pṛ) tathā cedanāsravacetanā na [syāt] | (u) yadidaṃ cetanātmakaṃ saivānāsravacetanā | (pṛ) avijñapteḥ kāyajātāyā api kiṃ tāratamyavibhāgo bhaviṣyati na vā | (u) yat sarve kāyāvayavāḥ vijñaptikarma kurvanti | tadupādāya sañcitāvijñaptirmahatī mahāvipākaprāpiṇī | (pṛ) avijñaptiriyaṃ kasmin sthāne vidyate | (u) karmapathasvarūpaṃ niyatamavijñaptisañcāyakam | vijñaptiḥ satī asatī vā bhavati | anyā tu cittāpekṣiṇī | yadi cittaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ bhavati | tadā satī | yadi cittaṃ mṛdu bhavati | tadā asatī | avijñaptiriyaṃ praṇidhānādapi utpadyate | yadi kaścitpraṇidadhāti- avaśyamahaṃ dāsyāmīti | yadi vā caityaṃ karomīti | so 'vaśyamavijñaptiṃ pratilabhate | (pṛ) kadā pratilabhyate 'vijñaptiriyaṃ | kadā praṇaśyati | (u) yathāvijñapti vastu vartate | yadi caityārāmādidānaṃ karoti | yāvaddattaṃ vastu na praṇaśyati | tāvatkālaṃ sadānuvartate | cittañcānusarati | noparamati | yathā kaściccittamutpādayati- mayedaṃ sadā kartavyam | yadi vā samaiḥ melayāmi, yadi vā cīvaraṃ dadāmīti | evamādi vastu cittagataṃ noparamati | tasmin samaye sadā pratilabhyate | yāvajīvamanurati ca | yathā pravrajyāśīlaṃ samādadāti | tasmātkālātsadā pratilabhyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) If that is so, then there would be no undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) volition. (Answer) That which has the nature of volition — that itself is undefiled volition. (Question) For <s>avijñapti</s> that arises from the body, will there be a gradation of degrees, or not? (Answer) When all the limbs of the body perform <s>vijñaptikarma</s> (manifest action), the <s>avijñapti</s> accumulated depending on that is great and brings about great ripening. (Question) In which place does this <s>avijñapti</s> exist? (Answer) The essential nature of the action-path (<s>karmapatha</s>) is necessarily the accumulator of <s>avijñapti</s>. <s>Vijñapti</s> may exist or may not exist. But another [<s>avijñapti</s>] depends on mind. If the mind is very firm, then it exists. If the mind is weak, then it does not exist. This <s>avijñapti</s> arises from a vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) as well. If someone resolves: 'I will certainly give' or 'I will make a <s>caitya</s>' — he necessarily obtains <s>avijñapti</s>. (Question) When is this <s>avijñapti</s> obtained? When does it perish? (Answer) As long as the object of <s>avijñapti</s> continues to exist. If one makes a gift of a <s>caitya</s>, a garden, or the like — as long as the given object does not perish, during that time [the <s>avijñapti</s>] constantly follows. And it follows the mind — it does not cease. Just as someone generates the mind: 'I should always do this' — whether 'I will bring together companions' or 'I will give a robe' — such mental objects do not cease. At that time, [<s>avijñapti</s>] is constantly obtained. And it persists as long as life. Just as one who undertakes the precepts of going forth (<s>pravrajyāśīla</s>) — from that time onward, it is constantly obtained.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- kāmadhātāveva vijñapteravijñaptirutpadyate | na rūpadhātāviti | kathamidam | (u) dhātudvaye 'pyutpadyate | kasmāt | rūpadhātukadevā api dharmaṃ pravadanti | buddhaṃ saṅghañca vandante | yathā manuṣyādaya iti kathaṃ vijñaptikarmato 'vijñaptirnotpadyate | kecidāhuḥ- vilīnāvyākṛtā nāstyavijñaptiriti | idamayuktam | vilīnāvyākṛtā gurutarakleśaḥ | kleśopacayo 'yamanuśaya ityucyate | avilīnāvyākṛtā paraṃ nāstyavijñaptiḥ | kasmāt | cittamidamavaraṃ mṛdu sat nopacayamutpādayati | yathā puṣpaṃ tilaṃ vāsayati na tṛṇavṛkṣādi | kecidāhuḥ- brahmalokādūrdhvaṃ nāsti vijñaptikarmacittamutpādakaṃ iti | kasmāt | vitarkavicārau hi vākkarma samutpādayataḥ | na tatra sto vitarkavicārauḥ | brahmalokopabhogacittamātraṃ
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: 'Only in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) does <s>avijñapti</s> arise from <s>vijñapti</s> — not in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>).' How is this? (Answer) It arises in both realms. Why? Because deities of the form realm also expound the <s>Dharma</s> and worship the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, just as humans and the like do — so how would <s>avijñapti</s> not arise from <s>vijñaptikarma</s>? Some say: 'In the obscured indeterminate (<s>vilīnāvyākṛta</s>) [state], there is no <s>avijñapti</s>.' This is not valid. In the obscured indeterminate [state], the defilements are heavier. This accumulation of defilements is called 'latent tendency' (<s>anuśaya</s>). In the unobscured indeterminate (<s>avilīnāvyākṛta</s>) [state] moreover, there is no <s>avijñapti</s>. Why? Because this mind, being inferior and weak, does not generate accumulation. Just as a flower perfumes sesame but not grass and trees and the like. Some say: 'Above the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, there is no mind that generates <s>vijñaptikarma</s>.' Why? Because <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) generate vocal <s>karma</s>, and those do not exist there [above the <s>Brahmaloka</s>]. The mere mind of enjoying the <s>Brahmaloka</s>

body.text: vākkarma samutpādayati | iti | tadayuktam | sattvāḥ karmānusāreṇa śarīramupādadate | ya ūrdhvaloka utpadyate | na sa brahmaloke vipākamupabhuñjyāt | ato jñāyate svabhūmikacittena vākkarma karotīti | yaduktaṃ bhavatā na tatra vitarkavicārau sta iti | tatpaścādvakṣyate sta iti |
body.translated_text: generates vocal <s>karma</s>.' This is not valid. Beings, following their <s>karma</s>, take up a body. One who is reborn in the upper world would not enjoy ripening in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. From this it is known that one performs vocal <s>karma</s> through the mind of one's own plane (<s>svabhūmikacittena</s>). As for your statement: '<s>Vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> do not exist there' — it will be stated later that they do exist.

body.text: (pṛ) āryā aparyavasannasaṃyojanaprahāṇā vijñaptikarma kurvanti na vā | (u) āryāḥ prakṛtito nāvadyaṃ karma kurvanti | (pṛ) śvādīnāṃ sattvānāṃ [vāg]dhvaniḥ vākkarma bhavati na vā | (u) asatyapyālāpaviśeṣe cittataḥ samutthānātkarmetyapyucyate | yadi vā vyaktalakṣaṇaṃ yadi vāhvānaṃ yadi vā veṇvādi sarvaṃ [tat] vākkarmetyucyate | idaṃ kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmāvaśyaṃ manovijñānādutpadyate | nānyavijñānāt | ataḥ puruṣāḥ svakāyikaṃ karma paśyanti svavācikaṃ karma śṛṇvanti ca | manovijñānasamutpannaṃ karma santatyāvicchinnaṃ sat svayaṃ paśyanti śṛṇvanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Do the Noble Ones (<s>ārya</s>) who have abandoned the fetters of incomplete attachment (<s>aparyavasannasaṃyojana</s>) perform <s>vijñaptikarma</s>, or not? (Answer) The Noble Ones do not by nature perform blameworthy <s>karma</s>. (Question) Do the sounds of dogs and the like constitute vocal <s>karma</s>, or not? (Answer) Even without a specific utterance, because it arises from mind, it is also called '<s>karma</s>.' Whether it is a distinct expression, or a calling sound, or bamboo flutes and the like — all are called 'vocal <s>karma</s>.' This bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> necessarily arises from mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) — not from other consciousnesses. Therefore persons see their own bodily <s>karma</s> and hear their own vocal <s>karma</s>. <s>Karma</s> arising from mind-consciousness, being unbroken in continuity, is itself seen and heard.

body.text: navakarmavargaḥ pañcadaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-fifteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Nine [Kinds of] <s>Karma</s> (<s>navakarmavarga</s>).

body.text: 116 daśākuśalakarmapathavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 116. Chapter on the Ten Unwholesome Action-Paths (<s>daśākuśalakarmapathavarga</s>)

body.text: sūtre bhagavānāha- daśākuśalakarmapathā yaduta prāṇātipātādi | pañcaskandhakalāpaḥ sattva ityucyate | tadāyuṣaśchedaḥ prāṇātipāto nāma | (pṛ) yadīme pañcaskandhāḥ pratikṣaṇavināśinaḥ | kena vadho bhavati | (u) pañcaskandhāḥ pratikṣaṇavināśino 'pi punaḥ punaḥ santatyā samutpadyante | tatsantatisamuccheda eva prāṇātipāto bhavati | prāṇātipātacittena ca prāṇātipātapāpaṃ labhate puruṣaḥ | (pṛ) kiṃ pratyutpannapañcaskandhānāṃ samucchedaḥ prāṇātipāto bhavati | (u) pañcaskandhasantatāvasti sattva ityākhyā | tatsantativināśaḥ prāṇātipātaḥ | na kṣaṇikeṣu sattva ityākhyāsti | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ kaścidanucarānavalambya sattvān hanti | atha vā dṛḍhāsinābhihatya sahasā sattvān hanti | tadā tasya pāpaṃ nāstīti | kathamidam | (u) te 'pi pāpaṃ labheran | kasmāt | te vadhapāpasamanvitāḥ | caturbhiḥ pratyayaiḥ khalu prāṇātipātapāpaṃ labhante | (1) sattvasattā, (2) sattvasattājñānam, (3) jighatsācittam, (4) tajjīvitoccheda iti | ebhiścaturbhirhetubhirmaṇḍitaḥ pumān kathamapāpī syāt |
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are ten unwholesome action-paths (<s>daśākuśalakarmapatha</s>), namely taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>) and the rest.' The collection of the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandhakalāpa</s>) is called a 'being' (<s>sattva</s>). The cutting off of its life-force is called 'taking life' (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>). (Question) If these five aggregates are destroyed at every moment, by whom is killing done? (Answer) Even though the five aggregates are destroyed at every moment, they arise again and again in continuity. The cutting off of that very continuity is taking life. And through a mind intent on taking life, a person obtains the sin of taking life. (Question) Is taking life the destruction of the present five aggregates? (Answer) In the continuity of the five aggregates, there is the designation 'being.' The destruction of that continuity is taking life — not in momentary [aggregates] is the designation 'being' [established]. (Question) Some say: 'A certain one, relying on subordinates, kills beings. Or else, striking with a sharp sword, he suddenly kills beings. In that case, he has no sin.' How is this? (Answer) They too would obtain sin. Why? Because they are endowed with the sin of killing. Through four conditions, one obtains the sin of taking life: (1) the existence of a being, (2) the knowledge that it is a being, (3) the intention to kill, (4) the cutting off of its life. A person furnished with these four causes — how could he be without sin?

body.text: adattādānamiti yadvastu yatpuruṣasambandhī tat tasmātpuruṣāccauryeṇa gṛhṇāti | tadadattādānamityucyate | atrāpi santi catvāraḥ pratyayāḥ- (1) dravyasya parasambandhitā,
body.translated_text: 'Taking what is not given' (<s>adattādāna</s>) — whatever object belongs to a certain person, and one takes it from that person by theft — that is called 'taking what is not given.' Here too there are four conditions: (1) the object belongs to another,

body.text: (2) parasambandhitājñānam | (3) cauryacittam, (4) cauryeṇa grahaṇam iti | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- nidhiḥ rājasambandhī | ya imaṃ gṛhṇāti | sa rājñaḥ pāpaṃ labhata iti | kathamidam | (u) bhūmadhyagatadravyasya na vicāraḥ | bhūmāvupari gataṃ dravyaṃ paraṃ rājasambandhi syāt | kasmāt | anāthapiṇḍadādaya āryā api hīdaṃ dravyaṃ gṛhṇanti | ato jñāyate nāsti pāpamiti | yaḥ svābhāvikadravyasya lābhaḥ na tat cauryam |
body.translated_text: (2) the knowledge that it belongs to another, (3) the intention to steal, (4) taking by theft. (Question) Some say: 'A treasure [found in the ground] belongs to the king. One who takes it obtains sin toward the king.' How is this? (Answer) Objects located in the middle of the earth are not subject to investigation. Objects located on the surface of the earth would further belong to the king. Why? Because Noble Ones such as <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> and others also take such objects. From this it is known that there is no sin. The obtaining of naturally-occurring objects is not theft.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi sarve padārthāḥ sādhāraṇakarmabhirutpadyante | kasmāt cauryeṇa pāpaṃ labhante | (u) sādhāraṇakarmahetoḥ samutpattāvapi asti hetoḥ prābalyadaurbalyam | yat [yasya] puruṣasya karmahetubalatiśayādhiṣṭhitaṃ tat dravyaṃ tatsambandhi | (pṛ) yadi kaściccaityāt saṅghādvā kiñcit kṣetragṛhādidravyamapaharati | katarasmāt pāpaṃ labhate | (u) bhagavataḥ saṅghasya vā dravye nāsti mamatācittam | asatyapi tataḥ pāpaṃ labhate | dravyamidaṃ niyamena bhagavataḥ saṅghasya vā sambandhi | tasya caurye adattādāne vā akuśalacittaṃ samutpannamityataḥ pāpaṃ labhate |
body.translated_text: (Question) If all objects arise through shared <s>karma</s> (<s>sādhāraṇakarma</s>), why does one obtain sin through theft? (Answer) Even though they arise from the cause of shared <s>karma</s>, there is strength and weakness of the cause. Whatever object is established through the preponderant force of a particular person's <s>karma</s>-cause — that object belongs to him. (Question) If someone steals some property from a <s>caitya</s> or from the <s>Saṅgha</s>, such as a field, dwelling, or the like — from whom does one obtain sin? (Answer) In the property of the Blessed One or of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, there is no mind of possessiveness. Even though that is absent, one obtains sin from it. This property certainly belongs to the Blessed One or to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Because an unwholesome mind arises at the time of stealing or taking what is not given — therefore one obtains sin.

body.text: kāmamithyācāra iti | yā [yasya] sattvasya jāyā na bhavati | tayā saha kāmacāraḥ | [tasya] kāmamithyācāraḥ | svajāyāyāmapi amārgeṇa kāmacāro 'pi kāmamithyācāra ityucyate | sarvāsāṃ strīṇāṃ santi pālakāḥ yanmātṛpitṛbhrātṛgaṇasvāmiputravadhvādayaḥ | pravrajitastrīṇāṃ rājādayaḥ pālakāḥ | (pṛ) gaṇikā na [kasyacit] jāyā bhavati | tayā saha kāmacāraḥ kathaṃ na kāmamithyācāraḥ | (u) alpavayaskā hi jāyā | yathoktaṃ vinaye- alpavayaskā jāyā yāvadekena śmaśrṛṇāntaritā iti | (pṛ) yadi kācidasvāminī strī svayamāgatya prārthayate jāyā bhavāmīti | kathamidam | (u) yā vastuto 'svāminī kasyacitsattvasya purato yathādharmamāgatā, [tayā saha gamanaṃ] na kāmamithyācāraḥ | (pṛ) pravrajitasya jāyāparigraheṇa kāmamithyācārādunmoko 'sti na vā | (u) nonmoko 'sti | kasmāt | na hyasti sa dharmaḥ | pravrajitasya dharmaḥ sadā kāmamithyācārādviratiḥ | parastrī- [gamana]āpattito 'tijaghanyaṃ pāpaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Sexual misconduct' (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) — sexual conduct with a woman who is not one's wife, or [the wife of] that [other] being — that is sexual misconduct. Even with one's own wife, sexual conduct by an improper method is also called 'sexual misconduct.' All women have guardians — namely parents, brothers, the community (<s>gaṇa</s>), the husband, sons, daughters-in-law, and the like. For women who have gone forth (<s>pravrajita</s>), kings and the like are the guardians. (Question) A courtesan (<s>gaṇikā</s>) is not anyone's wife. How is sexual conduct with her not sexual misconduct? (Answer) [Even she] is under-age — as stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>: 'An under-age girl is [considered as] a wife, up to one who is separated by a single beard-hair.' (Question) If a certain woman who has no master comes of her own accord and requests 'May I be [your] wife' — how is this? (Answer) One who in reality has no master, who has come before a certain being according to <s>dharma</s> — [sexual conduct with her] is not sexual misconduct. (Question) For one who has gone forth (<s>pravrajita</s>), is there release from sexual misconduct by taking a wife? (Answer) There is no release. Why? Because that <s>dharma</s> does not exist. The <s>dharma</s> of one who has gone forth is always abstention from sexual misconduct. [Such a transgression] is an exceedingly grave sin — worse than the offense of [going with] another's wife.

body.text: mṛṣāvāda iti | yatkāyabāṅmanobhiḥ parasattvān vañcayitvā mṛṣā pratipādayati | ayaṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ | pāpasya gurutaratvādbhagavānāha bahūnāṃ paśnasamādhiḥ mṛṣāvādaḥ | yāvadekasmin puruṣe pṛcchatyapi mṛṣāvādaḥ | kimuta bahūnām iti | yo vañcayitumabhīṣṭaḥ,
body.translated_text: 'False speech' (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>) — that by which, through body, speech, and mind, one deceives other beings and causes them to accept what is false — this is false speech. Because the sin is heavier [when done to many], the Blessed One said: 'False speech [directed at] a congregation of many persons is [graver].' Even when asking a single person, it is false speech — how much more so when [addressing] many! One who intends to deceive —

body.text: tasmātpāpaṃ labhate | yadi kaścitparaṃ vadati ahamamukamīdṛśaṃ vadāmīti | tadvastuno 'tattve 'pi na mṛṣāvādaḥ | kiñca saṃjñāmanusṛtya mṛṣāvādaḥ | yaḥ paśyan na paśyati saṃjñām | sa pṛṣṭo vadati nādrākṣamiti | tasya nāsti mṛṣāvādapāpam | iti yathā varṇitaṃ vinaye |
body.translated_text: from that, one obtains sin. If someone says to another: 'I say such-and-such to so-and-so' — even if the content is not true, it is not false speech. Moreover, false speech is according to one's perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>). One who, while seeing, [generates] the perception of not seeing — when asked, says 'I did not see' — for him there is no sin of false speech. Thus it is as described in the <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi kaścidvastuviparyayāt adṛṣṭvā vadati adrākṣamiti tasya kathaṃ na mṛṣāvādaḥ | (u) sarvāṇi puṇyapāpāni cittādhīnāni utpadyante | sa puruṣo 'dṛṣṭavastuni dṛṣṭasaṃjñāmutpādayatītyato nāsti pāpam | yathā [yasya] tāttvikasattve nāsti sattvasaṃjñā | asattve ca sattvasaṃjñotpannā | sa na vadhapāpaṃ labhate | (pṛ) yathā vastusati sattva utpannasattvasaṃjño vadhapāpaṃ labhate | tathā yadi dṛṣṭe dṛṣṭasaṃjñāmutpādayati | tadā na pāpaṃ syāt | natvadṛṣṭe dṛṣṭasaṃjñāmutpādayan na pāpaṃ labhata iti | (u) pāpamidaṃ sattvopādānakacittamupādāyotpadyate | ataḥ sattve satyapi sattvasaṃjñāvihīno na labhate pāpam | [tādṛśa]cittābhāvāt | asati sattve sattvasaṃjñāvān [vastutaḥ] sattvasyābhāvādapi na pāpaṃ labhate | sati sattve sattvasaṃjñāvān prāṇātipātapāpaṃ labhata eva | hetupratyayānāṃ samagratvāt | yasya dṛṣṭe vastuni adṛṣṭasaṃjñotpadyate | sa pṛṣṭo vadati nādrākṣamiti | sa saṃjñāviparyayābhāvāt na sattvān vañcayati | vastuviparyaye 'pi satyamityevocyate | yasyādṛṣṭe vastuni dṛṣṭasaṃjñotpadyate | sa pṛṣṭo vadati nādrākṣamiti | sa saṃjñāviparyayāt sattvān vañcayati | vastvaviparyaye 'pi mṛṣāvāda ityucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) If someone, through a reversal of the object, not having seen, says 'I saw' — how is that not false speech? (Answer) All merit and demerit arise depending on mind. That person generates the perception of having seen with regard to an unseen object — therefore there is no sin. Just as one who, in regard to a real being, does not have the perception of a being, and in regard to a non-being has the perception of a being — he does not obtain the sin of killing. (Question) Just as, when there is a real being, one who has generated the perception of a being obtains the sin of killing — so too, if one generates the perception of having seen with regard to what was seen, then there would be no sin. But generating the perception of having seen with regard to what was not seen — one would not thereby be free from sin. (Answer) This sin arises depending on a mind that apprehends beings. Therefore, even when there is a being, one who is devoid of the perception of a being does not obtain sin — because of the absence of such a mind. When there is no being, one who has the perception of a being — because of the actual absence of the being — also does not obtain sin. When there is a being and one has the perception of a being, one indeed obtains the sin of taking life — because of the completeness of the causes and conditions. For one who has the perception of not having seen with regard to a seen object — when asked, he says 'I did not see.' Because there is no reversal of perception, he does not deceive beings. Even though there is a reversal of the object, it is [considered] truth. For one who has the perception of having seen with regard to an unseen object — when asked, he says 'I did not see.' Because of the reversal of perception, he deceives beings. Even though there is no reversal of the object, it is called 'false speech.'

body.text: paiśunyamiti | yat kaścitparavibhedayiṣayā vākkarma karoti | tatpaiśunyamityucyate | yasya nāsti sambhedabuddhiḥ | paraḥ śrutvā svayaṃ bhedayati | sa na pāpabhāgbhavati | yastu vinayakuśalabuddhayā durjanān sambhedayati | sa sambhede kṛte 'pi na pāpabhāgbhavati | yaḥ saṃyojanānuśayena kaluṣitacitto na bhavati | sa vācaṃ vadannapi na pāpabhāgbhavati |
body.translated_text: Slander (<s>paiśunya</s>): when someone performs verbal <s>karma</s> with the desire to cause division among others, that is called slander. One who does not have the intention of causing division — if another, having heard [his words], causes division on his own — he does not become a partaker of sin. But one who, with the intention of wise disciplinary skill, causes division among wicked persons — even if the division is accomplished, he does not become a partaker of sin. One whose mind is not corrupted by the latent tendencies of the fetters (<s>saṃyojanānuśaya</s>) — even though he speaks, he does not become a partaker of sin.

body.text: pāruṣyamiti | yat kaścitkaṭu vadati hitakarañca na bhavati parasyopāyāsamātramicchati | tatpāruṣyamityucyate | yastu karuṇācittena hitaṃ kurvan kaṭu vadati | na tasyāsti pāpam | yathā nirarthakaprayukta upāyāse pāpamasti | [cikitsārthaṃ] kasmiṃścitkāyadeśe sūcyā vedhanaṃ kaṭvapi na pāpaṃ bhavati | tathā kaṭuvacanamapi | buddhā āryā api kurvantī dam | yathā rūgṇādīnāmupadeśaḥ | yaḥ saṃyojanānuśayakaluṣitacitto na bhavati | tena kṛtaṃ kaṭuvacanaṃ na pāpamityucyate | yathā vītarāgādayaḥ | yaḥ kaluṣitacittena kaṭu vadati | sa kleśotpattikāla eva pāpaṃ labhate |
body.translated_text: Harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>): when someone speaks harshly and does not benefit [the other], desiring only to cause distress to others, that is called harsh speech. But one who, with a mind of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), speaks harshly while doing what is beneficial — for him there is no sin. Just as purposeless exertion in distress is sinful, [but] piercing a certain part of the body with a needle [for the purpose of] medical treatment, though harsh, is not sinful — so too with harsh speech. The <s>Buddhas</s> and Noble Ones (<s>ārya</s>) also do this — as in the instruction given to the sick and the like. One whose mind is not corrupted by the latent tendencies of the fetters — harsh speech done by him is said to be without sin, just as for those who are free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>) and the like. One who speaks harshly with a corrupted mind obtains sin at the very time of the arising of the defilement.

body.text: sambhinnapralāpa iti | yadanṛju asatyārthabhāṣaṇaṃ sa sambhinnapralāpaḥ | akāṇḍe satyavacanamapi
body.translated_text: Idle chatter (<s>sambhinnapralāpa</s>): whatever crooked and false speech is uttered, that is idle chatter. Even truthful speech spoken at an improper time

body.text: sambhinnapralāpaḥ | satyamapi kāle vipattyānulomyenāhitakaratvāt sambhinnapralāpa ityucyate | satyavacane 'pi kāle cāhite amūlamanarthamakramaṃ vacanaṃ sambhinnapralāpaḥ | mohādikleśavikṣiptacittatayā vacanaṃ sambhinnapralāpaḥ | kāyamanasoranārjavamapi sambhinnaṃ karma | kintu bhūyasā vākkṛtameva vyavahārataḥ sambhinnapralāpa ityucyate | anyāni trīṇi vākkarmāṇi sambhinnapralāpasaṃmiśrāṇi bhavanti na vivekabhāgīni | yadi mṛṣāvādaḥ kaṭuvacanāñcāviviktam | tadā dvidhā bhavati mṛṣāvādaḥ sambhinnapralāpa iti | yadi mṛṣāvādo 'pi saṃbibhedayiṣayā akaṭuvacanaḥ | tadā tridhā bhavati mṛṣāvādaḥ paiśunyaṃ sambhinnapralāpa iti | yadi mṛṣāvādaḥ kaṭuvacanaḥ sambibhitsā ca | tadā caturdhā bhavati | yadi nāsti mṛṣāvādaḥ | kaṭuvacanamapi aviviktaṃ kevalamakāṇḍavacanamahitavacanamanarthavacanam | tadā sambhinnapralāpamātram | ayaṃ sambhinnapralāpo 'pi sūkṣmo dustyajaḥ | kevalaṃ buddhā eva tadindriyaṃ samucchedayanti | ato buddhā eva bhagavadvādaprasādhane śraddheyāḥ nānye |
body.translated_text: is idle chatter. Even truthful speech, when spoken at a time that conduces to misfortune, because it causes harm, is called idle chatter. Even in truthful speech, words that are baseless, purposeless, and disordered at the proper time are idle chatter. Speech uttered with a mind distracted by delusion and other defilements is idle chatter. Non-straightforwardness of body and mind too is discordant <s>karma</s>. However, because it is predominantly done through speech, it is conventionally called 'idle chatter.' The other three verbal <s>karmas</s> are mixed with idle chatter and are not separable. If false speech is inseparable from harsh speech, then it becomes twofold: false speech and idle chatter. If false speech is also [spoken] with the desire to cause division but without harsh words, then it becomes threefold: false speech, slander, and idle chatter. If false speech is harsh and also [spoken] with the desire to divide, then it becomes fourfold. If there is no false speech, and harsh speech too is inseparable — merely untimely speech, harmful speech, and purposeless speech — then it is merely idle chatter. This idle chatter too is subtle and difficult to abandon. Only the <s>Buddhas</s> alone completely eradicate that faculty. Therefore, only the <s>Buddhas</s> alone are to be trusted in establishing the speech of the Blessed One, and no others.

body.text: (pṛ) uktāḥ saptavidhāḥ karmapathāḥ | ka upayogaḥ punastrividhamānasakarmakathanena | (u) kecidvadanti- puṇyaṃ pāpamavaśyaṃ kāyavāgadhīnaṃ na cittamātrāt iti | ato vadanti cittamapi karmapathaḥ | trividhasyāsya mānasakarmaṇo balādutpadyate kāyikaṃ vācikamakuśalakarma iti | idaṃ trividhaṃ yadyapi gurutaram | mānasakarmaṇaḥ sūkṣmatvāt iti paścādvakṣyate | sarveṣāṃ leśānāmakuśalakarmotpādakatve 'pi idaṃ trividhaṃ paraṃ sattvānāmupāyāsakaratvādakuśalakarmapatha ityucyate | yadi rāgo madhyamo 'varo vā na sa karmapatho bhavati | rāgo 'yamadhimātraḥ paramadhirajya saṃpīḍecchayā sopāyaḥ kāyikavācikakarmotpādakatvāt rāgerṣyā karmapatho bhavati | pratighamohāvapi tathā | yadi moha eva sarvakleśātmaka ucyata iti matam | tasyaiva kāyavāgbhyāṃ sattvānāmupadravotpādakatvāt traividhyamucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) The seven courses of action (<s>karmapatha</s>) have been stated. What then is the purpose of stating the threefold mental <s>karma</s>? (Answer) Some say: 'Merit and sin necessarily depend on body and speech, not on mind alone.' Therefore they say that mind too is a course of action. Through the power of this threefold mental <s>karma</s>, unwholesome bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> arises. Although this threefold [mental karma] is more grave — because of the subtlety of mental <s>karma</s>, this will be explained later. Although all defilements produce unwholesome <s>karma</s>, this threefold [mental karma], because it predominantly causes distress to beings, is called an unwholesome course of action. If passion (<s>rāga</s>) is middling or inferior, it does not become a course of action. When this passion is intense, supremely dominant, and accompanied by the desire to oppress — because it produces bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>, passion-jealousy (<s>rāgerṣyā</s>) becomes a course of action. Aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) and delusion (<s>moha</s>) are likewise. If one holds the view that delusion alone is the nature of all defilements, then because it alone produces harm to beings through body and speech, its threefoldness is stated.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmānmoho mithyādṛṣṭirbhavati | (u) asti [sa]mohaviśeṣaḥ | kasmāt | na hi sarvo moho 'kuśalaḥ | yo moho mithyādṛṣṭipravṛttāvadhipatiḥ so 'kuśalaḥ karmapathaḥ | sarvāṇyakuśalāni etattrimukhādhīnāni bhavanti | yadi [vā] kaściddhanalābhāyākuśalaṃ karma karoti tadyathā suvarṇakārṣāpaṇāya prāṇinaṃ hanti | dveṣeṇa vā [akuśalaṃ karma karoti] tadyathā amitraṃ coraṃ vā hanti | atha vā na dhanalābhāya na dveṣeṇa, api tu mohabalenaiva parāparāvijñānāt prāṇinaṃ hanti | (pṛ) catvāro durgatipratyayāḥ sūtra uktā
body.translated_text: (Question) Why does delusion become wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>)? (Answer) There is a particular kind of delusion. Why? Because not all delusion is unwholesome.
