That delusion which is dominant in the operation of wrong view — that is the unwholesome course of action. All unwholesome [actions] are dependent on these three gateways. Or if someone commits unwholesome <s>karma</s> for the sake of material gain — for example, one who kills a living being for the sake of gold coins. Or [one commits unwholesome karma] through hatred — for example, one who kills an enemy or a thief. Or else, not for the sake of material gain nor through hatred, but through the power of delusion alone, not discriminating between right and wrong, one kills a living being. (Question) Four causes of the lower destinies are stated in the <s>sūtra</s>

body.text: rāgato dveṣato bhayato mohataśca durgatiṣu patantīti | idānīmatra kasmānnoktaṃ bhayato 'kuśalaṃ karmotpadyata iti | (u) bhayaṃ mohasaṅgṛhītam | yaducyate bhayata iti tanmohata eva bhavati | kasmāt | na jñānī yāvadāyurvināśapratyayamapi akuśalaṃ karma karoti | idañca pūrvaṃ pratyuktameva |
body.translated_text: : 'Through passion, through hatred, through fear, and through delusion, beings fall into the lower destinies.' Now, why is it not stated here that unwholesome <s>karma</s> arises from fear? (Answer) Fear is included in delusion. What is called 'from fear' is itself from delusion. Why? Because one who possesses knowledge does not commit unwholesome <s>karma</s> even when faced with the destruction of life. And this has already been answered previously.

body.text: yat kleśavivṛddhiḥ kāyikavācikarmotpādayati sa kālo 'kuśalakarmapatha ityucyate | asya trividhasya bhūyasā akuśalotpādakatvāt | (pṛ) kasmātkarmapatha ityucyate | (u) mana eva karma | tatra caratīti karmapatha ityucyate | antimatritaye pūrvaṃ carati | ādyasaptake paścāccarati | trīṇi karmapathāḥ na karma | sapta karmāṇi karma ca panthāśca | (pṛ) kaśātāḍanasurāpānādīnyakuśalakarmāṇyuktāni | kasmāddaśaivoktāni | (u) gurutarapāpatvādimāni daśoktāni | kaśātāḍanādīni sarvāṇi tatparivārāḥ paurvāparikāḥ | na surāpānaṃ prakṛtisāvadyam | nāpi paropadravakṛta | paropadravakṛditi svīkāre 'pi na surāpānaṃ tadbhavati |
body.translated_text: When the intensification of defilements produces bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>, that time is called an unwholesome course of action — because of the predominant production of the unwholesome by this threefold [mental karma]. (Question) Why is it called a 'course of action' (<s>karmapatha</s>)? (Answer) Mind itself is <s>karma</s>. It moves therein — therefore it is called a 'course of action.' In the last three [mental karmas], [mind] moves first. In the first seven [bodily and verbal karmas], it moves afterward. The three [mental karmas] are courses of action but not <s>karma</s>. The seven [bodily and verbal karmas] are both <s>karma</s> and courses. (Question) Unwholesome <s>karmas</s> such as beating with a whip, drinking intoxicants, and the like are stated. Why are only ten stated? (Answer) Because these ten are of graver sin, they are stated. Beating with a whip and the like are all their attendants, prior and subsequent. The drinking of intoxicants is not wrong by its own nature (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>). Nor is it done for the purpose of harming others. Even if one accepts that it causes harm to others, the drinking of intoxicants is not itself that [harm].

body.text: (pṛ) akuśalakarmapathā ime kutra vartante | (u) sarvatra pañcagatiṣu vartante | uttarakuruṣu kevalaṃ na santi | mithyākāmacārastribhirvastubhirutthāpitaḥ kāmarāgeṇa saṃsiddhaḥ | anye tribhirvastubhirutthāpitaḥ tribhirvastubhiḥ saṃsiddhaḥ | (pṛ) āryāḥ kimakuśalaṃ karma kuvanti na vā | (u) mānasākuśalakarmotpattāvapi na kāyikavācikakarmotpādayanti | mānasakarmaṇyapi dveṣacittamātramutpādayanti na vadhacittam | (pṛ) sūtra uktam- śaikṣā anyān śapamānā āhuḥ samucchinnavṛṣaṇo bhava iti | tatkatham | (u) [anyat] kiñcitsūtramāha- arhan śapata iti | ayaṃ kṣīṇāsrava puruṣaḥ prahīṇakleśamūlaḥ cittameva notpādayati | kiṃ puna śapeta iti | śaikṣasya śāpavacanamapi tathaiva syāt | āryā akuśalakarmasu avijñaptisaṃvaraṃ labhanta | kathaṃ kuryurakuśalam | na ca te durgatau patanti | yadyakuśalamutpādayanti | pateyurapi | yadyāryā ihādhvani akuśalaṃ karma kṛtvā durgatau na patanti | atītādhvani akuśalakarmavanta iti kasmānna patanti | (u) āryāṇāṃ manasi tattvajñāne samutpanne sarve 'kuśalakarmapathā mandā bhavanti yathā dagdhaṃ bījaṃ na punaḥ prarohati |
body.translated_text: (Question) Where do these unwholesome courses of action exist? (Answer) They exist in all five destinies. Only in <s>Uttarakuru</s> they do not exist. Sexual misconduct is produced by three factors and accomplished by sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>). The others are produced by three factors and accomplished by three factors. (Question) Do Noble Ones (<s>ārya</s>) commit unwholesome <s>karma</s> or not? (Answer) Even in the arising of mental unwholesome <s>karma</s>, they do not produce bodily or verbal <s>karma</s>. Even in mental <s>karma</s>, they produce only a mind of aversion, not a mind intent on killing. (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Trainees (<s>śaikṣa</s>), while cursing others, say: "May you be one whose testicles are cut off." ' How is this [to be understood]? (Answer) Another <s>sūtra</s> says: 'An <s>Arhat</s> curses.' This person whose outflows are destroyed (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>), whose roots of defilement are abandoned — he does not even produce such a mind. How much less would he curse? The cursing speech of a trainee too should be [understood] in the same way. Noble Ones obtain the non-manifest restraint (<s>avijñaptisaṃvara</s>) with respect to unwholesome <s>karmas</s>. How would they commit the unwholesome? And they do not fall into the lower destinies. If they were to produce the unwholesome, they would also fall. If Noble Ones in this present life, having done unwholesome <s>karma</s>, do not fall into the lower destinies — then why do they not fall because of unwholesome <s>karma</s> from past lives? (Answer) When the knowledge of reality has arisen in the minds of the Noble Ones, all unwholesome courses of action become weak — just as a burnt seed does not sprout again.

body.text: trīṇi ca viṣāṇi dvividhāni- durgatiprāpakāṇi tadaprāpakāṇīti | yāni durgatiprāpakāṇi tāni āryāṇāṃ prakṣīṇāni | karmakleśābhyāṃ hi śarīramupādīyate | āryāḥ karmayuktā api kleśavikalatvānna patanti | kiñca te ratnatrayākhyamahāsthānabalamavaṣṭabhya mahadakuśalaṃ kṣapayanti | yathā kaścidrājāśrita uttamarṇena na pīḍyate | te ca tīkṣṇaprajñāvidyā akuśalaṃ karma kṣapayanti | yathā kaścitkāye 'gniśaktivivṛddhyā duṣparipācaṃ paripācayati | teṣāṃ santi bahava upāyāḥ | kadācid buddhān smṛtvā kadācitkaruṇāṃ smṛtvā kuśalakarmahetubhi[rvā] akuśalebhyo vimuktiṃ labhante | yathā coro vahvalīkairaraṇyadurgamāśritya nopalabhyate | āryā ime jñānena vimuktimārgaṃ labhante | yathā gauḥ svāminaṃ yāti | vihaga ākāśaṃ niśrayate | dīrgharātraṃ kuśaladharmāṇāmabhyāsānna durgatau patanti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo nityaṃ kāyena śīlaṃ cittena prajñāmabhyasyati sa narakavedanīyaṃ karmābhimukhībhūya laghu vedayate iti | yathā cāha gāthā-
body.translated_text: And the three poisons are of two kinds: those that lead to the lower destinies and those that do not lead there. Those that lead to the lower destinies are exhausted in the Noble Ones. For a body is taken up through <s>karma</s> and defilements. The Noble Ones, even though possessing <s>karma</s>, do not fall because of the deficiency of defilements. Moreover, relying upon the great power of the Three Jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>), they destroy great unwholesome [karma] — just as someone who has taken refuge with a king is not oppressed by a creditor. They, possessing sharp wisdom-knowledge, destroy unwholesome <s>karma</s> — just as someone, through the increase of the power of fire in the body, digests what is difficult to digest. They have many means. Sometimes by recollecting the <s>Buddhas</s>, sometimes by recollecting compassion, through causes of wholesome <s>karma</s>, they obtain liberation from the unwholesome — just as a thief, relying on many allies and the inaccessible wilderness, is not caught. The Noble Ones obtain the path of liberation through knowledge — just as a cow goes to its master, just as a bird takes refuge in the sky. Through long practice of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, they do not fall into the lower destinies. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who constantly practices moral conduct with the body and wisdom with the mind — having confronted <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in hell, he experiences it lightly.' And as the verse says:

body.text:
carantaṃ karuṇācitte 'pramāṇe 'nirāvṛte |
gurukarmāṇi sarvāṇi na kiñcidupayanti ca || iti |
body.translated_text:
One who abides in compassionate mind, immeasurable, unobstructed —
all grave <s>karmas</s> do not at all approach him.

body.text: āryāṇāmeṣāñcitte 'kuśalaṃ karma na sthirībhavati | santaptāyasi patitaikajalabinduvat | āryāṇāṃ kuśalaṃ karma sudūragāmi khadira vṛkṣamūlavat | āryāśceme bahukuśalā alpākuśalāḥ | alpamakuśalaṃ bahukuśaleṣu vartamānaṃ na balavat yathā gaṅgāyāṃ kṣiptamekapalalavaṇaṃ na vikārayati tadrasam | āryāste puṇyaśraddhādinā dhanikāḥ | yathā daridra ekakarṣāpaṇāya pāpaṃ svīkaroti | na [tathā]dhanikaḥ śatasahasrebhyo 'pi pāpaṃ prāpnoti | āryamārgapraveśābdahumatā bhavanti | yathāryāḥ satyapi pāpe na narakaṃ praviśanti | yathā vyāghraśārdūlajāśvavarāhānāṃ(ṇāṃ) saha vivadamānānāṃ baliṣṭho jayaṃ labhate | āryāṇāmeṣāṃ cittāmāryamārgoṣitam | durgatikapāpāni na punarupāyāsayanti | yathā rājādhyuṣita ekāntagṛhe nānye praviśanti | āryāḥ svavihṛtisthānavihāriṇaḥ | na [teṣu] durgatikapāpakarmāṇyavakāśaṃ labhante | tadyathā gṛdhro vā kaṅka iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ | kiñcāryāścatusmṛtyupasthāneṣu cittaṃ pratibadhnanti | ato durgatikakarmāṇi nāvakāśaṃ labhante | śākhāniveśitavṛttaghaṭavat | dvividhasaṃyojanasamanvāgamāddhi durgatau patito yathākarma vipākaṃ vedayate | āryāstu eka [saṃyojana]prahāṇānna durgatau patanti | te sadā kuśalakarmavipākaṃ samādadata ityato
body.translated_text: In the minds of these Noble Ones, unwholesome <s>karma</s> does not become firm — like a single drop of water fallen upon heated iron. The wholesome <s>karma</s> of the Noble Ones reaches far — like the root of a <s>khadira</s> tree. These Noble Ones have much wholesome and little unwholesome [karma]. A small amount of unwholesome [karma] existing among much wholesome [karma] has no power — just as a single lump of salt thrown into the <s>Gaṅgā</s> does not alter its taste. The Noble Ones are wealthy through merit, faith, and the like. Just as a poor person accepts sin for the sake of a single coin, but a wealthy person does not incur sin even for the sake of a hundred thousand. Through entrance upon the Noble Path, beings become weighty. Just as Noble Ones, even though possessing sin, do not enter hell — like among tigers, leopards, fine horses, boars, and the like, when they quarrel together, the strongest one obtains victory. In the minds of these Noble Ones, the Noble Path is well-established. Sins leading to the lower destinies do not cause them distress again — just as when a place is occupied by a king, others do not enter that secluded dwelling. The Noble Ones abide in the abode of their own spiritual practice. Sinful <s>karmas</s> leading to the lower destinies do not find opportunity [in them] — like a vulture or a <s>kaṅka</s> bird, as the analogy goes. Moreover, the Noble Ones bind their minds to the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>catusmṛtyupasthāna</s>). Therefore, <s>karmas</s> leading to the lower destinies do not find opportunity — like a round pot placed upon branches. For through the accompaniment of the twofold fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), one falls into the lower destinies and experiences ripening according to <s>karma</s>. But the Noble Ones, through the abandonment of one [kind of] fetter, do not fall into the lower destinies. They always accumulate the ripening of wholesome <s>karma</s> — therefore

body.text: durgatikakarmāṇi nāvakāśaṃ labhante | yathā pūrvaṃ ṣaṭkarmavarge pratipāditaṃ naraka[vedanīyaṃ] karmalakṣaṇam | [tādṛśa]kāraṇābhāvādāryā na durgatau patanti ||
body.translated_text: <s>karmas</s> leading to the lower destinies do not find opportunity. As was previously established in the Chapter on the Six Kinds of <s>Karma</s>, the characteristics of <s>karma</s> whose ripening is to be experienced in hell [were explained]. Because of the absence of such causes, Noble Ones do not fall into the lower destinies.

body.text: daśākuśalakarmapathavargaḥ ṣoḍaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and sixteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Ten Unwholesome Courses of Action (<s>daśākuśalakarmapathavarga</s>).

body.text: 117 daśakuśalakarmapathavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 117. Chapter on the Ten Wholesome Courses of Action (<s>daśakuśalakarmapathavarga</s>)

body.text: daśakuśalakarmapathā yaduta prāṇātipātaviratiḥ yāvatsamyakdṛṣṭiḥ | ime daśaśīlasaṃvarasaṅgṛhītā aikakālikāḥ | dhyānamarūpasaṃvarasaṅgṛhītamapi aikakālikam | viratirnāma karmapathaḥ | sāvijñaptireva | (pṛ) vandanādīni puṇyāni anye karmapathāḥ santi | kasmādviratimātraṃ karmapatha ityucyate | (u) viratiprādhānyāt | imāni daśa karmāṇi dānādibhya utkṛṣṭāni | kasmāt | dānādinā labdhaḥ puṇyavipāko na śīladhāraṇasya [tulā]marhati | yathā daśavārṣikaḥ pumān prāṇātipātaviratipratyayamāyurvardhayati | daśākuśalakarmaṇāṃ pāpatvāt tadviratiḥ prakṛtitaḥ puṇyam | antimāni trīṇi kuśalakarmāṇi kuśalakarmāṇāṃ mūlam | tasmāddānādīni kuśalāni karmapathasaṅgṛhītāni | asmin karmapathe 'sti paurvāparyeṇopanidhyoktakaśātāḍanādiviratiḥ | ataḥ sarvāṇi kuśalāni atra saṅgṛhītāni ||
body.translated_text: The ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśakuśalakarmapatha</s>) are: abstention from taking life (<s>prāṇātipātavirati</s>) up to right view (<s>samyakdṛṣṭi</s>). These ten are included in the moral restraint of <s>śīla</s> (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>) and are simultaneous. <s>Dhyāna</s>, being included in the formless restraint (<s>arūpasaṃvara</s>), is also simultaneous. Abstention (<s>virati</s>) is the [wholesome] course of action. That is <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action) itself. (Question) Meritorious acts such as veneration and the like are other courses of action. Why is abstention alone called 'course of action'? (Answer) Because of the predominance of abstention. These ten <s>karmas</s> are superior to giving and the like. Why? The meritorious ripening obtained through giving and the like does not equal the upholding of moral conduct (<s>śīladhāraṇa</s>). Just as a ten-year-old man, through the condition of abstaining from taking life, increases his lifespan. Because the ten unwholesome <s>karmas</s> are sinful, abstention from them is naturally (<s>prakṛtitas</s>) meritorious. The last three wholesome <s>karmas</s> are the root of wholesome <s>karmas</s>. Therefore wholesome [actions] such as giving and the rest are included in the [ten] courses of action. In these courses of action, there is in sequence abstention from reviling, beating with a whip, striking, and the like. Therefore all wholesome [actions] are included herein.

body.text: daśakuśalakarmapathavargaḥ saptadaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and seventeenth chapter, the Chapter on the Ten Wholesome Courses of Action (<s>daśakuśalakarmapathavarga</s>).

body.text: 118 ādīnavavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 118. Chapter on the Danger [of Unwholesome Karma] (<s>ādīnavavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) akuśalakarmaṇāṃ kimādīnavam | (u) akuśalakarmabhirnarakādiduḥkhaṃ vedayate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- prāṇātipātapratyayaṃ narake patati | yadi manuṣyeṣūtpadyate | alpāyu rvindate | yāvadevaṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ | akuśakarmapratyayaṃ ciraṃ duḥkhamanubhavati | yathāvīcinarake 'pramāṇavarṣāṇyativāhayan nāyuḥ kṣapayati iti | sattvānāṃ vidyamānāḥ sarvā akuśalaparābhavahānipīḍā akuśalaiḥ [karmabhi]reva bhavanti | adṛṣṭākuśalakarmaṇāṃ mahopakāro 'sti | yathā sainikavyādhādayo nānena karmaṇā bahumānaṃ labhante | coravadhapratyayaṃ dhanabhānaṃ labhata iti yat bhavata āśayaḥ | tadidaṃ pūrvameva trikarmavarge pratyuktam | akuśalacārī garhānirbhatsanādīni
body.translated_text: (Question) What is the danger (<s>ādīnava</s>) of unwholesome <s>karmas</s>? (Answer) Through unwholesome <s>karmas</s>, one experiences the suffering of hell and the like. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Through the condition of taking life, one falls into hell. If one is reborn among humans, one obtains a short lifespan.' And so forth up to wrong view. Through the condition of unwholesome <s>karma</s>, one experiences suffering for a long time. Just as in the <s>Avīci</s> hell, one passes immeasurable years without exhausting one's lifespan. All the defeats, losses, and afflictions that befall sentient beings come about through unwholesome <s>karmas</s> alone. (Question) There is great benefit in unseen unwholesome <s>karma</s>. Just as soldiers, hunters, and the like — they gain respect through this <s>karma</s>. Your view is that 'through the condition of killing a thief, one obtains wealth and honor.' (Answer) That has already been refuted in the Chapter on the Three Karmas. One who practices the unwholesome encounters reproach, censure, and the like

body.text: duḥkhopāyāsāṅgāni vindate | pareṣāmaniṣṭaprāpakaṃ krūramityata ebhyo 'kuśalakarmabhyo viramitavyam | uktañca sūtre- prāṇātipātasya pañcāvadyāniḥ- (1) janānāmaśraddheyatā, (2) duryaśaḥprāptiḥ, (3) kuśalādviprakṛṣyākuśalapratyāsattiḥ, (4) maraṇakāle cittavipratisāraḥ, (5) ante durgatipatanam iti | prāṇātipātapratyayamalpasukhaṃ bahudduḥkhaṃ bhavati | akuśalakarmācaraṇaṃ puruṣacittaṃ saṃkleśayati | adhvanyadhvani samupacitasamudayaściraṃ duścikitso bhavati | akuśalacārī tamasastamaḥ praviṣṭaḥ pravṛttimārgatritayānna niryāṇaṃ labhate | akuśalacārī manuṣyadehopādānaṃ vṛthākaroti | yathoṣadhinicitāt himagirerviṣatṛṇasya samāhartātimūḍho bhavati | evaṃ daśakuśalakarmapathairmanuṣyadehaṃ labhate | kuśalamanācaran kevalaṃ mahatīṃ hānimeva karoti | kiṃ punarakuśalakarmasamādāne | kiñcākuśalacārī svakāyaṃ kāmayannapi na vastutaḥ svātmānaṃ kāmayate | svātmānaṃ rakṣannapi nātmānaṃ rakṣati | ātmapīḍākarakarmapratyayatvāt | puruṣo 'yaṃ kāyasaṅgataḥ tadyathāmitracoreṇa [saṅgataḥ] svātmana eva duḥkhakārakatvāt | yo 'kuśalamācarati | sa svayameva tatkāyaṃ corayati | kiṃ punaḥ paraḥ | akuśalakarmacaryā yadyapīdānīṃ nābhivyajyate vipāke tu adhyavasīyate | tasmādalpīyasyapi aśraddhā na kartavyā | yathālpīyo 'pi viṣaṃ puruṣaṃ hanti | yathā vā ṛṇamalpamapi krameṇa vṛddhyā vardhate | parasya kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ paraḥ sadā na vismarati | ataḥ kṛtaṃ ciraviprakṛṣṭamapi na śraddhātavyam | akuśalacārī na sukhe ramate | akuśalācaraṇāddevamanuṣyasukhādbhraśyati | asukharato mūḍhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ | akuśalacāriṇo duḥkhaṃ gāḍhaśocanīyaṃ bhavati | vipratisārādiduḥkhaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vedayate | ante tu durgatiduḥkhaṃ vedayate | akuśalakarmaphalāt vihāyasā gatvā samudre nimajyāpi na vimuktisthānaṃ labhate | yathā suvarṇatomaro buddhamanvadhāvat | sarvamakuśalaṃ mohotthitam | ato vidvān nānusmaret | uktañca sūtre- pramādaḥ śatruvatkuśaladharmān hanti iti | ato nānusmaret | kiñcākuśalaṃ karma buddhabodhisattvairarhadbhirāryaiḥ pañcabhijñairmaharṣibhiḥ puṇyapāpavedibhiravigītaṃ na bhavati | ato na kurvīta | paśyāmaḥ khalu pratyakṣamakuśalacittavaipulya eva bhāvavyāmohavikṣepopāyāsādhiduḥkhairvikṛtamukhavarṇaḥ pumānaprīto dṛśyata iti | kiṃ punaḥ kāyikavācikakarmotpādane | ebhiḥ pratyayairjñāyate akuśalānāmapramāṇānyavadyāni santīti ||
body.translated_text: — components of suffering and distress. Because it is cruel, causing others to obtain what is undesirable — therefore one should abstain from these unwholesome <s>karmas</s>. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Taking life has five faults: (1) untrustworthy in the eyes of people, (2) attaining a bad reputation, (3) being drawn away from the wholesome and approaching the unwholesome, (4) mental remorse at the time of death, (5) falling into a bad destination at the end.' Through the condition of taking life, there is little pleasure and much suffering. The practice of unwholesome <s>karma</s> defiles a person's mind. That which is accumulated over life after life becomes a long-standing disease difficult to cure. One who practices the unwholesome, having entered from darkness into darkness, does not find an exit from the triple path of [saṃsāric] engagement. One who practices the unwholesome makes the acquisition of a human body in vain. Just as from the <s>Himālaya</s> mountain filled with medicinal herbs, one who gathers poisonous grass is extremely deluded. In the same way, through the ten wholesome courses of action one obtains a human body. Not practicing the wholesome, one merely brings about great loss — how much more so when undertaking unwholesome <s>karma</s>! Furthermore, one who practices the unwholesome, even though he desires his own body, does not in reality desire his own self. Even though he protects his own self, he does not [truly] protect himself — because of being a condition for <s>karma</s> that causes self-affliction. This person is associated with the body just as one associated with an enemy-thief, because of being the cause of suffering to oneself. One who practices the unwholesome himself steals from that very body — how much more so from another? The practice of unwholesome <s>karma</s>, even though not manifest now, is determined at the time of ripening. Therefore, even the slightest faithlessness should not be entertained. Just as even a small amount of poison kills a person. Or just as even a small debt gradually increases through interest. Sin done against another — the other never forgets it. Therefore, even something done long ago should not be trusted. One who practices the unwholesome does not enjoy happiness. Through practicing the unwholesome, one falls away from the happiness of gods and humans. The foolish one who does not delight in happiness is pre-eminent [among fools]. The suffering of one who practices the unwholesome is deeply lamentable. He directly experiences the suffering of remorse and the like. And at the end, he experiences the suffering of a bad destination. Even going through the sky, one who bears the fruit of unwholesome <s>karma</s> cannot find a place of liberation even upon plunging into the ocean. Just as the golden spear pursued the <s>Buddha</s>. All unwholesome [action] arises from delusion (<s>moha</s>). Therefore the wise person should not recollect it. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), like an enemy, destroys wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' Therefore one should not recollect it. Furthermore, unwholesome <s>karma</s> is not unnoticed by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Noble Ones, and great seers possessed of the five superknowledges who know merit and sin. Therefore one should not commit it. We directly see indeed that when the unwholesome mind expands, a person, with distorted facial complexion, afflicted by delusion, confusion, distraction, distress, and extreme suffering, appears displeased. How much more so when bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> is produced? Through these reasons it is known that the faults of unwholesome [actions] are immeasurable.

body.text: ādīnavargo 'ṣṭādaśottaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and eighteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Danger [of Unwholesome Karma] (<s>ādīnavavarga</s>).

body.text: 119 trikarmagauravalāghavavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 119. Chapter on the Gravity and Lightness of the Three Karmas (<s>trikarmagauravalāghavavarga</s>)

body.text: triṣu karmasu kiṃ gurutaraṃ- kiṃ kāyikaṃ karma, vācikaṃ karma kiṃ vā mānasaṃ karma | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- kāyikaṃ vācikañca karma gurutaram | na mānasaṃ karmeti | kasmāt | kāyikavācikakarmaṇorniyamena satyatvāt | yathā pañcānantaryāṇi kāyaṃ vācañcopādāya kriyante | kāyo vāk ca karma niṣpādayati | yathā kaścidimaṃ sattvaṃ hanmīti cittamutpādya kāyavāgbhyāṃ tatkarma sādhayati | na mānasakarmamātreṇa prāṇivadhapāpaṃ vindate | nāpi cittotpādamātreṇa caityanirmāṇabrāhmapuṇyaṃ vindate | kāyavacasyasati mānasikakarmamātrasya na vipāko 'sti | yathā kaściccittamutpādayati dānaṃ dāsyāmīti | na tu prayacchati | na tasyāsti dānapuṇyam | nāpi praṇidhānamātreṇa vastu pariniṣpadyate | yathā kaścitsaṅghasya mahādānaṃ karomīti praṇidadhāti | na tu dadāti | tasya nāsti saṅghadānapuṇyam | mānasaṃ karma mahattaramiti cet [tadā] dānapuṇyaṃ labheta | tathā ca karmavipākaḥ vyāmohaḥ syāt | vinaye ca nāsti mānasyāpattiḥ | yadi mānasaṃ karma mahattaram | kasmānnāstyāpattiḥ | yadi cittamutpādayituḥ puṇyaṃ labhyata iti | tadā puṇyaṃ sulabhaṃ syāt | ācaritā kasmāt sulabhamidaṃ karma tyaktvā durācaraṇaṃ dānādikarma kuryāt | tathā cedakṣīṇapuṇyaḥ syāt | yathā kaścid vṛthā cittamātramutpādayati | nātyantaṃ vyāpriyate | [tadā] kasya kṣayaḥ | dhanaṃ parimitamityataḥ puṇya[mapi] kṣīyate | na cittotpādamātraṃ parasyopakaroti | apakaroti vā | yathā tarṣito bubhukṣitaḥ sattvaḥ pānamāhāramabhilaṣati | na mānasakarmaṇā vāryate | laukikānāṃ hānilābhāvatimātrau | cittaṃ laghu calaṃ durdamamityato 'kuśalākaraṇaṃ na kiñcit | tadā gurvī hāniṃ vinderan | ye puṇyacikīrṣayā kuśalacittamutpādayanti | te mahālābhamevāpnuyuḥ | idantu atyantaṃ duṣṭam | yadi mānasaṃ karma mahattaram, prāṇātipātacikīrṣācittamutpādayan narake patet | evaṃ ciropacitenāpi śīlādinā kimupakṛtaṃ syāt | śīlādikuśalācārāṇāṃ guṇā avyavasthitā bhaveyuḥ | kasmāt | ekacittotpādamātreṇa pāpalābhāt | uktañca sūtre- kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karma audārikam | ataḥ pūrvaṃ prajahyāt | audārikakleśaprahāṇāccittaṃ samādhīyata iti | yo 'brahmacaryacittamutpādayati | tasya maithunaṃ kṛtamiti śīlaṃ vipadyeta | yaścittotpādaḥ na tanmaithunam | etanmaithunacittavyatiriktaḥ ko dharmo maithunamityucyate | utpadyamānaṃ vijñaptikarma sarvaṃ kāyavacasā bhavati na mānasakarmaṇā | yathā parapuruṣanindā avaśyaṃ vākkarmādhīnā mṛṣāvādapāpaṃ gamayati | yatpūrvamuktaṃ caturbhiḥ pratyayaiḥ
body.translated_text: Among the three <s>karmas</s>, which is the most grave — bodily <s>karma</s>, verbal <s>karma</s>, or mental <s>karma</s>? (Question) Some say: 'Bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> is the most grave, not mental <s>karma</s>.' Why? Because bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> necessarily has reality. Just as the five heinous crimes (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) are committed through body and speech. Body and speech accomplish <s>karma</s>. Just as someone generates the thought 'I will kill this being' and accomplishes that <s>karma</s> through body and speech. One does not obtain the sin of killing merely through mental <s>karma</s>. Nor does one obtain the merit of constructing a <s>caitya</s> or the merit of the holy life (<s>brahmapuṇya</s>) merely through the production of a thought. When body and speech are absent, mental <s>karma</s> alone does not have ripening. Just as someone generates the thought 'I will give a gift' but does not give — he does not have the merit of giving. Nor is something accomplished merely through aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). Just as someone resolves 'I will make a great offering to the <s>Saṅgha</s>' but does not give — he does not have the merit of giving to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. If mental <s>karma</s> were the most grave, he would obtain the merit of giving. And then the ripening of <s>karma</s> would be confused. And in the <s>Vinaya</s>, there is no mental offense (<s>mānasyāpatti</s>). If mental <s>karma</s> were the most grave, why would there be no offense? If one who generates a thought obtains merit, then merit would be easy [to obtain]. Why would the practitioner, abandoning this easily accomplished <s>karma</s>, perform the difficult practice of giving and the like? If so, merit would be inexhaustible. Just as someone pointlessly generates mere thoughts — since there is never any exhaustion, whose exhaustion would there be? Wealth is limited — therefore merit too is exhausted. Mere thought-production does not benefit another, nor does it harm. Just as a thirsty and hungry being craves drink and food — it is not averted by mental <s>karma</s>. In the world, there are only two extremes: loss and gain. The mind is light, fickle, and difficult to tame — therefore its non-doing of the unwholesome amounts to nothing. Then they would encounter grave loss. Those who generate a wholesome mind with the desire to do merit would attain only great gain. But this is extremely wrong. If mental <s>karma</s> is the most grave, then one who generates a thought desiring to take life would fall into hell. If so, what benefit would there be even from moral conduct and the like long accumulated? The qualities of practicing wholesome conduct such as moral conduct and the like would become unstable. Why? Because of obtaining sin merely through the production of a single thought. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> is gross. Therefore one should first abandon it. Through the abandoning of gross defilements, the mind becomes concentrated.' One who generates a thought of unchastity — his moral conduct would be ruined as having committed sexual intercourse. But the generation of that thought is not that act of sexual intercourse. What <s>dharma</s> other than the thought of sexual intercourse is called 'sexual intercourse'? All manifest <s>karma</s> (<s>vijñaptikarma</s>) that arises is of body and speech, not of mental <s>karma</s>. Just as the censure of another person necessarily depends on verbal <s>karma</s>, leading to the sin of false speech. As was previously stated, through four conditions

body.text: prāṇātipātapāpaṃ labhate yaduta sattvasattā, sattvasattājñānaṃ, jighatsācittaṃ tajjīvitoccheda iti caturbhirvastubhiḥ pāpaṃ sidhyati | [ato] jñātavyaṃ na mānasaṃ karma gurutaramiti | yathā cāha bhagavān- yo bālaka ājanma karuṇāmabhyasyati | sa kimakuśalaṃ karmotpādayituṃ śankoti akuśalaṃ karma cetayate vā iti | ato jñāyate kāyikaṃ karmaivotpādayati na mānasaṃ karma iti |
body.translated_text: one obtains the sin of taking life — namely, the existence of a being, the knowledge that it is a being, the intention to kill, and the cutting off of its life — through these four things sin is accomplished. Therefore it should be known that mental <s>karma</s> is not the most grave. And the Blessed One said: 'A boy who from birth practices compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) — could he produce unwholesome <s>karma</s>, or does he intend unwholesome <s>karma</s>?' From this it is known that bodily <s>karma</s> alone produces [the result], not mental <s>karma</s>.

body.text: atrocyate | yat bhavānāha- kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmaiva gurutaraṃ na mānasam iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | sūtre bhagavānāha-
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: Your statement that 'bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> alone is the most grave, not mental' is not valid. Why? The Blessed One said in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
cittaṃ dharmasya vai mūlaṃ cittaṃ prabhuśca kiṅkaraḥ |
śubhāśubhaṃ tatsmarati vacanaṃ caraṇañca tat || iti |
body.translated_text:
The mind is indeed the root of <s>dharma</s>; the mind is both master and servant.
It recollects the auspicious and the inauspicious — that speech and that action.

body.text: ato jñāyate mānasaṃ karmaiva gurutaramiti | manoviśiṣṭatvena kāyikavācikakarmaṇo rviśeṣo 'sti | yathā uttamaṃ madhyamamadhamamityādi | vinā cittaṃ nāsti kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karma | sūtre vacanācca vijñaptikarma kṛtvā niyamena vipākaṃ vedayate | āha ca- saptaviśuddhipuṇyānāṃ trividhamānasakarmamātramupayojayati | imāni saptaviśuddhipuṇyāni puṇyasampatsūttamāni bhavanti | karuṇā ca mānasaṃ karma | sūtramāha- karuṇācittaṃ vipākaprāpakamiti | yathāha sūtram- purāhaṃ saptavarṣāṇi karuṇāsamudācaraṇānneemaṃ lokaṃ saptamahākalpān pratinivartāmīti | ato jñāyate mānasaṃ karmeva gurutaramiti | tadeva sarvān lokān vyāptuṃ śaknoti | mānasaṃ karma gurutaram | yathā mānasakarmavipākādaśītimahākalpahasrāṇyāyurbhavati | mānasakarmaṇaḥ śakti kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmātiśete | yathā kuśalacārī āyuṣo 'nte mithyādṛṣṭimutpādayan narake patati | akuśalacārī maraṇakāle samyagdṛṣṭimutpādayan deveṣūtpadyate | [tato] jñātavyaṃ mānasaṃ karma mahattaramiti | uktañca sūtre- pāpeṣu mithyādṛṣṭirgurutareti | āha- yo lokottarāṃ samyagdṛṣṭimutpādayati sa varṣaśatasahasyāṇi saṃsāre saṃsarannapi na durgatau patati iti | mānasakarmaṇo balaṃ kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmātiśete | yathoktamupālisūtre- tīrthiko maharṣiḥ [āgatya vadet] ekena manodaṇḍena nālandaṃ bhasmīkaromīti iti | yathā daṇḍakāraṇyāni ṛṣiṇāṃ manodaṇḍena [bhasmī]kṛtāni iti | mānasaṃ karmaiva vipākaprāpakam | yathoktaṃ
body.translated_text: Therefore it is known that mental <s>karma</s> alone is heavier. Because of the superiority of the mind, bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> have their distinction. Just as [there is] superior, middling, and inferior, and so forth. Without mind, there is no bodily or verbal <s>karma</s>. And because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>, having performed manifest (<s>vijñapti</s>) <s>karma</s>, one necessarily experiences ripening. And it is said: 'For the seven purities of merit (<s>saptaviśuddhipuṇya</s>), one employs only the three kinds of mental <s>karma</s>.' These seven purities of merit are the highest among accumulations of merit. And compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) is mental <s>karma</s>. The <s>sūtra</s> says: 'The mind of compassion leads to ripening.' As the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'Formerly, I practiced the cultivation of compassion for seven years — [through that merit] I shall not return to this world for seven great <s>kalpas</s>.' Therefore it is known that mental <s>karma</s> alone is heavier. It alone is able to pervade all worlds. Mental <s>karma</s> is heavier. Just as through the ripening of mental <s>karma</s>, one has a lifespan of eighty thousand great <s>kalpas</s>. The power of mental <s>karma</s> surpasses bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>. Just as one who practices the wholesome, at the end of life generating wrong view, falls into hell. One who practices the unwholesome, at the time of death generating right view, is reborn among the gods. Therefore it should be known that mental <s>karma</s> is greater. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Among sins, wrong view is the heaviest.' He said: 'One who generates the supramundane right view — even if he wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s> for a hundred thousand years, he does not fall into a lower destiny.' The power of mental <s>karma</s> surpasses bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>. As stated in the <s>Upāli Sūtra</s>: 'The non-Buddhist great seer, having come, would say: "By a single mental rod (<s>manodaṇḍa</s>), I reduce <s>Nālandā</s> to ashes."' Just as the <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> forests were reduced to ashes by the mental rod of the <s>ṛṣis</s>. Mental <s>karma</s> alone leads to ripening. As stated

body.text: sūtre- yo 'yamatra mṛtaḥ sa eva narakaṃ praviśati | sa eva deveṣūtpadyate hastamukteṣuvat iti | yathā mānasakarmaṇopacittairmaladharmairyāvadavaivartikanarakaṃ praviśati | [tathā] upacitaiḥ kuśaladharmairyāvannirvāṇam | caitasikasya savipākatvādeva kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ vipacyate | abhāve karmaṇo vipākābhāvāt | na vinā mānasaṃ karma kāyavākkarmaṇorvipāko 'sti | yanmanasā kāyaṃ vācañca niśritya kuśalamakuśalaṃ vā carati tatkāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmetyucyate | vināpi kāyikavācikakarmaṇanasakarmaṇo vipāko 'sti | na tu vinā mānasaṃ karma kāyikasya vācikasya vā vipākaḥ | ato jñāyate mānasaṃ karma gurutaraṃ na kāyikaṃ vācikam | iti |
body.translated_text: in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whoever dies here — that very one enters hell; that very one is reborn among the gods, like an arrow released from the hand.' Just as through mental <s>karma</s> one accumulates impure <s>dharmas</s> leading all the way to the irreversible hell — so too, through accumulated wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, all the way to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. It is because mental [<s>karma</s>] has ripening that bodily and verbal [<s>karma</s>] ripen. In the absence of <s>karma</s>, there is no ripening. Without mental <s>karma</s>, there is no ripening of bodily or verbal <s>karma</s>. When the mind, depending on the body and speech, engages in the wholesome or unwholesome — that is called 'bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>.' Even without bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>, mental <s>karma</s> has ripening. But without mental <s>karma</s>, bodily and verbal [<s>karma</s>] do not have ripening. Therefore it is known that mental <s>karma</s> is heavier, not bodily or verbal.

body.text: yadbhavatoktaṃ kāyikavācikakarmaṇorniyamena satyatvāt yathā pañcānantaryāṇi kāyaṃ vāca[ñcopādāya] kriyanta ityato gurutarāṇīti | tanna yujyate | yasmāt cetanā gurvī vastu ca guru tasmātkarma guru | na kāyavacasī guruṇī iti | cittanaiyatyātkarma niyamena satyam | yathā cittabalamātreṇa saddharmapadaṃ praviśati tathā cittabalenaiva cānantaryapāpaṃ sampādayati | asati citte mātāpitṛvadho 'pi nānantaryam | ato jñāyate kāyavacasī na balavatīti |
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'because bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> are necessarily real, just as the five heinous crimes (<s>ānantarya</s>) are performed through body and speech, therefore they are heavier' — that is not valid. Because the intention (<s>cetanā</s>) is grave and the object (<s>vastu</s>) is grave, therefore <s>karma</s> is grave — not because body and speech are grave. It is because of the fixity of mind that <s>karma</s> is necessarily real. Just as through the power of mind alone one enters the noble <s>Dharma</s>-stage, so too through the power of mind alone one brings about the sin of the heinous crimes (<s>ānantarya</s>). Without mind, even the killing of mother or father is not a heinous crime. Therefore it is known that body and speech are not powerful.

body.text: uktaṃ bhavatā kāye vāk ca karma vastu niṣpādayatīti | tanna yuktam | karmasamāpanaṃ niṣpattiḥ | parasyāyurapaharan prāṇātipātapāpaṃ labhate | na kāyikavācikakarmotpattikāle | karmasamāpane cittabalamavaśyamapekṣate | na kāyavacasī | yaduktaṃ bhavatā- vṛthācittotpādamātreṇa nāsti vipāka iti | tadayuktam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dṛḍhacittamutpādya tadaiva deveṣūtpadyate narake vādhaḥ patati iti | kathamāha mānasakarmaṇo na vipāko 'stīti | yaduktaṃ bhavatā- nāpi praṇidhānamātreṇa vastu sādhayatīti | tadapyayuktam | kasyacidutpannaṃ gabhīraṃ kuśalacittaṃ mahāsaṅgha[dāna]puṇyamapyatiśete | yadāha bhavān- nāsti mānasyāpattiriti | tadayuktam | yadākuśalacittamutpādayati tadaiva pāpaṃ labhate | yathāha bhagavān- santi vividhāni pāpāni kāyikavācikamānasapāpānīti | ato jñāyate 'kuśalacittotpādamātrama pāpamiti na labhyate | asaṃyojanamātraṃ śīlam, durdharatvāt | audārikaṃ pāpaṃ śīladhāraṇena vārayati | sūkṣmaṃ pāpaṃ samādhyādinā pariharati |
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'body and speech accomplish the object of <s>karma</s>' — that is not valid. The completion of <s>karma</s> is accomplishment. When one takes another's life, one obtains the sin of taking life — not at the time when bodily or verbal <s>karma</s> arises. At the completion of <s>karma</s>, the power of mind is necessarily relied upon — not body and speech. Your statement that 'through the mere arising of a futile mind, there is no ripening' — that is not valid. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Having generated a firm mind, at that very moment one is reborn among the gods, or falls below into hell, like [an arrow released from the hand].' How can you say that mental <s>karma</s> has no ripening? Your statement that 'not by mere aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) does one accomplish an object' — that too is not valid. For a certain person, a profound wholesome mind that has arisen surpasses even the merit of giving to a great assembly (<s>mahāsaṅgha</s>). Your statement that 'there is no mental offense (<s>āpatti</s>)' — that is not valid. When one generates an unwholesome mind, at that very time one obtains sin. As the Blessed One said: 'There are various sins — sins of body, speech, and mind.' Therefore it is known that the mere arising of an unwholesome mind is sinful — that cannot be maintained [to not exist]. The mere non-fettering is moral conduct — because [moral conduct] is difficult to maintain. One prevents gross sin through the maintenance of moral conduct. One removes subtle sin through concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) and the like.

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhavatā puṇyaṃ pāpañca sulabhaṃ syāditi | tadayuktam | cittabalasya tanutvāt janāḥ sulabhaṃ tyaktvā durlabhaṃ kurvanti | yathā karuṇācittādi, tatpuṇyamatimātrabahulam | na tu dānaṃ [tathā] | sattvā avarajñānabalāḥ karuṇādi mānasaṃ karma carituṃ na samarthā ityato
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'merit and sin would be easy [to obtain]' — that is not valid. Because the power of mental strength is thin, people abandon what is easy and do what is difficult. Just as the mind of compassion and the like — that merit is exceedingly abundant. But giving is not like that. Beings, having inferior power of knowledge, are unable to practice mental <s>karma</s> such as compassion and the like — therefore

body.text: dānādi kurvanti | prakīrṇakusamagandhādiṣu pūjopakaraṇeṣu viśuddhacittasya durlabhatvāt | yaduktamakṣīṇapuṇyaḥ syāditi | tatpratibrūmaḥ | sa yadi bodhibalayuktaḥ tadā akṣīṇaṃ kuśaladharmaṃ labhetaiva | yaduktaṃ mānasaṃ karma na kasyacidupakaroti apakaroti vā iti | tanna yujyate | kāyikavācikarmāṇi mānasakarmaṇāhṛtānīti na pradhānāni bhavanti | yadbalādutpadyate tat [tataḥ] pradhānam | sarva upakārāḥ karuṇācittavihārādhīnā bhavanti | kasmāt | karuṇāvihārabalātsamīraṇavṛṣṭayoḥ ṛtumanuvartamānayorapi bījaśatāni pacyante | yathā kalpādau taṇḍulāni svayamutpadyante puruṣāṇāṃ daśavarṣāyuḥkāle prāpte tatsarvaṃ nābhūta | kathamāha- karuṇācittamanupakārakamiti | karuṇāvihārī sarvāṇyakuśalamūlāni kṣapayati | akuśalakarmādhīnā hi sarva upadravāḥ | kathamāha- karuṇāvihāro mahopakāraka iti | yadi sarve sattvāḥ karuṇācitte virahanti | tadā sarve susthāna utpadyeran | na hi sarve prakṛtitaḥ puṇyaprayogamabhilaṣanti | ato jñāyate karuṇāpuṇyaṃ paramagabhīragahanamiti | kadācitkaruṇādānābhyāṃ sattvānupakurvanti | kadācitkaruṇāmātreṇa | karuṇāvihāriṇaḥ sattvā yadi kāyaṃ spṛśanti | yadi vā tacchāyāyāṃ nipatanti | sarvathā nivṛtiṃ labhante | jñātavyaṃ karuṇāpuṇyaṃ dānādibhya uttamamiti |
body.translated_text: they practice giving and the like. Because in offering-materials such as scattered flowers, incense, and the like, it is difficult to have a purified mind. Your statement that 'one's merit would be inexhaustible' — to that we reply: If he is endowed with the power of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), then he would indeed obtain inexhaustible wholesome <s>dharma</s>. Your statement that 'mental <s>karma</s> benefits or harms no one' — that is not valid. Bodily and verbal <s>karmas</s>, being brought about by mental <s>karma</s>, are not primary. That by whose power [something] arises — that is primary. All benefits depend on the practice of the mind of compassion. Why? Through the power of dwelling in compassion, even when wind and rain follow the seasons, hundreds of seeds ripen. Just as at the beginning of a <s>kalpa</s>, rice grains arise spontaneously — when humans reach the lifespan of ten years, all of that ceases to exist. How can you say that the mind of compassion is without benefit? One who dwells in compassion eradicates all unwholesome roots. For all calamities depend on unwholesome <s>karma</s>. How can you say that dwelling in compassion is of great benefit? If all beings were to be free from the mind of compassion, then all would be reborn in a good place. For not all by nature seek out the means of merit. Therefore it is known that the merit of compassion is supremely profound and impenetrable. Sometimes through both compassion and giving, one benefits beings. Sometimes through compassion alone. For beings who dwell in compassion — if they touch [another's] body, or if [beings] fall within their shadow — in every way, they obtain relief. It should be known that the merit of compassion is superior to giving and the like.

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhavatā- hānilābhāvatimātrāviti | tatpratyuktapūrvaṃ yanmanobalena sattvānupakaroti apakaroti ceti | ato jñāyate mānasaṃ karma gurutaramiti | yaduktaṃ ciropacitenāpi śīlādīnā na kiñcidupakṛtamiti | tadapyayuktam | kasmāt | manoviśuddhayā hi śīlaviśuddhiḥ | yadi mano na viśuddham | śīlamapi na viśuddhyati | yathedaṃ saptābrahmacaryasūtra uktam | viśuddhaśīlaśca mahāvipākaṃ pratilabhate | yathāha sūtrama- śīlavrataḥ prāṇihitaṃ mano 'nuyāyi bhavati | yaduta śīlaviśuddhyā iti | śīlaviśuddhau ca cittaṃ praśāmyati | nānyadharme [sati] | yaduktaṃ kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmādaurikam | ataḥ pūrvaṃ prajahātīti | tadayuktam | sūkṣmakuśalena mahāvipākaṃ labhate | yathā dhyānasamāpattau cetanā | yaduktaṃ yadyabrahmacaryacittamutpādayati tadā śīlaṃ vipadyeteti | tadayuktam | yasya mānasaṃ karmāviśuddham, tasya śīlamapi aviśuddham | puṇyapāpayorbhede labdhe saṃyojanaśīladharmayorbhedaḥ | yaduktaṃ tvayā- utpadyamānaṃ vijñaptikarma kāyavāgbhyāṃ bhavatīti | tat sāmānyataḥ pratyuktaṃ yaduta kāyikavācikakarmadharmabhede mānasakarmadharmabhedaḥ | kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karma avaśyaṃ vijñāpayitrā sidhyati | yathā caturbhiḥ pratyayaiḥ siddhaṃ prāṇātipātapāpaṃ na mānasakarma vinā bhavati | laukikāḥ satvā vadanti kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karmākuśalaṃ na tathā mānasamiti |
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'there is merely diminishment and gain' — that was previously refuted, namely that through the power of mind one benefits and harms beings. Therefore it is known that mental <s>karma</s> is heavier. Your statement that 'even through long-accumulated moral conduct and the like, nothing is benefited' — that too is not valid. Why? For the purification of moral conduct depends on the purification of the mind. If the mind is not purified, moral conduct too is not purified. As this is stated in the <s>Saptabrahmacarya Sūtra</s>. And one of purified moral conduct obtains great ripening. As the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'For one who upholds moral conduct, a mind that is beneficial to living beings follows along — namely, through the purification of moral conduct.' And in the purification of moral conduct, the mind becomes tranquil — not in any other <s>dharma</s>. Your statement that 'bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> are gross, therefore they are abandoned first' — that is not valid. Through subtle wholesome [<s>karma</s>], one obtains great ripening. Just as the intention (<s>cetanā</s>) in <s>dhyāna</s> and meditative attainment. Your statement that 'if one generates a mind of unchastity (<s>abrahmacaryacitta</s>), then moral conduct would be lost' — that is not valid. For one whose mental <s>karma</s> is impure, his moral conduct too is impure. When the distinction of merit and sin has been obtained, [then follows] the distinction of fetters and moral-conduct <s>dharmas</s>. Your statement that 'arising manifest (<s>vijñapti</s>) <s>karma</s> operates through body and speech' — that has been generally refuted, namely that in the distinction of the <s>dharmas</s> of bodily and verbal <s>karma</s>, [there is correspondingly] the distinction of the <s>dharma</s> of mental <s>karma</s>. Bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> are necessarily accomplished by one who makes [something] known (<s>vijñāpayitṛ</s>). Just as the sin of taking life accomplished through four conditions does not exist without mental <s>karma</s>. Worldly beings say: 'Bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> are unwholesome — not so mental [<s>karma</s>].'

body.text: mānasaṃ karma ca na janeṣūpaprayujyate nāpyupalabhyate 'stīti | pūrvañcoktaṃ puṇyapāpayorlakṣaṇam | tallakṣaṇatvānmānasaṃ karmaiva gurutaraṃ na kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: But mental <s>karma</s> is neither employed among people nor recognized to exist. And previously the characteristics of merit and sin were stated. Because it has those characteristics, mental <s>karma</s> alone is heavier — not bodily or verbal.

body.text: trikarmagauravalāghavavarga ekonaviṃśatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and nineteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Heaviness and Lightness of the Three Karmas (<s>trikarmagauravalāghavavarga</s>).

body.text: 120 karmahetuprakāśanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 120. Chapter on Illuminating the Cause of Karma (<s>karmahetuprakāśanavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- saṃkṣipyoktāni karmāṇi | karmedaṃ kāyopādānasya kāraṇam | kāyo duḥkhasvabhāvaḥ | atastaṃ nirodhayet | etatkāyaniroddhukāmena tatkarma prahātavyam | hetunirodhe phalasyāpi nirodhāt | yathā bimbamupādāya pratibimbam | bimbanirodhe pratibimbaṃ nirudhyate | ato duḥkhanirodhakāminā taddhetukarmaprahāṇāya vīryamārabdhavyam |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: <s>Karmas</s> have been stated in brief. This <s>karma</s> is the cause of the appropriation of the body. The body has suffering as its nature. Therefore one should bring it to cessation. One who desires to bring this body to cessation should abandon that <s>karma</s>. Because when the cause ceases, the effect too ceases. Just as, depending on the original image, a reflection [exists]; when the original image ceases, the reflection ceases. Therefore, one who desires the cessation of suffering should undertake effort for the abandonment of that causal <s>karma</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) karmataḥ kāya utpadyata itīdaṃ pratipādayitavyam | kasmāt | kecidāhuḥ- kāyaḥ prakṛtita utpadyata iti | kecidāhuḥ- maheśvarādutpadyata iti | kecidāhuḥ- mahāpuruṣātsambhūta iti | anye kecidāhuḥ- svabhāvaja iti | ato vaktavyaṃ kāraṇaṃ kathaṃ jñāyate karmata utpadyata iti | (u) idaṃ vividhaiḥ kāraṇairdūṣitam | jñātavyaṃ karmataḥ kāyamupādatta iti | padārthā nānāviprakīrṇajātaya iti jñātavyaṃ heturapi bhidyata iti | yathā paśyāmaḥ alakasandukakodravādīnāṃ bhedaḥ tadbījamasamaṃ jñāpayati iti | maheśvarādīnāṃ bhedābhāvāt na heturiti jñātavyam | karmaṇastu apramāṇavibhaktatvāt nānākāyā upādīyante | kiñca sajjanāḥ śraddhadhante yat karmopādāya kāya upādīyata iti | kasmāt | te hi sadācaranti dānaśīlakṣāntyādikuśaladharmān | viramyante ca prāṇātipātādyakuśaladharmebhyaḥ | ato jñāyate karmataḥ śarīramupādīyata iti | yadi karmopādāya śarīramupādīyate tadā tat nivartanīyam | tattvajñānalābhānmithyājñānaṃ prahīyate | mithyājñānaprahāṇātkāmakrodhādayaḥ kleśāḥ prahīyante | kleśānāṃ prahāṇādūrdhvajanmotpādakaṃ karmāpi prahīyate | tadā tvayaṃ kāyo nivartyate | īśvarādīnāṃ kāraṇatve tu na nivartayituṃ śakyate | īśvarādīnāmaprahātavyatvāt | ato jñāyate karmataḥ śarīramupādīyata iti | pratyakṣaṃ praśyāmaḥ khalu hetusadṛśaṃ phalam | yathā krodravātkodrava utpadyate śāleśca śāliḥ | evamakuśalakarmato 'niṣṭavipāko labhyate | kuśalakarmata iṣṭavipākaḥ | īśvarādīṣu tu nedṛśamasti | ataḥ karma kāyasya mūlam | neśvarādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) The proposition that 'the body arises from <s>karma</s>' must be established. Why? Because some say: 'The body arises from primordial nature (<s>prakṛti</s>).' Some say: 'It arises from <s>Maheśvara</s>.' Some say: 'It is produced from the Great Person (<s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>).' Others say: 'It is born of its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>).' Therefore it must be stated: How is it known that the cause is that [the body] arises from <s>karma</s>? (Answer) These [alternative views] have been refuted by various arguments. It should be known that the body is obtained from <s>karma</s>. Since things are of various kinds scattered into different classes, it should be known that the cause too is differentiated. Just as we see the differentiation of <s>alaka</s> grass, <s>sanduka</s>, <s>kodrava</s> grain, and the like — that indicates that their seeds are different. Since <s>Maheśvara</s> and the like do not have differentiation, they should be known as not being the cause. But since <s>karma</s> is differentiated immeasurably, various bodies are obtained. Furthermore, virtuous people have faith that the body is obtained depending on <s>karma</s>. Why? Because they always practice wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), and the like; and they abstain from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as killing and the rest. Therefore it is known that the body is obtained from <s>karma</s>. If the body is obtained depending on <s>karma</s>, then it can be averted. Through the attainment of the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), wrong knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) is abandoned. Through the abandonment of wrong knowledge, defilements such as desire, anger, and the rest are abandoned. Through the abandonment of defilements, the <s>karma</s> that produces further birth is also abandoned. Then this body is averted. But if <s>Īśvara</s> and the like were the cause, it could not be averted — because <s>Īśvara</s> and the like cannot be abandoned. Therefore it is known that the body is obtained from <s>karma</s>. We directly perceive that the fruit resembles the cause. Just as <s>kodrava</s> grain arises from <s>kodrava</s>, and rice from rice — so too, from unwholesome <s>karma</s>, undesirable ripening is obtained; from wholesome <s>karma</s>, desirable ripening. But with <s>Īśvara</s> and the like, there is nothing like this. Therefore <s>karma</s> is the root of the body, not <s>Īśvara</s> and the like.

body.text: paśyāmaḥ khalu pratyakṣaṃ padārthāḥ karmasambhūtā iti | akuśalakarmaṇā hi tāḍananigrahabandhanakaśādhātādiduḥkhānyanubhavanti | kuśalakarmapratyayañca yaśolābhasatkārādisukhānyanubhavanti | manojñapriyavādī manojñapriyavipākaṃ vindate | ato jñāyate karmataḥ śarīramupādīyate na maheśvarādibhya iti | laukikāḥ svayaṃ jānanti padārthāḥ karmahetasambhūtā iti | ata eva kṛṣyādikarma kurvanti | dānaśīlakṣāntyādipuṇyakarmāṇi ca kurvanti | nānta[rgṛha]mupaviśanti īśvarādibhya īpsitamākāṃkṣamāṇāḥ | ato jñāyate karmato vipāko labhyata iti | janā īśvarādīn kāraṇaṃ vadanto 'pi karmāṇi niśrayante yaduta svadehaṃ khedayanta upavāsādīn svīkurvanti ca | ato jñāyate karmahetukamiti | yadadṛṣṭaṃ vastu tatra paraśāsanamanusaret yadāryāṇāmācaritam | sarve cāryāḥ śīlādikuśaladharmān niśrayante yato jānanti karmahetorloko 'stīti | yadi śīlādivirataḥ na [sa] āryo bhavati | na kaścidāryaḥ śāsanapratidvandvikarmako bhavati | ato jñāyate karmaṇaḥ śarīramupādīyata iti | kiñca śīlādi karmaṇāmācaraṇādṛdhyabhijñānirmitādīni sādhayanti | ato jñāyate karmahetuka iti | narakādidurgatiṣu dveṣapradāśādayo bahulāḥ | ato jñāyate dveṣapradāśādinā durgatayo bhavantīti | yathā upari vṛkṣe phalaṃ dṛṣṭvā jānanti vṛkṣastaddheturiti | ato jñāyate karma dehasya mūlamiti | durgatau mohādayaḥ prabalā iti jñātavyaṃ kleśāḥ durgatikāraṇam | sarveṣāmakuśalānāṃ mohādhīnatvāt iti | durgatiṣūtpannā bahavaḥ, sugatiṣūtpannā alpāḥ | cakṣuṣā paśyāmaḥ khalu vadhādyakuśalacāriṇo bahavaḥ | kuśalacāriṇo 'lpā iti | ato jñāyate hiṃsādivṛttirdurgatikāraṇamiti | vadhādi sajjanā vigarhya na kurvanti | yadi jānanti nāśubhaphalānīti kasmāt nirākurvanti | sajjānānāṃ citte yadyakuśalamutpadyate tadaiva prayatnena nigṛhyate | akuśalavipākabhīrutvāt | [ato] jñātavyaṃ vadhādayo 'vaśyamakuśalavipākā iti | tathā nocet yatheṣṭaṃ kuryaḥ idameva paramaṃ sukhamiti | tadā hatvā sattvānāṃ bhojanaṃ paradravyāpahāraḥ yadi vā parastrīgamanaṃ imānyapi sukhāni bhaveyuḥ | āgāmiduḥkhabhīrutvāt tāni dūrataḥ pariharanti | ato jñāyate karmataḥ kāyo bhavatīti | samyak jñānabhāvanayā sāsravaṃ karma kṣīyate | na tadā kāya upādīyate | ato jñāyate karma tasya mūlamiti | arhato yadyapi sāsravakarmāṇi santi | samyak jñānabhāvanayā tu [tāni] nopacinoti | ato jñāyate karma kāyasya heturiti | kāyahetunirodhātkāyo 'pi nirudhyate | catussatyajñānāt satyāśrayāḥ kleśā na kadāpi punarudbhavanti | anudbhavānna bhavati kāyavān | vidvānevaṃ cintayan catussatyāni jijñāsati | ato jñāyate karma kāyasya heturiti | pratyaye vikale ca na
body.translated_text: We directly perceive that things are produced from <s>karma</s>. Through unwholesome <s>karma</s>, one experiences sufferings such as beating, suppression, bondage, whipping, and the like. Through the condition of wholesome <s>karma</s>, one experiences pleasures such as fame, gain, honor, and the like. One who speaks pleasant and agreeable words obtains pleasant and agreeable ripening. Therefore it is known that the body is obtained from <s>karma</s>, not from <s>Maheśvara</s> and the like. Worldly people themselves know that things are produced from <s>karma</s> as their cause. For this very reason, they perform <s>karmas</s> such as farming and the like, and they also perform meritorious <s>karmas</s> such as generosity, moral conduct, patience, and the like. They do not sit inside [their] houses expecting what is desired from <s>Īśvara</s> and the like. Therefore it is known that ripening is obtained from <s>karma</s>. People who speak of <s>Īśvara</s> and the like as the cause also rely on <s>karmas</s> — namely, they exert their own bodies and undertake fasting and the like. Therefore it is known that [things] have <s>karma</s> as their cause. Regarding unseen matters, one should follow the teaching of others, namely what is practiced by the Noble Ones. And all Noble Ones rely on wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as moral conduct and the like, because they know that the world exists due to <s>karma</s> as its cause. If one who abstains from moral conduct and the like is not a Noble One — no Noble One performs <s>karma</s> opposed to the teaching. Therefore it is known that the body is obtained from <s>karma</s>. Furthermore, through the practice of <s>karmas</s> such as moral conduct and the like, one accomplishes supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>), superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), magical creations (<s>nirmita</s>), and the like. Therefore it is known that [things] have <s>karma</s> as their cause. In the lower destinies (<s>durgati</s>) such as hell and the like, hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), fury (<s>pradāśa</s>), and the like are prevalent. Therefore it is known that the lower destinies come about through hatred, fury, and the like. Just as seeing fruit on a tree above, one knows that the tree is its cause. Therefore it is known that <s>karma</s> is the root of the body. In the lower destinies, delusion (<s>moha</s>) and the like are predominant — it should be known that defilements are the cause of the lower destinies, because all unwholesome [actions] are subject to delusion. Those born in the lower destinies are many; those born in the good destinies are few. We directly perceive that those who practice unwholesome conduct such as killing and the like are many, and those who practice the wholesome are few. Therefore it is known that the practice of violence and the like is the cause of the lower destinies. Virtuous people censure the practice of killing and the like and do not do it. If they knew that there were no unpleasant fruits, why would they refrain? In the minds of virtuous people, whenever the unwholesome arises, it is immediately restrained with effort — because of the fear of unwholesome ripening. Therefore it should be known that killing and the like necessarily [lead to] unwholesome ripening. If that were not so, one would do as one pleases, [thinking] 'this itself is the supreme happiness.' Then killing beings for food, stealing others' property, or going to others' wives — these too would be pleasures. Because of the fear of future suffering, they avoid these from afar. Therefore it is known that the body arises from <s>karma</s>. Through the cultivation of right knowledge (<s>samyak jñāna</s>), <s>karma</s> with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) is exhausted. Then no body is obtained. Therefore it is known that <s>karma</s> is its root. Even though an <s>Arhat</s> has <s>karma</s> with outflows, through the cultivation of right knowledge he does not accumulate [further karma]. Therefore it is known that <s>karma</s> is the cause of the body. Through the cessation of the cause of the body, the body too ceases. Through the knowledge of the four truths (<s>catussatya</s>), defilements that depend on the truths never arise again. Because of their non-arising, there is no one who possesses a body. The wise person, contemplating thus, aspires to know the four truths. Therefore it is known that <s>karma</s> is the cause of the body. And when the conditions are deficient,

body.text: kāyamupādatte | yathā śuṣkabhūmau bīje ca dagdhe na sarvo 'ṅkuraḥ prarohati | evaṃ vijñānasthitikṣetre tṛṣṇāsnehānabhiṣyandite karmabīje ca tattvajñānadagdhe nordhvadehāṅkuraḥ prarohati | vidvānetadvastu prajñāya vijñānasthitikṣetraṃ śoṣayituṃ karma bījaṃ dagdhuñca vīryamadhiṣṭhāya prayatate | ato jñāyate karma kāyopādānasya pratyaya iti ||
body.translated_text: one does not obtain a body. Just as in dry ground, when the seed has been burned, no sprout grows — so too, when the field of the station of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>) is not moistened by the moisture of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), and when the seed of <s>karma</s> has been burned by the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), the sprout of a future body does not grow. The wise person, having understood this matter, strives with energy (<s>vīrya</s>) to desiccate the field of the station of consciousness and to burn the seed of <s>karma</s>. Therefore it is known that <s>karma</s> is the condition for the obtaining of a body.

children.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-twentieth chapter, the Chapter on Illuminating Karma as the Cause (<s>karmahetuprakāśanavarga</s>).
The section on <s>karma</s> is completed.

body.text: 121 samudayasatyaskandhe kleśādhikāre ādyakleśalakṣaṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 121. Within the Aggregate of the Truth of Origination, in the Section on Defilements: the Chapter on the Initial Characteristic of Defilements (<s>ādyakleśalakṣaṇavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- uktāni karmāṇi | kleśā idānīṃ vakṣyante | malinacittasamudācāraḥ kleśa ityucyate | (pṛ) kiṃ malamucyate | (u) yat saṃsārasantānasya pravartakaṃ tanmalinacittamityucyate | tanmalinacittaprabhedā eva rāgadveṣamohādayaḥ | idaṃ malinacittaṃ kleśa ityucyate | pāpadharma ityapi, parihāṇidharmaḥ tirobhāvadharma paritapanadharma anupatanadharma ityādināmnāpyucyate | etanmalinacittābhyāsopacayo 'nuśaya ityucyate | na tu malinacitta utpannamātre 'nuśayaḥ | kleśā nāma rāgadveṣamohavicikitsāmānapañcadṛṣṭayaḥ | tatprabhedā aṣṭanavatiranuśayāḥ |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: <s>Karmas</s> have been explained. Defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) will now be explained. The arising of a defiled mind (<s>malinacittasamudācāra</s>) is called a defilement. (Question) What is called 'defilement' (<s>mala</s>)? (Answer) That which sets in motion the continuity of <s>saṃsāra</s> — that is called a defiled mind. The varieties of that defiled mind are passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), and the like. This defiled mind is called a defilement. It is also called by [the names] 'sinful <s>dharma</s>' (<s>pāpadharma</s>), 'subject to decline' (<s>parihāṇidharma</s>), 'subject to concealment' (<s>tirobhāvadharma</s>), 'subject to torment' (<s>paritapanadharma</s>), 'subject to downfall' (<s>anupatanadharma</s>), and so forth. The accumulated habitual cultivation of this defiled mind is called a 'latent tendency' (<s>anuśaya</s>). But a latent tendency does not [exist] merely at the first arising of a defiled mind. Defilements are: passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), and the five [wrong] views (<s>pañcadṛṣṭi</s>). Their subdivisions are ninety-eight latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>).

body.text: rāgaḥ prītisukhākhyastrividhaḥ | vibhavaprītisukhamapi rāga ityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- kāmatṛṣṇā bhavatṛṣṇā vibhavatṛṣṇā iti | vibhavo nāma prahāṇaṃ nirodhaḥ | sattvā duḥkhābhihatā skandhakāyaṃ parijihīrṣavo vibhavaṃ sukhaṃ manyante |
body.translated_text: Passion (<s>rāga</s>) is of three kinds, called joy (<s>prīti</s>) and happiness (<s>sukha</s>). Joy and happiness regarding annihilation (<s>vibhava</s>) are also called passion. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There is craving for sensual pleasures (<s>kāmatṛṣṇā</s>), craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>), and craving for annihilation (<s>vibhavatṛṣṇā</s>).' 'Annihilation' (<s>vibhava</s>) means abandonment, cessation. Beings, stricken by suffering, wishing to relinquish the aggregate-body (<s>skandhakāya</s>), regard annihilation as happiness.

body.text: (pṛ) prītisukhaṃ vedanālakṣaṇaṃ na nandirāgaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- aihikaṃ saumanasyamāmuṣmikaṃ saumanasyaṃ ihalaukikasukhavedanā āmuṣmikasukhavedanā ityarthamabhidadhāti iti | kiñcāha- aihikaṃ daurmanasyamāmuṣmikaṃ daurmanasyaṃ ihalaukikaduḥkhavedanā āmuṣmikaduḥkhavedanā ityarthamabhidadhāti | yathoktaṃ devatāpraśne- kiṃ nandati putraiḥ putravān | bhagavānāha- śocati putraiḥ putravān ityādi |
body.translated_text: (Question) Joy and happiness have the characteristic of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), not of delight-and-passion (<s>nandirāga</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Elation in this world and elation in the next world, pleasant feeling in this world and pleasant feeling in the next world — this is what is meant.' Furthermore it says: 'Displeasure in this world and displeasure in the next world, painful feeling in this world and painful feeling in the next world — this is what is meant.' As stated in the question of the deities: 'What delights in sons? The person who has sons.' The Blessed One said: 'The person who has sons grieves through sons,' and so forth.

body.text: atrocyate | rāgo nandyaṅgam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā | sukhavedanāyāṃ rāgo 'nuśayaḥ | kabalīkārāhāre 'sti nandirasti rāgaḥ | nandikṣayādrāgakṣaya iti | ato jñātavyaṃ rāgaḥ prītyaṅgamiti | idaṃ tvanavadyam | kena tat jñāyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- samudayasatyaṃ yaduta tarṣaṇaṃ iti | kasyābhidhānaṃ tarṣaṇam | yat punarbhavalipsā | kiṃlakṣaṇamidaṃ tarṣaṇam | yat rāgaṃ niśritya vividhalipsā | (pṛ) yadyucyate punarbhavalipsā tarṣaṇalakṣaṇamiti | kasmātpunarucyate rāgaṃ niśritya vividhalipseti | (u) asti punastarṣaṇalakṣaṇam | vividhalipseti viśiṣṭalakṣaṇavacanam | vītarāgasyāpyasti vividhalipsātarṣaṇaṃ yaduta salilādilipsā | neyaṃ samudayasatyasaṅgṛhītam | yadrāgamupadāya punarbhavalipsā, tattarṣaṇaṃ samudayasatyasaṅgṛhītam |
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: Passion is a component of delight. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is conditioned by feeling.' And: 'In pleasant feeling, passion becomes latent (<s>anuśaya</s>).' And: 'In material nutriment (<s>kabalīkārāhāra</s>), there is delight, there is passion. Through the exhaustion of delight, the exhaustion of passion.' Therefore it should be known that passion is a component of delight. This is blameless. How is that known? As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>) is craving (<s>tarṣaṇa</s>).' What is designated as 'craving'? That which is the desire for further becoming (<s>punarbhavalipsā</s>). What is the characteristic of this craving? That which, depending on passion, is the manifold desire [for objects]. (Question) If it is said that the desire for further becoming is the characteristic of craving, why is it further said 'depending on passion, manifold desire'? (Answer) There is a further characteristic of craving. 'Manifold desire' is a statement of the specific characteristic. Even one who is free from passion has manifold desire-craving — namely, the desire for water and the like. This is not included in the truth of origination. That craving which, depending on passion, is the desire for further becoming — that is included in the truth of origination.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi tarṣaṇamapi nandiḥ, rāgo 'pi nandiḥ kasmāducyate rāgaṃ niśrityeti | (u) ādyotpannaṃ tarṣaṇam | vivṛddho rāgaḥ | atastaṃ niśrityetyucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- nandisambandho loka iti | ato nandireva rāgaḥ | uktañca sūtre- nirodhaṃ varjayitvā rāgo daurmanasyañca sarve 'kuśalā dharmā iti | tatra rāga eva nandiḥ | daurmanasyaṃ dveṣaḥ | yathocyate dveṣo daurmanasyamiti tadā jñāyate nandiḥ rāga ityupyucyata iti | ato 'ṣṭādaśamanaupavicāreṣu na kleśā ucyante kevalaṃ vedanā ucyante | ato jñāyate nandyaṅgaṃ rāga iti | pṛthagjanā vītarāgā na vedayante sukham | vītadveṣāśca na duḥkhaṃ vedayante | vītamohā nāduḥkhamasukhaṃ vedayante | kena tat jñāyate | tṛtīyavedanāyāmucyate pṛthagjanā asyā vedanāyā na jānanti samudayaṃ, na jānanti nirodhaṃ, na jānanti āsvādaṃ, na jānanti ādīnavaṃ na jānanti nissaraṇam | ato 'duḥkhāsukhavedanāyāmavidyānuśayo 'nuśete | ime pṛthagjanāḥ sadā pañcadharmān tān na jānantītyato 'duḥkhāsukhavedanāyāṃ sadāvidyānuśayaṃ rvanti | yo 'vidyānuśayaḥ tadvedanopavicārasvabhāvājñānam | evaṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ sukhaduḥkhamanaupavicārāveva
body.translated_text: (Question) If craving too is delight (<s>nandi</s>), and passion too is delight, why is it said 'depending on passion'? (Answer) Craving, having arisen at first, [is craving]. Having grown, it is passion. Therefore it is said 'depending on that.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The world is bound by delight' — therefore delight itself is passion. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Excluding cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), passion and displeasure — all are unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' Therein, passion itself is delight; displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>). When it is said 'hatred is displeasure,' then it is known that delight is also called passion. Therefore, among the eighteen mental investigations (<s>manaupavicāra</s>), defilements are not mentioned — only feelings are mentioned. Therefore it is known that passion is a component of delight. Ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who are free from passion do not experience happiness. Those free from hatred do not experience suffering. Those free from delusion do not experience neither-painful-nor-pleasant [feeling]. How is this known? Regarding the third feeling, it is said: 'Ordinary beings do not know the origination of this feeling, do not know its cessation, do not know its gratification, do not know its danger, and do not know its escape.' Therefore, in the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, the latent tendency of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) becomes latent. These ordinary beings constantly do not know those five <s>dharmas</s> — therefore in the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, they always have the latent tendency of ignorance. The latent tendency of ignorance is the not-knowing of the nature of that feeling-investigation (<s>vedanopavicāra</s>). Thus, for ordinary beings, the mental investigations of pleasure and suffering are themselves

body.text: rāgapratighau | yadādāvāgatya citte vartate [sā] vedanetyucyate | tadeva cittamadhimātraṃ kleśa ityucyate |
body.translated_text: passion (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>pratigha</s>). What first arrives and operates in the mind is called 'feeling.' That very mind, when excessive, is called a 'defilement.'

body.text: samudayasatyaskandhe kleśādhikāre ādyakleśalakṣaṇavargaṃ ekaviṃśatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one-hundred-and-twenty-first chapter, the Chapter on the Initial Characteristic of Defilements, within the Section on Defilements in the Aggregate of the Truth of Origination (<s>ādyakleśalakṣaṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 122 rāgalakṣaṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 122. Chapter on the Characteristic of Passion (<s>rāgalakṣaṇavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- navasaṃyojaneṣu rāgo 'yamātridhātupratipratisaṃyuktastṛṣṇetyucyate | saptānuśayānāmaṅgaṃ dvidhā bhavati- kāmarāgo bhavarāga iti | kasmāt | kecidūrdhvadhātudvaye vimuktisaṃjñāmutpādayanti | ato bhagavānāha- sthānamidaṃ bhava iti | bhavo nāma janma | asati rāge na janma bhavati ityataḥ pṛthagucyate bhavarāga iti | na tu kāmarāgamātram | kecidāhuḥ- kāmarāgamātraṃ kleśaḥ | kṣīṇakāmarāgo vimukto nāma iti | ato bhagavānāha- ārūpyadhyāne 'pyasti bhavarāga iti | pradarśayati ca bhagavān tatra[āpi] bhavaḥ sūkṣmaḥ pravartata iti | ataḥ pṛthagucyate 'yaṃ rāgaḥ | daśākuśalakarmapatheṣu caturṣu bandhaneṣu ca kāmarāga ityākhyā bhavati | kāmarāgasya paradravyalipyetyākhyā | pañcanīvaraṇānāṃ pañcāvarabhāgīyasaṃyojanānāñca kāmakāmanetyākhyā bhavati | [tatra]kāmakāmanā nāma pañcakāma [guṇā]nāṃ kāmakāmanā | trayāṇāmakuśalamūlānāmakuśalamūlarāga ityākhyā | akuśalamūlarāgo nāma akuśalamūlānāmupacayanam | ayaṃ rāgo yadyadhamācaraṇaḥ tadā akuśalarāga ityākhyā | yathā paradravyāpaharaṇaṃ, yāvaccaityasaṅghadravyādānam | yadyamṛtasattvasya māṃsabubhukṣā, yadi vā mātṛbhaginīsvasrācāryapatnīḥ pravrajitapatnīṃ svapatnīṃ vāmārgeṇa jigamiṣati | ayamakuśalarāga ityucyate | yat svadravyaṃ na tyaktumicchati | tatkārpaṇyam | kārpaṇyaṃ rāga eva | vastuto 'sati guṇe astīti vaktumanyapreraṇamakuśalarāgaḥ | sati guṇe anyasya tadvijijñāpayiṣā rāgotpādanam | bahudānasya bahudravyasya vā lipsā, sā bahurāgatā | yadalpadravyasyālpadānaṃ labdhvā priyataraṃ kāmayate na tṛpyati | [iya]masantuṣṭiḥ | gotrakulabandhuyaśorūpasampadyauvanajīvitādiṣu yadabhiṣvaṅgaḥ [sa] mada ityucyate | yaccatuḥsatkārarāgaḥ [tat] tṛṣṇācatuṣṭayamityucyate |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Among the nine fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), this passion (<s>rāga</s>), connected with the three realms (<s>tridhātu</s>), is called 'craving' (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). Among the seven latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), it is divided twofold — desire-passion (<s>kāmarāga</s>) and existence-passion (<s>bhavarāga</s>). Why? Some generate the perception of liberation in the two upper realms. Therefore the Blessed One said: 'This state is existence (<s>bhava</s>).' Existence means birth (<s>janma</s>). In the absence of passion, birth does not occur — therefore existence-passion is stated separately. It is not merely desire-passion. Some say: 'Only desire-passion is a defilement. One whose desire-passion is exhausted is called liberated.' Therefore the Blessed One said: 'Even in the formless <s>dhyānas</s>, there is existence-passion.' And the Blessed One demonstrates that even there, subtle existence operates. Therefore this passion is stated separately. In the ten unwholesome action-paths and the four bonds (<s>bandhana</s>), it receives the designation 'desire-passion.' Desire-passion's designation is 'coveting another's property' (<s>paradravyalipyā</s>). In the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) and the five lower fetters (<s>pañcāvarabhāgīyasaṃyojana</s>), it receives the designation 'craving for sensual pleasure' (<s>kāmakāmanā</s>). Therein, 'craving for sensual pleasure' means the craving for the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>pañcakāmaguṇa</s>). Among the three unwholesome roots (<s>akuśalamūla</s>), it receives the designation 'root-passion of the unwholesome' (<s>akuśalamūlarāga</s>). 'Root-passion of the unwholesome' means the accumulation of the unwholesome roots. When this passion practices what is inferior, it receives the designation 'unwholesome passion' (<s>akuśalarāga</s>). Such as the stealing of another's property, up to the taking of <s>caitya</s> and <s>Saṅgha</s> property. Such as the craving for the flesh of a being that has not [yet] died, or desiring to go by an improper method to one's mother, sister, sister-in-law, teacher's wife, wife of a renunciant, or one's own wife. This is called 'unwholesome passion.' When one does not wish to relinquish one's own property — that is miserliness (<s>kārpaṇya</s>). Miserliness is passion itself. Urging another to speak of a quality that does not really exist — that is unwholesome passion. When a quality does exist, the desire to make another know it — that is the generation of passion. The desire for much giving or much property — that is great passion. When, having obtained a small gift or small property, one desires more and is not satisfied — that is dissatisfaction (<s>asantuṣṭi</s>). The clinging to family lineage, clan, kinship, fame, beauty, prosperity, youth, life, and the like — that is called 'intoxication' (<s>mada</s>). The fourfold passion for the four kinds of honor — that is called 'the fourfold craving' (<s>tṛṣṇācatuṣṭaya</s>).

body.text: ayañca rāgo dvividhaḥ kāmarāgaḥ upakaraṇarāga iti | punardvividhaḥ ātmarāga ātmīyarāga iti | ādya ādyātmikapratyayaḥ | aparo bāhyapratyayaḥ | ūrdhvadhātudvaye rāga ekāntenādhyātmikapratyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: And this passion is twofold: desire-passion (<s>kāmarāga</s>) and passion for accessories (<s>upakaraṇarāga</s>). Again twofold: passion for the self (<s>ātmarāga</s>) and passion for what belongs to the self (<s>ātmīyarāga</s>). The first has an internal condition. The other has an external condition. In the two upper realms, passion is exclusively with an internal condition.

body.text: punaḥ pañcavidhaḥ- rūparāgaḥ, saṃsthānarāgaḥ, sparśarāgaḥ, iryāpathapralāparāgaḥ, sarvarāga iti | rūparasagandhaśabdasparśarāgaḥ pañcakāmaguṇarāgaḥ | ṣaṭsu sparśeṣūtpannā tṛṣṇā ṣaḍviṣayarāgaḥ | tisṛṣu vedanāsu rāgo 'sti sukhavedanāyāmasti lipsārāgaḥ, tatparipālanarāgaḥ | duḥkhavedanāyāmasti alipsārāgaḥ tatparijihīrṣārāgaḥ | aduḥkhāsukhavedanāyāmasti moharāgaḥ | santi cāsya rāgasya navāṅgāni | yathoktaṃ mahānidānasūtre- tṛṣṇāṃ pratītya yatheṣṭavastuparyeṣaṇā | yathā kaścit anena vastunā duḥkhito vastvantaraṃ paryeṣate | yathoktam- sukhī na paryeṣate duḥkhī tu bahu paryeṣate | rāgavivṛddhiḥ paryeṣaṇā | paryeṣaṇākāle yallabhyate [sa] tṛṣṇālābhaḥ | lābhaṃ pratītya viniścayaḥ | idaṃ grāhyamidamagrāhyamiti yaccittanirdhāraṇaṃ sa viniścayaḥ | viniścayaṃ pratītya chandarāgaḥ | chandarāgaṃ pratītyādhyavasānam | adhyavasānaṃ nāma pragāḍhacchandaḥ | adhyavasānaṃ pratītya parigrahaḥ | parigraho nāma upādānam | upādānaṃ pratītya mātsaryam | mātsaryaṃ pratītya ārakṣā | ārakṣādhikaraṇaṃ daṇḍādānaśastrādānādi | imāni navāṅgāni punarapi navāṅgagāni | rāgo 'yaṃ kālamanusṛtya adhamaḥ, madhyamaḥ, uttamaḥ, adhamādhamaḥ, adhamamadhyamaḥ, adhamottamaḥ, madhyamādhamaḥ, madhyamamadhyamaḥ, madhyamottamaḥ, uttamādhamaḥ, uttamamadhyama, uttamottama iti | rāgasya cāsya laukikāṅgāni daśa bhavanti | tadyathā priyarūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā citte idaṃ [priya]miti vacanaṃ karoti | tato rāgaṃ janayati | praṇidhānaṃ karoti | anusmarati | yathāśikṣitaṃ prakaṭayati | hryapatrapāṃ vismarati | sadā svayaṃ purovartate | pramatto bhavati | unmatto bhavati | murcchāmaraṇaṃ [karoti] | idaṃ rāgalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: Again fivefold: passion for form (<s>rūparāga</s>), passion for shape (<s>saṃsthānarāga</s>), passion for touch (<s>sparśarāga</s>), passion for deportment and talk (<s>iryāpathapralāparāga</s>), and all-inclusive passion (<s>sarvarāga</s>). Passion for form, taste, smell, sound, and touch is the passion for the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>pañcakāmaguṇarāga</s>). Craving arisen in the six contacts is the passion for the six objects (<s>ṣaḍviṣayarāga</s>). In the three feelings, there is passion: in pleasant feeling, there is the passion of desire for obtaining and the passion of guarding what is obtained. In painful feeling, there is the passion of desire for non-obtaining and the passion of desiring to avoid it. In neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there is the passion of delusion (<s>moharāga</s>). And this passion has nine components. As stated in the <s>Mahānidānasūtra</s>: Dependent on craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), there is seeking (<s>paryeṣaṇā</s>) of desired objects. Just as someone, afflicted by this thing, seeks another thing. As stated: 'One who is happy does not seek; one who is suffering seeks much.' The growth of passion is seeking. What is obtained at the time of seeking — that is the gain of craving (<s>tṛṣṇālābha</s>). Dependent on gain, there is determination (<s>viniścaya</s>). The mental resolve 'this is to be taken, this is not to be taken' — that is determination. Dependent on determination, there is desire-passion (<s>chandarāga</s>). Dependent on desire-passion, there is adherence (<s>adhyavasāna</s>). Adherence means intense desire (<s>pragāḍhacchanda</s>). Dependent on adherence, there is appropriation (<s>parigraha</s>). Appropriation means clinging (<s>upādāna</s>). Dependent on clinging, there is avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>). Dependent on avarice, there is guarding (<s>ārakṣā</s>). Because of guarding, there is the taking up of sticks, weapons, and the like. These nine components are in turn each [divisible into] nine components.
