body.text: tṛṣṇādīni navasaṃyojanāni | (pṛ) kasmād dṛṣṭiṣu dvidhā parāmarśa ucyate | (u) śīlavrataparāmarśasya durvimokatvāt | yathā uḍupamoghapatitaṃ dustaraṃ bhavati | tathāyamapi | evaṃ cintayati- ahamanena śīlena svarga utpatsya iti | tadarthañca jalamajjana dahanapraveśabhṛgupatanādīni nānā duḥkhānyanubhavāmīti | laukikā na śīlavrataparāmarśasya doṣaṃ paśyanti | ata uktaṃ bhagavatā saṃyojanamiti | taṃ śīlavrataparāmarśaṃ niśritya aṣṭāṅgamārgamupekṣante | so 'samyaṅmārgo 'vyavadānamārgo duḥkhāntānuvartanamityucyate | śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ pravrajitānāṃ vinibandhaḥ | kāmā gṛhasthānām | śīlavrataparāmarśī yadyapi nānāpravrajyādharmānācarati | tathāpi vṛthā na kiñcidanena labhyate | sa naihikaṃ sukhaṃ vindate, paratra ca mahadduḥkhamanubhavati | yathāgovratikaḥ saṃsiddhavratiko gaurbhavati | vikṣiptavrato narake patati | tacchīlavrataparāmarśamupādāya samyaṅ mārgaṃ samyaṅ mārgacāriṇañcāpavadati | śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ tīrthikānāṃ mānotpattisthānam | [ta] evaṃ cintayanti- ahamanena dharmeṇānyamatiśeya iti | śīlavrataparāmarśahetunā ṣaṇṇavatidhā vibhaktā dharmā santi | śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ sthūladarśana ityato bahūnāṃ satvānāṃ gocaraḥ | prajñāmārgastvatisūkṣmo durdarśanaḥ | laukikā na prajānanti tadācaraṇahitam | sā ca dṛṣṭirjanānāṃ cittaṃ harati | ato bālā bahavastaṃ dharmamācaranti | sā gurvī pāpikā dṛṣṭirityucyate | samyaṅmārgācārasya pratilomyenāmārgatvāt |
body.translated_text: The nine fetters are craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) and the rest. (Question) Why is clinging to views (<s>parāmarśa</s>) spoken of in two ways among the [wrong] views? (Answer) Because clinging to precepts and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) is difficult to liberate from. Just as a boat caught in an unnavigable channel becomes difficult to cross — so too is this [clinging]. One thinks thus: 'Through this moral conduct, I shall be born in heaven.' And for that purpose, one experiences various sufferings such as immersion in water, entering fire, leaping from cliffs, and the like. Worldly people do not see the fault of clinging to precepts and rituals. Therefore the Blessed One called it a 'fetter' (<s>saṃyojana</s>). Depending on that clinging to precepts and rituals, they disregard the Noble Eightfold Path. That is called a wrong path, an impure path, and 'following along to the end of suffering.' The clinging to precepts and rituals is a fetter for renunciants. Sensual pleasures [are a fetter] for householders. One who clings to precepts and rituals, even though he practices various religious observances of going forth — still, it is in vain; nothing is obtained by this. He does not find happiness in this life, and in the next life he experiences great suffering. Just as a cow-vow practitioner (<s>govratikaḥ</s>), when the vow is fulfilled, becomes a cow; when the vow is broken, he falls into hell. Because of that clinging to precepts and rituals, one disparages the right path and the practitioner of the right path. The clinging to precepts and rituals is the ground for the arising of conceit among the non-Buddhists (<s>tīrthika</s>). They think thus: 'Through this <s>dharma</s>, I surpass others.' Because of the cause of clinging to precepts and rituals, <s>dharmas</s> are divided in ninety-six ways. The clinging to precepts and rituals, being a gross view, is the domain of many beings. But the path of wisdom is extremely subtle and difficult to see. Worldly people do not understand the benefit of its practice. And that view captivates the minds of people. Therefore many fools practice that <s>dharma</s>. It is called a 'grave, sinful view' — because of going contrary to the practice of the right path.

body.text: dṛṣṭiparāmarśo yenāsaddharmābhiniviṣṭastatparihartumasamartho bhavati | tadṛṣṭiparāmarśasya balam | tadvalena ca saṃyojanāni dṛḍhāni bhavanti | (pṛ) śaknapraśne kasmātkevalamuktamīrṣyāmātsaryasaṃyojanā devāmanuṣyā iti | (u) idaṃ kleśadvayamatigrāmyaṃ javanyam | kasmāt | paśyāmaḥ khalu parasattvān kṣutpipāsāpīḍitān, mātsaryacittatvānnātikrāntān | [te] parato labdhaṃ dṛṣṭvāpi īrṣyāsūyācittamutpādayanti sotkaṇṭhāsantāpam | anena kāraṇena ca daridrāṇāṃ nīcānāṃ kutsitānāmatejasvināñca sthāne patanti | śakrasya devānāmindrisyaitatsaṃyojanaṃ bahutaramasakṛdāgatya cittaṃ pīḍayati | ato bhagavān vacanamāha | tatsaṃyojanadvayaṃ gurupāpakasya nidānam | kasmāt | tadupādāya gurūṇi pāpakarmāṇyudbhavanti |
body.translated_text: Clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>) is that by which one who is attached to wrong <s>dharma</s> is unable to relinquish it. That is the power of clinging to views. And through that power, the fetters become firm. (Question) In the question of <s>Śakra</s>, why was it stated simply: 'The gods and humans have the fetters of jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>)'? (Answer) These two defilements are extremely vulgar and swift. Why? We directly see that beings afflicted by hunger and thirst, because of having a mind of avarice, do not go beyond [their own interests]. Having seen what others have obtained, they even generate a mind of jealousy and malice, with longing and torment. And through this cause, they fall into the place of the poor, the low, the despised, and the powerless. For <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, this twofold fetter comes repeatedly and afflicts the mind. Therefore the Blessed One spoke those words. That twofold fetter is the basis for grave sin. Why? Dependent on it, grave sinful <s>karmas</s> arise.

body.text: triṣu viṣeṣu rāgaḥ pratighaśca gurupāpakamutpādayati | tayorvivṛdhyā tatsaṃyojanadvayamutpadyate | tatsaṃyojanadvayaṃ striyaṃ puruṣañca pīḍayati | durutsargañca bhavati | kasmāt | yaḥ kuśalacittaṃ nibhṛtaṃ bhāvayati | so 'tyantamīrṣyāsūyaṃ samucchedayati | dānañca nibhṛtamabhyasyānte sarvamātsaryacittaṃ samucchedayati | karmavipākamapaśyan tadgurutaravastu tyajatīdamati duṣkaram | yathā kasyacitsvata utkṛṣṭavastulābhinaṃ putrameva paśyataścittaṃ duṣprītikaṃ bhavati | kaḥ punarvādaḥ śatrum | tatsaṃyojanadvayoḥ priyaviprayaniścitatvādatiduṣkaraḥ parityāgaḥ | asmāt karmapratyayāt bhagavatā kevalamuktam ||
body.translated_text: In the three [kinds of] distinctions, passion (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) produce grave sin. Through the increase of those two, this twofold fetter arises. That twofold fetter afflicts both women and men. And it is difficult to abandon. Why? One who diligently cultivates a wholesome mind — he completely eradicates jealousy and malice. And one who diligently practices giving — he eventually completely eradicates all minds of avarice. But not seeing the ripening of <s>karma</s>, abandoning a more valuable thing is indeed difficult. Just as someone, seeing his own son who has obtained a more valuable thing, becomes displeased in mind — how much more so regarding an enemy? Because the abandoning of this twofold fetter is determined by separation from the beloved, it is exceedingly difficult to relinquish. For this very karmic reason, the Blessed One spoke [of them] alone.

body.text: navasaṃyojanavargaḥ saptatriṃśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and thirty-seventh chapter, the Chapter on the Nine Fetters (<s>navasaṃyojanavarga</s>).

body.text: 138 prakīrṇapraśnavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 138. Chapter on Miscellaneous Questions (<s>prakīrṇapraśnavarga</s>)

body.text: śāstramāha- sarve kleśā bhūyasā daśānuśayasaṅgṛhītāḥ | ato daśānuśayānupādāya śāstraṃ racitavyam | daśānuśayā iti rāgapratighabhānāvidyāvicikitsāḥ pañcadṛṣṭayaśca | (pṛ) daśakleśamahābhūmikadharmāḥ tadyathā aśrāddhayaṃ kausīdyaṃ muṣitasmṛtitā vikṣepo 'vidyāsamprajanyamayoniśomanaskāro mithyādhimokṣa auddhatyaṃ pramādaśca | ime dharmāḥ sarvakleśacittaiḥ sadā samprayuktāḥ | kathamidam | (u) satprayogaḥ pūrvaṃ khaṇḍita eva | caitasikaścaikaika evotpadyate | ato na yujyate | na ca san nyāyo bhavati | kenedaṃ jñāyate |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: All defilements are for the most part included in the ten latent tendencies (<s>daśānuśaya</s>). Therefore the treatise should be composed based on the ten latent tendencies. The ten latent tendencies are: passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and the five [wrong] views (<s>pañcadṛṣṭi</s>). (Question) There are ten <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the great ground of defilements (<s>daśakleśamahābhūmikadharma</s>) — namely, faithlessness (<s>āśrāddhya</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), loss of mindfulness (<s>muṣitasmṛtitā</s>), distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), non-clear-comprehension (<s>asamprajanya</s>), wrong attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>), wrong determination (<s>mithyādhimokṣa</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), and heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). These <s>dharmas</s> are always conjoined (<s>samprayukta</s>) with all defiled minds. How is this? (Answer) The [theory of] conjunction with the existent (<s>satprayoga</s>) has been refuted previously. And mental factors arise only one at a time. Therefore this is not valid. Nor is this principle correct. How is this known?

body.text: kiñcidakuśalacittakuśalaśraddhāsamanvitamasti | kiñcidakuśalacittaṃ śraddhāsamanvitaṃ nāsti | tathā vīryādikamapi | ato jñāyate na sarvakleśacitteṣu te daśa dharmāḥ santīti | yadbhavānāha- middhamauddhatyaṃ sarvakleśacitteṣu vartata iti | tadayuktam | yadā cittaṃ līnaṃ bhavati | tasmin samaye middhasamanvitaṃ syāt | nauddhatyacitte syāt itīdṛśā doṣāḥ santi |
body.translated_text: Some unwholesome mind is endowed with wholesome faith. Some unwholesome mind is not endowed with faith. Likewise with effort (<s>vīrya</s>) and the rest as well. From this it is known that those ten <s>dharmas</s> do not exist in all defiled minds. Your statement that 'torpor (<s>middha</s>) and restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>) operate in all defiled minds' is not valid. When the mind is sluggish, at that time it would be endowed with torpor, but not with restless mind — such faults exist.

body.text: (pṛ) kāmadhātau sakalā daśakleśāḥ santi | rūpadhātāvārūpyadhātau ca dveṣavarjitā avaśiṣṭāḥ santi | kathamidam | (u) tatrāpi santīrṣyādayaḥ | kenedaṃ jñāyate | sūtra uktam- mahābrahmā brahmakāyikānāmantryāha mā bhavanto śramaṇaṃ gautamamupasaṅkramantu | iheva tiṣṭhata jarāmaraṇasyāntaṃ lapsyadhve iti | iyamīrṣyā | īrṣyāsattvādveṣo 'pi bhavet | uktañca sūtre- [atha khalu kevadhaṃ] mahābrahmā taṃ bhikṣuṃ bāhau gṛhītvā ekamantamapanayitvā taṃ bhikṣumetadavocat- ahamapi na jānāmi yatremāni catvāri mahābhūtānyapariśeṣāṇi nirudhyante iti | evaṃ māyācittena brahmakāyikānāṃ vañcanaṃ māyetyucyate | yadāha- ahamasmi [mahābrahmā] kartā nirmātā śreṣṭha.......iti | ayaṃ pramādaḥ | ityādīni chidrāṇi santi | īdṛśānāṃ pāpakānāṃ kleśānāṃ sattvāt jñātavyamasti ca [tatrā] akuśalamiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) In the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), all ten defilements exist. In the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) and formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>), the remaining ones exist excluding hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>). How is this? (Answer) Even there, jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and the like exist. How is this known? It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Mahābrahmā</s> addressed the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods: "Do not approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. Stay right here — you will obtain the end of old age and death."' This is jealousy. Because jealousy exists, hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) too would exist. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Then <s>Kevadha Mahābrahmā</s>, having seized that monk by the arm and drawn him aside, said to that monk: "I too do not know where these four great elements cease without remainder."' Thus, deceiving the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods with a mind of deception — this is called 'deception' (<s>māyā</s>). When he said: 'I am <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, the creator, the maker, the most excellent...' — this is heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). Such and similar flaws exist. Because of the existence of such sinful defilements, it should be known that even there, the unwholesome exists.

body.text: kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ- mātāpitrupādhyāyācāryādiṣu yo rāgaḥ sa kuśalarāgaḥ | anyapadārthādiṣu rāgo 'kuśalarāgaḥ | anyeṣāmupakāro 'pakāro vā yanna kriyate | [aya]mavyākṛtarāgaḥ | asaddharme durvijñādiṣu dveṣaḥ kuśaladveṣaḥ | saddharmadveṣaḥ prāṇidveṣaśca akuśaladveṣaḥ | yo 'sattvapadārthadveṣaḥ avyākṛtadveṣo ['yam] | yanmānaṃ niśritya mānaṃ samucchedayati ayaṃ kuśalamānaḥ | anyasya sattvasyāvamānamakuśalamānaḥ | avidyādiṣvapyevaṃ [vaktavyam] |
body.translated_text: Certain <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: Whatever passion toward mother, father, teacher, preceptor, and the like — that is wholesome passion (<s>kuśalarāga</s>). Passion toward other objects and the like is unwholesome passion (<s>akuśalarāga</s>). That which neither benefits nor harms others is indeterminate passion (<s>avyākṛtarāga</s>). Hatred toward wrong <s>dharma</s>, ignorant persons, and the like is wholesome hatred (<s>kuśaladveṣa</s>). Hatred toward the true <s>Dharma</s> and hatred toward living beings is unwholesome hatred (<s>akuśaladveṣa</s>). Hatred toward non-sentient objects is indeterminate hatred (<s>avyākṛtadveṣa</s>). Whatever conceit through reliance on which one eradicates conceit — that is wholesome conceit (<s>kuśalamāna</s>). The contempt of another being is unwholesome conceit. The same should be said regarding ignorance and the rest.

body.text: kiñcāhurābhidharmikāḥ- yaḥ kuśalaḥ na [sa] kleśo bhavati | (pṛ) kāmadhātau satkāyadṛṣṭimavyākṛtā vadanti | kasmāt | yadi satkāyadṛṣṭirarakuśalā | sarve pṛthagjanā ātmacittamutpādayanti | nā[nena] narake patanīyā bhavanti | ato 'vyākṛteti
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: What is wholesome is not a defilement. (Question) In the desire realm, they say the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) is indeterminate. Why? If <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> were unwholesome, then all ordinary beings generate the thought of self — they would not have to fall into hell because of that. Therefore they say

body.text: vadanti | kathamidam | (u) satkāyadṛṣṭiriyaṃ sarvakleśānāṃ mūlam | kathamavyākṛtā | sa pareṣāmātmāstīti vadan patati | tadā kathamavyākṛtā bhavet | evamantagrahadṛṣṭirapi [vaktavyā] | (pṛ) yadi mithyādṛṣṭiṃ pravartayitvā saṃśaye pātayati | kimidamakuśalam | (u) nedamakuśalam | kasmāt | varaṃ saṃśaya eva pātayati na mithyādṛṣṭāvatārayati |
body.translated_text: it is indeterminate. How is this? (Answer) This <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> is the root of all defilements. How could it be indeterminate? One who says to others 'the self exists' falls [into sin]. Then how could it be indeterminate? Likewise with the view of grasping at extremes (<s>antagrahadṛṣṭi</s>). (Question) If one, having set wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) in motion, causes [someone] to fall into doubt — is this unwholesome? (Answer) This is not unwholesome. Why? It is better indeed to cause [someone] to fall into doubt than to cause [someone] to enter wrong view.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- kāmadhātvāptāḥ kleśāḥ sarve kāmabhavasantānakarāḥ | evaṃ rūparūpyadhātvāptā api | kathamidam | (u) tṛṣṇaiva bhavasantānakarī | nandipūrvikā hi jātiḥ | āha ca- duḥkhasamudayastṛṣṇeti | api cāha- bhojanakāmarāgāditṛṣṇā sukhamiti | ato yathāsthānaṃ janma vedayate | mithyādṛṣṭyādiṣu naivamartho 'sti | sūtre yadyupyuktaṃ- mānapratyayā jātiriti | tathāpi manāpūrvakatṛṣṇayotpadyate | evaṃ dveṣo 'pi | ato jñāyate tṛṣṇayā sarve bhavasantānāṃ bhavantīti |
body.translated_text: Some say: Defilements pertaining to the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) all produce the continuity of desire-realm existence. Likewise with those pertaining to the form and formless realms. How is this? (Answer) Craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) alone produces the continuity of existence. For birth is preceded by delight (<s>nandī</s>). And it is said: 'The origination of suffering is craving.' And further it is said: 'Craving for food, sensual passion, and the like — that is pleasure.' Therefore, according to the [relevant] plane, one experiences birth. In wrong view and the like, there is not such a meaning. Even though it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Birth is conditioned by conceit (<s>māna</s>),' even so, craving arises preceded by conceit. Likewise with hatred. From this it is known that through craving, all existential continuities come about.

body.text: (pṛ) kleśeṣu kati satyadarśanaheyāḥ kati bhāvanāheyāḥ | (u) rāgapratighamānāvidyā dvidhā satyadarśanaheyā bhāvanāheyāśca | anye ṣaṭ satyadarśanamātraheyāḥ | (pṛ) śaikṣajanasyāpyastyahaṃbuddhiḥ | ato jñāyate 'nimittanirūpaṇasatkāyadṛṣṭibhāgaḥ śaikṣajanasyāheya iti | (u) [ahaṃ] māno 'yaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ | nimittanirūpaṇā hi dṛṣṭiḥ | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- īrṣyāmātsaryakaukṛtyamāyādayo bhāvanāheyā iti | kathamidam | (u) ime sarve dvidhāpi bhavanti satyadarśanaheyā bhāvanāheyāśceti | kenedaṃ jñāyate yathā nāthaputrādayo bhagavacchrāvakān satkāralā bhino dṛṣṭvā īrṣyācittamutpādayamāsuḥ | iyamīrṣyā mārgadarśino niruddhetyato jñāyate satyadarśanaheyeti | kaścitpūrvaṃ bhagavacchrāvakeṣu matsarī san nādadat | mārgadarśanalabdhaḥ paraṃ prāyacchat | tadā mātsaryamidaṃ satyadarśanaheyam | yathā sunakṣatrādīnāṃ kaukṛtyaṃ satyadarśanaheyamapi | yathā srotaāpannasya narakapatanapratyayaḥ aṣṭamaloke kāyavedakamāyā ca satyadarśanaheyāpi |
body.translated_text: (Question) Among defilements, how many are to be abandoned by the seeing of truth (<s>satyadarśanaheyā</s>) and how many by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheyā</s>)? (Answer) Passion, aversion, conceit, and ignorance are twofold — to be abandoned by the seeing of truth and to be abandoned by cultivation. The other six are to be abandoned by the seeing of truth alone. (Question) Even a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) has the thought 'I.' From this it is known that the component of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> that involves the investigation of signs (<s>nimittanirūpaṇa</s>) is not to be abandoned for the trainee. (Answer) This 'I' is conceit (<s>māna</s>), [not] view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). For the investigation of signs is a view. (Question) Some say: 'Jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>), remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), deception (<s>māyā</s>), and the like are to be abandoned by cultivation.' How is this? (Answer) All of these are also twofold — to be abandoned by the seeing of truth and by cultivation. How is this known? Just as <s>Nāthaputra</s> and others, having seen the disciples of the Blessed One obtaining much honor, generated a mind of jealousy. This jealousy, having been abandoned through the seeing of the path, ceases — from this it is known to be abandoned by the seeing of truth. Someone who was previously avaricious toward the disciples of the Blessed One and did not give — having obtained the seeing of the path, he afterward gave. Then this avarice is to be abandoned by the seeing of truth. Just as the remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) of <s>Sunakṣatra</s> and the like is to be abandoned by the seeing of truth. Just as the deception of a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) — the cause of falling into hell, the bodily experience in the eight [lower] worlds, and deception too — is to be abandoned by the seeing of truth.

body.text: (pṛ) kleśeṣu kati duḥkhadarśanaheyāḥ kati samudayanirodhamārgadarśanaheyāḥ kati bhāvanāheyāḥ | (u) pūrvoktāḥ satyadarśanaheyāḥ ṣaḍanuśayāścaturdhā bhavanti duḥkhadarśanaheyāḥ samudayanirodhamārgadarśanaheyāḥ | anye catvāro 'nuśayāḥ pañcadhā bhavanti | (pṛ) satkāyadṛṣṭirantagrahadṛṣṭirduḥkhadarśanamātraheyāḥ | śīlavrataparāmarśo dvidhā duḥkhadarśanamārgadarśanaheyāḥ | kathamidam |
body.translated_text: (Question) Among defilements, how many are to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering (<s>duḥkhadarśanaheyā</s>), how many by the seeing of origination, cessation, and the path, and how many by cultivation? (Answer) The six latent tendencies previously stated as to be abandoned by the seeing of truth are fourfold — to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. The other four latent tendencies are fivefold [including cultivation]. (Question) The view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the view of grasping at extremes (<s>antagrahadṛṣṭi</s>) are to be abandoned only by the seeing of suffering. The clinging to moral rules and observances (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) is twofold — to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and by the seeing of the path. How is this?

body.text: (u) sarve kleśā vastuto nirodhasatyadarśanakāle prahīyante | ataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyādayo na duḥkhadarśanamātraheyāḥ syuḥ | satkāyadṛṣṭiścaturṣu satyeṣu bhramati | pañcaskandhā anityāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ | ātmā tu nānityo na pratītyasamutpannaḥ | pañcaskandhāḥ sanirodhāḥ, ātmā tvanirodhaḥ, mārga ātmadṛṣṭervirodhidharmaḥ | ataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭiścaturdhā heyā | antagrahadṛṣṭirapi caturdhā heyā | kasmāt | yogī samudayasambhūtaṃ duḥkhaṃ dṛṣṭvā ucchedadṛṣṭiṃ vyāvartayati | mārgalabdhaṃ nirodhaṃ dṛṣṭvā śāśvatadṛṣṭiṃ vyāvartayati | śīlavrataparāmarśo 'pi caturdhā | hetau sati phalamasti | ato duḥkhaṃ paśyan prajānāti- śīlaṃ duḥkhaṃ, nānena viśuddhirlabhyata iti | idaṃ samudayadarśanaheyam | mithyādṛṣṭyā nirvāṇamapodyate, yadanayā dṛṣṭyā viśuddhirlabhyata iti | idaṃ nirodhadarśanaheyam | anayā mārgo 'podyate- idaṃ mārgadarśanaheyam | yathā dṛṣṭiparāmarśo mithyādṛṣṭyāśriteti caturdhā heyaḥ | evaṃ śīlavrataparāmarśo 'pi syāt |
body.translated_text: (Answer) In reality, all defilements are abandoned at the time of seeing the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>). Therefore <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the like would not be to be abandoned merely by the seeing of suffering. <s>Satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> ranges across [all] four truths. The five aggregates are impermanent, dependently arisen. But the self is not impermanent, not dependently arisen. The five aggregates are subject to cessation, but the self is not subject to cessation. The path is a <s>dharma</s> opposed to the view of self. Therefore <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> is to be abandoned in four ways. The view of grasping at extremes is also to be abandoned in four ways. Why? The <s>yogin</s>, having seen that suffering arises from origination, averts the annihilationist view (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>). Having seen that cessation is obtained through the path, he averts the eternalist view (<s>śāśvatadṛṣṭi</s>). The clinging to moral rules and observances is also [to be abandoned] in four ways. When the cause exists, the fruit exists. Therefore, seeing suffering, one understands: 'Moral conduct is suffering — purification is not obtained through it.' This is to be abandoned by the seeing of origination. Through wrong view, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is denied — that by which purification is obtained. This is to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation. Through this [clinging], the path is denied — this is to be abandoned by the seeing of the path. Just as clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), being based on wrong view, is to be abandoned in four ways — so too would the clinging to moral rules and observances.

body.text: (pṛ) tathā cenna syuraṣṭanavatiranuśayāḥ | sarve 'nuśayā bhūmivaśātprahīyante na dhātuvaśāt | aṣṭanavatiranuśayā iti nānto bhavati | (pṛ) rāgo māno mithyādṛṣṭiṃ varjayitvā anyāścatasro dṛṣṭayo duḥkhadaurmanasyendriye varjayitvā [tadanya]trividhendriyasamprayuktāḥ | dveṣo 'pi sukhasaumanasyendriye varjayitvā [tadanya]trividhendriyasamprayuktaḥ | avidyā pañcendriyasamprayuktā | mithyādṛṣṭirvicikitsā ca duḥkhendriyavarjaṃ caturindriyasamprayuktā | dveṣamrakṣapāpamātsaryerṣyāśca daurmanasyendriyamātra samprayuktāḥ | kathamidam | (u) samprayogo nāstīti pūrvameva dūṣitam | paścādapi vakṣyate pañcasu vijñāneṣu nāsti kleśa iti | bhavataḥ śāsane rāgaḥ saumanasyendriyasamprayuktaḥ | mātsaryantu na tathā ityatra nāsti hetuḥ | mātsaryasya rāgāṅgatvāt | evaṃ māno na daurmanasyendriyasamprayukta ityatrāpi nāsti hetuḥ | ato jñāyate bhavadbhiruktaṃ sarvaṃ svasaṃjñānusmaraṇavikalpamātramiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) If so, there would not be ninety-eight latent tendencies. All latent tendencies are abandoned through the force of the plane (<s>bhūmi</s>), not through the force of the realm (<s>dhātu</s>). [The number] ninety-eight latent tendencies would not be an exhaustive [count]. (Question) Passion, conceit, and the four views excluding wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) are conjoined with the threefold faculty, excluding the displeasure faculty (<s>daurmanasyendriya</s>). Hatred is conjoined with the threefold faculty, excluding the pleasure and elation faculties (<s>sukhasaumanasyendriya</s>). Ignorance is conjoined with the five faculties. Wrong view and doubt are conjoined with four faculties, excluding the suffering faculty (<s>duḥkhendriya</s>). Hatred, hypocrisy (<s>mrakṣa</s>), sinfulness, avarice, jealousy, and the like are conjoined with the displeasure faculty alone. How is this? (Answer) [The theory of] conjunction does not exist — this has been refuted previously. And it will also be stated later that 'in the five consciousnesses there is no defilement.' In your teaching, passion is conjoined with the elation faculty (<s>saumanasyendriya</s>), but avarice is not likewise — there is no reason for this. Because avarice is a limb of passion. Likewise, [the claim that] conceit is not conjoined with the displeasure faculty — there is no reason for this either. From this it is known that everything stated by you is merely the conceptual discrimination of designation-recollection.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- duḥkhaharśanaheyāḥ pañcamithyādṛṣṭayo vicikitsā rāgapratighamānaviprayuktāvidyāḥ | samudayasatya[darśana]heyāśca mithyādṛṣṭidṛṣṭiparāmarśavicikitsā rāgapratighamānaviprayuktāvidyāśca ime sarvatragānuśayā anye 'sarvatragānuśayāḥ | kathamidam | (u) sarve sarvatragāḥ | kasmāt | sarveṣāṃ mithohetupratyayatvāt | mama[śāsane]mithyādṛṣṭau rāgo bhavati, nāsti duḥkhaṃ yāvannāsti mārgaḥ | tasyāṃ dṛṣṭāvabhiniviṣṭa ātmānamunnamayati | yadi śṛṇoti duḥkhamiti, tadā vidviṣati | sa ca rāgo nirodhasatyālambanaḥ | dveṣo
body.translated_text: (Objection) Some say: The five wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) to be abandoned by the insight into the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) dissociated from attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), and pride (<s>māna</s>); and the wrong views, clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), doubt, and ignorance dissociated from attachment, aversion, and pride, which are to be abandoned by the insight into the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>) — these are the universally pervasive latent tendencies (<s>sarvatraga-anuśaya</s>), while the others are non-universally pervasive latent tendencies. How is this? (Reply) All are universally pervasive. Why? Because they are mutually causes and conditions for one another. In my [teaching], attachment arises with regard to wrong view — 'there is no suffering' up to 'there is no path.' One who is firmly attached to that view exalts himself. If he hears 'this is suffering,' then he feels aversion. And that attachment has the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) as its object. The aversion

body.text: nirvāṇadveṣyapi bhavati | nirvāṇenāpyātmana uccamatirbhavati | tadvanmārgeṇāpi, anye 'pyanuśayāḥ sarvatragā iti draṣṭavyam | kāmadhātvāptāḥ kleśā rūpadhātvālambanāḥ | yathā rāgeṇa sukhamabhinandati | dveṣeṇāśubhaṃ vidviṣati | tena dharmeṇātmānamunnamayati, tatpradhānā bhavanti [rūpadhātau] na kāmadhātau | yathā kāmadhātukakleśārūpadhātvālambanāḥ tathā rūpadhātukādṛṣṭayādayaḥ kleśā api kāmadhātvālambanāḥ | evamārūpyadhātāvapi | kiñceme kleśāḥ sāmānyaviśeṣalakṣaṇālambanāḥ | kasmāt | rāgaḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇālambano 'pi caturo devān tadadhastanāṃśca saṃkleśayati | yathāha dīrghanakhasūtram- sarvaṃ kṣamata itīdaṃ saṃrāgāya | sarvaṃ na kṣamata itīdamasaṃrāgāya iti | sarvaṃ na kṣamata itīdaṃ saṃrāgāya | sarvaṃ kṣamata itīdamasaṃrāgāya | tena kleśenātmānamunnamayati | kleśo 'yaṃ kāyavākkarma pravartayati | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre- īdṛśīṃ dṛṣṭimutpādya īdṛśaṃ vastu vadati yadasti jīva ityādi |
body.translated_text: also becomes aversion toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Even through <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, one develops a sense of superiority over the self. Likewise with the path — other latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) too should be understood as universally pervasive. The defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) belonging to the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) take the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) as their object. Just as through attachment one delights in pleasure, through aversion one hates what is impure, and through that quality one exalts oneself — these become predominant in the form realm, not in the desire realm. Just as the defilements of the desire realm take the form realm as their object, so too the views and other defilements of the form realm take the desire realm as their object. The same applies to the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>). Moreover, these defilements take both general and specific characteristics as their objects. Why? Because attachment, even when taking a general characteristic as its object, afflicts the four classes of gods and those below them. As the <s>Dīrghanakha-sūtra</s> states: 'Everything is acceptable' — this leads to attachment (<s>saṃrāga</s>). 'Nothing is acceptable' — this leads to non-attachment. 'Nothing is acceptable' — this leads to attachment. 'Everything is acceptable' — this leads to non-attachment. Through that defilement, one exalts oneself. This defilement sets in motion bodily and verbal action (<s>kāyavākkarma</s>). Why? For it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'Having generated such a view, one speaks of such a thing, saying there exists a soul (<s>jīva</s>)' and so forth.

body.text: te sarve kleśāḥ ṣaṣṭhavijñāne vartante | na pañcasu vijñāneṣu | kasmāt | ṣaṣṭhavijñānasya saṃjñopagatvāt | sarve ca kleśāḥ saṃjñāsambhūtāḥ | tathā no cet satkāyadṛṣṭyādayo 'pi pañcasu vijñāneṣu varteran | kasmāt | cakṣuṣā rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadati ahaṃ paśyamīti | tathā mānavicikitsādiṣvapi | (pṛ) sūtra uktam- ṣaṭ tṛṣṇākāyā iti | kathamucyate pañcasu vijñāneṣu na kleśāḥ santīti | (u) yathā ṣaṇmanaupavicārā manovijñāne vartante | kevalaṃ cakṣurādibhirāhṛtā ityataḥ ṣaṇmanaupavicārā ityucyante | tathedamapi | manovijñāne hi vidyamānaṃ vikalpakāraṇaṃ na pañcasu vijñāneṣu | ato jñāyate pañca vijñāneṣu na santi kleśā iti ||
body.translated_text: All those defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) operate in the sixth consciousness (<s>ṣaṣṭhavijñāna</s>, i.e., the mind consciousness), not in the five [sense] consciousnesses. Why? Because the sixth consciousness is accompanied by conceptualization (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and all defilements arise from conceptualization. If this were not so, then the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and others would also operate in the five consciousnesses. Why? Because having seen a form with the eye, one says 'I see.' The same applies to pride (<s>māna</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and so on. (Objection) It is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'There are six groups of craving (<s>tṛṣṇākāya</s>).' How then can you say that defilements do not exist in the five consciousnesses? (Reply) Just as the six kinds of mental engagement (<s>manaupavicāra</s>) operate in the mind consciousness alone — they are merely called 'six kinds of mental engagement' because they are initiated by the eye and other [sense faculties] — so too is this case. For the conceptual discrimination (<s>vikalpa</s>) that exists in the mind consciousness does not exist in the five consciousnesses. Therefore it is known that defilements do not exist in the five consciousnesses.

body.text: prakīrṇapraśnavargo 'ṣṭastriṃśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, the Chapter on Miscellaneous Questions (<s>prakīrṇapraśnavarga</s>).

body.text: 139 doṣaprahāṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 139. Chapter on the Abandonment of Faults (<s>doṣaprahāṇavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- kleśā navavidhā- adhamamadhyamottamā adhamādhamādhamamadhyamādhamottamā madhyamādhama madhyamamadhyamamadhyamottamā uttamādhamottamamadhyamottamottamā iti | jñānamapi navavidham | kleśeṣūttamottamaḥ pūrvaṃ praheyaḥ | adhamādhamo 'nte praheyaḥ | adhamādhapajñānenottamottamakleśaṃ prajahāti | yāvaduttamottamajñānena adhamādhamakleśaṃ prajahāti iti | kathamidam | (u) apramāṇacittaiḥ kleśān sarvān prajahāti | kasmāt | sūtre bhagavānāha- tadyathā dakṣaḥ
body.translated_text: (Objection) Some say: The defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) are of nine kinds — inferior (<s>adhama</s>), middling (<s>madhyama</s>), and superior (<s>uttama</s>); inferior-inferior, inferior-middling, inferior-superior; middling-inferior, middling-middling, middling-superior; superior-inferior, superior-middling, and superior-superior. Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is also of nine kinds. The superior-superior defilement is to be abandoned first, and the inferior-inferior one is to be abandoned last. By inferior-inferior knowledge, one abandons the superior-superior defilement, up to: by superior-superior knowledge, one abandons the inferior-inferior defilement. How is this? (Reply) One abandons all defilements through immeasurable (<s>apramāṇa</s>) mental states. Why? The <s>Bhagavān</s> stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'Just as a skilled

body.text: karmakaro hastena paraśumādāya cakṣuṣā muṣṭipradeśaṃ dṛṣṭvā yānyaṃśasahasrāni pratidinaṃ kṣīyamāṇāni tānyagaṇayanannapi kṣīṇamātraṃ dṛṣṭvā prajānāti idaṃ kṣīṇamiti | tathā sa bhikṣurapi mārgacaryāṃ bhāvayan kānyadya kṣīṇāṇyāsravasahasrāṇi kāni hyaḥ kṣīṇānyāsravahasrāṇīti agaṇayannapi kṣīṇamātre prajānāti kṣīṇa āsrava iti | ato jñāyate 'pramāṇai jñānaiḥ kleśāḥ kṣīyanta natvaṣṭha nava vā iti |
body.translated_text: craftsman, taking an axe in hand, looking with his eye at the place of the handle, though unable to count the many thousands of portions worn away each day, upon seeing that a portion has been worn away, knows 'this has been worn away' — so too that monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>), cultivating the practice of the path (<s>mārgacaryā</s>), though unable to count which thousands of outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) are worn away today and which thousands of outflows are worn away now, knows with respect to the worn-away portion that the outflow is worn away.' Therefore it is known that defilements are destroyed by immeasurable forms of knowledge, not by eight or nine [fixed categories].

body.text: (pṛ) kaṃ samādhiṃ niśritya kaḥ kleśa prahīyate | (u) saptapratiśaraṇānyupādāya kleśān samucchedayati | yathoktaṃ sūtre bhagavatā- prathamadhyānamupādāyāsravāṇāṃ kṣayo yāvadākiñcanyāyatanamupādāyāsravāṇāṃ kṣaya iti | tāni saptapratiśaraṇāni vināpi āsravāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ karoti | yathoktaṃ susīmasūtre- atikramya saptaniśrayānāsravakṣayamanuprāpnotīti | ato jñāyate kāmadhātukasamādhiṃ niśrityāpi āsravakṣayaṃ pratilabhata iti |
body.translated_text: (Objection) Depending on which <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is which defilement abandoned? (Reply) Depending on the seven supports (<s>saptapratiśaraṇa</s>), one completely cuts off the defilements. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'Depending on the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>); up to: depending on the base of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), the destruction of the outflows.' Even without those seven supports, one can bring about the destruction of the outflows. As stated in the <s>Susīma-sūtra</s>: 'Having transcended the seven supports, one attains the destruction of the outflows.' Therefore it is known that even depending on a concentration belonging to the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), one can attain the destruction of the outflows.

body.text: (pṛ) satyadarśanaheyāḥ kleśā nārūpyasamādhiṃ niśritya prahīyeran | tasya yogino rūpalakṣaṇabhaṅgāt | (u) idaṃ pūrvameva prayuktam | yadārūpyasamādhi[rapi] rūpamavalambata iti | (pṛ) pūrvaṃ prathamadhyānādvītarāgaḥ kiṃ krameṇa dvitīyadhyānādīn prāpnoti kiṃ vā ekakālameva | (u) krameṇa bhavitavyam | prathamadhyāne vītarāgasya dvitiyadhyānādīnāmutpatteḥ | (pṛ) kiṃ kāmadhātāvasti kramaḥ | (u) kleśānāṃ pratikṣaṇaniruddhatvātsyādapi kramaḥ | yathā ca yāmyā devāḥ pariṣvaṅge kāmaṃ sādhayanti | tuṣitā devāḥ pāṇiṃ gṛhītvā kāmaṃ sādhayanti | nirmāṇaratā vāgālāpena kāmaṃ sādhayanti | paranirmitavaśavartino devā ākāraṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmaṃ sādhayanti | [evaṃ] jñātavyaṃ kāmadhātukakleśāḥ krameṇāpi kṣīyanta iti | kecidāhuḥ- puṇyaguṇapratyayaṃ tatrotpadyante | na kleśaprahāṇena | praṇītakāmatvāt tatsādhane viśeṣaḥ | mṛdvindriyatvātpariṣvaṅgena kāmaṃ sādhayanti | tīkṣṇendriyatvādākāraṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmaṃ sādhayanti iti |
body.translated_text: (Objection) The defilements to be abandoned by the insight into truth (<s>satyadarśana</s>) should not be abandoned depending on a formless (<s>ārūpya</s>) concentration, because for that practitioner (<s>yogin</s>) the characteristic of form (<s>rūpalakṣaṇa</s>) would be destroyed. (Reply) This has already been established earlier — that the formless concentration also takes form as its object. (Objection) After becoming free from attachment (<s>vītarāga</s>) toward the first <s>dhyāna</s>, does one attain the second <s>dhyāna</s> and so forth gradually or all at once? (Reply) It must be gradual, because the second <s>dhyāna</s> and so forth arise for one who is free from attachment in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. (Objection) Is there also a gradual sequence in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>)? (Reply) Because defilements cease moment by moment, there may indeed be a gradual sequence. Just as the <s>Yāma</s> gods fulfill desire through embrace, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods fulfill desire by taking the hand, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods fulfill desire through verbal conversation, and the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods fulfill desire by merely seeing a gesture — thus it should be understood that the defilements of the desire realm are also destroyed gradually. Some say: They arise there as a result of merit (<s>puṇya</s>), not through the abandonment of defilements. Because desire has been refined, there is a distinction in its fulfillment. Those with soft faculties (<s>mṛdvindriya</s>) fulfill desire through embrace; those with sharp faculties (<s>tīkṣṇendriya</s>) fulfill desire by merely seeing a gesture.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- bhāvanāheyāḥ kleśāḥ krameṇā prahīyante | pūrvaṃ kāmadhātvāptāḥ pañcādrūpārūpyāptāḥ | satyadarśanaheyāstvekakālaṃ prahīyanta iti | kathamidam | (u) yathā satyadarśanaheyāḥ sarve kleśā nirodhasatyadarśanena prahīyante | uktapūrvamidam yat nirodhadarśanapraheyāḥ
body.translated_text: (Objection) Some say: The defilements to be abandoned through cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>) are abandoned gradually — first those belonging to the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), then the five belonging to the form and formless realms. But those to be abandoned by the insight into truth (<s>satyadarśanaheya</s>) are abandoned all at once. How is this? (Reply) Just as all defilements to be abandoned by the insight into truth are abandoned through the insight into the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) — this has been stated before — that the defilements of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and others

body.text: satkāyadṛṣṭyādayaḥ kleśāḥ sarve nirodhasatyadarśanena prahīyante | ūṣmadharmādārabhya anityādyākāraiḥ pañcaskandhalakṣaṇāni bhāvayitvā ādau praheyāḥ kleśā nirodhadarśanena kṣīyante |
body.translated_text: to be abandoned through the insight into cessation — all defilements are abandoned through the insight into the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatyadarśana</s>). Beginning from the warm stage (<s>ūṣmadharma</s>), having cultivated the characteristics of the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandha</s>) through aspects such as impermanence (<s>anitya</s>) and others, the defilements to be abandoned first are destroyed through the insight into cessation.

body.text: (pṛ) kāmadhātvāptaduḥkha[satya]bhāvanayā kāmadhātukasaṃyojanāni prajahāti | samudayasatyabhāvanāyāpyevam | yathā kāmadhātau tathā naivasaṃjñānāṃ saṃjñāyatane 'pi | kāmadhātukanirodha[satya]bhāvanayā traidhātukasaṃyojanāni prajahāti | evaṃ mārga[bhāvanayā]pi | kathamidam | (u) nirodhajñaḥ kleśān prajahāti | ato bhavaduktaṃ na yujyate | (pṛ) [nanu] sūtra uktam- pañcaskandhānanityādinā bhāvayitvā srotaāpattipalaṃ yāvadarhatphalaṃ vindate iti | kathamāha bhavān nirodhasatyadarśanamātreṇa kleśān prajahātīti | (u) imān pañcaskān bhāvayan prajānāti nirodhamiśrabhāvanām | ataḥ prajahāti kleśānuśayān | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhikṣurbhāvayati idaṃ rūpaṃ, ayaṃ rūpasamudayaḥ, ayaṃ rūpanirodha iti sarvadā mama paśyato dharmaṃ vijānataḥ kleśāḥ prahīyanta iti | jñātavyaṃnirodhasatyadarśanena kleśānāṃ kṣaya iti | pañcaskandhā duḥkham tataḥ kleśāḥ samutpadyante | yadā pañcaskandhānāṃ nirvāṇamupaśamaṃ paśyati | tadā duḥkhasaṃjñā sampannā bhavati | ato jñāyate skandhānāṃ nirodhaṃ paśyataḥ kleśāḥ kṣīyanta iti | yathoktam- dharmānupādāyākāyasvabhāvamekamupekṣācittamāśritya prahāṇamiti | akāyasvabhāva eva nirodhaḥ | yo rūpamakāyasvabhāvaṃ yāvadvijñānamakāyasvabhāvaṃ paśyati so 'tyantavisaṃyogabhāgbhavati | trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni nirvāṇasya pratyayāḥ | vimokṣamukhairebhireva kleśān prajāhāti | nānyopāyaiḥ | ato jñāyate 'saṃskṛtālambano mārga eva kleśān prajahātīti | ato bhavadukto [yaḥ] kleśaprahāṇadharmo nāyaṃ yuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Objection) Through the cultivation of the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>) pertaining to the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), one abandons the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) of the desire realm. The same applies to the cultivation of the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>). As in the desire realm, so too in the realm up to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). Through the cultivation of the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) pertaining to the desire realm, one abandons the fetters of all three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>). The same applies to the cultivation of the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>). How is this? (Reply) One who knows cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) abandons the defilements. Therefore what you have said is not correct. (Objection) But it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'Having cultivated the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandha</s>) as impermanent and so forth, one attains the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) up to the fruit of arhatship (<s>arhatphala</s>).' How then can you say that one abandons defilements merely through the insight into the truth of cessation? (Reply) One who cultivates these five aggregates comes to know the cultivation that includes cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). Thereby one abandons the latent defilements (<s>kleśānuśaya</s>). As stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'The monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>) cultivates: this is form (<s>rūpa</s>), this is the origination of form, this is the cessation of form — for one who always sees and comprehends the <s>Dharma</s>, the defilements are abandoned.' Therefore it should be known that the destruction of defilements is through the insight into the truth of cessation. The five aggregates are suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>); from them the defilements arise. When one sees the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and pacification of the five aggregates, then the perception of suffering (<s>duḥkhasaṃjñā</s>) is fully accomplished. Therefore it is known that when one sees the cessation of the aggregates, the defilements are destroyed. As it is stated: 'Not grasping at phenomena, relying on a single mind of equanimity (<s>upekṣācitta</s>) whose nature is bodilessness (<s>akāyasvabhāva</s>), there is abandonment.' The nature of bodilessness is itself cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). One who sees form as bodiless in nature, up to consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) as bodiless in nature — that one becomes a partaker of ultimate separation (<s>atyantavisaṃyoga</s>). The three gates of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>) are the conditions for <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Through these very gates of liberation one abandons the defilements, not by other means. Therefore it is known that the path whose object is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) alone abandons the defilements. Therefore the method of abandoning defilements stated by you is not correct.

body.text: śāstramāha- kleśānāmevaṃjātīyānāmapramāṇāni viklapasvabhāvāni bhavanti [iti] vimuktiprārthibhirjñātavyam | kasmāt | etadbandhadoṣajñānabalādvimucyate | yadā kaścicchatruṃ vijñāya dūrīkaroti | yathā vā viṣamamārgaṃ jñātvā varjayati | evaṃ kleśānapi | kleśabandho 'tisūkṣmo vemacitramasurarājaṃ bavandha | yāvadbhavāgraṃ satvāḥ kleśabaddhāḥ | ato jñātavyaṃ teṣāmādīnavam | sattvā yādadbhavāgramājavañjavapatitāḥ | yataḥ kleśānāmādīnavajñānaṃ na paśyanti | aprahīṇasaṃyojanatvādaprahīṇa ātmamāno vardhate | tatastu vimatikaukṛtye bhavataḥ | ataḥ kleśadoṣairmā vañcitaḥ syāmiti jñātavyam | yat satvā viśuddhaṃ paramaṃ nirvāṇasukhamupekṣante pratyutātitucchaṃ kāmasukhaṃ bhavasukhaṃ kāmayante tadidaṃ sarvaṃ kleśānāṃ doṣaḥ | yadā kleśān
body.translated_text: The treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) states: It should be known by those who seek liberation (<s>vimukti</s>) that the defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) of the same type are immeasurable and of the nature of conceptual discrimination (<s>vikalpa</s>). Why? Because through the knowledge of the faults of this bondage, one is liberated. Just as when someone, having recognized an enemy, keeps him at a distance; or just as one, having known a dangerous path, avoids it — so too with the defilements. The bondage of defilements is extremely subtle — it bound <s>Vemacitra</s>, the king of the <s>Asuras</s>. Beings are bound by defilements up to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). Therefore one should know the danger of these [defilements]. Beings fall headlong all the way up to the summit of existence because they do not see the knowledge of the danger of defilements. Because the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) are not abandoned, self-conceit (<s>ātmamāna</s>) that has not been abandoned increases. From that arise doubt and regret (<s>vimati</s>, <s>kaukṛtya</s>). Therefore one should know: 'May I not be deceived by the faults of the defilements.' That beings disregard the pure, supreme bliss of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and instead desire the trifling pleasure of sensuality (<s>kāmasukha</s>) and the pleasure of existence (<s>bhavasukha</s>) — all this is the fault of the defilements. When one abandons the defilements

body.text: prajahāti tadā mahāhitaṃ pratilabhante | ataḥ kleśadoṣāṇāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ kuryāt | vimukterāvaraṇadharmā yaduta kleśāḥ | kleśānāmaprahāṇe naivāsti vimuktinidānam | kasmāt | kleśāḥ kāmanidānam | kleśānuyāyī kāyo bhavati | kāyānuyāyi duḥkham | ato duḥkhaviyogārthī kleśānāṃ prahāṇāya vīryamārabheta ||
body.translated_text: one attains great benefit. Therefore one should cultivate the knowledge and vision of the faults of the defilements. The defilements are the obstructing factors (<s>āvaraṇadharma</s>) of liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). Without the abandonment of defilements, there is simply no basis for liberation. Why? The defilements are the cause of [rebirth in] existence (<s>kāma</s>). The body follows after the defilements. Suffering follows after the body. Therefore, one who desires separation from suffering should exert effort (<s>vīrya</s>) for the abandonment of the defilements.

body.text: kleśaprahāṇavarga ekonacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and thirty-ninth chapter, the Chapter on the Abandonment of Defilements (<s>kleśaprahāṇavarga</s>).

body.text: 140 vidyāhetuvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 140. Chapter on the Cause of Knowledge (<s>vidyāhetuvarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) kleśāḥ kāyasya nidānamityetadvidyā syāt | kasmāt | tīrthikā hi nedaṃ śraddadhante | kecidāhuḥ- kāyo 'hetuko 'pratyayaḥ, tṛṇavṛkṣavat svayaṃbhūta iti | kecidāhuḥ - padārthā maheśvarādibhiḥ sṛṣṭā iti | kecidāhuḥ- padārthāḥ kālasvabhāvajāḥ iti | kecidāhuḥ- paramāṇusamavāyajā iti | evaṃjātīyavacanāni vidyā syuḥ | (u) karmaṇaḥ kāyo bhavatīdaṃ pūrvameva sādhitam | tatkarma kleśebhyaḥ sambhūtam | ataḥ kleśāḥ kāyasya nidānam |
body.translated_text: (Objection) That the defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) are the cause of the body — would this be knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>)? Why? For the non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthika</s>) do not accept this. Some say: The body is without cause and without conditions, self-arisen like grass and trees. Some say: Things are created by <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) and others. Some say: Things arise from time (<s>kāla</s>) and inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). Some say: They arise from the combination of atoms (<s>paramāṇusamavāya</s>). Would statements of this kind be knowledge? (Reply) That the body comes from action (<s>karma</s>) — this has already been established previously. That action arises from the defilements. Therefore the defilements are the cause of the body.

body.text: (pṛ) kathaṃ jñāyate kleśahetukaṃ karmeti | (u) prajñapticittamavidyetyucyate | prajñapticittakaḥ karmāṇyupacinoti | ato jñāyate kleśapratyayaṃ karma bhavatīti | arhanna karmāṇyupacinoti na niṣpādayati | ato jñāyate karmāṇi kleśasiddhānīti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatāsūtre- yaḥ pratilabdhavidyaḥ sanyastāvidyaḥ sa kiṃ pāpakaṃ karma puṇyaṃ karma āneñjyañca karma karoti na vā | no bhagavan iti | nāsti cānāsravaṃ karma | ato jñāyate prajñaptyanuyāyī kevalaṃ karmāṇi karotīti | anāsravaṃ cittaṃ na prajñaptimavalambata iti na karmāṇi karoti | śaikṣasya nāsti caryā | yathoktaṃ sūtre- śaikṣajanaḥ pratyāgataṃ nācarati, niruddhaṃ na karotīti | kriyālakṣaṇā hi caryā | caryaiva karmetyucyate | anāsravaṃ cittañca na caryālakṣaṇamityato nāstyanāsravaṃ karma | tasmāt sarvāṇi kāyavedanīyakarmāṇi kleśahetusambhūtāni | prahīṇakleśo na punarjanmānubhavati | ato jñāyate vidyamānaḥ kāyaḥ kleśahetu[ka] iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) How is it known that <s>karma</s> is caused by defilements (<s>kleśa</s>)? (Answer) The mind of designation (<s>prajñapticittam</s>) is called ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). One with the mind of designation accumulates <s>karmas</s>. Therefore it is known that <s>karma</s> arises through the condition of defilements. An <s>Arhat</s> does not accumulate <s>karmas</s> nor bring them to completion. Therefore it is known that <s>karmas</s> are accomplished through defilements. As the Blessed One stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who has obtained knowledge and has laid down ignorance — does he or does he not perform sinful <s>karma</s>, meritorious <s>karma</s>, and imperturbable <s>karma</s>?' 'No, Blessed One.' And there is no outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>karma</s>. Therefore it is known that one who follows designation alone performs <s>karmas</s>. The outflow-free mind does not rely on designation, and therefore does not perform <s>karmas</s>. For the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), there is no conduct. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The learner does not practice what has returned; he does not perform what has ceased.' For conduct has the characteristic of action. Conduct itself is called <s>karma</s>. And the outflow-free mind does not have the characteristic of conduct — therefore there is no outflow-free <s>karma</s>. Therefore all bodily <s>karmas</s> that produce experience arise from the cause of defilements. One whose defilements are abandoned does not experience further birth. Therefore it is known that the existing body is caused by defilements.

body.text: (pṛ) sarve sattvā akleśatayā jāyante | paścāttu kleśāḥ samudbhavanti | yathā puruṣasya jananakāle 'vidyamānaṃ daśanaṃ paścādutpadyate | (u) na yukta[mida]m | kleśavāneva
body.translated_text: (Question) All beings are born without defilements. Afterward, the defilements arise — just as a person's teeth do not exist at birth but appear later. (Answer) This is not correct. One who has defilements alone

body.text: [jāyate] yatra bhavalakṣaṇaṃ kvarodanādi jananakāle pratyakṣamasti | ato jñāyate kleśaiḥ sahaiva sarve jāyanta iti | pratyakṣaṃ paśyāmaḥ khalu sattvā bahavo varcaḥkuṭyādiṣu prasūyante na tu śilādiṣu | gandharasādyāsaṅgāttatra prasūyanta iti draṣṭavyam | ato jñāyate kleśavaśādutpadyanta iti | (pṛ) narakādau na janma labheran | kasmāt | na hi kaścinarakādau sukhaṃ kāmayeta | (u) mohabalādviparyayacittā utpadyante | mriyamāṇā dūrato narakaṃ dṛṣṭvā idaṃ padmasara iti tadāsaṅgāttatrotpadyante | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo nibiḍitasthāne vipulaṃ sthānaṃ labheyamiti mriyate sa pakṣiṣūtpadyate | yaḥ paritarṣito mriyate sa jalajanturjāyate | yaḥ śītārto mriyate sa tapananarake jāyate | yastāpatarṣito mriyate sa śītanarake jāyate | yo maithunakāmāsaktaḥ sa caṭakeṣu jāyate | ya āhārāsaktaḥ sa kuṇapeṣu kīṭo jāyate | iti | kāmāsaṅgahetunā akuśalāni karoti | akuśalapratyayadārḍhyātphalavipākaṃ vedayate | kāyāsaktyā karmāṇi vipākajanakāni | kasmāt | kāyāsaktasya mohabalānmānādayaḥ kleśā jāyante | tataḥ karmaṇi sañcinoti | karmabalādgatiṣūtpadyate |
body.translated_text: is born — for the characteristics of becoming (<s>bhava</s>), such as crying and the like at the time of birth, are directly perceived. Therefore it is known that all beings are born together with defilements. We see directly that many beings are born in latrines and the like, but not on rocks and the like. It should be understood that they are born there because of attachment to smells, tastes, and the like. Therefore it is known that they are born under the power of defilements. (Question) One should not obtain birth in the hells and the like. Why? For no one desires happiness in the hells and the like. (Answer) Through the power of delusion (<s>moha</s>), they are born with perverted minds. When dying, seeing hell from afar, [thinking] 'This is a lotus pond,' through attachment to it they are born there. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who, in a confined place, dies wishing to obtain a spacious place — he is born among birds. One who dies parched with thirst — he is born as an aquatic creature. One who dies afflicted by cold — he is born in the Heating (<s>tapana</s>) hell. One who dies tormented by heat and thirst — he is born in the Cold (<s>śīta</s>) hell. One who is attached to sexual intercourse — he is born among sparrows. One who is attached to food — he is born as a worm in corpses.' Through the cause of attachment to sensual pleasures, one performs unwholesome deeds. Through the firmness of the unwholesome condition, one experiences the ripening of the fruit. Through attachment to the body, <s>karmas</s> produce ripening. Why? For one attached to the body, through the power of delusion, conceit and other defilements arise. From those, one accumulates <s>karma</s>. Through the power of <s>karma</s>, one is born in the [various] destinies.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi kleśapratyayena kāyo bhavati | prahīṇakleśasya pañcaskandhasantāno na syāt | (u) kāyo 'yaṃ pūrvaṃ kleśajātaḥ | [idānīṃ] kleśeṣu prahīṇeṣvapi tadvegabalātkāyaḥ punarna prahīyate | yathā daṇḍena cakrabhramaṇam | muhūrtaṃ daṇḍe viramatyapi [cakram] bhramatyeva na tu śāmyati | (pṛ) yadi pūrvakarmakleśavegātkāyo bhavati | tadā prahīṇakleśaḥ pūrvakarmakleśavegātpunaḥ kāyamupādadyāt | (u) nimittagrahādvijñānamavaśyaṃ tiṣṭhati | ayaṃ prakṣīṇapūrvakarmavegaḥ | idānīmanimittavimokṣamukhaṃ bhāvayan nordhvadehamupādatte | yathā tatpapāṣāṇe na bījāni prarohanti | evaṃ jñānāgninā vijñānasthitiṣu dagdhāsu na vijñānabījaṃ prarohati |
body.translated_text: (Question) If the body arises through the condition of defilements, then one whose defilements are abandoned would not have the continuity of the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>). (Answer) This body was previously born from defilements. Even now, when defilements have been abandoned, through the momentum of that [prior] force, the body is not abandoned again — just as a wheel is set in motion by a stick. Even when the stick stops for a moment, the wheel continues to spin and does not stop. (Question) If the body exists through the momentum of prior <s>karma</s> and defilements, then one whose defilements are abandoned would, through the momentum of prior <s>karma</s> and defilements, take up a body again. (Answer) Because of grasping at signs (<s>nimittagraha</s>), consciousness necessarily persists. [But] this one's prior <s>karma</s>-momentum is exhausted. Now, cultivating the signless gateway to liberation (<s>animittavimokṣamukha</s>), he does not take up a further body — just as seeds do not sprout on a rock. In the same way, when the stations of consciousness have been burned by the fire of knowledge, the seed of consciousness does not sprout.

body.text: ūrdhvasantānaḥ samucchidyate | saṃskārapratyayavaikalyāt na punaḥ santāno bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre bhagavatā- vijñānaṃ bījam | karmasaṃskārāḥ kṣetram | rāgatṛṣṇā salilam | avidyā avakiraṇam | ebhiḥ pratyayairāyatyāṃ kāyamupādatta iti | arhatastveṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ vaikalyānnāyatyāṃ kāyo bhavati iti jñātavyaṃ kleśapratyayā kāyavedaneti | vigatakleśasya duḥkhajñānādicittamasti | idānīmupapattivedako na paśyati taccittamastīti | ato jñāyate vigatakleśo nopapatiṃ vedayata iti | (pṛ) srotaāpannādināṃ duḥkhādicittamasti | ta upapattikāle 'pi na paśyanti astīti | (u) arhatāṃ jñānabalaṃ sudṛḍham | sarve 'pi kleśā notkarṣanti | ato mriyamāṇā upapattivedanāṃ pratighnanti | srotaāpannādīnāṃ jñānabalantu na tathā | ato na dṛṣṭāntaḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: The further continuity is cut off. Because of the deficiency of the condition of formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), there is no further continuity. As the Blessed One stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Consciousness is the seed. <s>Karma</s>-formations are the field. Craving and passion (<s>rāgatṛṣṇā</s>) are the water. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the covering.' Through these conditions, one takes up a body in the future. But for the <s>Arhat</s>, because of the deficiency of these conditions, there is no future body. Thus it should be known that the body is conditioned by defilements. One who is free from defilements has the mind of knowledge of suffering and the like. Now, one who experiences rebirth does not perceive that mind as existing. Therefore it is known that one free from defilements does not experience rebirth. (Question) Stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) and the like have the mind of knowledge of suffering and the like. They too, at the time of rebirth, do not perceive it as existing. (Answer) The power of knowledge of <s>Arhats</s> is very firm. All defilements whatsoever do not stir [them]. Therefore, when dying, they destroy the experience of rebirth. But the power of knowledge of stream-enterers and the like is not like that. Therefore [their case] does not serve as a counter-example.

body.text: bhavatoktaṃ yathā daśanaṃ paścātkrameṇa bhavati tathā kleśā apīti | idamayuktam | kasmāt | arhanto 'nāsravaprajñādadghakleśā ityato notpadyeran | yathā dagdhaṃ bījaṃ na punaḥ prarohati | pratyakṣaṃ khalu loke 'smin kleśajaḥ kāya iti | yathā kāmarāgātkāyarūpaṃ vikriyate | tathā dveṣādapi | ato jñāyate āyatyāṃ pañcaskandhā api kleśajā iti |
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'just as teeth appear gradually later, so too do defilements' — this is incorrect. Why? Because <s>Arhats</s>, their defilements having been burned by outflow-free wisdom (<s>anāsravaprajñā</s>), would not arise again — just as a burned seed does not sprout again. We see directly in this world that the body is born from defilements. Just as the bodily form is transformed through the passion of sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>), so too through hatred. Therefore it is known that the five aggregates in the future too are born from defilements.

body.text: (pṛ) paśyāmaḥ khalu āhārapratyayāḥ pañcaskandhā utpadyante | tathāpi nocyate āhāraḥ kāyavedanāpratyaya iti | (u) āhāraścittaprajñaptito rūpādīnāṃ janakaḥ | kleśāstu na tathā, aprajñaptito rūpādijanakāḥ | ato jñāyate kleśāḥ kāyapratyayā iti | pratyakṣaṃ khalu caṭakādayaḥ kāmabahulāḥ, sarpādayo dveṣabahulāḥ, sūkarādayo mohabahulāḥ | jñātavyamime sattvā avaśyaṃ pūrvābhyāsasañcitamaithunarāgādikleśā ityatasteṣūtpadyanta iti | (pṛ) utpattisthāna dharmastathā na tu pūrvābhyāsasañcitakleśahetukam | (u) tathā cainmaithunarāgādayo nirhetukāḥ syuḥ | nedaṃ sambhavati | iti jñātavyaṃ pūrvābhyāsasañcitahetunā bhavatīti | kāmakrodhādiṣu kleśeṣūddīpiteṣu hananādipāpāni kurvanti | tebhyaḥ pāpebhyo dṛṣṭa eva badhabandhanādiduḥkhamanu bhavanti | kleśeṣvalpeṣu śīladhāraṇakuśalābhyāsādihitaṃ labhante | tatkuśalaśīlamupādāya dṛṣṭa eva khyātiyaśolābhasatkārādisukhaṃ labhante | yatheha loke lābho hāniśca kleśahetukā, tathāmuṣminnapyevamiti jñāyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) We see that the five aggregates arise through the condition of food (<s>āhāra</s>). Yet it is not said that food is the condition for the experience of the body. (Answer) Food, through the designation of mind, generates form and the like. But defilements are not like that — they generate form and the like without [mere] designation. Therefore it is known that defilements are the condition of the body. We see directly that sparrows and the like are abundant in sensual desire, serpents and the like are abundant in hatred, pigs and the like are abundant in delusion. It should be known that these beings necessarily have defilements of sexual passion and the like accumulated through prior habituation — therefore they are born among those [species]. (Question) It is the nature of the place of birth, not the cause of defilements accumulated through prior habituation. (Answer) If that were so, sexual passion and the like would be without cause. This is not possible. Therefore it should be known that it arises through the cause accumulated by prior habituation. When defilements such as sensual desire, anger, and the like are inflamed, [beings] commit sins such as killing and the like. From those sins, they experience suffering such as imprisonment, bondage, and the like in this very present life. When defilements are slight, through the practice of maintaining moral conduct, wholesome habituation, and the like, they obtain benefit. Through that wholesome conduct, in this very present life they obtain happiness such as fame, reputation, gain, honor, and the like. Just as in this world gain and loss are caused by defilements, so too in the other world — thus it is known.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi kleśahetukaḥ kāyo bhavati | tadā samucchidyeta saṃsāre gatāgatam | kasmāt | kleśavivṛddhyā durgatau patati sa eva pāpakāyamanubhūya kleśān punarvardhayati | sadā ca vimuktiheturahitaḥ | evañca na susthāne janma labheta | yadi puṇyavardhanāya
body.translated_text: (Question) If the body is caused by defilements, then the coming and going in <s>saṃsāra</s> would be cut off. Why? Through the increase of defilements, one falls into a bad destiny. That very [being], having experienced a sinful body, increases the defilements again. And he is always devoid of the cause of liberation. Thus he would not obtain birth in a good place. If, for the increase of merit

body.text: puṇyakāyamupādate | tadā punarapi na dusthāna utpadyeta | evañca na syātsaṃsāre gatāgatam | (u) jano 'yaṃ durgatau patito 'pi kadācitkuśalacittabhāgbhavati | susthāna utpanno 'pi kadācidakuśalacittamutpādayati | ataḥ saṃsāre gatāgataṃ na samucchidyate | rāgādikleśānāṃ tanutvataḥ susthāne janmānuvartate | teṣāmeva mahatvato duḥsthāne janmānuvartate yathā sūkaraśvādayaḥ | alpakeśatvataḥ susthāne jāyata iti yathā [kaścit] kleśatanutvāt dānaśīlādikarmācaran ṣaṭsu kāmadeveṣūtpadyate | prahīṇābrahmacaryārāgatvādviśiṣṭadhyānasukhaṃ pratilabhate | prahīṇarūpasaṃkleśatvādviśiṣṭasamādhisukhaṃ pratilabhate | sarvasaṃyojanānāṃ kṣaye 'nupamaṃ nirvāṇasukhaṃ pratilabhate | ato jñāyate kāyo 'yaṃ kleśahetuka iti |
body.translated_text: he takes up a meritorious body, then again he would not be born in a bad place. Thus there would be no coming and going in <s>saṃsāra</s>. (Answer) This person, even though fallen into a bad destiny, sometimes develops a wholesome mind. And one born in a good place sometimes generates an unwholesome mind. Therefore the coming and going in <s>saṃsāra</s> is not cut off. Through the thinning of defilements such as passion and the like, birth continues in good places. Through the greatness of those very [defilements], birth continues in bad places — as in the case of pigs and dogs and the like. Through the smallness of defilements, one is born in good places — as when someone, through the thinning of defilements, practicing giving, moral conduct, and other <s>karmas</s>, is born among the six desire-realm gods (<s>kāmadeva</s>). Through the abandonment of passion for sensual misconduct, one obtains the distinguished happiness of <s>dhyāna</s>. Through the abandonment of the defilements of the form realm, one obtains the distinguished happiness of <s>samādhi</s>. Upon the destruction of all fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), one obtains the incomparable happiness of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore it is known that this body is caused by defilements.

body.text: paśyāmaḥ khalu sattvā kudeśabhūmau ratā durjanaiḥ saha kutsitamadhivasantīti sarvamāsaṅgādbhavati | ato jñāyate saṃsāre sattvānāmadhivāso 'pyāsaṅgādbhavati | yathā śalabhā bhāsvararūparāgātpradīpadagdhā bhavanti | āsaktiriyaṃ na jñānadbhavati | kasmāt | śalabhā ime na jānanti agnirduḥkhasparśa ityatastatra patanti | tathā sattvāḥ paunarbhavikaduḥkhapatitā avidyāpratyayakāmatṛṣṇārta utpadyante | yathā matsyā aṅkuśaṃ grasantaḥ, hariṇāḥ śabdānu cāriṇaḥ | te sarve kāmāsaṅgānmriyante | yathā ca kaścit kāmāsaktyā viprakṛṣṭāṃ vidiśaṃ gacchan na pratinivartate | tat sarvaṃ kleśājjātamiti draṣṭavyam | yathā vṛkṣasya mūle 'nunmūlite sa vṛkṣaḥ punaḥ prarohati | tathā rāgamūle 'nunmūlite duḥkhavṛkṣa sadā vartate | yathāha bhagavān-
body.translated_text: We see indeed that beings delight in bad lands and terrains, dwelling wretchedly together with wicked people — all of this comes from attachment. Therefore it is known that the dwelling of beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> too comes from attachment. Just as moths, through passion for a luminous form, are burned by a lamp — this attachment does not come from knowledge. Why? Because these moths do not know that 'fire is a painful contact,' and therefore they fall into it. In the same way, beings who have fallen into the suffering of repeated existence (<s>punarbhava</s>), tormented by craving for sensual pleasures (<s>kāmatṛṣṇā</s>) conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), are born [again]. Just as fish swallow the hook, and deer follow [enticing] sounds — they all die because of attachment to sensual pleasures. And just as someone, through attachment to sensual pleasures, goes to a distant region and does not return — all of that should be seen as born from defilements. Just as when the root of a tree is not uprooted, that tree sprouts again, so when the root of passion (<s>rāga</s>) is not uprooted, the tree of suffering always persists. As the Blessed One said:

body.text:
yathāpi mūle 'nupadrute dṛḍhe cchinno 'pi vṛkṣaḥ punareva rohati |
evamapi tṛṣṇānuśaye 'nuddhṛte nirvartayati duḥkhamidaṃ punaḥ punaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
Just as when the root is undamaged and firm, a tree though cut grows again;
so too, when the latent tendency of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is not uprooted, this suffering arises again and again.

body.text: kāyo 'yamaśuciranityo duḥkhaṃ śūnyo 'nātmakaḥ | svato 'vidyāṃ vinā ko jñānī tat vyayaduḥkhaṃ kāmayamāno vedayeta | yathāndho malinavāso ratnābharaṇamiti pralobhitaḥ syāt | tathāvidyāndhībhūta ādīnavabahulānaśucīn pañcaskandhānanubhavati | ātmamatyā duḥkhamapi kāyamanubhavan na tyajati | anātmabuddhau tu prajahāti | yathāha śāriputraḥ- viśuddhasaṃvara- pratilabdhamārgo mriyamāṇo 'bhinandati | tadyathā viṣakumbhe bhagne | ato
body.translated_text: This body is impure, impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self. Without ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), what wise person would desire and experience the suffering of its decay? Just as a blind person might be deceived [into thinking] that a soiled garment is a jeweled ornament, so one blinded by ignorance experiences the impure five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) that are full of danger. Through the notion of self, even while experiencing a body that is suffering, one does not abandon it. But with the understanding of non-self, one relinquishes it. As <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'One who has pure restraint, who has obtained the path, rejoices when dying — just as when a vessel of poison is broken.' Therefore

body.text: jñāyate kleśapratyayo 'yaṃ kāya iti | ajñānādasmin kāya āsajyate | yathā citrakāraṇḍo 'śucisamṛddhaḥ | anapāvṛto ramaṇīyaḥ | apāvṛte tu pūtitṛṇāni [dṛśyante] | yathā viṣasarpasampūrṇe gṛhaprakoṣṭhe 'prajvalite ca dīpe sukhādhyavasānaṃ bhavati | [viṣasarpa]darśane tu tadapaiti | tathā sattvā api avidyāyāṃ satyāṃ loke 'bhiramante | utpannāyāntu vidyāyāṃ cittaṃ nirvidyate | evaṃ kāmatṛṣṇā bhavasya mūlam | kasmāt | kāmatṛṣṇayā hi prārthayate | prārthanā hi dvividhā- kāmaprārthanā bhavaprārthanā iti | pratyutpanneṣu kāmeṣu prārthanā kāmaprārthanā | punarbhavaprārthanā bhavaprārthanā | ato jñāyate kāmatṛṣṇā bhavasya mūlamiti | pañcaskandhāsaktau satkāyadṛṣṭirutpadyate yadutāhamityātmavādopādānam | tadupādānamupādāyānyāni trīṇyupādānāni bhavanti | upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ | bhavapratyayā jātiriti jñātavyaṃ kleśāḥ kāyasya mūlamiti |
body.translated_text: it is known that this body is conditioned by defilements. Through ignorance, one becomes attached to this body. Just as a decorated basket is filled with impurities — when unopened it appears delightful, but when opened, rotten grass is seen. Just as in a room of a house filled with poisonous snakes, when the lamp is not lit, there is the settling into happiness; but upon seeing the poisonous snakes, that [happiness] departs. In the same way, when ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) exists, beings delight in the world. But when knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) has arisen, the mind becomes disenchanted. Thus, craving for sensual pleasures (<s>kāmatṛṣṇā</s>) is the root of becoming (<s>bhava</s>). Why? Because through craving for sensual pleasures, one yearns. Yearning is of two kinds: yearning for sensual pleasures (<s>kāmaprārthanā</s>) and yearning for existence (<s>bhavaprārthanā</s>). Yearning for present sensual pleasures is craving for sensual pleasures. Yearning for further existence is craving for existence. Therefore it is known that craving for sensual pleasures is the root of becoming. When there is attachment to the five aggregates, the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) arises — namely, the clinging to the doctrine of self (<s>ātmavādopādāna</s>) as 'I.' Depending on that clinging, the other three clingings (<s>upādāna</s>) come into being. Existence (<s>bhava</s>) is conditioned by clinging. Birth (<s>jāti</s>) is conditioned by existence. Thus it should be known that defilements are the root of the body.

body.text: kāyo 'yaṃ duḥkham | duḥkhakāye 'smin sukhasaṃjñāviparyaya utpadyate | tena sukhaviparyayeṇa viparītatṛṣṇā pravartate | tathā viparītatṛṣṇayā punarbhavaṃ vedayate | ato jñāyate kāmatṛṣṇāpratyayaḥ kāyo bhavatīti | kāyo 'yamāhārapratyayāttiṣṭhati | kabalīkārāhārāsaktyā na kāmadhātumativartate | yathoktaṃ karmaskandhe- gandharasāsaktyā varcaḥkuṭyādiṣūtpadyate | spraṣṭavyāsaktyā garbhāvāsa utpadyate | śītoṣṇasparśāsaktyā aṇḍajaḥ svedajo vā bhavati | iti sarve na kāmadhātumatikrāmanti | dhātusparśamupādāya tisro vedanā bhavanti | ataḥ sparśapratyayā vedanetyucyate | manaḥsañcetanāhāro 'pyevam | punarbhavasamutthānāya praṇidadhāti idamahaṃ kariṣyāmīti | jñādarśanavihīnaṃ vijñānaṃ punarbhavaprāpakakāmatṛṣṇāmūlaṃ bhavati | evaṃ catvāra āhārāḥ kāmatṛṣṇādhīnāḥ | sarve hi sattvā āhāreṇa jīvanti | ato jñāyate tṛṣṇāpratyayā jātiriti |
body.translated_text: This body is suffering. In this body of suffering, the perversion of the perception of pleasure (<s>sukhasaṃjñāviparyaya</s>) arises. Through that perversion of pleasure, perverted craving (<s>viparītatṛṣṇā</s>) operates. Likewise, through perverted craving, one experiences renewed existence (<s>punarbhava</s>). From this it is known that the body arises through the condition of sensual craving (<s>kāmatṛṣṇā</s>). This body persists through the condition of nutriment (<s>āhāra</s>). Through attachment to material food (<s>kabalīkārāhāra</s>), one does not transcend the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). As stated in the Chapter on <s>Karma</s>: 'Through attachment to smell and taste, one is born in cesspits and the like. Through attachment to tangible objects, one is born in the womb-abode. Through attachment to the contact of cold and heat, one becomes egg-born or moisture-born.' Thus, all do not transcend the desire realm. Depending on the contact of the sense-elements (<s>dhātu</s>), three feelings arise. Therefore it is said: 'Feeling is conditioned by contact.' The nutriment of mental volition (<s>manaḥsañcetanāhāra</s>) is likewise. One resolves for the arising of renewed existence: 'I shall do this.' Consciousness devoid of knowledge and vision, having sensual craving as its root, leads to renewed existence. Thus the four nutriments are dependent on sensual craving. For all beings live by nutriment. From this it is known that birth is conditioned by craving.

body.text: catasro jātayaḥ- aṇḍajo jarāyujaḥ saṃsvedaja upapāduka iti | maithunakāmatṛṣṇayā aṇḍajo jarāyujaśca | gandharasādyāsaṅgāt saṃsvedajopapattiṃ vedayate | yathābhilaṣitaṃ gurukarmopacīya upapādukajanma vedayate | ato jñāyate catvāro jātivibhāgāḥ kāmatṛṣṇādhīnā iti | catasraḥ kāyavedanāḥ- kaścidātmaghātako na paraghātaka ityādayaścatasraḥ | tāḥ
body.translated_text: The four kinds of birth are: egg-born (<s>aṇḍaja</s>), womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>), moisture-born (<s>saṃsvedaja</s>), and spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>). Through the sensual craving for sexual intercourse, one becomes egg-born or womb-born. Through attachment to smell, taste, and the like, one experiences moisture-born rebirth. Through the accumulation of weighty <s>karma</s> as desired, one experiences spontaneous birth. From this it is known that the four divisions of birth are dependent on sensual craving. The four bodily feelings are: one who kills himself but not others, and so forth — these four. They

body.text: sarvāḥ kāmatṛṣṇāviśeṣā bhavanti | ato jñāyate kāmatṛṣṇāpratyayaḥ kāyo bhavatīti | catasro vijñānasthitayaḥ- rūpopagaṃ vijñānaṃ tiṣṭhat rūpapratiṣṭhitaṃ rūpārambaṇaṃ nandyupasevanam | vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāreṣvapyevam | na tūcyate vijñānameva vijñānasthitiriti | vijñānakāle kleśābhāvāt | ato jñāyate kleśapratyayaḥ kāyo bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: are all varieties of sensual craving. From this it is known that the body arises through the condition of sensual craving. The four stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>) are: consciousness established in form, supported by form, with form as its object, sustained by delight. Likewise with feeling, perception, and formations. But it is not said that consciousness itself is a station of consciousness. Because at the time of consciousness, defilements are absent. From this it is known that the body arises through the condition of defilements.

body.text: dvādaśanidānāni cāvidyādhīnāni | kasmāt | prajñaptyanuyāyicittamavidyā | tāmavidyāmupādāya pravartate [karma]puṇyopagamapuṇyopagamāneñjyopagam | kāmasaṃlālitaṃ puṇyopagam | duḥkhasampīḍitamapuṇyopagam | maitrīkaruṇādicittasaṅgṛhītamāneñjyopagam | teṣāṃ karmaṇāmanugāmivijñānaṃ punarbhave tiṣṭhati | vijñānaṃ niśritya bhavanti nāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanasparśavedanāḥ | imāni catvāri pūrvādhvanīnakarmakleśavipākāḥ | punarimāṃ vedanāmupādāya pravartate tṛṣṇopādānaṃ bhavaḥ | ime karmakleśā āyatyāṃ jātijarāmaraṇādīnyutpādayanti | evaṃ dvādaśāṅgabhavasantatiravidyāmūlikā | ato jñāyate kleśapratyayaḥ kāyo bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: The twelve links of dependent origination (<s>dvādaśanidāna</s>) are also dependent on ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Why? Ignorance is the mind that follows conceptual designation (<s>prajñapti</s>). Depending on that ignorance, [<s>karma</s>] operates — meritorious (<s>puṇyopaga</s>), demeritorious (<s>apuṇyopaga</s>), and imperturbable (<s>āneñjyopaga</s>). What is fostered by sensual pleasure is meritorious. What is afflicted by suffering is demeritorious. What is embraced by the mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and the like is imperturbable. The consciousness that accompanies those <s>karmas</s> is established in renewed existence. Depending on consciousness, there arise name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>), the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), and feeling (<s>vedanā</s>). These four are the ripening of <s>karma</s> and defilements of the past life. Again, depending on this feeling, craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), and existence (<s>bhava</s>) operate. These are the <s>karma</s> and defilements that in the future produce birth (<s>jāti</s>), old age, death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>), and the rest. Thus the continuity of the twelve-linked existence has ignorance as its root. From this it is known that the body arises through the condition of defilements.

body.text: saṃsāro 'nādiḥ | kenedaṃ jñāyate | uktaṃ hi sūtre- karmapratyayāni cakṣurādīnīndriyāṇi | karma tṛṣṇāhetukam | tṛṣṇā avidyāhetukā | avidyā ayoniśomanaskārahetukā | ayoniśomanaskāraścakṣurhetuko rūpapratyayo mohātpravṛtta iti | ato jñāyate saṃsāracakramanādīti | īśvarādayaḥ kāraṇamiti vadato na bhavatyanādiḥ | tattu na sambhavati | ato jñāyate kleśapratyayaḥ kāya iti | kleśānāmātyantikanirodhe vimuktirlabhyate | sattvānāṃ dehā nānā vijātīyāḥ | īśvarādīkāraṇatve vaijātyaṃ na syāt | kleśakarmaṇāṃ bahuvidhatvāt dehā api naike |
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> is beginningless. How is this known? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The sense-faculties such as the eye and the rest are conditioned by <s>karma</s>. <s>Karma</s> has craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) as its cause. Craving has ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) as its cause. Ignorance has unwise attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>) as its cause. And unwise attention has the eye as its cause, form as its condition, and proceeds from delusion.' From this it is known that the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless. Those who say that God (<s>Īśvara</s>) and the like are the cause — for them it would not be beginningless. But that is not tenable. From this it is known that the body arises through the condition of defilements. Through the complete cessation of defilements, liberation is obtained. The bodies of sentient beings are of various, diverse kinds. If God and the like were the cause, there would be no such diversity. Because <s>karma</s> and defilements are of many kinds, bodies too are not of a single kind.

body.text: dvāviṃśatāvindriyeṣu ṣaḍindriyāṇyupādāya ṣaḍvijñānāni bhavanti | tatrāsti strīpuruṣendriyam | sarvadharmāṇāmeṣāṃ santatyavicchedāt jīvitamityucyate | jīvitaṃ kasyendriyaṃ bhavati, yaduta karmaṇaḥ | karmedaṃ kleśānāṃ hetuḥ | kleśā vedanāniśritā ityataḥ pañca vedanā indriyāṇi bhavanti | evamanyonya[hetu] pravṛttā saṃsārasantatiḥ | śraddhādīnīndriyāṇi
body.translated_text: Among the twenty-two faculties (<s>indriya</s>), depending on the six faculties, the six consciousnesses arise. Therein, there are the female faculty (<s>strīndriya</s>) and the male faculty (<s>puruṣendriya</s>). Because the continuity of all <s>dharmas</s> is uninterrupted, it is called 'life' (<s>jīvita</s>). Whose faculty is this life? It is the faculty of <s>karma</s>. This <s>karma</s> is the cause of defilements. Defilements are based on feeling — therefore the five feelings are faculties. Thus, the continuity of <s>saṃsāra</s> proceeds through mutual causation. Depending on the faculties of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the rest,

body.text: niśritya santatiṃ vicchedayati | evaṃ dvāviṃśatīndriyaiḥ saṃsāre yātyāyāti ca | ato jñāyate kleśaiḥ kāyo bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: one severs the continuity. Thus, through the twenty-two faculties, one goes and comes in <s>saṃsāra</s>. From this it is known that the body arises through the condition of defilements.
