(Reply:) That is not so. Why? All final mind-moments that arise dependent on visual consciousness would [then] recollect. They would never forget. Because they have arisen [from that condition].

body.text: na vastuto yujyate | ato jñāyate manovijñānamapi nānusmarati | yathākāśānusmaraṇam, rūpaghaṭādigrahaḥ | sarve 'pi padārthastucchā abhāvātmakāḥ mṛṣāgṛhītāḥ | ataḥ sarve padārthā abhāvātmakāḥ |
body.translated_text: In reality, this does not hold. Therefore it is known that mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) too does not recollect. Like the recollection of space — the grasping of form, pots, and so forth — all objects are empty and of the nature of non-existence, grasped through delusion. Therefore all objects are of the nature of non-existence.

body.text: yadi vadasi cakṣuḥ paśyatīti | kiṃ rūpaṃ prāpya paśyati kiṃ vāprāpya paśyati | yadi prāpya [paśyatīti] tadā na paśyati | cakṣurnātītalakṣaṇamitīdaṃ pūrvameva pratipāditam | yadyaprāpya paśyatīti | tadā sarvasthaṃ rūpaṃ paśyet | na vastutaḥ paśyati | ato jñāyate nāprāpya paśyatīti | (pṛ) rūpaṃ jñānagocaragataṃ cakṣuḥ paśyati | (u) ko nāma jñānagocaraḥ | (pṛ) yasmin kāle cakṣuḥ paśyati | [sa]jñānagocaraḥ ityucyate | (u) yadi cakṣuraprāptamapi jñānagocara ityucyate sarvasthaṃ rūpaṃ jñānagocaraḥ syāt | ataḥ prāpyāprāpyobhayathā na paśyati | ato jñāyate rūpamadṛśyamiti | yadi sati pūrvameva cakṣuṣi rūpe ca paścāccakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | tadedaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ nirāśrayaṃ niṣpratyayañca syāt | yadyekakāla[mutpadyate] tadā na cakṣūrūpapratyayaṃ cakṣurvijñānamityākhyāyate | aikakālikayormitho hetutvābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: If you say the eye sees — does it see form by reaching it or without reaching it? If by reaching [it], then it does not see, for it has already been demonstrated earlier that the eye has the characteristic of not going out. If without reaching [it], then it would see form everywhere. In reality it does not see [everywhere]. Therefore it is known that it does not see without reaching. (Objection:) The eye sees form that has come within the range of cognition. (Reply:) What exactly is the range of cognition? (Objection:) The time when the eye sees — that is called the range of cognition. (Reply:) If even what the eye has not reached is called the range of cognition, then all forms everywhere would be within the range of cognition. Therefore, whether by reaching or not reaching, in both ways it does not see. Therefore it is known that form is invisible. If the eye and form exist first, and visual consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) arises afterward, then this visual consciousness would be without support and without condition. If [they] arise at the same time, then visual consciousness could not be called 'conditioned by the eye and form,' because things that are simultaneous cannot be causes of each other.

body.text: kiñca cakṣuścaturmahābhūta[mayam] | yadi cakṣuḥ paśyati | śrotrādīnyapi paśyeyuḥ | caturmahābhūtasāmyāt | evaṃ rūpamapi [paśyet] | cakṣurvijñānaṃ syāt sāyatanaṃ nirāyatanaṃ vā | ubhayathāsti doṣaḥ | tathā hi- yadi ca cakṣurvijñānaṃ cakṣurāśritaṃ, tadā sāyatanam | yadi padārtho nirāyatanaḥ tadā āśritya tiṣṭhatīti na labhyate | yadi bravīṣi vijñānaṃ cakṣuṣo 'lpabhāga utpadyate yadi vā vyāpyotpadyate | yadi vobhayoścakṣuṣorekakālamutpadyate | tadā sāyatanaṃ bhavati | sāyatanatve sāvayavam | evaṃ sati bahubhirvijñānairekaṃ vijñānaṃ sidhyati | ityayaṃ doṣaḥ | bahūnāṃ vijñānānāmaikakālikatvadoṣaścāsti | ekaikavijñānāvayavo na vijānāti avayavī tu vijānāti | vastutastu nāstyavayavī ityayaṃ doṣaḥ | yadi nirāyatanaṃ, tadā na cakṣurāśritaṃ syāt ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the eye is composed of the four great elements (<s>caturmahābhūta</s>). If the eye sees, then the ear and other [sense faculties] should also see, since they equally consist of the four great elements. Likewise, form too [should see]. Visual consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) would be either with a sense base (<s>sāyatana</s>) or without a sense base (<s>nirāyatana</s>). There is a defect in both cases. For if visual consciousness depends on the eye, then it has a sense base. If an object has no sense base, then one cannot say it 'abides depending on' [the eye]. If you say that consciousness arises in a portion of the eye, or arises pervading it, or arises at the same time in both eyes — then it has a sense base. Having a sense base means having parts (<s>sāvayava</s>). In that case, one consciousness would be established through many consciousnesses. This is the defect. And there is also the defect of the simultaneity of many consciousnesses. Each individual part of consciousness does not cognize, but the composite whole cognizes. But in reality there is no composite whole — this is the defect. If it is without a sense base, then it would not depend on the eye.

body.text: abhāvasthāpanavargaḥ saptacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the establishment of non-existence (<s>abhāvasthāpanavarga</s>), the one hundred and forty-seventh.

body.text: 148 śabdakhaṇḍanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 148. The chapter on the refutation of sound (<s>śabdakhaṇḍanavarga</s>).

body.text: abhāvavādyāha- ekatvagraha eva nāsti | kasmāt | cittaṃ hi kṣaṇikam | śabdo 'pi kṣaṇikaḥ | yathā vadanti puruṣa iti | aya [mekatva]vādo na śrāvyaḥ | kasmāt | "pu" śravaṇamanu vijñānaṃ na "ruṃ" śṛṇoti | "ruṃ" śrutvā śṛṇoti ṣam | iti nāstyekaṃ vijñānamakṣaratrayagrāhakam | ato nāsti vijñānamekatvavādagrāhakam | ato jñāyate śabdo na śrāvya iti | vikṣiptacittaḥ śabdaṃ śṛṇoti | samāhitacittastu na śṛṇoti | samāhitacittena tattvaṃ jñeyaṃ bhavati | ataḥ śabdo na śravaṇīyaḥ | śabdo 'yaṃ prāpya aprāpya vā ubhayathāpi na śravaṇīyaḥ | ubhayathāpyaśravaṇīyatvānnāsti śabdaḥ |
body.translated_text: The proponent of non-existence (<s>abhāvavādin</s>) says: The grasping of unity itself does not exist. Why? Because the mind (<s>citta</s>) is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>). Sound (<s>śabda</s>) too is momentary. For example, when they say '<s>puruṣa</s>' — this doctrine of unity should not be listened to. Why? The consciousness following the hearing of 'pu' does not hear 'ruṃ.' Having heard 'ruṃ,' it hears 'ṣam.' Thus there is no single consciousness that grasps three syllables. Therefore there is no consciousness that grasps the doctrine of unity. Therefore it is known that sound should not be listened to. One whose mind is distracted hears sound. But one whose mind is concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>) does not hear it. Reality (<s>tattva</s>) should be known through a concentrated mind. Therefore sound should not be listened to. This sound, whether by reaching or not reaching — in both ways it should not be listened to. Because it is not to be listened to in both ways, sound does not exist.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- śrotramākāśasvabhāvamiti | tamya padārthābhāvarūpatvāt ākāśa ityākhyā | ato nāsti śrotram | śrotrābhāvāt śabdo nāsti | śabdakāraṇaṃ nāstītyataḥ śabdo nāsti | śabdakāraṇaṃ mahābhūtasaṃśleṣaḥ | ayaṃ saṃśleṣadharmo nopalabhyate | kasmāt | ye dharmā vibhinnasvabhāvāḥ, na te saṃśliṣyante | ye na vibhinnasvabhāvāḥ, kathaṃ teṣāṃ svataḥ saṃśleṣaḥ | ekatra sthitamapi kṣaṇikam | ato na saṃśleṣo labhyate |
body.translated_text: Some say: The ear (<s>śrotra</s>) is of the nature of space (<s>ākāśa</s>). Since that [space] is of the nature of non-existence of objects, it is called space. Therefore the ear does not exist. Because the ear does not exist, sound does not exist. The cause of sound does not exist, therefore sound does not exist. The cause of sound is the conjunction of the great elements (<s>mahābhūtasaṃśleṣa</s>). This property of conjunction is not perceived. Why? Those <s>dharmas</s> that have distinct natures do not conjoin. Those that do not have distinct natures — how can there be conjunction among them by their own nature? Even what exists in one place is momentary. Therefore conjunction cannot be obtained.

body.text: śabdakhaṇḍanavargo 'ṣṭacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the refutation of sound (<s>śabdakhaṇḍanavarga</s>), the one hundred and forty-eighth.

body.text: 149 gandharasasparśakhaṇḍanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 149. The chapter on the refutation of smell, taste, and touch (<s>gandharasasparśakhaṇḍanavarga</s>).

body.text: na gandho grāhyaḥ | kasmāt | na hi ghrāṇavijñānaṃ vikalpayati | ayaṃ campakagandhaḥ ime 'nye gandhā iti | manovijñāna[mapi] na gandhaṃ jighrati | tasmānmanovijñānamapi na vikalpayati campakagandhamimam | (pṛ) yadyapi camapakagandhamimaṃ na vikalpayati | kintu gandhaṃ gṛhṇātyeva | (u) maivam | yathā kaściccampakavṛkṣamalabdhvā mohāccampakabuddhimutpādayati | tathā gandhamalabdhvā mohādgrandhabuddhimutpādayati | pūrvoktavat gandhaḥ prāpto vā aprāpto gṛhyata ityubhayathāsti doṣaḥ | tasmānnāsti gandhaḥ | tathā raso 'pi sparśo 'pi nāsti | kasmāt | sūkṣmādyavayaveṣveva sparśajñānaṃ notpadyata iti yathāpūrvaṃ vaktavyam | ato nāsti sparśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Smell (<s>gandha</s>) is not graspable. Why? Because olfactory consciousness (<s>ghrāṇavijñāna</s>) does not conceptualize 'this is the scent of champaka (<s>campaka</s>), these are other scents.' Mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) too does not smell the scent. Therefore mental consciousness also does not conceptualize 'this champaka scent.' (Objection:) Even though it does not conceptualize 'this champaka scent,' still it grasps the scent. (Reply:) That is not so. Just as someone, not having obtained a champaka tree, through delusion produces the cognition of champaka, so too, not having obtained the scent, one produces through delusion the cognition of scent. As stated before, whether the scent is reached or not reached when grasped — there is a defect in both cases. Therefore smell does not exist. Likewise, taste (<s>rasa</s>) too and touch (<s>sparśa</s>) too do not exist. Why? Because tactile cognition does not arise in the subtle primary parts — this should be stated as before. Therefore touch does not exist.

body.text: gandharasasparśakhaṇḍanavarga ekonapañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the refutation of smell, taste, and touch (<s>gandharasasparśakhaṇḍanavarga</s>), the one hundred and forty-ninth.

body.text: 150 manovijñānakhaṇḍanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 150. The chapter on the refutation of mental consciousness (<s>manovijñānakhaṇḍanavarga</s>).

body.text: manovijñānamapi dharmānna gṛhṇāti | kasmāt | manovijñānaṃ hi na pratyutpannān rūparasagandhasparśān gṛhṇāti | [yat] atītamanāgataṃ tannāstīti pūrvamuktameva | ato manovijñānaṃ na rūpādīn gṛhṇāti | (pṛ) yadi manovijñānaṃ rūpādīn dharmān na jānāti | svātmānaṃ [vā] jānīyāt | (u) na [kaścit] dharmaḥ svātmānaṃ jānāti | kasmāt | na pratyutpanne svātmavedanaṃ sambhavati | tadyathā asi[dhārā] na svātmānaṃ chinatti | atītānāgatayorasaddharmatvāt nānyaccittamasti | ato manovijñānaṃ na khātmānaṃ vijānāti |
body.translated_text: Mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) too does not grasp <s>dharmas</s>. Why? Because mental consciousness does not grasp present form (<s>rūpa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), and touch (<s>sparśa</s>). That which is past or future does not exist — this has been stated previously. Therefore mental consciousness does not grasp form and the rest. (Objection:) If mental consciousness does not know <s>dharmas</s> such as form, it should at least know itself. (Reply:) No <s>dharma</s> knows itself. Why? Because self-awareness (<s>svātmavedana</s>) is not possible in the present moment. Just as a sword-edge does not cut itself. Past and future being unreal <s>dharmas</s>, there is no other mind [to know it]. Therefore mental consciousness does not know itself.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi kaścit paracittaṃ jānāti | tadā tanmanovijñānaṃ caittadharmaṃ jānātyeva | (u) yathā kasyacit cittaṃ svātmānamajñātvāpi cintā bhavati ahaṃ cittavāniti | evaṃ paracitte 'pi | yo 'nāgatadharmo 'bhāva[rūpaḥ] so 'pi jñānajanakaḥ | paracittamapyevamiti cetko doṣaḥ | dharmālambanaṃ mana iti [mataṃ] bahudhā duṣṭam | yathā manaḥ prāpyālambate vijānāti | [vā] aprāpyālambate | manaśca na rūpādīnanusmaret | ebhirdoṣairna manovijñānaṃ dharmān vijānāti ||
body.translated_text: (Question) If someone knows another's mind, then that mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) would indeed know the mental factors (<s>caittadharma</s>). (Answer) Just as someone's mind, even without knowing itself, has the thought 'I am one who has a mind' — so too with another's mind. A future <s>dharma</s> that is of the nature of non-existence also generates knowledge. If the same applies to another's mind, what fault is there? The view that 'the mind has <s>dharmas</s> as its object' is flawed in many ways: whether the mind cognizes by contact or without contact; and the mind would not recollect form and the like. Through these faults, the mind-consciousness does not cognize <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: manovijñānakhaṇḍanavargaḥ pañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and fiftieth chapter, the Chapter on the Refutation of Mind-Consciousness (<s>manovijñānakhaṇḍanavarga</s>).

body.text: 151 hetuphalakhaṇḍanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 151. Chapter on the Refutation of Cause and Effect (<s>hetuphalakhaṇḍanavarga</s>)

body.text: abhāvavādyāha- yadyasti phalam | hetau pūrvaṃ san vā guṇa utpadyeta | pūrvamasan[vā] guṇa utpadyeta | ubhayathā cāsti doṣaḥ | yathā dvayorhastayoḥ pūrvamasan śabdo bhavati | dadhihetau pūrvamasat dadhi, dadhi utpādayati | śakaṭahetau pūrvamasamat śakaṭaṃ, śakaṭamutpādayati | ato na hetau pūrvaṃ san guṇaḥ phalamutpādayati |
body.translated_text: The proponent of non-existence (<s>abhāvavādin</s>) says: If there is an effect — either a quality that previously exists in the cause would arise, or a quality that previously does not exist in the cause would arise. In both cases there is a fault. Just as a sound that did not previously exist in the two hands comes into being; yogurt that did not previously exist in the cause of yogurt — yogurt is produced; a cart that did not previously exist in the cause of a cart — a cart is produced. Therefore, a quality that previously exists in the cause does not produce the effect.

body.text: bhavato yadi mataṃ hetau pūrvamasan guṇaḥ phalamutpādayatīti | tadā rūparahitavāyusūkṣmareṇū rūpamutpādayet | tathā cet vāyū rūpavān syāt | vajrādīnāṃ gandhavattā syāt | dṛṣṭe paśyāmaḥ khalu śuklatantuḥ śuklapaṭaṃ sādhayati | kṛṣṇatantuḥ kṛṣṇapaṭaṃ sādhayati | yadi
body.translated_text: If your view is that a quality not previously existing in the cause produces the effect, then wind and subtle particles devoid of form would produce form. If that were so, wind would possess form. Diamonds and the like would possess smell. In what is directly seen, we observe that white threads produce white cloth, and black threads produce black cloth. If

body.text: hetau pūrvamasan guṇaḥ phalaṃ sādhayati | kasmāt śuklatantuḥ śukla[paṭa]meva sādhayati na kṛṣṇam | ato na hetau pūrvamasan guṇaḥ phalamutpādayati |
body.translated_text: a quality not previously existing in the cause produces the effect, why does a white thread produce only white cloth and not black? Therefore, a quality not previously existing in the cause does not produce the effect.

body.text: imau dvāvapi dṛṣṭāntau duṣṭau | ato nāsti phalam | yadi hetau satkāryam, tadā notpadyeta | kathaṃ sadutpadyeta | yadyasat | tadapi notpadyeta | asatkathamutpadyeta | (pṛ) dṛṣṭe paśyāmaḥ khalu ghaṭaṃ kiyamāṇam kathaṃ nāsti ghaṭa iti | (u) ghaṭo 'yaṃ pūrvamakṛtaḥ kathaṃ karaṇīyaḥ | tasyaivābhāvāt | yadi pūrvaṃ kṛta eva | kathaṃ karaṇīyaḥ | tasya sattvāt | (pṛ) kriyamāṇaḥ kriyata ityucyate | (u) nāsti kriyamāṇam | kasmāt | yaḥ kṛtabhāgaḥ sa kṛtakoṭau patati | yo 'kṛtabhāgaḥ [so] 'kṛtakoṭau patati | ato nāsti kriyamāṇam | yadi ghaṭaḥ kriyāvān, atīto 'nāgataḥ pratyutpanno vā syāt | atīto na kriyāvān | niruddhatvāt | anāgato na kriyāvān asattvāt | pratyutpanno 'pi na kriyāvān, bhūyamānatvāt |
body.translated_text: Both these examples are flawed. Therefore the effect does not exist. If the effect pre-exists in the cause (<s>satkārya</s>), it would not arise — how could what already exists arise? If it does not pre-exist (<s>asatkārya</s>), it too would not arise — how could what does not exist arise? (Question) We see directly that a pot is being made — how can you say the pot does not exist? (Answer) This pot was previously unmade — how is it to be made? Because of its very non-existence. If it was already made previously, how is it to be made? Because of its [already] existing. (Question) That which is being made is said to be 'being made.' (Answer) There is no 'being made.' Why? The portion that is already made falls into the category of 'made.' The portion that is not yet made falls into the category of 'not made.' Therefore there is no 'being made.' If a pot possesses action, it would be past, future, or present. The past does not possess action, because it has ceased. The future does not possess action, because it does not [yet] exist. The present too does not possess action, because it is [already] coming into being.

body.text: kārakamupādāya kriyāvataḥ karma sidhyati | tatra kāraka eva vastuto nopalabhyate | tathā hi | śīrṣādyavayaveṣu kriyāvṛttyabhāvānnāsti kārakaḥ | kārakābhāvāt kriyāvṛttirapi nāsti | hetuḥ kāryasya pūrvaṃ vā, kiṃ vā paścāt, kiṃ vā samakālam, sarvathā na yujyate | kasmāt | yadi pūrvaṃ hetuḥ paścātkāryam | hetau niruddhe kena phalamutpadyeta yathā avidyamānaḥ pitā kathaṃ putramutpādayet | yadi paścāddhetuḥ pūrvaṃ phalam | hetuḥ svayamanutpannaḥ kathaṃ phalamutpādayet | yathā anutpannaḥ pitā kaḥ putramutpādayati | yadi hetuḥ phalañca samakālam na tarhi ayaṃ nyāyaḥ | yathā dve śṛṅge yugapadudbhūte nocyete vāmadakṣiṇe 'nyonyahetuke | siddhāntā ime trayo 'pi ayuktāḥ | ato nāsti phalam |
body.translated_text: Depending on an agent, the action of one who possesses action is accomplished. But therein, the agent itself is in reality not apprehended. For in the parts such as the head and the like, because of the absence of the occurrence of action, there is no agent. Because of the absence of an agent, there is no occurrence of action either. Whether the cause is prior to the effect, or subsequent, or simultaneous — in all cases it is not valid. Why? If the cause is prior and the effect subsequent — when the cause has ceased, by what would the effect be produced? Just as a non-existent father — how could he produce a son? If the cause is subsequent and the effect prior — the cause, not yet itself arisen, how could it produce the effect? Just as an unborn father — who produces a son? If the cause and effect are simultaneous, then this is not valid reasoning — just as two horns arising simultaneously are not said to be left and right, mutually caused by one another. These three positions are all invalid. Therefore the effect does not exist.

body.text: hetuphale ime yadyekaṃ, yadi vā nānā | ubhayathāsti doṣaḥ | kasmāt | yadi nānā | tadā tantūn vihāya paṭaḥ syāt | yadyekam | tantupaṭayorvibhāgo na syāt | laukikā na paśyanti kañcana dharmaṃ hetuphalayorapṛthagbhāvarūpam |
body.translated_text: If cause and effect are one, or if they are different — in both cases there is a fault. Why? If they are different, then cloth would exist apart from threads. If they are one, there would be no distinction between threads and cloth. Worldly people do not see any <s>dharma</s> that is of the nature of non-difference between cause and effect.

body.text: yadyasti phalam | syāt svakṛtaṃ parakṛtamubhayakṛtamahetukṛtaṃ vā | sarvamidamayuktam | kasmāt | na kaściddharmaḥ svātmānaṃ karoti | yadyasti svarūpataḥ | kiṃ svātmakriyayā | yadi nāsti svarūpataḥ | kaḥ karoti svātmakriyām | na ca paścāmaḥ kañcana dharmaṃ svātmānaṃ
body.translated_text: If the effect exists, it would be self-made, other-made, made by both, or made without a cause. All of this is invalid. Why? No <s>dharma</s> makes itself. If it exists by its own nature, what need is there for self-making? If it does not exist by its own nature, who performs the self-making? And we do not see any <s>dharma</s>

body.text: kurvantam | ato nāsti svakṛtan | parakṛtamayuktam | kasmāt | cakṣūrūpayorvijñānotpattau vṛttyabhāvāt na parakṛtam | kartṛtvasaṃjñābhāvātsarve dharmā akartṛkāḥ | yathā "bījasya naivaṃ bhavati- ahamaṅkuramabhinirvartayāmīti | cakṣuṣo rūpasya naivaṃ bhavati- āvāṃ saha vijñānamabhinirvartayāva iti | ataḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ nāsti kartṛtvasaṃjñā | ubhayakṛtamapyayuktam | svakṛtaparakṛtadoṣasattvāt | ahetukṛtamapi na yuktam | hetāvāsati phalamapi nāstītyucyate | yadi caturdhāpi nāsti | kathamasti phalam | yadyasti, ucyeta |
body.translated_text: making itself. Therefore the self-made does not exist. The other-made is also invalid. Why? Because in the production of consciousness from the eye and form, there is no occurrence of [separate agency] — therefore it is not other-made. Because of the absence of the notion of agency, all <s>dharmas</s> are without an agent. Just as 'the seed does not have [the thought]: "I produce the sprout." The eye and form do not have [the thought]: "We two together produce consciousness."' Therefore, for all <s>dharmas</s>, there is no notion of agency. Made by both is also invalid — because the faults of both self-made and other-made exist. Made without a cause is also not valid — because when the cause does not exist, it is said that the effect too does not exist. If it does not exist in any of the four ways, how does the effect exist? If it does exist, let it be stated.

body.text: phalamidaṃ yadi kriyācittapūrvakaṃ syāt, yadi vākriyācittapūrvakaṃ syāt | yadi kriyācittapurvakam | garbhe 'pi bālānāṃ cakṣurādikāyāvayaveṣu kaḥ sacittatvaṃ karoti | īśvarādayo 'pi na kurvanti | pūrvakṛtasya karmaṇo 'pi nāsti kriyācittam | karmedamatītagatam | kathaṃ kriyācittaṃ bhavet | ato na karmaṇo 'pyasti cittam | yadyakriyācittapūrvakamiti | kathaṃ parasya duḥkhakṛt duḥkhaṃ labhate | parasya sukhakṛt sukhaṃ labhate | dṛṣṭe ca karmakaraṇe citte vikalpayati- evaṃ kartavyaṃ, evaṃ na kartavyamiti | yadi nāsti kriyācittam | kathamayaṃ vibhāgo bhavet | ataḥ sacittapūrvakamacittapūrvakaṃ sarvamayuktam | evamādayaḥ sarve 'pīndriyaviṣayā nopalabhyante | ato nāsti dharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: This effect — would it be preceded by a mind of intentional action, or not preceded by a mind of intentional action? If preceded by a mind of intentional action — then in the womb, who makes the parts of the body such as eyes and the like of infants with intention? <s>Īśvara</s> and others also do not make them. And previously performed <s>karma</s> does not have a mind of intentional action — that <s>karma</s> has passed away. How could it have a mind of intentional action? Therefore even <s>karma</s> does not have a mind [of intention]. If it is not preceded by a mind of intentional action — then how does one who causes suffering to another obtain suffering, and one who causes happiness to another obtain happiness? In what is directly seen, when performing an action, one discriminates in the mind: 'This should be done; this should not be done.' If there is no mind of intentional action, how would this discrimination exist? Therefore, whether preceded by mind or not preceded by mind — all is invalid. All sense faculties and their objects and the like are not apprehended in this way. Therefore <s>dharma</s> does not exist.

body.text: hetuphalakhaṇḍanavarga ekapañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and fifty-first chapter, the Chapter on the Refutation of Cause and Effect (<s>hetuphalakhaṇḍanavarga</s>).

body.text: 152 lokasatyavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 152. Chapter on Conventional Truth (<s>lokasatyavarga</s>)

body.text: uttaramucyate | yat bhavān nānākāraṇairbravīti- sarve dharmāḥ śūnyā iti | tanmatamayuktam | kasmāt | pūrvamevoktaṃ mayā- yadi sarvamabhāva[rūpa]m | śāstramidamapyabhāvarūpam | nāpi sarvadharmeṣu ityādiśūnyatādūṣaṇamaprativadannapi śūnyatāṃ sthāpayasi | ato na sarvadharmā abhāvātmakāḥ | yadbhavatoktaṃ- nāstīndriyaṃ, nāstipratyaya ityādi | na tadasmābhiḥ pratipāditam | kasmāt | bhagavān sūtre svayamidaṃ nyaṣedhīt | yaduta pañca vastūnyacintyāni
body.translated_text: The reply is stated: Your assertion through various reasons that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are empty' — that view is invalid. Why? I have already stated previously: 'If everything is of the nature of non-existence, then this <s>śāstra</s> too is of the nature of non-existence.' And you, without refuting the refutation of emptiness — [namely,] 'not in all <s>dharmas</s>' and so forth — establish emptiness. Therefore all <s>dharmas</s> are not of the nature of non-existence. Your statement that 'sense faculties do not exist, conditions do not exist' and so forth — that has not been established by us. Why? The Blessed One himself prohibited this in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are five matters that are inconceivable (<s>acintya</s>)

body.text: lokavastu, sattvavastu, karmapratyayatāvastu, dhyānaniṣṭhāvastu, tathāgatavastu iti | idamasarvajñaḥ puruṣo 'bhyūhya na nitīrayituṃ śaknoti | tathāgatāḥ kevalaṃ dharmavivecanajñānasamarthāḥ | śrāvakāḥ pratyekabuddhāśca nirvāṇajñānamātragatiṃgatā dharmāṇāṃ vivecanajñānasyekadeśalābhinaḥ | tathāgatāḥ paraṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sarvākāraṃ prakṛtito naissvābhāvyaṃ viśeṣasāmānyalakṣaṇāni sarvāṇi pratividhyanti | yathā puruṣālayādayaḥ padārthāḥ suvināśā duṣkalpāḥ | evaṃ śūnyatājñānaṃ sulabham | dharmāṇāṃ pravicayajñānaṃ durutpādam |
body.translated_text: : the matter of the world (<s>lokavastu</s>), the matter of sentient beings (<s>sattvavastu</s>), the matter of the conditionality of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmapratyayatāvastu</s>), the matter of the attainment of <s>dhyāna</s> (<s>dhyānaniṣṭhāvastu</s>), and the matter of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatavastu</s>).' This cannot be determined through conjecture by a person who is not omniscient. The <s>Tathāgatas</s> alone are capable of the knowledge that discriminates <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> have reached only the extent of the knowledge of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and are partial attainers of the knowledge of discriminating <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, supreme, penetrate all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects — their intrinsic naturelessness (<s>naiḥsvābhāvya</s>), and all their specific and general characteristics. Just as entities such as a person's dwelling and the like are easily destroyed and difficult to construct, so too the knowledge of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is easy to obtain, but the knowledge of discriminating <s>dharmas</s> is difficult to produce.

body.text: (pṛ) yathā bhagavatā bodhimaṇḍagatena dharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pratilabdham | yathā ca bhagavatopadiṣṭam | tattathaiva bhaviṣyati | (u) bhagavān sarvadharmānupadiśannapi na sarvākāramupadiśati | vimuktyarthatvābhāvāt | tadyathā bhagavānupadiśati sarvadharmāḥ pratītya samutpannā iti | nopadiśatyekaikaśaḥ kiṃpratyaya iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Just as the Blessed One, having gone to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), obtained the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>, and just as the Blessed One taught — so it will be. (Answer) The Blessed One, even while teaching all <s>dharmas</s>, does not teach them in all aspects — because not all [teachings] serve the purpose of liberation. For example, the Blessed One teaches: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>).' He does not teach one by one what is the condition for what.

body.text: duḥkhanāśanaprayojanamātramapekṣitamiti[tat]- upadiśati | vicitrāṅkādīni rūpāṇi nṛttagītādayo nādā gandharasasparśā apramāṇaviśeṣā nopadeśyāḥ | upadeśe 'pi nāsti mahaddhitam ityata īdṛśaṃ vastu nopadiśati bhagavān | na [tāni] na santīti vaktuṃ śakyate | yathā kaścit citrāṅkanādidharmavikalpamajñātvā vadati tāni na santīti | tathā bhavānapi yatkimapyasādhayitvā vadati nāstīdaṃ- vastu iti | jñātustu asti | ajñātuḥ punarnāsti | yathā jātyandho vadati nāsti kṛṣṇamavadātaṃ vā, mayādṛṣṭatvāt | na cādṛṣṭatvādrūpāṇi na santīti sambhavati | yadyevam, pratītyasiddhatvānna santi sarve dharmā iti vaktuṃ pāryate |
body.translated_text: Only the purpose of destroying suffering is considered — [therefore] he teaches [accordingly]. Various forms such as paintings and the like, sounds such as dancing and singing, smells, tastes, and tactile sensations of immeasurable variety — these are not taught. Even if taught, there is no great benefit — therefore the Blessed One does not teach such matters. It cannot be said that they do not exist. Just as someone who, not knowing the discriminations of <s>dharmas</s> such as painting and the like, says 'those do not exist' — so too you, without having established anything, say 'this thing does not exist.' But for one who knows, it exists. For one who does not know, it does not exist — just as a person blind from birth says 'there is no black or white, because I have not seen them.' But it is not possible that because they are not seen, forms do not exist. If that is so, because they are not independently established, it cannot be said that 'all <s>dharmas</s> do not exist.'

body.text: tathāgatāḥ sarvajñā iti śraddheyamasmābhiḥ | tathāgatastu āha- santi pañca skandhā iti | ato jñāyate rūpādayaḥ sarvadharmāḥ santi yathā ghaṭādayaḥ saṃvṛtitaḥ santīti ||
body.translated_text: That the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are omniscient — this should be believed by us. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> has said: 'The five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) exist.' Therefore it is known that all <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the like exist — just as pots and the like exist conventionally (<s>saṃvṛti</s>).

body.text: lokasatyavargo dvipañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and fifty-second chapter, the Chapter on Conventional Truth (<s>lokasatyavarga</s>).

body.text: 153 dharmacittanirodhavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 153. Chapter on the Cessation of <s>Dharma</s>-Mind (<s>dharmacittanirodhavarga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) pūrvamuktaṃ- bhavatā trividhacittanirodho nirodhasatyamiti | hetupratyayākhya prajñapti [citta]nirodho jñāta eva | idānīṃ vaktavyaṃ kiṃ dharmacittaṃ, kathaṃ tasya nirodha iti | (u) santi vastutaḥ pañcaskandhā iti cittaṃ dharmacittamityucyate | pañcaskandhān śūnyān dṛṣṭvā samyagbhāvayato dharmacittaṃ nirudhyate | (pṛ) yogī paśyati pañcaskandhān śūnyān yaduta pañcaskandheṣu nāsti nityadharmaḥ sthiradharmo 'vināśadharmo 'vipariṇāmadharma ātmāmīyadharma iti | te śūnyā ityucyante | na tu skandhāneva na paśyatīti | (u) yogāvacaro naiva paśyati pañcaskandhān | kasmāt | yogāvacaraḥ saṃskṛtālambanacittaṃ prahāya asaṃskṛtālambanacittaṃ pratilabhate | ato yogāvacaraḥ pañcaskandhān na paśyati, skandhanirodhamātraṃ paśyati | pañcaskandhānāṃ darśane na śūnyā ityucyante | skandhānāmevāśūnyatvāt | evaṃ śūnyatājñānantu vikalaṃ syāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) Previously you stated: 'The cessation of the threefold mind is the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>).' The cessation of the mind based on cause and condition, [namely] the designation-mind (<s>prajñapticitta</s>), is already understood. Now it should be stated: What is the <s>dharma</s>-mind, and how is its cessation? (Answer) The mind that [holds] 'the five aggregates truly exist' is called the <s>dharma</s>-mind. Having seen that the five aggregates are empty and having properly cultivated [this insight], the <s>dharma</s>-mind ceases. (Question) The <s>yogin</s> sees the five aggregates as empty — namely, in the five aggregates there is no permanent <s>dharma</s>, no stable <s>dharma</s>, no indestructible <s>dharma</s>, no unchanging <s>dharma</s>, no self, no 'mine.' They are called 'empty.' But it is not that he does not see the aggregates themselves. (Answer) The practitioner (<s>yogāvacara</s>) does not see the five aggregates at all. Why? The practitioner, having abandoned the mind whose object is the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), obtains the mind whose object is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). Therefore the practitioner does not see the five aggregates — he sees only the cessation of the aggregates. If the five aggregates were seen, they would not be called 'empty' — because the aggregates themselves would be non-empty. In that case, the knowledge of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) would be incomplete.

body.text: (pṛ) yogāvacaro rūpaṃ nairātmyataḥ śūnyaṃ paśyati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yogāvacara idaṃ rūpaṃ paśyati yāvadidaṃ vijñānaṃ śūnyaṃ ṣaśyati iti | na tu rūpādayaḥ pañcaskandhā na santīti jñātavyam | (u) astīdaṃ vacanaṃ, na tu vyavadānā[rthaka]m | yathoktaṃ dharmamudrāsūtre- yogāvacaraḥ paśyati rūpādīn dharmān anityalakṣaṇān vikṣepalakṣaṇān vināśalakṣaṇān māyālakṣaṇān nirvedalakṣaṇān iti | idaṃ śūnyākhyamapi na vyavadānātmakam | puruṣo 'yaṃ [ya]dante pañcaskandhānāṃ nirodhaṃ paśyati | taddarśanaṃ tāvadvayavadānā[tmakam] ato jñāyate pañcaskandhānāṃ nirodhaṃ paśyatīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) The practitioner sees form as empty of self (<s>nairātmya</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The practitioner sees this form, up to this consciousness, as empty.' But it should not be understood that form and the other five aggregates do not exist. (Answer) This statement exists, but it does not [serve] the purpose of purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>). As stated in the <s>Dharmamudrā-sūtra</s>: 'The practitioner sees form and other <s>dharmas</s> as having the characteristic of impermanence, the characteristic of dispersion, the characteristic of destruction, the characteristic of illusion, and the characteristic of disenchantment.' This [statement about] 'empty' too is not of the nature of purification. This person who in the end sees the cessation of the five aggregates — that seeing alone is of the nature of purification. Therefore it is known that he sees the cessation of the five aggregates.

body.text: (pṛ) saṃskṛtālambanajñānena kasmānna vyavadānaṃ labhate | (u) yogāvacarasya pañcaskandhasaṃjñāpravṛttasya kadācitprajñapticittaṃ punarbhavet | ataḥ saṃskṛtālambanacittena na vyavadānaṃ labhate | pañcaskandhānāṃ nirodhaṃ sākṣātkurvatastu na tat punarabhimukhībhabati | prajñaptikāraṇanirodhasya
body.translated_text: (Question) Why does one not attain purification through knowledge that has conditioned objects? (Answer) For the <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner of meditation) in whom the perception of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) has arisen, the mind of <s>prajñapti</s> (conventional designation) may arise again. Therefore, through a mind with conditioned objects, one does not attain purification. But for one who directly realizes the cessation of the five <s>skandhas</s>, that [perception] does not turn back again. Because the cessation of the cause of <s>prajñapti</s> (conventional designation) has been

body.text: prasādhitatvāt prajñaptisaṃjñā nānuvartate | tadyathā kaścana vṛkṣaḥ krakacakṛtto bhasmasātkṛtaḥ prakṣīṇaḥ | na [tatra] vṛkṣasaṃjñā prahīṇā punaranuvartate | tathā idamapi | bhagavān rādhamāha- sattvaṃ tathā vibhida, vidhama, yathā nopatiṣṭhati iti | kiñcāhaikaṃ sūtrama- rūpaṃ rādha tathā vibhida, vidhama yathā nopatiṣṭhati iti | ato jñāyate yaḥ sattvaparibhedaḥ iyaṃ prajñaptiśūnyatā | yo rūpaparibhedaḥ iyaṃ dharmaśūnyateti |
body.translated_text: established, the perception of <s>prajñapti</s> (conventional designation) does not recur. Just as a certain tree, cut by a saw, reduced to ashes, and destroyed — the perception of 'tree' once abandoned does not recur again. So too is this case. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to <s>Rādha</s>: 'Destroy and scatter the being such that it does not arise again.' And further, in another <s>sūtra</s> he said: 'Destroy and scatter form, <s>Rādha</s>, such that it does not arise again.' From this it is known that the destruction of the being is <s>prajñaptiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of designation), and the destruction of form is <s>dharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of dharmas).

body.text: bhāvanā ca dvividhā- śūnya[tā]bhāvanā nairātmyabhāvanā iti | śūnyatābhāvanā ca yat prajñaptisattvādarśanam | yathā kaścit jalaṃ nāstīti ghaṭa śūnyaṃ paśyati | tathā pañcaskandheṣu pudgalo nāstīti [tān] śūnyān paśyati | yat dharmān na paśyati | idaṃ nairātmyamityucyate | uktañca sūtre- nairātmyajñānalābhī samyagvimucyate iti | ato jñāyate rūpasvabhāvanirodho vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānasvabhāvanirodho nairātmyamityucyate | naiḥsvābhāvyameva nairātmyam | (pṛ) yadi naiḥsvābhāvyaṃ nairātmyamityucyata iti | kimidānīṃ na santi vastutaḥ pañcaskandhāḥ | (u) na santi vastutaḥ | santi tu saṃvṛtitaḥ | kasmāt | bhagavānāha- saṃskārāḥ saṃvṛtitaḥ santi māyāvat nirmitavat | na tu paramārthataḥ | paramārthataḥ śūnyamiti vacanam- ayamarthasatyataḥ śūnyo na saṃvṛtisatyata iti | paramārthaśca yaduta rūpaṃ śūnyamakiñcanam yāvadvijñānaṃ śūnyamakiñcanam | ato yadrūpādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ śūnyatādarśanaṃ tat paramārthaśūnyatādarśanamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is of two kinds: meditation on emptiness (<s>śūnyatābhāvanā</s>) and meditation on non-self (<s>nairātmyabhāvanā</s>). Meditation on emptiness is the non-perception of the conventionally designated being. Just as someone sees a pot as empty, thinking 'there is no water,' so too one sees the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as empty, thinking 'there is no <s>pudgala</s> (person) in them.' When one does not perceive <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), this is called <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self). And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who attains the knowledge of non-self is perfectly liberated.' From this it is known that the cessation of the own-nature of form, the cessation of the own-nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is called <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self). Absence of own-nature itself is non-self. (Question) If absence of own-nature is called non-self, then do the five <s>skandhas</s> not exist in reality? (Answer) They do not exist in ultimate reality. But they exist conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtitaḥ</s>). Why? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations) exist conventionally, like an illusion, like a magical creation, but not ultimately.' The statement that they are ultimately empty means: 'This is empty from the standpoint of ultimate truth, not from the standpoint of conventional truth.' And the ultimate is namely that form is empty and void, up to consciousness being empty and void. Therefore, the seeing of the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s> such as form and others is called the seeing of ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadi pañca skandhāḥ saṃvṛtisatyataḥ santi | kasmāducyante rūpādayo dharmāḥ paramārthasatyā iti | (u) sattvānāṃ kṛta ucyante | santi kecit pañcaskandheṣu samutpannaparamārthasaṃjñāḥ | tadarthamucyante pañca skandhāḥ paramārthataḥ śūnyā iti | (pṛ) kiṃ nu khalu sūtre noktam asti karma asti phalam, kārakastu nopalabhyate iti | (u) ayaṃ hetuḥ dharmaṇāṃ kārakākhyo nopalabhyata itīdaṃ prajñaptiśūnyatābhidhānam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dharmāḥ prajñaptisaṃjñāmātram | prajñaptisaṃjñā ca yaduta avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvajjarāmaraṇaduḥkhasamudayanirodho bhavati iti | asmādvacanāt jñāyate pañcaskandhā api paramārthato na santīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) If the five <s>skandhas</s> exist from the standpoint of conventional truth, why are <s>dharmas</s> such as form and others called ultimately true? (Answer) This is said for the sake of beings. There are some who have generated the perception of ultimate reality regarding the five <s>skandhas</s>. For their sake it is said that the five <s>skandhas</s> are ultimately empty. (Question) Has it not been stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There is <s>karma</s> (action), there is <s>phala</s> (fruit), but no agent is found'? (Answer) This reason — that no agent called the doer of <s>dharmas</s> is found — is a statement of <s>prajñaptiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of designation). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Dharmas</s> are merely designations and perceptions. And designation-perception is namely: conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) are formations (<s>saṃskārāḥ</s>), up to the cessation of the origination of the mass of old age, death, and suffering.' From this statement it is known that even the five <s>skandhas</s> do not exist ultimately.

body.text: mahāśūnyatāsūtre 'pyuktam- ya āha idaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, tasya jarāmaraṇam iti | ya āha- sa eva jīvaḥ tadeva śarīram, anyo jīvo 'nyat śarīram iti | idamekārthakam, vyañjanameva nānā | yeṣāmeṣā dṛṣṭiḥ na te macchrāvakā na brahmacāriṇa iti | yat tasya jarāmaraṇaṃ pratiṣidhyate tat prajñaptikhaṇḍanam | yadidaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ pratiṣidhyate | tat pañcaskandhakhaṇḍanam | kiñcāha- jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ madhyamā pratipadityucyate | nāsti jarāmaraṇaṃ paramārthata ityuktamiti jñātavyam | saṃvṛtita ucyate jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamiti | yathā ghaṭasaṃjñātyaye nāsti ghaṭaḥ paramārthataḥ | evaṃ rūpādidharmāṇāmatyaye nāsti rūpaṃ paramārthataḥ | uktañca sūtre- yo dharmo māyā sa mṛṣā | yo dharmo 'māyā, sa eva paramārthaḥ iti | sarve saṃskṛtadharmā vipariṇāmitvāt māyā ityucyante | māyātvādabhūtāḥ | abhūtatvānna paramārthasantaḥ | yathāha gāthā-
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mahāśūnyatāsūtra</s> also it is said: 'He who says "this is aging-and-death, to him belongs aging-and-death." He who says "the life-force is identical with the body, or the life-force is different from the body" — these are one in meaning, differing only in expression. Those who hold this view are not my disciples, not practitioners of the holy life.' The denial of 'his aging-and-death' is the refutation of <s>prajñapti</s> (conventional designation). The denial of 'this is aging-and-death' is the refutation of the five <s>skandhas</s>. Further, it is said: 'Aging-and-death conditioned by birth is called the middle path.' One should know that it is stated: 'Aging-and-death does not exist ultimately.' Conventionally it is said: 'Aging-and-death is conditioned by birth.' Just as when the perception of a pot ceases, the pot does not exist ultimately, so too when <s>dharmas</s> such as form cease, form does not exist ultimately. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whatever <s>dharma</s> is an illusion, that is false. Whatever <s>dharma</s> is not an illusion, that itself is the ultimate.' All conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, because of their being subject to change, are called illusions. Because they are illusions, they are unreal. Because they are unreal, they do not ultimately exist. As the verse says:

body.text:
abhūtabaddho loko 'yaṃ suniścitavatprabhāsate |
asat dṛṣṭaṃ sadābhāsamasadvai parayā dhiyā || iti |
body.translated_text:
This world, bound by unreality, shines forth as if firmly established;
The unreal appears as real, but by the highest wisdom it is seen as not real.

body.text: ato
body.translated_text: Therefore, one should know that even the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are empty.

body.text: jñātavyaṃ skandhā api śūnyā iti |

nirodhasatyadarśanaṃ mārgalābha ityucyate | ato jñāyate nirodhaḥ paramārthasan, na skandhā iti | yadi skandhāḥ paramārthasantaḥ, yogāvacaro 'pi dṛṣṭvā mārgalābhī syāt | vastutastu na tathā | ato jñāyate pañcaskandhā na paramārthasanta iti | skandhanirodhaśca satyam | ato jñāyate skandhā na satyamiti | na sambhavati skandhāḥ satyaṃ skandhābhāvo 'pi satyamiti vaktum | dṛśyasya sarvasya mohahetukatvāt | yathā na kaścidavañcitalocano māyāṃ paśyati | tathā yo 'mugdhaḥ na sa paśyati skandhān | ataḥ skandhā na paramārthasantaḥ | uktañca sūtre- yatrāsmīti tatreñjitam | skandheṣu cāsti asmīti | yathāhānandaḥ- dharmānupādāya asmīti sidhyati yaduta rūpaskandhaṃ yāvadvijñānaskandhamupādāyeti | sthavirā bhikṣavaḥ kṣemakamāhuḥ- kimasmīti vadasi | kṣemakaḥ pratyāha- na khalvāyuṣmanto rūpamasmīti vadāmi | nāpyanyatrarūpādasmīti vadāmi | evaṃ yāvadvijñānamapi | api ca me āyuṣmantaḥ pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu
body.translated_text: The seeing of the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) is called the attainment of the path. From this it is known that <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) is ultimately real, not the <s>skandhas</s>. If the <s>skandhas</s> were ultimately real, the <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator) too, upon seeing them, would attain the path. But in reality it is not so. From this it is known that the five <s>skandhas</s> are not ultimately real. And the cessation of the <s>skandhas</s> is true. From this it is known that the <s>skandhas</s> are not true. It is not possible to say that the <s>skandhas</s> are true and the absence of the <s>skandhas</s> is also true, because all that is seen has delusion as its cause. Just as no one with undeceived eyes sees an illusion, so one who is undeluded does not see the <s>skandhas</s>. Therefore the <s>skandhas</s> are not ultimately real. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Where there is the thought "I am," there is agitation. And in the <s>skandhas</s> there is the thought "I am."' As <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'The thought "I am" is established by depending on <s>dharmas</s>, namely by depending on the form-aggregate up to the consciousness-aggregate.' The elder monks said to <s>Kṣemaka</s>: 'What do you mean when you say "I am"?' <s>Kṣemaka</s> replied: 'Venerable ones, I do not say that form is "I am," nor do I say "I am" apart from form. So too up to consciousness. However, venerable ones, in the five aggregates of clinging,

body.text: asmīti adhigatam | [ayamahamasmīti na samanupaśyāmi] | iti | ayaṃ sūtrāśayaḥ- śaikṣajanāḥ kadācit smṛtivikṣepādasmimānamutpādayanti | samāhitasmṛtikasya pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu asmimānaṃ niruddhameva | puṣpavat | na mūlakāṇḍaśākhāpatrāṇyeva puṣpam | nāpyanyatra tebhya puṣpam | evameva na rūpā dīni asmīti [vadāmi] | nāpyanyatra rūpādibhyaḥ asmīti [vadāmi] | evamasminirodhapratyayamasmimānaṃ na pravartate | ato jñāyate pañcopādānaskandhā api śūnyā iti |
body.translated_text: the thought "I am" has been apprehended. [But I do not perceive "this I am."] This is the intent of the <s>sūtra</s>: <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) practitioners sometimes, through distraction of mindfulness, generate the conceit of "I am" (<s>asmimāna</s>). For one whose mindfulness is concentrated, the conceit of "I am" regarding the five aggregates of clinging is entirely ceased. Like a flower — the petals, roots, trunk, branches, and leaves are not themselves the flower, nor is the flower something apart from them. In the same way, I do not say that form and the rest are "I am," nor do I say "I am" apart from form and the rest. Thus, with the cessation of this [basis], the conceit of "I am" does not operate. From this it is known that even the five aggregates of clinging are empty.

body.text: yogāvacaraḥ sarvanimittāni nirudhyānimittaṃ sākṣātkuryāt | yadi vastusat nimittam, kimarthaṃ nānusmarati | na tīrthikānāmiva rūpaprahāṇakāle jñāyate vastusat rūpaṃ, parantu nānusmaryata iti | yogī avaśyaṃ rūpādīnāṃ skandhānāṃ nirodhaṃ paśyati nirodhadarśanāt animitte 'vatarati | ato jñāyate rūpādayo na paramārthasanta iti | yatra santi pañcaskandhāḥ tatrāsmīti buddhirbhavati | pañcaskandhā na santītyato 'smīti buddhirnirudhyate | ataḥ skandhāḥ sarve śunyāḥ | phenasūtre bhagavānāha- yadi puruṣaḥ phenapiṇḍaṃ paśyet yoniśa upaparīkṣeta | sa[tat]tucchakañcaiva jānīyāt | evameva bhikṣuryadi rūpaskandhaṃ samyagupaparīkṣate | sa[taṃ] riktakañcaiva jānāti, tucchakañcaiva[jānāti], asārakañcaiva[jānati], vikṣepalakṣaṇañcaiva jānāti | vedanāmupaparīkṣate yathā buddhudam, saṃjñā [mupaparīkṣate]yathā marīcikām, saṃskārā[nupaparīkṣate] yathā kadalīm, vijñāna[mupaparīkṣate] yathā māyām | tatra pañca dṛṣṭāntāḥ śūnyārthanirūpaṇāḥ | kasmāt | paśyāmaḥ khalu cakṣuṣā phenamapacīyamānamabhāvatāṃ yāti | tathā budbudādīnyapi | ato jñāyate skandhā na paramārthasanta iti | ye jinaputrāḥ saṃsārāt paramanirviṇṇāḥ | [te]dharmāṇāṃ prakṛtito 'nutpādamākiñcanyañca paśyanti | ato ye 'nityaṃ
body.translated_text: The <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator) should cease all signs (<s>nimitta</s>) and directly realize the signless (<s>animitta</s>). If the signs were real in substance, why would one not recollect them? It is not as with the non-Buddhists (<s>tīrthikas</s>) at the time of abandoning form, where form is known to be substantially real but is simply not recollected. The <s>yogī</s> necessarily sees the cessation of the <s>skandhas</s> of form and the rest; from seeing cessation, one enters the signless. From this it is known that form and the rest are not ultimately real. Where the five <s>skandhas</s> exist, there the thought "I am" arises. When the five <s>skandhas</s> do not exist, the thought "I am" ceases. Therefore all <s>skandhas</s> are empty. In the <s>Phenasūtra</s> (Sūtra of Foam), the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If a person sees a lump of foam and examines it wisely, he would know it to be hollow and empty. Just so, monks, if one rightly examines the form-aggregate, one knows it to be hollow, empty, insubstantial, and characterized by disintegration. One examines feeling as like a water bubble, perception as like a mirage, formations as like a plantain tree, and consciousness as like a magical illusion.' In that passage, the five similes illustrate the meaning of emptiness. Why? Because we see with our eyes that foam, as it dissolves, goes to non-existence. So too with bubbles and the rest. From this it is known that the <s>skandhas</s> are not ultimately real. Those sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) who are supremely disgusted with <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) see the primordial non-arising and voidness of <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, those who see impermanence

body.text: paśyanti | [teṣāṃ] vikṣepavināśaduḥkhalakṣaṇameva bhavati | ye niḥsvabhāvaṃ paśyanti, anyalakṣaṇābhāvāt te duḥkhacaryāṃ paripūrayanti | etattrividhaduḥkhaparipūraṇaṃ vimuktiprāpakamityucyate | [ataḥ] sarvadharmāḥ śūnyā iti jñātavyam |
body.translated_text: [for them] there is only the characteristic of disintegration, destruction, and suffering. Those who see the absence of own-nature, due to the absence of any other characteristic, fulfill the practice of suffering. This threefold fulfillment of suffering is called the means of attaining liberation. Therefore, one should know that all <s>dharmas</s> are empty.

body.text: śūnyatā ca vimokṣamukham | śūnyatā ceyaṃ na kevalaṃ sattvaśūnyatātmikā | dharmaśūnyatā[tmikā]pi cāsti | yathoktam- cakṣurutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati | nirudhyamānaṃ na kvacidgacchati | tadā prajānāti atītamanāgataṃ cakṣuḥ śūnyamiti | pratyutpannaṃ cakṣurapi caturmahābhūtavikalpitamityataḥ śūnyamiti | yathāha bhagavān- yaccakṣuṣi māṃsapiṇḍe khakkaṭaṃ kharagataṃ sa pṛthivī [dhātu]ḥ ityādi | ya imāṃ śūnyatāṃ pratilabhate sa vadati nāsti yatkiñciditi | kiñcāha- sarvasaṃskārāḥ prahīyanta iti prahāṇasvabhāvāḥ | vimucyanta iti vimuktikhabhāvāḥ | nirudhyanta iti nirodhasvabhāvāḥ iti | ato jñāyate sarve saṃskārā niruddhā bhavantīti | yadi vastusantaḥ saṃskārāḥ tadā na syuḥ samyak prahāṇavimuktinirodhāḥ | nirodhaścābhāva ityucyate | ato draṣṭavyaṃ paramārthataḥ saṃskārāḥ sarve 'bhāvātmakāḥ saṃvṛtitastu santi saṃskārā iti ||
body.translated_text: Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is the gateway to liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>). And this emptiness is not merely the emptiness of beings (<s>sattvaśūnyatā</s>); there is also the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaśūnyatā</s>). As stated: 'The eye, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go anywhere. Then one understands that the past and future eye is empty. The present eye too, being a conceptual construction of the four great elements (<s>caturmahābhūta</s>), is therefore empty.' As the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That which in the lump of flesh of the eye is hard and solid is the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>),' and so on. One who realizes this emptiness says: 'There is nothing whatsoever.' Further it is said: 'All <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations) are abandoned — their nature is abandonment. They are liberated — their nature is liberation, which is like space. They cease — their nature is cessation.' From this it is known that all formations are ceased. If formations were substantially real, then there would not be proper abandonment, liberation, and cessation. And cessation is called non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>). Therefore one should see that ultimately all formations are of the nature of non-existence, but conventionally formations exist.

body.text: dharmacittanirodhavargastripañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: End of the one hundred and fifty-third chapter, the chapter on the cessation of the <s>dharma</s>-mind (<s>dharmacittanirodhavarga</s>).

body.text: 154 nirodhavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 154. Chapter on Cessation (<s>Nirodhavarga</s>)

body.text: yannirvāṇālambanaṃ tat śūnyacittamityucyate | (pṛ) nirvāṇamasaddharmaḥ | cittaṃ kimālambate | (u) cittamidaṃ yatkiñcatābhāvamālambate | idaṃ pūrvameva pratipāditam | nirvāṇajñānatvāt | (pṛ) śūnyacittamidaṃ kutra nirudhyate | (u) sthānadvaye [nirudhyate] (1) acittakasamādhimupasampannasya (2) anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇaṃ praviṣṭhasya santānasamucchede vā nirudhyate | kasmāt | hetupratyayanirodhāt | acittakasamādhāvālambananirodhāt [tat] nirudhyate | santāne samucchidyamāne punaḥ karmakṣayāt [tat] nirudhyate |
body.translated_text: That which has <s>nirvāṇa</s> as its object is called the emptiness-mind (<s>śūnyacitta</s>). (Question) <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is a non-existent <s>dharma</s>. What does the mind take as its object? (Answer) This mind takes as its object the absence of all things whatsoever. This has been established previously, because it is the knowledge of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. (Question) Where does this emptiness-mind cease? (Answer) It ceases in two situations: (1) for one who has entered the mindless concentration (<s>acittakasamādhi</s>), and (2) for one who has entered <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>), or it ceases at the cutting off of the continuum (<s>santāna</s>). Why? Because of the cessation of causes and conditions. In the mindless concentration, it ceases due to the cessation of the object (<s>ālambana</s>). When the continuum is cut off, it ceases due to the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> (action).

body.text: śāstramāha- etāni trīṇi cittāni nirodhayato yogāvacarasya karmakleśā naiva punaḥ samudācaranti (pṛ) kasmāt na samudācaranti | (u) puruṣo 'yaṃ nairātmyasampanna ityataḥ karmakleśā nirudhyante | yathā pradīpo dharmaśca sati niśraye vartate | asati niśraye na vartate | evamātmacitte niśraye sati karmakleśānāṃ samudayaḥ | asati tu na samudayaḥ | anāsravā samyagdṛṣṭiḥ sarvāṇi nimittāni tathā pradahati yathā na kiñcidavaśiṣyate | yathā kalpāgniḥ pṛthivyādin niḥśeṣaṃ dahati | nimittābhāvāt karmakleśānāṃ na punaḥ samudayo bhavati | asmicittakasya tu karmakleśāḥ samudyanti | arhataḥ śūnyatājñānagatiṃgatasya asmimānarahitasya na punaḥ samudyanti |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: When the practitioner of <s>yoga</s> (<s>yogāvacara</s>) suppresses these three types of mind (<s>citta</s>), <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) never again arise. (Question) Why do they not arise? (Answer) Because this person is endowed with <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are suppressed. Just as a lamp and a <s>dharma</s> exist when there is a support, and do not exist when there is no support, so too when the mind of self (<s>ātma-citta</s>) exists as support, there is the arising of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>; but when it does not exist, there is no arising. The uncontaminated right view (<s>anāsravā samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) burns all signs (<s>nimitta</s>) such that nothing whatsoever remains, just as the fire at the end of the <s>kalpa</s> burns the earth and other elements without remainder. Due to the absence of signs, there is no further arising of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>. But for one who has the notion of 'I am' (<s>asmi-cittaka</s>), <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> do arise. For the <s>Arhat</s> who has entered the course of <s>śūnyatā</s>-knowledge and is free from the conceit of 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>), they do not arise again.

body.text: asya nūtnakarmānupacaye 'pi prāktanakarmahetunā kasmānnopapattirbhavati | (u) samyak- prajñayā tatkarmavināśānna vipākabhāgbhavati | yathā dagdhaṃ bījaṃ na punaḥ prarohati | asati ca tṛṣṇācitte na karmāṇi pacyante | yathā anabhiṣyanditāyāṃ bhūmau bījaṃ na prarohati | yogāvacarasyāsya sarvavijñānasthitiṣu sarvanimittanirodhe vijñānaṃ nirāśrayaṃ bhavati | ato nāstyupapattyāyatanam | yathā bījamanāśrayaṃ notpadyate | karmakleśapauṣkalyāt kāyamupādatte | apauṣkalye tu nirudhyate |
body.translated_text: Even though there is no accumulation of new <s>karma</s> for this one, why does rebirth not occur due to the cause of previous <s>karma</s>? (Answer) Through right <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), because that <s>karma</s> is destroyed, it does not become subject to fruition (<s>vipāka</s>). Just as a burnt seed does not sprout again. And when the mind of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā-citta</s>) does not exist, <s>karmas</s> do not ripen, just as a seed does not sprout on ground that has not been irrigated. For this practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, when all signs (<s>nimitta</s>) are suppressed in all stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>), consciousness becomes without support (<s>nirāśraya</s>). Therefore there is no basis for rebirth (<s>upapattyāyatana</s>), just as a seed without support does not arise. Through the fullness of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>, one takes up a body; but when there is no such fullness, it ceases.

body.text: sa kleśābhāvāt vikalahetupratyayaḥ satsvapi karmasu nopapattiṃ vedayate | sattvāḥ kleśahetorgatiṣu kāyaṃ vedayante | kāyaṃ vedayata ityataḥ tasya karmāṇi vipākaṃ prayacchanti | asati kleśe kāyo na vedyate | kāyavedyabhāvāt karmāṇi kasya vipākaṃ prayacchanti | yathā adharmeṇa prabalamadhitiṣṭhati uttamarṇo nāvakāśaṃ labhate | tathā yogāvacaro 'pi | saṃsāre 'vartamānasya santyapi karmāṇi na vipākaṃ prayacchanti | yathā baddhaṃ puruṣamanye janā yatheṣṭaṃ nindanti | evaṃ kleśabaddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ karmatāratamyavaśāt [kleśāḥ] vipākaṃ prayacchanti | pratilabdhavimokṣe tu nāvakāśaṃ labhante |
body.translated_text: Due to the absence of <s>kleśas</s>, his causes and conditions being incomplete, he does not experience rebirth even though <s>karmas</s> exist. Beings experience a body in the realms of existence (<s>gati</s>) due to the cause of <s>kleśas</s>. Because they experience a body, their <s>karmas</s> give fruition (<s>vipāka</s>). When <s>kleśa</s> is absent, a body is not experienced. Since there is no body to be experienced, to whom do the <s>karmas</s> give fruition? Just as when someone unlawfully dominates with force, the creditor finds no opportunity — so too for the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>. For one who does not continue in <s>saṃsāra</s>, even existing <s>karmas</s> do not give fruition, just as other people freely revile a bound person. Thus for beings bound by <s>kleśas</s>, [the afflictions] give fruition according to the degree of <s>karma</s>. But when liberation is attained, they find no opportunity.

body.text: svīyaṃ karma ca vipākaṃ prayacchati | śūnyacaryāvihāritvādasya puruṣasya dharmeṣu svalakṣaṇa[saṃjñā] nāstītyataḥ karmāṇi na vipākaṃ prayacchanti | yathā dattīkṛtasya putrasya dāyabhāgo nāsti | tathedamapi | kleśabalena ca karmāṇi pravartante | kleśavege kṣīṇe tu na tāni pravartante | yathā cakraṃ gatisthamapi vegakṣayānna punaḥ pravartate | kleśabale ca karmāṇi
body.translated_text: One's own <s>karma</s> also gives fruition. Because this person dwells in the practice of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), since there is no perception of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa-saṃjñā</s>) with regard to <s>dharmas</s>, <s>karmas</s> do not give fruition. Just as an adopted son has no share in the inheritance, so too is this case. And <s>karmas</s> operate through the force of <s>kleśas</s>. But when the momentum of <s>kleśas</s> is exhausted, those do not operate, just as a wheel, even while in motion, does not continue turning when its momentum is spent. And through the force of <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karmas</s>

body.text: vikārayanti | yathā sutavatsalāyā mātuḥ raktaṃ stanyaṃ pariṇamate | niruddhavātsalyacittāyāstu na punaḥ pariṇamate | evaṃ kleśabalāt karma vipākaṃ prayacchati | [kleśa]virahe tu na prayacchati | ayañca puruṣaḥ śīlasamādhiprajñādiguṇairbhāvitakāyaḥ | tatprabhāvamāhātmyāt karmāṇi nāvakāśaṃ labhante | ataḥ sadapi prāktanaṃ karma na vipākaṃ prayacchati | evamasya prāktanaṃ karma pratyutpanne kiñci[dvipāka]marpayati | nūtnaṃ tu karma na karoti | yathāgnirindhanānāṃ bhasmībhāve śāmyati | evamayaṃ puruṣo 'pi vedanīyābhāvānnirudhyate | [iti] trividhacittānāṃ nirodhātsarvaduḥkhebhyo 'tyantaṃ vimucyate | ato vidvān trividhacittāni nirundhyāt ||
body.translated_text: produce transformation. Just as the blood of an affectionate mother transforms into breast milk, but for one whose mind of maternal affection has ceased, it no longer transforms. Thus through the force of <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s> gives fruition; but in the absence of <s>kleśas</s>, it does not give fruition. And this person has a body cultivated through virtues such as <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Through the power and greatness of those, <s>karmas</s> find no opportunity. Therefore even existing previous <s>karma</s> does not give fruition. Thus his previous <s>karma</s> yields some [fruition] in the present, but he does not create new <s>karma</s>. Just as a fire is extinguished when the fuel is reduced to ashes, so too this person ceases due to the absence of anything to be experienced. Through the cessation of the three types of mind, he is completely liberated from all suffering. Therefore the wise one should suppress the three types of mind.

body.text: nirodhavargaścatuḥpañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), the one hundred and fifty-fourth.

body.text: nirodhasatyaskandhaḥ samāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: The section on the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatyaskandha</s>) is completed.

body.text: atha mārgasatyaskandhaḥ
body.translated_text: Now the section on the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatyaskandha</s>).

body.text: 155 mārgasatyaskandhe samādhyadhikāre samādhihetuvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 155. In the section on the truth of the path, in the topic of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration): the chapter on the causes of <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: śāstramāha- idānīṃ mārgasatyaṃ vicāryate | mārgasatyam- āryo 'ṣṭāṅgiko mārgaḥ samyak dṛṣṭiryāvat samyak samādhiḥ | āryo 'ṣṭāṅgiko mārgaḥ saṃkṣipya dvividhaḥ (1) samādhiḥ parikaraśca (2) jñānamiti |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: Now the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) is to be examined. The truth of the path is the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>ārya aṣṭāṅgika mārga</s>) — right view (<s>samyak dṛṣṭi</s>) up to right concentration (<s>samyak samādhi</s>). The Noble Eightfold Path is summarized as twofold: (1) <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and its auxiliaries, and (2) <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge).

body.text: idānīṃ samādhirvicārayitavyaḥ | (pṛ) kiṃlakṣaṇā samādhiḥ | (u) cittasyaikatrāvasthānaṃ samādhilakṣaṇam | (pṛ) kathaṃ cittamekatrāvatiṣṭhate | (u) bahulīkṛtabhāvanayā tatrāvatiṣṭhate | yadi bahuvāraṃ na bhāvayati tadā kṣiprameva vikṣipyate | (pṛ) kathaṃ bhāvayitavyam | (u) yathāsukhaṃ bhāvayitavyam | (pṛ) kathaṃ sukhayati | (u) kāyacittayordauṣṭhalyaṃ duḥkham | praśrabdhidharmeṇa kāyacittayordauṣṭhalye 'panīte sukhaṃ bhavati | (pṛ) kathaṃ praśrabdhirbhavati | (u) prītipratyayaṃ kāyacitte dānte bhavataḥ | (pṛ) kathaṃ prītirbhavati | (u) triratnasmaraṇadharmaśravaṇādinā cittaprāmodyāt bhavati | (pṛ) kathaṃ cittaprāmodyaṃ bhavati | (u) pariśuddhaśīladhāraṇāt cittasyaukaukṛtye bhavati |
body.translated_text: Now <s>samādhi</s> is to be examined. (Question) What is the characteristic of <s>samādhi</s>? (Answer) The one-pointed abiding of the mind (<s>citta</s>) is the characteristic of <s>samādhi</s>. (Question) How does the mind abide in one point? (Answer) Through repeated cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), it abides therein. If one does not cultivate many times, then it is quickly distracted. (Question) How should one cultivate? (Answer) One should cultivate with ease. (Question) How does one find ease? (Answer) Rigidity of body and mind is suffering. When the rigidity of body and mind is removed through the quality of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), there is ease. (Question) How does <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility) arise? (Answer) Through joy (<s>prīti</s>), the body and mind become tamed. (Question) How does <s>prīti</s> (joy) arise? (Answer) Through the gladness of mind arising from remembering the Three Jewels (<s>triratna</s>), hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and so forth. (Question) How does gladness of mind arise? (Answer) Through maintaining pure moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), the mind becomes free from remorse.

body.text: (pṛ) uktaḥ samādhihetuḥ | idānīṃ kasya samādhirhetuḥ | (u) ayaṃ yathābhūtajñānasya hetuḥ | yathābhūtajñānaṃ śūnyatājñānam | yathoktaṃ yogāvacaraḥ samāhitacitto viśuddhacitto vinīvaraṇacittaścittaratho 'calacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti duḥkhamāryasatyaṃ duḥkhasamudayaṃ dukhanirodhaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāmimārgamāryasatyam iti | ato yathābhūtajñānalipsunā samādhi bhāvanāyāṃ vīryamārabdhavyam | vikṣiptacittasya laukikasūtraśilpādihitameva na bhavati | kiṃ punarlokottaraṃ hitam | ato jñāyate laukikaṃ lokottarañca hitaṃ samāhitacittenaiva labhyate | sarvañca sat kuśalaṃ samyak jñānādhīnam | sarvamasadakuśalaṃ mithyājñānādhīnam | yathoktaṃ sūtre avidyā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvaṅgamākuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samāpattaye | anvagevāhrīkyamanapatrāpyam |
body.translated_text: (Question) The cause of <s>samādhi</s> has been stated. Now, what is <s>samādhi</s> the cause of? (Answer) It is the cause of knowledge as it truly is (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>). Knowledge as it truly is means the knowledge of emptiness (<s>śūnyatājñāna</s>). As stated: The practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, with concentrated mind, purified mind, mind freed from the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), with the mind as vehicle, with unshaken mind, knows as it truly is: suffering is a Noble Truth, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering is a Noble Truth. Therefore, one who desires knowledge as it truly is should exert effort in the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s>. For one with a distracted mind, even worldly benefit such as secular learning and crafts does not occur — how much less supramundane benefit? Therefore it is known that both worldly and supramundane benefit are obtained only through a concentrated mind. All that is good and wholesome is dependent on right knowledge; all that is bad and unwholesome is dependent on wrong knowledge. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'O monks, ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the forerunner for the attainment of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; following upon it are shamelessness and lack of moral dread.'

body.text: vidyā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvaṅgamā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samāpattaye anvageva hrīḥ apatrāpyam | iti | samādhistu samyagjñānasya hetuḥ | ato jñāyate sarvaṃ satkuśalaṃ samādhimupādāya bhavatīti | tasmāt bhāvanāyāṃ yogaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'O monks, knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) is the forerunner for the attainment of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; following upon it are moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>apatrāpya</s>).' Thus, <s>samādhi</s> is the cause of right knowledge. Therefore it is known that all good and wholesome things come about through <s>samādhi</s>. Hence one should make effort in cultivation.

body.text: samādhihetuvargaḥ pañcapañcāduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the causes of <s>samādhi</s>, the one hundred and fifty-fifth.

body.text: 156 samādhilakṣaṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 156. The chapter on the characteristics of <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) uktaṃ bhavatā cittasyaikatrāvasthānaṃ samādhilakṣaṇamiti tatra samādhiścittañcaikaṃ uta bhinnam | (u) na te bhinne | kecidāhu- samādhiścittañca bhinne | samādhilabdhacittamekatrāvatiṣṭhata iti | sadapīdaṃ vacanamayuktārthakam | yadi cittaṃ samādhilabdhamālambane 'vatiṣṭhata iti | samādhiriyamapi ālambane 'vatiṣṭhamānā samādhyantaramupādāyāvatiṣṭheta | evamanavasthā bhavati | tattu na sambhavati | yadīyaṃ samādhiḥ prakṛtito 'vasthānamiti | cittamapi na samādhimupādāyāvatiṣṭheta | ataḥ samādheranyat cittamiti yadvacanaṃ tadaprakṛṣṭārthakam | vedanāsaṃjñādayaścetasikadharmā apyālambane 'vatiṣṭhante | te 'pi kaṃ dharmamupādāyāvatiṣṭhanta itīdaṃ vaktavyam | yadi vedanāsaṃjñādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ samādhirasti | tulyaḥ pūrvadoṣaḥ syāt | sūtre ca cittasyaikāgratā samādhilakṣaṇamiti kevalamuktam | na tu cittaṃ samādhilabdhamavatiṣṭhata iti | ato jñāyate na yuktamiti | cittasyaikāgratetyukte nānyadharmaḥ prakāśito bhavati | yathā pūrvamuktam- yatra cittaṃ sukhi bhavati tasminnālambane 'vatiṣṭhata iti | cittasya koṭiḥ samādhirna pṛthagbhavatīti draṣṭavyam | yathā cittaṃ dīrghakālāvasthānaṃ samādhirityucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) You have stated that the one-pointed abiding of the mind is the characteristic of <s>samādhi</s>. In that case, are <s>samādhi</s> and mind one or different? (Answer) They are not different. Some say that <s>samādhi</s> and mind are different, that the mind having obtained <s>samādhi</s> abides in one point. But even this statement has an unreasonable meaning. If the mind abides on an object having obtained <s>samādhi</s>, then this <s>samādhi</s> itself, while abiding on the object, would need to rely on another <s>samādhi</s> to abide — thus there would be an infinite regress. And that is not possible. If this <s>samādhi</s> abides by its own nature, then the mind too would not need <s>samādhi</s> to abide. Therefore the statement that mind is other than <s>samādhi</s> has no real meaning. Mental factors (<s>cetasika dharma</s>) such as feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) also abide on an object — it must then be stated: relying on what <s>dharma</s> do they abide? If each of feeling, perception, and so on has its own <s>samādhi</s>, the same fault as before would apply. In the <s>sūtra</s> it is merely stated that one-pointedness of mind is the characteristic of <s>samādhi</s>, but not that the mind abides having obtained <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore it is known that this [view] is not correct. When one-pointedness of mind is spoken of, no separate <s>dharma</s> is indicated. As stated earlier: where the mind is happy, it abides on that object. One should see that the culmination of the mind is <s>samādhi</s>, not something separate. Just as when the mind abides for a long time, it is called <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) samādhiriyaṃ kiṃ sāsravā utānāsravā | (u) samādhirdvividhā sāsravā anāsravā ceti | laukikā dhyānasamādhayaḥ sāsravāḥ | dharmāvasthāmupasampannasya samādhayo 'nāsravā ityucyante | kasmāt | kālo 'yaṃ yathābhūtajñānadarśanamityucyate | tasya kālasya dvividhaṃ nāma samādhiriti prajñā ceti | cittasamādhānāt samādhiḥ | yathābhūtaprajñānāt
body.translated_text: (Question) Is this <s>samādhi</s> with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) or without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>)? (Answer) <s>Samādhi</s> is of two kinds: with outflows and without outflows. Worldly <s>dhyāna</s> concentrations are with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). The concentrations of one who has attained the state of <s>dharma</s> are called without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>). Why? Because this is the time called 'seeing things as they truly are' (<s>yathābhūtajñānadarśana</s>). That time has two names: <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Due to the settling of the mind, it is <s>samādhi</s>; due to knowing things as they truly are, it is

body.text: prajñā | cittasamādhānaṃ trividhaṃ kuśalamakuśalamavyākṛtamiti | tatra kuśalena cittasamādhānameva samādhiḥ | natvakuśalena avyākṛtena vā | sā samādhirdvividhā ekā vimuktihetuḥ aparā avimuktihetuḥ | vimuktiheturnāma niyatamūlakam | kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ- anāsravasamādhireva niyatamūlamiti | sa vādo na yuktaḥ | sāsravānāsravā yadi vimuktiṃ karoti | sā sarvāpi niyatamūlamityucyeta |
body.translated_text: <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). The settling of the mind (<s>cittasamādhāna</s>) is threefold: wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). Among these, only the wholesome settling of the mind is <s>samādhi</s>, not the unwholesome or the indeterminate. That <s>samādhi</s> is of two kinds: one is a cause of liberation (<s>vimuktihetū</s>), the other is not a cause of liberation. 'Cause of liberation' means having a definite root (<s>niyatamūla</s>). Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say that only uncontaminated <s>samādhi</s> (<s>anāsrava samādhi</s>) has a definite root. That view is not correct. If both contaminated and uncontaminated [<s>samādhi</s>] produce liberation, then all of it would be called 'having a definite root.'

body.text: samādhiriyaṃ yathālambanāvasthānaṃ tridhā vibhajyate | parīttā vipulā apramāṇā ceti | cittaṃ kiñcitkālamavasthāya yadi parīttamālambanaṃ paśyati[tadā] parīttetyucyate | anye dve api tathā | samayavaśātrividhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati | pragrahalakṣaṇaṃ vyutthānalakṣaṇaṃ tyāgalakṣaṇamiti | citte 'balīne vyutthānalakṣaṇamupayoktavyam | citta uddhata pragrahalakṣaṇaṃ prayoktavyam | dānte ca citte tyāgalakṣaṇaṃ prayoktavyam | yathā suvarṇakāraḥ suvarṇaṃ dravayati tāpayati secayati kāle ca sthapayati | yadi sadā tāpayati | tadā dravībhavati | sadā secane ghanībhavati | sadā sthapanesphūryate | evaṃ yogāvacarasya cittamapi | kampitasyāpragrahe sadā vikṣepaḥ | avalīnasyāvyutthāne kausīdyam | dāntasyātyāge punaradamanam | yathā ca dānto 'śvaḥ pravege pragṛhyate | dandhaḥ [kaśayā]tāḍyate | dāntaḥ parityajyate | evaṃ yogāvacarasya dāntaṃ cittamapi |
body.translated_text: This <s>samādhi</s> is divided threefold according to its abiding on the object: limited (<s>parītta</s>), extensive (<s>vipula</s>), and immeasurable (<s>apramāṇa</s>). If the mind, having abided for some time, perceives a limited object, it is called 'limited.' The other two are likewise. According to the occasion, there are three characteristics: the characteristic of restraining (<s>pragraha</s>), the characteristic of arousing (<s>vyutthāna</s>), and the characteristic of equanimity (<s>tyāga</s>). When the mind is sluggish, the characteristic of arousing should be applied. When the mind is agitated, the characteristic of restraining should be applied. When the mind is tamed, the characteristic of equanimity should be applied. Just as a goldsmith melts, heats, sprinkles, and at the right time sets aside the gold — if he always heats it, it melts away; if he always sprinkles it, it hardens; if he always sets it aside, it cracks. So too is the mind of the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>. Without restraining the agitated, there is constant distraction; without arousing the sluggish, there is laziness; without equanimity toward the tamed, there is excessive taming. Just as a tamed horse is restrained when it gallops, a slow one is struck with a whip, and a tamed one is left alone — so too is the tamed mind of the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>.

body.text: samādherasyāstrividha upāyaḥ samādhyavatāropāyaḥ samādhyavasthānopāyaḥ samādhivyutthānopāya iti | yathādharmaṃ samādhāvatarati | ayaṃ samādhyavatāropāyaḥ | samādhisthito na calati | ayaṃ samādhyavasthānopāyaḥ | yathādharmaṃ samādhervyuttiṣṭhate | ayaṃ samādhivyutthānopāyaḥ | (pṛ) kathamimān trividhānupāyān pratilabhate | (u) yogāvacaraḥ svacittalakṣaṇaṃ gṛhṇan evaṃ pragṛhṇan evaṃ vyuttiṣṭhan evaṃ parityajan samādhāvavatarati | tathā nirgacchati ca | (pṛ) sākṣādeva samādhigrahe ka upayoga upāyasya | (u) trividhopāyān pravartamānasya ādīnavo bhavati | yathepsitañca na vindate | avataritumicchan vyutiṣṭheta vyutthātumicchan punaravataret | itīdṛśā doṣāḥ santi | lābhaṃ hāniṃ manyeta | hāniñca lābham | yathā kiñcidviśuddharūpaṃ kiñcitprakāśarūpañca dṛṣṭvā vadeta- mahāhitaṃ labdhamiti | anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamityādyanusmarataḥ cittaṃ na sukhi bhavati | pratyuta hānikaramiti vadet |
body.translated_text: There are three methods for this <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration): the method of entering <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samādhyavatāropāya</s>), the method of remaining in <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samādhyavasthānopāya</s>), and the method of emerging from <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samādhivyutthānopāya</s>). One enters <s>samādhi</s> in accordance with the <s>dharma</s> — this is the method of entering <s>samādhi</s>. One who is established in <s>samādhi</s> does not waver — this is the method of remaining in <s>samādhi</s>. One emerges from <s>samādhi</s> in accordance with the <s>dharma</s> — this is the method of emerging from <s>samādhi</s>. (Question) How does one attain these three methods? (Answer) The <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner of yoga), grasping the characteristics of one's own mind, thus taking hold, thus emerging, thus relinquishing, enters <s>samādhi</s>. And likewise exits. (Question) If <s>samādhi</s> can be grasped directly, what is the use of the method? (Answer) For one who proceeds with the three methods, faults arise. And one does not obtain what is desired. Wishing to enter, one would emerge; wishing to emerge, one would enter again — such are the defects. One would consider gain as loss, and loss as gain. For instance, upon seeing some pure form or some luminous form, one would say 'A great benefit has been obtained.' For one who recollects 'impermanent, suffering, empty' and so forth, the mind does not become happy. On the contrary, one would say 'this is harmful.'

body.text: (pṛ) yogāvacarasya kasmāt kadācitsamādhilābho 'sti kadācinnāsti | (u) samādhilābhasya catvāraḥ pratyayāḥ- (1) ihādhvani yunakti, (2) pūrvakāyapratyayaḥ (3) samādhilakṣaṇaṃ sugṛhṇāti, (4) śrutvā samādhidharmānanuvartayati iti | samādhibhāvanāścaturvidhāḥ- (1) sadāprayogī naikāgraṃ carati | (2) ekāgraṃ carati na sadāprayukto bhavati | (3) sadāprayuktaśca bhavati ekāgrañca carati | (4) na sadā prayukto naikāgraṃ carati | kiñca santi caturvidhāḥ bahukuśalaḥ alpaprajñaḥ, alpakuśalo bahuprajñaḥ, bahukuśalo bahuprajñaḥ, alpakuśalo 'lpaprajña iti | eṣutṛtīyo yogāvacaro 'vaśyaṃ labhate | caturtho nāvaśyaṃ labhate | prathamadvitīyau yadi dāntau samau tadā labhete ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Why does the <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner of yoga) sometimes attain <s>samādhi</s> and sometimes not? (Answer) There are four conditions for attaining <s>samādhi</s>: (1) one yokes oneself in this path, (2) the condition of a previous body, (3) one grasps well the characteristics of <s>samādhi</s>, (4) having heard the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>samādhi</s>, one follows them. The cultivations of <s>samādhi</s> are fourfold: (1) one is always engaged but does not practice one-pointedly; (2) one practices one-pointedly but is not always engaged; (3) one is always engaged and also practices one-pointedly; (4) one is neither always engaged nor practices one-pointedly. Furthermore, there are four types: one of much merit (<s>bahukuśala</s>) but little wisdom, one of little merit but much wisdom, one of much merit and much wisdom, and one of little merit and little wisdom. Among these, the third <s>yogāvacara</s> certainly attains [<s>samādhi</s>]. The fourth does not necessarily attain it. The first and second, if they are restrained and balanced, then they attain it.

body.text: samādhilakṣaṇavargaḥ ṣaṭpañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter on the Characteristics of <s>Samādhi</s> (<s>samādhilakṣaṇavarga</s>), the one hundred and fifty-sixth.

body.text: 157 trisamādhivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 157. Chapter on the Three <s>Samādhis</s> (<s>trisamādhivarga</s>).
