body.text: (pṛ) uktaṃ sūtre- trayaḥ samādhayaḥ ekāṅgabhāvanasamādhiḥ, ubhayāṅgabhāvanasamādhiḥ aryaḥ samyaksamādhiriti | kimidam | (u) ekāṅgabhāvana iti yat samādhiṃ bhāvayati na prajñām | prajñāṃ vā bhāvayati na samādhim | ubhayāṅgabhāvana iti samādhiṃ bhāvayati prajñāñca bhāvayati | ayaṃ laukikasamādhirūṣmādidharmagataḥ | āryaḥ samyaksamādhiriti yaddharmāvasthāmupasampanno nirodhasatyaṃ sākṣātkaroti | sa āryaḥ samyagityucyate | kenedaṃ jñāyate | yathā sthaviro bhikṣurāha- yogāvacaraḥ samādhinā cittaṃ bhāvayan prajñāmupādāya kleśān pratiṣedhayati | prajñayā cittaṃ bhāvayan samādhimupādāya kleśān pratiṣedhayati | samādhinā prajñayā ca cittaṃ bhāvayan svabhāvamupādāya vimucyate | svabhāvo nāma yaḥ prahāṇasvabhāvaḥ viyogasvabhāvo nirodhasvabhāvaḥ | samādhiprajñayoryugapatprapūraṇādāryaḥ samyagityucyate | yathā samādhiprajñābhyāṃ vimuktilabdhaḥ sarvaśo vimuktaityucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are three <s>samādhis</s> — the <s>samādhi</s> of one-sided cultivation (<s>ekāṅgabhāvanāsamādhi</s>), the <s>samādhi</s> of two-sided cultivation (<s>ubhayāṅgabhāvanāsamādhi</s>), and the noble right <s>samādhi</s> (<s>ārya samyaksamādhi</s>).' What does this mean? (Answer) 'One-sided cultivation' means that one cultivates <s>samādhi</s> but not wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), or cultivates wisdom but not <s>samādhi</s>. 'Two-sided cultivation' means that one cultivates both <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom. This is a worldly <s>samādhi</s> (<s>laukikasamādhi</s>) pertaining to the <s>dharmas</s> of the heat stage (<s>ūṣmādi</s>) and the like. 'The noble right <s>samādhi</s>' means that having attained the stage of <s>dharma</s>-abiding, one directly realizes the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>). That is called noble and right. How is this known? As the elder monk (<s>sthavira bhikṣu</s>) said: 'The <s>yogāvacara</s>, cultivating the mind through <s>samādhi</s>, relying on wisdom, restrains the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Cultivating the mind through wisdom, relying on <s>samādhi</s>, he restrains the <s>kleśas</s>. Cultivating the mind through both <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom, relying on the own-nature, one is liberated.' The own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) means the nature of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasvabhāva</s>), the nature of separation (<s>viyogasvabhāva</s>), the nature of cessation (<s>nirodhasvabhāva</s>). Because both <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom are simultaneously fulfilled, it is called noble and right. Just as one who has attained liberation through both <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom is said to be completely liberated.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- ekāṅgabhāvana iti yadi samādhimupādāya raśmiṃ paśyati na rūpāṇi | yadi(vā)rūpāṇi paśyati na raśmim | ubhayāṅgabhāvana iti yat rūpañca paśyati raśmiñca paśyati | āryaḥ samyaksamādhiriti yat śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ pratilabdhaḥ samādhiḥ
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: 'One-sided cultivation' means that if one relies on <s>samādhi</s>, one sees radiance (<s>raśmi</s>) but not forms (<s>rūpa</s>); or if one sees forms, one does not see radiance. 'Two-sided cultivation' means that one sees both forms and radiance. 'The noble right <s>samādhi</s>' means the <s>samādhi</s> attained through both the trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and the one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>)

body.text: iti | kathamidam | (u) raśmimātraṃ paśyati na rūpamiti nāsti kiñcana sūtram sūtre kevalamuktam- ahaṃ prakṛtito raśmimapaśyaṃ rūpamapyapaśyam | idānīṃ raśmirvinaṣṭaḥ, rūpamapi na paśyāmīti | bhavatā ca vaktavyaṃ kena kāraṇena raśmiṃ paśyati na rūpam ityādi | iti nāvocaḥ |
body.translated_text: — thus it is said. How is this? (Answer) There is no <s>sūtra</s> at all that says one sees only radiance but not form. In the <s>sūtra</s>, it is merely stated: 'Previously I did not see radiance, nor did I see form. Now the radiance has disappeared, and I do not see form either.' And you should explain for what reason one sees radiance but not form, and so forth. But this was not stated.

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktaṃ- trayaḥ samādhayaḥ śūnyato 'nimitto 'praṇihita iti | eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ samādhīnāṃ ko bhedaḥ | (u) yadi yogāvacaro na paśyati sattvaṃ nāpi dharmam | ayamucyate śūnyataḥ [samādhi]riti | īdṛśe śūnye[yadi]grāhyanimittaṃ nāsti | ayaṃ śūnya evānimittaḥ | śūnye ca nāsti praṇihitaṃ kiñcana | ayaṃ śūnyaḥ[samādhi]revāpraṇihita ityucyate | atastrayo 'pyekārthakāḥ | (pṛ) tathā cet kasmāt traya ityucyante | (u) śūnyaṃ bhāvayediti śūnyatāsamartha āha | śūnyaṃ bhāvayan hitaṃ labhate yaduta nimittaṃ na paśyatīti | nimittādarśanādanimittaḥ | animittatvādapraṇihītaḥ | apraṇihitatvānna kāyaṃ vedayate | kāyāvedanātsarvaduḥkhānmucyate | ityādi hitāni śūnyatābhāvanayā labhate | ata ucyate traya iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are three <s>samādhis</s> — emptiness (<s>śūnyata</s>), signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), and wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>).' What is the distinction among these three <s>samādhis</s>? (Answer) If the <s>yogāvacara</s> perceives neither a being (<s>sattva</s>) nor a <s>dharma</s>, this is called the <s>samādhi</s> of emptiness (<s>śūnyata</s>). In such emptiness, if there is no sign (<s>nimitta</s>) to be grasped, this very emptiness is signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>). And in emptiness, there is nothing to wish for — this very emptiness <s>samādhi</s> is called wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>). Therefore, all three are of one meaning. (Question) If so, why are they said to be three? (Answer) 'One should cultivate emptiness' — this is stated from the standpoint of the capacity of emptiness. Cultivating emptiness, one obtains a benefit, namely that one does not perceive signs. From not perceiving signs, there is signlessness. From signlessness, there is wishlessness. From wishlessness, one does not experience the body. From not experiencing the body, one is freed from all suffering. And so forth — these benefits are obtained through the cultivation of emptiness. Therefore it is said to be three.

body.text: kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ yaḥ samādhiḥ śūnyānātmākāreṇa bhavati ayaṃ śūnya ityucyate | ya ākāro 'nityato duḥkhato hetutaḥ samudayato janakataḥ pratyayato mārgato yathāvadācarato niryāṇato bhavati | ayamapraṇihitaḥ | ya ākāro nirodhata upaśamataḥ praṇītato viyogato bhavati | ayamanimitta iti | kathamidam | (u) yadāha bhavān- anityato duḥkhata ākāraḥ apraṇihita iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | bhagavān sadā vadati yadanityaṃ tadeva duḥkham | yat dukhaṃ tadevānātmakam iti | nairātmyaṃ prajānan na punaḥ praṇidadhāti | ato jñāyate śūnyatvācca na praṇidadhātīti | hetutaḥ samudayato janakataḥ pratyayata ākāra iti matam | tat tathaiva syāt | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre- yatkiñcitsamudayalakṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ tannirodhalakṣaṇamiti paśyan nirvidyate iti | mārge ca na bhavedapraṇihita ākāraḥ | kasmāt | praṇidhānaṃ hi tṛṣṇāṅgam | yathāsūtramuktam hīnaṃ madhyamaṃ praṇidhānaṃ na mārga āsaktijanakam | ato na bhavedapraṇihita ākāraḥ | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- pañcānāṃ skandhānāṃ nirodhānnirodha ityucyate iti jñātavyam | śūnya eva nirodha ityucyate | na
body.translated_text: Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> (Abhidharma scholars) say: The <s>samādhi</s> that has the aspect of emptiness and non-self is called 'emptiness.' The aspect that has the character of impermanence, suffering, cause, origination, production, condition, path, right practice, and leading to liberation — this is 'wishlessness' (<s>apraṇihita</s>). The aspect that has the character of cessation, peace, excellence, and separation — this is 'signlessness' (<s>ānimitta</s>). How is this? (Answer) What you say — that the aspect of impermanence and suffering is wishlessness — is not correct. Why? The Blessed One always says: 'Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering. Whatever is suffering, that is without self.' Knowing non-self, one no longer has wishes. Therefore it is known that because of emptiness, one does not wish. As for the view that the aspects of cause, origination, production, and condition [constitute wishlessness] — that too would be the same. Why? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whatever has the characteristic of origination, all that has the characteristic of cessation' — seeing thus, one becomes disenchanted. And the aspect of wishlessness should not apply to the path. Why? For aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) is a limb of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Inferior and middling aspirations are not the path; they give rise to attachment.' Therefore the aspect of wishlessness should not apply. Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'From the cessation of the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), it is called cessation' — this should be understood. Emptiness itself is called cessation. Not

body.text: tatrāsti praṇidhānam | kāyatṛṣṇā hi praṇidhānaṃ bhavati | ato jñāyate ime traya ekārthakā iti na syādbheda iti |
body.translated_text: — therein is there aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). For aspiration for the body arises from craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). Therefore it is known that these three are of one meaning, and there should be no distinction.

body.text: (pṛ) kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- trayaḥ samādhayaḥ śūnyaśūnyaḥ, apraṇitāpraṇihitaḥ, animittānimitta iti | kathamidam | (u) śūnyena pañcaskandhān śūnyān dṛṣṭvā ekena śūnyena punarimaṃ śūnyaṃ śūnyīkaroti | ayaṃ śūnyaśūnya ityucyate | apraṇihitena pañcaskandhān nirvidya apraṇihitena punarimamapraṇihitaṃ nirvedayati | ayamapraṇihitāpraṇihitaḥ | animittena pañcaskandhān praśāntān dṛṣṭvā animittena punaranimittaṃ na gṛhṇāti | ayamanimittānimittaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are three <s>samādhis</s> — emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyaśūnya</s>), wishlessness of wishlessness (<s>apraṇitāpraṇihita</s>), and signlessness of signlessness (<s>animittānimitta</s>).' How is this? (Answer) Having seen the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) as empty through emptiness, one further empties this emptiness itself with another emptiness — this is called emptiness of emptiness. Having become disenchanted with the five aggregates through wishlessness, one further becomes disenchanted with this wishlessness through [another] wishlessness — this is wishlessness of wishlessness. Having seen the five aggregates as quiescent through signlessness, one further does not grasp this signlessness through [another] signlessness — this is signlessness of signlessness.

body.text: (pṛ) ābhidharmikā āhuḥ- traya ime samādhayaḥ sāsravā iti | kathamidam | (u) ime na sāsravāḥ | kasmāt | samayasyāsyā nāsravānuśayatvāt | samādhirayaṃ śūnyādipradhānaḥ | kathaṃ sāsravo bhavet | (pṛ) yadi śūnyādayaḥ samādhayo vastutaḥ prajñātmakāḥ | kathaṃ samādhirityucyate | (u) samādhīnāṃ bhedāt | samādhiśca yathābhūtajñānadarśanādhāyakatvāt samādhirityucyate | phale hetūpacārāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: These three <s>samādhis</s> are with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). How is this? (Answer) These are not with outflows. Why? Because of the non-outflow nature of this <s>samādhi</s>'s agreement. This <s>samādhi</s> has emptiness and the like as its principal [objects]. How could it be with outflows? (Question) If emptiness and the other <s>samādhis</s> are in reality of the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), how are they called <s>samādhi</s>? (Answer) Because of the divisions of <s>samādhi</s>. And <s>samādhi</s>, because it serves as the basis for seeing things as they truly are (<s>yathābhūtajñānadarśana</s>), is called <s>samādhi</s>. This is a designation of the cause by the name of the effect.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ- śūnyaśūnyādayaḥ samādhayo 'śaikṣajanamātralabhyā nānyairiti | kathamidam | (u) śaikṣajanā api labheyuḥ | kasmāt | yogāvacareṇa hi sāsravāṇāmanāsravāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodho 'dhigantavyaḥ | ataḥ śaikṣajanairapi anāsravadharmāṇāṃ nirodho 'dhigantavyaḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: The <s>samādhis</s> of emptiness of emptiness and the like are attainable only by those who are beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), not by others. How is this? (Answer) Those who are still in training (<s>śaikṣa</s>) should also be able to attain them. Why? Because the <s>yogāvacara</s> must realize the cessation of all <s>dharmas</s>, both with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) and without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>). Therefore, those in training too should realize the cessation of <s>dharmas</s> without outflows.

body.text: trisamādhivargaḥ saptapañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter on the Three <s>Samādhis</s> (<s>trisamādhivarga</s>), the one hundred and fifty-seventh.

body.text: 158 catussamādhibhāvanāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 158. Chapter on the Four Cultivations of <s>Samādhi</s> (<s>catussamādhibhāvanāvarga</s>).

body.text: asti samādhibhāvanā dṛṣṭadharmasukha [vihāra]āyaṃ saṃvartate | asti samādhibhāvanā jñānadarśana[pratilābha]āya saṃvartate | asti samādhibhāvanā smṛtisamprajanyāya saṃvartate | asti samādhibhāvanā āsravāṇāṃ kṣayāya saṃvartate | yaḥ samādhiḥ dṛṣṭadharmasukhaprāpako yaduta dvitīyadhyānādayaḥ | [sā prathamā bhavanā |]kenedaṃ jñāyate | bhagavānāha- dvitīyadhyānaṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ nāmne saṃvartate anyadharmāya saṃvartate yathā piṇḍapātāya śrāvastyāṃ praveśa iti |
body.translated_text: There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that leads to the happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukha</s>). There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that leads to the attainment of knowledge and vision (<s>jñānadarśana</s>). There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that leads to mindfulness and clear comprehension (<s>smṛtisamprajanya</s>). There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that leads to the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>). The <s>samādhi</s> that yields the happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life is, namely, the second <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and so forth. [This is the first cultivation.] How is this known? The Blessed One said: 'The second <s>dhyāna</s>, born of <s>samādhi</s>, [yields] joy and happiness (<s>prītisukha</s>)' — it does not lead to any other <s>dharma</s>, just as entering <s>Śrāvastī</s> is for the purpose of alms-round (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) prathamaṃ dhyānamapi saprītisukham | kasmānnocyate sa dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra iti | (u) prathamadhyānasya cittavikṣepakavitarkavicāravyāmiśritatvāt na taducyate dṛṣṭadharmasukhamiti (pṛ) dvitīyadhyānasyāpi santi prītyādayaścittavikṣepakā dharmāḥ | kasmāducyate sukhamiti | (u) sarvavitarkavicārapūrvakaṃ cittaparigrahāt prītyādayaḥ sukhamityucyante, duḥkhākārataḥ paraṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhamityucyate | prathamadhyāne duḥkhamaudārikam | dvitīyadhyānādiṣu duḥkhaṃ sūkṣmam | sūkṣmaduḥkhatvāt sukhamityākhyāṃ labhate |
body.translated_text: (Question) The first <s>dhyāna</s> also has joy and happiness. Why is it not called 'the happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life'? (Answer) Because the first <s>dhyāna</s> is mixed with thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and examination (<s>vicāra</s>), which are disturbers of the mind, it is not called 'the happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life.' (Question) But the second <s>dhyāna</s> also has joy (<s>prīti</s>) and other <s>dharmas</s> that disturb the mind. Why is it called happiness? (Answer) Because all thought and examination have been previously restrained, joy and the rest are called happiness. From the aspect of suffering, all beyond that is called suffering. In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, suffering is gross. In the second <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond, suffering is subtle. Because the suffering is subtle, it obtains the designation 'happiness.'

body.text: (pṛ) dvitīyadhyānādayaḥ sāṃparāyikasukhavihārā api bhavanti | kasmāt dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāramātramucyate | (u) yathājātaśatroḥ sāndṛṣṭikaṃ śrāmaṇyaphalamuktam | pratyāsatyocyate [tathā] | pañcakāmasukhānāṃ bhedāyocyate dṛṣṭadharmasukha[vihāra i]ti | yadi pañcakāmasukhāsaktaḥ kaścit, ato na dhyānabhāgbhavati | tadarthamāha- pañcakāmasukhānāṃ viyoge paramaṃ dṛṣṭadharmasukhaṃ pratilabhadhva iti | buddhā na sāṃparāyikakāyavedanaṃ praśaṃsanti | ato nābhidadhati sāmparāyikaṃ sukham | laukikā vadanti sukhaṃ gṛhasthasya na pravrajitasyeti | ato bhagavānāha- idaṃ pravrajitasya dṛṣṭadharme sukhamiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) The second <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond also constitute happiness pertaining to future lives (<s>sāṃparāyikasukha</s>). Why is only 'the happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life' mentioned? (Answer) Just as the visible fruit of the ascetic life was spoken of to <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, it is stated on account of its immediacy. It is called 'the happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life' to distinguish it from the pleasures of the five sensual desires (<s>pañcakāmasukha</s>). If someone is attached to the pleasures of the five sensual desires, they cannot partake of <s>dhyāna</s>. For that purpose, he said: 'Having separated from the pleasures of the five sensual desires, attain the supreme happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life.' The <s>Buddhas</s> do not praise the bodily sensation of future lives. Therefore they do not affirm the happiness pertaining to future lives. Worldly people say that happiness belongs to the householder, not to the renunciant. Therefore the Blessed One said: 'This is the happiness of the renunciant in seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life.'

body.text: imāścatasraḥ samādhibhāvanāḥ sarvā dṛṣṭadharmasukha[vihārā]ya saṃvartante | prathamāyā nāmopacārāt kevalamucyate dṛṣṭadharmasukha[vihārāye]ti |
body.translated_text: All these four cultivations of <s>samādhi</s> lead to the happiness of seeing <s>dharmas</s> in the present life. The first is called thus merely by way of designation (<s>nāmopacāra</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadīmāścasraḥ samādhibhāvanā nānāhitāni sādhayanti | kasmātkevalamucyante catvārīmāni hitāni | (u) hitaṃ dvividhaṃ laukikaṃ lokottaramiti | dvitīyā samādhibhāvanā laukikahitāya bhavati yaduta jñānadarśanam | jñānaṃ nāmāṣṭavimokṣāyatanadaśakṛtsnāyatanādihitam | darśanaṃ pañcābhijñādihitam | kasmāt | cakṣuṣā dṛśyamānatvāt hitamidaṃ darśanamityucyate | idaṃ raśmigrahamupādāya siddhatvāt jñānadarśanamiti bhavati | yat raśmilakṣaṇamityucyate dvitīyamidaṃ lokottaraṃ hitam |
body.translated_text: (Question) If these four cultivations of concentration (<s>samādhibhāvanā</s>) accomplish various benefits, why are only four benefits stated? (Answer) Benefits are of two kinds: mundane (<s>laukika</s>) and supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>). The second cultivation of concentration is for mundane benefit, namely knowledge and vision (<s>jñānadarśana</s>). Knowledge means the benefit of the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>), the bases of [infinite] space (<s>āyatana</s>), the ten totalities (<s>daśakṛtsnāyatana</s>), and the like. Vision means the benefit of the five superknowledges (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>) and the like. Why? Because this benefit is seen with the eye, it is called 'vision.' This is established depending on the grasping of radiance — therefore it is called 'knowledge and vision.' What is called 'the characteristic of radiance' — this is the second, the supramundane benefit.

body.text: pañcaskandhān samprajānātīti samprajanyam | ataḥ sūtra uktam- sasmṛtisamprajanyo
body.translated_text: Clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>) means to fully comprehend the five aggregates. Therefore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The practitioner (<s>yogāvacara</s>) endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension

body.text: yogāvacaro yā vedanā vitarkāḥ saṃjñā utpadyante sarvā[stāḥ] pratijānāti iti | vedanānāṃ prajñānaṃ nāma sparśapratyayā vedanā, nāsti tu vedaka iti | vitarkānāṃ prajñānaṃ nāma ahamiti vitarkaḥ; kathaṃ [sa] na bhavet | yaḥ strīpuruṣādiprajñaptisaṃjñāvikalpaḥ, tatsaṃjñāpratibhedanā vitarkā na bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- vitarkaḥ kiṃ nidānaḥ | [vitarkaḥ] [prapañca] saṃjñā [saṃkhyā] nidāna iti | ato jñāyate prajñaptisaṃjñāpratibhedanāt smṛtisamprajanyaṃ nāma | smṛtisamprajanyenāsravakṣayo labhyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yogāvacaraḥ pañcānāṃ skandhānāmudayavyayānudarśī skandhānāṃ nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti iti | ato jñāyate | sarvāṇi laukikāni lokottarāṇi hitāni caturṣu saṅgṛhītānīti |
body.translated_text: — whatever feelings, thoughts, and perceptions arise, he fully recognizes all of them.' The full understanding of feelings means: 'Feeling is conditioned by contact — but there is no experiencer.' The full understanding of thoughts means: The thought 'I' — how could it not arise? The conceptual discrimination of conventional designations such as 'woman,' 'man,' and the like — the breaking apart of those perceptions is [what ensures that] thoughts do not arise. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'What is the cause of thought? Thought has perception of proliferation (<s>prapañcasaṃjñā</s>) as its cause.' From this it is known that the breaking apart of the perception of conventional designation is what is called 'mindfulness and clear comprehension.' Through mindfulness and clear comprehension, the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) is obtained. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The practitioner, contemplating the arising and passing away of the five aggregates, directly realizes the cessation of the aggregates.' From this it is known that all mundane and supramundane benefits are included in the four [cultivations of concentration].

body.text: (pṛ) kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ- caturthadhyāne 'rhatphalaṃ pratilabhamānasya ānantaryamārga āsravakṣaya ityucyate iti | kathamidam | (u) na hi tatrāsti viśiṣṭahetuḥ caturthadhyānamātrasyānantaryamārga āsravakṣayo nānyasyeti | ata[sta]nna yujyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) Certain <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say: 'For one who attains the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) is called the destruction of the outflows.' How is this? (Answer) There is no special reason that the uninterrupted path of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> alone is the destruction of the outflows and not of any other [stage]. Therefore that is not correct.

body.text: samādhibhāvanā ca trividhahitāya saṃvartate- (1) dṛṣṭadharmasukha[vihārā]ya, (2) jñānadarśana [pratilābhā]ya, (3) āsravakṣayāya ca | dvividhāya vā saṃvartate | uktavadekāntakṣayārthatvāt suviśuddhyarthatvāt, saṃsārakṣayārthatvāt, nānāsvabhāvavivekārthatvāt mārgamupadiśati cakṣuṣmān | tatra pūrve trayaḥ prahāṇasyābhidhānam, antimo jñānasya | nātra bhagavān dṛṣṭadharmasukha[vihāra]māha |
body.translated_text: The cultivation of concentration is conducive to three kinds of benefit: (1) for the happiness of dwelling in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukha[vihāra]</s>), (2) for the attainment of knowledge and vision, and (3) for the destruction of the outflows. Or it is conducive to two kinds [of benefit]. As stated — because it is exclusively for the purpose of destruction, for the purpose of thorough purification, for the purpose of the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and for the purpose of the discernment of the diverse own-natures — the one with eyes teaches the path. Therein, the first three are the designation of abandonment; the last is of knowledge. The Blessed One does not here speak of the happiness of dwelling in the present life.

body.text: catussamādhibhāvanāvargo 'ṣṭapañcāśaduttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and fifty-eighth chapter, the Chapter on the Four Cultivations of Concentration (<s>catussamādhibhāvanāvarga</s>).

body.text: 159 caturapramāṇasamādhivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 159. Chapter on the Four Immeasurable Concentrations (<s>caturapramāṇasamādhivarga</s>).

body.text: maitrī karuṇā muditā upekṣā | [tatra] maitrī nāma vyāpādaviruddhaṃ kuśalacittam | yathā suvijñaḥ suvijñāya sadā hitaṃ prārthayate | tathā yogāvacaro 'pi sarvasatvānāṃ kṛte sadā sukhaṃ prārthayate | ato 'yaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ suvijño bhavati | (pṛ) kiṃ nāma suvijñasya
body.translated_text: Loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). Therein, loving-kindness is a wholesome mind that is opposed to ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>). Just as a good friend always wishes benefit for a good friend, so too the practitioner always wishes happiness for the sake of all beings. Therefore he becomes a good friend of all beings. (Question) What is the characteristic of a good friend

body.text: lakṣaṇam | (u) nityaṃ lakṣyata aihikāmuṣmikahitasukhaprakarṣaprārthanāṃ kurvan naiva viruddhāsukhaprārthanām | tathā yogāvacaro 'pi sattvānāṃ sukhameva prārthayate nāsukham |
body.translated_text: (Answer) He is always seen to earnestly wish for the highest prosperity of benefit and happiness in this life and the next, and never to wish for what is opposed [to that], namely unhappiness. So too the practitioner wishes only happiness for beings, not unhappiness.

body.text: karuṇā vihiṃsāviruddhaṃ maitracittam | kasmāt | sattvānāṃ sukhaprārthanatvāt | (pṛ) dveṣavihiṃsayoḥ ko bhedaḥ | (u) citte dveṣasmṛtimutpādya satvān tāḍayituṃ vihisituṃ vā icchati | dveṣoddhitaṃ kāyavākkarma vihiṃsetyucyate | dveṣo vihiṃsāyā hetuḥ | dveṣākāṃkṣī avaśyaṃ pradāśamācarati |
body.translated_text: Compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) is a mind of loving-kindness that is opposed to harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>). Why? Because it wishes happiness for beings. (Question) What is the difference between hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) and harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>)? (Answer) Having generated the thought of hatred in the mind, one desires to strike or harm beings. Bodily and verbal action impelled by hatred is called 'harmfulness.' Hatred is the cause of harmfulness. One who harbors the desire for hatred necessarily commits cruelty.

body.text: muditā īrṣyāviruddhaṃ maitracittam | īrṣyā nāma parasyotkarṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā akṣamamāṇasyotpanno 'sūyāvyāpādaḥ | yogāvacarasya sarvasattvānāṃ lābhaprakarṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahatī prītirbhavati yathātmano hitalābhe |
body.translated_text: Sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) is a mind of loving-kindness opposed to envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>). Envy is the displeasure and ill-will born of jealousy that arises for one who cannot tolerate seeing the prosperity of another. For the practitioner, seeing the great gains of all beings, there arises great delight, just as at one's own beneficial gain.

body.text: (pṛ) kimimāni trīṇi maitrī[rūpāṇi]ā (u) maitracittasyaiva trayaḥ prakārāḥ | kasmāt | avyāpādo maitrī | na kaścidadviṣan duḥkhinaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā dayate | yadā sarveṣu sattveṣu paramaṃ maitracittaṃ kaścidduḥkhopadravasambhrāntaṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭveva samācaratitasmin samaye pravṛttaṃ maitracittaṃ karuṇetyucyate | atha vā kaścit parasya duḥkhe karuṇāmutpādayannapi na parasyotkarṣe pramuditacitto bhavati | kenedaṃ jñāyate | kaścitsapatnasya duḥkhaṃ dṛṣṭavaiva karuṇāyate | kiṃ punarlabdhavijayaṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā [na] pramodyata iti | yogāvacaraḥ sarvasattvān samṛddhilābhino dṛṣṭvā svābhedataḥ pramuditacitto bhavati | iyaṃ muditetyucyate | ato jñāyate maitrīcittaviśeṣaḥ karuṇā muditā ceti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Are these three [merely] forms of loving-kindness? (Answer) They are three modes of the mind of loving-kindness itself. Why? Non-hatred is loving-kindness. No one who is without hatred, upon seeing a suffering being, fails to feel compassion. When the supreme mind of loving-kindness toward all beings [is active], seeing a son distressed by the affliction of suffering — the mind of loving-kindness that operates at that time is called 'compassion.' Or, someone may generate compassion toward the suffering of another, yet not have a joyful mind at another's prosperity. How is this known? Someone may feel compassion upon merely seeing the suffering of a rival. But how much more would he not rejoice upon seeing his own son succeed in victory? The practitioner, seeing all beings gaining prosperity, has a joyful mind without distinction [between self and other]. This is called 'sympathetic joy.' From this it is known that compassion and sympathetic joy are modes of the mind of loving-kindness.

body.text: (pṛ) kasyopekṣayā upekṣā | (u) śatruṃ mitrañca paśyato maitracittaṃ na samamasti | mitre 'dhikam | udāsīne na tulyam | śatrau tu alpam | tathā karuṇā muditāpi | ato yogāvacaro mitre maitramupekṣya śatrau śātravamupekṣya cittasāmyaṃ cikīrṣati | paścāt sarvasattveṣu samacitto bhavati | tathā karuṇā muditāpi | ataḥ sūtra uktam- rāgapratighaprahāṇāyopekṣāṃ bhāvaya iti | (pṛ) tathā cet na pṛthagastyupekṣācittam | cittasāmyamātramupekṣāṃ bhavati | (u) pūrvamevoktaṃ mayā maitracittaviśeṣāḥ karuṇāmuditādaya iti | maitracittañcottamādhamamadhyadharmaistrividham | trayāṇāmeṣāṃ samabhāva upekṣā | yathā vadanti uttamamaitracittena trīṇi dhyānāni bhāvayatīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Of what is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) the equanimity? (Answer) For one who looks upon enemy and friend, the mind of loving-kindness is not equal — it is greater toward a friend, not equal toward an indifferent person, and slight toward an enemy. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy. Therefore the practitioner, setting aside friendliness toward friends and enmity toward enemies, wishes to make the mind equal. Afterward, he becomes equal-minded toward all beings. Likewise with compassion and sympathetic joy. Therefore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For the abandonment of passion and aversion, cultivate equanimity.' (Question) If so, the mind of equanimity would not be a separate [immeasurable]. It would be merely the equality of mind that constitutes equanimity. (Answer) I have already stated that compassion, sympathetic joy, and the rest are modes of the mind of loving-kindness. The mind of loving-kindness is threefold through superior, middling, and inferior <s>dharmas</s>. The equal state of these three is equanimity. As they say: 'Through the supreme mind of loving-kindness, one cultivates the three <s>dhyānas</s>.'

body.text: (pṛ) kenopāyena tanmaitracittaṃ pratilabhate | (u) uttaratna vakṣyante pratighasyādīnavāḥ | tānādīnavān prajñāya maitracittaṃ bhāvayati | maitracittasya hitaguṇañca paśyati | yathoktaṃ sūtre maitracetovihārī sukhaṃ svapiti | sukhaṃpratipadyate | na pāpakaṃ svapnaṃ paśyati | devatā rakṣanti | manuṣyāṇāṃ priyo bhavati | [amanuṣyāṇāṃ priyo bhavati |] nāsmai agnirvā viṣaṃ vā śastraṃ vā kramate | [uttaramapratividhyan brahmalokopago bhavati] iti | imānyāniśaṃsāni śrutvā bhāvayati | yogāvacaro 'nusmarati- ahaṃ vyāpādamutpādya ahameva vipākamanubhavāmi nānya iti | ato vyāpādamakṛtvā maitracittaṃ bhāvayati | kiñca yogāvacaro manasi karoti ahamalpakena pāpakena anyasya kṛtena bahūni pāpakāni tacchataguṇāni tadabhinnānyanubhavāmi | ataḥ pāpakāni parivarjayediti | uktañca sūtre- pañca dveṣaprahāṇakāraṇāni sadānusmartavyānīti | vyāpādaśca yogāvacarasya nālaṃ bhavati | aṣṭa kuśalāniṃśasāni pūrvamanusmaret | pāpakāni varjayato vyāpādaḥ śāmyati | puruṣasya pūrvādhvani mātā vā syāt, garbhiṇī prasavitrī ca madarthaḥ duḥkhaṃ vyavasyamānā syāt | atha vā syāt mama pitā bhrātā bhāryā putro vā | kathaṃ dveṣṭavyam | iti | anusmareccāgāminyadhvani mama pitā mātā bhrātā vā bhavet iti | arhan pratyekabuddho buddho vā bhavediti [anusmaraṇaṃ] kuryāt | kathaṃ dveṣṭavyam | durjanān dṛṣṭvā pāpakamācaran ubhayoradhvanorduḥkhaṃ vedayate | ato na dveṣṭavyam | pūrvañca nibhṛtaṃ paśyet janasya svabhāvaḥ kuśalo 'kuśala iti | yadi durjano mama [akuśala]mādadhāti, kasmādahaṃ dviṣāmi | yathāgninā dagdho nā[gniṃ]dviṣet | kleśopahataḥ piśācapīḍita iva na svātantryabhāgbhavati | iti pūrvaṃ paśyan kimarthaṃ dviṣati | yena pratyayena kṣāntiṃ bhāvayati | taṃ dharmamanusmaret | tadā vyāpādaḥ śāmyati, maitracittañca vardhate | kṣāntiguṇo yogāvacaro 'nuvicintayati- ahaṃ yadi paraṃ dviṣāmi | tadā pṛthagjanasya grāmīṇasya tasya [mama] ca nāsti bhedaḥ | ataḥ kṣantavyamiti | yathāha bhagavān gāthām-
body.translated_text: (Question) By what method does one obtain that mind of loving-kindness? (Answer) Later the dangers of aversion will be stated. Having recognized those dangers through wisdom, one cultivates the mind of loving-kindness. And one sees the beneficial qualities of the mind of loving-kindness. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who dwells in the abode of loving-kindness sleeps happily, awakens happily, does not see bad dreams, deities protect him, he becomes dear to humans, [he becomes dear to non-humans,] neither fire, nor poison, nor weapons prevail against him, [without further effort he is reborn in the <s>Brahma</s>-world].' Having heard these benefits, one cultivates [loving-kindness]. The practitioner reflects: 'If I generate ill-will, I myself experience the ripening — not another.' Therefore, not generating ill-will, he cultivates the mind of loving-kindness. Furthermore, the practitioner considers: 'Through even a small evil done by another, I experience that evil a hundredfold, identical [in nature].' Therefore one should avoid evil deeds. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Five causes for the abandonment of hatred should always be recollected.' And hatred is not fitting for the practitioner. He should first recollect the eight wholesome advantages. By avoiding evil, hatred subsides. One should reflect: 'In a previous life, this person may have been my mother, or she who bore me in the womb and endured suffering for my sake. Or he may have been my father, brother, wife, or son. How can one hate [such a being]?' One should also recollect: 'In the future, he may become my father, mother, or brother.' One should reflect: 'He may become an <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, or a <s>Buddha</s>. How can one hate [him]?' Seeing wicked persons committing evil deeds, one reflects: 'They experience suffering in both lives.' Therefore one should not hate. One should first look calmly at the nature of a person — whether wholesome or unwholesome. If a wicked person inflicts unwholesomeness upon me, why should I hate? Just as one burned by fire does not hate the fire. One struck by defilements, like one afflicted by a spirit, has no autonomy. Seeing thus, why does one hate? Through the condition by which one cultivates patience, one should recollect that <s>dharma</s>. Then hatred subsides and the mind of loving-kindness grows. The practitioner reflects on the virtue of patience: 'If I hate another, then there is no difference between me and the common, ordinary person.' Therefore one should be patient. As the Blessed One spoke this verse:

body.text:
suvinīto yathā hastī sahate śaramastrakam
tathā cāhamapīhaiva titikṣe sarvapāpakam || iti |
body.translated_text: 'Just as a well-trained elephant endures arrows and weapons, so too shall I endure all evil here.'

body.text: api cāha gāthām-
body.translated_text: And he spoke this verse:

children.translated_text: 'Abuse, slander, reproach, and enmity —

children.text: na kṣametādhamaḥ sattvaḥ śilavṛṣṭiṃ yathā khagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: an inferior being cannot endure these, just as a bird cannot endure a hailstorm.'

body.text:
aślīlamapavādañca vigarhīṃ pratighaṃ tathā |
kṣameta hi māhasattvaḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ yathā gajaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: 'Abuse, slander, reproach, and enmity — a great being endures these, just as an elephant endures a shower of flowers.'

body.text: ataḥ kṣantavyam | tadakuśalaṃ guṇaḥ pariṇamate | akuśalebhyo guṇasaṃsiddheḥ | yogāvacara ime sattvā mūḍhā avijñā bālasamānā na vidveṣyā iti prajānāti | ityanenopāyena maitracittaṃ bhāvayati |
body.translated_text: Therefore one should be patient. That unwholesome [treatment] is transformed into virtue — because virtue is accomplished from [enduring] the unwholesome. The practitioner understands: 'These beings are deluded, ignorant, like children — they are not to be hated.' By such means one cultivates the mind of loving-kindness.

body.text: (pṛ) kathaṃ karuṇāṃ bhāvayati | (u) yogāvacaro 'lpasukhino duḥkhabahulān dṛṣṭvā karuṇāyate | kathamahaṃ duḥkhini sattve punarduḥkhamāadhyām iti | atyantasukhāsaktān dṛṣṭvā ca cintayati- kathamahaṃ parapraṇihitaṃ hāpayeyamiti | ataḥ karuṇāyate | duḥkhinaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭadharme duḥkhitvāt duḥkhī bhavati | sukhinaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā anitya[sukha]tvāt duḥkhī bhavati | ataḥ sarve sattvā duḥkhabhāgina ādāvante vā na vimuktilābhina ityanena pratyayena karuṇāyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) How does one cultivate compassion? (Answer) The practitioner, seeing that beings have little happiness and much suffering, feels compassion. [He reflects:] 'How could I inflict further suffering on a being already suffering?' And seeing those excessively attached to happiness, he reflects: 'How could I destroy what another has wished for?' Therefore he feels compassion. Seeing a suffering being, he becomes sorrowful because of the suffering in the present life. Seeing a happy being, he becomes sorrowful because of the impermanence of happiness. Therefore all beings are partakers of suffering — neither at the beginning nor at the end do they obtain liberation. Through this condition, he feels compassion.

body.text: (pṛ) kathaṃ muditāṃ bhāvayati | (u) yogāvacaraḥ parahiterṣyālutā pṛthagjanalakṣaṇamiti dṛṣṭvā muditāṃ bhāvayati | cintayati caivam- sattvānāṃ sukhamutpādayeyamiti | [yadi] paraḥ svayaṃ labhate | tadā sa māṃ satkaroti | ato muditāmutpādayet | taderṣyādṛṣṭirvṛthā nāsti kimapi hitam | na paramupahanti | pratyutātmānameva hiṃsati | yathoktañca sūtre- īrṣyā saṃyojanā iti | tatsaṃyojanaparijihīrṣayā muditāmutpādayati |
body.translated_text: (Question) How does one cultivate sympathetic joy? (Answer) The practitioner, seeing that envy toward the prosperity of others is the characteristic of an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), cultivates sympathetic joy. He reflects thus: 'I should generate happiness for beings.' If another obtains it by himself, then he honors me. Therefore one should generate sympathetic joy. That envious view is in vain — there is nothing beneficial in it. It does not harm another; rather, it harms oneself alone. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Envy is a fetter (<s>saṃyojana</s>).' Wishing to abandon that fetter, one generates sympathetic joy.

body.text: (pṛ) kathamupekṣāṃ carati | (u) viṣamacitte doṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā cittasāmyacikīrṣayā upekṣāṃ carati | yogāvacaro rāgapratighacitte doṣadarśanādupekṣācaryāṃ bhāvayati |
body.translated_text: (Question) How does one practice equanimity? (Answer) Seeing the fault in an uneven mind, one practices equanimity with the wish to make the mind equal. The practitioner, seeing the fault in the mind of passion and aversion, cultivates the practice of equanimity.

body.text: (pṛ) idamapramāṇacittaṃ kasyāṃ bhūmau vartate | (u) triṣu dhātuṣu vartate | (pṛ) ābhidharmikāḥ kecidāhuḥ- tṛtīyadhyānādūrdhvaṃ nāsti saumanasyendriyam iti | kathamidam |
body.translated_text: (Question) In which plane (<s>bhūmi</s>) does this immeasurable mind operate? (Answer) It operates in the three realms. (Question) Certain <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say: 'Above the third <s>dhyāna</s>, the faculty of mental happiness (<s>saumanasyendriya</s>) does not exist.' How is this?

body.text: (u) nāhaṃ vadāmi muditacittaṃ saumanasyendriyasvabhāvamiti | kintu parahite 'kaluṣamuditacittatā muditetyucyate | catvārīmānyapramāṇāni prajñāsvabhāvāni |
body.translated_text: (Answer) I do not say that the mind of sympathetic joy has the nature of the faculty of mental happiness. Rather, an unpolluted joyful mind toward the prosperity of others is called 'sympathetic joy.' These four immeasurables have the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) kathamārūpyadhātau catvāryapramāṇāni bhavanti | rūpalakṣaṇena hi sattvo vikalpyate | tatra rūpaṇe rūpalakṣaṇaṃ kathaṃ bhavet | (u) arūpasattvā api vikalpanīyāḥ | yathoktaṃsūtre- sarūpārūpyādiṣu kuryāditi | kiñcoktaṃsūtre- śubhavipākapratilābhaparamāṃ maitracetovimuktiṃ bhāvayati | ākāśānantyāyatanapratilābhaparamāṃ karuṇā[cetovimuktiṃ] bhāvayati | vijñānānantyāyatanapratilābhaparamāṃ muditā[cetovimuktiṃ]bhāvayati | ākiñcanyāyatanapratilābhaparamāmupekṣā[cetovimuktiṃ]bhāvayati | iti | ato jñāyate ārūpye 'pi santyapramāṇānīti | (pṛ) ekaikasyāṃ bhūmāvekamapramāṇamasti | kiṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatane kimapi nāsti | (u) sarveṣvapyāyataneṣu sarvāṇi santi | atyadhimaitrībhāvanayā paraṃ śubhāyatanamutpadyate | karmaṇāṃ sarūpavipākajanakatvāt | yaḥ sattvānāṃ sukhākāṃkṣī sa sukhavipākaṃ labhate | tathā karuṇāpi | kāyādhīnatayā bhūyasā duḥkhānāṃ samudayaḥ | ākāśe ca rūpaṃ nāstītyato vijñānānantyāyatanacittasyālambane paramasukhavihāritvāt | ākiñcanyāyatanaparamā upekṣeti | yogāvacaraḥ saṃjñāpariklāntatvādākiñcanyāyatanamupasampadya viharati | naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatane 'pi apramāṇamasti | atisūkṣmātvānnopalabhyata iti nocyate | sarveṣvapyāyataneṣu sarvamasti iti bāhulyavaśāt ucyate | śubhe maitryāṃḥ paramādhikyāt ityevamādi | dhyānasamādhiṣu catvāryapramāṇacittāni vipākavedanāpradhānāni sattvālambanatvāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) How can the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) exist in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm)? For a being is distinguished by the characteristic of form. How can the characteristic of form exist where there is no form? (Answer) Formless beings too must be distinguished. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One should practice toward those with form, in the formless realm, and so on.' Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One cultivates the <s>maitrī-cetovimukti</s> (liberation of mind through loving-kindness) directed toward attaining excellent <s>vipāka</s> (karmic fruition). One cultivates the <s>karuṇā-cetovimukti</s> (liberation of mind through compassion) directed toward attaining the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (base of infinite space). One cultivates the <s>muditā-cetovimukti</s> (liberation of mind through sympathetic joy) directed toward attaining the <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s> (base of infinite consciousness). One cultivates the <s>upekṣā-cetovimukti</s> (liberation of mind through equanimity) directed toward attaining the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s> (base of nothingness).' From this it is known that the <s>apramāṇas</s> exist even in the formless realm. (Question) In each plane there is one <s>apramāṇa</s>. Is there nothing at all in the <s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s> (base of neither perception nor non-perception)? (Answer) In all bases, all of them exist. Through the supreme cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), the excellent realm of pleasant rebirth arises, because <s>karmas</s> produce results corresponding to their nature. One who wishes happiness for beings obtains a happy <s>vipāka</s>. Likewise with <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) — since suffering predominantly arises due to dependence on the body, and since there is no form in space, the mind of the <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s> dwells in supreme happiness with regard to its object. <s>Upekṣā</s> (equanimity) has its highest expression in the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>. The <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner), being wearied by perception, attains and dwells in the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>. Even in the <s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>, the <s>apramāṇa</s> exists, but because it is extremely subtle, it is not apprehended, and therefore it is not spoken of. It is said that all exist in all bases, speaking in terms of predominance — as with loving-kindness being supreme in the pleasant realm, and so forth. In the <s>dhyāna</s>-concentrations, the four <s>apramāṇa</s>-minds have <s>vipākavedanā</s> (resultant feeling) as predominant, because they take beings as their object.

body.text: (pṛ) ābhidharmikā āhuḥ- catvāryapramāṇāni kāmadhātukasattvamātrālambanā nīti | tatkatham | (u) kasmānnānyasattvālambanāni tāni | vaktavyo 'tra hetuḥ | bhagavānapramāṇasūtra āha- iha bhikṣurmaitrasahagatena cetasā ekāṃ diśaṃ[sphuritvā viharati | tathā] dvitīyāṃ tathā tṛtīyāṃ caturthī ityūrdhvamadhastiryak[sarvadā sarvatratāyai] sarvāvantaṃ lokaṃ [maitrasahagatena cetasā] sphuritvā viharati iti | rūpārūpyakadhātukasattvā anityā bhaṅgurā durgati gāmina ityasti hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say that the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) take only beings of the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) as their object. How is this? (Answer) Why should they not take other beings as their object? A reason must be stated here. The Blessed One said in the <s>Apramāṇa-sūtra</s>: 'Here a monk, having pervaded one direction with a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), dwells thus. Likewise the second, likewise the third, the fourth, above, below, and across — everywhere, in every way, he pervades the entire world with a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> and dwells thus.' Beings of the <s>rūpa</s> and <s>ārūpya</s> realms are impermanent, perishable, and headed toward lower destinies — this is the reason.

body.text: (pṛ) ābhidharmikā āhuḥ- kāmadhātugato yogāvacara evāpramāṇānyupasampadya viharatīti | kathamidam | (u) sarvāyatanajātāḥ sarva upasampadya viharanti | (pṛ) yadi tanna jātā api upasampadya viharanti | tadā na puṇyaṃ kṣīyeta | tatra nityamutpadyeran | (u) yathā tatra dhyānādīn kuśaladharmānusampadya viharanto 'pi[tato]nivartante | tathā maitrādīnapi (pṛ) yadyayaṃ nyāyaḥ | kasmānna kṣipraṃ nivartante | (u) astīdṛśaṃ karma satyapi nivṛttihetau na nivartante | yathā kāma[dhātuka]devādayaḥ satyapi kuśalakarmaṇi durgatāvupapadyante | tathedamapi ||
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say that only a <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner) born in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) attains and dwells in the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables). How is this? (Answer) Those born in all bases, all of them attain and dwell in them. (Question) If even those not born there attain and dwell in them, then merit would not be exhausted, and they would always be reborn there. (Answer) Just as those dwelling there, having attained <s>dhyānas</s> and other wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, do not thereby always remain there, so too those born elsewhere who attain the <s>apramāṇas</s> are not necessarily reborn there. The practice of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and other immeasurables is not a cause for rebirth in a particular realm, but rather produces its own specific <s>vipāka</s> (karmic result).

body.text: (pṛ) maitrasamādhivihāriṇaṃ kasmānna viṣaṃśastramagnirvā kramate | (u) kuśalapuṇyaghanagabhīramakuśalāni nādhitiṣṭhanti devaiḥ surakṣitatvāt | (pṛ) sūtramāha- maitrasahagataṃ smṛtisambodhyaṅgaṃ bhāvayati iti | sāsravānāsravayoḥ kathaṃ sahabhāvanā | (u) maitrī[smṛti]sambodhyaṅgenānugatā bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yadi kaścidekāgracittena dharmaṃ śṛṇoti | tadā pañcanīvaraṇāni prahāya saptasambodhyaṅgāni bhāvayati | dharmāśravaṇe 'pi sambodhyaṅgāni bhāvayati | iti | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- bhāvayatha bhikṣavo maitracittam, pratijānāmi anāgāmiphalaṃ prāpsyatheti | maitracittaṃ yadyapi na saṃyojanaṃ hāpayati | [tathāpi]pūrvameva maitracittena puṇyaguṇajñānahitasañcayādāryamārgaprajñāṃ labdhvā saṃyojanāni prajahāti | ata ucyate maitrī bhāvanayā anāgāmiphalaṃ labhata iti | maitrī bhāvanayā sambodhyaṅgamapyevam |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why do poison, weapons, and fire not overpower one who dwells in the <s>maitrī-samādhi</s> (concentration of loving-kindness)? (Answer) Because of the dense and profound mass of wholesome merit, unwholesome factors cannot prevail, and because one is well-protected by the <s>devas</s> (gods). (Question) The <s>sūtra</s> says: 'One cultivates the <s>smṛti-sambodhyaṅga</s> (mindfulness factor of awakening) accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).' How can there be combined cultivation of the defiled and the undefiled? (Answer) <s>Maitrī</s> is accompanied by the <s>smṛti-sambodhyaṅga</s>. That is, when <s>maitrī</s> is cultivated, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) follows it, and mindfulness is not a separate object of cultivation.

body.text: (pṛ) arhan prahīṇasattvasaṃjñaḥ | kathamapramāṇāni bhāvayati | (u) arhan maitracittamupasampadya viharannapi namaitrakarmasiddhiṃ sañcinoti | upapattivedanābhāvāt | (pṛ) buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākaruṇā katham | (u) buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ naiva mīmāṃsājñānamasti | dharmāṇāmatyantaśūnyatāṃ prajānanto 'pi pṛthagjaneṣu gabhīraṃ mahākaruṇāmācaranti |
body.translated_text: (Question) An <s>arhat</s> has abandoned the perception of beings. How does he cultivate the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables)? (Answer) An <s>arhat</s>, even while attaining and dwelling in the mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), does not accumulate the accomplishment of <s>maitrī-karma</s>, because there is no <s>upapattivedanā</s> (rebirth-feeling). (Question) How is the <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones? (Answer) The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, do not possess speculative knowledge. Even while fully knowing the absolute emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>,

body.text: (pṛ) karuṇāyā mahākaruṇāyāśca ko bhedaḥ | (u) kṛpācittamātraṃ karuṇā | kriyāṃ sādhayatīti mahākaruṇā | kasmāt | bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ duḥkhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatkṣayāya vīryamārabhate | apramāṇakalpeṣu bhāvanāsādhyatvānmahākaruṇetyucyate | ājñendriyeṇa sattvānāṃ
body.translated_text: (Question) What is the difference between <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) and <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion)? (Answer) Mere compassionate mind is <s>karuṇā</s>. That which accomplishes action is <s>mahākaruṇā</s>. Why? Because the <s>bodhisattva</s>, seeing the suffering of beings, exerts effort toward its cessation. Because it is accomplished through cultivation over immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), it is called <s>mahākaruṇā</s>. Through the <s>ājñendriya</s> (faculty of final knowledge), seeing the

body.text: duḥkhaṃ dṛṣṭvā [tat] apaneṣyāmīti niyamena cittoddhāpanaṃ mahākaruṇā | upakārabahuleti mahākaruṇā | apratihateti mahākaruṇā | kutaḥ | karuṇācittaṃ hi parasya pāpakaṃ smṛtvā pratighātamutpādayet | mahākaruṇā tu nānāvidhaparamapāpakeṣvapi apratihatagatirbhavati | karuṇācittaṃ kadācit ghanaṃ, kadācit tanīyaḥ, na samaṃ bhavati | sarvatra sameti mahākaruṇā | ātmano hitaṃ tyaktvā parasya hitamātramākāṃkṣata iti mahākaruṇā | karuṇā tu naivamityayaṃ bhedaḥ | buddhe maitryādi mahadityucyate | karuṇā tu [kadācit] duḥkhākāṃkṣiṇīti kevaletyucyate ||
body.translated_text: suffering of beings, the firm resolve of mind 'I will remove that suffering' is <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion). Because it is abundant in benefit, it is <s>mahākaruṇā</s>. Because it is unobstructed, it is <s>mahākaruṇā</s>. Why? For the mind of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), recollecting another's evil, might produce obstruction. But <s>mahākaruṇā</s>, even toward those of various and extreme evil, proceeds without obstruction. The mind of <s>karuṇā</s> is sometimes intense and sometimes

body.text: caturapramāṇasamādhivarga ekonaṣaṣṭuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter one hundred and fifty-nine: the chapter on the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables).

body.text: 160 pañcāṅgāryasamādhivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 160. Chapter on the five-limbed noble <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).

body.text: uktaṃ hi sūtre- pañcāṅga[bhūtā] āryasamādhayaḥ yaduta prītiḥ sukhaṃ cittaviśuddhiḥ prakāśalakṣaṇaṃ bhāvanālakṣaṇamiti | prītiḥ prathamadvitīyadhyānayoḥ | prītilakṣaṇaṃ samamiti ekāṅgamucyate | tṛtīyadhyāne prītivirahāt sukhaṃ pṛthagekamaṅgamucyate | caturthadhyāne cittaviśuddhistṛtīyamaṅgamucyate | imāni trīṇyaṅgānyāśrityotpadyate prakāśabhāvanālakṣaṇam | prakāśalakṣaṇaṃ bhāvanālakṣaṇasya hetuṃ kṛtvā pañcaskandhān paribhedayati | pañcaskandhānāṃ śūnyatābhāvanaṃ bhāvanālakṣaṇamityucyate | nirvāṇagāmitvādāryam |
body.translated_text: For it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The noble <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) have five limbs, namely: <s>prīti</s> (joy), <s>sukha</s> (happiness), <s>cittaviśuddhi</s> (purity of mind), <s>prakāśalakṣaṇa</s> (the characteristic of luminosity), and <s>bhāvanālakṣaṇa</s> (the characteristic of cultivation).' <s>Prīti</s> (joy) belongs to the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>. Since the characteristic of <s>prīti</s> is the same in both, it is called one limb. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, due to the absence of <s>prīti</s>, <s>sukha</s> (happiness) is separately counted as one limb. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>cittaviśuddhi</s> (purity of mind) is the third limb.

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- pañca āryasamādhijñānāni | katamāni imāni | (u) bhagavān svayamāha- yogī cintayati mamāyaṃ samādhirāryo nirāmiṣa iti prathamajñānamutpadyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are five knowledges of the noble <s>samādhi</s>. What are they?' (Answer) The Blessed One himself said: 'The <s>yogī</s> (practitioner) reflects: "This <s>samādhi</s> of mine is noble, free from sensory pleasure" — thus the first knowledge arises.'

body.text: samādhirayamakāpuruṣasevita iti dvitīyajñānamutpadyate | samādhirayaṃ śāntaḥ praṇītaḥ prītipraśrabdhilabdha iti tṛtīyajñānamutpadyate | ayaṃ samādhiḥ pratyutpannasukha āyatyāñca sukhavipāka iti caturthajñānamutpadyate | sa khalu punarahamimaṃ samādhiṃ smṛta eva samāpadye smṛta eva vyuttiṣṭhāmīti pañcamaṃ jñānamutpadyate | iti | anena samādhāvapi jñānamastīti bhagavān prakāśayati | cittadhāraṇā paraṃ nāsti | samādhiṃ bhāvayato yadi kleśā bhavanti | [tadā tān] tatrotpannaṃ jñānamapanayati | samādhiṃ kṛtvā āryaṃ nirāmiṣaṃ chandayāmītīdaṃ prathamajñānamucyate | āryo nirāmiṣo yadutākāpuruṣasevita ityayaṃ paṇḍitapragītaḥ | akāpuruṣā yadāryajanāḥ | jñānalābhitvātkāpuruṣā na bhavanti | [yat] jñānaṃ prajñaptiṃ bhinatti | idaṃ dvitīyajñānamityucyate | rāgādikleśānāmalpīyasāṃ nirodhāt śāntam | śāntatvāt praṇītam | kleśādīnāṃ visaṃyogāllabdhaṃ visaṃyogalabdhamityucyate | ayaṃ vītarāgamārgaḥ- idaṃ tṛtīyajñānaṃ bhavati | kleśaprahāṇasākṣātkārāt kṣemaṃ śāntaṃ labhate | tāpavinirmuktaṃ sukhaṃ pratyutpannasukhamāyatīsukham, pratyutpannaṃ sukhaṃ kleśavinirmuktaṃ sukham | āyatyāṃ sukhaṃ yannirvāṇasukham | idaṃ caturthajñānaṃ bhavati | yogī nityamanimittacitto viharati | ato nityaṃ smṛto vyuttiṣṭhati smṛtaḥ samādhimusampadyate | idaṃ pañcamaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati | tasmādyadi pañcamajñānamidaṃ notpannaṃ, utpādayitavyam | yadyutpannaṃ samādhiphalaṃ labdhameva ||
body.translated_text: 'This <s>samādhi</s> is not practiced by base persons' — thus the second knowledge arises. 'This <s>samādhi</s> is peaceful, sublime, attained through the calming of <s>prīti</s> (joy)' — thus the third knowledge arises. 'This <s>samādhi</s> is happy in the present and yields happy <s>vipāka</s> (fruition) in the future' — thus the fourth knowledge arises. 'Moreover, I enter this <s>samādhi</s> mindfully and emerge from it mindfully' — thus the

body.text: pañcāṅgāryasamādhivargaḥ ṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter one hundred and sixty: the chapter on the five-limbed noble <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).

body.text: 161 ṣaṭsamādhivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 161. Chapter on the six <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations).

body.text: (pṛ) uktaṃ sūtre- samādhayaḥ ṣaṭ aṣṭyekalakṣaṇabhāvanā ekalakṣaṇatvāya saṃvartate | astyekalakṣaṇabhāvanā nānālakṣaṇatvāya saṃvartate | astyekalakṣaṇabhāvanā ekalakṣaṇanānālakṣaṇatvāya saṃvartate | evaṃ nānālakṣaṇabhāvanāpi | katamānīmāni | (u) ekalakṣaṇamitīdaṃ dhyānasamādhiḥ syāt | dhyānasamādherekālambana ekāgratāviharaṇāt | nānālakṣaṇamitīdaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ bhavet | dharmāṇāṃ nānāsvabhāvasya [pari]jñānāt | pañcaskandhādidharmāṇāmupāyatvāt | (pṛ) kathamekalakṣaṇā bhāvanā ekalakṣaṇatvāya saṃvartata iti | (u) yat kaścit samādhimupādāya punaḥ samādhimutpādayati | ekalakṣaṇā nānālakṣatvāya saṃvartata iti
body.translated_text: (Question) It is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are six <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). There is cultivation of a single characteristic that leads to a single characteristic. There is cultivation of a single characteristic that leads to multiple characteristics. There is cultivation of a single characteristic that leads to both single and multiple characteristics. Likewise with the cultivation of multiple characteristics.' What are these? (Answer) 'Single characteristic' refers to <s>dhyāna-samādhi</s> (meditative concentration). The single characteristic of <s>dhyāna-samādhi</s>

body.text: yadi kaścit samādhimupādāya jñānadarśanamutpādayati | ekalakṣaṇā bhāvanā ekalakṣaṇanānālakṣaṇatvāya saṃvartata iti yadi kaścit samādhimupādāya dhyānasamādhiṃ pañcaskandhopāya ñcotpādayati | evaṃ nānālakṣaṇabhāvanāpi |
body.translated_text: If someone, based on <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), gives rise to knowledge and vision — the cultivation of a single characteristic leads to both single and multiple characteristics. If someone, based on <s>samādhi</s>, gives rise to <s>dhyāna-samādhi</s> and produces the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — likewise with the cultivation of multiple characteristics.

body.text:
(pṛ) kecidārmidharmikā āhuḥ- ekalakṣaṇā bhāvanā ekalakṣaṇatvāya saṃvartata iti yadi kaścit caturthadhyānamupādāya arhatphalaṃ sākṣātkaroti tat | ekalakṣaṇā bhāvanā nānālakṣaṇāya saṃvartata iti yat kaścit caturthadhyānamupādāya pañcābhijñāḥ sākṣātkaroti tat | ekalakṣaṇā bhāvanā ekalakṣaṇanānālakṣaṇāya saṃvartata iti yat kaścit caturthaṃ dhyānamupādāyārhatphalaṃ pañcābhijñāśca sākṣātkaroti tat | nānālakṣaṇā bhāvanā nānālakṣaṇāya saṃvartata iti yat kaścit pañcāṅgabhūtasamādhīnupādāyārhatphalaṃ pañcābhijñāśca sākṣātkaroti | tathā anyau dvāvapi | kathamidam | (u) [atra] heturvaktavyaḥ | kasmāt caturthadhyānamarhatphalañcaikalakṣaṇam | pañcāṅga[bhūta]samādhiḥ pañcābhijñāśca nānālakṣaṇā iti | pañcāṅgāni nāśrīyante | pañcāṅgasamādhiścaturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ prakāśalakṣaṇo bhāvanālakṣaṇaḥ | kathaṃ tānyāśritya arhatphalaṃ labhate | kasmāt | avaśyaṃ dhyānamekamāśritya arhatphalaṃ labhate | kiñca prakāśalakṣaṇamāśrityāpi arhatphalaṃ labheta | tasmānnāsti [hetuḥ] |
kecidāhuḥ- ṣaḍvidhāḥ samādhisamāpattayaḥ ānulomikasamāpattiḥ, prātilomikasamāpattiḥ ānulomikaprātilomikasamāpattiḥ ānulomikavyutkrāntiḥ prātilomikavyutkrāntiḥ ānulomikaprātilomikavyutkrāntiriti | kathamidam | (u) kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ yogī nirodhasamāpattāvatāramicchatītyato dhyāneṣu samāpatti (= praveśa) vyutthāne kramike | tasmānna syāt yadi vānulomyena yadi vā prātilomyena yadi vānulomyaprātilomyena vyutkramādiḥ | pañcasamāpattivyutthānaiḥ kiṃ hitaṃ labhate | yogī nirodhasamāpattiṃ prāpayituravaśyaṃ kramaśo 'vataret kramaśaśca vyuttiṣṭhet | yadyuttamabhūmibhāk kasmātpunaradho bhūmimavatarati | adhobhūmiḥ kaṇṭakabhūtā | yathā na kaścitpunarbālakrīḍāyāmabhiramate | yathā ca vidagdho jano na punarabhiramate mūḍhe | tathedamapi syāt |
body.translated_text:
(Question) Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> (Abhidharma scholars) say: Cultivation of a single characteristic leads to a single characteristic — this is when someone, relying on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), directly realizes the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>. Cultivation of a single characteristic leads to multiple characteristics — this is when someone, relying on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, directly realizes the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). Cultivation of a single characteristic leads to both single and multiple characteristics — this is when someone, relying on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, directly realizes both the fruit of <s>Arhat</s> and the five <s>abhijñās</s>. Cultivation of multiple characteristics leads to multiple characteristics — this is when someone, relying on the five-limbed <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), directly realizes both the fruit of <s>Arhat</s> and the five <s>abhijñās</s>. Likewise for the other two as well. How is this? (Answer) Here a reason must be stated. Why are the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and the fruit of <s>Arhat</s> of a single characteristic, while the five-limbed <s>samādhi</s> and the five <s>abhijñās</s> are of multiple characteristics? The five limbs are not relied upon. The five-limbed <s>samādhi</s> has the characteristic of illumination among the four <s>dhyānas</s>, being a characteristic of cultivation. How can one obtain the fruit of <s>Arhat</s> by relying on them? Because one necessarily obtains the fruit of <s>Arhat</s> by relying on a single <s>dhyāna</s>. Moreover, one could also obtain the fruit of <s>Arhat</s> by relying on the characteristic of illumination. Therefore there is no [valid reason].
Some say: There are six kinds of <s>samādhi</s> attainments — progressive attainment, reverse attainment, progressive-and-reverse attainment, progressive transcendence, reverse transcendence, and progressive-and-reverse transcendence. How is this? (Answer) Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: Because a <s>yogī</s> (practitioner) wishes to enter the attainment of cessation, the attainment (i.e., entry) and emergence from the <s>dhyānas</s> must be sequential. Therefore, whether progressively, or reversely, or progressively-and-reversely, there should be no transcendence and so forth. What benefit is obtained by emerging from the five attainments? A <s>yogī</s> must necessarily descend sequentially and emerge sequentially in order to reach the attainment of cessation. If one abides in the highest stage, why would one descend again to a lower stage? The lower stage is like a thorn. Just as no one delights again in childish play, and just as a refined person does not delight again in foolishness, so it would be in this case as well.

body.text: yaduktaṃ vyutkrāmatīti | idamayuktam | sūtre kevalamuktaṃ kramikā dhyānasamādhīnāṃ
body.translated_text: What was said about 'transcending' — this is unreasonable. In the <s>sūtra</s> it is merely stated that the attainments of the <s>dhyānas</s> and <s>samādhis</s> are sequential

body.text: samāpattaya iti | yadi yogī vyutkrāmati ātṛtīyam | kasmānna vyutkrāmati ācaturthapañcamam | balānubhāvasadṛśamidamiti yadi matam | yathā kaścit śreṇimāruhya ekaṃ sopānaṃ vyutkramet na dvau | dṛṣṭānto 'yamapi naikāntikaḥ | mahābaliṣṭhaḥ kaścit catvāri sopānānyapi vyutkramet | śataṃ pakramān prakramamāṇo 'pi kaścidasti | ato na yujyate | sūtre yadyapyuktaṃ bhagavatā nirvāṇaṃ samāpadyamāno 'nulomapratilomaṃ vyutkramya dhyānasamādhīn samāpadyata iti | sūtramidaṃ samyagarthaviruddham | na średdheyam | satyapi vacane 'smin nāyamartho yuktaḥ | kasmāt | yadi yogino nirodhasamāpattāvatāraṃ vadati tadānulomyena samāpattiḥ syāt naikakṣaṇe pañcadhā | yogī yadi sākṣānnirodhasamāpattyavatāramicchati tadā naikakṣaṇe syāt | yadi dhyānasamādhiṣu svacittaṃ bubhukṣati, vaśitvāparihāṇitvāt anulomapratilomaṃ vyuttiṣṭhati samāpadyate vyutkrāmati ca | yathā kaścidaśvamārūḍho yadi pratibalaruddhaḥ, tadā nāvaśyaṃ pratinivartate | yadi damanaṃ niṣevitumicchati | tadā rahasi [karoti] |
body.translated_text: attainments. If a <s>yogī</s> transcends, it is up to the third. Why does one not transcend up to the fourth or fifth? If one thinks this is according to the measure of one's power — just as someone climbing a staircase might skip one step but not two — this analogy is also not conclusive. Someone of great strength could skip even four steps. There are even those who take a hundred strides while striding forth. Therefore this is not tenable. Although it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> that the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), while entering <s>Nirvāṇa</s> (final cessation), entered the <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> attainments by transcending them progressively and reversely — this <s>sūtra</s> contradicts the correct meaning and should not be believed. Even if such a statement exists, this meaning is not tenable. Why? If it speaks of the <s>yogī</s>'s entry into the attainment of cessation, then the attainment should be progressive, not fivefold in a single moment. If the <s>yogī</s> directly wishes to enter the attainment of cessation, then it should not be fivefold in a single moment. If the <s>yogī</s> desires to enjoy his own mind in the <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> states, then because of mastery and non-decline, he emerges and enters progressively and reversely, and transcends. Just as someone mounted on a horse, if blocked by an opposing force, does not necessarily turn back; but if he wishes to practice training, then he does so in private.

body.text: yaduktam- adhobhūmiḥ kaṇṭaka[bhūtā] | na [tatra] samāpadyeteti | adhobhūmera jayāt punaḥ samāpadyate | yogigocaramārgatvāt | yaduktaṃ yathā na kaścit bālakrīḍāyāmabhiramata iti | [tatra] nidānaṃ kadācidbālakrīḍātmakaṃ bhavati | yathā kaścidvṛddho naṭaḥ sarvadā nṛtyati na tṛpto bhavati | śikṣaṇārthatvāt | evamāryaḥ anulomapratilomaṃ dhyāneṣu vyuttiṣṭhati samāpadyate vyutkrāmati ca devamanuṣyāṇāṃ pradarśanakāmitvāt maharṣīṇāṃ samādhiṣu vaśitābalācca | bhagavān parinirvāṇagamanakāle paramapraṇītadhyānasamādhibhirvāsitaśarīratvāt svatantraṃ samāpadyata vyudatiṣṭhat anulomaṃ pratilomaṃ vyudakrāmīt | anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇagataṃ bhagavantaṃ paśyan sarvebhyo 'kuśalasaṃskārebhyo nirvidyeta | ato bhagavānasmin dharme 'dbhutaṃ premāviścakāra |
body.translated_text: What was said — the lower stage is like a thorn, one would not enter it — [the answer is]: Because the lower stage has been conquered, one enters it again. Because it is the path within the range of the <s>yogī</s>. What was said — that no one delights in childish play — [the answer is]: Sometimes the cause is indeed of the nature of childish play. Just as an old actor always dances and is never satisfied, because it is for the purpose of instruction. Similarly, a noble one emerges from, enters, and transcends the <s>dhyānas</s> progressively and reversely, because he wishes to demonstrate to gods and humans, and because of the power of mastery that the great <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) have in the <s>samādhis</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, at the time of his passing into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final nirvana), because his body was permeated by the most excellent <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> states, freely entered, emerged from, and transcended them progressively and reversely. Seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s> gone to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder, one would become disenchanted with all unwholesome <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> inspired wonder and love in this <s>Dharma</s> (teaching).

body.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ samyagarthaviruddhamiti yat bhavānavocat | tadidamayuktam | yat bhavatoktaṃ kasmānna vyutkrāmati yāvaccaturthamiti | [tat] bodhisattvapiṭaka uktaṃ vyuktrāntilakṣaṇam- prathamadhyānāt vyutkramya nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpadyate | nirodhasamāpattervyutkramya yāvadvikṣiptacittamavatarati iti | cittabala mahimnā evaṃ śankoti ||
body.translated_text: What you said — that this <s>sūtra</s> contradicts the correct meaning — that is unreasonable. What you said — why does one not transcend up to the fourth — [the answer is]: In the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> (Bodhisattva Collection), the characteristic of transcendence is stated: From the first <s>dhyāna</s>, transcending, one enters the attainment of cessation; from the attainment of cessation, transcending, one descends even to a distracted mind. By the greatness of the power of mind, one is able to do thus.

body.text: ṣaṭsamādhivarga ekaṣaṣṭayuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: End of the chapter on the six <s>samādhis</s>, the one hundred and sixty-first.

body.text: 162 saptasamādhivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 162. Chapter on the Seven <s>Samādhis</s>

body.text: śāstramāha- sapta niśrayāḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ niśrityāsravakṣayaṃ labhate | yavadākiñcanyāyatanaṃ niśrityāsravakṣayaṃ labhata iti | niśrayo nāma yat saptadhyānānyupādāyāryajñānaṃ pratilabhate | yathoktam- samāhitasya yathābhūtajñānamutpadyata iti | pratilabdhadhyānasamādhimātraṃ kañcana sampannaṃ vadati | ato bhagavānāha- nāyaṃ sampanna iti | samādhimimaṃ niśritya āsravāṇāṃ kṣayākhyaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ dharmaṃ prārthayīta | ata ucyate niśraya iti |
body.translated_text: The treatise says: There are seven supports — relying on the first <s>dhyāna</s>, one obtains the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements); up to relying on the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), one obtains the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>. A support means that relying on the seven <s>dhyānas</s>, one attains noble knowledge (<s>āryajñāna</s>). As stated: 'For one who is concentrated, knowledge of things as they truly are arises.' It speaks of someone who has merely attained the <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> as accomplished. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This one is not [truly] accomplished.' Relying on this <s>samādhi</s>, one should seek the distinguished <s>Dharma</s> called the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>. Therefore it is called a support.

body.text: (pṛ) kathamimān dhyānasamādhīn niśrityāsravāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ labhate | (u) bhagavānāha- yogī yenākāreṇa yenālambanena prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate sa yogī tadākāraṃ tadālambanaṃ na punaḥ smarati | kintu paśyati prathamadhyāne yadrūpāṇi yadi vā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni rogato gaṇḍataḥ śalyato 'ghato 'nityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmataḥ | evaṃ paśyataścittamāsravebhyo vimokṣāya nirvidyate | yāvadākiñcanyāyatanamapyevam | parantu trīṇyākāśānantyāyatanā[dī]ni ārūpyadarśanīyāni | yogī kāmadhātumohitaḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ nirvāṇamiti paśyati | tattu paścāllabhate | ato bhagavānāha- mā manyadhvaṃ nirvāṇasukhalakṣaṇamiti | kintu paśyata prathamadhyāne pañcaskandhānāmaṣṭādīnavān iti | tathā niśrayāntareṣvapi |
body.translated_text: (Question) How does one obtain the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> by relying on these <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> states? (Answer) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: The <s>yogī</s>, by whatever mode and whatever object he enters the first <s>dhyāna</s>, that <s>yogī</s> no longer recalls that mode and that object. Rather, he sees in the first <s>dhyāna</s> whatever forms there are, or feelings, perceptions, formations, and consciousnesses, as disease, as a boil, as a dart, as a calamity, as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as non-self. Seeing thus, his mind becomes disenchanted for the sake of liberation from the <s>āsravas</s>. Up to the sphere of nothingness likewise. However, the three [formless attainments] beginning with the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>) are to be viewed as formless. The <s>yogī</s>, deluded by the desire realm, sees the first <s>dhyāna</s> as <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. But that he obtains later. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do not think this is the characteristic of the bliss of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Rather, see in the first <s>dhyāna</s> the eight defects of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates).' Likewise in the other supports as well.

body.text: (pṛ) kāmadhātuḥ kasmānna niśraya ityucyate | (u) uktaṃ hi susīmasūtre- atikramya sapta niśrayān asti āryamārgapratilambhanam iti | ato jñāyate kāmadhāturapyastīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) not called a support? (Answer) It is said in the <s>Susīmasūtra</s>: 'Transcending the seven supports, there is attainment of the noble path.' Therefore it is known that the desire realm also exists [as a basis for practice].

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- prathamadhyānasāmantakamaprāptabhūmiṃ niśritya [api] arhatphalaṃ labhata iti | kathamidam | (u) maivam | yadyaprāptā bhūmirniśrayo bhavati | tadāsti
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: Relying on the preliminary stage of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, even on an unattained level, one obtains the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>. How is this? (Answer) This should not be so. If an unattained level were a support, then there is

body.text: doṣaḥ | yadyaprāptāṃ bhūmiṃ labdhuṃ śaknoti | kasmānna prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate | ato na yuktamidam | (pṛ) naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ kasmānna niśraya ityucyate | (u) na tatrāsti saṃjñānam | samādhau bhūyasā prajñālpīyasī | ato nocyate [sa] niśrayo bhavatīti | saptasaṃjñāsamādhayastu sapta niśrayā bhavanti | kasmādāha bhagavān saptaniśrayāḥ sapta saṃjñāsamādhaya iti | (u) tīrthikā atattvajñatvāt saṃjñāmātramāśrayante | sarve niśryāḥ saṃjñākaluṣitā na vimokṣāya bhavanti ityataḥ saṃjñāsamādhirityākhyā | āryāstu saṃjñāṃ bhaṅktvā samādhimimaṃ niśritya āsravāṇāṃ kṣayamupādadate | ato niśraya ityākhyā | yathoktaṃ yogī dharmānimān paśyati rogato gaṇḍata iti | naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamapi saṃjñayā asaṃjñānānna saṃjñāsamādhirityucyate |
body.translated_text: a fault. If one can obtain an unattained level, why does one not enter the first <s>dhyāna</s>? Therefore this is not tenable. (Question) Why is the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) not called a support? (Answer) There is no cognition there. In <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom is for the most part diminished. Therefore it is not said to be a support. The seven <s>saṃjñā-samādhis</s> (perception-concentrations) are the seven supports. Why does the <s>Bhagavān</s> say the seven supports are the seven <s>saṃjñā-samādhis</s>? (Answer) The <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), because they do not know the true reality, rely merely on perception. All supports are tainted by perception and do not lead to liberation — therefore they are called <s>saṃjñā-samādhi</s> (perception-concentration). But the noble ones, having broken through perception, rely on this <s>samādhi</s> and take up the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>. Therefore it is called a support. As stated: 'The <s>yogī</s> sees these <s>dharmas</s> as disease, as a boil, and so forth.' The sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, because it is neither perception nor non-perception, is not called a <s>saṃjñā-samādhi</s>.

body.text: saptasamādhivargo dviṣaṣṭayuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: End of the chapter on the seven <s>samādhis</s>, the one hundred and sixty-second.

body.text: 163 aṣṭavimokṣavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 163. Chapter on the Eight <s>Vimokṣas</s> (Liberations)

body.text: śāstramāha- sūtra uktaṃ- aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ- adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati iti prathamo vimokṣaḥ | yogāvacaro 'nena vimokṣeṇa rūpāṇyabhibhāvayati | kenedaṃ jñāyate | dvitīyavimokṣe hyuktam- adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi iti | adhyātmarūpaparibhedanādāha- ādhyātmamarūpasaṃjñīti | ato jñāyate yogāvacaraḥ prathamavimokṣe krameṇa kāyarūpamabhibhavatīti | dvitīyavimokṣaṃ prāpya tatra rūpamabhibhūtameva | bāhyarūpamātramasti | tṛtīyavimokṣe bāhyarūpamapyabhibhūtam | ato na paśyati adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā rūpañca | idaṃ rūpaśūnyamityākhyāyate | yathoktaṃ pārāyaṇasūtre-
body.translated_text: The treatise says: It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) are: 'Having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally' — this is the first <s>vimokṣa</s>. A <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditation practitioner) overcomes forms by means of this <s>vimokṣa</s>. How is this known? In the second <s>vimokṣa</s> it is stated: 'Not having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally.' Because one has broken through internal form, it says 'not having the perception of form internally.' Therefore it is known that the <s>yogāvacara</s> gradually overcomes bodily form in the first <s>vimokṣa</s>. Having reached the second <s>vimokṣa</s>, that form has already been overcome. Only external form remains. In the third <s>vimokṣa</s>, external form too is overcome. Therefore one does not see either internal or external form. This is declared to be 'void of form.' As stated in the <s>Pārāyaṇasūtra</s>:

body.text:
rūpalakṣaṇavidhvaṃsī sarvān kāmān jahāti ca |
antarbahiśca no paśyan ahaṃ pṛcchāmi vastvidam || iti |
body.translated_text:
Destroying the characteristic of form, one abandons all desires;
Seeing neither within nor without — I ask about this matter.

body.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ
body.translated_text: From this point

body.text: caturṣu vimokṣeṣu cittaṃ vijñānaśūnyamityāha | yathoktaṃ ṣaḍdhātusūtre- yo bhikṣavaḥ pañcasu dhātuṣu atyantanirviṇṇaḥ, [tasya] anyat jñānamātramasti iti |
body.translated_text: in the four [remaining] <s>vimokṣas</s>, the mind is said to be void of consciousness. As stated in the <s>Ṣaḍdhātusūtra</s> (Six Elements Sūtra): 'O monks, for one who is completely disenchanted with the five elements, there remains only mere knowledge.'

body.text: jñātavyaṃ caturṣu vimokṣeṣu vijñānānyanubhavatīti | aṣṭamavimokṣe sarveṣāṃ kṣayaḥ | kasmāt rūpanirodhe cittanirodhe saṃskṛtānāmātyantikanirodhaḥ | idamevārhatphalamityucyate | evaṃ krameṇa kṣayabhāk bhavati | ime 'ṣṭavimokṣāḥ |
body.translated_text: It should be known that in the four <s>vimokṣas</s>, one experiences the consciousnesses. In the eighth <s>vimokṣa</s>, there is the cessation of all. Why? Because with the cessation of form and the cessation of mind, there is the ultimate cessation of all conditioned things (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). This itself is called the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>. Thus, step by step, one comes to partake of cessation. These are the eight <s>vimokṣas</s>.

body.text: kaścidāha- prathamau dvau vimokṣāvaviśuddhau | tṛtīyastu viśuddha iti | nedaṃ yujyate | kasmāt ayaṃ vimokṣa iti nāsti [yatkiñcit | yasya] aviśuddhabhāvanayā vimokṣaṃ labhate | viśuddhabhāvanayāpi nāsti vimokṣaḥ | kevalaṃ śūnyabhāvanayā vimokṣaṃ labhate | tīrthikā viśuddhāviśuddhabhāvanāṃ bhajantena vimokṣabhāgina ityākhyāyante |
body.translated_text: Someone says: The first two <s>vimokṣas</s> are impure, while the third is pure. This is not tenable. Why? There is nothing whatsoever [in this concept that] this is a <s>vimokṣa</s> — one who obtains liberation through impure cultivation. Nor is there liberation through pure cultivation [alone]. One obtains liberation solely through the cultivation of emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>). The <s>tīrthikas</s> who practice pure and impure cultivation are called those who do not partake of liberation.

body.text: (pṛ) tīrthikā api rūpalakṣaṇaṃ vināśa(ya)nti | kathamidam | (u) tīrthikā vimokṣādhimuktyā rūpalakṣaṇaṃ vināśayanti na tu śūnyabhāvanayā | kasmāt | yathābhāvanādhimuktiprayogaṃ mṛtaparityaktaṃ kāyaṃ śmāśānikakṛmayo bhakṣayanti ityādi paśyanti | (pṛ) tīrti(rthi)kā rūpavinirmuktamārūpyasamādhiṃ vindante | [teṣāṃ] ārūpyavimokṣo bhavet | (u) tīrthikānāṃ satyapi ārūpyasamādhau [tatra] āsaṅgānna[sa]vimokṣa ityucyate | āryāḥ punarārūpyasamādhimupādāya caturaḥ skandhān rogata ityādyaṣṭabhirākāraiḥ paśyanti | ato vimokṣa ityucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) also destroy the characteristics of form. How is this? (Answer) The <s>tīrthikas</s> destroy the characteristics of form through the resolve of liberation, but not through the contemplation of emptiness. Why? According to their practice of contemplative resolve, they see how worms in the charnel ground devour a dead and abandoned body, and so forth. (Question) The <s>tīrthikas</s> attain the formless <s>ārūpya-samādhi</s> (formless concentration) free from form. They should have the formless <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation). (Answer) Although the <s>tīrthikas</s> possess the formless <s>samādhi</s>, because of their attachment therein, it is not called <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation). The noble ones, however, taking the formless <s>samādhi</s> as basis, contemplate the four <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) through eight aspects beginning with 'as a disease.' Therefore it is called <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation).

body.text: (pṛ) bhavānavocat- nirodhasamāpattirarhatphalamiti | idamayuktam | kasmāt | śaikṣā api aṣṭavimokṣabhāja ucyante | nirodhasamāpattirāsravakṣayātmiketi bhavatoktam | tathā ca śaikṣā āsravakṣayabhājaḥ syuḥ | (u) sūtre sāmānyalakṣaṇena nirodha uktaḥ | na tu vivicya ayaṃ cittanirodhaḥ ayaṃ kleśakṣaya iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- nirodho dvividhaḥ [kṣaya]nirodhaḥ anupūrvanirodha iti | dvividhaṃ nirvāṇaṃ dṛṣṭadharmanirvāṇam ātyantikanirvāṇamiti | kiñcāha kṣemo dvividhaḥ- [avara]kṣemaḥ paramakṣema iti | kṣemalābho 'pi dvividhaḥ [avara]kṣemalābhaḥ paramakṣemalābha iti | ataḥ śaikṣajanānāṃ pratilabdho na pāramāthikanirodhaḥ | kiñcoktaṃ
body.translated_text: (Question) You stated that <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> (the attainment of cessation) is the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>. This is improper. Why? Because <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners) are also said to partake of the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations). You stated that <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> consists in the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows). If so, then <s>śaikṣas</s> would also partake of the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>.
