(Answer) In the <s>sūtra</s>, cessation is spoken of by its general characteristic. It does not distinguish 'this is the cessation of mind and mental factors' and 'this is the destruction of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Cessation is twofold: cessation through destruction and sequential cessation.' <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is also twofold: <s>nirvāṇa</s> in this very life and ultimate <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Furthermore it says: 'Security is twofold: lesser security and supreme security.' 'The attainment of security is also twofold: the attainment of lesser security and the attainment of supreme security.' Therefore what is attained by <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners) is not the ultimate cessation. Furthermore it is stated

body.text: sūtre nirodhasamāpattimupasampanno bhikṣuḥ kṛtakaraṇīya iti | yadi nirodhasamāpattirnārhatphalam, tadā kṛtakaraṇīya iti nābhidadhyāt |
body.translated_text: in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who has entered the <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> (attainment of cessation) has accomplished what was to be done.' If <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> were not the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>, then it would not be declared that 'he has accomplished what was to be done.'

body.text: (pṛ) kiṃ śaikṣā vastuto nāṣṭavimokṣān labhante | (u) sūtra uktaṃ śaikṣo navānupūrvasamādhīn labhata iti | na tūktaṃ kṣayanirodhaṃ pratilabhata iti | yogāvacaro yadi kṣayanirodhaṃ pratilabdhvā na dhyānasamādhīn samāpadyate | ayaṃ prajñāvimukta ityucyate | yadi dhyānasamādhīn samāpadyate na kṣayanirodhaṃ labhate | [tadā] kāyasākṣītyucyate | yadyubhayaṃ labhate | tadā ubhayato vimukta ityucyate | kasmāt | kleśā eko bhāgaḥ | dhyānasamādhyāvaraṇadharmā aparo bhāgaḥ | ubhābhyāṃ bhāgābhyāṃ vimukta ubhayato[bhāga]vimukta ityucyate | (pṛ) anupūrva[vihāre]ṣu nirodho vimokṣeṣu nirodhaśca kiṃ nānā | (u) vyañjanamekam | arthastu nānā | anupūrveṣu nirodhaścittacaittānāṃ nirodhaḥ | vimokṣeṣu nirodhaḥ kleśānāṃ nirodhaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- saṃskārāṇāmanupūrvanirodhaḥ | tathāhi- prathamadhyānaṃ samāpannasya vāk nirudhyate | dvitīyadhyānaṃ samāpannasya vitarkavicārā niruddhā bhavanti | tṛtīyadhyānaṃ samāpannasya prītirnirudhyate | caturthadhyānaṃ samāpannasya sukhaṃ nirudhyate | ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samāpannasya rupasaṃjñā niruddhā bhavati | vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ samāpannasya ākāśānantyāyatanasaṃjñā niruddhā bhavati | ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ samāpannasya vijñānānantyāyatanasaṃjñā niruddhā bhavati | naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ samāpannasya ākiñca nyāyatanasaṃjñā niruddhā bhavati | nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannasya saṃjñā ca vedanā ca niruddhā bhavati | iti | eṣu nirodheṣu nirodho viśiṣṭo yaduta yogāvacaro rāgadveṣamohebhyo nirviṇṇo vimucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) Do the <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners) not in reality attain the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations)? (Answer) The <s>sūtra</s> states that a <s>śaikṣa</s> attains the nine sequential <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). But it does not state that he attains the cessation through destruction. If a practitioner, having attained the cessation through destruction, does not enter the <s>dhyāna-samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations), he is called 'liberated by wisdom' (<s>prajñā-vimukta</s>). If he enters the <s>dhyāna-samādhis</s> but does not attain the cessation through destruction, then he is called a 'body-witness' (<s>kāya-sākṣin</s>). If he attains both, then he is called 'liberated in both ways' (<s>ubhayato-bhāga-vimukta</s>). Why? The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are one part; the factors obstructing <s>dhyāna-samādhi</s> are another part. One who is liberated from both parts is called 'liberated in both ways.' (Question) Is the cessation in the sequential [abidings] and the cessation in the <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) different? (Answer) The term is the same, but the meaning is different. The cessation in the sequential [abidings] is the cessation of mind and mental factors. The cessation in the <s>vimokṣas</s> is the cessation of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The sequential cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) [is as follows]:' For one who has entered the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), speech ceases. For one who has entered the second <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) have ceased. For one who has entered the third <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>prīti</s> (joy) ceases. For one who has entered the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) ceases. For one who has entered the sphere of infinite space, the perception of form has ceased. For one who has entered the sphere of infinite consciousness, the perception of the sphere of infinite space has ceased. For one who has entered the sphere of nothingness, the perception of the sphere of infinite consciousness has ceased. For one who has entered the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the perception of the sphere of nothingness has ceased. For one who has entered the <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> (attainment of cessation), perception and feeling have ceased. Among these cessations, the cessation that is supreme is this: the practitioner, being disgusted with desire, hatred, and delusion, is liberated.

body.text: (pṛ) kathaṃ jñāyate anupūrveṣu cittacaittānāṃ nirodhaḥ vimokṣeṣu kleśānāṃ nirodha iti | (u) nirodhastulyārtho 'pi medavān syāt | anupūrveṣūcyate saṃjñāvedayitanirodha iti | vimokṣeṣu avidyāvedanāsparśanirodha iti | kasmāt | prajñaptito hi vedanotpadyate | prajñaptibhede vedanā nirudhyate | sūtreṣvastīdṛśo vibhāgaḥ | yadyāha- kaṇṭhato yogāvacaraḥ
body.translated_text: (Question) How is it known that in the sequential [abidings] there is cessation of mind and mental factors, while in the <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) there is cessation of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)? (Answer) Although 'cessation' has the same meaning, one who is discerning should distinguish. In the sequential [abidings] it is said 'the cessation of perception and feeling.' In the <s>vimokṣas</s> it is said 'the cessation of ignorance, feeling, and contact.' Why? Because feeling arises depending on conceptual designation. When the conceptual designation is broken, feeling ceases. In the <s>sūtras</s> there is such a distinction. If one says: 'From the throat, the practitioner

body.text: kṣayanirodhalābhīti | tadā [sa] kṛtakaraṇīya iti | jñātavyaṃ nirvāṇaṃ sakṣātkurvataḥ sarve kleśā nirudhyanta iti | na tvāha cittacaittā nirudhyanta iti | (pṛ) yadyaṣṭavimokṣāḥ kleśanirodhadharmakāḥ | tadā sarve 'rhantaḥ sarvadā labheran | (u) sarve labhante | na tu samāpadyante | ye dhyānasamādhīn sākṣātkurvanti te samāpadyante | (pṛ) yogāvacarasya yadi na santi dhyānasamādhayaḥ | kathaṃ sa kāyacittaśūnyatāṃ labhate kleśāṃśca kṣapayati | (u) ayaṃ samādhiyukto 'pi na sākṣātkaroti | asti punastaṭidupamasamādhiḥ | [imaṃ] samādhimupādāya kleśān kṣapayati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- mama bhikṣavaścīvaramupāditsoḥ kleśo bhavati | cīvaramupādāya punaḥ kleśo na bhavati | ityādi | kasmāt | taṭidupamasamādhicittaṃ vajropamaṃ tattvajñānaṃ kleśān bhinatti | artho 'yaṃ bhagavatā tṛtīyabala uktaḥ yaduta dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisaṃkleśavyavadānavibhāgayathābhūtajñānam | tatra dhyānaṃ nāma catvāri dhyānāni | kecidāhuḥ- catvāri dhyānāni catvāro 'rūpasamādhayaḥ sarve dhyānamityucyante | vimokṣaḥ aṣṭavimokṣāḥ | samādhirekakṣaṇataṭidupamasamādhiḥ | samāpattiḥ dhyānavimokṣasamādhiṣu vaśitābalalābhaḥ yathāha- śāriputraḥ- saptabodhyaṅgeṣu samāpattiṃ vyutthānañca vaśīkaromi iti | ato jñāyate prajñāvimuktasyārhataḥ santi dhyānasamādhayaḥ | kintu na [tatra] samāpadyate | abhyāsaprakarṣāt samāpattiṃ vaśīkaroti |
body.translated_text: attains the cessation through destruction,' then he has accomplished what was to be done. It should be known that when one directly realizes <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) cease — but it is not said that mind and mental factors cease. (Question) If the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) have the nature of the cessation of <s>kleśas</s>, then all <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones) should always attain them. (Answer) All attain them, but not all enter into them. Those who directly realize the <s>dhyāna-samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations) enter into them. (Question) If a practitioner does not possess <s>dhyāna-samādhis</s>, how does he attain the emptiness of body and mind and destroy the <s>kleśas</s>? (Answer) Even one who is endowed with <s>samādhi</s> may not directly realize [the higher ones]. However, there is the lightning-like <s>samādhi</s> (<s>taḍid-upama-samādhi</s>). By means of this <s>samādhi</s>, one destroys the <s>kleśas</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), when I wished to take up a robe, there was affliction. Having taken up the robe, there was no more affliction.' And so forth. Why? The mind of the lightning-like <s>samādhi</s> is the diamond-like knowledge of reality (<s>vajropama-tattvajñāna</s>) that shatters the <s>kleśas</s>. This meaning was spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) in the third power, namely: 'The knowledge as it really is of the defilement and purification of <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments).' Therein, '<s>dhyāna</s>' refers to the four <s>dhyānas</s>. Some say: the four <s>dhyānas</s> and the four formless <s>samādhis</s> are all called '<s>dhyāna</s>.' '<s>Vimokṣa</s>' refers to the eight <s>vimokṣas</s>. '<s>Samādhi</s>' refers to the single-moment lightning-like <s>samādhi</s>. '<s>Samāpatti</s>' refers to the mastery and power over <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>vimokṣas</s>, and <s>samādhis</s>, as <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'I exercise mastery over entering and rising from the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening).' From this it is known that the <s>arhat</s> liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñā-vimukta</s>) possesses <s>dhyāna-samādhis</s>, but does not enter into them. Through excellence of practice, one exercises mastery over the attainment.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmādarhan na dhyānasamādhīnāṃ prakṛṣṭamabhyastā bhavati | (u) puruṣo 'yaṃ pratilabdhamārgaḥ kṛtakṛtyo bhavati | upekṣābhinavāt na samyagabhyasyati | yadyupekṣācittaṃ nāsti tadāsamāpattiṃ samāpadyate iti nāsti dūṣaṇam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yogāvacaraścatura ṛddhipādān samyagabhyasan himavantaṃ parvatarājaṃ tathā dhamati yathā reṇuparyavasannaṃ bhavati | kiṃ punarmaraṇamavidyām iti | ato jñāyate aṣṭavimokṣeṣūcyate āsravakṣayanirodhaḥ na nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpadyata iti | uktañca sūtre- asti vidyāsvabhāvaḥ asti śūnyasvabhāvaḥ, astyākāśānantyāyanasvabhāvaḥ, asti vijñānānantyāyata(na)svabhāvaḥ astyākiñcanyāyatanasvabhāvaḥ asti naivasaṃjñāsaṃjñāyatanasvabhāvaḥ asti nirodhasvabhāvaḥ | avidyāmupādāyāsti vidyāsvabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is the <s>arhat</s> (worthy one) not one who has practiced the <s>dhyāna-samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations) to the highest degree? (Answer) This person, having attained the path and accomplished what was to be done, does not practice properly due to the freshness of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). If there is no mind of equanimity, then there is no fault in saying he enters the attainment. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A practitioner who properly cultivates the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi-pādas</s>) blows away the king of mountains <s>Himavat</s> just as dust settles. How much more so death and ignorance!' From this it is known that in the eight <s>vimokṣas</s>, it is the cessation through the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) that is spoken of, not the entering of <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s>. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There is the nature of knowledge, there is the nature of emptiness, there is the nature of the sphere of infinite space, there is the nature of the sphere of infinite consciousness, there is the nature of the sphere of nothingness, there is the nature of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, there is the nature of cessation. Depending on ignorance, there is the nature of knowledge.'

body.text: aśūnyamupādayāsti śūnyasvabhāvaḥ | rūpamupādāyāstyākāśānantyāyatanasvabhāvaḥ | akāśānantyāyatanasvabhāvamupādāyāsti vijñānānantyāyatanasvabhāvaḥ | vijñānānantyāyatanasvabhāvamupādāyāstyākiñcanyāyatanasvabhāvaḥ | ākiñcanyāyatanasvabhāvamupādāyāsti naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasvabhāvaḥ | pañcaskandhānupādāyāsti nirodhasvabhāva iti | pañcaskandhān prajñaptilakṣaṇān yo na paribhedayati tasyāvidyā bhavati | yastān paribhedayati | tasya bhavati vidyāsvabhāvaḥ | yathā bhagavān ekaṃ bhikṣumanuśāsti- śūnyeṣu sarvasaṃskāreṣu saṃskārān śūnyān bhāvayitvā damaya svacittam iti | yathā kaścitpradīpamādāya śūnyāgāraṃ praviśya paśyati sarvaṃ śūnyamiti | [tathā] yogāvacaro rūpamupādāyādhigacchati rūpamidaṃ niruddhamiti | ayaṃ śūnyasvabhāva ityucyate | tīrthikā ākāśānantyāyanamupādāya pratilabhante rūpādviyujyante | yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamupādāya ākiñcanyāyatanāt viyujyante |
body.translated_text: Depending on the non-empty, there is the nature of emptiness. Depending on form, there is the nature of the sphere of infinite space. Depending on the nature of the sphere of infinite space, there is the nature of the sphere of infinite consciousness. Depending on the nature of the sphere of infinite consciousness, there is the nature of the sphere of nothingness. Depending on the nature of the sphere of nothingness, there is the nature of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Depending on the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), there is the nature of cessation. One who does not analyze the five <s>skandhas</s> with their characteristics of conceptual designation has ignorance. One who analyzes them has the nature of knowledge. Just as the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) instructed a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk): 'All <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) being empty, having cultivated the emptiness of formations, tame your own mind.' Just as someone taking a lamp and entering an empty house sees that everything is empty, so the practitioner, depending on form, realizes 'this form has ceased.' This is called the 'nature of emptiness.' The <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), depending on the sphere of infinite space, attain it and become separated from form, and so on up to depending on the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, they become separated from the sphere of nothingness.

body.text: skandhānupādāyāsti nirodhasvabhāva iti | yogāvacara[ścintayati]- yatkiñcanamanaskāraḥ yatkiñcanakṛtakaraṇam sarveṣāṃ nirodhaḥ śreyāniti | ayaṃ skandhānupādāyāsti nirodhasvabhāva iti |
body.translated_text: Depending on the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), there is the nature of cessation. The practitioner contemplates: 'Whatever mental engagement, whatever action — the cessation of all of them is the best.' This is what is meant by 'depending on the <s>skandhas</s>, there is the nature of cessation.'

body.text: (pṛ) ime svabhāvāḥ kaṃ samādhiṃ niśritya pratilabhyante | (u) sūtra uktam- vidyāsvabhāvo yāvat naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasvabhāvaḥ sarvaṃ khayaṃ samādhisamāpattiviharaṇātpratilabhate yaduta saṃskṛtamārgaviharaṇātpratilabhata iti | kasmāt | ādyo rūpajñānālambano vidyāsvabhāvaḥ | dvitīyasvabhāvo 'pi rūpopādāno rupamupādāya tathā vivecayati yathā śūnyaṃ bhavati | evaṃ yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasvabhāvaḥ, sarve saṃskṛtadharmāḥ śūnyā iti nirodhasamāpattyā nirodhaṃ pratilabhate | atra sarveṣāṃ saṃskṛtadharmāṇāṃ kṣayanirodhāt | ato jñāyate atrokto nirodhaḥ kṣayanirodho nirvāṇamiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Depending on what <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) are these natures attained? (Answer) The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'The nature of knowledge, up to the nature of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — all of these are attained through abiding in <s>samādhi-samāpatti</s> (meditative attainment), that is, through abiding in the conditioned path.' Why? The first, the nature of knowledge, has form-cognition as its object. The second nature also takes form as its basis and analyzes it such that it becomes empty. Thus, up to the nature of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — all conditioned <s>dharmas</s> being empty — through the <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> (attainment of cessation), one attains cessation. Here, because of the cessation through destruction of all conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, from this it is known that the cessation spoken of here is the cessation through destruction, which is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) ime vimokṣāḥ kasyāṃ bhūmau bhavanti | (u) yogāvacaro rūpaparibhedecchayā kāmadhātupratilabdhaṃ samādhiṃ vā rūpadhātupratilabdhaṃ vā samādhiṃ niśrayamāṇo rūpaṃ śūnyaṃ pratilabhate | sarvabhūmigataṃ cittañca śūnyaṃ pratilabhate | (pṛ) eṣu vimokṣeṣu kati sāsravāḥ kati anāsravāḥ | (u) śūnyasvabhāvatvāt sarve 'nāsravāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Question) In what ground do these <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) occur? (Answer) The practitioner, wishing to analyze form, relying on a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) attained in the desire realm or a <s>samādhi</s> attained in the form realm, realizes the emptiness of form and realizes the emptiness of mind belonging to all grounds. (Question) Among these <s>vimokṣas</s>, how many have <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) and how many are without <s>āsravas</s>? (Answer) Because they all have the nature of emptiness, all are without <s>āsravas</s> (outflows).

body.text: aṣṭavimokṣavargastriṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), the one hundred and sixty-third.

body.text: 164 aṣṭābhibhvāyatanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 164. The chapter on the eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (spheres of mastery).

body.text: adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī [eko] bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttāni suvarṇadurvarṇāni | tānyabhibhūya jānāti paśyati | evaṃ saṃjñī ca bhavati | idaṃ prathamamabhibhvāyatanam | adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati adhimātrāṇi[suvarṇadurvarṇānīti vistaro yāvat] idaṃ dvitīya[mabhibhvāyatana]m | adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttāni [suvarṇadurvarṇānīti yāvat] idaṃ tṛtīya[mabhibhvāyatana]m | adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhī rūpāṇi paśyati adhimātrāṇi [suvarṇadurvarṇānīti yāvat] idaṃ [caturthamabhibhvāyatana]m | adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanirbhāsāni tadyathā umakāpuṣpaṃ[sampannaṃ] vārāṇaseyaṃ vā vastraṃ[nīlaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ nīlanidarśanaṃ nīlanirbhāsam | tāni khalu rūpāṇyabhibhūya jānāti paśyati | evaṃsaṃjñī ca bhavatīdaṃ] pañcama[mabhibhvāyatana]m | ṣaṣṭhaṃ pītāni paśyati | saptamaṃ- raktāni paśyati | aṣṭamaṃ- avadātāni paśyati | yogāvacara evamapramāṇāni rūpāṇi paśyati | kasmāt | na kevalaṃ santīmāni nīlādīni catvāri rūpāṇi | saṃkṣipyakathanādaṣṭābhibhvāyatanāni bhavanti | yogāvacaro yadā śūnyatayā rūpāṇi paribhedayati | tadā abhibhvāyatanamityucyate |
body.translated_text: One who, having the perception of form internally, sees forms externally that are limited, of good and bad color — having mastered those, he knows and sees. Thus he has such a perception. This is the first base of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>). One who, having the perception of form internally, sees forms externally that are immeasurable, [of good and bad color — the full description as before] — this is the second base of mastery. One who, having the perception of non-form internally, sees forms externally that are limited, [of good and bad color — as before] — this is the third base of mastery. One who, having the perception of non-form internally, sees forms externally that are immeasurable, [of good and bad color — as before] — this is the fourth base of mastery. One who, having the perception of non-form internally, sees forms externally that are blue, of blue color, of blue appearance — just as the <s>umā</s> flower is excellent, or a cloth of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> [that is blue, of blue color, of blue aspect, of blue appearance. Having mastered those very forms, he knows and sees. Thus he has such a perception — this is] the fifth base of mastery. The sixth: one sees yellow [forms]. The seventh: one sees red [forms]. The eighth: one sees white [forms]. The <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner of meditation) sees immeasurable forms in this way. Why? Not only do these four forms of blue and the like exist. Through summarized exposition, there are eight bases of mastery. When the <s>yogāvacara</s> penetrates forms through emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), then it is called a 'base of mastery.'

body.text: (pṛ) ka idaṃ pratilabhate | (u) ime bhagavataḥ śrāvakā nānye | (pṛ) imānyaṣṭābhibhvāyatanāni kasyā bhūmau bhavanti | (u) kāmadhātau bhavanti | (pṛ) kiṃ sāsravāṇi utānāsravāṇi | (u) pūrvaṃ sāsravāṇi santi śūnyatayā rūpāṇāṃ paribhede 'nāsravāṇi bhavanti | (pṛ) kasmādayaṃ dharmaḥ kevalamabhibhvāyatanamityucyate | (u) idaṃ yogāvacarāṇāmabhyāsaktamāyatam | ato bhagavān śrāvakāṇāṃ kṛta āha- abhibhvāyatanamiti | tadālambanābhibhavapradarśanārtham ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Who obtains this? (Answer) These are the disciples (<s>śrāvaka</s>) of the Blessed One, not others. (Question) To which plane (<s>bhūmi</s>) do these eight bases of mastery belong? (Answer) They belong to the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). (Question) Are they with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) or without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>)? (Answer) Previously they are with outflows; upon the penetration of forms through emptiness, they become without outflows. (Question) Why is this <s>dharma</s> called merely a 'base of mastery'? (Answer) This is the domain extensively practiced by <s>yogāvacaras</s>. Therefore the Blessed One, having done so for the disciples, said 'base of mastery' — for the purpose of demonstrating the mastery over those objects.

body.text: aṣṭābhibhvāyatanavarga ścatuṣpaṣṭayuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and sixty-fourth chapter, the Chapter on the Eight Bases of Mastery (<s>aṣṭābhibhvāyatanavarga</s>).

body.text: 165 navānupūrva[vihāreṣu]prathamadhyānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 165. The first chapter on the first <s>dhyāna</s> among the nine successive abidings (<s>navānupūrvavihāra</s>).

body.text: navānupūrvavihārāḥ- catvāri dhyānāni catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ nirodhasamāpattiśca | prathamaṃ dhyānam- yathoktaṃ sūtre yogāvacaro vivicyaiva kāmairvivicyākuśalai
body.translated_text: The nine successive abidings are: the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). The first <s>dhyāna</s> — as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>yogāvacara</s>, being secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome

body.text: dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharatīti | (pṛ) prathamadhyānalakṣaṇamātraṃ vaktavyam | kasmātpunarucyate vivicyaiva kāmairiti | (u) kecidapavadanti nāsti kāmavivikto loka iti | laukikānāṃ [sadā] pañcakāmeṣu sthitatvāt | na hi kaściccakṣuṣā rūpaṃ na paśyati | śrotreṇa śabdaṃ na śṛṇoti, ghrāṇena gandhaṃ na jighrati, rasanayā rasaṃ na rasayati, kāyena na sparśānanubhavatīti | ata ucyate vivicyaiva kāmairiti | kāmo nāma kāmacittaṃ na rūpādiḥ | yathoktam- rūpādayaḥ padārthā na kāmā iti | kathaṃ tajjānīmaḥ | vyavasāyī khalu rūpādiṣu sthitvaiva kāmaṃ prajahāti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- rūpādayastadbhāgā na kāmā bhavanti iti | ato rāgacittaṃ kāma ityucyate | yasya rāgacittaṃ bhavati sa kāmān paryeṣate | kāmaparyeṣaṇāpratyayaṃ rāgapratidhavadhavihiṃsā akuśalā dharmā anuvartante | yathoktaṃ mahānidānasūtre- tṛṣṇāṃ pratītya paryeṣaṇā ityādi | ato jñāyate kāmarāgairviviktatvāt vivicyaiva kāmairiti | kecidāhuḥ- rūpādibhiḥ pañcakāma[guṇai]rviviktaṃ kāmairviviktamiti | vivicyākuśalai rdharmairiti pañcanīvaraṇairviviktam |
body.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s>, with applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>), with joy (<s>prīti</s>) and pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) born of seclusion, enters upon and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>.' (Question) Only the characteristic of the first <s>dhyāna</s> should be stated. Why then is it said 'secluded from sensual desires'? (Answer) Some deny it, saying 'there is no world that is free from sensual desires.' Because worldly beings always abide in the five kinds of sensual pleasure, no one does not see form with the eye, does not hear sounds with the ear, does not smell odors with the nose, does not taste flavors with the tongue, does not experience tangible objects with the body. Therefore it is said 'secluded from sensual desires.' 'Sensual desire' (<s>kāma</s>) means the mind of desire (<s>kāmacitta</s>), not form and the like. As stated: 'Objects such as form and the like are not desires.' How is this known? Indeed, one who has undertaken the practice, while still abiding in [the domain of] form and the like, abandons desire. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Objects such as form and the like partake of that [domain] — they are not desires.' Therefore the mind of passion (<s>rāgacitta</s>) is called 'desire.' One who has the mind of passion seeks sensual pleasures. Dependent on the pursuit of sensual pleasures, passion, aversion, harm, and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> follow. As stated in the <s>Mahānidāna Sūtra</s>: 'Dependent on craving, there is pursuit,' and so forth. From this it is known that 'secluded from sensual desires' means secluded from the passions of sensual desire. Some say: 'Secluded from sensual desires' means secluded from the five kinds of sensual pleasure (<s>kāmaguṇa</s>). 'Secluded from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>' means secluded from the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>).

body.text: prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ vikṣiptacittāsannatvātsavitarkam | yogāvacarasyāpariniṣpannasamādhibalasya cittavikṣepasyodayātsavitarkam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- savitarka savicāraṃ vihāraṃ viharāmīti | [ato] jñātavyaṃ bhagavānavocat- vikṣiptacittaṃ vitarka iti | vitarko 'yaṃ kramaśaścittasamādhānapravṛttau vicāro bhavati | yadā samādhipariniṣpattyā cittaṃ na bhūyasā vikṣipati tadā vicāraḥ | vicāro 'yaṃ yogāvacamanutartayan dhyānāntarālaṃ prāpnoti | vitarkavicāraviviktasya prītilābhe vivekajā prītiricyate | prītiriyaṃ prathamalabdhā kāyaṃ sukhayatīti sukhaṃ bhavati | vitarkavicāraviveka[jā] prītirekālambanasthitā dhyānamityucyate | dhyānasyāsya vitarkavicāravyākulatvāt kāyāntaravipākaṃ pratilabhate | asyottamamadhyamādhamavibhāgātsanti brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitā mahābrahmāṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: The first <s>dhyāna</s>, because of its proximity to the scattered mind, has applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>). Because the power of concentration of the <s>yogāvacara</s> is not yet fully accomplished, and because the distraction of mind arises, it has applied thought. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'I abide in a state with applied thought and sustained thought.' From this it should be known that the Blessed One said: 'The scattered mind is applied thought.' This applied thought, through the gradual progression toward the settling of the mind in concentration, becomes sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>). When, through the full accomplishment of concentration, the mind is no longer greatly distracted, then there is sustained thought. This sustained thought, following the <s>yogāvacara</s>, attains the intermediate stage of <s>dhyāna</s>. When one is free from applied thought and sustained thought and obtains joy (<s>prīti</s>), the joy born of seclusion is enhanced. This joy, first obtained, makes the body comfortable — thus there is pleasure (<s>sukha</s>). The joy born of freedom from applied thought and sustained thought, established on a single object — that is called '<s>dhyāna</s>.' Because this <s>dhyāna</s> is disturbed by applied thought and sustained thought, one obtains rebirth in another body. Through the division of this [dhyāna] into superior, middling, and inferior, there are the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s> [gods].

body.text: (pṛ) yadi vitarkavicāraviveka[jā] prītiḥ prathamaṃ dhyānam | tadā na syāt pañcāṅgaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam | yadi vitarkavicāravivekaḥ, dvitīyadhyānasya ko bhedaḥ | uktañca sūtre- prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ savitarkaṃ savicāram | anyat praśrabdhisukham anyā ca prītiriti | yadi prītireva sukham, tadā saptasambodhyaṅgeṣu prasrabdhibodhyaṅgaṃ na pṛthaguktaṃ syāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) If joy born of freedom from applied thought and sustained thought is the first <s>dhyāna</s>, then the first <s>dhyāna</s> would not be five-factored. If there is freedom from applied thought and sustained thought, what would be the difference from the second <s>dhyāna</s>? And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The first <s>dhyāna</s> has applied thought and sustained thought.' Furthermore, the pleasure of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhisukha</s>) is one thing, and joy (<s>prīti</s>) is another. If joy is itself pleasure, then among the seven factors of awakening (<s>sambodhyaṅga</s>), the factor of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhibodhyaṅga</s>) would not be stated separately.

body.text: (u) prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ na syātpañcāṅgamiti bhavadvacanamayuktam | na hyucyate pañcāṅgāni prathamadhyānasvabhāvā iti | prathamadhyānasyāsannabhūmāvimau vitarkavicārau sta ityaṅgamityucyete |
body.translated_text: (Answer) Your statement that 'the first <s>dhyāna</s> would not be five-factored' is untenable. For it is not said that the five factors are the essential nature of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Because applied thought and sustained thought are in the domain proximate to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, they are called 'factors.'

body.text: (pṛ) yadyāsannabhūmiko dharmagaṇo 'ṅgamiti | prathamaṃ dhyānamapi pañcakāma[guṇā]nāṃ pratyāsannamiti [te] aṅgāni vaktavyāni syuḥ | (u) pañcakāma[guṇā]na pratyāsannā bhavanti | yogāvacaracittaṃ hi [ta]dviviktameva | prathamadhyānānantarañca na kāmacittamudeti | pañcakāmaguṇāśca na prathamadhyānasyāṅgāni vartante | aṅgaṃ nāma kāraṇam | bhāga eva kāraṇam | yathāryamārgāṅgāni sañcitāni kāraṇānityādi | tathā vitarkavicārāvapi prathamadhyānasya kāraṇam | yat yogāvacara ālambane samāhitaḥ, [tato] vyāvartane punassamādhinimittamupādāya tatrālambane cittaṃ samādhāya maulikaṃ nimittaṃ manasi karoti | imau vitarkavicārau | ato jñāyate vitarkavicārau prathamadhyānasya kāraṇamiti | dvitīyadhyāne cittasamādhānaṃ sthitameva | ato na tau kāraṇam | dhyānadvayasamanantarañca na vitarkavicārau bhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) If a group of <s>dharmas</s> in the proximate domain is a factor, then the first <s>dhyāna</s> too is proximate to the five kinds of sensual pleasure — those should [also] be stated as factors. (Answer) The five kinds of sensual pleasure are not proximate. For the mind of the <s>yogāvacara</s> is secluded from them. And immediately after the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the mind of sensual desire does not arise. And the five kinds of sensual pleasure are not factors of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. A 'factor' means a cause. A component is itself a cause. Just as the factors of the Noble Path, when gathered, are causes, and so forth. Thus applied thought and sustained thought too are causes of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. When the <s>yogāvacara</s> is settled on the object, upon turning away [from the object], he again takes up the sign of concentration and settles the mind on that object, bringing the fundamental sign to attention. These are applied thought and sustained thought. From this it is known that applied thought and sustained thought are causes of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. In the second <s>dhyāna</s>, the settling of mind in concentration is already established. Therefore those two are not causes [of it]. And immediately after both [the first and second] <s>dhyānas</s>, applied thought and sustained thought do not occur.

body.text: yadāha bhavān prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ vitarkavicārasahagatamiti | tadayuktam | prathamadhyāna utpanne 'tha vitarkavicārau bhavataḥ | tayoḥ pratyāsannatvāt tatsahagatamityucyate | yathā śiṣyeṇa saha gacchatīti kiñcidviprarṣe 'pi sahetyucyate | amyā bhūmerjananahetukatayā vitarkavicārau staḥ | yathā bhūtapīḍitaḥ puruṣo [bhūta] anudgrame 'pi pīḍita ityucyate | puruṣasyāsya bhūtadūṣitasya punarudbhavapratyayo 'stīti [kṛtvā] pīḍita ityucyate | sukhavedanaiva prītiḥ | kintu vibhajyocyate | praśrabdhito 'pi sukhaṃ pṛthagucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- praśrabdhakāyaḥ sukhaṃ vedayata iti |
body.translated_text: Your statement that 'the first <s>dhyāna</s> is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought' — that is untenable. When the first <s>dhyāna</s> has arisen, applied thought and sustained thought then exist. Because of their proximity, it is said to be 'accompanied by them.' Just as one who 'goes together with a student' — even when somewhat separated, it is said 'together with.' Because these two are the generative causes of that [dhyāna's] domain, applied thought and sustained thought exist. Just as a person afflicted by a spirit (<s>bhūta</s>), even when the spirit has not manifested, is called 'afflicted' — because there is a condition for the re-arising of this person's spirit-affliction, he is called 'afflicted.' Joy (<s>prīti</s>) is itself pleasant feeling (<s>sukhavedanā</s>). But it is spoken of analytically. Pleasure from tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) is also stated separately as pleasure. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One whose body is tranquil experiences pleasure.'

body.text: (pṛ) tathā cet kathaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ pañcāṅgamityucyate | (u) kālataḥ pañcocyante | yathā saptabodhyaṅgāni kālābhisandhiṃ labdhvā caturdaśa bhavanti | tatrocyate asti kāyapraśrabdhiḥ asti cittapraśrabdhiriti | na tu vastuto 'sti kāyapraśrabdhiḥ | cittameva sukhitamiti [tat] kāyo 'pi vedayate | evaṃ prītirapi prathamataḥ kāyagatā prītisukhamityucyate | prītiḥ prathamalabdhalakṣaṇā sukhaṃ bhavati | paścātparaṃ prītirityāyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) If so, how is the first <s>dhyāna</s> called 'five-factored'? (Answer) It is called 'five' from the standpoint of time. Just as the seven factors of awakening, when distinguished by time, become fourteen. Therein it is said: 'There is bodily tranquility and there is mental tranquility.' But in reality there is no bodily tranquility. It is only because the mind is happy that the body too experiences [happiness]. Thus joy too — initially pertaining to the body — is called 'joyful pleasure' (<s>prītisukha</s>). Joy has the characteristic of being first obtained, and [then] becomes pleasure. Afterward, it further comes to be [called] 'joy.'

body.text: kālabhedāt | na hyasti pṛthak praśrabdhidharmaḥ | prītau jātamātrāyāṃ kāyacitte aduṣṭhule sukumāre dānte ca bhavata ityataḥ praśrabdhirityucyate | yathā rogiṇaścaturmahābhūtānāṃ nirodhaḥ, arogiṇaścaturmahābhūtānāmudayaḥ tadā ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sukhīti nāma | evaṃ praśrabdhirapi | praśamane 'pi praśrabdhirityuktam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- saṃskārāṇāmanupūrvanirodhaḥ- tathāhi- prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannasya vāk niruddhā bhavati | yāvannirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannasya saṃjñā vedanā ca niruddhā bhavati | iti | ato nāsti pṛthak praśrabdhidharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Because of the temporal distinction. For there is no separate <s>dharma</s> of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>). When joy has just arisen, body and mind become not coarse, become delicate and tamed — therefore it is called 'tranquility.' Just as for a sick person, there is the cessation of the four great elements; and for a healthy person, there is the arising of the four great elements — then this person is called 'happy.' So too with tranquility. Even in the sense of pacification, 'tranquility' is used. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The successive cessation of formations — thus, for one who has entered the first <s>dhyāna</s>, speech has ceased. Up to one who has entered the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), perception and feeling have ceased.' Therefore there is no separate <s>dharma</s> of tranquility.

body.text: yadi mataṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ vitarkavicārasamprayuktamiti tadapi na yuktam | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre- yadi yogāvacaraḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate | tadā vāk niruddhā bhavati iti vitarkavicārau ca vāco hetuḥ | kathaṃ vāco heturasti, vāk ca niruddhā bhavati | yadi mataṃ vitarkavicārau yadyapi vartete | vyavahāramātraṃ niruddhaṃ bhavatīti | tadā kasyacit kāmadhātukacittagatasya avyavahārakāle 'pi [viatarkavicāra]rodho bhavet |
body.translated_text: If you hold that the first <s>dhyāna</s> is conjoined with applied thought and sustained thought, that too is not valid. Why? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'If the <s>yogāvacara</s> enters the first <s>dhyāna</s>, then speech has ceased.' And applied thought and sustained thought are the cause of speech. How can the cause of speech exist while speech has ceased? If you hold that applied thought and sustained thought, though they exist, their expression alone has ceased — then for someone with a mind belonging to the desire realm, even at the time of non-expression, there would be cessation of applied thought and sustained thought [by the same logic].

body.text: (pṛ) prathamadhyāne vitarkavicārau na staḥ | āryastṛṣṇīṃbhāvaḥ syāt | bhavāṃstu dvitīyadhyānamāryatūṣṇīṃbhāvamāha | na prathamadhyānam | ato jñāyate prathamadhyāne vitarkavicārau syātām iti | (u) vitarkavicārapratyāsannatvānnāha āryatūṣṇīṃbhāva iti | na tu vitarkavicārasamprayuktatvāt | uktañca sūtre- prathamadhyānasya śabdaḥ kaṇṭaka iti | ato nāha tūṣṇībhāva iti | (pṛ) prathamadhyānasya kasmāt śabdaḥ kaṇṭako bhavati | (u) prathamadhyāne samādhigataṃ cittaṃ kusume salilavat peśalam | dvitīyadhyānādau samādhigataṃ cittaṃ sarjarasrasataruvat sudṛḍhan | sparśādayo 'pi prathamadhyānasya kaṇṭakāḥ | sparśasya prathamadhyānasyotthāpakatvāt | na tathā dvitīyadhyānādeḥ | kasmāt | prathamadhyāne pañcavijñānānāmavyupaśabhāt | dvitīyadhyānādau ca teṣāṃ vyupaśamāt ||
body.translated_text: (Question) In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, applied thought and sustained thought do not exist. Then there would be the noble silence (<s>āryatūṣṇīṃbhāva</s>). But you say the second <s>dhyāna</s> is the noble silence, not the first <s>dhyāna</s>. From this it is known that applied thought and sustained thought exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. (Answer) Because of the proximity of applied thought and sustained thought, [the first dhyāna] is not called 'noble silence.' It is not because it is conjoined with applied thought and sustained thought. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Sound is a thorn to the first <s>dhyāna</s>.' Therefore it is not called 'silence.' (Question) Why is sound a thorn to the first <s>dhyāna</s>? (Answer) In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the mind that has attained concentration is delicate like a flower on water. In the second <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond, the mind that has attained concentration is firmly established like sap in a <s>sarja</s> tree. Touch and the like too are thorns to the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Because touch can cause emergence from the first <s>dhyāna</s>. But not so from the second <s>dhyāna</s> onward. Why? Because in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the five consciousnesses have not been pacified. But in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond, they are pacified.

body.text: navānupūrva [vihāre]ṣu prathamadhyānavargaḥ pañcaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and sixty-fifth chapter, the Chapter on the First <s>Dhyāna</s> among the Nine Successive Abidings (<s>navānupūrvavihāra</s>).

body.text: 166 dvitīyadhyānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 166. Chapter on the Second <s>Dhyāna</s>.

body.text: punaśca yogāvacaraḥ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditation practitioner)

body.text: vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamāt adhyātmaṃ samprasādanaṃ cetasa ekotibhāvamavitarkamavicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyadhyānamupasampadya viharati | (pṛ) yadi vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamāt dvitīyadhyānam, tarhi prathamadhyānaṃ savitarkaṃ savicārameṣṭavyam | yathā dvitīyadhyāne prītirastīti vyupaśāntaprīti tṛtīyadhyānamityucyate | (u) yathā prathamadhyāne duḥkhendriye 'satyapi dvitīyadhyāne duḥkhendriyavyupaśama ucyate | tathedamapi | (pṛ) prathamadhyāne duḥkhendriye 'satyapi [pañca] vijñānāni santi | vijñānāni ca duḥkhendriyasyāśrayāḥ | ata ucyate prathamadhyāne duḥkhendriyasyāvyupaśamaḥ | (u) prathamadhyāne santyapi vijñānāni na duḥkhendriyasyāśrayā bhavanti | (pṛ)pañcavijñānasvabhāvo duḥkhendriyasyāśraya[tā] | svābhāvyātprathamaṃ dhyānaṃ saduḥkhamucyate | (u) tathā ce ddaurmanasyendriyaṃ manovijñānasvabhāvajamiti sarvatra bhavet | (pṛ) adhunā kasmāducyate prathamadhyāne duḥkhendriyavyupaśamaḥ | (u) prathamadhyānasamādhicittapratyāsannam | asamāhitacittaḥ kāmadhātukapratīsaṃyuktāni vijñānānyutpādayati | tatra duḥkhendriyaṃ bhavati | ato nocyate prathamadhyāne duḥkhe[ndriya]vyupaśamaḥ | (pṛ) tathā cet prathamadhyānamapi daurmanasyendriyapratyāsannam | tat daurmanasyendriyamapi vaktavyaṃ yadi dvitīyatṛtīyadhyānayorniruddham | (u) kāmāśrayaṃ daurmanasyendriyaṃ kāmaśrayaprītijananam | suviśuddhaprītilābhino 'viśuddhaprītirnirudhyate | ataḥ prathamadhyāne nāsti daurmanasyendriyam | asamādhiṃ niśritya duḥkhendriyamutpadyate | prathamadhyānasya vikṣiptacittapratyāsannatvāt na [tasya] vyupaśama ucyate | yathā tṛtīyadhyāne duḥkhaṃ nāsti | ucyate ca duḥkhasya sukhasya ca prahāṇāt caturthadhyānamupasampadya viharatīti | tathedamapi |
body.translated_text: through the subsiding of <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), with inner tranquility, with one-pointedness of mind, without <s>vitarka</s>, without <s>vicāra</s>, born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), with <s>prīti</s> (rapture) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness), enters and dwells in the second <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). (Question) If the second <s>dhyāna</s> arises from the subsiding of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, then the first <s>dhyāna</s> should be established as possessing <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. Just as because <s>prīti</s> exists in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, the third <s>dhyāna</s> is called 'with <s>prīti</s> subsided.' (Answer) Just as though the pain-faculty does not exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the subsiding of the pain-faculty is spoken of in the second <s>dhyāna</s> — so it is here also. (Question) Even though the pain-faculty does not exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the five <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) exist there. And the <s>vijñānas</s> are the supports of the pain-faculty. Therefore it is said that the pain-faculty has not subsided in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. (Answer) Even though the <s>vijñānas</s> exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, they are not supports of the pain-faculty. (Question) The nature of the five <s>vijñānas</s> is to be the support of the pain-faculty. By this inherent nature, the first <s>dhyāna</s> is called 'with pain.' (Answer) If so, then since the displeasure-faculty is born from the nature of <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness), it would exist everywhere. (Question) Then why is the subsiding of the pain-faculty spoken of in the first <s>dhyāna</s>? (Answer) Because it is proximate to the <s>samādhi</s>-mind of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. One whose mind is not concentrated produces <s>vijñānas</s> associated with the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm). There the pain-faculty exists. Therefore, the subsiding of the pain-faculty is not spoken of in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. (Question) If so, the first <s>dhyāna</s> is also proximate to the displeasure-faculty. Then the displeasure-faculty should also be stated as ceasing in the second and third <s>dhyānas</s>. (Answer) The displeasure-faculty is based on the <s>kāmadhātu</s> and generates joy based on the <s>kāmadhātu</s>. For one who has obtained thoroughly purified <s>prīti</s>, impure <s>prīti</s> ceases. Therefore, the displeasure-faculty does not exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. The pain-faculty arises depending on non-concentration. Because the first <s>dhyāna</s> is proximate to a distracted mind, the subsiding of that is not spoken of. Just as in the third <s>dhyāna</s> there is no pain, yet it is said 'through the abandoning of pain and happiness, one enters and dwells in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>' — so it is here also.

body.text: yogāvacaraḥ prathamadhyāne 'paripūrṇasamādhiḥ sadā vitarkavicārābhyāṃ vikṣipyata ityata ucyate dvitīdhyāne vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśama iti | adhyātmaṃ samprasādanamiti | dvitīyadhyāne nibhṛtaścittasamādhānādvikṣepaḥ sadā nāvakāśaṃ labhate | adhyātmamavikṣiptacittatvādadhyātmaṃ samprasādanamityākhyā | idaṃ dvitīyadhyānasya rūpam | cetasa ekotibhāvamavitarkamavicāramiti | cetasa ekotibhāvaścetasa
body.translated_text: The <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditation practitioner), having incomplete <s>samādhi</s> in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, is always disturbed by <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>; therefore it is said that in the second <s>dhyāna</s> there is the subsiding of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. 'Inner tranquility' means: in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, being composed, disturbance never finds opportunity due to mental concentration. Because the mind is undistracted inwardly, it is called 'inner tranquility.' This is the characteristic of the second <s>dhyāna</s>. 'One-pointedness of mind, without <s>vitarka</s>, without <s>vicāra</s>' means: one-pointedness of mind is the

body.text: ekasmin mārge viharaṇaṃ dhyānamityucyate | idamevādhyātmaṃ samprasādanam | etatsamādhilābhāt vitarkavicārau na bhavataḥ | na yathā prathamadhyāne caittā vitarkavicārasthāḥ | uta ucyate avitarkamavicāramiti |
body.translated_text: dwelling in a single path is called <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). This itself is 'inner tranquility.' From obtaining this <s>samādhi</s>, <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> do not arise. Not as in the first <s>dhyāna</s> where mental factors are based on <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. Therefore it is said 'without <s>vitarka</s>, without <s>vicāra</s>.'

body.text: samādhijaṃ prītisukhamiti | prathamadhyāne vivekātprītiṃ labhate | atra tu samādhipariniṣpattyā prītiṃ labhate | ata āha samādhijamiti | (pṛ) prathamadhyānagataprīteḥ dvitīyadhyānagataprīteśca ko bhedaḥ | (u) prathamadhyāne daurmanasyavyupaśamāt prītiḥ | dvītīyadhyāne duḥkhavyupaśamāt prītiḥ | prathamadhyāne prītiraviśuddhaprītivirodhitayā labhyate | yadyubhe api prīti tṛṣṇāpratyaye | tathāpi prathamadhyāne sātipeśalā |
body.translated_text: 'Born of <s>samādhi</s>, with <s>prīti</s> (rapture) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness)' means: in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, one obtains <s>prīti</s> from seclusion. But here, one obtains <s>prīti</s> through the perfection of <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore it says 'born of <s>samādhi</s>.' (Question) What is the difference between the <s>prīti</s> of the first <s>dhyāna</s> and the <s>prīti</s> of the second <s>dhyāna</s>? (Answer) In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>prīti</s> arises from the subsiding of displeasure. In the second <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>prīti</s> arises from the subsiding of pain. In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>prīti</s> is obtained in opposition to impure <s>prīti</s>. Even though both <s>prītis</s> have <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) as their condition, still in the first <s>dhyāna</s> it is exceedingly subtle.

body.text: (pṛ) etādṛśo 'rthaḥ kiṃ sāsravaḥ kimanāsravaḥ | (u) sarvaṃ sāsravam | ātmasaṃjñāyāṃ satyāmasti prītiḥ | yasyānāsravaṃ cittam | tasya nāstyātma[saṃjñā] | ātmano 'sattvānnāsti prītiḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) Is such a state <s>sāsrava</s> (with outflows) or <s>anāsrava</s> (without outflows)? (Answer) All is <s>sāsrava</s>. When the notion of self exists, there is <s>prīti</s>. For one whose mind is <s>anāsrava</s>, there is no notion of self. Because the self does not exist, there is no <s>prīti</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) asatyāsrave nāsti prītiritīdamapyayuktam | bhagavān saptasambodhyaṅgeṣu prītisambodhyaṅgamāha | prītisambodhyaṅgantu anāsravam | ato jñāuyate 'styanāsravā prītiriti | uktañca sūtre- prītimanaskasya kāyaḥ praśrabhyati | praśrabdhakāyaḥ sukhaṃ vedayate iti | yadi nāstyanāsravā prītiḥ | nāstyanāsravā praśrabdhiḥ nāstanāsravaṃ sukhamityapi bhavet | paramakuśaladharmacāriṇaḥ pariṣadgaṇān paśyato bhagavataḥ prītirbhavati | ato jñāyate 'styanāsravā prītiriti | (u) saptabhiḥ sambodhyaṅgairanāsravāṃ prītimadhigacchatīti tava[mata]midamayuktam | sambodhyaṅgaṃ dvividhaṃ sāsravamanāsravañceti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yasmin samaye yogāvacaro dharmaṃ śṛṇoti | asya pañca nīvaraṇāni tasmin samaye na bhavanti, saptabodhyaṅgāni ca tasmin samaye bhāvanāparipūriṃ gacchanti | sambodhiśca asaṃmbodhijñānasyākhyā | yadi sambodhāya bhavanti | aviśuddhādidharmāṇāmācaraṇaṃ sambodhyaṅgamucyeta | bhavānāha- nāstyanāsravā prītirityapi syāditi | pūrvaṃ prītau samutpannāyāṃ paścādanāsravaṃ yadyathābhūtadarśanaṃ pratilabhate | na ca sarvāḥ praśrabdhayaḥ prītiṃ pratītya bhavanti | yathā dvitīyadhyāne
body.translated_text: (Question) That there is no <s>prīti</s> when there are no <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) — this too is improper. The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) taught <s>prīti-sambodhyaṅga</s> (rapture as a factor of awakening) among the seven <s>sambodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening). And <s>prīti-sambodhyaṅga</s> is <s>anāsrava</s>. Therefore it is known that <s>anāsrava prīti</s> exists. And it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one whose mind has <s>prīti</s>, the body becomes tranquil. One whose body is tranquil experiences <s>sukha</s> (happiness).' If there is no <s>anāsrava prīti</s>, then there would be no <s>anāsrava praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility) and no <s>anāsrava sukha</s> either. When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, practitioner of the highest wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, sees the assemblies, <s>prīti</s> arises. Therefore it is known that <s>anāsrava prīti</s> exists. (Answer) That one attains <s>anāsrava prīti</s> through the seven <s>sambodhyaṅgas</s> — this view of yours is improper. The <s>sambodhyaṅgas</s> are of two kinds: <s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'At the time when a <s>yogāvacara</s> listens to the <s>Dharma</s>, the five <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances) do not exist at that time, and the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> reach fulfillment of cultivation at that time.' And <s>sambodhi</s> is the name for non-awakening knowledge. If they exist for the sake of <s>sambodhi</s>, then the practice of impure and other <s>dharmas</s> would also be called <s>sambodhyaṅga</s>. You said 'there would also be no <s>anāsrava prīti</s>' — but first, when <s>prīti</s> has arisen, afterwards one attains <s>anāsrava</s> true seeing. And not all <s>praśrabdhis</s> (tranquilities) arise dependent on <s>prīti</s>. Just as in the second <s>dhyāna</s>

body.text: prītirnāsti, asti ca praśrabdhiḥ | na vayaṃ brūmo jñānavinirmukto 'sti pṛthagvedanādharma iti | idamanāsravaṃ prathamataścittagataṃ sukhamityucyate | ato 'styanāsravaṃ sukham | na tu prītiṃ pratītya bhavati | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- kāyacittayordauṣṭhalyāpanayanaṃ praśrabdhiḥ | anāsrava[jñāna]pratilambhakāle kāyacittayordāntatvāt astyanāsravā praśrabdhiḥ | bhagavān sadopekṣācitte viharatītyata āha- asti bhagavataḥ prītiriti | idaṃ vastu prakāśayitavyam |
body.translated_text: <s>prīti</s> does not exist, yet <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility) exists. We do not say that apart from knowledge there exists a separate <s>dharma</s> of feeling. This <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free) <s>sukha</s> (happiness) is primarily called happiness belonging to the mind. Therefore <s>anāsrava sukha</s> exists, but it does not arise dependent on <s>prīti</s>. Furthermore, it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Praśrabdhi</s> is the removal of rigidity of body and mind.' At the time of attaining <s>anāsrava jñāna</s> (outflow-free knowledge), because body and mind are tamed, <s>anāsrava praśrabdhi</s> exists. The <s>Bhagavān</s> always dwells with a mind of equanimity — therefore it is said that the <s>Bhagavān</s> has <s>prīti</s>. This matter should be clarified.

body.text: yasya nāstyātmā | na tasyāsti prītiḥ | yadyarhato 'sti prītiḥ | daurmanasyamapi bhavet | vastutastu nāsti daurmanasyam | ato jñāyate nāsti prītiriti | (pṛ) yathā dvitīyadhyāye 'sti prītiḥ nāsti tu daurmanasyam | tathā arhato 'pi prītirasti na daurmanasyam | ko doṣaḥ | (u) sarveṣu dhyānasamādhiṣu asti daurmanasyaṃ yathā indriyārtheṣūcyate | daurmanasyaṃ prītiśca yāvadbhavāgraṃ[bhavati] | sukhaduḥkhe ca yāvaccatvāri dhyānāni kāyamanugacchataḥ | kiñca tṛtīyadhyānagataḥ prītervirāgādupekṣako viharatītyucyate | ato nāstyanāsravā prītiriti | yadyasti, kathaṃ virāgāditi vacanaṃ bhavet | anāsrave citte ca prīti rna bhavet | prītayaḥ sarvāḥ prajñaptisaṃjñāvikalpaṃ niśritya bhavanti |
body.translated_text: For one who has no self, there is no <s>prīti</s> (rapture). If an <s>Arhat</s> has <s>prīti</s>, then <s>daurmanasya</s> (displeasure) would also exist. But in reality, <s>daurmanasya</s> does not exist. Therefore it is known that <s>prīti</s> does not exist. (Question) Just as in the second <s>dhyāna</s> there is <s>prīti</s> but no <s>daurmanasya</s>, so too for the <s>Arhat</s> there is <s>prīti</s> but no <s>daurmanasya</s> — what is the fault? (Answer) In all <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhis</s> there is <s>daurmanasya</s>, just as it is said regarding the sense-objects. <s>Daurmanasya</s> and <s>prīti</s> extend up to the peak of existence. <s>Sukha</s> (happiness) and <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) accompany the body up through the four <s>dhyānas</s>. Furthermore, one who has attained the third <s>dhyāna</s> is said to dwell as an equanimous observer through detachment from <s>prīti</s>. Therefore <s>anāsrava prīti</s> does not exist. If it did exist, how could the statement 'through detachment' be made? And in an <s>anāsrava</s> mind, <s>prīti</s> would not arise. All <s>prītis</s> arise depending on conceptual designation and <s>saṃjñā-vikalpa</s> (notional discrimination).

body.text: (pṛ) tathā cet prathamadvitīyadhyānayornāstyanāsravā vedanā | uktaṃ hi sūtre- prathamadvitīyadhyānayoḥ kevalaṃ prītirasti na caitasikaṃ sukhamiti | idānīṃ prītirapi nāsti | kimasti punaḥ | (u) iyaṃ prītiḥ prītervirāgādityādi nānāsravaṃ dhyānamāha | kiñcitpunaḥ sūtramāha- anāsravaṃ dhyānam, yadyogāvacaro yadākāraṃ yadālambanaṃ prathamadhyānamupasampadya viharati | na tadākāraṃ tadālambanaṃ smarati | kintu paśyati prathamadhyānagatāni rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni rogato gaṇḍato yāvadanātmataḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) If so, then in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s> there is no <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free) feeling. For it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'In the first and second <s>dhyānas</s> there is only <s>prīti</s>, not mental <s>sukha</s> (happiness).' Now if <s>prīti</s> also does not exist, what then remains? (Answer) This <s>prīti</s> — 'through detachment from <s>prīti</s>' and so forth — does not refer to <s>anāsrava dhyāna</s>. Moreover, another <s>sūtra</s> states regarding <s>anāsrava dhyāna</s>: 'When a <s>yogāvacara</s> enters and dwells in the first <s>dhyāna</s> with whatever aspect and whatever object, he does not recall that aspect and that object. Rather, he sees the <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> as disease, as a boil, up to as non-self.'

body.text: (pṛ) rogato gaṇḍataḥ śalyato 'ghata ityetāni catvāri lokacaritāni nānāsravāṇi | ata idaṃ sūtraṃ pramāṇīkṛtya nānāsravaṃ sādhayituṃ śaknoṣi | (u) ime catvāra ākārā duḥkhasya nāmāntarāṇi | ato 'nāsravāṇi | (pṛ)śaikṣasyāpi kiṃ nāstyanāsravā prītiḥ | (u) mārgacittagatasya nāsti prītiḥ | vyavahāragatasya tvasti | aśaikṣasya sarvadā nāsti | (pṛ) uktaṃ hi sūtre- prītisukhacittena catvāri satyāni pratilabhata iti | kathamāha- nāstyanāsravā prītiriti | (u) anātmacittameva sukham |
body.translated_text: (Question) 'As disease, as a boil, as a thorn, as a misfortune' — these four are worldly conventions and are not <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free). Therefore you cannot use this <s>sūtra</s> as authority to establish that they are <s>anāsrava</s>. (Answer) These four aspects are alternative names for <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). Therefore they are <s>anāsrava</s>. (Question) Does a <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) also not have <s>anāsrava prīti</s>? (Answer) For one whose mind is on the path, there is no <s>prīti</s>. But for one engaged in conventional activity, there is. For an <s>aśaikṣa</s> (non-learner), there is never any. (Question) For it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'With a mind of <s>prīti</s> and <s>sukha</s>, one realizes the four truths.' How then can you say there is no <s>anāsrava prīti</s>? (Answer) The mind of non-self itself is <s>sukha</s>.

body.text: yogāvacaraḥ pratilabdhānātmacitto viparyayaṃ vināśayati | paramārthajñānāttu cittaṃ pramodyate | na pṛthagasti prītiḥ | kiñca tatsūtraṃ prakāśayati na prītyā paramārthajñānaṃ pratilabhata iti | ata evamucyate ||
body.translated_text: The <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditation practitioner), having obtained the mind of non-self, destroys <s>viparyaya</s> (wrong views). Through <s>paramārtha-jñāna</s> (ultimate knowledge), the mind rejoices. There is no separate <s>prīti</s> (rapture). Furthermore, that <s>sūtra</s> clarifies that one does not attain <s>paramārtha-jñāna</s> through <s>prīti</s>. Therefore it is stated thus.

body.text: dvitīyadhyānavargaḥ ṣaṭṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter on the second <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the one hundred and sixty-sixth.

body.text: 167 tṛtīyadhyānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 167. Chapter on the third <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).

body.text: prītyāśca virāgādupekṣako viharati smṛtaḥ samprajānan sukhañca kāyena pratisaṃvedayate yadāryā ācakṣante upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārīti tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati |
body.translated_text: Through detachment from <s>prīti</s> (rapture), one dwells as an equanimous observer, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences <s>sukha</s> (happiness) with the body. As the <s>Āryas</s> (Noble Ones) declare: 'Equanimous, mindful, dwelling in happiness' — one enters and dwells in the third <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmāt prītyāśca virāgāditi | (u) yogāvacaraḥ prītau paribhramediti virāgaḥ | prītiśceyaṃ saṃjñāvikalpajā, cañcalā pravṛttilakṣaṇā | prathamata ārabhya duḥkhānuyāyinī | hetunānena virāgaḥ | yogāvacaraḥ śāntaṃ tṛtīyadhyānaṃ labhamāno dvitīyadhyānaṃ prajahāti | prītijaṃ sukhañca mandam | prītivirāgajaṃ sukhaṃ gabhīram | yathā kaścit putrabhāryādibhiḥ sadā na prīto bhavati | prīteḥ saṃjñāvikalpajatvāt | sukhaṃ na saṃjñāvikalpajamiti sadā bhavati | tathā yogāvacaro 'pi prītiṃ prathamata āgatāṃ tu sukhaṃ manyate | paścāttu [tato] nirvidyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is it said 'through detachment from <s>prīti</s>'? (Answer) The <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditation practitioner) would be distracted by <s>prīti</s>, therefore there is detachment. And this <s>prīti</s> is born of <s>saṃjñā-vikalpa</s> (notional discrimination), is unstable, has the characteristic of activity. From the very beginning it is accompanied by <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). For this reason there is detachment. The <s>yogāvacara</s>, obtaining the peaceful third <s>dhyāna</s>, abandons the second <s>dhyāna</s>. The <s>sukha</s> (happiness) born of <s>prīti</s> is mild. The <s>sukha</s> born of detachment from <s>prīti</s> is profound. Just as someone is never always pleased with wife, children, and the like — because <s>prīti</s> is born of <s>saṃjñā-vikalpa</s>. But <s>sukha</s>, not being born of <s>saṃjñā-vikalpa</s>, is constant. So too the <s>yogāvacara</s> at first considers <s>prīti</s> to be <s>sukha</s>, but later becomes disenchanted with it.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi kaściddharmapīḍitaḥ, sa tu śītaṃ sukhaṃ manyate | yogāvacaraḥ kena duḥkhena pīḍitaḥ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ sukhaṃ manyate | (u) dvitīyadhyāne prītiścañcalasaṃjñoditā kaṇṭakāhativat, yogāvacaro 'nayā prītyā pīḍita iti aprītisamādhau sukhasaṃjñāṃ karoti | (pṛ) dharmaduḥkhāstitvavaśāt śītaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati | yadi dharmavivikto bhavati | na tadā śītaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati | yogāvacaraḥ prītiviviktaḥ kasmātpunastṛtīyadhyāne sukhasaṃjñāṃ karoti | (u) sukhajananaṃ dvitīyadhyānaṃ kadācit duḥkhavartanātsambhavati | yathā dharmaduḥkhinaḥ śītaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati | kadācit duḥkhavivekāt sambhavati | yathā vipriyavivekaḥ | yathā bhagavān kauśāmbibhikṣuvivikta āha- ahaṃ sukhīti | tathedamapi calasaṃjñāviviktaḥ tṛtīyadhyāne sukhasaṃjñā karoti | yathā pañcakāmaguṇavivekātprathamaṃ dhyānaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: (Question) If someone is afflicted by a <s>dharma</s> (condition), he considers cold to be <s>sukha</s> (happiness). By what <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) is the <s>yogāvacara</s> afflicted that he considers the third <s>dhyāna</s> to be <s>sukha</s>? (Answer) In the second <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>prīti</s> (rapture) arises with unstable notions, like being struck by a thorn; the <s>yogāvacara</s>, afflicted by this <s>prīti</s>, generates the perception of <s>sukha</s> in the <s>samādhi</s> without <s>prīti</s>. (Question) Due to the existence of <s>dharma</s>-suffering, cold becomes <s>sukha</s>. If one is free from that <s>dharma</s>, then cold is no longer <s>sukha</s>. When the <s>yogāvacara</s> is free from <s>prīti</s>, why does he still generate the perception of <s>sukha</s> in the third <s>dhyāna</s>? (Answer) The second <s>dhyāna</s>, which produces <s>sukha</s>, sometimes involves painful states. Just as for one afflicted by a <s>dharma</s>-condition, cold becomes <s>sukha</s>. Sometimes it arises from separation from pain — just as separation from what is unpleasant is pleasant. Just as when the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was separated from the quarreling monks of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, he said: 'I am happy.' So too here, being separated from unstable notions, one generates the perception of <s>sukha</s> in the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Just as the first <s>dhyāna</s> is <s>sukha</s> through separation from the five strands of sensual pleasure.

body.text: upekṣaka iti | prītervirāgāditi śāntaṃ bhavati | yogāvacaraḥ pūrvaṃ prītisaṃsaktamanā bahudhā vikṣiptaḥ | idānīṃ tato virāgāccittaṃ śāmyati | ata upekṣaka ityucyate | smṛtaḥ samprajānan iti | prītyādīnavādetadubhayaṃ sadopanīyate | na tena prītirāgatā prabhinnā bhavati | kiñca smṛta iti prīterādīnavaṃ smarati | samprajānān prītāvādīnavaṃ paśyati | sukhañca kāyena pratisaṃvedayata iti | prītiviraktasyopekṣakasyopekṣaiva sukham | aniñjanānīṣatvāt | nedaṃ sukhaṃ saṃjñāvikalpajam | ataḥ sukhañca kāyena pratisaṃvedayata iti nāma | yattadāryā ācakṣanta upekṣaka iti | ācakṣaṇaṃ nāma laukikānanusṛtya sukhamiti kathanam | yathācakṣante naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamiti | anāsaktacittatvāt upekṣaka iti | smṛtimān sukhavihārīti | puruṣo 'yaṃ prajñāyopekṣate yat prītāvādīnavaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirvidyata ityataḥ sūpekṣāṃ labhate | kalyāṇasmaraṇaṃ yat prītāvādīnavasmaraṇam | tatrāpi vaktavyaṃ samprajānan iti | smṛtyā sāhacaryāt nocyate | sukhamiti paramasukham | ata āryā ācakṣanta upekṣaka iti |
body.translated_text: "Equanimous" (<s>upekṣaka</s>) — because of detachment from <s>prīti</s> (joy), [the mind] becomes tranquil. The <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator), previously with a mind attached to <s>prīti</s>, was distracted in many ways. Now, through detachment from that, the mind becomes calm. Therefore he is called "equanimous" (<s>upekṣaka</s>). "Mindful and clearly comprehending" (<s>smṛtaḥ samprajānan</s>) — both these [qualities] are always brought in to counteract the faults of <s>prīti</s>. It is not that <s>prīti</s> once arrived is thereby destroyed. Furthermore, "mindful" (<s>smṛta</s>) means he remembers the faults of <s>prīti</s>; "clearly comprehending" (<s>samprajānan</s>) means he sees the dangers in <s>prīti</s>. "And he experiences <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) with the body" — for the equanimous one who is detached from <s>prīti</s>, equanimity itself is <s>sukha</s>, because there is no agitation or longing. This <s>sukha</s> is not born of conceptual discrimination (<s>saṃjñāvikalpa</s>). Therefore it is called "he experiences <s>sukha</s> with the body." "That which the Noble Ones (<s>āryāḥ</s>) declare as 'equanimous'" — this declaration means speaking of <s>sukha</s> in conformity with worldly convention, just as they declare "the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception" (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). Because of non-attachment of the mind, [he is called] "equanimous." "Mindful, dwelling in <s>sukha</s>" — this person through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is equanimous, because having seen the faults in <s>prīti</s>, he becomes disenchanted, and thereby attains good equanimity. Wholesome recollection (<s>kalyāṇasmaraṇa</s>) is the recollection of the faults in <s>prīti</s>. There too, "clearly comprehending" should be stated, but it is not mentioned because of its constant association with mindfulness. "<s>Sukha</s>" means the supreme <s>sukha</s>. Therefore the Noble Ones declare [him] "equanimous."

body.text: (pṛ) tṛtīyadhyāne 'sti sukhapratisaṃvedanam | kasmādāha- upekṣāsukhamiti | (u) nāhamasmin śāstre vadāmi vedanāvyatiriktaṃ pṛthagasti upekṣāsukhamiti | sukhaprītisaṃvedanamevopekṣāsukham | (pṛ) tathā cet caturthadhyāne sukhapratisaṃvedanaṃ vaktavyam | upekṣāyāḥ sattvāt | (u) caturthadhyāne 'pi sukhapratisaṃvedanamastīti vadāmi | kintu tṛtīyadhyānasukhasya prahāṇādevamucyate | (pṛ) yadi sukhapratisaṃvedanasamanvitam | kasmāt | prathamadvitīyadhyānayoḥ prītirityākhyā | tṛtīyadhyāne sukhamiti | (u) saṃjñāvikalpasya sattvāt prītiḥ | tasyābhāvāt sukham | yogāvacarasya tṛtīyadhyāne samāhitacittavṛttitvena saṃjñāvikalpasyābhāvāt sukhamityucyate | tṛtīyadhyānapravṛttyupaśamasya lābhācca sukhamityucyate | yatā iñjanamīṣaṇacittamāryā duḥkhamiti vadanti | iñjanaṃ nāma vikalpasyābhidhānam | tadeva sukham ||
body.translated_text: (Question) In the third <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption) there is the experience of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure). Why then does [the sūtra] say "the <s>sukha</s> of equanimity" (<s>upekṣāsukha</s>)? (Answer) I do not say in this treatise that there exists a separate "<s>sukha</s> of equanimity" apart from <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). The experience of pleasurable joy is itself the <s>sukha</s> of equanimity. (Question) If so, then in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> too, the experience of <s>sukha</s> should be stated, since <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) exists there. (Answer) I do say that the experience of <s>sukha</s> exists in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> as well. But it is expressed this way because of the abandonment of the <s>sukha</s> of the third <s>dhyāna</s>. (Question) If it is accompanied by the experience of <s>sukha</s>, why is it called "<s>prīti</s>" (joy) in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, but "<s>sukha</s>" in the third <s>dhyāna</s>? (Answer) Because of the presence of conceptual discrimination (<s>saṃjñāvikalpa</s>), it is <s>prīti</s>; because of the absence of that, it is <s>sukha</s>. Since in the third <s>dhyāna</s> the <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator) has concentrated mental activity and conceptual discrimination is absent, it is called <s>sukha</s>. Also because of the attainment of the cessation of the activity of the third <s>dhyāna</s>, it is called <s>sukha</s>. As the Noble Ones (<s>āryāḥ</s>) say that agitation, that is, the slight [movement of] mind, is <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) — "agitation" (<s>iñjana</s>) is a designation for conceptual discrimination (<s>vikalpa</s>). The absence of that itself is <s>sukha</s>.

body.text: tṛtīyadhyānavargaḥ saptaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter on the Third <s>Dhyāna</s>, the one hundred and sixty-seventh.

body.text: 168 caturthadhyānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 168. Chapter on the Fourth <s>Dhyāna</s>.

body.text: sukhasya ca duḥkhasya ca prahāṇātpūrvameva saumanasyadaurmanasyānāmastaṅgamādaduḥkhamasukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati | (pṛ) yadi pūrvameva
body.translated_text: "With the abandonment of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) and <s>duḥkha</s> (pain), and with the previous disappearance of <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) and <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental pain), [the meditator] enters and dwells in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), which is neither painful nor pleasurable (<s>aduḥkha-asukha</s>), purified by <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) and <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness)." (Question) If previously

body.text: duḥkhasya prahāṇam | kasmādatrocyate | yadyavaśyaṃ vaktumiṣṭam, vaktavyaṃ pūrvameva prahāṇāditi | yathā pūrvameva saumanasyadaurmanasyānāmastaṅgamāditi | (u) caturthadhyānamaniñjanam | tadāniñjanalakṣaṇasādhanāyocyate nāsti caturthī vedaneti | kasmāt | iñjanaṃ nāma kampanārambhaḥ | yogāvacarasya sukhasukhābhidrutasya cittamiñjate | citta iñjite rāgadveṣau bhavataḥ | sukhasya duḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt cittaṃ neñjate |
body.translated_text: the abandonment of <s>duḥkha</s> (pain) [has already occurred], why is it stated here? If it must necessarily be stated, it should say "with the previous abandonment," just as it says "with the previous disappearance of <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) and <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental pain)." (Answer) The fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is free from agitation (<s>aniñjana</s>). To establish the characteristic of non-agitation, it is said that the fourth <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) does not exist. Why? "Agitation" (<s>iñjana</s>) means the onset of trembling. When the <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator) is assailed by <s>sukha</s>, the mind is agitated. When the mind is agitated, <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) arise. With the abandonment of <s>sukha</s> and <s>duḥkha</s>, the mind is not agitated.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi caturthadhyānaṃ hitatamaṃ vedyate | kasmātsukhamiti nocyate | (u) vedanāyā astaṅgamādaduḥkhamasukhamityucyate | yatredaṃ sukhamiti cittaṃ smarati prajānāti | tat sukhamityucyate | tṛtīyadhyānakasukhaviviktasya caturthadhyānasya lābhānna sukhamiti gaṇyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) If the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is experienced as most beneficial, why is it not called "<s>sukha</s>" (pleasure)? (Answer) Because of the disappearance of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), it is called "neither painful nor pleasurable" (<s>aduḥkha-asukha</s>). Where the mind remembers and cognizes "this is <s>sukha</s>," that is called <s>sukha</s>. Since the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is separated from the <s>sukha</s> of the third <s>dhyāna</s> and is attained [beyond it], it is not reckoned as <s>sukha</s>.

body.text: upekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhamiti | atropekṣā pariśuddhā | anīṣaṇatvāt | triṣu dhyāneṣvasti īṣaṇaṃ yadidaṃ sukhamiti | asmiṃśca dhyāne smṛtirapi pariśuddhā | kasmāt | tṛtīyadhyāne sukhāsaṅgitvāt smṛtirvyākulā | caturthadhyānaṃ prāpya sukharāgasya prahāṇāt smṛtiḥ pariśuddhā |
body.translated_text: "Purified by <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) and <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness)" — here <s>upekṣā</s> is purified because there is no longing. In the [first] three <s>dhyānas</s> there is longing, namely [the thought] "this is <s>sukha</s>." In this <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is also purified. Why? Because in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, mindfulness is disturbed due to attachment to <s>sukha</s>. Upon attaining the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, with the abandonment of the attachment to <s>sukha</s>, mindfulness becomes purified.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmāccaturthadhyāne na samprajanyamuktam | (u) yadyuktaṃ smṛtipariśuddhamiti | samprajanyamuktameveti veditavyam | anayordvayordharmayormitho 'vyabhicārāt | kiñcāyaṃ dhyānasamādhimārgaḥ na samprajanyamārgaḥ | samprajanyasya prajñā[rūpa]tvānnocyate | tṛtīyadhyānasya caramabhāge 'pi nocyate samprajanyam | upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārīti kevalamucyate | nocyate upekṣakaḥ smṛtisamprajanyavān sukhavihārīti | smṛtiriyaṃ dhyānasamādhiṃ sādhayati | yadi kasyacit samādhirasiddhā, [tasya] saṃjñāmādāya smṛtiḥ sādhayati | tena kevalamucyate | uttamaguṇamupekṣāṃ prāptasya nādhamaguṇo manaskāro 'pekṣyate | ataḥ samprajanyaṃ nocyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is <s>samprajanya</s> (clear comprehension) not mentioned in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>? (Answer) When "purified by mindfulness" is stated, it should be understood that <s>samprajanya</s> is implied, because these two <s>dharmas</s> are mutually inseparable. Moreover, this is the path of <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration), not the path of <s>samprajanya</s>. Because <s>samprajanya</s> has the nature of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), it is not mentioned. Even in the final stage of the third <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samprajanya</s> is not mentioned — it simply says "equanimous, mindful, dwelling in <s>sukha</s>" and does not say "equanimous, possessing mindfulness and clear comprehension, dwelling in <s>sukha</s>." This mindfulness accomplishes the <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhi</s>. If someone's <s>samādhi</s> is not accomplished, mindfulness accomplishes it by taking hold of the concept. Therefore only [mindfulness] is stated. For one who has attained the supreme quality of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), an inferior quality of mental attention is not required. Therefore <s>samprajanya</s> is not mentioned.

body.text: (pṛ) aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā avidyāṅgam | caturthadhyāne bhūyasā samprajanyaviruddham | ato nocyate samprajanyam | (u) tathā cet aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā nānāsravā syāt | sukhavedanāyāḥ kāmāṅgatvāt | na ca [sā]nāsravā | (pṛ) tṛtīyadhyāne svabhūmidoṣavirodhāyocyate samprajanyam | parabhūmidoṣavirodhāya cocyate smṛtiḥ | caturthadhyāne svabhūmirnaivaṃ duṣṭetyatyato nocyate samprajanyam | (u) caturthadhyāne 'pi asti kāmādidoṣaḥ | ato vaktavyaṃ samprajanyam | atra kāmadoṣo 'tisūkṣmaḥ duravabodhaḥ ato 'vaśyaṃ vaktavyaṃ syāt | anyabhūmau vaktavyamapi nocyate | ato jñāyate yathāsmatprativacanaṃ syāditi |
body.translated_text: (Question) The neither-painful-nor-pleasurable <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) is a factor of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, [this] largely contradicts <s>samprajanya</s> (clear comprehension). Therefore <s>samprajanya</s> is not mentioned. (Answer) If so, then the neither-painful-nor-pleasurable <s>vedanā</s> would not be free from <s>āsravas</s> (defilements). Since pleasurable <s>vedanā</s> is a factor of <s>kāma</s> (sensual desire), yet it is not [said to be] with defilements. (Question) In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samprajanya</s> is stated to counteract the faults of one's own level, and <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is stated to counteract the faults of other levels. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, one's own level is not thus corrupted, so <s>samprajanya</s> is not mentioned. (Answer) In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> too there are faults such as <s>kāma</s> (sensual desire). Therefore <s>samprajanya</s> should be stated. Here the fault of <s>kāma</s> is extremely subtle and difficult to comprehend, so it should necessarily be stated. Even in other levels where it should be stated, it is not. Therefore, it is known that [the explanation] should be as I have answered.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmāccaturthadhyāna āśvāsapraśvāsanirodhaḥ | (u) praśvāsaḥ kāyaṃ cittañcāśrayate | kenedaṃ jñāyate | yadā cittaṃ sūkṣmaṃ, tadā śvāso 'pi sūkṣmaḥ | caturthadhyāne cittamacalamityata āśvāsapraśvāsau niruddhau | yathā kaścit paramaklānto bhāraṃ vahati | parvataṃ vā ārohati tadāśvāsaḥ sthūlo bhavati | śvasanakāle [punaḥ] sūkṣmaḥ | tathā caturthadhyāne 'pyevamacalasaṃjñayā cittamupaśāntamityata āśvāsapraśvāsau niruddhau | kecidvadanti yoginaścaturthadhyānakacaturmahābhūtalābhitayā kāyagataromakūpāḥ saṃvṛtāḥ | ataḥ śvāso niruddha iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | annapānarasapravāhaḥ kāyamabhivyāpnoti | yadi romakūpāḥ saṃvṛtāḥ, na samudācaret | vastutastu na sambhavati | ato jñāyate caturthadhyānacittabalameva śvāsanirodhakamiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is there cessation of inhalation and exhalation (<s>āśvāsa-praśvāsa</s>) in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>? (Answer) Exhalation depends on the body and the mind. How is this known? When the mind is subtle, the breath is also subtle. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, the mind is unmoving, therefore inhalation and exhalation cease. Just as when someone extremely exhausted carries a heavy load or climbs a mountain, the breathing becomes coarse, but at the time of [normal] breathing it is subtle — similarly in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, because the mind has become tranquil through the perception of immovability, inhalation and exhalation cease. Some say that because the <s>yogin</s> (practitioner) in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> attains the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements), the pores of the body are closed, and therefore breath ceases. That is incorrect. Why? The flow of the essence of food and drink pervades the body. If the pores were closed, [this flow] would not occur. But in reality, that does not happen. Therefore it is known that it is the power of the mind in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> alone that causes the cessation of breath.

body.text: (pṛ) caturthadhyāne nāsti sukhā vedanā | tatra kathamasti tṛṣṇānuśayaḥ | uktaṃ hi sūtre- sukhavedanāyāṃ tṛṣṇānuśaya iti | (u) tatrāsti sūkṣmā sukhā vedanā | audārikasukhaprahāṇātparamucyate aduḥkhamasukhamiti | yathā samīraṇaprakampitapradīpaḥ | yadi nigūḍhagṛhe nikṣipyate | tadā na kampate | tatrāvaśyamasti khalu sūkṣmo vātaḥ | audārikavātābhāvāttu na kampate | tathā caturthadhyāne 'pyasti sūkṣmaṃ sukham | audārikasukhaduḥkhaprahāṇādaduḥkhamasukhamityākhyāyate ||
body.translated_text: (Question) In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> there is no pleasurable <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). How then can there be a latent tendency of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) there? For the <s>sūtra</s> states: "In pleasurable <s>vedanā</s>, the latent tendency of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> [exists]." (Answer) There exists a subtle pleasurable <s>vedanā</s> there. Because of the abandonment of gross <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), it is called "neither painful nor pleasurable" (<s>aduḥkha-asukha</s>). Just as a lamp shaken by the wind — if it is placed in a sheltered room, it does not flicker. Yet there certainly exists a subtle breeze there; but because of the absence of a strong wind, it does not flicker. Similarly, in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> too there exists a subtle <s>sukha</s>. Because of the abandonment of gross <s>sukha</s> and <s>duḥkha</s>, it is designated as "neither painful nor pleasurable."

body.text: caturthadhyānavargo 'ṣṭaṣaṣṭhyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter on the Fourth <s>Dhyāna</s>, the one hundred and sixty-eighth.

body.text: 169 ākāśānantyāyatanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 169. Chapter on the <s>Ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (Sphere of the Infinity of Space).

body.text: sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt pratighasaṃjñānāmastaṅgamāt nānātvasaṃjñānāmamanaskārā danantam ākāśam ityākāśānantyāyatanamupasampadya viharati | rūpasaṃjñā nāma rūparasagandhasparśasaṃjñāḥ | yogāvacaraḥ kasmāt[tāḥ] samatikrāmati | yadeṣu rūpeṣu pratighaḥ antarāyaḥ | nānātvasaṃjñā yat ghaṇṭābheryādayaḥ | etāḥ saṃjñā vividhakleśānāṃ vividhakarmaṇāṃ vividhaduḥkhānāṃ hetavaḥ | ato hetoḥ samatikrāmati | sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikrāntasya
body.translated_text: "By completely transcending perceptions of form (<s>rūpasaṃjñā</s>), with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance (<s>pratighasaṃjñā</s>), by not attending to perceptions of diversity (<s>nānātvasaṃjñā</s>), [thinking] 'space is infinite,' one enters and dwells in the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of the infinity of space)." Perceptions of form (<s>rūpasaṃjñā</s>) are the perceptions of form, taste, smell, and touch. Why does the <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator) transcend these? Because in these forms there is resistance (<s>pratigha</s>), [which is] an obstruction. Perceptions of diversity (<s>nānātvasaṃjñā</s>) are [perceptions of things] such as bells, drums, and the like. These perceptions are causes of various <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), various <s>karmas</s> (actions), and various <s>duḥkhas</s> (sufferings). For this reason, [the meditator] transcends them. When one who has completely transcended perceptions of form

body.text: pratighasaṃjñā nirudhyate | pratighasaṃjñānirodhe nānātvasaṃjñā na bhavati | tatra saṃkṣepānnoktam asya samatikramādasya nirodha iti |
body.translated_text: perceptions of resistance (<s>pratighasaṃjñā</s>) cease. With the cessation of perceptions of resistance, perceptions of diversity (<s>nānātvasaṃjñā</s>) do not arise. There, in brief, it is stated that with the transcendence of one, the other ceases.
