body.text: kecidāhuḥ- sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñeti cakṣurvijñānāśritā saṃjñā iti | pratighasaṃjñeti śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyavijñānāśritā saṃjñā | nānātvasaṃjñeti manovijñānāśritā saṃjñā | iti | idamayuktam | kasmāt | pratighasaṃjñā nirudhyata iti vadato rūpaṃ saṅgrahītameva | kasmāt pṛthagucyate | rūpasaṃjñāṃ pratighasaṃjñāñca vinā nāsti pṛthaṅmanovijñānāśritaṃ rūpam | ato na vaktavyaṃ pṛthaṅ nānātvasaṃjñeti | iti yathāpūrvaṃ vaktavyam |
body.translated_text: Some say: "Perceptions of form" (<s>rūpasaṃjñā</s>) means perception dependent on eye-consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>). "Perceptions of resistance" (<s>pratighasaṃjñā</s>) means perception dependent on ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness. "Perceptions of diversity" (<s>nānātvasaṃjñā</s>) means perception dependent on mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>). This is incorrect. Why? When one says "perceptions of resistance cease," form (<s>rūpa</s>) is already included. Why then is it stated separately? Apart from perceptions of form and perceptions of resistance, there is no separate form dependent on mind-consciousness. Therefore one should not separately state "perceptions of diversity." Thus it should be explained as [we have done] previously.

body.text: ākāśānantyāyatanamupasampadya viharatīti | yogāvacaraḥ rūpasaṃjñābhibhavapariśrāntatvādākāśānantyāyatanaṃ bhāvayati | antaścakṣurghrāṇagrīvādyākāśasaṃjñāṃ gṛhṇāti | bahiḥ kūpaguhādvārāntarvṛkṣavāṭikādyākāśasaṃjñāṃ gṛhṇāti | kiñcāyaṃ kāyo maraṇavipannaḥ smaśānāgninā dagdhaḥ praṇaśyati | ato jñāyate kāyo 'yaṃ pūrvaṃ sākāśa iti |
body.translated_text: "One enters and dwells in the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of the infinity of space)" — the <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator), being exhausted from overcoming perceptions of form, cultivates the sphere of the infinity of space. Internally, he apprehends the perception of space in the eyes, nose, throat, and so forth. Externally, he apprehends the perception of space in wells, caves, doorways, inside trees, enclosures, and the like. Moreover, this body, destroyed by death, is burned by the cremation fire and perishes. From this it is known that this body was previously [pervaded by] space.

body.text: (pṛ) ayamākāśasamādhiḥ kimālambanena bhavati | (u) ādita ākāśālambanaḥ svīyaskandhālambanaḥ parakīyaskandhālambanaśca siddho bhavati | kasmāt | karuṇāśīrṣaka evaṃ cintayati- sattvā dayanīyā rūpasaṃjñāpīḍitā iti | (pṛ) samādhirayaṃ kaṃ sattvamavalambate | (u) sarvasattvānavalambate | (pṛ) yogāvacaro 'yaṃ rūpasaṃjñāviviktaḥ | kathaṃ rūpasattvānavalambate | (u) ayaṃ rūpamavalambate | rūpe tu cittaṃ na suprabuddhaṃ nābhiraktaṃ nābhyāsaktam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- āryaḥ pañcakāmaguṇān dṛṣṭvā saṃsmaran na tatrābhinandati na prabodhayati nādhyavasāya tiṣṭhati | tato bhīto nivartate | yathā tāpāt carmacchedaḥ | nirvāṇamanusmarataścittaṃ tatra suprabuddhaṃ bhavati iti | evamayamapi rūpamavalambamāno na [tatrā]bhinandyādhyavasāya tiṣṭhati | yathā ca yogāvacaro rūpasaṃjñāvivikto 'pi ākāśāntena caturthadhyānamavalambate | yathā arūpasamādhiranāsravaṃ rūpamabalambate | na tatra doṣo 'sti | akleśāyatanatvāt | tathānyadapi syāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) On what object does this space-<s>samādhi</s> (concentration) depend? (Answer) Initially it depends on the object of space, on one's own <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), and on the <s>skandhas</s> of others — thus it is established. Why? One who has compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) as the chief [motivation] thinks thus: "Beings are pitiable, tormented by perceptions of form." (Question) What being does this <s>samādhi</s> take as its support? (Answer) It takes all beings as its support. (Question) This <s>yogāvacara</s> (meditator) is separated from perceptions of form. How then does he take as support beings who have form? (Answer) He does take form as support, but the mind is not fully awakened toward form, not delighted, not attached. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: "The Noble One (<s>ārya</s>), having seen and recollecting the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>pañcakāmaguṇa</s>), does not rejoice in them, does not arouse [attachment], does not remain fixated upon them. He turns away from them, frightened. Just as skin shrinks from heat." When recollecting <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the mind becomes fully awakened toward it. Similarly, this one too, while taking form as support, does not rejoice and remain fixated upon it. And just as the <s>yogāvacara</s>, though separated from perceptions of form, takes the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> as support through the medium of space; and just as the formless <s>samādhi</s> takes as support the undefiled form — there is no fault in that, because it is not a basis of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements). Likewise should other [cases] also be understood.

body.text: (pṛ) ākāśaṃ rūpāyatanasvabhāvam | kathamidamālambya rūpasaṃjñāḥ samatikrāmati | (u) samādhirayamasaṃskṛtākāśāvalambitvāt rūpāṇi samatikrāmati | (pṛ) samādhirayaṃ nāsaṃskṛtamākāśamavalambate | kasmāt | asmin samādhyupāye cakṣurādimadhya[gata]mākāśamuktam | ato jñāyate saṃskṛtamākāśamavalambata iti | na coktaṃ sūtre asaṃskṛtākāśasya lakṣaṇam | saṃskṛtākāśalakṣaṇamatramuktaṃ yatra rūpaṃ nāsti tadākāśamiti | ato nāsaṃskṛtamākāśam | (u) na rūpasvabhāvāmākāśamucyate | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre ākāśamarūpamadṛśyamapratighamiti | (pṛ) asti punaḥ sūtravacanam- ālokaṃ pratītyākāśaṃ jānīma iti | na rūpaṃ vihāyāstyanyo dharma ālokaṃ pratītya jñāpyaḥ | (u) rūpābhāva ākāśa ityucyate | rūpāṇyālokena jñāpyāni | ata ālokaṃ pratītya rūpābhāvo jñāyate | natvākāśamasti |
body.translated_text: (Question) <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) has the nature of the <s>rūpāyatana</s> (form sense-base). How does one transcend the <s>rūpasaṃjñās</s> (perceptions of form) by taking this as an object? (Answer) This <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) transcends forms because it takes unconditioned <s>ākāśa</s> (space) as its object. (Question) This <s>samādhi</s> does not take unconditioned <s>ākāśa</s> as its object. Why? In the method of this <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>ākāśa</s> situated between the eye and other [sense-faculties] is spoken of. From this it is known that it takes conditioned <s>ākāśa</s> as its object. Moreover, the characteristic of unconditioned <s>ākāśa</s> is not stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. The characteristic of conditioned <s>ākāśa</s> is stated here as 'where there is no form, that is <s>ākāśa</s>.' Therefore there is no unconditioned <s>ākāśa</s>. (Answer) <s>Ākāśa</s> is not said to have the nature of form. Why? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> that '<s>ākāśa</s> is formless, invisible, and non-resistant.' (Question) But there is a <s>sūtra</s> statement: 'Depending on light, we know <s>ākāśa</s>.' Apart from form, there is no other <s>dharma</s> that can be known depending on light. (Answer) The absence of form is called <s>ākāśa</s>. Forms are known through light. Therefore, depending on light, the absence of form is known — but <s>ākāśa</s> does not [positively] exist.

body.text: tamasyapi ākāśaṃ jñāyate | andho hastenāpi ākāśaṃ jānāti | daṇḍenāpi ākāśamidamiti jānāti | ato jñāyate ākāśaṃ na rūpasvabhāvamiti | na rūpamebhiḥ pratyayairjñāpyate | rūpamidañca sapratigham | ākāśamapratigham | ānyādiḥ rūpāṇyatyantaṃ kṣapayati | natvākāśam | yadyākāśaṃ kṣīyate, kimātmakaṃ bhavet | (pṛ) rūpasyotpādesatyākāśamastameti | yathā bhittāvudbhūtāyāṃ na punarākāśamasti | (u) tatra rūpamutpannam | nānena rūpeṇa yatkiñcit kṣīyate | kasmāt | rūpābhāvo hyākāśam | nahyabhāvaḥ punarabhāvaḥ kartuṃ śakyaḥ | ato na rūpākāśaṃ kṣapayati | bhavānāha- ākāśaṃ rūpamiti | na tatrāstikāraṇaṃ yenedaṃ rūpaṃ bhavet | (pṛ) paśyāmaḥ khalu dvārādāvākāśam | pratyakṣadṛṣṭe na kāraṇāpekṣā | (u) ākāśaṃ na pratyakṣadṛśyamiti pūrvameva dūṣitatvāt- yat tamasyapi jñāpyamityādi |
body.translated_text: Even in darkness, <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is known. A blind person knows <s>ākāśa</s> even by hand. One knows 'this is <s>ākāśa</s>' even by a stick. From this it is known that <s>ākāśa</s> does not have the nature of form. Form is not known by these conditions. Moreover, this form is resistant, while <s>ākāśa</s> is non-resistant. Fire and the like completely destroy forms, but not <s>ākāśa</s>. If <s>ākāśa</s> were destroyed, what would its nature be? (Question) When form arises, <s>ākāśa</s> ceases to exist, just as when a wall has appeared, there is no longer <s>ākāśa</s> there. (Answer) There, form has arisen. Nothing whatsoever is destroyed by this form. Why? Because <s>ākāśa</s> is the absence of form. An absence cannot be made into another absence. Therefore form does not destroy <s>ākāśa</s>. You say '<s>ākāśa</s> is form.' There is no cause there by which this would be form. (Question) We indeed see <s>ākāśa</s> in doorways and such. When something is seen by direct perception, there is no need for a cause. (Answer) That <s>ākāśa</s> is not directly perceptible has already been refuted previously — by the argument that it is known even in darkness, and so forth.

body.text: (pṛ) yadyākāśaṃ na rūpam | ko dharma idaṃ bhavati | (u) abhāvadharma ākāśam | yatra[rūpaṃ] nāstīti vacanam tatrākāśaṃ bhavati | (pṛ) uktañca sūtre- ṣaḍ dhāturayaṃ puruṣakāya iti | kiñcāha- ākāśamadṛśyamarūpamapratighamiti | yadyabhāvadharmaḥ,
body.translated_text: (Question) If <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is not form, what <s>dharma</s> is it? (Answer) <s>Ākāśa</s> is a <s>dharma</s> of absence. The statement 'where there is no form' — there <s>ākāśa</s> exists. (Question) It is also stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'This person-body consists of six <s>dhātus</s> (elements).' Furthermore it says: '<s>Ākāśa</s> is invisible, formless, and non-resistant.' If it is a <s>dharma</s> of absence,

body.text: naiva vaktuṃ śakyate | na hi śaśaśṛṅgadṛśyamarūpamapratighamityucyate | (u) yo vastusan dharmaḥ sa sarvaḥ pratiṣṭhito bhavati | yathā nāma rūpāśritam, rūpañca nāmāśritam | ākāśantvanāśritamato 'bhāvadharma iti jñāyate | yadbhabhavānāha- ākāśaṃ dhāturiti | tadapi na yuktam | kasmāt | rūpe rūpaṃ pratihanyate rūpamasati viruddharūpe vivardhate | anenārthenāha bhagavān- ṣaḍdhātuko 'yaṃ puruṣakāya iti | [yat] bhavānāha- na hi śaśaśṛṅga madṛśyamarūpamapratighamityucyata iti | tadapyayuktam | kasmāt | sarvathā ākāśavaśāllabhyate | asti kṛtakamatītānāgatavastvādi | nedṛśamasti śaśaśṛṅgādau | (pṛ) cittamapyevamarūpamamūrtamapratigham | nāstīti vaktavyam | (u) cittantu karma karoti yadālambanamupādatte | ākāśamakarmakam | abhāvamātreṇa kṛtakāstitālābhādabhāvadharma iti jñāyate ato 'yaṃ samādhiradita ākāśamavalambate |
body.translated_text: it cannot be stated at all. For one does not say 'a hare's horn is invisible, formless, and non-resistant.' (Answer) Whatever <s>dharma</s> has real existence is established [somewhere]. Just as name depends on form, and form depends on name, <s>ākāśa</s> however is unsupported — therefore it is known to be a <s>dharma</s> of absence. As for what you said — '<s>ākāśa</s> is a <s>dhātu</s> (element)' — that too is not correct. Why? When form is present, form is obstructed; when opposing form is absent, form expands. In this sense the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This person-body consists of six <s>dhātus</s>.' As for what you said — 'one does not say a hare's horn is invisible, formless, and non-resistant' — that too is incorrect. Why? In every respect, [these attributes] are obtained on account of <s>ākāśa</s>. There exist fabricated things, past and future entities, and the like. Such [attributes] do not exist for a hare's horn and the like. (Question) <s>Citta</s> (mind) too is likewise formless, immaterial, and non-resistant. Should it be said to be non-existent? (Answer) But <s>citta</s> performs action — it apprehends objects. <s>Ākāśa</s> is without action. Being known merely as absence, since [its] existence is obtained only as a fabrication, it is known to be a <s>dharma</s> of absence. Therefore this <s>samādhi</s> initially takes <s>ākāśa</s> as its object.

body.text: (pṛ) samādhirayaṃ katamāṃ bhūmimavalambate | (u) sarvā bhūmiḥ nirodhamārgañcāvalambate | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- arūpasamāpattayo nirodhālambanā api ayaṃ anumānajñānabhāgīyaṃ nirodhamātramālambate | na dṛṣṭajñānabhāgīyaṃ nirodham | iti | tatkatham | (u) sarvaṃ nirodhamavalambate | dṛṣṭadharmajñānena pratyutpannasvabhūmi[gata]nirodhamavalamyate | anumānajñānenānyanirodhamavalambate | evaṃ mārgo 'pi | sarvapratipakṣāvalambitvāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) What level does this <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) take as its object? (Answer) It takes all levels and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) and <s>mārga</s> (path) as its objects. (Question) Some say: 'The formless attainments, even those having <s>nirodha</s> as their object, take as their object merely cessation belonging to inferential knowledge, not cessation belonging to direct knowledge.' How is this? (Answer) It takes all cessation as its object. By direct knowledge of present phenomena, one takes as object the cessation pertaining to one's own level. By inferential knowledge, one takes as object other cessation. Likewise with the <s>mārga</s> (path), because it takes all antidotes as its object.

body.text: (pṛ) ārūpyadhātugatāḥ sattvā anyabhūmikacittamutpādayanti na vā | (u) anyabhūmikacittamanāsravacittañcotpādayanti | (pṛ) tathā cet kathaṃ na cyutirbhavati | (u) karmavipāke vartamānattvānna cyavate | yathā kāmadhātau rūpadhātau cābhijñābalādanyasmin rūpe anyasmin citte sthito 'pi na cyavate | tathā tatrāpi | (pṛ) ākāśānantyāyatanasamādherākāśāyatanasya kṛtsnāyatanasya ca ko bhedaḥ | (u) ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samāpitsorupāyamārgaḥ kṛtsnamityākhyāyate | samādhisamāpattiḥ sampannā ākāśasamādhisamāpattiḥ ? | tatra samādherhetuphala[bhāvo] bhūmiḥ sarvā sāsravā [vā]anāsravā | yadi samādhiḥ, samādhiṃ vinā yadi saṃkleśaḥ yadi vā vvavadānam sarvamākāśānantyāyatanamityākhyāyate ? ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Do beings reborn in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm) produce <s>citta</s> (mind) of other levels or not? (Answer) They produce <s>citta</s> of other levels and also uncontaminated <s>citta</s>. (Question) If so, how is it that there is no falling away? (Answer) Because the <s>karmavipāka</s> (karmic fruition) is still ongoing, one does not fall away, just as in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) and <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), through the power of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), even while abiding in another form or another mind, one does not fall away. Likewise there too. (Question) What is the difference between the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana-samādhi</s> (concentration of the base of infinite space), the <s>ākāśāyatana</s> (base of space), and the <s>kṛtsnāyatana</s> (totality base)? (Answer) The <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> — when one wishes to attain it, the means-path is called <s>kṛtsna</s> (totality). When the <s>samādhi</s>-attainment is accomplished, it is the <s>ākāśa-samādhi-samāpatti</s> (space concentration attainment). Therein, the cause-and-effect relationship of the <s>samādhi</s>, the level, all that is with or without <s>āsrava</s> (defilements) — whether it is the <s>samādhi</s> itself, or without the <s>samādhi</s>, whether defilement or purification — all of this is called <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>.

body.text: ākāśānantyāyatanavarga ekonasaptatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and sixty-ninth chapter, the Chapter on the Base of Infinite Space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatanavarga</s>).

body.text: 170 ārūpyasamādhitritayavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 170. Chapter on the Triad of Formless Concentrations (<s>ārūpyasamādhitritayavarga</s>)

body.text: sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramya [anantaṃ vijñānamiti] vijñānānantyāyatanamupasampadya viharati | yogāvacaro rūpātparamanirviṇṇo rūpapratipakṣadharmamapyupekṣate | yathā nadīṃ tīrtvā uḍupaṃ tyajati | yathā vā coraṃ niṣkāsya nivartayitumicchati | tathā yogāvacaro 'pi ākāśaṃ pratītya rūpaṃ paribhedayan [ākāśa]mapi parijihīrṣati |
body.translated_text: Having completely transcended the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (base of infinite space), [thinking] 'consciousness is infinite,' one enters and abides in the <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s> (base of infinite consciousness). The <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner of yoga), being thoroughly disenchanted with form, also relinquishes the <s>dharma</s> that is the antidote to form, just as one who has crossed a river abandons the raft, or just as one who has expelled a thief wishes to turn back. Likewise the <s>yogāvacara</s> too, having broken apart form depending on <s>ākāśa</s> (space), also wishes to abandon <s>ākāśa</s> itself.

body.text: vijñānānantyāyatanamiti yogāvacaro vijñānenānantamākāśamityavalambamānaḥ tadā anantaṃ vijñāna[mapi ālambate] | ata ākāśamupekṣya vijñānamavalambate | yathā rūpapariśrānta ākāśamālambate | tathā ākāśapariśrānta upaśamecchayā vijñānamātramālambate | pudgalo 'yaṃ vijñānenākāśamālambata ityato vijñānapradhāna ityucyate | ato vijñānamātramālambate |
body.translated_text: The <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s> (base of infinite consciousness) — the <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner), while taking as object 'space is infinite' by means of consciousness, at that time also takes infinite consciousness as object. Therefore, relinquishing <s>ākāśa</s> (space), one takes consciousness as object. Just as one who is wearied by form takes <s>ākāśa</s> as object, so too one who is wearied by <s>ākāśa</s>, desiring tranquility, takes mere consciousness as object. Since this <s>pudgala</s> (person) takes <s>ākāśa</s> as object by means of consciousness, it is said to be 'consciousness-predominant.' Therefore one takes mere consciousness as object.

body.text: yogāvacaro vijñānenālambanamanuvartayan kālamanuvartata ityato 'nantamasti | tatpariśramanirviṇṇo vijñānaṃ paribhidya tatparijihīrṣayā ākiñcanyāyatanamupasampadya viharati | [tadā] evaṃ cintayati vijñānamasti tatra duḥkham | mama yadyasti anantaṃ vijñānam, tadā avaśyamante duḥkhena bhāvyam iti | ato vijñānālambanacittaṃ pragṛhṇāti | cittasya [parama]sūkṣmatvāt ākiñcanyamityucyate |
body.translated_text: The <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner), continuing to follow the object by means of consciousness, continues through time — therefore it is infinite. Being disenchanted and wearied by that exertion, breaking through consciousness and wishing to abandon it, one enters and abides in the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s> (base of nothingness). Then one thinks thus: 'Where there is consciousness, there is suffering. If I have infinite consciousness, then inevitably in the end there will be suffering.' Therefore one restrains the mind that takes consciousness as object. Because of the extreme subtlety of <s>citta</s> (mind), it is called <s>ākiñcanya</s> (nothingness).

body.text: punarevaṃ cintayati- akiñcanyamitīyaṃ saṃjñā | saṃjñā ca duḥkhopāyāyāsāya bhavati rogato gaṇḍataḥ | yasya saṃjñā nāsti sa punarmūḍho bhavati | yadākiñcanyaṃ paśyāmi tadeva kiñcidbhavati | ataḥ saṃjñābhyo na vimokṣalabdhaḥ | yogāvacaraḥ saṃjñāṃ vipadaṃ āsajñikaṃ sammohaṃ paśyati | iti naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamupasampadya viharati | śāntaṃ praṇītañca yat naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamityucyate | pṛthagjanāḥ sadotrastā asaṃjñāṃ sammohaṃ manyante | ato nātyantaṃ cittaṃ niroddhumalaṃ bhavanti |
body.translated_text: Then one further thinks thus: '<s>Ākiñcanya</s> (nothingness)' — this is a <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception). And perception leads to suffering, exertion, and affliction — like a disease, like a boil. One who has no perception becomes confused. When I perceive nothingness, that itself becomes something. Therefore, from perceptions there is no liberation obtained. The <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner) sees perception as calamity and non-perception as delusion. Thus one enters and abides in the <s>naiva-saṃjñā-nāsaṃjñāyatana</s> (base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception). That which is the <s>naiva-saṃjñā-nāsaṃjñāyatana</s> is said to be peaceful and sublime. Ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), being constantly frightened, consider non-perception as delusion. Therefore they are not able to completely cease <s>citta</s> (mind).

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- asaṃjñisattvā api cittaṃ niroddhumalamiti | tadayuktam |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'Even <s>asaṃjñisattvas</s> (non-percipient beings) are able to cease <s>citta</s> (mind).' That is incorrect.

body.text: kasmāt | yadi rūpadhātau cittaṃ niroddhumalaṃ bhavanti kasmādārūpyadhātau nālam | (pṛ) rūpadhātuḥ rūpavānityataścittaṃ nirodhayanti | ārūpyadhātau prāgeva rūpaṃ niruddham, idānīṃ punaścittaṃ nirudhyate rūpacittayoryugapannirodhaṃ paśyata utrāsasammohaḥ syāt | (u) yat tatra vartamānaṃ na [tat] nirodhakam | tadantarājāyamānantu nirodhakaṃ syāt | yathā nirodhasamāpattau | (pṛ) cittanirodhasya phalamāsaṃjñikam | ato rūpacittanirodhe 'tyantadoṣāya bhavati | (u) nirodhasamāpatterapi sacittakatā phalam | tathedamapi | yadi phalamasamucchinnam, [tadā] phalastha iti nāma | yathā nirmitagataṃ rūpam nirmitacitte punaḥ phalamutpādayati | ato nātyantaṃ nirudhyate | ato rūpadhātau na cittanirodho vaktavyaḥ | yadyucyate | arūpadhātāvapi vaktavyaḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: Why? If in the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) they are able to cease <s>citta</s> (mind), why are they not able in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm)? (Question) Because the <s>rūpadhātu</s> possesses form, they cease <s>citta</s>. In the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s>, form has already been ceased previously; if now <s>citta</s> is also ceased, seeing the simultaneous cessation of both form and <s>citta</s>, there would be terror and confusion. (Answer) What is present there is not what causes cessation. Rather, what arises in between would be the cause of cessation, as in the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (attainment of cessation). (Question) The fruit of the cessation of <s>citta</s> is the <s>āsaṃjñika</s> (non-percipient state). Therefore, in the cessation of both form and <s>citta</s>, there is an extreme fault. (Answer) The <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> too has as its fruit the state of having <s>citta</s>. Likewise this too. If the fruit is uninterrupted, then one is called 'abiding in the fruit.' Just as form that has gone to a magically created [state] produces fruit again in the magically created <s>citta</s>, therefore it is not completely ceased. Therefore, in the <s>rūpadhātu</s>, cessation of <s>citta</s> should not be maintained. If it is maintained, then it should also be maintained in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s>.

body.text: asaṃjñi samāpattau ca na cittaṃ nirudhyeta | kasmāt | yogāvacaro 'vaśyaṃ cittanirvedāt cittavirāgāt cittaṃ nirodhayati | yadi cittanirviṇṇa evārūpadhātau notpadyeta | kiṃ punaḥ rūpadhātāvutpadyeta iti | pṛthagjanāścitte gabhīramātmasaṃjñāmutpādayanti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dīrgharātraṃ [hyetat bhikṣavaḥ] aśrutavataḥ] pṛthagjanasya adhyavasitaṃ mamāyitaṃ parāmṛṣṭam etanmama eṣo 'hamasmi eṣa ma ātmeti | ato na niśśeṣaṃ nirvidyate virajyate | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- tīrthikāḥ trayāṇāmupādānānāṃ samucchedaṃ nirodhamupadiśanti nātmavādopādānasya iti | ato na cittaṃ niroddhumalam | yathā markaṭopamasūtram [aśrutavān] pṛthagjanaḥ kāyaṃ virajyeta na cittam | varaṃ [bhikṣavaḥ aśrutavān] pṛthagjana imaṃ cāturmahābhautikaṃ kāya[mātmata] upagacchet na tveva cittam | tatkasya hetoḥ | dṛśyate 'yaṃ [bhikṣava ścāturmahābhautikaḥ] kāya [ekamapi varṣaṃ] tiṣṭhan.....daśa varṣāṇi [tiṣṭhan] yāvacchatavarṣāṇyapi tiṣṭhan | yacca khalu [etadbhikṣava] ucyate cittamityapi mana ityapi vijñānamityapi tat rātyāśca divasasya cātyayena anyadevotpadyate anyannirudhyate | tadyathā [bhikṣavaḥ]
body.translated_text: In the <s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s> (non-percipient attainment) too, <s>citta</s> (mind) would not be ceased. Why? The <s>yogāvacara</s> (practitioner) necessarily ceases <s>citta</s> due to disenchantment with <s>citta</s> and dispassion toward <s>citta</s>. If one who is disenchanted with <s>citta</s> were not to be reborn in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), would one instead be reborn in the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm)? Ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) generate a deep perception of self regarding <s>citta</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For a long time, monks, the unlearned ordinary person has settled upon, claimed as mine, and grasped at [this mind, thinking] "this is mine, this I am, this is my self."' Therefore one does not become completely disenchanted or dispassionate. Furthermore it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) teach the cutting off and cessation of three kinds of <s>upādāna</s> (attachment), but not of attachment to the doctrine of self.' Therefore they are not able to cease <s>citta</s>. As the <s>Markaṭopama-sūtra</s> (Simile of the Monkey Sūtra) [says]: 'The unlearned ordinary person may become dispassionate toward the body but not toward <s>citta</s>. It would be better, monks, for the unlearned ordinary person to regard this body made of the four great elements as self rather than <s>citta</s>. For what reason? This body made of the four great elements, monks, is seen to last for one year... ten years... even up to a hundred years. But that which is called <s>citta</s>, or <s>manas</s>, or <s>vijñāna</s> — that, with the passing of night and day, arises as one thing and ceases as another.' Just as, monks,

body.text: markaṭa [araṇya upavane caran] śākhāṃ gṛhṇāti | tāṃ muktvā anyāṃ gṛhṇāti | ekameva bhikṣavo yadidamucyate cittamityapi mana ityapi vijñānamityapi | tat rātyāśca divasasya cātyāyena anyadevotpadyate anyannirudhyate |] tatra śrutavān [bhikṣavaḥ] āryaśrāvakaḥ pratītya samutpādameva sādhukaṃ yoniśo manasikaroti | ato 'nityamityeva prajānāti iti | pratītyasamutpādasyājñātā vedanāviśeṣādijñānaṃ vikalpayati | sarve tīrthikā avikalpapratyayajñānatvāt na cittaṃ nirodhayitumalam | pṛthagjanāśca rūpavirāgiṇo ['pi] cittāvirāgitvānnālaṃ vimoktum | ye yugapaccittaṃ niroddhumalam | te kasmānnālaṃ vimoktum |
body.translated_text: a monkey roaming in a forest grove seizes a branch, and having released it, seizes another. [Likewise] 'That one thing, monks, which is called <s>citta</s>, or <s>manas</s>, or <s>vijñāna</s> — that, with the passing of night and day, arises as one thing and ceases as another.' Therein, the learned noble disciple thoroughly and carefully attends to <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) itself. Therefore one understands it as impermanent. One who does not understand <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> fabricates knowledge of distinctions in <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and the like. All <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), because their knowledge has conditions that are without discrimination, are not able to cease <s>citta</s>. And ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), even though dispassionate toward form, because they are not dispassionate toward <s>citta</s>, are not able to be liberated. Those who are able to simultaneously cease <s>citta</s> — why are they not able to be liberated?

body.text: kiñca pṛthagjanāḥ [citta]nirodhabhīrutayā nirvāṇe nālaṃ śāntaśivasaṃjñāmutpādayitum | yathoktaṃ sūtre- naiṣo 'hamasmi, naitanmameti pṛthagjanānāmutrāsapadam śāntaśivasaṃjñāṃ notpādayati | kathaṃ cittaṃ niroddhumalaṃ bhavet | pṛthagjanānāñca dharmo [yat] uttamāṃ bhūmiṃ pratītyāvarāṃ bhūmiṃ vijahāti | ato nāsti cittanirodhapratyayaḥ | kintu samādhibalena sūkṣmasaṃjñāmabhimukhīkṛtya cittasya prabodhāt vadati nāsti saṃjñeti | audārikasaṃjñāmutpādayan tadaiva [tataḥ] cyutaḥ patati | [sa cāsaṃjñītyucyate |] yathā alpajño 'jña iti | yathā vā alpadaśano 'daśana iti | yathā vā sammūrchābhraṣṭacetanāḥ suṣuptāḥ krimayaḥ śītibhūtamakarāḥ | yathā vā naivasaṃjñānasaṃjñāyatanamityucyate | tathā tatrāpi vastutaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ satyāmapi saṃvṛtito 'saṃjñītyucyate |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), being afraid of the cessation of mind (<s>cittanirodha</s>), are unable to generate the perception of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as peaceful and auspicious (<s>śāntaśiva</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'This is not myself, this is not mine' — this, being a ground of terror for ordinary persons, does not generate the perception of the peaceful and auspicious. How then could one be capable of ceasing the mind? And it is the nature (<s>dharma</s>) of ordinary persons that, having attained a higher stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), they abandon the lower stage. Therefore, there is no condition for the cessation of mind. Rather, by the power of <s>samādhi</s>, having directed [awareness] toward subtle perception (<s>sūkṣmasaṃjñā</s>), one says 'there is no perception' because of the mind's awakening [from gross perception]. When one generates gross perception (<s>audārikasaṃjñā</s>), at that very moment one falls, having departed [from that attainment]. [And that one is called 'without perception' (<s>asaṃjñin</s>).] Just as one of little knowledge is called 'ignorant.' Or just as one of little sight is called 'sightless.' Or just as those whose consciousness is lost through fainting, or those in deep sleep, or worms, or sea-creatures (<s>makara</s>) that have become cold. Or just as it is called the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). Similarly, even there, although perception exists in reality, conventionally it is called 'without perception.'

body.text: ārūpyasamādhitrayavargaḥ saptatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter on the three formless <s>samādhis</s> (<s>ārūpyasamādhitraya</s>), the one hundred and seventieth.

body.text: 171 nirodhasamāpattivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 171. Chapter on the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>).

body.text: sarvaśonaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ samatikramya saṃjñāvedayitanirodhaṃ kāyena spṛṣṭvā viharati | (pṛ) dhyāneṣu kasmānnocyate sarvaśaḥ samatikramyeti | arūpasamāpattiṣu ca
body.translated_text: Having completely transcended the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), one abides having directly realized with the body the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedayitanirodha</s>). (Question) Why is it not said 'having completely transcended' in the case of the <s>dhyānas</s>? And in the formless attainments (<s>arūpasamāpatti</s>),

body.text: nokto 'staṅgamaḥ | (u) uktaṃ khalvasmābhiḥ dhyānasamādhiṣu santi vitarkavicāraprītisukhādayo dharmā iti ato nocyate sarvaśaḥ samatikramyeti | (pṛ) ākāśānantyāyatane rūpacittamastīti pratipāditameva | ato 'rūpeṣvapi na vaktavyaṃ sarvaśaḥ samatikramyeti (u) ākāśānantyāyatanasamāpattiṃ samāpanno rūpacittādvimucyate, na vitarkavicārādibhyo dharmebhyaḥ | kecidāhuḥ- samatikramo vyupaśamo 'staṅgamaḥ sarvamekārthakam, vyañjanameva nānā iti | ārūpyasamāpattiṣu ca cittaṃ susthiram | avarabhūmau cittaṃ vikṣepakampyam | ato nocyate sarvaśaḥ samatikramyeti | (pṛ) yat sahaivoktaṃ asti kaṇṭako yaduta rūpasaṃjñā ityādi | tat kasmāducyate cittaṃ susthiramiti | (u) yadyapi sahaivokta masti kaṇṭaka iti | tathāpi caturthadhyānamacalamityākhyāyate | evamarūpasamāpattiṣu samāpattibalamahimnā susthiramityākhyā labhyate |
body.translated_text: the cessation [of those factors] is not stated. (Answer) We have already explained that in the <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhis</s> there exist <s>dharmas</s> such as applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>), sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), happiness (<s>sukha</s>), and so forth — therefore it is not said 'having completely transcended.' (Question) It has already been established that in the sphere of the infinity of space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>) there exists a form-mind (<s>rūpacitta</s>). Therefore, even in the formless [attainments], one should not say 'having completely transcended.' (Answer) One who has entered the attainment of the sphere of the infinity of space is freed from the form-mind, but not from <s>dharmas</s> such as applied thought, sustained thought, and so forth. Some say: transcending, calming, and cessation are all of one meaning — only the expression differs. And in the formless attainments, the mind is very stable. In the lower stage, the mind is disturbed by agitation. Therefore it is not said 'having completely transcended.' (Question) It was stated together [in the <s>sūtra</s>]: 'There is a thorn, namely the perception of form,' and so forth. Why then is it said that the mind is stable? (Answer) Although it was stated together that 'there is a thorn,' nevertheless the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is called 'unshakable' (<s>acala</s>). Similarly, in the formless attainments, by the greatness of the power of the attainment, the designation 'stable' is obtained.

body.text: (pṛ) śaikṣo na nirodhasamāpattiṃ labheta | naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasya sarvaśo 'natikramāt | (u) śaikṣo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatane sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ vyupaśamaṃ paśyati | kintu na paśyati teṣāmanutpādam | ata uktadoṣo labhyate | yat bhavatā pūrvamuktaṃ navānupūrvikeṣu cittacaittānāṃ nirodha iti tat virudhyate | (u) nirodhasamāpattirdvividhā- kleśānāṃ kṣayarūpā kleśānāmakṣayarūpā iti | kleśānāṃ kṣayarūpā vimokṣeṣu vartate kleśānāmakṣayarūpā anupūrvaṃ [vihāre]ṣu vartate | (1) kleśānāṃ nirodhānnirodhasamāpattiḥ, (2) cittacaittānāṃ nirodhānnirodhasamāpattiḥ | kleśānāṃ nirodho 'ṣṭamavimokṣaḥ | tedevārhatphalam | arhatphalañca sarvasaṃjñānāṃ punaranutpādako vyupaśama eva | atra saṃjñānāṃ vyupaśame 'pi anyasaṃyojanānāṃ sattvāt punaranutpādikā na bhavati |
body.translated_text: (Question) A learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) should not obtain the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), because one has not completely transcended the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. (Answer) A learner, in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, sees the calming of all formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), but does not see their non-arising. Therefore the stated fault is obtained. What you previously said — that in the nine successive [attainments], the cessation of mind and mental factors (<s>cittacaitta</s>) [occurs] — that is contradicted. (Answer) The attainment of cessation is of two kinds: one that is the destruction of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), and one that is not the destruction of defilements. That which is the destruction of defilements operates among the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>); that which is not the destruction of defilements operates in the successive abodes. (1) From the cessation of defilements, there is the attainment of cessation; (2) from the cessation of mind and mental factors, there is the attainment of cessation. The cessation of defilements is the eighth liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>). That itself is the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> (<s>arhatphala</s>). And the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> is precisely the calming that prevents the re-arising of all perceptions. Here, even though there is calming of perceptions, because other fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) still exist, it does not become the [complete] non-re-arising.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi yogavacaro navānupūrvavihāraiścittaṃ nirodhayati | srotaāpannādayaḥ kathaṃ cittanirodhadharmaṃ sākṣātkurvanti | (u) anupūrvavihāreṣu nirodho mahānirodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) If the practitioner (<s>yogavacara</s>) ceases the mind through the nine successive abodes (<s>anupūrvavihāra</s>), how do stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) and others directly realize the <s>dharma</s> of mind-cessation? (Answer) Cessation in the successive abodes is the great cessation (<s>mahānirodha</s>).

body.text: yadi kaścit dhyānasamāpattīḥ sādhu bhāvayati, mārgacittabaladārḍhyādimaṃ nirodhaṃ labhate | yadi nāsti tadbalam, tadā nirodhasamāpattirnedṛśaṃ mahābalaṃ vindate | ato 'nupūrvavihārā uktāḥ | anyatrāpyasti nirodhacittam | yathā caturthadhyāne cittacaittān nirundhya āsaṃjñike praviśati | prathamadhyānādau kasmānna nirodhaḥ | anyatrāpi ca nirodhacittārtho bhavet | yathoktaṃ sūtre srotaāpannādayo nirodhaṃ sākṣātkurvanti | niruddhacittameva nirodha ityucyate na punaranyo 'sti dharmo nirodha iti | ato jñāyate imā navabhūmīrvihāyāpyasti cittanirodha iti |
body.translated_text: If someone properly cultivates the <s>dhyāna</s>-attainments, by the strength and firmness of the path-mind (<s>mārgacitta</s>) and such, one obtains this cessation. If that strength is absent, then the attainment of cessation does not attain such great power. Therefore the successive abodes are taught. But elsewhere too there is a mind of cessation (<s>nirodhacitta</s>). Just as in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, having ceased mind and mental factors, one enters the sphere without perception (<s>asaṃjñika</s>). Why is there no cessation from the first <s>dhyāna</s> onward? And elsewhere too there could be a mind directed toward cessation. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: stream-enterers and others directly realize cessation. The ceased mind itself is called 'cessation' — there is no other <s>dharma</s> that is cessation. From this it is known that even beyond these nine stages, there is cessation of mind.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi nirodhasamāpattau sarvacittacaittān nirodhayati | kasmātsaṃjñāvedayitanirodhamātramucyate | (u) sarvāṇi cittāni veditānītyucyante | veditañcedaṃ dvividhaṃ- saṃjñāveditaṃ prajñāveditamiti | saṃjñāveditaṃ saṃskṛtālambanaṃ cittam | saṃjñākārāṇāṃ prajñaptigatatvāt prajñaptiśca dvividhā- hetusaṃghātaprajñaptiḥ dharmaprajñaptiśceti | ataḥ sarvasaṃskṛtālambanaṃ cittaṃ saṃjñā bhavati | prajñāveditaṃ asaṃskṛtālambanaṃ cittam | ataḥ saṃjñāveditanirodha ityuktau sarvanirodha ukto bhavati |
body.translated_text: (Question) If in the attainment of cessation one ceases all mind and mental factors, why is it called merely 'the cessation of perception and feeling'? (Answer) All minds are called 'known' (<s>vedita</s>). And this 'known' is of two kinds: known through perception (<s>saṃjñāvedita</s>) and known through wisdom (<s>prajñāvedita</s>). The mind whose object is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtālambana</s>) is known through perception. Because the aspects of perception are conventional in nature, and convention is of two kinds: convention of causal aggregation (<s>hetusaṃghātaprajñapti</s>) and convention of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaprajñapti</s>). Therefore, all mind whose object is conditioned is perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>). The mind whose object is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtālambana</s>) is known through wisdom. Therefore, when one says 'cessation of perception and feeling,' it means the cessation of everything is stated.

body.text: (pṛ) sarveṣu cittacaitteṣu prādhānyāt saṃjñāveditaṃ kevalamucyate | kasmāt | kleśānāmasti bhāgadvayam- tṛṣṇābhāgo dṛṣṭibhāga iti | veditādutpadyate tṛṣṇābhāgaḥ | saṃjñāto dṛṣṭibhāgaḥ | kāmadhātau rūpadhātau ca veditaṃ pradhānam | arūpyadhātau tu saṃjñā pradhānā | ato dvividhamevoktam | vijñānasthitiṣu ca saṃjñāveditamātramuktam | vijñānasthitīnāṃ cittādutthitatvādeva saṃskāra ityākhyā | saṃjñāveditanirodha ityuktau ca sarvacittacaittānāṃ nirodha ukto bhavati | cittacaittānāṃ tato 'vyabhicārāt | (u) maivam | bhavānāha- prādhānyāt [saṃjñāveditaṃ] kevalamucyata iti | [tadā] cittamātraṃ vaktavyam | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi tatra tatra (?) sūtre- cittaṃ khalvadhipattiḥ dvividhānāṃ kleśānāmāśrayaḥ | cittasyaiva vikalpāt saṃjñāveditamityucyate | iti | ato vaktavyaṃ cittameva | citte cokte sugamam | ato bhavaduktirna [saṃbhavati] |
body.translated_text: (Question) Among all mind and mental factors, perception and feeling alone are mentioned because of their predominance. Why? Defilements have two aspects: the aspect of craving (<s>tṛṣṇābhāga</s>) and the aspect of views (<s>dṛṣṭibhāga</s>). From feeling arises the aspect of craving. From perception arises the aspect of views. In the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) and the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), feeling is predominant. In the formless realm (<s>arūpyadhātu</s>), perception is predominant. Therefore only these two are mentioned. And in the stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>), only perception and feeling are mentioned. Because the stations of consciousness arise from mind, they are called 'formations' (<s>saṃskāra</s>). When one says 'cessation of perception and feeling,' the cessation of all mind and mental factors is stated, because they are invariably concomitant with mind and mental factors. (Answer) This is not correct. You say that perception and feeling alone are mentioned because of predominance. [Then] mind alone should be stated. Why? For it is said in various <s>sūtras</s>: 'Mind indeed is the sovereign, the basis of the two kinds of defilements. It is only through the differentiation of mind that perception and feeling are spoken of.' Therefore mind alone should be stated. And when mind is stated, it is easily understood. Therefore your statement does not hold.

body.text: (pṛ) samāpattiriyaṃ kasmāducyate kāyena spṛṣṭvā viharatīti | (u) aṣṭavimokṣāḥ sarve kāyena spṛṣṭvā viharantīti vaktavyāḥ | ayaṃ nirodhadharmaḥ anabhilāpavedyatvāt kāyena sākṣātkarotītyāha | tadyathā apāṃ spraṣṭā tacchaityaṃ prajānāti | na tu śrotā prajānāti | tathedamapi | acittadharmatvāt iyaṃ kāyena sākṣātkarotīti syāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is it said of this attainment that 'one abides having directly realized it with the body'? (Answer) All eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>) should be described as 'abiding having directly realized with the body.' This <s>dharma</s> of cessation, because it is to be experienced beyond verbal expression, one directly realizes it with the body — thus it is said. Just as one who touches water knows its coldness, but one who merely hears [about it] does not know it. So too is this. Because it is a <s>dharma</s> without mind (<s>acittadharma</s>), one directly realizes it with the body — this could be [the explanation].

body.text: (pṛ) yadbhavānāha- nirodhasamāpattiracittadharma iti | na tat yujyate | kasmāt | samāpattimimāṃ samāpannaḥ sattva [eva] bhavati | loke ca nāsti ko 'pi sattvo 'cittaka ityato 'yuktam | uktañca sūtre- āyurūsma vijñānamime trayo dharmāḥ sadāvyabhicāriṇa iti | ato nāsti niruddhacittaḥ [sattvaḥ] | sarve ca sattvāścaturbhirāhārairjīvanti | nirodhasamāpattimupasampannasya na santyāhārāḥ | kasmāt | nahyayaṃ kabalīkāramāhāraṃ bhunakti | sparśādayo 'pi niruddhāḥ | ato nāstyāhāraḥ | cittañca cittādutpadyate | citte 'smin niruddhe nānyaccittamutpadyate | samanantarapratyayābhāvāt kathamūrdhvabhāvi cittamutpadyeta | kiñcānupadhiśeṣanirvāṇapraviṣṭamātraṃ cittaṃ samucchinnasantati sat nirudhyate | nānyatra[gataṃ] nirudhyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- rūpeṇa kāmān samatikrāmati | arūpeṇa rūpaṃ samatikrāmati | nirodhena sarvacetanāmanaskārān samatikrāmati iti | cittameva cetanā manaskāro bhavatītyavaśyaṃ nirodhena taṃ samatikrāmati | sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇalābhinaḥ kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ nirudhyate | nirūpadhiśeṣanirvāṇalābhino 'kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ nirudhyate | ityayameva tathāgataśāsane samyagarthaḥ | nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannaśca na mṛta ityucyate | cittanirodho hi maraṇam | yadi niruddhaṃ cittaṃ punarjāyate | mṛtaśca punarjāyeta | nirvāṇaṃ praviṣṭo 'pi punarjāyeta | tadā tu naiva vimokṣaḥ | vastutastu na tathā | ataścittaṃ na nirudhyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) What you have said — that the attainment of cessation is a <s>dharma</s> without mind — is not correct. Why? A being who has entered this attainment is still a sentient being (<s>sattva</s>). And in the world, there is no sentient being without mind. Therefore it is incorrect. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Life-force (<s>āyus</s>), warmth (<s>ūṣman</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) — these three <s>dharmas</s> are always inseparable.' Therefore there is no [sentient being] whose mind has ceased. And all sentient beings live by four kinds of nutriment (<s>āhāra</s>). For one who has entered the attainment of cessation, there are no nutriments. Why? For this one does not consume material food (<s>kabalīkārāhāra</s>). Contact (<s>sparśa</s>) and the rest have also ceased. Therefore there is no nutriment. And mind arises from [preceding] mind. When this mind has ceased, no other mind arises. In the absence of the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), how could a subsequent mind arise? Furthermore, the mind of one who has entered <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>) ceases with its continuum cut off. It does not cease having gone elsewhere. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'By form one transcends desires. By the formless one transcends form. By cessation one transcends all volition (<s>cetanā</s>) and mental engagement (<s>manaskāra</s>).' Mind itself is volition and mental engagement — therefore one must transcend it through cessation. For one who attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s> with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>), the defiled mind ceases. For one who attains <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder, the undefiled mind ceases. This is precisely the correct meaning in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And one who has entered the attainment of cessation is not called 'dead.' For the cessation of mind is death. If the ceased mind were to arise again, then the dead too would arise again, and one who has entered <s>Nirvāṇa</s> would also arise again. In that case, there would be no liberation at all. But in reality, it is not so. Therefore, the mind does not cease.

body.text: atrocyate | yadbhavānāha- nāstyacittakaḥ sattva iti acitta[tā] sāmye 'pi maraṇe 'sti bhedaḥ | yathā sūtre paripṛcchati- yo 'yaṃ [bhante] mṛtaḥ [kālakṛtaḥ] yaścāyaṃ
body.translated_text: To this we reply: What you have said — that there is no sentient being without mind — although the absence of mind is the same [in both cases], there is a difference in death. As it is asked in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Venerable sir, one who has died [and passed away] and one who has

body.text: saṃjñāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannaḥ | anayoḥ kiṃ nānākaraṇam | pratyāha- yo 'yaṃ [gṛhapate] mṛtaḥ [kālakṛtaḥ] | tasya āyurūṣma vijñānamitīmāni trīṇyekāntaniruddhāni | yaścāyaṃ [gṛhapate] saṃjñāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannaḥ | tasya cittamātraṃ niruddham, āyurūṣma tu kāyād vibhaktaṃ vartate iti | ato 'cittakaḥ sattvo bhavediti | puruṣasyāsya cittaṃ sa tatasthitilābhi bhavati | [sthiti]lābhabalāt sacitta ityākhyā | na tu sa tarupāṣāṇasamaḥ | yadbhavānavocat- trīṇi vastūnyavyabhicārīṇīti | tat kāmarūpadhātukasattvārthatayoktam | arūpadhātāvastyāyuḥ, asti vijñānam, natvasti ūṣma | nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannasya cāstyāyuḥ astyūṣma, natvasti vijñānam | asmin sūtre 'pyuktam vijñānaṃ kāyādvibhaktamiti | atastrīṇyavibhaktānīti yat vacanaṃ, tat yatra santi tatroktam |
body.translated_text: entered the cessation of perception and feeling — what is the difference between these two?' The reply is: 'Householder, one who has died [and passed away] — for that one, life-force, warmth, and consciousness, these three are completely ceased. But householder, one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling — for that one, mind alone has ceased, while life-force and warmth continue operating separately from the body.' Therefore, a sentient being can be without mind. For this person, the mind obtains a state of stability there. By the power of [that] stability, it is designated as 'having mind.' But that one is not equal to a tree or a stone. As for what you said — 'the three things are inseparable' — that was stated with reference to beings of the desire realm and form realm. In the formless realm, there is life-force and consciousness, but no warmth. For one who has entered the attainment of cessation, there is life-force and warmth, but no consciousness. In this <s>sūtra</s> too it is said that consciousness is separated from the body. Therefore, the statement that the three are inseparable is stated only where they [all] exist.

body.text:
yadavocadbhavān- āhāraṃ vinā kathaṃ jīvediti | kāyo 'yaṃ pūrvatanīnamanaḥ sañcetanāhārāt pratyutpanne vartate | śītādisparśāt kāyaṃ sandhatte | yaduktaṃ bhavatā cittaṃ pratītya cittamutpadyata | [tatra] cittaṃ cittāntarasya kārakahetuḥ | kārakahetau niruddhe cittāntaramutpādayati | (pṛ) kathaṃ niruddhaṃ cittaṃ cittāntaramutpādayati | yathā cakṣū niruddhaṃ sat na tadvijñānaṃ janayati | (u) yathā niruddhaṃ karma vipākamutpādayati | tathedamapi | yanmanaḥ yacca manovijñānam ime dve mithaḥ pratisambandhinī | na tathā cakṣuścakṣurvijñānam | ato 'hetuḥ | yadavocaḥ santānasamuccheda eva cittaṃ nirudhyata iti | tadayuktam | trividho hi nirodhaḥ- rūpanirodhaḥ cittanirodhaḥ kadācidrūpacittobhayanirodhaḥ, kadācidrūpasya nirodho na tu cittasya yathā nirodhasamāpattisamāpanne | kadācidrūpacittobhayanirodhaḥ yathā santānasamucchede |
yadavocaḥ nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpanno na mṛta ityucyata iti | puruṣasyāsya nāyurūṣma niruddham | mṛtasya trīṇyapi niruddhānīti | ayaṃ bhedaḥ | puruṣasyāsya ca āyurūṣma pratītya cittaṃ punarutpadyate | na tathā mṛtasya | yaduktaṃ bhavatā- yadi niruddhaṃ cittaṃ punarjāyate,
body.translated_text:
You said: 'How can one live without <s>āhāra</s> (nutriment)?' This body exists in the present due to the nutriment of <s>manas</s> (mind) and <s>sañcetanā</s> (volition) from previous lives. Through contact with cold and other sensations, it sustains the body. As you stated, <s>citta</s> (mind) arises dependent on <s>citta</s>. [There] <s>citta</s> is the productive cause (<s>kārakahetu</s>) of another <s>citta</s>. When the productive cause has ceased, it produces another <s>citta</s>. (Question) How does a ceased <s>citta</s> produce another <s>citta</s>? Just as the eye, having ceased, does not generate its corresponding consciousness. (Answer) Just as ceased <s>karma</s> produces <s>vipāka</s> (fruition), so too is this. <s>Manas</s> (mind) and <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness) — these two are mutually interconnected. The eye and eye-consciousness are not so. Therefore your argument is without basis. You said that <s>citta</s> ceases only at the cutting off of the <s>santāna</s> (continuum) — that is not tenable. For <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) is threefold: cessation of <s>rūpa</s> (form), cessation of <s>citta</s>, and sometimes cessation of both <s>rūpa</s> and <s>citta</s>; sometimes there is cessation of <s>rūpa</s> but not of <s>citta</s>, as in one who has attained the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment); and sometimes cessation of both <s>rūpa</s> and <s>citta</s>, as in the cutting off of the continuum.
You said that one who has attained the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> is not called 'dead.' For this person, <s>āyus</s> (life-force) and <s>ūṣma</s> (warmth) have not ceased. For a dead person, all three have ceased — this is the distinction. And for this person, dependent on <s>āyus</s> and <s>ūṣma</s>, <s>citta</s> arises again. Not so for a dead person. As you stated: 'If ceased <s>citta</s> is born again,

body.text: tadā na vimokṣa iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | nirvāṇaṃ praviṣṭasya pūrvakarmavedyāni āyurūṣmavijñānāni niruddhāni | na punarutpadyante | asya tu āyurūṣmaṇoranirodhe pūrvakālīnaṃ cittamutpadyate | yathā nirodhasamāpattivarga uktam- nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannaḥ ṣaḍāyatanāni kāyajīvitañca pratītya punarvyuttiṣṭhata iti | ataścittaṃ punarutpadyate | nirvāṇaṃ praviṣṭasya cittaṃ paraṃ na punarutpadyate | ato jñāyate samāpattiriyamacittaketi |
body.translated_text: then there is no <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation)' — that is not tenable. Why? For one who has entered <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>āyus</s> (life-force), <s>ūṣma</s> (warmth), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), which are to be experienced through prior <s>karma</s>, have ceased. They do not arise again. But for this one, when <s>āyus</s> and <s>ūṣma</s> have not ceased, the <s>citta</s> of the previous time arises. As stated in the chapter on the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment): 'One who has attained the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> re-emerges dependent on the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) and bodily life.' Therefore <s>citta</s> arises again. For one who has entered <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>citta</s> does not arise again thereafter. Thus it is known that this attainment is without <s>citta</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmādetatsamāpattervyutthitasya dattaṃ dṛṣṭadharme vipākaṃ prāpayati | (u) etatsamāpattervyutthitasya cittaṃ paramaśāntam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- nirodhasamāpattervyutthitasya cittaṃ nirvāṇabhāgīyam iti | asya ca dhyānasamāpattibalaṃ sudṛḍham | tadāśritya prajñāpi mahatī | prajñāmahimnā dāyako viśiṣṭaṃ vipākaṃ vindate | yathā śatasahasraśrāvakāṇāṃ satkārako naikabuddhasya [satkāra]samāno bhavati | atra prajñayaiva viśeṣo na saṃyojanasamucchede | tathedamapi | imāṃ samāpattiṃ samāpannasya bahulasaddharmavāsitacittatvāt mahāphalamutpadyate | yathā sukṛṣṭe kṣetre sasyamavaśyaṃ bahulaṃ bhavati | lokānnirviṇṇasya dānaṃ mahāvipākaṃ prāpayati | nirodhasamāpattervyutthito lokātparamanirviṇṇa ityatastatsatkāro viśiṣṭaḥ | viśuddhacittasya dānaṃ mahāvipākaprāpakam | nāviśuddhacittasya puruṣo 'yaṃ prajñaptyāpi na kliṣṭacittaḥ | ata[sta]tsatkāro mahāvipākaprāpakaḥ | kiñcāyaṃ sadā paramārthasatye tiṣṭhati | anye saṃvṛtisatye vartante | puruṣo 'yaṃ sadā saraṇadharme vartate | kasmāt | saṃskṛtālambanaṃ cittaṃ saraṇaṃ bhavati | uktañca sūtre-
body.translated_text: (Question) Why does a gift given to one who has emerged from this attainment produce fruition visible in this very life? (Answer) The <s>citta</s> of one who has emerged from this attainment is supremely tranquil. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>citta</s> of one who has emerged from the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment) partakes of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' And one's strength of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) attainment is very firm. Relying on that, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) too is great. Through the greatness of <s>prajñā</s>, the donor obtains distinguished fruition. Just as honoring a hundred thousand <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) does not equal [honoring] a single <s>Buddha</s>. Here the distinction lies in <s>prajñā</s> alone, not in the eradication of fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>). So too is this. For one who has attained this <s>samāpatti</s>, because the <s>citta</s> has been long imbued with the true <s>Dharma</s>, great fruit arises — just as in a well-cultivated field, the crop will certainly be abundant. A gift from one who is disgusted with the world produces great <s>vipāka</s> (fruition). One who has emerged from the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> is supremely disgusted with the world — therefore honoring such a one is distinguished. A gift from one with a purified <s>citta</s> brings great <s>vipāka</s>; not so from one with an impure <s>citta</s>. This person, even by designation, does not have a defiled <s>citta</s>. Therefore honoring such a one brings great <s>vipāka</s>. Furthermore, this person always abides in <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth). Others abide in <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth). This person always abides in the <s>dharma</s> of refuge. Why? Because <s>citta</s> that has conditioned phenomena as its object becomes a refuge. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
tṛṇadoṣāṇi kṣetrāṇi rāgadoṣā iyaṃ prajā |
tasmāddhi vītarāgeṣu dattamasti mahāphalam || iti |
body.translated_text:
Fields have the fault of weeds; this populace has the fault of passion.
Therefore, a gift given to those free from passion bears great fruit.

body.text: rāgapratyayā prajñaptisaṃjñā | asyāḥ samāpattervyutthito nirvāṇālambana ityataḥ prajñaptisaṃjñayā viviktaḥ | api coktaṃ sūtre- yasya dānapateḥ satkāraṃ bhuṅktvā apramāṇasamādhimupasampadya
body.translated_text: The designation-concept (<s>prajñaptisaṃjñā</s>) is conditioned by passion. One who has emerged from this attainment has <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as object, and therefore is free from the designation-concept. Moreover, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Having partaken of the offering of the donor, one enters and abides in the immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: viharati | ayaṃ dānapattiḥ tatpratyayamapramāṇapuṇyaṃ labhate iti | nirodhasamāpattervyutthitasya [yat] nirvāṇālambanaṃ cittam | idamucyate 'pramāṇam | ato dṛṣṭa eva vipākaṃ labhate | kiñca aṣṭabhirguṇai ralaṅkṛtamidaṃ puṇyakṣetram- samyak dṛṣṭiḥ, nirvāṇālambanaṃ cittaṃ anyāni cāṅgāni taiḥ samanvāgataṃ bhavati | ata[statra dattaṃ] dṛṣṭavipākaṃ janayati |
body.translated_text: . This donor obtains immeasurable merit conditioned by that.' The <s>citta</s> of one who has emerged from the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment) has <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as its object. This is called 'immeasurable.' Therefore one obtains fruition in this very life. Furthermore, this field of merit is adorned with eight qualities: right view, <s>citta</s> having <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as its object, and the other factors — one is endowed with these. Therefore [a gift] given there produces visible fruition.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- nirodhasamāpattiścittaviprayuktasaṃskāro laukikadharmaśceti | tatkatham | (u) yathoktavat etatsamāpattervyutthitasya paramaśāntyādayo guṇā bhavanti | neme guṇā laukikāḥ syuḥ | (pṛ) nirodhasamāpattirdharmāṇāṃ pratirodhārthā | tena dharmeṇa hi cittaṃ notpādayati | ataścittaviprayuktasaṃskāraḥ syāt | yathā tapte 'yasmi kārṣṇyaṃ na bhavati | tāpāpagame punarbhavati | tathedamapi syāt | (u) tathā cet nirvāṇamapi cittaviprayuktasaṃskāraḥ syāt | kasmāt | nirvāṇaṃ pratītya hi nānye skandhāḥ samutpadyante | yadi nirvāṇaṃ na cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra iti | iyaṃ samāpattirapi na cittaviprayuktasaṃskāraḥ syāt | yogāvacarāṇāmīdṛśo dharmaḥ syāt nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpanne praṇihitānugamanāccittaṃ na pravartate | ato na vaktavyo viprayuktasaṃskāra iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: 'The <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment) is a <s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s> (formation dissociated from mind) and a worldly <s>dharma</s>.' How is that? (Answer) As stated, one who has emerged from this attainment has qualities such as supreme tranquility and the rest. These qualities would not be worldly. (Question) The <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> is for the purpose of obstructing <s>dharmas</s>. By that <s>dharma</s>, it does not produce <s>citta</s>. Therefore it should be a <s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>. Just as when iron is heated, blackness does not exist; when the heat is removed, it exists again. So too should this be. (Answer) If so, then <s>Nirvāṇa</s> too would be a <s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>. Why? Because dependent on <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, no other <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) arise. If <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not a <s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>, then this attainment too should not be a <s>cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra</s>. For practitioners, the <s>dharma</s> is such that when one has attained the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>, <s>citta</s> does not operate due to the following of one's prior resolution. Therefore it should not be called a <s>viprayuktasaṃskāra</s> (dissociated formation).

body.text: (pṛ) imāṃ samāpattimevānupūrvaṃ samāpadyata iti kimanupūrvameva vyuttiṣṭheta | (u) anupūrvameva vyuttiṣṭhate | krameṇa caudārikaṃ cittaṃ samāpadyate | (pṛ) sūtra uktamnirodhasamāpattervyutthitaṃ cittaṃ prathamaṃ trayaḥ sparśāḥ spṛśanti- aniñjyaḥ [sparśaḥ] animittaḥ [sparśaḥ] apraṇihitaḥ [sparśa] iti | kasmādevam | (u) asaṃskṛtālambane citte vidyamānaḥ sparśaḥ aniñjyaḥ animittaḥ apraṇihita iti nāma | śūnyata evāniñjyaḥ | saṃskṛtālambanasya cittasya laghutvādastīñjanaṃ yadrūpavedanādīnāṃ grahaṇam | śūnye[sati] animittam | animitte [sati] rāgādi kimapi nāsti | acittako 'yaṃ prathamaṃ nirvāṇamālambya tataḥ saṃskṛtamālambate | ata ucyate vyutthāne trayaḥ sparśāḥ spṛśantīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) One enters this attainment progressively — so should one not also emerge progressively? (Answer) One does emerge progressively. Gradually, grosser <s>citta</s> is attained. (Question) The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'When one who has emerged from the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment), the <s>citta</s> is first touched by three contacts: the immovable contact, the signless contact, and the wishless contact.' Why is this so? (Answer) The contact present in a <s>citta</s> that has the unconditioned as its object is called 'immovable,' 'signless,' and 'wishless.' In <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) itself it is immovable. Because the <s>citta</s> that has conditioned phenomena as its object is light, there is agitation — namely, the grasping of form, feeling, and the rest. In emptiness [there being no such grasping], it is signless. In the signless, passion and the rest do not exist at all. This one, being without <s>citta</s>, first takes <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as object, and then takes conditioned phenomena as object. Therefore it is said: 'Upon emergence, three contacts touch [the mind].'

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannasya cittaṃ sāsravam | samāpattivyutthitasya cittaṃ sāsravaṃ kadācidanāsravaṃ kadāciditi | kathamidam | (u) na sāsravam | yogāvacara etatsamāpattisamīpsayā prathamata eva sarvān saṃskārān paribhedayati | paribhedātsamāpadyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: 'The <s>citta</s> of one who has attained the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment) is <s>sāsrava</s> (with outflows). The <s>citta</s> of one who has emerged from the attainment is sometimes <s>sāsrava</s> (with outflows) and sometimes <s>anāsrava</s> (without outflows).' How is this? (Answer) It is not <s>sāsrava</s>. A practitioner, desiring this attainment, first thoroughly penetrates all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations). Through penetration, one attains [the cessation].

body.text: vyutthitasya nirvāṇālambanaṃ cittamevābhimukhī bhavati | ato jñāyate sarvathā anāsravamiti |
body.translated_text: The <s>citta</s> of one who has emerged faces only <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as its object. Therefore it is known to be entirely <s>anāsrava</s> (without outflows).

body.text: sūtra uktam- [saṃjñāvedayita]nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpadyamānasya bhikṣornaivaṃ bhavati] ahaṃ [saṃjñāvedayita]nirodhaṃ samāpadye iti | vyutthitasya api naivaṃ bhavati [ahaṃ vyuttiṣṭhāmīti | tathā cen kathaṃ samāpadyate | (u) nityaṃ bhāvitatvāt samāpattibalaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ bhavati | tathā cintanāsattve 'pi samāpadyate | yogāvacaro 'yaṃ saṃskṛtā[lambana]samucchedāt tathābhūtaṃ nirodhaṃ samāpadyate | yadi cittamagṛhya saṃskṛtamālambate | tadā na samāpanno nāma | ataḥ sūtramāha [atha khalvasya] pūrvameva tathācittaṃ bhāvitaṃ bhāvati [yat tat tathātvāya] upanayati iti |
body.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'For a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who is entering the <s>saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation of perception and feeling), the thought does not occur: "I am entering the cessation of perception and feeling." Nor does one who has emerged think: "I am emerging."' If so, then how does one enter? (Answer) Because it has been constantly cultivated, the strength of the attainment is very firm. Even without such deliberation, one enters. This practitioner, through the complete elimination of conditioned [objects], enters cessation in just that manner. If <s>citta</s>, having grasped [something], takes conditioned phenomena as its object, then one is not said to have attained [cessation]. Therefore the <s>sūtra</s> says: 'Previously, one's <s>citta</s> has been so cultivated that it leads to that very state.'

body.text: (pṛ) yadi nāsti śūnyādanyadupalabhyam | tadā asaṃskṛtālambanaṃ cittaṃ bhāvayitvā kamupakāraṃ labhate | (u) dīrghakālaṃ bhāvitatvāt samāpattidārḍhye jñānadarśanaṃ suniścitaṃ bhavati | yathā saṃskṛtālambanaṃ cittaṃ paśyato 'pi nāsti kṣaṇikādanyat | dīrghakāla bhāvitaṃ cittamātrantu sudṛḍhaṃ bhavati | tathedamapi syāt ||
body.translated_text: (Question) If there is nothing to be apprehended other than <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), then what benefit does one obtain by cultivating a <s>citta</s> that has the unconditioned as its object? (Answer) Because it has been cultivated for a long time, when the attainment becomes firm, knowledge and vision become well-established. Just as when seeing that <s>citta</s> which has conditioned phenomena as its object, there is nothing other than the momentary — yet <s>citta</s> cultivated for a long time becomes merely very firm. So too should this be.

body.text: nirodhasamāpattivarga ekasaptatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment) is the one hundred and seventy-first.

body.text: 172 daśakṛtsnāyatanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 172. Chapter on the Ten <s>Kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (Totality-bases)

body.text: pūrvālambanamakampayitvā cittabalavaśitā kṛtsnāyatanamityucyate | yogāvacaraḥ parīttanimittaṃ gṛhītavān adhimuktibalena tat vipulayati | kasmāt | samāhitacittabalāt tattve 'vatarataḥ sarvaṃ śūnyaṃ bhavati | adhimuktāvavatarataḥ pūrvagṛhītaṃ nimittamanuvartate | (pṛ) ko 'yamadhimuktisvabhāvaḥ | (u) nīlādīni rūpāṇyapramāṇāni | tanmūlāni
body.translated_text: By making the previous object unshakable, the mastery of <s>citta</s>-power is called <s>kṛtsnāyatana</s> (totality-base). A practitioner, having grasped a limited sign, expands it through the power of <s>adhimukti</s> (determination). Why? Because through the power of concentrated <s>citta</s>, when one enters into the truth, everything becomes empty. When one enters through <s>adhimukti</s>, the previously grasped sign continues. (Question) What is the nature of this <s>adhimukti</s>? (Answer) Forms such as blue and the rest are immeasurable. Their bases

body.text: saṃkṣipya catvāri, pṛthivyādīni catvāri mahābhūtāni, catvāri ca rūpāṇāṃ mūlāni etadaṣṭakaparicchinnamidamākāśam | vijñānamanantamākāśaṃ prajānātīti anantamapi | yasmāt sāntadharmo nānantaṃ gṛhṇāti | imāni daśa bhavanti |
body.translated_text: are condensed into four — the four great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>): earth, water, fire, and wind — and four bases of forms. This eightfold [totality] is delimited as space. Consciousness knows space as infinite, and so it too is infinite. Because a finite <s>dharma</s> cannot grasp the infinite. These are the ten [totality-bases].

body.text: (pṛ) pṛthivyāmasti tu dravyato 'bādi | yogī kathaṃ pṛthivīmātraṃ bhāvayati | (u) dīrghakālaṃ tat bhāvayan sadā pṛthivīnimittaṃ gṛhṇāti | tataḥ pṛthivīmātraṃ paśyati nānyadvastu | (pṛ) yoginā dṛṣṭaṃ pṛthivīnimittaṃ dravyataḥ pṛthivī na vā | (u) adhimuktibalāt darśane pṛthivī bhavati na dravyato bhavati pṛthivī | (pṛ) nirmāṇabalāt bhūyamānaṃ nirmitamapi kiṃ na dravyam | (u) nirmitaṃ samādhibalātsiddhamityataḥ kṛtakaṃ vastu yaduta prabhā aptejādi ca |
body.translated_text: (Question) In earth there actually exist water and the rest as substances. How does the practitioner cultivate earth alone? (Answer) Cultivating it for a long time, one always grasps the sign of earth. Then one sees only earth and no other substance. (Question) Is the sign of earth seen by the practitioner earth in substance or not? (Answer) Through the power of <s>adhimukti</s> (determination), in perception it is earth, but it is not earth in substance. (Question) If through the power of creation things come into being, would not what is created also be substantial? (Answer) What is created is accomplished through the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and therefore is a fabricated thing — namely, light, water, fire, and so forth.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ- aṣṭakṛtsnāyatanāni caturthadhyānamātre vartanta iti | tat katham | (u) yadi vartanta kāmadhātau triṣu dhyāneṣu ca ko doṣaḥ | antime dve kṛtsnāyatane pratyekaṃ svabhūmau bhavetām | tāni ca daśa sāsravāṇi | ālambanākampitvāt | (pṛ) ākāśaṃ kiṃ rūpapratighalakṣaṇam | (u) yogī adhimuktyā ca cakṣuḥśrotrādyākāśalakṣaṇaṃ śūnyaṃ gṛhṇāti | na sākṣādravyasadrūpaṃ paribhedayati | ato 'pi ādhimuktikamityākhyā [tasya] |
body.translated_text: (Question) Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say: 'The eight <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality-bases) exist only in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).' How is that? (Answer) If they exist [there], what fault is there in their existing in the desire realm and the [first] three <s>dhyānas</s> as well? The last two <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> would each exist in their own plane. And all ten are <s>sāsrava</s> (with outflows), because the object is unshakable. (Question) Is <s>ākāśa</s> (space) characterized by the resistance of form? (Answer) The practitioner, through <s>adhimukti</s> (determination), grasps the empty characteristic of space [as in] the eye, ear, and other [sense-organs]. One does not directly penetrate the true nature of substance. Therefore it is also called '<s>ādhimuktika</s>' (based on determination).

body.text: (pṛ) uktañca sūtre- sarvapṛthivīsamādhiṃ samāpannasyaivaṃ bhavati- ahameva pṛthivī, pṛthivyevāhamiti | kasmādevaṃ bhavati | (u) [sva]cittaṃ sarvavyāpi paśyati | ataścintayati sarvamahamiti | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- ayaṃ samādhiḥ kāmadhātvāptapṛthivyādimātramālambata iti | kathamidam | (u) yadi kāmadhātvāptapṛthivyādi sarvamālambate ko doṣaḥ | prajñaptyācāyaṃ samādhiranyān dharmānavalambate | tatra kaḥ punardoṣo 'sti | kiñcāyaṃ samādhiradhimuktito 'bhūtamālambanaṃ bhāvayati | nāsti tu kiñcidabhūtaṃ pṛthivyādi | (pṛ) bhagavataḥ śrāvakā api bhūmyādi bhāvayanti | kathamidam | (u) yadi śaikṣajanā bhāvayanti | sarvaṃ tat paribhedārtham | (pṛ) vastuto nāsti khalu sarvaṃ pṛthivī ityādīni | kathamayaṃ samādhirviparyasto na bhavati | (u) bhāvanāyāmasyāmasti mohabhāgaḥ | tatrātmadṛṣṭeḥ samudbhavāt | aśubhādibhāvanā yadyapi na paramārthasatyam | tathāpi vairāgyānukūlā bhavati | na tathā bhāvaneyam | ato 'sti mohabhāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is also said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one who has attained the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) of all-earth, this occurs — "I alone am earth, earth alone is I."' Why does this occur? (Answer) One sees one's own mind as all-pervading. Therefore one thinks, 'Everything is I.' (Question) Some say that this <s>samādhi</s> takes as its object only the earth and such elements obtained in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm). How is this? (Answer) If it takes as its object all earth and such elements obtained in the <s>kāmadhātu</s>, what fault is there? By designation, this <s>samādhi</s> does not depend on other <s>dharmas</s>. What fault then exists there? Moreover, this <s>samādhi</s> cultivates an unreal object through conviction. But there is nothing unreal about earth and such elements. (Question) Even the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) cultivate earth and such. How is this? (Answer) If those in training cultivate them, all of that is for the purpose of discernment. (Question) In reality, 'everything is earth' and such statements do not hold. How then is this <s>samādhi</s> not a perversion? (Answer) In this meditation there is a portion of delusion, because <s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s> (self-view) arises from it. Although the meditation on the impure and such is not ultimate truth, it is still conducive to dispassion. This meditation is not like that. Therefore there is a portion of delusion.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmānna bhāvayati anantaṃ vedanādi | vijñānamātrantu bhāvayati | (u)
body.translated_text: (Question) Why does one not meditate on the infinite <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and such? One meditates only on <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). (Answer)

body.text: grāhyaṃ pṛthivyādi | vijñānaṃ grāhakam | ato vijñānaṃ bhāvayati na vedanādi | vedanādi ca cittasya prabheda iti pratipāditameva pūrvam | kiñca yogī na paśyati vedanādi sarvatra vyāpi | sarvatra suḥkhaduḥkhavedanayorabhāvāt | bhagavataḥ śrāvakā ye 'smin samādhau viharanti | teṣāmavināśārthālambanatvāt | yatastadālambanaṃ yogino 'bhiniveśāyatanaṃ bhavati | yadi tadvinaśyati tadā pṛthagjanasamaḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: Earth and such are the graspable objects. <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is the grasper. Therefore one meditates on <s>vijñāna</s>, not on <s>vedanā</s> and such. Moreover, it was already established earlier that <s>vedanā</s> and such are divisions of the mind. Furthermore, the practitioner does not see <s>vedanā</s> and such as pervading everywhere, because pleasant and painful <s>vedanā</s> (feelings) do not exist everywhere. As for the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) of the <s>Bhagavat</s> who abide in this <s>samādhi</s>, for them it serves as an object for the purpose of non-destruction, because that object becomes a basis for the practitioner's attachment. If that were destroyed, then one would become equal to an ordinary person.

body.text: daśakṛtsnāyatanavargo dvisaptatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and seventy-second chapter, the Chapter on the Ten <s>Kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (Totality Bases).

body.text: 173 daśasaṃjñāsu anityasaṃjñāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 173. Chapter on the Perception of Impermanence among the Ten Perceptions (<s>daśasaṃjñāsu anityasaṃjñāvarga</s>)

body.text: anityasaṃjñā, duḥkhasaṃjñā, anātmasaṃjñā, āhāre pratikūlasaṃjñā, sarvaloke 'nabhiratisaṃjñā, aśubhasaṃjñā, maraṇasaṃjñā, prahāṇasaṃjñā, virāgasaṃjñā, nirodhasaṃjñā [cetidaśa saṃjñāḥ] | anityasaṃjñā yadanitye anityamiti samāhitaḥ prajānāti | (pṛ) kasmātsarvamanityam | (u) sarve hi dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ | hetupratyayavināśātsarve 'nityatāṃ yānti |
body.translated_text: The perception of impermanence (<s>anityasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of suffering (<s>duḥkhasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of non-self (<s>anātmasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of repulsiveness in food (<s>āhāre pratikūlasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of non-delight in the entire world (<s>sarvaloke anabhiratisaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the impure (<s>aśubhasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of death (<s>maraṇasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of dispassion (<s>virāgasaṃjñā</s>), and the perception of cessation (<s>nirodhasaṃjñā</s>) — these are the ten perceptions. The perception of impermanence is when one in concentration correctly knows the impermanent as impermanent. (Question) Why is everything impermanent? (Answer) All <s>dharmas</s> are dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>). Through the destruction of causes and conditions, all go to impermanence.

body.text: (pṛ) na yuktamidam | keciddharmāḥ pratītyasamutpannā api nānityāḥ | yathā tīrthikānāṃ sūtramāha- triṇāciketasya kartā śāśvate pade jāyate iti | brahmakāuyikāśca śāśvatāḥ | (u) bhavatāṃ śāsane 'pyuktam śakro devānāmindraḥ kratuśataṃ kṛtvā punaḥ patatīti | uktañca gāthāyām- śakrādayaḥ śatasahasrādhikānāṃ kratūnāmanuṣṭhātāro 'nityāḥ kṣīyanta itri | kratūnāṃ śatasahasramapi na vartate | ato jñāyate triṇāciketo 'nitya iti | śakro devānāmindro devendrādikāyabhāgaśca kṣīyate | ataḥpratītyasamutpannā dharmā anityāḥ | kiñca bhavatāṃ vedaḥ pūjyo 'bhimataḥ | vede punaruktam- vidyayā amṛtamaśnuta iti | yathāha- ādityavarṇo mahāpuruṣo lokasvabhāvamatītaḥ | tatpuruṣānugatamanasko 'mṛtamaśnute | na punaranyo mārgo 'stīti | "aṇoḥ puruṣasyāṇurātmā, mahato mahānātmā sadā kāye śete | ya imamātmānaṃ na veda | tasya vedādāvadhīyānasyāpi na kaścanopakāra iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) This is not correct. Some <s>dharmas</s>, though dependently arisen, are not impermanent. As the <s>sūtra</s> of the non-Buddhists states: 'The performer of the triple <s>Nāciketa</s> fire-rite is born in an eternal state.' And the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods are eternal. (Answer) In your own teaching it is also stated that <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, having performed a hundred sacrifices, falls again. And it is said in a verse: '<s>Śakra</s> and others, who performed more than a hundred thousand sacrifices, are impermanent and perish.' Even a hundred thousand sacrifices do not endure. Therefore it is known that the performer of the triple <s>Nāciketa</s> rite is impermanent. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, and the bodily portion of <s>Devendra</s> and such — all perish. Therefore dependently arisen <s>dharmas</s> are impermanent. Moreover, in your tradition the <s>Veda</s> is honored and esteemed. Yet in the <s>Veda</s> it is said: 'Through knowledge one attains immortality.' As stated: 'The great <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the color of the sun, has transcended the nature of the world. One whose mind follows that <s>Puruṣa</s> attains immortality. There is no other path.' 'The <s>ātman</s> (self) of the minute <s>puruṣa</s> is minute; the <s>ātman</s> of the great is great — it always rests in the body. One who does not know this <s>ātman</s>, even though studying the <s>Veda</s> from the beginning, derives no benefit.'

body.text: brahmakāyikāśca sarve 'nityāḥ | kasmāt | bhavatāṃ śāsane hyuktam- brahmā sahāṃpatirapi guṇānāṃ [prakarṣāya] sadā kratuṃ yajamāno vrataṃ dhatte iti | yadi kāyo nitya iti prajānāti | kasmāt puṇyaṃ karoti | śrūyate ca bhavatāṃ granthe vacanam- asti brahmaṇaḥ [sahāṃ] patermaithunarāgaḥ | sati ca tasmin dveṣādayaḥ sarve kleśā avaśyaṃ bhavanti | satsu kleśeṣu avaśyamasti pāpakarma | evaṃ pāpī kathaṃ nityaṃ vimokṣaṃ pratilabheta | na ca sarva ṛṣayo devān yajante | nāpi sarve brahmayānaṃ caranti | yadīdaṃ nityaṃ, tadā sarvathā tadācareyuḥ | sarve ca padārthā anityāḥ | kasmāt | yāni pṛthivyaptejovāyavo bhūtāni | tāni kalpāvasāne kṣīyamāṇāni na kiñcidavaśiṣyante | kālaśca cakravatpravartate | ato jñāyate 'nityānīti | śīlasamādhiprajñādyapramāṇaguṇasampannā mahānto dīpaṅkarabuddhādayaḥ pratyekabuddhā mahāsammatādayaḥ kalpādyā rājānaḥ sarve 'pyanityāḥ | kaḥ padārtho nityo bhavet | api ca bhagavānāha- yatkiñcitsamudayadharma, sarvaṃ tat vyayadharma iti | yathoktaṃ gomayapiṇḍisūtre- atha khalu bhagavān parīttaṃ gomayapiṇḍaṃ pāṇinā gṛhītvā taṃ bhikṣumetadavocat- nāsti kiñcidīdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ [yat rūpaṃ] nityaṃ dhruvaṃ [śāśvataṃ] avipariṇāmadharma [śāśvatasaṃjñam] iti | asminneva sūtre punarvistaraśa uktam- śakrabrahmacakravartirājānāṃ [ye] phalavipākāḥ [te sarve] 'pi atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā iti | ato jñāyate sarvamanityamiti |
body.translated_text: And all the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods are impermanent. Why? Because in your own teaching it is said: 'Even <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s> always performs sacrifices and observes vows for the enhancement of his qualities.' If he knows the body to be eternal, why does he perform merit? And it is heard in your scripture: '<s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s> has desire for sexual union.' When that exists, hatred and all other <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) necessarily arise. When <s>kleśas</s> exist, there necessarily is sinful <s>karma</s>. Being thus sinful, how could he attain eternal liberation? Not all <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) worship the gods, nor do all follow the path of <s>Brahmā</s>. If this were eternal, then they would all practice it in every way. And all things are impermanent. Why? Because the elements — earth, water, fire, and wind — at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle) perish and nothing remains. And time revolves like a wheel. Therefore it is known that they are impermanent. The great ones such as <s>Dīpaṅkara Buddha</s>, endowed with immeasurable qualities of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, kings from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> such as <s>Mahāsammata</s> — all are impermanent. What thing could be permanent? Moreover, the <s>Bhagavat</s> said: 'Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of cessation.' As stated in the <s>Gomayapiṇḍi Sūtra</s>: 'Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, taking a small ball of cow dung in his hand, said to that monk: "There is no form like this that is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change."' In that very <s>sūtra</s> it is further stated in detail: 'The fruition-results of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the wheel-turning kings — all have passed, ceased, and undergone change.' Therefore it is known that everything is impermanent.

body.text: traidhātukasya sarvasyāyuḥ parimitam | avīcinarakasya paramāyurekaḥ kalpaḥ | saṅghātanarakasya kalpārdham | anyeṣāṃ kiñcidūnaṃ vā adhikaṃ vā | nāgādīnāmāyuradhikataramekaḥ kalpaḥ | pretānāmadhikataramāyuḥ saptavarṣasahasrāṇi | [pūrva]videhānāmāyuḥ pañcāśaduttaravarṣaśatadvayam | [avara]godānīyānāmāyuḥ pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi | uttarakurūṇāṃ niyatāmāyurvarṣasahasram | jambūdvīpināmāyurapramāṇakalpā vā daśavarṣāṇi vāyuḥ | cāturmahārājikānāṃ devānāmāyuḥ pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi | yāvadbhavāgrāṇāmāyuraṣṭavarṣasahasrāṇi | ato jñāyate traidhātukaṃ sarvamanityamiti |
body.translated_text: The lifespan of all beings in the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>) is limited. The maximum lifespan in <s>Avīci</s> hell is one <s>kalpa</s>. In <s>Saṅghāta</s> hell it is half a <s>kalpa</s>. For others it is somewhat less or more. The lifespan of <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings) and such is at most one <s>kalpa</s>.
