body.translated_text: In the chapter on the path, it was shown that <s>śīla</s> is like a pillar. <s>Śīla</s> is the rampart of the city of the mind of <s>dhyāna-samādhi</s> (meditative concentration). <s>Śīla</s> is the bridge for crossing the flood of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). <s>Śīla</s> is the seal for entering the assembly of virtuous persons. <s>Śīla</s> is the embankment of the field of the eightfold noble path. Just as water does not remain in a field without an embankment, so too without purified <s>śīla</s>, the water of <s>samādhi</s> does not remain. (Question) Who is one of purified <s>śīla</s>? (Answer) The practitioner (<s>yogī</s>) whose disposition is not inclined toward evil actions, who fears the criticism of the next world and so forth — he is called one of purified <s>śīla</s>. Moreover, the practitioner maintains purified <s>śīla</s> for the purification of the mind. As stated in the <s>Saptamaithunārāga-sūtra</s>: 'Even when the body is without offense, if the mind is impure, then <s>śīla</s> too is impure.' The conditions for breaking <s>śīla</s>

body.text: sarve kleśāḥ | teṣāṃ pragrahe pariśuddhaśīlo bhavati | śrāvakāṇāṃ śīlaṃ nirvāṇārthameva | tathāgatamārgārthī mahākaruṇācittena sarvasattvānāṃ kṛte na śīlalakṣaṇaṃ samādatte | śīlamidaṃ [tathā] karoti yathā bodhisvabhāvo bhavati | īdṛśaṃ śīlaṃ pariśuddhamityucyate |
body.translated_text: are all the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). When these are restrained, one has purified <s>śīla</s>. The <s>śīla</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) is solely for the purpose of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. One who seeks the path of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with a mind of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), does not undertake <s>śīla</s> with the characteristic [limited to oneself] but for the sake of all beings. Such <s>śīla</s> is practiced so as to become the nature of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Such <s>śīla</s> is called purified.

body.text: abhisambodhiriti | uktaṃ hi sūtre- dvau khalvāyuṣman pratyayau samyakdṛṣṭerutpādāya parato ghoṣo yoniśo manaskāra iti | parato ghoṣa evābhisambodhiḥ | (pṛ) tathā cet abhisambodhimātramucyate | (u) uktaṃ hi sūtre- [anyataro] 'rhan bhagavantaṃ pṛcchati sma ekānte niṣaṇṇasya mama evamabhavat- abhisambodhisampadā tu mārgapratilābhasya vikalaḥ pratyaya iti | bhagavānavocat | maivaṃ vocaḥ yābhisaṃbodhiḥ sā tu mārgasya pratilābhasya sakalaḥ pratyayaḥ | kasmāt | jātijarāvyādhimaraṇāḥ sattvā ātmano 'bhisambodhiṃ labhamānā hi jātijarāvyādhimaraṇebhyo vimucyante iti | sattvāḥ sambodhimupādāya śīlādīn pañcadharmāt vipulayanti | tadyathā sālavṛkṣo himavantamupādāya pañca vastūni vardhayati | bhagavān svayameva sambodhyabhirataḥ | yathā prathamamārgalabdhasyaivamabhavat- yadi kaścidaguraḥ, tadā so 'paritrāso 'satkāracittaḥ sadā akuśaladharmaviparyasto 'nupaśamacaryaśca bhavati | kenācāryavān syām | kamupaniśritya tiṣṭhāmi | evaṃ cintayan sarvān matto 'viśiṣṭhānadrākṣam | tadaiva smṛtirudapādi pratilabdho mayā dharmaḥ yamupādāyābhisambuddhaḥ tameva dharmamupaniśrayiṣya iti | brahmādayo deva api prāśaṃsan nāsti kaścit buddhādviśiṣṭaḥ, sarve buddhāḥ saddharmagurukā iti | abhisambodhiśca pradīpasadṛśā |
body.translated_text: Regarding '<s>abhisambodhi</s>' (awakening): For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are indeed, venerable one, two conditions for the arising of right view: the voice of another (<s>parato ghoṣa</s>) and proper attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>).' The voice of another is precisely <s>abhisambodhi</s>. (Question) If that is so, is only <s>abhisambodhi</s> being spoken of? (Answer) For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A certain <s>arhat</s> asked the <s>Bhagavān</s> while seated at one side: "I had this thought: <s>abhisambodhi</s> is an incomplete condition for the attainment of the path." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Do not speak thus. <s>Abhisambodhi</s> is indeed a complete condition for the attainment of the path. Why? Because beings subject to birth, old age, disease, and death, by obtaining their own <s>abhisambodhi</s>, are liberated from birth, old age, disease, and death."' Beings, on the basis of <s>sambodhi</s> (awakening), develop the five qualities beginning with <s>śīla</s>. Just as a <s>sāla</s> tree, on the basis of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas), develops five substances. The <s>Bhagavān</s> himself delighted in <s>sambodhi</s>. Just as the one who first attained the path had this thought: 'If there is no teacher, then one would be fearless, disrespectful, always perverted by unwholesome qualities, and without the practice of pacification. Whose student should I be? On whom should I rely and abide?' Reflecting thus, he saw that all were not superior to himself. Then the recollection arose: 'The <s>dharma</s> which I have attained, on the basis of which I became fully awakened — I shall rely on that very <s>dharma</s>.' <s>Brahmā</s> and the other deities also praised: 'There is no one superior to the <s>Buddha</s>; all <s>Buddhas</s> revere the true <s>dharma</s>.' And <s>abhisambodhi</s> is like a lamp.

body.text: yathā kaścit sacakṣuṣko 'pi pradīpaṃ vinā na paśyati | tathā yoginaḥ puṇyaguṇatīkṣṇendriyatāpratyaye satyapi abhisambodhiṃ vinā na bhavati kaścanopakāraḥ | (pṛ) kā nāmābhisambodhiḥ | (u) yena puruṣaḥ saddharmān vardhayati sābhisambodhiḥ | sarve ca sajjanāḥ saddharme pratitiṣṭhanti [iti sā] sarvā devamanuṣyalokeṣvabhisambodhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as someone with eyesight cannot see without a lamp, so too for the practitioner, even when conditions of merit, virtue, and keen faculties are present, without <s>abhisambodhi</s> there is no benefit whatsoever. (Question) What then is <s>abhisambodhi</s>? (Answer) That by which a person develops wholesome qualities (<s>saddharma</s>) is <s>abhisambodhi</s>. And all virtuous persons are established in the true <s>dharma</s> — that is <s>abhisambodhi</s> throughout the worlds of gods and humans.

body.text: (3) indriyeṣu guptadvārateti yā samyak smṛtiḥ | yogī svātmānamanārakṣya na paśyati | ekāgracittaḥ samyak smṛtiṃ puraskṛtyaiva paśyet | saṃprajanyamiti ca [tasya] nāma | anena samprajanyena purotamālambanaṃ paryādāti | tatparyādānānna nimittamudgṛhṇāti | nimittānudgrahaṇāt na prajñaptimanusarati | indriyāṇāmagopane nimittodgrahaṇāt kleśāḥ pañcendriyāṇi strotovat pravartayanti | tadaiva śīlādīn saddharmān vināśayati | ya indriyeṣu guptadvāro bhavati tasya śīlādayaḥ sudṛḍhā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: (3) Regarding 'guarding the doors of the sense faculties (<s>indriyeṣu guptadvāratā</s>)': this is right mindfulness (<s>samyak smṛti</s>). The practitioner, without guarding himself, does not see rightly. Only with a one-pointed mind, placing right mindfulness at the forefront, does he see. Clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) is also its name. Through this clear comprehension, he takes hold of the foremost object. By taking hold of it, he does not grasp at signs (<s>nimitta</s>). By not grasping at signs, he does not follow after conceptual designations. When the sense faculties are unguarded, through the grasping of signs, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) drive the five sense faculties like a current. Then it destroys the wholesome qualities beginning with <s>śīla</s>. For one who guards the doors of the sense faculties, <s>śīla</s> and the other qualities become firmly established.

body.text: (4) bhojane ca mātrajñateti | na rūpabalāya [na] maithunāya [na] kāmānāmāsvādāya bhojanam | [yāvadevāsya] kāyasya yāpanāya | (pṛ) yogī kasmātkāyayāpanaṃ karoti | (u) saddharmasya bhāvanāyai | yaḥ saddharmāduparamate tasya mārgo na bhavati | asati mārge duḥkhādvisaṃyogo na bhavati | yadi kaścit kuśalasya bhāvanāyai na bhunakti | tadā [sa] vadhakaṃ corameva puṣṇāti | dānapateḥ puṇyañca vināśayati | janānāṃ satkārañca modhayati | evaṃ na bhuñjyāt janānāṃ bhojanam | (pṛ) bhojane ca kā mātrā | (u) yathā kāyaṃ yāpayati | sā mātrā | (pṛ) kiṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjyāt | (u) yat bhojanaṃ śītoṣṇādi vyādhiṃ kāmakrodhādyādhiñca na vardhayati | tat bhuñjyāt | tadapi bhojanaṃ yathākālaṃ bhuñjyāt | bhojanamidamasmin kāle śītoṣṇakāmakrodhādhivyādhiṃ vardhayatīti prajānan na bhuñjyāt |
body.translated_text: (4) Regarding 'knowing the right measure in food (<s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s>)': food is not for the sake of physical beauty, nor for sexual pleasure, nor for the enjoyment of desires — but only for the sustenance of this body. (Question) Why does the practitioner sustain the body? (Answer) For the cultivation of the true <s>dharma</s>. One who ceases from the true <s>dharma</s> has no path. Without the path, there is no separation from suffering. If someone does not eat for the cultivation of the wholesome, then he is merely nourishing a murderous thief. He destroys the merit of the donor. And he renders the respect of people fruitless. Thus one should not eat the food of others [carelessly]. (Question) What is the right measure in food? (Answer) That which sustains the body — that is the measure. (Question) What food should one eat? (Answer) Whatever food does not increase illness from cold, heat, and so forth, nor increases afflictions of desire, anger, and so forth — that one should eat. Moreover, one should eat that food at the proper time. Knowing 'this food at this time increases illness from cold, heat, desire, anger, and affliction,' one should not eat it.

body.text: (pṛ) tīrthikā vadanti- yaḥ pariśuddhamāhāraṃ bhuṅkte sa pariśuddhaṃ puṇyaṃ vindate | yat yatheṣṭhamabhimatarūparasagandhasparśavat approkṣitamabhinimantritaṃ bhuñjyate tat pariśuddhamityucyate | kathamidam | (u) bhojane nāsti pratiniyatā pariśuddhiḥ | kasmāt | yadi
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) say: 'One who eats pure food obtains pure merit. That which is eaten as desired, possessing pleasing form, taste, fragrance, and touch, unsprinkled and uninvited — that is called pure.' How is this? (Answer) There is no fixed purity in food. Why? If

body.text: paribhogenāhāro 'pariśuddho bhavati | sarva āhārā nāparibhojyāḥ | yathā stanyaṃ vatsaparibhuktam | madhu makṣikāparibhuktam | āpaḥ krimiparibhuktāḥ | kusumaṃ bhramaparibhuktam | phalaṃ pakṣiparibhuktam ityādi | kiñcāyaṃ kāyo 'śucisambhūtaḥ | kāyasvabhāvo 'śuciḥ aśuciparipūrṇaḥ | āhāraḥ pūrvamevāśuciḥ paścādapi kāyaṃ praviṣṭo naikadhāśucirbhavati | doṣaviparyayeṇa paraṃ śuciriti mithyā vadanti | (pṛ) yadyatyantamaśuciḥ [kāyaḥ] | tadā caṇḍālādibhiḥ ko viśeṣaḥ | (u) prāṇātipātādviratiradattādānādviratirmithyā jīvādviratirityādinā anurūpamāhāraṃ labdhvā āhāre ca pratikūlasaṃjñāṃ dṛṣṭvā prajñājalaprokṣitamatha tāvadbhuṅkte | na kevalaṃ jalaprokṣitaṃ punaḥ śucirbhavati |
body.translated_text: food becomes impure through being consumed [by another], then all foods would be unfit to eat. For example: milk has been consumed by the calf; honey has been consumed by bees; water has been consumed by worms; flowers have been consumed by bees; fruits have been consumed by birds, and so forth. Moreover, this body is born from impurity. The nature of the body is impure; it is filled with impurities. Food is already impure before [consumption], and after entering the body it becomes impure in many ways. Those who, through the reversal of faults, falsely claim it to be 'pure' are speaking wrongly. (Question) If the body is ultimately impure, then what is the difference from <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts) and the like? (Answer) Through abstention from killing, abstention from stealing, abstention from wrong livelihood, and so forth, obtaining appropriate food and perceiving food with the notion of repulsiveness, one eats having sprinkled it with the water of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). It is not that food merely sprinkled with water becomes pure.

body.text: (5) rātrya ādyāntimabhāge jāgaraṇateti | yogī prajānāti vyavasāyādhīnā kāryasiddhiriti | ato na nidrāti | paśyati na middhaṃ vṛthā, nānena kiñcillabhyata iti | yadi bhavān middhaṃ sukhaṃ manyate | tat sukhamatyalpaṃ dṛṣṭañca apāryapravacanam | kiñca yogī kleśaiḥ samamekatra nābhiramate | yathā kaściccoraiḥ saha vāse nābhiramate | kathaṃ kaścit loke corāṇāṃ raṇabhūmau nidrāsyati | ato na nidrāti |
body.translated_text: (5) Regarding 'wakefulness in the first and last portions of the night (<s>jāgaraṇa</s>)': the practitioner knows that the accomplishment of the task depends on diligent effort. Therefore he does not sleep. He sees that torpor (<s>middha</s>) is fruitless — nothing is gained by it. If you consider torpor to be happiness, that happiness is extremely small and is seen to be contrary to the noble teaching. Moreover, the practitioner does not delight in dwelling together with the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Just as someone does not delight in living with thieves — how could one sleep on the battlefield of thieves in this world? Therefore he does not sleep.

body.text: (pṛ) middhaṃ gāḍhamāgataṃ kathaṃ niruṇaddhi | (u) ayaṃ bhagavacchāsanāsvādane 'dhicittaṃ prītiñca labdhvā niruṇaddhi | saṃsāre ca jarāvyādhimaraṇadoṣānanusmarataścittaṃ bibhyati | ato na nidrāti | kiñca yogī paśyati- manuṣyakāyo labdhaḥ samagrāṇīndriyāṇi, prāptaṃ buddhaśāsanamanargham, sādhvasādhuviveko 'tiduṣkaraḥ, idānīṃ taraṇaṃ nānviṣyāmi, kadā vimokṣiṣya iti | ato middhaṃ tiraskartuṃ vīryamārabhate |
body.translated_text: (Question) How does one ward off torpor when it comes on strongly? (Answer) By tasting the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching and obtaining the higher mind and joy (<s>prīti</s>), one wards it off. And as one recollects the faults of old age, disease, and death in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), the mind becomes fearful. Therefore one does not sleep. Moreover, the practitioner sees: 'A human body has been obtained, the sense faculties are complete, the priceless teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> has been encountered, the discernment between good and evil is extremely difficult — if I do not now seek the crossing, when shall I be liberated?' Therefore he arouses energy (<s>vīrya</s>) to overcome torpor.

body.text: samādhipariṣkāreṣu ādyapañcasamādhipariṣkāravarga ekāśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and eighty-first chapter, the first chapter on the five requisites of <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samādhipariṣkāra</s>), in the section on the path (<s>mārgavarga</s>).

body.text: 182 akuśalavitarkavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 182. Chapter on unwholesome thoughts (<s>akuśalavitarkavarga</s>).

body.text: kuśalavitarkasampannateti | yadi kaścidanidrannapi akuśalavitarkānutpādayati yaduta kāmavitarko vyāpādavitarko vihiṃsāvitarko jātivitarko janapadavitarko 'maraṇavitarkaḥ parānugrahavitarkaḥ parāvamanyanāvitarka ityādayaḥ | varaṃ middham, naiṣāmakuśalānāṃ vitarkāṇāmutpādaḥ | naiṣkramyādikuśalavitarkān samyaganusmaret yaduta naiṣkramyavirtarko 'vyāpādāvihiṃsāvitarko 'ṣṭamahāpuruṣavitarkaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Endowed with wholesome thoughts' — if someone, even while awake, generates unwholesome thoughts, such as the thought of sensual desire (<s>kāmavitarka</s>), the thought of ill-will (<s>vyāpādavitarka</s>), the thought of harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsāvitarka</s>), the thought of kinsmen (<s>jātivitarka</s>), the thought of country (<s>janapadavitarka</s>), the thought of immortality (<s>amaraṇavitarka</s>), the thought of patronizing others (<s>parānugrahavitarka</s>), the thought of contempt for others (<s>parāvamanyanāvitarka</s>), and the like — then sleep is preferable to the arising of these unwholesome thoughts. One should rightly recollect the wholesome thoughts of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>) and the like, namely the thought of renunciation, the thought of non-ill-will (<s>avyāpāda</s>), the thought of non-harmfulness (<s>avihiṃsā</s>), and the eight thoughts of a great person (<s>aṣṭamahāpuruṣavitarka</s>).

body.text: kāmavitarka iti | yat kāmaṃ niśritya pañcakāmaguṇeṣūtpannavitarkaḥ paśyati hitaṃ sukhamiti | ayaṃ kāmavitarkaḥ | sattvānāṃ vihiṃsārtho[vitarko] vyāpādavitarko vihiṃsāvitarkaḥ | yogī nānusmaredimāṃstrīn vitarkān | kasmāt | tānanusmaran hi gurutaraṃ pāpaṃ vindate | pūrvamukta eva kāmādīnāmādīnavaḥ | teṣāmādīnavatvānnānusmaret |
body.translated_text: The thought of sensual desire means: depending on sensual pleasures, a thought arises in regard to the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>pañcakāmaguṇa</s>), seeing them as beneficial and pleasant. This is the thought of sensual desire. A thought for the purpose of harming beings is the thought of ill-will and the thought of harmfulness. The practitioner (<s>yogin</s>) should not recollect these three thoughts. Why? By recollecting them, one incurs even graver sin. The dangers of sensual desire and the rest have already been stated previously. Because of their dangerous nature, one should not recollect them.

body.text: (pṛ) mohavitarkaḥ kasmānnoktaḥ | (u) ime trayo 'kuśalavitarkāḥ kramikāḥ | anye kleśāstu naivaṃ bhavanti | yogī kadācitpañcakāmaguṇānusmaraṇātkāmavitarkamutpādayati | kāmitālābhāvdyāpādo bhavati | vyāpādasaṃsiddhā vihiṃsā | ato nokto mohādiḥ | mohasaṃsiddhameva phalaṃ yaduta vyāpādaḥ | yadi vyāpādādakuśalaḥ karmānto bhavati | te trayo vitarkā akuśalakarmahetavo bhavanti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- ayaṃ valmīko rātrau dhūmāyati | divā prajvalati | [yatkhalu bhikṣo divā karmāntānārabhya rātrā]vanuvitarkayati [anuvicārayati] idaṃ [rātrau] dhūmāyanam | [yatkhalu bhikṣo rātrāvanuvitarkayitvā divā] karmāntān [prayojayati kāyena vācā manasā | idaṃ [divā] prajvalanam |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is the thought of delusion (<s>mohavitarka</s>) not mentioned? (Answer) These three unwholesome thoughts are sequential. But other defilements are not like that. The practitioner sometimes, through the recollection of the five strands of sensual pleasure, generates the thought of sensual desire. From the non-obtaining of what is desired, ill-will arises. Harmfulness is accomplished from ill-will. Therefore delusion and the rest are not mentioned. The fruit accomplished from delusion is ill-will. If from ill-will unwholesome action follows, then these three thoughts become the causes of unwholesome <s>karma</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'This anthill smokes at night and blazes by day. That which, having undertaken actions by day, one thinks about and deliberates upon at night — this is the smoking at night. That which, having thought about and deliberated upon at night, one carries out by day through body, speech, and mind — this is the blazing by day.'

body.text: jñātivitarka iti | jñātivaśādutpadyante 'nusmaraṇāni | jñātiḥ kṣemakhukhaṃ vindatu
body.translated_text: The thought of kinsmen means: recollections arise on account of kinsmen. One wishes: 'May my kinsmen find safety and happiness.'

body.text: itīcchati | tasya vināśavihiṃsāmanusmarataḥ śoka utpadyate | yat jñātibhirekakāryāṇyanusmarati [ayaṃ] jñātivitarkaḥ | yogī nānusmaredimaṃ vitarkam | kasmāt | pūrvameva hi pravrajyākāle jñātīn tyaktavān | idānīṃ tadvikarmāśrayaṇaṃ nānurūpaṃ bhavati | yadi pravrajitaḥ imaṃ jñātivitarkamanusmarati | tadā gṛhaparivāraparityāgo vṛthākiñcitsādhanaḥ | jñātisnehādadhyavasānaṃ bhavati | adhyavasānādārakṣā | ārakṣāpratyayaṃ daṇḍādānaśastrādānādikarmānukramaṃ pravartate | ato notpādayet jñātivitarkam | jñātisamāgame ca kuśaladharmaṃ na vardhayati | yoginā smartavyaṃ sarveṣu sattveṣu jananamaraṇapravāhapravṛtteṣu nāsti jñātirajñātiḥ | kasmāt paryāsajyate iti | saṃsāre jñātyarthameva śokakaruṇaparidevāśrūṇi mahāsāgaranirvartanāni bhavanti | idānīṃ punaradhyavasāne duḥkhamanavasthameva | sattvāśca kāryanimittaṃ hi mithaḥ snihyanti | nāsti tu kutracit snehanaiyatyam | jñātīnāmanusmaraṇamidaṃ mohalakṣaṇam | laukikā mūḍhāḥ svahitavihīnāḥ parahitaṃ kāmayante | jñātimanusmarataḥ svahitamatyalpaṃ bhavati | ityebhiḥ [kāraṇaiḥ] yogī na jñātivitarkamutpādayet |
body.translated_text: Recollecting the destruction and harm [of kinsmen], grief arises. That which recollects affairs shared with kinsmen — this is the thought of kinsmen. The practitioner should not recollect this thought. Why? Because at the very time of going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), one already abandoned one's kinsmen. Now, taking refuge in activities concerning them is not fitting. If one who has gone forth recollects this thought of kinsmen, then the abandonment of home and family is in vain — nothing is accomplished. From affection for kinsmen comes attachment. From attachment comes guarding. From the condition of guarding, a sequence of actions such as taking up sticks and weapons follows. Therefore one should not generate the thought of kinsmen. And in the company of kinsmen, one does not increase in wholesome <s>dharma</s>. The practitioner should reflect: 'In the flow of birth and death that pervades all beings, there is neither kinsman nor non-kinsman. Why then is one attached?' In <s>saṃsāra</s>, for the sake of kinsmen alone, the tears of grief, sorrow, and lamentation are enough to fill the great ocean. Now, if one again becomes attached, there is nothing but endless suffering. And beings are affectionate toward each other merely because of shared purposes — there is no constancy in affection anywhere. This recollection of kinsmen has the characteristic of delusion. Worldly people, deluded and devoid of their own benefit, desire the benefit of others. For one who recollects kinsmen, one's own benefit becomes exceedingly small. For these reasons, the practitioner should not generate the thought of kinsmen.

body.text: janapadavitarka iti | yogī [kaścit] cintayati- amuko janapadaḥ sukhaḥ kṣemaḥ śivaḥ, tatra gatvā nibhṛtaṃ sukhaṃ lapsya iti | cittañca capalaṃ sarvatra bhramaṇadarśanakāṃkṣīti | yogī nedṛśaṃ vitarkamutpādayet | kasmāt | sarveṣu hi janapadeṣu asti kaściddoṣaḥ | kaścijjanapado 'tiśītaḥ | kaścidatyuṣṇaḥ | kaścit kṣāmabahalaḥ | kaściccorabahulaḥ | evamādayo vividhā doṣāḥ santītyato na cintayet | yaścapalaḥ sa dhyānasamādheḥ parihīyate | yatrābhirataḥ kuśaladharmaṃ vardhayati ayaṃ ramaṇīya ityucyate | ka upayogo janapadānāṃ paryālokanena | sarvo janapado dūrata eva śrāvyo nāvaśyaṃ gatvā ślāghanīyaḥ | laukikā bahudhā duṣṭā iti vacanāt | janapadeṣu bhramaṇī nānāduḥkhānyanubhavati | kāyo 'yaṃ duḥkhahetuḥ | duḥkhahetumimaṃ kāyaṃ dhṛtvā yatra yatra gacchati tatra tatra duḥkhānyanubhavati | sukhaduḥkhavedanā karmakāraṇādhīnā | sudūraṃ gacchato 'pi nāsti kaścanopakāraḥ | ato na janapadavitarkamutpādayet |
body.translated_text: The thought of country means: the practitioner thinks — 'Such-and-such a country is pleasant, safe, and peaceful; having gone there, I shall quietly obtain happiness.' And the mind is fickle, desiring to wander about seeing everything. The practitioner should not generate such a thought. Why? In all countries, there is some fault. Some country is excessively cold. Some is excessively hot. Some is plagued by famine. Some is infested with thieves. Various faults of this kind exist — therefore one should not think [thus]. And one who is fickle falls away from <s>dhyāna</s> and concentration. Wherever one is content and increases in wholesome <s>dharma</s> — that place is called 'delightful.' What use is there in surveying countries? Every country is [merely] pleasant to hear about from afar — not necessarily praiseworthy upon visiting. Because it is said: 'Worldly people are wicked in many ways.' One who wanders among countries experiences various sufferings. This body is a cause of suffering. Carrying this body, which is a cause of suffering, wherever one goes, there one experiences sufferings. The experience of pleasant and painful feelings depends on the cause of <s>karma</s>. Even for one who travels very far, there is no benefit whatsoever. Therefore one should not generate the thought of country.

body.text: amaraṇavitarka iti | yogī cintayatyevam- mārgo mayā paścādbhāvayitavyaḥ | ādau sūtravinayābhidharmakṣudrakapiṭakabodhisattvapiṭakānyadhyetavyāni | bāhyagranthāśca suvistaramabhyasitavyāḥ | bahavaḥ śiṣyā ārjayitavyāḥ | kalyāṇamitramupasthāya caturastūpān vanditvā janāna mahādānaṃ kartuṃ protsāhya ca paścānmārgo bhāvayitavya iti | [aya]mamaraṇavitarkaḥ | naivaṃ cintayet yogī | kasmāt | na hi maraṇakālo niyataḥ | na pūrvameva jñeyaḥ | vṛttyantareṣu vyāpṛtena na mārgo bhāvituṃ śakyaḥ | paścānmaraṇakāle samupasthite cittaṃ kaukṛtyena pīḍyate | mayāyaṃ kāyo vṛthā poṣitaḥ na kiñcillabdham | paśubhiḥ samaṃ mriyata iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- pṛthagjano viṃśatidhā svacittaṃ nigṛhyevaṃ cintayet- vibhinnākāraveṣamātraṃ mama vṛthā [sarvaṃ] na kiñcillabdham, yāvadāmaraṇamadānto bhaviṣyāmīti | paṇḍito na karotyakāryam | yathoktaṃ dharmapade-
body.translated_text: The thought of immortality means: the practitioner thinks thus — 'The path should be cultivated by me later. First I should study the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, <s>Abhidharma</s>, <s>Kṣudraka</s> collections, and the <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s>. The outer treatises too should be thoroughly studied in detail. Many disciples should be gathered. Having attended upon a virtuous friend, having venerated the four <s>stūpas</s>, and having encouraged people in great giving — only afterward should the path be cultivated.' This is the thought of immortality. The practitioner should not think thus. Why? The time of death is not fixed. It cannot be known beforehand. While occupied with other activities, one is unable to cultivate the path. Afterward, when the time of death is at hand, the mind is tormented by remorse: 'I have nourished this body in vain — nothing was obtained. I die like an animal.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'An ordinary person should discipline his own mind in twenty ways and reflect thus: "Of diverse appearance, garb, and measure, for me [all is] in vain — nothing is obtained; until death, I shall remain untamed."' A wise person does not do what should not be done. As stated in the <s>Dharmapada</s>:

body.text: yeṣāñca susamārabdhā nityaṃ kāyagatā smṛtiḥ
body.translated_text: 'For those in whom mindfulness of the body is always well-established, who never engage in what should not be done, who are constant in their practice — for the mindful and clearly comprehending, the outflows come to an end.'

body.text:
akṛtyaṃ te na sevante nityaṃ sātatyakāriṇaḥ |
smṛtānāṃ samprajānānāmastaṃ gacchanti cāsravāḥ || iti |
api coktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
catussatyeṣvalābhī [yaḥ] kāmān labdhumupāyataḥ |
yatnena vīryamātiṣṭhet bhṛśaṃ tatparipālane || iti |
body.translated_text: 'One who has not obtained [realization of] the four truths should, by skillful means, strive to obtain the desired [goal], and diligently exert effort in its preservation.'

body.text: ato nāmaraṇavitarkamutpādayet | amaraṇavitarkaśca mūḍhasya prāṇitam | ko jñānī tṛṇāgre 'vaśyāyabinduvat jīvitamadhruvaṃ jñātvā kṣaṇamekaṃ jīveyamiti [manyeta] | uktañca sūtre- bhagavānavocat kathaṃ pūnaryūyaṃ bhikṣavo bhāvayatha maraṇasmṛtim | [anyataro
body.translated_text: Therefore one should not generate the thought of immortality. The thought of immortality is the life of a deluded person. What wise person, knowing that life is as impermanent as a dewdrop on the tip of a blade of grass, would think 'I shall live for even a single moment'? And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: The Blessed One said: 'How then, monks, do you cultivate the recollection of death?' [One

body.text: bhikṣu]rbhagavantamavocat- [iha mamaivaṃ bhavati- aho vata] ahaṃ sapta varṣāṇi na jīveyamiti | evamapacayo 'bhūta yāvanmuhūrtaṃ na [jīveya]miti | anya[taro bhikṣurbhagavantametadavocat] ahaṃ ṣaḍ varṣāṇi na jīveyamiti | evamapacayo 'bhūt- yāvanmuhūtamapi [na jīveya]miti | evamukte bhagavān tān bhikṣūnetadavocat- yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ pramattā [viharatha, dandhā]maraṇasmṛtiṃ bhāvayatha iti | anyataro bhikṣu [rbhagavanta]mupetyāvocat[mamaivaṃ bhavati aho bata] ahaṃ [tadantaraṃ] na jīveyaṃ yadantaraṃ āśvasitvā praśvasāmi praśvasitvā vāśvasāmi iti | bhagavānavocat- sādhu sādhu tvaṃ [khalu bhikṣo] bhāvayasi maraṇasmṛtim iti | ato notpādayedamaraṇasaṃjñām |
body.translated_text: monk] said to the Blessed One: 'Here, I think thus — may I not live for seven years.' Thus there was a gradual reduction until [one said]: 'May I not live even for a moment.' Another monk said to the Blessed One: 'May I not live for six years.' Thus there was a gradual reduction until [one said]: 'May I not live even for a moment.' When this was said, the Blessed One said to those monks: 'You, monks, dwell heedlessly. You cultivate the recollection of death sluggishly.' Another monk approached the Blessed One and said: 'I think thus — may I not live for the interval between breathing in and breathing out, or between breathing out and breathing in.' The Blessed One said: 'Good, good! You indeed, monk, cultivate the recollection of death.' Therefore one should not generate the perception of immortality.

body.text: parānugrahavitarka iti [yad]bandhāvanugrahaprāpaṇamicchati | yadyevaṃ cintayati- amukaṃ dhanamānasukhānāṃ dānamācarayāmi | amukastu nopaiti iti | yogī nedṛśaṃ vitarkamutpādayet | kasmāt | nānayā smṛtyā parasya sukhaṃ dukhaṃ vā prāpayati | kintu samāhitaṃ cittameva vikṣipati | (pṛ) parasyānugrahacikīrṣā kiṃ karuṇācittaṃ nanu | (u) yogī mārgamarthayan cintayetpāramārthikaṃ hitaṃ yaduta anityatādi | yadyapyatra kiñcitpuṇyamasti tathāpi mārgapratirodhakasya hitamalpaṃ, doṣastu bahulaḥ | samāhitacittasya vikṣepāt | yo vyagracittatayā parasya hitamanusmarati | sa kāmāsaktyā nādīnavaṃ paśyati | ato nānucintayet |
body.translated_text: The thought of patronizing others means: one who wishes to bring benefit to kinsmen. If one thinks thus: 'I shall procure the giving of wealth, honor, and happiness for such-and-such a person. But that person does not approach [me].' The practitioner should not generate such a thought. Why? By this mindfulness, one neither brings happiness nor suffering to another. Rather, it merely scatters the concentrated mind. (Question) Is not the wish to benefit another the mind of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>)? (Answer) The practitioner, seeking the path, should contemplate the ultimate benefit, namely impermanence and the like. Even though there is some merit in this [patronizing thought], the benefit of obstructing the path is small, while the fault is great — because of scattering the concentrated mind. One who, with a distracted mind, recollects the benefit of another — he does not see the danger of attachment to sensual pleasures. Therefore one should not think [thus].

body.text: parāvamanyanāvitarka iti | yadyogī cintayati- gotravaṃśākṛtirūpadhanamānanaipuṇyeṣu śīlatīkṣṇendriyatvadhyānasamādhiprajñādiṣu ca nāyaṃ matsama iti | nedṛśaṃ yogī vitarkamutpādayet | kasmāt | sarveṣāṃ vastunāmanityatvāt | ya uttamo 'dhama iti | teṣu ko viśeṣo 'sti | eṣāṃ kāyakeśaromanakhadantaṃ sarvamaśuci, samaṃ bhavati na viṣamam | jarāvyādhimaraṇādivipadapi samā | sarveṣāṃ sattvānāmadhyātmaṃ bahirdhā ca duḥkhavihiṃsāpi samā na
body.translated_text: The thought of contempt for others means: the practitioner thinks — 'In lineage, family, appearance, beauty, wealth, honor, skill, moral conduct, sharpness of faculties, <s>dhyāna</s>, concentration, wisdom, and the like — this person is not my equal.' The practitioner should not generate such a thought. Why? Because all things are impermanent. As for one being superior and another inferior — what distinction is there among them? The hair, body-hair, nails, and teeth of all of these — everything is impure, and equal, not unequal. The misfortune of old age, sickness, death, and the like is also equal. For all beings, inwardly and outwardly, suffering and harm too are equal, not

body.text: viṣamā | pṛthagjanānāṃ dhanasamṛddhiḥ pāpapratyayā | dhanasamṛddhiśca na dīrghakālikī | [ataḥ] punardaridro bhavati | ato na parāvamanyanāvitarkamutpādayet | ayaṃ māno 'vidyāṅgam | vidvān kathamimaṃ vitarkamutpādayiṣyati ||
body.translated_text: unequal. The prosperity of wealth among ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) is conditioned by sin. And the prosperity of wealth is not long-lasting. Therefore one becomes poor again. Therefore one should not generate the thought of contempt for others. This conceit is a limb of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). How would a wise person generate this thought?

body.text: akuśalavitarkavargo dvyaśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and eighty-second chapter, the Chapter on Unwholesome Thoughts (<s>akuśalavitarkavarga</s>).

body.text: 183 kuśalavitarkavargaḥ |
body.translated_text: 183. Chapter on Wholesome Thoughts (<s>kuśalavitarkavarga</s>).

body.text: naiṣkramyavitarka iti pravivekābhilāṣicittatā | yat pañcakāmaguṇebhyo rūpārūpyadhātubhyaśca pravivekaḥ | asmin praviveke 'bhilāṣo naiṣkramyavitarkaḥ | pravivekābhilāṣādasmā dduḥkhānāmasambhavāt | kāmāsaktivaśāddhi duḥkhaṃ bhavati | asatyāṃ kāmāsaktau sukhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: The thought of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramyavitarka</s>) is the mind that desires seclusion (<s>praviveka</s>). Seclusion means separation from the five strands of sensual pleasure, from the form realm, and from the formless realm. The desire for this seclusion is the thought of renunciation. Because of the desire for seclusion, sufferings do not arise. For suffering comes from attachment to sensual pleasures. When there is no attachment to sensual pleasures, there is happiness.

body.text: vitarkeṣu dvau vitarkau sukhaṃ yadutāvyāpadavitarko 'vihiṃsāvitarkaḥ | kasmāt | dvau hīmau vitarkau kṣemavitarkau | yathoktaṃ tathāgatavarge- tathāgatasya khalu dvau vitarkau nityamupatiṣṭhato yaduta yogakṣemavitarkaḥ pravivekavitarkaśca iti | yogakṣemavitarkaḥ avyāpādāvihiṃsāvitarka eva | pravivekavitarko naiṣkramyavitarkaḥ | trīnimān vitarkayataḥ puṇyaṃ vardhate | samāhitacittattāpi sidhyati | cittaṃ viśudhyate ca | trīnimān vitarkān vitarkayan paryutthānāni pratihanti | paryutthānānāṃ samucchedāt prahāṇaṃ sākṣātkaroti | kiñca yogī pravivekāmilāṣayā bahūnāṃ kuśaladharmāṇāmupacayādāśu vimucyate |
body.translated_text: Among thoughts, two thoughts are happy, namely the thought of non-ill-will (<s>avyāpādavitarka</s>) and the thought of non-harmfulness (<s>avihiṃsāvitarka</s>). Why? Because these two thoughts are thoughts of welfare (<s>kṣema</s>). As stated in the Chapter on the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Two thoughts constantly attend the <s>Tathāgata</s>, namely the thought of welfare and the thought of seclusion.' The thought of welfare is the thought of non-ill-will and non-harmfulness. The thought of seclusion is the thought of renunciation. For one who thinks these three, merit increases, the state of concentrated mind is also accomplished, and the mind is purified. By thinking these three thoughts, one wards off the active defilements (<s>paryutthāna</s>). Through the complete eradication of the active defilements, one directly realizes abandonment. Furthermore, through the practitioner's desire for seclusion and the accumulation of many wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one is quickly liberated.

body.text: aṣṭamahāpuruṣavitarka iti alpecchasyāyaṃ dharmo nā[yaṃ dharmo] mahecchasya | santuṣṭasyā[yaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ dharmo 'santuṣṭasya] | praviviktasya [ayaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ dharmaḥ
body.translated_text: The eight thoughts of a great person (<s>aṣṭamahāpuruṣavitarka</s>) are: 'This <s>dharma</s> is for one of few desires, not for one of many desires. This <s>dharma</s> is for one who is content, not for one who is discontent. This <s>dharma</s> is for one who dwells in seclusion, not for one who

body.text: saṅgaṇikārāmasya] | ārabdhavīryasya [ayaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ dharmaḥ kusīdasya] | upasthitasmṛtikasya [ayaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ dharmo muṣṭasmṛtikasya] | samāhitasya [ayaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ dharmo 'samāhitasya] | prajñāvato ['yaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ dharmo duṣprajñasya] | niṣprapañcārāmasyāyaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ dharmaḥ prapañcārāmasya itīme 'ṣṭau |
body.translated_text: one who delights not in socializing] — of one who has aroused energy [this is the <s>dharma</s>, not the <s>dharma</s> of the indolent] — of one with established <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) [this is the <s>dharma</s>, not the <s>dharma</s> of one who has lost <s>smṛti</s>] — of one who is concentrated [this is the <s>dharma</s>, not the <s>dharma</s> of one who is unconcentrated] — of one possessing <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) [this is the <s>dharma</s>, not the <s>dharma</s> of one of poor wisdom] — of one who delights in freedom from <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation), this is the <s>dharma</s>, not the <s>dharma</s> of one who delights in <s>prapañca</s> — these are the eight.

body.text: alpeccho yogī yo mārgaṃ bhāvayitumapekṣitamicchati | na bahu prārthayate anyadanupayuktam | ayamalpecchaḥ | santuṣṭa iti | kaścit [kenacit] kāraṇena vā śīlāya vā parasya cittaprasādanāya vālpaṃ gṛhṇāti na tu santuṣṭacitto bhavati | yo 'lpaṃ gṛhītvā santuṣṭacitto bhavati | ayaṃ santuṣṭaḥ | kaścidalpaṃ gṛhītvāpi ramaṇīyaṃ kāmayate | ayamalpeccho na santuṣṭaḥ | yo 'lpalābhena tṛpyati sa santuṣṭaḥ | (pṛ) yadyapekṣitagrāhī alpeccha iti | sarve sattvā alpecchā bhaveyuḥ | eṣāṃ pratyekamapekṣitatvāt | (u) yogī anāsaktattittatayā gṛhṇāti upayogārthamātraṃ, na bahu gṛhṇāti | na tu yathā laukikā yaśomaṇḍanavardhanāya bahu gṛhṇānti | (pṛ) yogī kasmādalpecchayaḥ santuṣṭo bhavati | (u) [sa] hi paripālanādāvādīnavaṃ paśyati | anupayuktadravyasaṅgrahaḥ sammūḍhasya lakṣaṇam | pravrajito na bahu sañcinvannavadātavasanaiḥ samo bhavet | tādṛśadoṣasattvādalpecchaḥ santuṣṭo bhavati | yogī yadi nālpecchaḥ santuṣṭaḥ, tadā kāmacittaṃ kramaśo vardheta | dhanalābhitvādaprārthanīyaṃ prārthayīta | dhanalābhābhilāṣaśca naiva saṃśāmyati | [tatra] adhyavasāyitvāt | pravivekasukhāya pravrajito dhanakāmitayā tatkaraṇīyaṃ vismarati | kleśānapi na prajahāti | kasmāt | bāhyapadārthāneva na prajahāti | kaḥ punarvāda ādhyātmikān dharmān prajahātīti | lābhadṛṣṭirvipattivihiṃsāhetuḥ | yathā karakavṛṣṭiḥ sasyāni vināśayati | ataḥ satatamalpecchasantuṣṭatāṃ bhāvayet |
body.translated_text: <s>Alpeccha</s> (having few desires): a <s>yogī</s> who desires only what is necessary for cultivating the path, who does not seek much that is useless — this is one of few desires. As for being content (<s>santuṣṭa</s>): someone may, for some reason, or for the sake of moral conduct, or to please another's mind, accept little, yet not be content in mind. One who, having accepted little, is content in mind — this is the contented one. Someone may accept little yet desire what is pleasant — this one has few desires but is not contented. One who is satisfied with small gains is contented. (Question) If one who accepts only what is needed is called one of few desires, then all beings would be of few desires, since each has their own needs. (Answer) The <s>yogī</s> accepts without attachment, only for the purpose of use, and does not accept much — not like worldly people who accept much for the sake of enhancing fame and adornment. (Question) Why does the <s>yogī</s> of few desires become contented? (Answer) Because he sees the faults in guarding and so forth. Accumulating useless possessions is the mark of a deluded person. A renunciant who hoards much would be no different from white-clad laypeople. Because of such faults, one of few desires becomes contented. If the <s>yogī</s> were not of few desires and contented, then the mind of desire would gradually increase; due to gaining wealth, one would seek what should not be sought; and the craving for wealth never ceases — because of one's determination in that regard. One who has gone forth for the happiness of solitude, due to desire for wealth, forgets what should be done. One does not even abandon the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Why? Because one does not even abandon external things — how much less would one abandon internal <s>dharmas</s>? The view attached to gain is a cause of calamity and harm, just as a hailstorm destroys crops. Therefore, one should constantly cultivate having few desires and contentment.

body.text: dṛśyate ca deyasya padārthasya pratyarpaṇaṃ duṣkaram | yaṭhā ṛṇī [ṛṇa]mapratyarpayan paścāttadduḥkhaṃ vyathāmanubhavati iti | lābhasatkāradṛṣṭiḥ buddhādibhiḥ sajjānaistyaktā |
body.translated_text: And it is seen that returning a thing that has been given is difficult, just as a debtor who does not repay his debt later experiences that suffering and distress. The view attached to gain and honor has been abandoned by the <s>Buddha</s> and other virtuous ones.

body.text: yathāha bhagavān- nāhaṃ lābhasatkāramanuprāpnomi mā lābhasatkāro māmanuprāpnotviti | ayañca yogī saddharmasantuṣṭatvāllābhasatkāraṃ prajahāti | yathāha bhagavān- devā na pratilabhante naiṣkramyasukhaṃ pravivekasukhamupaśamasukhaṃ yathā mayā pratilabdham | ato lābhasatkāraṃ prajahāmi iti | yathāha śāriputraḥ-
body.translated_text: As the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'I do not pursue gain and honor; may gain and honor not pursue me.' And this <s>yogī</s> abandons gain and honor because he is contented with the true <s>dharma</s>. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The <s>devas</s> do not obtain the happiness of renunciation, the happiness of solitude, the happiness of tranquility, as I have obtained them. Therefore I abandon gain and honor.' As <s>Śāriputra</s> said:

body.text:
animittaṃ bhāvayitvā cāhaṃ śūnyasamādhinā |
samīkṣe sarvavastūni kheṭapiṇḍān yathā bahiḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Having cultivated the signless, through the emptiness <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),
I regard all things as spittle-lumps cast outside.' Thus it is said.

body.text: kiñca yogī paśyati na kāmopabhogena tṛptirbhavati | yathā lavaṇodakaṃ piban na tarṣaṇamapanayati iti prajñāṃ prarthayānastṛpto bhavati |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>yogī</s> sees that there is no satisfaction through the enjoyment of desires, just as one who drinks salt water does not quench thirst — thus one who seeks <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) remains unsatisfied.

body.text: mahecchaḥ sadā prārthanāmutpādayan bahu prārthayitvālpaṃ vindate | ataḥ sadā khidyate | paśyāmaśca bhikṣārthī janairavamanyate na satkriyate yathālpecchaḥ | pravrajito mahatprārthayata ityakāryametat | janairdattasyāgrahaṇantu yuktarūpam | ato 'lpecchāsantuṣṭimācaret |
body.translated_text: One of great desires (<s>maheccha</s>), constantly generating cravings, though seeking much, obtains little. Therefore one is always distressed. And we see that one who begs for alms is despised by people and not respected, unlike one of few desires. That a renunciant should seek much — this is improper conduct. But not accepting what people offer would be appropriate. Therefore one should practice having few desires and contentment.

body.text: pravivikta iti yat gṛhasthapravrajitayoḥ kāyikapravivekasamācāraḥ kleśeṣu mānasapravivekasamācāraḥ ayaṃ pravivekaḥ | (pṛ) yogī kasmātpravivikto bhavati | (u) pravrajitā apratilabdhamārgā api pravivekārāmā bhavanti | avadātavasanādayaḥ tatsthānagatastrīrūpavikṣepāvakṛṣṭā na tatra kadācitsukhino bhavanti | praviveke tu cittaṃ sūpaśamaṃ bhavati | yathā salilamanāvilaṃ prakṛtitaḥ svaccham | ataḥ praviveke carati | pravivekadharmo 'yaṃ gaṅgānadīvālukāsamairbuddhairabhisaṃstutaḥ | kenedaṃ jñāyate | bhagavān grāmopakaṇṭhe niṣaṇṇaṃ bhikṣuṃ dṛṣṭvā aprītamanasko bhavati | śūnyāyatane ca śayānaṃ bhikṣuṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavān prītamanasko bhavati | tatkasya hetoḥ | grāmopakaṇṭhe niṣṣaṇṇasya bhikṣorbahubhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ samāhitacittavikṣepe labdhavyaṃ na labhyate sākṣātkartavyaṃ na sākṣātkriyate | śūnyāyatane śayānasya kiñcitkausīdye satyapi samādhyāśāsambhave cittaṃ parigṛhyate | parigṛhītaṃ cittaṃ vimucyate | nimittodgrahamupādāya ca kāmādayaḥ kleśāḥ samudbhavanti | śūnyāyatane na rūpādīni nimittāni santīti kleśāḥ suprahāṇāḥ | yathāgnirasatīndhane svataḥ śāmyati | uktañcasūtre- yo bhikṣuḥ saṅgaṇikāvihārarataḥ sambhāṣyarataḥ [sa] gaṇādavivikta ityataḥ sāmayikīmeva vimuktiṃ na
body.translated_text: As for being secluded (<s>pravivikta</s>): the practice of physical seclusion between householders and renunciants, and the practice of mental seclusion from the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — this is seclusion. (Question) Why does the <s>yogī</s> become secluded? (Answer) Even renunciants who have not attained the path delight in seclusion. White-clad laypeople and others, drawn by the distraction of the forms of women at their places, are never happy there. But in seclusion, the mind becomes well-calmed, just as water that is undisturbed is naturally clear. Therefore one dwells in seclusion. This quality of seclusion has been praised by <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. How is this known? By the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words

body.text: pratilabhate | kaḥ punarvādaḥ akopyāṃ vimuktiṃ pratilabhata iti | praviviktavihārī punarubhayaṃ sākṣātkurute | iti | yathā pradīpo vātaviviktaḥ prakāśate | evaṃ yogī pravivekavihāritayā tattvajñānaṃ vindate |
body.translated_text: one attains. How much more so would one attain the unshakeable <s>vimukti</s> (liberation)! Furthermore, one who dwells in seclusion directly realizes both. Thus, just as a lamp sheltered from the wind shines brightly, so the <s>yogī</s>, through dwelling in seclusion, obtains the knowledge of reality.

body.text: ārabdhavīrya iti | yogī yadi samyakpradhānamācaran akuśaladharmān prajahāti kuśaladharmāṃśca sañcinoti | [tadā] tatra samyakpradhānāmācaratīti ārabdhavīrya ityucyate | evañca bhagavacchāsane hitaṃ pratilabhate | tatkasya hetoḥ | [sa hi] kuśaladharmasañcayena pratidinamabhivardhate | yathotpalapadmādīni yathāsalilamabhivardhante | kausīdyacārī punaḥ kāṣṭhamusalavat prathamābhinirvartanādārabhya pratidīnamapacīyate | ārabdhavīryasya arthapratilābhitayā cittaṃ sadā pramudyate | kausīdyacārī tu akuśaladharmanivṛttacittaḥ satataṃ duḥkhopadravamanubadhnāti | ārabdhavīryasya ca kṣaṇe kṣaṇe kuśaladharmo nityamabhivardhate, nāpacīyate | vīryaprakṛṣṭamācarannāpnoti prakṛṣṭaṃ sthānaṃ yaduta buddhānāṃ gatim | yathoktaṃ sūtre bhagavatā ānandaṃ prati prakṛṣṭaṃ vīryamabhyasan buddhagatiṃ yātīti | ārabdhavīryasya cittasamādhīḥ sulabhaḥ | mandendriya ārabdhavīryaḥ saṃsārādevāśu mucyate | tīṣṇendriyaḥ kusīdastu na vimucyate | yadasti kiñcidaihikamāmuṣmikaṃ laukikaṃ lokottaraṃ hitaṃ, tat sarvaṃ vīryamupādāya bhavati | sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ yadasti alābhavyasanaṃ, tat sarvaṃ kausīdyamupādāya bhavati | evaṃ kusīdasya doṣamārabdhavīryasya guṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vīryamanusmarati |
body.translated_text: As for having aroused energy (<s>ārabdhavīrya</s>): if the <s>yogī</s> practices the <s>samyakpradhāna</s> (right exertion) properly, abandoning unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and accumulating wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, then he is said to be one of aroused energy because he practices right exertion. And thus he attains benefit in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. For what reason? Because through the accumulation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, he increases day by day, just as lotuses and water-lilies grow as water rises. But one who practices laziness, like a wooden pestle, diminishes day by day from its initial creation. For one of aroused energy, the mind always rejoices due to the attainment of the goal. But one who practices laziness, being unwholesome

body.text: upasthitasmṛtika iti | kāyavedanācittadharmeṣu sadā smṛtiṃ samupasthāpayati | (pṛ) eṣāṃ caturṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ smṛtyā kīdṛśaṃ hitaṃ vindate | (u) pāpakā akuśalā dharmā na cittamāgacchanti | yathā surakṣite na pāpakaḥ puruṣo 'vatarati | yathā ca ghaṭaḥ pūrṇo na punarudakamādatte | evamasya puruṣasya kuśaladharmasampūrṇasya na pāpakāni prasajyante | yo bhāvitasamyaksmṛtikaḥ sa vimuktibhāgīyān sarvān kuśaladharmān saṅgṛhṇāti | yathā samudrāmbupāyinaḥ sarvāṇi strotāṃsi pītāni bhavanti | sarveṣāmudakānāṃ samudravartitvāt | asyāḥ smṛterbhāvayitā svatantracaryāsthāne viharatītyucyate | kleśamāro na kiñcidākopayati kākolūkadṛṣṭāntavat | asya ca cittaṃ supratiṣṭhitaṃ duṣkampanaṃ bhavati | yathā vṛtto
body.translated_text: As for having established mindfulness (<s>upasthitasmṛtika</s>): one constantly establishes <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) regarding body, feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>. (Question) What benefit does one obtain through mindfulness of these four <s>dharmas</s>? (Answer) Evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> do not enter the mind, just as an evildoer does not descend into a well-guarded place. And just as a full pot does not take in more water, so for this person who is filled with wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, evil things do not arise. One who has cultivated right mindfulness gathers all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that partake of liberation, just as when the ocean's waters are drunk, all streams are consumed. Of all waters

body.text: ghaṭaḥśikyamadhiniviśyate | sa cāciramevārthaṃ lapsyate | yathoktaṃ bhikṣuṇīsūtre- bhikṣuṇya ānandametadavocan- iha bhadanta [ānanda] vayaṃ catṛṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu supratiṣṭhitacittā viharantya [udāraṃ] pūrveṇāparaṃ viśeṣaṃ samprajānāma iti | ānando 'vocat- evametat bhaginya evametat bhaginya iti |
body.translated_text: the pot rests in the sling. And one will obtain the goal before long. As stated in the <s>Bhikṣuṇī-sūtra</s>: The nuns said to <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Here, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, we dwell with minds well-established in the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), and we fully comprehend the progressive distinction from former to later states.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'So it is, sisters, so it is.'

body.text: samāhita iti | cittasamādhiṃ bhāvayataḥ pravaro 'rtho bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- samāhito yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti iti | anena manuṣyakāyenātimānuṣadharmo bhavati yaduta kāyenodakarmamagniñcā[vagāhya] nirgacchati | vihāyasā gamane ca svatantra ityādi | kiñcāsya sukhaṃ bhavati yat yāvaddevāḥ sahāṃpatibrahmādayo 'pi nāpnuvanti | ayaṃ yat kartavyaṃ tat karotītyucyate | yadakartavyaṃ na tat karoti | samāhitasya saddharmaḥ sadā vardhate samāhitasya cittaṃ nānutapyate | ayaṃpravrajyāphalabhāgbhavati tathāgataśāsanānuyāyī ca | nānyapuruṣavat vṛthā satkāraṃ svīkaroti | ayameva dānapuṇyaṃ vipācayati nānye | ayañca samāhitadharmo buddhairāryaiśca niṣevitaḥ | sarveṣāṃ kuśaladharmāṇāṃ samārjanāya yogyaśca bhavati | yadi samāhitasya siddhirbhavati tadā āryamārgasya pratilābho bhavati | yadi na siddhiḥ, tadā śubhadeveṣūpapadyate yaduta rūpārūpyadhātau | tatkasya hetoḥ | na hi dānādinā īdṛśaṃ kāryaṃ pratilabhate yadekāntataḥ pāpakānāmakaraṇam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo daharo yuvā ājanma maitrīṃ bhāvayati | sa kiṃ pāpakaṃ cittamutpādayet | pāpakaṃ vā cintayet | no hīdaṃ bhagavan | [tatkasya hetoḥ] [tatsamādhiprabhāva eṣaḥ | iti | cittasamādhiśca tattvajñānasya pratyayaḥ | tattvaprajñā sarvān saṃskārān kṣapayati | saṃskārāṇāṃ kṣayāt sarve duḥkhopāyāsāḥ śāmyanti | yogī sarvāṇi laukikāni lokottarāṇi smaranneva kuryāt na klamathena kāryaṃ prayojayan | anye pudgalāstena labdhaṃ pramātuṃ cittameva notpādayanti | ata āha- samāhito 'rthamāpnotīti |
body.translated_text: As for being concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>): for one who cultivates <s>cittasamādhi</s> (mental concentration), the supreme goal is attained. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who is concentrated knows things as they truly are.' With this human body, one attains superhuman <s>dharmas</s>, namely, one enters and emerges from water and fire with the body, and is free in traveling through the sky, and so forth. Moreover, one has happiness that even the <s>devas</s> including <s>Sahāṃpati Brahmā</s> do not attain. This one does what should be done, it is said, and does not do what should not be done. For the concentrated one, the true <s>dharma</s> always increases; the mind of the concentrated one has no remorse. This one becomes a partaker of the fruit of renunciation, and thus

body.text: prajñāvāniti | prajñāvataścitte kleśā na sambhavanti | yadi sambhavanti, tadaiva nirudhyante yathā taptāyaḥpātre patitā jalakaṇikā | prajñāvataścitte saṃjñā nāvirbhavanti | yadyāvirbhavanti, tadaiva nirudhyante yathā tṛṇāgre 'vaśyāyabinduḥ sūrya uditamātre śuṣyati | yaḥ prajñācakṣuṣkaḥ sa buddhadharmaṃ paśyati | yathā cakṣuṣmataḥ sūrya upayogāya kalpate | prajñāvān buddhasya dharmadāyabhāgityucyate | yathā jātaḥ putraḥ pitrordhanabhāgbhavati | prajñāvāneva sa jīva ityucyate | anye mṛtā iti | prajñāvān tattvamārgikaḥ, mārgasya parijñānāt | prajñāvāneva bhagavataḥ śāsanā[mṛta]rasaṃ vetti | yathā avipariṇatajihvendriyaḥ pañcarasān vivecayati | prajñāvān bhagavacchāsane samāhito na kampate tadyathā śailo na vāyunā kampyate | prajñāvān śrāddha ityucyate | catuḥ śraddhālābhitayā parānanuyāyitatvāt | āryaprajñendriyapratilābhī jinauraso bhavati | anye bāhyāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ | ata ucyate prajñāvānarthaṃ vindata iti |
body.translated_text: "One who possesses <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)" — in the mind of one possessing <s>prajñā</s>, <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) do not arise. If they do arise, they are immediately extinguished, just as a drop of water falling onto a heated iron vessel [evaporates instantly]. In the mind of one possessing <s>prajñā</s>, [false] <s>saṃjñās</s> (perceptions) do not manifest. If they do manifest, they are immediately extinguished, just as a dewdrop on the tip of a blade of grass dries up the moment the sun has risen. One who has the eye of <s>prajñā</s> sees the <s>Buddhadharma</s>. Just as the sun serves the purpose of one who has eyes. One possessing <s>prajñā</s> is called an heir to the <s>dharma</s>-inheritance of the <s>Buddha</s>. Just as a son who is born becomes an heir to his parents' wealth. Only one possessing <s>prajñā</s> is said to be truly alive; others are [as good as] dead. One possessing <s>prajñā</s> is a seeker of truth, because of complete knowledge of the path. Only one possessing <s>prajñā</s> knows the nectar-taste of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. Just as one whose tongue-faculty is unimpaired discriminates among the five flavors. One possessing <s>prajñā</s>, being concentrated in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching, does not waver — just as a mountain is not shaken by the wind. One possessing <s>prajñā</s> is called "faithful" (<s>śrāddha</s>), because having obtained the four kinds of faith, one does not follow others. One who attains the noble <s>prajñendriya</s> (faculty of wisdom) becomes a true son of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror). Others are outsiders, ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjanas</s>). Therefore it is said: "One possessing <s>prajñā</s> obtains the goal."

body.text: niṣprapañcārāma iti | yadekānekatvavādaḥ sa prapañcaḥ | yathā ānandaḥ śāriputraṃ pṛcchati- ṣaṇṇām [āyuṣman] sparśāyatanānāmaśeṣavirāganirodhādasti anyatkiñcit | śāriputraḥ pratyāha[mā hyevamāyuṣman] | ṣaṇṇā[māyuṣman] sparśāyatanānāmaśeṣavirāganirodhādastyanyatkiñciditi
body.translated_text: "One who delights in non-proliferation" (<s>niṣprapañcārāma</s>) — the doctrine of unity and multiplicity is <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation). As <s>Ānanda</s> asks <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Through the complete fading away and cessation of the six sense-bases of contact, venerable one, does anything else exist?" <s>Śāriputra</s> replies: "Do not say so, venerable one! Through the complete fading away and cessation of the six sense-bases of contact, there is something else"

body.text: vadan aprapañcaṃ prapañcayasi | nāsti kiñciditi, asti ca nāsti cānyaditi, naivāsti no ca naivāstyanyaditi ca praśne prativacanamapi tathā syāt |
body.translated_text: — by saying this, you proliferate what is non-proliferation. Whether the question is "nothing exists," "something exists and something does not exist," or "neither exists nor does not exist" — the answer too would be the same.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmādidamaprapañcam | (u) ayaṃ vastuta ātmadharmapraśnaḥ yadyekaḥ yadi vāneka iti | ato na pratyuvāca | ātmā ca na niyataḥ | pañcaskandheṣu kevalaṃ prajñaptyābhidhīyate | yadyasti kiñciditi | yadi vā nāsti kiñciditi pratibrūyāt, tadā śāśvatocchedapātaḥ syāt | yat pratītyasamudenātmavyavahāraḥ sa niṣprapañcaḥ | yadi paśyati sattvaṃ śūnyaṃ dharmāśca śūnyā iti sa niṣprapañcārāmaḥ | ato niṣprapañcārāmā bhagavacchāsane 'rthaṃ vindante | iyaṃ kuśalavitarkasampadā |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is this non-proliferation? (Answer) This is essentially a question about the self and <s>dharmas</s> — whether it is one or many. Therefore he did not reply. The <s>ātman</s> (self) is not fixed; it is designated merely by convention upon the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). Whether one says "something exists" or "nothing exists" — if one were to answer thus, then there would be a fall into eternalism (<s>śāśvata</s>) or annihilationism (<s>uccheda</s>). That which is the conventional designation of the self through <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) — that is non-proliferation. If one sees that beings are <s>śūnya</s> (empty) and <s>dharmas</s> too are <s>śūnya</s>, that person delights in non-proliferation (<s>niṣprapañcārāma</s>). Therefore, those who delight in non-proliferation find the goal in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. This is the accomplishment of wholesome reasoning (<s>kuśalavitarkasampad</s>).

body.text: kuśalavitarkavargastryaśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and eighty-third chapter, the Chapter on Wholesome Reasoning (<s>kuśalavitarkavarga</s>).

body.text: 184 antimapañcasamādhipariṣkāravargaḥ
body.translated_text: 184. Chapter on the Examination of the Last Five <s>Samādhis</s> (<s>antimapañcasamādhipariṣkāravarga</s>).

body.text: (7) kalyāṇādhimuktisampaditi | yogī yat nirvāṇe 'bhiramaṇaḥ saṃsāraṃ vidveṣayati | iyaṃ kalyāṇādhimuktiḥ | evamadhimuktaḥ kṣipraṃ vimuktibhāgbhavati | nirvāṇābhiratasya cittaṃ na kutracidabhiniviśate | nirvāṇābhiratasya nāsti bhayam | yadi pṛthagjanasya cittaṃ nirvāṇamanusmarati | tadaiva santrāso bhavati- ahamatyantaṃ nakṣyāmīti |
body.translated_text: (7) The accomplishment of wholesome disposition (<s>kalyāṇādhimuktisampad</s>) — when a <s>yogī</s> delights in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and becomes disgusted with <s>saṃsāra</s>, this is wholesome disposition. One thus disposed quickly becomes a partaker of liberation (<s>vimuktibhāg</s>). The mind of one who delights in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> does not attach itself anywhere. One who delights in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has no fear. But if an ordinary person's (<s>pṛthagjana</s>'s) mind contemplates <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, then immediately terror arises — thinking "I shall be utterly annihilated."

body.text: (pṛ) kena pratyayena nirvāṇe 'dhimucyate | (u) yogī lokamanityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmakaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirvāṇe upaśamasaṃjñāmutpādayati | pudgalo 'yaṃ svābhāvikakleśapratanubhūto nirvāṇabhāṇakaṃ śṛṇoti | tadā [tasya] cittaṃ tatrādhimucyate | yadi vā kalyāṇamitrāt yadi vā sūtrādhyayanāt saṃsāra ādīnavaṃ śṛṇoti | yathā anavarāgrasūtre pañcadevadūtasūtre coktam | tadā saṃsārānnirviṇṇo nirvāṇe 'dhimucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) By what condition does one become disposed toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? (Answer) The <s>yogī</s>, seeing the world as impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self, generates the perception of peace (<s>upaśamasaṃjñā</s>) regarding <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. This person, whose <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) have naturally become attenuated, hears the description of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Then his mind becomes disposed toward it. Whether through a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) or through the study of <s>sūtras</s>, one hears the dangers of <s>saṃsāra</s> — as stated in the <s>Anavarasūtra</s> and the <s>Pañcadevadūtasūtra</s>. Then, being disgusted with <s>saṃsāra</s>, one becomes disposed toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: (8) pradhānīyāṅgasampaditi | yathoktaṃ sūtre- pañca pradhānīyāṅgāni |
body.translated_text: (8) The accomplishment of the predominant factors (<s>pradhānīyāṅgasampad</s>) — as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: "There are five predominant factors"

body.text: katamāni [pañca] | iha [bhikṣavo] bhikṣuḥ śrāddho bhavati | aśaṭho bhavati | alpābādho bhavati | ārabdhavīryo bhavati | prajñāvān bhavatīti | śraddhāvān nāma[yaḥ] triṣu ratneṣu caturṣu satyeṣu ca vigatavicikitso bhavati | vigatavicikitsatvāt kṣipraṃ samādhiḥ sidhyati | śraddhāvataḥ prītibahulatvācca kṣipraṃ samādhiḥ sidhyati | śraddhāvān susamāhito dāntaśca bhavati | ato 'pi sahasā samādhiṃ vindate | (pṛ) yadi samādhinā prajñotpadyate | atha vicikitsāṃ prajahāti | kathamidānīṃ samādheḥ pūrvamevocyate vigatavicikitsa iti | (u) bahuśrutatvāt kiñcidvicikitsāṃ prajahāti | na samādhilābhāt | adhimuktakulotpannaḥ śrāddhena sahavṛttikaḥ sadādhimukticittaṃ bhāvayan apratilabdhasamādhirapi vicikitsāṃ na karoti | evamādi |
body.translated_text: "What are the five? Here, monks, a monk is faithful (<s>śrāddha</s>). He is sincere (<s>aśaṭha</s>). He has few illnesses (<s>alpābādha</s>). He is energetic (<s>ārabdhavīrya</s>). He possesses wisdom (<s>prajñāvān</s>)." One who is faithful is one who has eliminated doubt regarding the Three Jewels (<s>triratna</s>) and the Four Noble Truths (<s>catuḥsatya</s>). Because doubt has been eliminated, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is quickly accomplished. Because the faithful person has abundant joy (<s>prīti</s>), <s>samādhi</s> is quickly accomplished. The faithful person is well-concentrated and tamed. Therefore too he quickly attains <s>samādhi</s>. (Question) If <s>prajñā</s> arises through <s>samādhi</s>, and then one abandons doubt — how then is it said that one is "free from doubt" even before <s>samādhi</s>? (Answer) Through being learned (<s>bahuśruta</s>), one abandons some doubt; not from the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>. One born in a family of [right] disposition, who associates with the faithful and constantly cultivates a mind of right disposition — even without having attained <s>samādhi</s>, does not harbor doubt. And so forth.

body.text: aśaṭha iti | ṛjucittasya nāsti kiñcidgopanīyam | sadapi sutīrṇaṃ bhavati | yathā kaścidbhiṣajamupetya vyādhisvarūpamuktvā sucikitso bhavati | alpābādha iti | sa pūrvarātre 'pararātre ca vyavasyati, na viramati | yadyābādhābahulaḥ, tanmārgacaryāyā antarāyo bhavati | ārabdhavīrya iti | mārgārthitvāt sadā viryamārabhate | ato 'gniṃ manthāno na viramamāṇo sahasāgniṃ vindate | prajñāvāniti | prajñāvattvena caturṇāmaṅgānāṃ phalaṃ bhavati yaduta mārgaphalam |
body.translated_text: "Sincere" (<s>aśaṭha</s>) — for one whose mind is straight, there is nothing to conceal. One is always well-disposed. Just as someone who approaches a physician and describes the nature of his illness is well-treated. "Having few illnesses" (<s>alpābādha</s>) — he exerts himself in both the first and last watches of the night, and does not cease. If one has many illnesses, it becomes an obstacle to the practice of the path. "Energetic" (<s>ārabdhavīrya</s>) — because one is a seeker of the path, one constantly exerts energy. Therefore, like one who churns fire without ceasing and quickly obtains fire. "Possessing wisdom" (<s>prajñāvān</s>) — through possessing wisdom, the fruit of the four [predominant] factors is realized, namely the fruit of the path.

body.text: (pṛ) smṛtyupasthānadharmā api pradhānīyāṅgāni | kasmāt kevalamete pañca dharmā uktāḥ | (u) yadyapi sakalamaṅgam | tathāpīme dharmā mukhyatamāḥ yogibhirapyapekṣyante | ata ime kevalamuktāḥ | sarveṣāṃ pāpakānāṃ parivarjanaṃ sarveṣāṃ kuśalānāṃ sañcayaśca yogino 'ṅgam | yathā......... sūtre varṇitam |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) are also predominant factors. Why are only these five <s>dharmas</s> mentioned? (Answer) Although all factors are included, these <s>dharmas</s> are the most important and are sought even by <s>yogīs</s>. Therefore only these are mentioned. The avoidance of all unwholesome actions and the accumulation of all wholesome actions are the factors of the <s>yogī</s>, as described in the <s>sūtra</s>...

body.text: (9) vimuktyāyatanasampaditi yat pañcavimuktyāyatanāni | ihaśāstā [anyataro vā] gurusthānīyaḥ [sa brahmacārī] bhikṣūnāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | yathā yathā dharmaṃ deśayati | tathā tathā [tasmin dharme] arthapratisaṃvedī ca dharmapratisaṃvedī ca bhavati | [tasyārtha]pratisaṃvedino
body.translated_text: (9) The accomplishment of the bases of liberation (<s>vimuktyāyatanasampad</s>) — there are five bases of liberation. Here the Teacher, or someone of the rank of teacher, a fellow practitioner, teaches the <s>dharma</s> to the monks. As he teaches the <s>dharma</s>, the [listener] comprehends the meaning and comprehends the <s>dharma</s>. For one who comprehends the meaning

body.text: dharmapratisaṃvedinaḥ prītirjāyate | prītamanasaḥ kāyaḥ praśrabhyate | praśrabdhakāyaḥ sukhaṃ vedayate | sukhinaścittaṃ samādhīyate | idaṃ prathamaṃ vimuktyāyatanam | yatra bhikṣo[rapramattasyātāpinaḥ] prahitātmano viharato ['vimuktaṃ] cittaṃ vimucyate | [aparikṣīṇā] vā āsravāḥ parikṣayaṃ gacchanti | [ananuprāptaṃ] vā anuttaraṃ yogakṣemamanuprāpnoti | dvitīyaṃ [vimuktyāyatanaṃ] vistareṇa sūtrādhyayanam | tṛtīyaṃ pareṣāṃ dharmadeśanā | caturthaṃ vimukte sthāne dharmāṇāmanuvitarkaḥ anuvicāraḥ | pañcamaṃ samādhinimittasya sugrahaṇaṃ yaduta navanimittādīni yathāpūrvamuktāni |
body.translated_text: and comprehends the <s>dharma</s>, joy (<s>prīti</s>) arises. For one whose mind is joyful, the body becomes tranquil. One whose body is tranquil experiences pleasure (<s>sukha</s>). For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. This is the first base of liberation. For a monk who dwells diligently, ardently, with resolute mind — the unliberated mind becomes liberated; or the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) that have not been destroyed go to destruction; or one attains the unsurpassed security from bondage (<s>yogakṣema</s>) that had not yet been attained. The second [base of liberation] is extensive study of <s>sūtras</s>. The third is teaching the <s>dharma</s> to others. The fourth is reflective examination (<s>anuvitarka</s>) and sustained reflection (<s>anuvicāra</s>) on the <s>dharmas</s> in a secluded place. The fifth is the firm grasping of the sign of <s>samādhi</s>, namely the nine signs (<s>navanimitta</s>) and so forth as previously stated.

body.text: (pṛ) śāstā [anyataro] vā gurusthānīyaḥ sabrahmacārī kasmāt bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | (u) dharmasamāpādānena mahāntamarthamāpnoti | ityato deśanāṃ karoti | sabrahmacāryayaḥ śāstāramupādāya pravrajitaḥ | indriyāṇāṃ paripācanāya dharmaṃ deśayati | gurusthānīyaḥ sabrahmacārī samānakarmatvācca dharmadeśanāṃ karoti | bhikṣavo 'vaśyaṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvantītyataśca [dharma]deśanāṃ karoti | ime pudgalā viśuddhaśīlādiguṇasampannāḥ tadyathā subhājanaṃ samṛddhiṃ samādātuṃ bhavyam ityato dharmadeśanāṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Why does the Teacher, or someone of the rank of teacher, a fellow practitioner, teach the <s>dharma</s> to the monks? (Answer) By accomplishing the <s>dharma</s>, one attains a great goal. Therefore one teaches. The fellow practitioner, having gone forth following the Teacher, teaches the <s>dharma</s> in order to ripen the faculties (<s>indriyas</s>). The fellow practitioner of teacher's rank teaches the <s>dharma</s> because of sharing the same practice. The monks must necessarily listen to the <s>dharma</s>, and therefore [the teacher] teaches. These persons are endowed with qualities such as purified morality (<s>viśuddhaśīla</s>) — just as a good vessel is fit to receive prosperity — and therefore teaches the <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: imāstisraḥ prajñāḥ dharmapratisaṃvedo bahuśrutamayī prajñā | arthapratisaṃvedaścintāmayī prajñā | abhābhyāmubhābhyāṃ jāyate prītiḥ yāvatsamāhitasya yathābhūtajñānaṃ jāyate | iyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā | āsāṃ trisṛṇāṃ prajñānāṃ trīṇi phalāni bhavanti yaduta nirvedo vairāgyaṃ vimuktiḥ | dharmaṃ śrutvādhītya ca pareṣāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | iyaṃ bahuśrutamayī prajñā | dharmānanuvitarkayati anuvicārayati | iyaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | samādhinimittaṃ sugṛhṇāti | iyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā |
body.translated_text: These three kinds of <s>prajñā</s> are: comprehension of <s>dharma</s> is <s>prajñā</s> born of learning (<s>bahuśrutamayī prajñā</s>); comprehension of meaning is <s>prajñā</s> born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>). From both of these, joy arises, up to the point where, for one who is concentrated, knowledge of things as they really are (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>) arises — this is <s>prajñā</s> born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>). These three kinds of <s>prajñā</s> have three fruits, namely: disenchantment (<s>nirveda</s>), dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), and liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). Having heard and studied the <s>dharma</s>, one teaches the <s>dharma</s> to others — this is <s>prajñā</s> born of learning. One examines and reflects upon the <s>dharmas</s> — this is <s>prajñā</s> born of reflection. One firmly grasps the sign of <s>samādhi</s> — this is <s>prajñā</s> born of cultivation.

body.text: (pṛ) yā cittavimuktiḥ [yaśca] āśravakṣayaḥ | anayoḥ ko bhedaḥ | (u) samādhinā kleśānāṃ vyāvṛttiścittavimuktiḥ | kleśānāmatyantaprahāṇamāsravakṣayaḥ | (pṛ) śīlādayo dharmā api vimuktyāyatanam | yathoktaṃ- śīlavataścittaṃ na vipratisarati | avipratisāriṇaḥ prītirjāyata ityādi | kadācit dānadihetorapi vimuktirbhavati | kasmādime pañcaiva dharmā uktāḥ | (u)prādhānyātta evoktāḥ | (pṛ) eṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kiṃ prādhānyam | (u) vimukteḥ sannikṛṣṭo hetuḥ | śīlādayastu viprakṛṣṭāḥ | (pṛ) kathaṃ jñāyate sannikṛṣṭo heturiti | (u) yogī dharmaṃ śrutvā prajānāti skandhāyatanadhātūn | taddharmakalāpamātre nāstyātmeti | ataḥ prajñaptirbhajyate | tatprajñaptibhaṅga eva vimuktirityākhyāyate | ataḥ sannikṛṣṭo hetuḥ | uktañca sūtre- bahuśrutasyāniśaṃsā yaduta paraśāsanaṃ nānuvartate, cittaṃ susamādhīyate ityādi | anenāpi jñāyate sannikṛṣṭo heturiti | tathāgataśāsane mahān lābho 'sti, kleśān nirodhayati, nirvāṇañca yātītyādi | asminnupaśamadharme śrotā vā adhyetā vā anuvicintayitā vā kṣipraṃ vimucyate | ataḥ sannikṛṣṭo hetuḥ | dānena mahatpuṇyaṃ vindate | śīlena gauravam | bāhuśrutyena prajñām | prajñayā āsravāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ vindate na puṇyaṃ gauravaṃ vā | ato jñāyate sannikṛṣṭo heturiti | śāriputrādayo mahāprājñā iti kīrtyante | [tat] sarvaṃ bahuśrutyāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) What is the difference between liberation of mind (<s>cittavimukti</s>) and destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (<s>āśravakṣaya</s>)? (Answer) The turning away of <s>kleśas</s> through <s>samādhi</s> is liberation of mind. The complete abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> is the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>. (Question) <s>Dharmas</s> such as morality (<s>śīla</s>) and so forth are also bases of liberation. As stated: "For one who is moral, the mind does not become remorseful. For one free from remorse, joy arises" — and so forth. Sometimes liberation occurs even through the cause of giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the like. Why are only these five <s>dharmas</s> mentioned? (Answer) Because of their primary importance, only these are stated. (Question) What is the primary importance of these <s>dharmas</s>? (Answer) They are proximate causes of liberation. But morality and the like are remote [causes]. (Question) How is it known that they are proximate causes? (Answer) The <s>yogī</s>, having heard the <s>dharma</s>, understands the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements). In that mere collection of <s>dharmas</s>, there is no self — thus the [false] designation is broken. That very breaking of designation is called liberation. Therefore it is a proximate cause. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: "The benefit of being learned is that one does not follow the teachings of others, and the mind becomes well-concentrated" — and so forth. By this too it is known that it is a proximate cause. In the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching there is a great gain — one extinguishes the <s>kleśas</s> and goes to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — and so forth. In this <s>dharma</s> of peace, whether one is a listener, a student, or a reflector, one is quickly liberated. Therefore it is a proximate cause. Through giving (<s>dāna</s>), one obtains great merit. Through morality (<s>śīla</s>), one obtains respect. Through learning (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>), one obtains <s>prajñā</s>. Through <s>prajñā</s>, one obtains the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> — not merit or respect. Therefore it is known that it is a proximate cause. <s>Śāriputra</s> and others are celebrated as greatly wise — all that is from their learning.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi bāhuśrutyena cittaṃ susamādhīyate | ānandaḥ kasmāt prathame 'ntime ca yāme vimuktiṃ nālabhata | (u) ānando na yāvanmastakamupadhāne nyadhatta tāvadeva vimuktimalabhata | ato 'sadadbhutadharme 'vartata | kasmānna kṣipram | ānandasyatasmin samaye vīryaṃ kiñcidduṣṭamāsīt | atimātraklāntatvānnālabhata vimuktim | ānando 'smin yāma āsravāṇāṃ kṣayamanuprāpnomīti praṇidadhyau | yathā ca bodhisattvo bodhimaṇḍe praṇihitavān | kastādṛśabalo yathā ānandaḥ | sarvamidaṃ bāhuśrutyabalam |
body.translated_text: (Question) If through learning the mind becomes well-concentrated, why did <s>Ānanda</s> not attain liberation in the first and last watches of the night? (Answer) <s>Ānanda</s>, at the very moment he had not yet laid his head on the pillow, attained liberation. Therefore he dwelt in the marvelous <s>dharma</s>. Why not sooner? At that time, <s>Ānanda</s>'s energy was somewhat impaired. Because of excessive fatigue, he did not attain liberation [earlier]. <s>Ānanda</s> made a resolve: "In this watch, I shall attain the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>." Just as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> made his resolve at the seat of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) — who else has such power of vision as <s>Ānanda</s>? All this is the power of learning (<s>bāhuśrutyabala</s>).

body.text: (10) anāvaraṇateti- yāni trīṇyāvaraṇāni karmāvaraṇaṃ, vipākāvaraṇaṃ kleśāvaraṇamiti | yasyemānyāvaraṇāni na santi | na sa duḥsthāne patati | yo 'kṣaṇebhyomuktaḥ sa mārgaṃ samādātuṃ bhavyo bhavati | sa caturbhiścakraiḥ sampanna ityucyate | [tāni] pratirūpadeśavāsaḥ satpuruṣopāśrayaḥ ātmasamyakpraṇidhiḥ pūrve ca kṛtapuṇyatā iti | [sa] catvāri srotaāpattyaṅgāni ca sādhayati yaduta satpuruṣasaṃvāsaḥ saddharmaśravaṇaṃ, yoniśomanaskāro dharmānudharmapratipattiḥ | rāgādīn trīn dharmānapi samutsṛjati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- trīn dharmānaprahāya na jarāvyādhimaraṇāni santarati | iti |
body.translated_text: (10) Regarding 'without obstruction' — there are three obstructions: <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (obstruction of action), <s>vipākāvaraṇa</s> (obstruction of ripening), and <s>kleśāvaraṇa</s> (obstruction of afflictions). One who does not have these obstructions does not fall into a miserable state. One who is freed from the unfavorable conditions (<s>akṣaṇa</s>) becomes capable of undertaking the path. He is said to be endowed with four wheels: [these are] dwelling in a suitable place, reliance on good persons, right resolution of oneself, and having accumulated merit in the past. [He] also accomplishes the four limbs of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattyaṅga</s>), namely: association with good persons, hearing the true <s>dharma</s>, proper mental attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>), and practice in accordance with the <s>dharma</s>. He also abandons three <s>dharmas</s> beginning with <s>rāga</s> (passion). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Without abandoning three <s>dharmas</s>, one does not cross beyond old age, disease, and death.'

body.text: (11) anāsaktateti | "nāvaratīramupagacchati | na pāratīramupagacchati | na madhye saṃsīdati | na sthala utsīdiṣyati | na manuṣyagrāho bhaviṣyati | nāmanuṣyagrāho bhaviṣyati | nāvartagrāho bhaviṣyati | nāntaḥpūtī bhaviṣyati" | avaratīramiti ṣaṇṇāmādhyātmikānāmāyatanāmadhivacanam | pāratīramīti ṣaṇṇāṃ bāhyānāmāyatanānāmadhivacanam | madhye saṃsīdati iti nandirāgasyādhivacanam | sthala utsāda iti asmimānasyādhivacanam | katamo manuṣyagrāhaḥ | [iha] bhikṣurgṛhisaṃsṛṣṭo viharati | [katamo] 'manuṣyagrāhaḥ | [iha bhikṣurekatya ekatyo] 'nyataraṃ devanikāyaṃ praṇidhāya brahmacaryaṃ carati | ayamucyate 'manuṣyagrāha iti | āvartagrāha iti pañcānāṃ kāmaguṇānamadhivacanam | [katamaśca] antaḥpūtibhāvaḥ | iha bhikṣurekatyo duśśīlo bhavati | pāpadharmā aśuciḥ śaṅkāsmarasamācāro 'brahmacārī | ayamucyate 'ntaḥpūtibhāva iti |
body.translated_text: (11) Regarding 'non-attachment' — 'He does not approach the near shore. He does not approach the far shore. He does not sink in the middle. He will not be stranded on dry land. He will not be seized by humans. He will not be seized by non-humans. He will not be seized by a whirlpool. He will not become inwardly rotten.' 'The near shore' is a designation for the six internal <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases). 'The far shore' is a designation for the six external <s>āyatanas</s>. 'Sinking in the middle' is a designation for <s>nandirāga</s> (delight and passion). 'Being stranded on dry land' is a designation for <s>asmimāna</s> (the conceit 'I am'). What is 'being seized by humans'? [Here] a <s>bhikṣu</s> dwells in association with householders. What is 'being seized by non-humans'? [Here a bhikṣu,] aspiring to one or another class of <s>devas</s>, practices the holy life. This is called 'being seized by non-humans.' 'Being seized by a whirlpool' is a designation for the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>kāmaguṇa</s>). [And what is] 'inward rottenness'? Here a <s>bhikṣu</s> is of bad conduct, of evil character, impure, of suspicious and secretive behavior, not a true celibate. This is called 'inward rottenness.'

body.text: yasyāsti ādhyātmikāyataneṣu ātmagrahaḥ | tasya bāhyāyataneṣu ātmiyagrahaḥ | ādhyātmikabāhyāyatanebhyo nandirāgo bhavati | atastatraiva nimajjate | tebhyastu ahaṅkāro jāyate | kasmāt | yadi kaścitkāyāsaktaḥ sukhī bhavatītyato ['paraḥ] kaścidāgatya laghu
body.translated_text: One who has the grasping of self in the internal <s>āyatanas</s>, for him there is grasping of 'mine' in the external <s>āyatanas</s>. From both internal and external <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>nandirāga</s> (delight and passion) arises. Therefore one sinks right there. From these, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) is born. Why? If someone attached to the body becomes happy, and then [another] person comes and slightly

body.text: nindati | tadā [tasya]māno jāyate | evamātmīyanandirāgāhaṅkārāstaccittaṃ vikṣepayanto 'nyānapi nirvartayanti |
body.translated_text: criticizes, then pride (<s>māna</s>) arises [in him]. Thus the sense of 'mine,' <s>nandirāga</s> (delight and passion), and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), disturbing his mind, produce still other [afflictions].

body.text: (pṛ) dṛṣṭānte 'smin kiṃ stroto bhavati | yadyāryo 'ṣṭāṅgikamārgaḥ srotaḥ | tadā ṣaḍādhyātmikabāhyāyatanāni pārau na syuḥ | nandirāgādayo madhyaugha āvartaḥ pūtibhāvo 'pi ca na syuḥ | yadi kāmatṛṣṇā srotaḥ | kathamimānanuvartya nirvāṇamanuprāpnoti | (u) āryo 'ṣṭāṅgikamārga eva srotaḥ | dṛṣṭānto nāvaśyaṃ sarvākāraiḥ samāno bhavati | yathāyaṃ dāruskandho 'ṣṭākṣaṇavinirmukto mahārṇavaṃ gacchati | evaṃ bhikṣurogho 'kṣaṇairvinirmukta āryāṣṭāṅgikamārgaṃ stroto 'nuvartyaṃ nirvāṇa[mahārṇava]mavatarati | yathā kumbhasadṛśaṃ stanamiti vacanaṃ tadākāramātraṃ gṛhṇāti na kāṭhinyaṃ mārdavaṃ vā | yathā ca candropamaṃ vadanamiti vacanaṃ śobhā pauṣkalyaṃ gṛhṇāti na tadākāram | kiñca yogī āryamārganirgato 'dhyātmabahirdhāyataneṣvāsajyate | na tu yathāyaṃ dāruskandhaḥ strotomadhyagatastasmin pāre 'smin vā āsajyate pūtībhavati vā | ityādi |
body.translated_text: (Question) In this simile, what is the stream? If the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>) is the stream, then the six internal and external <s>āyatanas</s> would not be the two shores, and <s>nandirāga</s> and the rest — the mid-current, the whirlpool, and rottenness — would also not apply. If craving for sensual pleasures (<s>kāmatṛṣṇā</s>) is the stream, how can one follow it and reach <s>nirvāṇa</s>? (Answer) The noble eightfold path itself is the stream. A simile need not correspond in every respect. Just as this log, freed from eight unfavorable conditions, reaches the great ocean, so too a <s>bhikṣu</s>, freed from unfavorable conditions, following the stream of the noble eightfold path, descends into the great ocean of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Just as when one says 'a breast like a water-pot,' one grasps only the shape, not the hardness or softness; and just as when one says 'a face like the moon,' one grasps the beauty and fullness, not the shape.
