Moreover, a <s>yogī</s> who has entered the noble path becomes attached to internal and external <s>āyatanas</s>, but not in the way this log, being in the middle of the stream, gets stuck on the far shore or the near shore, or becomes rotten. And so forth.

body.text: śāstrācārya āha- yathā gaṅgāstroto niyamena mahārṇavaṃ prāpnoti | evamāryāṣṭāṅgikamārgastroto niyamena nirvāṇaṃ prāpnoti |
body.translated_text: The author of the <s>śāstra</s> says: Just as the stream of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> inevitably reaches the great ocean, so the stream of the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>) inevitably reaches <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: evaṃ saṃkṣipyaikādaśamādhipariṣkārā uktāḥ, yeṣu satsu niyamena samādhirlabhyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in brief, the eleven accessories of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) have been explained. When these are present, <s>samādhi</s> is inevitably attained.

body.text: antimapañcasamādhipariṣkāravargaścaturaśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and eighty-fourth chapter, the Chapter on the Last Five Accessories of <s>Samādhi</s>.

body.text: 185 ānāpānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 185. Chapter on <s>Ānāpāna</s> (Mindfulness of Breathing).

body.text: ānāpānasya ṣoḍaśākārā yaduta sasmṛta evāśvasiti smṛta eva praśvasiti | dīrghaṃ vā āśvasan dīrghamāśvasimīti prajānāti dīrghaṃ vā praśvasan dīrghaṃ praśvasimīti prajānāti || hrasvaṃ vā āśvasan hrasvamāśvasimīti prajānāti | hrasvaṃ praśvasan hrasvaṃ praśvasimīti
body.translated_text: There are sixteen aspects of <s>ānāpāna</s> (mindfulness of breathing), namely: 'Mindfully he breathes in, mindfully he breathes out. Breathing in long, he knows "I breathe in long." Breathing out long, he knows "I breathe out long." Breathing in short, he knows "I breathe in short." Breathing out short, he knows "I breathe out short"'

body.text: prajānāti || sarvakāyapratisaṃvedī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || sarvakāyapratisaṃvedī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || praśrambhayan kāyasaṃskāramāśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | praśrambhayan kāyasaṃskāraṃ praśvasiṣyamīti śikṣate || prītipratisaṃvedī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | prītipratisaṃvedī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || sukhapratisaṃvedī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | sukhapratisaṃvedī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || cittasaṃskārapratisaṃvedī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | cittasaṃskārapratisaṃvedī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || prasrambhayan cittasaṃskāramāśvasiṣyāmiti śikṣate | praśrambhayan cittasaṃskāraṃ praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || cittapratisaṃvedī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | cittapratisaṃvedī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || abhipramodayan cittamāśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | abhipramodayan cittaṃ praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || samādadhan cittamāśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | samādadhan cittaṃ praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || vimocayan cittamāśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | vimocayan cittaṃ praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || anityānudarśī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | anityānudarśī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || virāgānudarśī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | virāgānudarśī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || nirodhānudarśī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | nirodhānudarśī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate || pratinissargānudarśī āśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate | pratinissargānudarśī praśvasiṣyāmīti śikṣate |
body.translated_text: 'He trains thus: "I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in calming the bodily formation." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out calming the bodily formation." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in experiencing rapture (<s>prīti</s>)." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out experiencing rapture." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in experiencing happiness (<s>sukha</s>)." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out experiencing happiness." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in experiencing the mental formation (<s>cittasaṃskāra</s>)." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out experiencing the mental formation." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in calming the mental formation." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out calming the mental formation." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in experiencing the mind (<s>citta</s>)." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out experiencing the mind." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in gladdening the mind." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out gladdening the mind." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in concentrating the mind." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out concentrating the mind." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in liberating the mind." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out liberating the mind." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in contemplating impermanence." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out contemplating impermanence." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in contemplating dispassion (<s>virāga</s>)." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out contemplating dispassion." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in contemplating cessation (<s>nirodha</s>)." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out contemplating cessation." He trains thus: "I shall breathe in contemplating relinquishment (<s>pratinissarga</s>)." He trains thus: "I shall breathe out contemplating relinquishment.'

body.text: (pṛ) kathamānāpānasya dīrghaṃ hrasvaṃ vā bhavati | (u) yathā kaścitparvatamārohati | yadi vā [vā] bhāraṃ vahati | [tadā] klāntaḥ hrasvaṃ śvasati | tathā yogyapi audārike citte pravṛtte hrasvaṃ [śvasati] | audārikacittamiti capalaṃ rogavikṣiptaṃ cittam | dīrghaṃ śvasatīti yadi yogī sūkṣmacitte sthitaḥ, [tadā] tasyāśvāsapraśvāsā dīrghā bhavanti | kasmāt | sūkṣmacittānuvartina āśvāsapraśvāsā api sūkṣmā anupatanti | yathā tasyaiva klāntasya viśrāntasya āśrāsapraśvāsā sūkṣmā anupatanti | tasmin samaye dīrghā aśvāsa praśvāsā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: (Question) How can breathing be long or short? (Answer) Just as when someone climbs a mountain or carries a heavy load, being exhausted, he breathes in short breaths — so too a <s>yogī</s>, when the mind is coarse, breathes in short breaths. 'Coarse mind' means an agitated mind, a mind disturbed by illness. 'Breathing long' means when a <s>yogī</s> abides in a subtle mind, then his in-breaths and out-breaths become long. Why? Because the in-breaths and out-breaths that follow the subtle mind also become subtle. Just as for that very exhausted person, when rested, the in-breaths and out-breaths become subtle — at that time the in-breaths and out-breaths become long.

body.text: sarvakāya[pratisaṃvedī]ti | yogī kāye tucchādhimuktaḥ sarvaromakūpeṣu vāyumantarbahiścāriṇaṃ paśyati | praśrambhayan kāyasaṃskāramiti | dhātubalalābhino vyupaśāntacittasya yogina audārikā āśvāsapraśvāsā vyupaśāntā bhavanti | tadā yogī kāyammṛtyupasthānasamanvito bhavati | prītipratisaṃvedīti | asmātsamādhidharmādasya citte mahatī prītirbhavati | prakṛtito vidyamānāpi naivaṃ bhavati | asmin samaye prītipratisaṃvedītyākhyāyate | sukhapratisaṃvedīti | prīteḥ sukhaṃ jāyate | kasmāt | prītamanasaḥ kāyaḥ praśrabhyate, praśrabdhakāyaḥ sukhaṃ vindate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- prītamanasaḥ kāyaḥ praśramyate | praśrabdhakāyaḥ sukhaṃ vedayate | iti |
body.translated_text: 'Experiencing the whole body' — the <s>yogī</s>, with the conviction that the body is empty, sees the breath moving inward and outward through all the pores. 'Calming the bodily formation' — for the <s>yogī</s> who has attained strength of the elements and whose mind is pacified, the coarse in-breaths and out-breaths become pacified. At that time the <s>yogī</s> becomes endowed with the foundation of mindfulness directed toward the body and death. 'Experiencing rapture' — from this <s>dharma</s> of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), great rapture (<s>prīti</s>) arises in his mind. Although it exists by nature, it does not manifest thus [ordinarily]. At this time it is called 'experiencing rapture.' 'Experiencing happiness' — from rapture, happiness (<s>sukha</s>) is born. Why? For one whose mind is joyful, the body becomes tranquil; one whose body is tranquil experiences happiness. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one whose mind is joyful, the body becomes tranquil. One whose body is tranquil experiences happiness.'

body.text: cittasaṃskārapratisaṃvedīti | yogī prītāvādīnavaṃ paśyati | rāgajanakatvāt | rāgo 'yaṃ cittasaṃskāraḥ cittādutpannatvāt | vedanāyāṃ rāgo jāyata ityato vedanāṃ cittasaṃskāraṃ paśyati | praśrambhayan cittasaṃskāramiti | yogī paśyati vedanāto rāgo jāyate | tat praśrambhayataścittamupaśāmyati | audārikavedanāmapi praśrambhayatīti praśrambhayan cittasaṃskāramityucyate | cittapratisaṃvedīti | yogī praśrambhayan vedanāsvādaṃ paśyati cittaṃ śāntaṃ na līnaṃ noddhatam | cittamidaṃ kasmiṃścitsamaye punarlīnaṃ bhavati | tasmin samaye 'bhipramodayati | yadi punaruddhatam | tasmin samaye samādadhāti | yadyubhayadharmavinirmuktam | tasmin samaye samutsṛjet | ata ucyate vimocayan cittamiti | evaṃ yogī samāhito 'nityākāramutpādayati | anityākāreṇa kleśān prajahāti | ayaṃ nirodhākaraḥ | kleśānāṃ prahāṇāccittaṃ nirvidyate | ayaṃ virāgākāraḥ | viraktacittatayā sarveṣāṃ pratinissargamanuprāpnoti | ayaṃ prati nissargākāraḥ | evamanupūrvaṃ vimuktimanuprāpnotīti ṣoḍaśākārā ānāpānasmṛterbhavanti |
body.translated_text: 'Experiencing the mental formation' — the <s>yogī</s> sees the danger in rapture, because it generates <s>rāga</s> (passion). This passion is a mental formation (<s>cittasaṃskāra</s>), because it arises from the mind. Since passion arises in regard to feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), he sees feeling as a mental formation. 'Calming the mental formation' — the <s>yogī</s> sees that passion arises from feeling; by calming that, the mind becomes pacified. He also calms coarse feeling — therefore it is called 'calming the mental formation.' 'Experiencing the mind' — the <s>yogī</s>, calming the relishing of feeling, sees that the mind is peaceful, neither sluggish nor restless. This mind at some time becomes sluggish again; at that time he gladdens it. If again it becomes restless, at that time he concentrates it. If it is freed from both states, at that time he releases it. Therefore it is said 'liberating the mind.' Thus the <s>yogī</s>, being concentrated, produces the aspect of impermanence (<s>anityākāra</s>). Through the aspect of impermanence, he abandons the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). This is the aspect of cessation (<s>nirodhākāra</s>). Through the abandonment of afflictions, the mind becomes disenchanted. This is the aspect of dispassion (<s>virāgākāra</s>). Through dispassion of mind, one attains the relinquishment of all. This is the aspect of relinquishment (<s>pratinissargākāra</s>). Thus, progressively attaining liberation, there are sixteen aspects of <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing).

body.text: (pṛ) kasmādānāpānasmṛtirāryavihāra iti divyavihāra iti brahmavihāra iti śaikṣavihāra iti aśaikṣavihāra iti cocyate | (u) vāyurākāśe viharati | ākāśalakṣaṇaṃ rūpalakṣaṇaṃ prakaṭayati | rūpalakṣaṇamidaṃ śūnyameva | śūnyataivāryavihāra ityāryavihāro
body.translated_text: (Question) Why is <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing) called a noble abiding (<s>āryavihāra</s>), a divine abiding (<s>divyavihāra</s>), a <s>Brahmā</s>-abiding (<s>brahmavihāra</s>), a learner's abiding (<s>śaikṣavihāra</s>), and also a non-learner's abiding (<s>aśaikṣavihāra</s>)? (Answer) The breath dwells in space. The characteristic of space reveals the characteristic of form. This characteristic of form is nothing but empty. Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) itself is the noble abiding — thus it is a noble abiding

body.text: bhavati | śubhadeveṣūtpatyarthatvāt divyavihāraḥ | upaśamaprāpaṇārthatvāt brahmavihāraḥ | śaikṣadharmapratilābhārthatvāt śaikṣavihāraḥ | aśaikṣārthatvādaśaikṣavihāraḥ |
body.translated_text: It is a divine abiding because it leads to rebirth among the <s>Śubha</s> (pure) <s>devas</s>. It is a <s>Brahmā</s>-abiding because it leads to tranquility. It is a learner's abiding because it leads to the attainment of the qualities of a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>). It is a non-learner's abiding because it serves the purpose of a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadyaśubhabhāvanayā kāyādvirakto vimuktimanuprāpnoti | ka upayoga ebhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirākāraiḥ | (u) aśubhabhāvanayā alabdhavairāgyasya ātmadurviṇṇasya kāyacitte vyāmohite syātām | yathā duṣṭamauṣadhaṃ sevamānasya vyādhiḥ punarbhavati | evamaśubhabhāvanayā durnivedo bhavati | yathā valgumuttitīrṣayā bhikṣavo 'śubhabhāvanayā atīva nirviṇṇā viṣapānabhṛgupatanādibhirvividhairātmānaṃ dhnanti sma | na tathā ime ṣoḍaśākārā vairāgyaprāpakā api na durnivedajanakā bhavantītyato viśiṣyante | kiñca ayamākāraḥ sulabhaḥ svakāyāvalambitvāt | aśubhā[kārastu] suvināśaḥ | ayamākāraḥ sūkṣmaḥ svakāyavipariṇāmakatvāt | aśubhākāra audārikaḥ | asthikaṅkālavipariṇāmaduṣṭaḥ | ayamākāraḥ sarveṣāṃ kleśānāṃ bhedakaḥ | aśubhākārastu maithunarāgamātrasya kasmāt | sarve hi kleśā vitarkaṃ pratītya jāyante | ānāpānasmṛteśca sarvavitarkopacchedārthatvāt |
body.translated_text: (Question) If through the contemplation of the unpleasant (<s>aśubhabhāvanā</s>) one becomes dispassionate toward the body and attains liberation, what is the use of these sixteen aspects? (Answer) For one who has not attained dispassion through the contemplation of the unpleasant and who is poorly disenchanted with himself, body and mind may become confused. Just as for one who takes bad medicine, the illness returns — so through the contemplation of the unpleasant, harmful disgust may arise. Just as at <s>Valgu</s>, <s>bhikṣus</s> desiring to cross over, through the contemplation of the unpleasant becoming excessively disgusted, killed themselves by various means such as drinking poison and jumping off cliffs. These sixteen aspects, though they lead to dispassion, do not generate harmful disgust — therefore they are superior. Moreover, this method is easily accessible because it depends on one's own body. The contemplation of the unpleasant is easily destroyed. This method is subtle because it involves the transformation of one's own body. The contemplation of the unpleasant is coarse, being tainted by the transformation of skeletons. This method breaks all afflictions. But the contemplation of the unpleasant [breaks] only sexual passion. Why? Because all afflictions arise dependent on discursive thought (<s>vitarka</s>), and <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> serves to cut off all discursive thought.

body.text: (pṛ) anāpānaṃ kiṃ kāyānubandhi kiṃ cittānubandhi | (u) kāyānubandhi cittānubandhi ca | kasmāt | garbhāśayagatasyābhāvāt jñāyate kāyādhīnamiti | caturthadhyānādikasyācittakasya cābhāvāt jñāyate cittānubandhīti | (pṛ) āśvāsapraśvāso 'bhūtvotpannaścittādhīno na syāt | kasmāt | sa na manaso vaśādutpadyate | yathā anyadvastu smarati citte sadā āśvāsapraśvāsā bhavanti | yathā [bhukta] āhāraḥ svayaṃ paripacyate | yathā ca pratibimbaṃ svayaṃ pravartate na puruṣaḥ karoti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Is breathing (<s>ānāpāna</s>) dependent on the body or dependent on the mind? (Answer) It is dependent on both the body and the mind. Why? Because it is absent for one who is in the womb — from this it is known to be dependent on the body. Because it is absent for one in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond, and for one without mind — from this it is known to be dependent on the mind. (Question) Inhalation and exhalation, arising from non-existence, would not be dependent on the mind. Why? They do not arise through the power of the mind. Just as when one is mindful of some other object, inhalation and exhalation still continue. Just as eaten food digests by itself. And just as a reflection operates by itself — a person does not make it.

body.text: (u) āśvāsapraśvāso 'bhūtvotpadyate na smṛtivaśāt | kintu pratyayasāmagryotpadyate | sacittasyāsti acittakasya punarnāsti | ato jñāyate cittādhīna iti | yathācittañca bhidyate | audārikacittasya hrasvaḥ | sūkṣmacittasya dīrghaḥ | ānāpānaṃ bhūmyadhīnaṃ cittādhīnam | ānāpāna(bhūmi)gatasya ānāpānabhūmirapyasti | [tasya] tasmin samaye cittamapyasti | ānāpānabhūmirnāma kāmadhātu strīṇi dhyānāni ca | ya
body.translated_text: (Answer) Inhalation and exhalation arise from non-existence, not through the power of mindfulness, but through the assemblage of conditions. They exist for one who has mind, but not for one without mind. From this it is known to be dependent on the mind. And it varies according to the mind: for a coarse mind, [breathing is] short; for a subtle mind, [breathing is] long. Breathing (<s>ānāpāna</s>) is dependent on the plane (<s>bhūmi</s>) and dependent on the mind. For one who is in the plane of breathing, the plane of breathing exists; and at that time, mind also exists. The plane of breathing consists of the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) and the three <s>dhyānas</s>. One who

body.text: ānāpānabhūmigataḥ [tasya] asti tu ānāpānabhūmi- cittam | acittakasya tasmin samaye [tadbhūmi]cittamapi nāsti | ānāpānavihīnabhūmigatasya tasmin samaye [tadbhūmiścitta]mapi nāsti |
body.translated_text: is in the plane of breathing has the mind belonging to the plane of breathing. But for one without mind, at that time, the mind belonging to that plane also does not exist. And for one who is in a plane devoid of breathing, at that time, the mind belonging to that plane also does not exist.

body.text: (pṛ) śvāsa utpadyamāna kiṃ pūrvamāśvasati | kiṃ vā pūrvaṃ praśvasati | (u) upapattikāle pūrvamāśvasati | maraṇakāle 'nte praśvasati | evaṃ caturthadhyāne nirgamanapraveśāvapi | (pṛ) ānāpānasmṛtiriyaṃ kathaṃ paripūrṇā bhavati | (u) yogī yadi ṣoḍaśākārān pratilabhate | tasmin samaye paripūrṇā bhavati | kecicchāstācāryā vadanti- ṣaḍibhaḥ pratyayaiḥ paripūrṇeti | [ṣaṭ pratyayā] yaduta gaṇanā anubandhanā śamatho vipaśyanā vivartanaṃ pariśuddhiḥ | gaṇanā ānāpānagaṇanā ekata ārabhya yāvaddaśa | triprakārā gaṇanā samā vā atiriktā vā nyūnā vā | samā nāma daśasu satsu daśeti gaṇayati | atiriktā nāma ekādaśasu daśeti gaṇayati | nyūnā nāma navasu daśeti gaṇayati | anubandhanaṃ nāma yoginaścittamānāpānamanubadhnāti | vipaśyanā nāma yogī āśvāsapraśvāsān kāyānubaddhān maṇiṣu sūtravatpaśyati | śamatho nāma cittasyānāpāne pratiṣṭhāpanam | vivartanaṃ nāma cittaṃ pratītya kāyasya pravṛttiḥ, cittaṃ pratītya ca vedanāyāḥ | pratyutpannacittadharmo 'pyevam | pariśuddhirnāma yogini sarvakleśaiḥ sarvākṣaṇaiśca vimukte cittaṃ pariśudhyati |
body.translated_text: (Question) When breath arises, does one first inhale or first exhale? (Answer) At the time of birth, one first inhales. At the time of death, one finally exhales. Likewise, even in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, there is exit and entry. (Question) How does this mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>) become complete? (Answer) When the <s>yogī</s> obtains the sixteen aspects, at that time it becomes complete. Certain treatise-masters say it is complete through six conditions. The six conditions are: counting (<s>gaṇanā</s>), following (<s>anubandhanā</s>), calm (<s>śamatha</s>), insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>), turning away (<s>vivartana</s>), and purification (<s>pariśuddhi</s>). 'Counting' is the counting of breaths, starting from one up to ten. Counting is of three kinds: even, excessive, or deficient. 'Even' means when there are ten, one counts ten. 'Excessive' means when there are eleven, one counts ten. 'Deficient' means when there are nine, one counts ten. 'Following' means the <s>yogī</s>'s mind follows the breathing. 'Insight' means the <s>yogī</s> sees inhalation and exhalation bound to the body like a thread through beads. 'Calm' means the settling of the mind on the breathing. 'Turning away' means the operation of the body dependent on the mind, and of feeling dependent on the mind. The <s>dharma</s> of the present mind is also thus. 'Purification' means when the <s>yogī</s> is freed from all defilements and all unfavorable conditions, the mind becomes purified.

body.text: neme 'vaśyaniyatāḥ | kasmāt | ākāreṣu gaṇānubandhanarūpayo dvayodharmayornāvaśyamupayogo bhavati | yato yogī kevalamānāpāne cittaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayan sarvān vitarkānupacchedayati | yaḥ ṣoḍaśavidhamācarituṃ samarthaḥ sa paripūrṇa ityucyate | idaṃ paripūrṇalakṣaṇañcāniyatam | mṛdvindriyācaritaṃ tīkṣṇendriyasyāparipūrṇam |
body.translated_text: These [six] are not necessarily fixed. Why? Among the aspects, the two <s>dharmas</s> of counting and following are not necessarily employed. Because the <s>yogī</s>, by merely settling the mind on the breathing, cuts off all discursive thoughts (<s>vitarka</s>). One who is able to practice the sixteen modes is called 'complete.' And this characteristic of completeness is not fixed. What is practiced by one of dull faculties is not complete for one of sharp faculties.

body.text: (pṛ) ānāpānasūtre 'smin kasmāduktam- āhārāya bhavatīti | (u) ānāpānastimitasya kāyaḥ sukhī bhavati | yathā madhurānnabhujaḥ kāyaḥ prahlādyate | ataḥ āhārāya bhavatītyucyate | (pṛ) eṣu ṣoḍaśākāreṣu kimānāpānaṃ saṃsmarati | (u) asya puruṣeṇa
body.translated_text: (Question) In this <s>ānāpāna</s> (breathing) <s>sūtra</s>, why is it stated 'it serves as nutriment'? (Answer) When the breathing is stilled, the body becomes comfortable. Just as one who eats sweet food — the body is refreshed. Therefore it is said 'it serves as nutriment.' (Question) Among these sixteen aspects, does one recall the breathing? (Answer) For this person

body.text: pañcaskandhān nirākartumupāya ityākhyā | pañcaskandheṣu nirākṛteṣu prajñaptirnirākṛteti kaḥ punarupayoga ānāpānasmṛtyā | idameva kāyānusmṛtirityucyate | caturdhā kāyamanusmaratīti kāyānusmṛtiḥ |
body.translated_text: it is declared to be the means for removing the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>). When the five aggregates have been removed, conventional designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) is removed — what then is the further use of mindfulness of breathing? This itself is called 'mindfulness of the body' (<s>kāyānusmṛti</s>). Contemplating the body in four ways is mindfulness of the body.

body.text: (pṛ) smṛtiratītālambanā | āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ pratyutpannāḥ | kasmāt tat smṛtirbhavati | (u) idaṃ prajñaptibhedakaṃ jñānamanusmṛtināmnocyate | caitasikadharmāṇāmanyonyaṃ nāma bhavati | yathā daśasaṃjñādayaḥ smṛtipūrvaṃ kriyamāṇatvāt anusmṛtirityucyate | dīrghahrasvādīnāṃ nāryavihāra ityabhidhānam | kathaṃ vihāravirhīnaṃ smṛtyupasthānamityākhyāyate | uktañca sūtre yogī ānāpānaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ dīrgha[māśvasan] vā [śikṣate] hrasvaṃ vā sarvakāyapratisaṃvedī vā praśrambhayan kāyasaṃskāraṃ vā [śikṣate] | tasmin samaye kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: (Question) Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) has a past object. Inhalation and exhalation are present. How then is that mindfulness? (Answer) This knowledge that differentiates conventional designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) is not called 'recollection' (<s>anusmṛti</s>). Mental factors (<s>caitasikadharma</s>) have names for one another. Just as the ten perceptions (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and the like — because they are done preceded by mindfulness, they are called 'recollection.' Long, short, and the like are not called noble abidings (<s>āryavihāra</s>). How then is what is devoid of [noble] abiding called a 'foundation of mindfulness' (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)? And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>yogī</s>, training in breathing, trains in long inhalation, or in short, or in experiencing the entire body, or in calming the bodily formation.' At that time, there is the foundation of mindfulness of the body (<s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>).

body.text: ayamādya upāyamārgaḥ | viśuddhaye bhavatītyato 'nte prahāṇamārrga ityucyate | atra anityādyākāro 'sti | asminsūtre paraṃ noktam | anyasmin sūtretūktam- yogī ānāpāne [sthitaḥ] kāye samudayadharmānudarśī vyayadharmānudarśī, samudayavyayadharmānudarśī viharatīti | āha- kāyamanityaṃ paśyatītyādi | caturthe paramanityādyākāraḥ paripūrṇatvāduktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is the initial method-path (<s>upāyamārga</s>). Because it leads to purification, at the end it is called the 'path of abandonment' (<s>prahāṇamārga</s>). Herein there are aspects such as impermanence and the like. In this <s>sūtra</s>, the further [stages] are not stated. But in another <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'The <s>yogī</s>, established in breathing, abides contemplating the arising nature in the body, the passing-away nature, the arising-and-passing-away nature.' It says: 'One sees the body as impermanent,' and so forth. In the fourth [foundation of mindfulness], because the aspects of impermanence and the like are complete, it is stated.

body.text: ānāpānavargaḥ pañcāśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and eighty-fifth chapter, the Chapter on Breathing (<s>ānāpānavarga</s>).

body.text: 186 samādhyapakṣāla vargaḥ
body.translated_text: 186. Chapter on the Impurities of Concentration (<s>samādhyapakṣālavarga</s>).

body.text: samādhirayaṃ tatpratibandhibhirapakṣālairvinirmuktaḥ san mahaddhitaṃ sādhayati | samādhyapakṣālamiti yaduta audārikī prītiḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- mamaudārikaṃ prītiprāmodyaṃ cittasya dūṣaṇamabhūt iti | yogī notpādayedidamaudārikaṃ prītipramodyam | rāgādidoṣāṇāṃ samāhita cittavikṣepakatvāt |
body.translated_text: This concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), when freed from its obstructive impurities (<s>apakṣāla</s>), accomplishes great benefit. The impurity of concentration is coarse joy (<s>audārikī prīti</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'My coarse delight and elation (<s>prītiprāmodya</s>) was a corruption of the mind.' The <s>yogī</s> should not generate this coarse delight and elation. Because defilements such as passion and the like distract a concentrated mind.

body.text: (pṛ) dharmādutpadyamānaṃ prītiprāmodyaṃ kathaṃ notpādayet | (u) yoginaḥ śūnya tāmanusmarato na prītipramodyaṃ jāyate | asti sattva iti saṃjñayā hi prītiprāmodyaṃ jāyate | pañcasu skandheṣu nāsti sattvaḥ, kathaṃ prītiprāmodyaṃ bhaviṣyati | yogī evamanusmaret- hetupratyayai vividhā dharmā jāyate yadutātapālokādayo dharmāḥ | tatra kiṃ prītiprāmodyam | ye prītiprāmodyakarā dharmāḥ te sarve parimārgitā vyagravikṣepakā iti paśyato yogina audārikaṃ prītiprāmodyaṃ nirudhyate | yogī punarmahāntamarthaṃ prārthayate | nātapālokādibhirdharmairayaṃ bhavati | ato na prītiprāmodyaṃ jāyate | yogī nirodhalakṣaṇaṃ lābhaṃ paśyatītyato nātapālokādibhiḥ [tasya] prītiprāmodyaṃ bhavati | ayaṃ yogī upaśamaṃ bhāvayan kleśānāṃ kṣayamicchati | ato na prītiprāmodyamutpādayati | īdṛśaiḥ pratyayairaudārikaṃ prītiprāmodyamupaśamayati |
body.translated_text: (Question) How could one not generate delight and elation arising from the <s>Dharma</s>? (Answer) For the <s>yogī</s> who recollects emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), delight and elation do not arise. For it is through the perception 'a being exists' that delight and elation arise. In the five aggregates there is no being — how then would delight and elation arise? The <s>yogī</s> should recollect thus: 'Through causes and conditions, various <s>dharmas</s> arise, such as sunlight and the like. What delight and elation is there in that?' Those <s>dharmas</s> that produce delight and elation — all of them, when sought after, are seen to be disturbing and distracting. For the <s>yogī</s> who sees thus, coarse delight and elation cease. Furthermore, the <s>yogī</s> aspires to a great purpose. It is not achieved through <s>dharmas</s> such as sunlight and the like. Therefore delight and elation do not arise. The <s>yogī</s> sees that the characteristic of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is the [true] attainment — therefore delight and elation do not arise for him from sunlight and the like. This <s>yogī</s>, cultivating tranquility (<s>upaśama</s>), desires the destruction of defilements. Therefore he does not generate delight and elation. Through such conditions, he pacifies coarse delight and elation.

body.text: bhīrutā ca samādherapakṣālaḥ | ahaṅkāramālambanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīrutāṃ janayati | loke yāni bhairavasthānāni tāni sarvāṇi yogī paśyati | tāni sarvāṇi anityaṃ vikṣepakamiti parīkṣya [tāni] nānuvidadhīta | kasmāt | dhyānaniṣaṇṇadharme 'styayaṃ bhairavadarśanasya pratyayaḥ | nānena bhīrutāṃ janayet | sarvamidamabhūtaṃ śūnyaṃ māyāvat | bālānāṃ vañcanamatattvam | evaṃ cintayato
body.translated_text: Fear (<s>bhīrutā</s>) is also an impurity of concentration. Having seen the object of ego-grasping (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), one generates fear. Whatever terrifying places exist in the world — the <s>yogī</s> sees all of them. Having examined that all of them are impermanent and distracting, one should not attend to them. Why? In the <s>dharma</s> of one seated in <s>dhyāna</s>, there is a condition for the seeing of frightening things. One should not generate fear from this. All of this is unreal, empty, like an illusion — the deception of fools, not reality. For one who contemplates thus

body.text: bhīrutā viyujyate | dharmān śūnyānupāśrayato nāsti bhīrutā | vihārabalādidaṃ vailakṣaṇyamanubhavāmītyanusmaran na bibhyāt | kiñca kāye śīlaśrutādiguṇasampadasti | na hiṃsāprayogapratyaya ityanusmarato na bhavati bhīrutā | yogyayaṃ mārge paramābhirata ityataḥ kāyajīvite 'napekṣo bhavati | kasmāt bibhyāt | kiñcāsya cittaṃ sadā samyaksmṛtau tiṣṭhati | ato bhīrutā nāvakāśaṃ labhate | śūralakṣaṇānusmaraṇācca na bibheti | bhīrutā ceyamabalīnatālakṣaṇam | evamādinā bhīrutāmapasārayati |
body.translated_text: fear is dispelled. For one who relies on <s>dharmas</s> as empty, there is no fear. Recollecting 'I experience this strangeness through the power of the abiding' — one should not be afraid. Furthermore, one's body is endowed with the accomplishment of virtues such as moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), learning (<s>śruta</s>), and the like. Recollecting that there is no condition for the application of harm, fear does not arise. This <s>yogī</s>, being supremely delighted in the path, becomes indifferent to body and life. Why would he be afraid? Furthermore, his mind always abides in right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>). Therefore fear does not find an opportunity. And through the recollection of the characteristics of a hero, he does not fear. This fear has the characteristic of weakness (<s>abalīnatā</s>). Through such and similar [means], he wards off fear.

body.text: adamaḥ samādherapakṣālaḥ | [adamo] yat yogī śītavātādibhirvyādhimān | yadi vātiklāntijarāmaraṇapratyayairadāntakāyo bhavati | rāgatṛṣṇerṣyādibhiḥ kleśairadāntacittasya dhyānasamādhayo naśyanti | ato yogī svakāyacitte saṃrakṣan damayet |
body.translated_text: Lack of self-control (<s>adama</s>) is an impurity of concentration. Lack of self-control is when the <s>yogī</s> becomes ill from cold, wind, and the like. If through excessive fatigue, old age, death, and such conditions the body becomes untamed, and through defilements such as passion, craving, jealousy, and the like the mind becomes untamed — the <s>dhyānas</s> and <s>samādhis</s> are destroyed. Therefore the <s>yogī</s>, guarding his own body and mind, should tame them.

body.text: vailakṣaṇyañca samādherapakṣālaḥ | [velakṣaṇyaṃ] yat malinatvalakṣaṇam | kiñcidamalinatālakṣaṇamapi dhyānasamādhīnāṃ vikṣepakam | yathā dānādilakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: Strangeness (<s>vailakṣaṇya</s>) is also an impurity of concentration. Strangeness is the characteristic of impurity. But even a certain characteristic of non-impurity is a distraction from <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> — such as the characteristic of giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the like.

body.text: vaiṣamyañca samādherapakṣālaḥ | [vaiṣamyaṃ] yat vīryaṃ duṣṭhulaṃ yadi vātilīnam | duṣṭhulasya kāyacitte 'tiklānte | atilīna[vīryo] na samādhinimittaṃ gṛhṇāti | ubhāvapi samādheścyutau bhavataḥ | yathā vartakāpoto gāḍhaṃ gṛhīto 'tilkānto bhavati | śithilaṃ gṛhīto hastādutpatet | yathā vā dāntā vīṇāyāstantryo 'tyāyatā vātiśithilā vā ubhayathā na svaraṃ sādhayanti | ārabdhavīryaṃ pravegavat tadā duṣaṇāvasānaṃ bhavet | yathā bhagavānanuruddhamāha- atyārabdhavīryasya kausīdyaṃ bhavet iti | kasmāt | atyārabdhavīryo hi vastvaprasādhya kausīdye patet | atilīnavīryo 'pi na vastu sādhayati | ato vaiṣamyaṃ samādherapakṣālo bhavati |
body.translated_text: Imbalance (<s>vaiṣamya</s>) is also an impurity of concentration. Imbalance is when effort (<s>vīrya</s>) is either too coarse or too lax. When coarse, body and mind become overly fatigued. When too lax, one does not grasp the sign of concentration (<s>samādhinimitta</s>). Both lead to falling from concentration. Just as a baby quail — if grasped too tightly, it becomes overly fatigued; if grasped loosely, it flies from the hand. Or just as the strings of a well-tuned <s>vīṇā</s> — if overly taut or overly slack, in both cases they do not produce a proper sound. Effort that is aroused with excessive speed — then its end would be a fault. Just as the Blessed One said to <s>Anuruddha</s>: 'For one of excessively aroused effort, sluggishness would arise.' Why? One of excessively aroused effort, failing to accomplish the task, falls into sluggishness. One of overly lax effort also does not accomplish the task. Therefore imbalance is an impurity of concentration.

body.text: amanaskāraḥ samādherapakṣālaḥ | amanaskāro nāma saddharmāmanaskāraḥ | manaskāraprītidharme satyapi nāsti vedayitam (?) | samādhinimittamanaskṛtya bāhyarūpasya manaskāraścāmanaskāraḥ | yogī cittaikāgryeṇārabdhavīryo vedanīyadharmaṃ manasi kuryāt | yathā tailapātramāharet |
body.translated_text: Inattention (<s>amanaskāra</s>) is an impurity of concentration. Inattention means inattention to the true <s>Dharma</s>. Even when the <s>dharma</s> that delights in attention exists, there is no experiencing [of it]. Attending to external form while neglecting the sign of concentration — this is inattention. The <s>yogī</s>, with one-pointed mind and aroused effort, should attend to the <s>dharma</s> that is to be experienced. Just as one would carry a vessel of oil [without spilling].

body.text: vaiparītyañca samādherapakṣālaḥ | [vaiparītyaṃ] yat rāgabahulaḥ karuṇācaritamupādatte | dveṣabahalo 'śubhaṃ bhāvayati | imau dvāvapi pratītyasamutpādaṃ bhāvayataḥ | atilīne citte śamathaṃ bhāvayati | atyuddhate citte vīryamārabhate | anayo dvayościttayorupekṣāmācarati | idaṃ vaiparītyam |
body.translated_text: Perversion (<s>vaiparītya</s>) is also an impurity of concentration. Perversion is when one who is abundant in passion (<s>rāga</s>) takes up the practice of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>); one who is abundant in hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) cultivates the contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubha</s>). These two should both cultivate dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). When the mind is too lax, one cultivates calm (<s>śamatha</s>). When the mind is too agitated, one arouses effort (<s>vīrya</s>). Regarding both these [extremes of] mind, one should practice equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). This is perversion.

body.text: abhijalpaḥ samādherapakṣālaḥ | [abhijalpo] yat vitarkavicārabāhulyam | vitarkavicārāṇāmabhijalpahetutvāt | cittañca nālambane sudṛḍhapratibaddhaviharaṇaṃ, nābhiramate |
body.translated_text: Excessive talk (<s>abhijalpa</s>) is an impurity of concentration. Excessive talk is the abundance of applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>). Because applied thought and sustained thought are the cause of excessive talk. And the mind does not abide firmly bound to the object, and does not find delight [in it].

body.text: lakṣaṇagrahaṇañca samādherapakṣālaḥ | lakṣaṇaṃ trividham- yat śamathalakṣaṇamārambhalakṣaṇamupekṣālakṣaṇamiti | punastrividhaṃ samādhau samāpattilakṣaṇaṃ sthitilakṣaṇaṃ vyutthānalakṣaṇam iti | īdṛśalakṣaṇānāṃ pravibhāgākuśalo yogī dhyānācyavate |
body.translated_text: Grasping at characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇagrahaṇa</s>) is also an impurity of concentration. Characteristics are of three kinds: the characteristic of calm (<s>śamathalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of exertion (<s>ārambhalakṣaṇa</s>), and the characteristic of equanimity (<s>upekṣālakṣaṇa</s>). Furthermore, there are three kinds in concentration: the characteristic of entry into <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samāpattilakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of abiding (<s>sthitilakṣaṇa</s>), and the characteristic of emergence (<s>vyutthānalakṣaṇa</s>). A <s>yogī</s> who is unskilled in the analysis of such characteristics falls from <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: mānañcasamādherapakṣālaḥ | yadāha- ahameva samādhimupasampadya viharāmi na tu sa itīdaṃ mānaṃ bhavati | yadāha- sa evopasampadya viharati nāhamitīdaṃ mānakalpaṃ bhavati | yadyapratilabdhasamādhirāha- pratilabdhavāniti | idamadhimānam | apraṇītasamādhau praṇītasaṃjñāmutpādayati idaṃ mithyāmānam |
body.translated_text: Pride is also an obstacle to <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). When one says 'I alone have attained <s>samādhi</s> and abide in it, but not he' — this is pride. When one says 'He alone has attained and abides, not I' — this is akin to pride. If one who has not attained <s>samādhi</s> says 'I have attained it' — this is excessive pride (<s>adhimāna</s>). When one generates the perception of excellence regarding an unexcellent <s>samādhi</s>, this is false pride (<s>mithyāmāna</s>).

body.text: rāgādidharmā api samādhyapakṣālāḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo bhikṣurekadharmeṇa samanvitaḥ sa na paśyati cakṣuranityamiti | [katamo 'sāvekadharmaḥ] rāgaḥ iti | (pṛ) sarve 'vītarāgāḥ sattvā kiṃ na paśyanti cakṣuranityamiti | (u) vacanamidaṃ kiñcit nyūnam | pratyutpanne
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmas</s> (mental factors) such as <s>rāga</s> (passion) and others are also obstacles to <s>samādhi</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whichever <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) is endowed with a single <s>dharma</s>, he does not see that the eye is impermanent.' [What is that single <s>dharma</s>?] '<s>Rāga</s> (passion).' (Question) Do all beings who are not free from passion not see that the eye is impermanent? (Answer) This statement is somewhat incomplete. Regarding the present —

body.text: samutpannarāgo na paśyati cakṣuranityamiti iti vaktavyam | [rāga]samanvite 'pi kaścidbhedaḥ | keṣāñcidrāgādayo ghanatarāḥ sadā cittamāviśanti | tadā [teṣāṃ te] samādhiṃ pratibadhnanti | tanubhūtāstu na sadāviśanti | tadā nāpakṣālā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: — it should be stated that one in whom passion has arisen does not see that the eye is impermanent. Even among those endowed with [passion], there is some distinction. For some, <s>rāga</s> and other [afflictions] are very dense and constantly invade the mind. Then they obstruct <s>samādhi</s>. But when they have become attenuated, they do not constantly invade. Then they are not obstacles.

body.text: sūtre coktā srayodaśa kṛṣṇadharmāḥ samādhipratikūlāḥ trayodaśa śukladharmāḥ samādhyanukūlāḥ | yadbhagavānāha- trīṇa dharmānaprahāya na jarāvyādhimaraṇaṃ tarati | [katame trayaḥ] rāgadveṣamohāḥ | trīn dharmānaprahāya na samucchedayati rāgadveṣamohān | [katame trayaḥ |] satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo vicikitsā | atha santi trayo dharmāḥ ayoniśomanaskāro duścaritamatilīnacittatā | atha santi trayo dharmā muṣitasmṛtitā, asamprajanyaṃ vikṣiptacittatā iti | atha santi trayo dharmā auddhatyamindriyeṣvaguptadvāratā śīlavipannatā | atha santi trayo dharmāḥ asrāddhyaṃ dauśśīlyaṃ kausīdyamiti | atha santi trayo dharmāḥ sajjane 'ratiḥ saddharmaśravaṇe dveṣaḥ paradoṣaprakaṭane prītiḥ | ata santi trayo dharmaḥ agauravatā saṃkathyadūṣaṇaṃ duṣprajñasevanam | trīn dharmānaprahāya na prajahāti asatkāraṃ saṃkathyadūṣaṇaṃ duṣprajñasevanam [katame trayaḥ |] ahrīkyamanapatrāpyaṃ pramādaḥ | ahrīkyamanapatrāpyaṃ pramādaṃ prahāya prajahāti asatkāraṃ saṃkathyadūṣaṇaṃ duṣprajñasevanam | [evaṃ] yāvatsatkāyadṛṣṭiṃ śīlavrataparāmarśaṃ vicikitsāṃ prajahan prajahāti rāgadveṣamohān jarāvyādhimaraṇāni ca tarati |
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s>, thirteen unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> (factors) opposed to <s>samādhi</s> and thirteen wholesome <s>dharmas</s> favorable to <s>samādhi</s> are stated. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Without abandoning three <s>dharmas</s>, one does not cross over old age, sickness, and death.' [What are the three?] '<s>Rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion).' 'Without abandoning three <s>dharmas</s>, one does not eradicate passion, aversion, and delusion.' [What are the three?] '<s>Satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body), <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (clinging to rites and rituals), and <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt).' Then there are three <s>dharmas</s>: <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> (improper mental attention), misconduct, and a mind that is excessively withdrawn. Then there are three <s>dharmas</s>: confused mindfulness (<s>muṣitasmṛti</s>), lack of clear comprehension (<s>asamprajanya</s>), and a distracted mind. Then there are three <s>dharmas</s>: restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), unguarded sense-doors, and moral failure. Then there are three <s>dharmas</s>: lack of faith (<s>āśrāddhya</s>), moral corruption (<s>dauśśīlya</s>), and laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>). Then there are three <s>dharmas</s>: displeasure with good people, hatred toward hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, and delight in proclaiming the faults of others. Then there are three <s>dharmas</s>: disrespectfulness, corruption of discourse, and association with the unwise. 'Without abandoning three <s>dharmas</s>, one does not abandon disrespect, corruption of discourse, and association with the unwise.' [What are the three?] 'Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), and heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>).' By abandoning shamelessness, lack of moral dread, and heedlessness, one abandons disrespect, corruption of discourse, and association with the unwise. [Thus] up to abandoning <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>, and <s>vicikitsā</s>, one abandons passion, aversion, and delusion, and crosses over old age, sickness, and death.

body.text: atra jarāvyādhimaraṇānāṃ taraṇameva yannirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇam | rāgadveṣamohānāṃ samuccheda evārhatphalaṃ sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇam | saktāyadṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśavicikitsānāṃ samuccheda eva yacchrāmaṇyaphalam | ayoniśomanaskāraduścaritātilīnacittānāṃ samuccheda eva yadūṣmagatādinirvedhabhāgīyakuśalamūlam | muṣitasmṛtyasaṃ prajanyavikṣiptacittānāṃ samuccheda eva yat caturṇāṃ smṛtyupasthānānāṃ bhāvanā | auddhatyendriyeṣvaguptadvāratāśīlavipannatānāṃ samuccheda eva yat pravrajitaśīlasamādānam | sajjanāratisaddharmaśravaṇadveṣaparadoṣaprakaṭanaprītināṃ, aśrāddhayadauśśīlyakausīdyānāṃ, asatkārasaṃkathyadūṣaṇaduṣprajñasevanānāṃ, ahrīkyānapatrāpyapramādānāñca samuccheda eva yat gṛhiṇaḥ pariśuddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the crossing over of old age, sickness, and death is precisely <s>nirupādhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s> (nirvāṇa without remainder). The eradication of passion, aversion, and delusion is the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>-ship, which is <s>sopādhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s> (nirvāṇa with remainder). The eradication of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>, and <s>vicikitsā</s> is the fruit of the stream-enterer (<s>śrāmaṇya</s>). The eradication of improper mental attention, misconduct, and an excessively withdrawn mind is the wholesome root of the <s>ūṣmagata</s> (heat) stage and the other stages leading to disenchantment (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). The eradication of confused mindfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and a distracted mind is the cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>). The eradication of restlessness, unguarded sense-doors, and moral failure is the undertaking of the moral discipline of one gone forth (<s>pravrajita</s>). The eradication of displeasure with good people, hatred toward hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, and delight in proclaiming others' faults; of faithlessness, moral corruption, and laziness; of disrespect, corruption of discourse, and association with the unwise; and of shamelessness, lack of moral dread, and heedlessness — is the deep purification.

body.text: kasmāt | yat kaścit rahogataḥ pāpakaṃ kṛtvā na lajjate tadāhrīkyam | yat sa pāpakacittapravṛtterūrdhvaṃ saṅghamadhye 'pi pāpakaṃ kṛtvā nāpatrapate | tadanapatrāpyam | saddharmamūlātkuśaladharmadvayādbhaṣṭasya sadākuśaladharmānuvartanaṃ pramādaḥ | ebhistribhirdharmaiḥ samanvito gurusthānīyenacāryeṇānuśiṣṭhaṃ na samādatte | sā agauravatā | ācāryaśāsanasya viparyayācaraṇaṃ saṃkathyadūṣaṇam | evaṃ sati ācāryaṃ parivarjya ciraṃ durjanopasadanaṃ duṣprajñasevanam | ebhyo 'nūtpannamahrīkyamagauravatā | anapatrapādbhavati saṃkathyadūṣaṇam | pramādādbhavati durjanopasadanam | ato 'śrāddho bhūtvā dauḥśīlyaṃ samādāya kusīdo bhavati | durjanaṃ sevamānaḥ [ārya]śāsanamaśraddadhāna āha- nāsti duṣkṛtasya vipāka iti | duṣkṛtamācaran vipākaṃ vindata iti śṛṇvanmātro vā kukkaṭaśvādidharmaṃ samādāyātyantikapāpameva kāṅkṣate | taddharmaṃ samādāya na kiñciddhitamavindateti kausīdyamutpādayati | kausīdyāt sajjane 'prīto bhavati yat tattvato nāsti samyak caryāvihārīti | saddharmaśravaṇaṃ dviṣan āha samyak caritadharmā mithyādharmāḥ nāsti tataḥ kaścanopakāra iti | cittakaṣāyāt paradoṣaprakaṭane prīta āha- parasya dharmacaryāto matsadṛśaṃ nāsti kiñcilabdhamiti | evaṃ kleśānāmanigṛhītavataścittamuddhataṃ bhavati | auddhatyādindriyāṇāmasamādadhānasya śīlaṃ vipadyate | śīlavipattyā smṛtirmuṣitā bhavati | asamprajanye viharataścittaṃ vikṣipyate | ayoniśomanaskāraśca jāyate | jātāyoniśomanaskāratvāt durmārge carati | durmārge caran nārthaṃ pratilabhate | ataścittaṃ mugdhamatilīnaṃ bhavati | cittasya mohāt na trīṇi saṃyojanāni samucchedayati | asamucchinnatrisaṃyojanatvānna rāgādikleśān prajahati | tato vyādhyādayaḥ sarvā vipattayaśca bhavanti | eṣāṃ viruddhāḥ śukladharmāḥ |
body.translated_text: Why? When someone, being in seclusion, does something evil and is not ashamed — that is shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>). When that person, following the arising of evil intentions, does evil even in the midst of the <s>Saṅgha</s> and feels no moral dread — that is lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>). When one who has fallen from the root of the true <s>Dharma</s> and from the pair of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> constantly follows unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — that is heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). One endowed with these three <s>dharmas</s> does not accept the instruction of the teacher who occupies a position of authority. That is disrespectfulness. Acting contrary to the teacher's instructions is corruption of discourse. Being thus, having abandoned the teacher, prolonged association with bad people is association with the unwise. From these, when shamelessness has not yet arisen, disrespectfulness arises. From lack of moral dread comes corruption of discourse. From heedlessness comes association with bad people. Therefore, becoming faithless, one undertakes moral corruption and becomes lazy. Associating with bad people, not trusting the [noble] teaching, one says: 'There is no ripening of evil deeds.' Engaging in evil conduct and encountering its ripening, or merely hearing about it, one undertakes the <s>dharma</s> of the dog-vow (<s>kukkuṭa</s>) and the like, aspiring only to absolute evil. Having undertaken that <s>dharma</s> and finding no benefit whatsoever, one generates laziness. From laziness, one becomes displeased with good people, thinking that there truly is no proper practice and conduct. Hating the hearing of the true <s>Dharma</s>, one says: 'The properly practiced <s>dharmas</s> are false <s>dharmas</s>; there is no benefit from them.' From the affliction of mind, delighting in proclaiming others' faults, one says: 'From another's <s>Dharma</s>-practice, there is nothing comparable to mine that has been gained.' Thus, for one who has not restrained the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the mind becomes agitated. Due to restlessness, for one who does not guard the sense faculties, morality decays. Due to the decay of morality, mindfulness becomes confused. When one abides without clear comprehension, the mind becomes distracted. And improper mental attention arises. Because of the arising of improper mental attention, one walks the wrong path. Walking the wrong path, one does not attain the goal. Therefore the mind becomes bewildered and excessively withdrawn. Due to the delusion of mind, one does not eradicate the three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>). Because the three fetters are not eradicated, one does not abandon the <s>kleśas</s> of passion and the rest. From that, disease and all other misfortunes arise. The wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are the opposites of these.

body.text: śokaḥ samādherapakṣālaḥ | tasmin varṣe māse ayane samādhimamukaṃ nālabha iti cintayato yoginaḥ śoko jāyate |
body.translated_text: Grief (<s>śoka</s>) is an obstacle to <s>samādhi</s>. When the <s>yogin</s> (practitioner) reflects 'In that year, in that month, in that half-year, I did not attain such-and-such <s>samādhi</s>' — grief arises.

body.text: prītyāsvādane 'bhiniveśo 'pi samādhyapakṣālaḥ | anabhiratiśca samādherapakṣālaḥ | pratirūpadeśakalyāṇamitrādipratyayān labdhvāpi na cittamabhiramate |
body.translated_text: Attachment to the taste of joy (<s>prīti</s>) is also an obstacle to <s>samādhi</s>. And displeasure (<s>anabhirati</s>) is an obstacle to <s>samādhi</s>. Even having obtained conditions such as a suitable place and good spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), the mind does not delight.

body.text: kāmādīni nīvaraṇāni samādherapakṣālā bhavanti | saṃkṣipya yāvaccīvarapiṇḍapātādayo dharmāḥ kuśalamūlāpakarṣaḥ akuśalamūlaprakarṣaśca sarvāṇi samādherapakṣālāni bhavanti | iti buddhvā yatnena tānyapanetuṃ paryeṣeta ||
body.translated_text: The hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) beginning with sensual desire (<s>kāma</s>) are obstacles to <s>samādhi</s>. In brief, all <s>dharmas</s> including robes (<s>cīvara</s>) and alms-food (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>), the diminishing of wholesome roots and the increase of unwholesome roots — all of these are obstacles to <s>samādhi</s>. Having understood this, one should strive with effort to remove them.

body.text: samādhyapakṣālavargaḥ ṣaḍaśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the one hundred and sixteenth chapter, the Chapter on Obstacles to <s>Samādhi</s>.

body.text: 187 śamathavipaśyanāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 187. Chapter on <s>Śamatha</s> (Calm Abiding) and <s>Vipaśyanā</s> (Insight)

body.text: (pṛ) bhagavān tatra tatra sūtre bhikṣūnāmantryāha- [iha bhikṣuḥ] araṇyagato vāyatanagato vā vṛkṣamūlagato vā śūnyāgāragato vā manasi kuryāt dvau dharmau yaduta śamatho vipaśyanāca iti | yadi sarve dhyānasamadhyādidharmā manasi kartavyāḥ | kasmāt śamathavipaśyanāmātramāha | (u) śamatho nāma samādhiḥ | vipaśyanā prajñā | sarve ca kuśaladharmā bhāvanājātā iti dvāvimau parigṛhītau | vikṣiptacittagatāḥ śrutacintāmayādiprajñā apyatra saṅgṛhītāḥ | ābhyāṃ dvābhyāmeva mārgadharmaṃ karoti | kasmāt | śamatho hi saṃyojanā vyāvartayati | vipaśyanā samucchedayati |
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) here and there in the <s>sūtras</s>, saying: '[Here a <s>bhikṣu</s>], having gone to the forest, or to an empty place, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, should attend to two <s>dharmas</s>, namely <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).' If all <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) are to be attended to, why did he mention only <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>? (Answer) <s>Śamatha</s> is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). <s>Vipaśyanā</s> is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). And all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) are included in these two. Even the <s>prajñā</s> born of hearing and reflection (<s>śrutacintāmayā</s>) associated with a distracted mind is also included here. By means of these two alone, one accomplishes the <s>dharma</s> of the path. Why? Because <s>śamatha</s> turns away the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), and <s>vipaśyanā</s> eradicates them.

body.text: śamathastṛṇagrahopamaḥ vipaśyanā asinā tallavanopamā | śamatho bhūmimārjanopamaḥ | vipaśyanā gomayavikīrṇanopamā | śamatho rajomārjanopamaḥ | vipaśyanā jalena kṣālanopamā | śamatho jale nimajjanopamaḥ | vipaśyanā agnāvuttāpanopamā | śamatho gaṇḍopamaḥ | vipaśyanā śastracikitsopamā | śamathaḥ sirodgamopamaḥ | vipaśyanā raktapāṭanopamā | śamathaścittadamanopamaḥ | vipaśyanā atilīnacittavyutthānopamā | śamathaḥ suvarṇasya culukīkaraṇopamaḥ | vipaśyanā adhidhamanopamā | śamathaḥ sūtrapātopamaḥ | vipaśyanā bhūmisamīkaraṇopamā | śamathaḥ sandaśinyā sandaṃśopamaḥ | vipaśyanā śastreṇa kṛntanopamā | śamathaḥ kavacopamaḥ | vipaśyanā bhaṭānāṃ śastrādānopamā | śamathaḥ samīkriyopamāḥ | vipaśyanā śaṅkuvedhopamā | śamatho medaḥsevanopamaḥ | vipaśyanā auṣadhapradānopamā | śamathaḥ suvarṇakuṭṭanopamaḥ | vipaśyanā bhājanakaraṇopamā |
body.translated_text: <s>Śamatha</s> is like grasping with a hand; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like cutting with a sword in a forest. <s>Śamatha</s> is like sweeping the ground; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like spreading cow dung. <s>Śamatha</s> is like wiping away dust; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like washing with water. <s>Śamatha</s> is like immersion in water; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like heating in fire. <s>Śamatha</s> is like a lump [of medicine]; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like treatment with a sharp instrument. <s>Śamatha</s> is like rising to the head; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like dyeing with color. <s>Śamatha</s> is like taming the mind; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like rousing a mind that is excessively withdrawn. <s>Śamatha</s> is like smelting gold; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like blowing upon it. <s>Śamatha</s> is like the warp of thread; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like leveling the ground. <s>Śamatha</s> is like gripping with tongs; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like cutting with a blade. <s>Śamatha</s> is like armor; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like warriors taking up weapons. <s>Śamatha</s> is like bringing together; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like piercing with a pin. <s>Śamatha</s> is like applying fat; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like administering medicine. <s>Śamatha</s> is like hammering gold; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is like fashioning a vessel.

body.text: laukikāḥ sattvāḥ sarve sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā iti dvayorantayoḥ patitāḥ | śamathaḥ sukhaṃ tyajati | vipaśyanā dukhaṃ pariharati | kiñca saptasu viśuddhiṣu śīlaviśuddhiścittaviśuddhiśca śamathaḥ | anyāḥ pañca vipaśyanā | aṣṭamahāpuruṣavitarkeṣu ṣaḍvitarkāḥ śamathaḥ |
body.translated_text: Worldly beings all fall into one of two extremes: pleasure or pain. <s>Śamatha</s> relinquishes pleasure; <s>vipaśyanā</s> removes pain. Furthermore, among the seven purifications (<s>viśuddhi</s>), purification of morality (<s>śīlaviśuddhi</s>) and purification of mind (<s>cittaviśuddhi</s>) constitute <s>śamatha</s>. The other five constitute <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Among the eight contemplations of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣavitarka</s>), six contemplations constitute <s>śamatha</s> —

body.text: dvau vipaśyanā | caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu trīṇi śamathaḥ | caturthaṃ vipaśyanā | catvāri ṛddhipādāni śamathaḥ | catvāri samyakpradhānāni vipaśyanā | pañcasu indriyeṣu catvārīndriyāṇi śamathaḥ | prajñendriyaṃ vipaśyanā | evaṃ balamapi | saptasu bodhyaṅgeṣu trīṇi bodhyaṅgāni śamathaḥ | trīṇi bodhyaṅgāni vipaśyanā | smṛtistu ubhayagā | aṣṭasu mārgāṅgeṣu trīṇyaṅgāni śīlam | dve aṅge śamathaḥ | trīṇyaṅgāni vipaśyanā | śīlamapi śamathānubandhi | śamatho rāgaṃ samucchedayati | vipaśyanā avidyāmapanayati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- śamatho bhāvitaścittaṃ bhāvayati | cittaṃ bhāvitaṃ rāgaṃ prajahāti | vipaśyanā bhāvitā prajñāṃ bhāvayati | prajñā bhāvitā avidyāṃ prajahāti iti | kāmaviyuktatvāt cittaṃ vimucyate | avidyāviyuktatvāt prajñā vimucyate | tadubhayavimukti lābhino na punaḥ kiñcidavaśiṣyate | ato dvayamātramuktam |
body.translated_text: — two constitute <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Among the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), three constitute <s>śamatha</s>; the fourth constitutes <s>vipaśyanā</s>. The four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) constitute <s>śamatha</s>. The four right efforts (<s>samyakpradhāna</s>) constitute <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Among the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), four faculties constitute <s>śamatha</s>; the faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñendriya</s>) constitutes <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Likewise with the powers (<s>bala</s>). Among the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), three factors constitute <s>śamatha</s>; three factors constitute <s>vipaśyanā</s>; but mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) belongs to both. Among the eight path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>), three factors constitute morality (<s>śīla</s>); two factors constitute <s>śamatha</s>; three factors constitute <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Morality too is connected with <s>śamatha</s>. <s>Śamatha</s> eradicates passion (<s>rāga</s>); <s>vipaśyanā</s> removes ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Śamatha</s>, when cultivated, cultivates the mind. The mind, when cultivated, abandons passion. <s>Vipaśyanā</s>, when cultivated, cultivates wisdom. Wisdom, when cultivated, abandons ignorance.' Because one is separated from desire, the mind is liberated. Because one is separated from ignorance, wisdom is liberated. For the one who has gained both liberations, nothing further remains. Therefore only these two are mentioned.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi śamatho vipaśyanā cittaṃ bhāvayati prajñāṃ bhāvayati | cittaprajñābhāvitvāt rāgamavidyāñca prajahāti | kasmānniyama ucyate | śamathaścittaṃ bhāvayan rāgaṃ prajahāti | vipaśyanā prajñāṃ bhāvayantī avidyāṃ prajahātīti | (u) vikṣiptacittakasya cittasantānāni rūpādiṣu samudācaranti | santanyamānamidaṃ cittaṃ śamathaṃ labhate | tacchamanāducyate śamathaścittaṃ bhāvayatīti | śamitāccittājjāyate prajñā | ata ucyate vipaśyanā prajñāṃ bhāvayatīti | utpannavipaśyanasyordhvaṃ yatkiñcidbhāvitaṃ sarvaṃ bhāvitā prajñetyucyate | ādyā prajñā vipaśyanā paścāprajñetyucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) If <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> cultivate mind and wisdom respectively, and through the cultivation of mind and wisdom one abandons passion and ignorance, why is there a fixed rule stated that <s>śamatha</s> cultivates the mind and abandons passion, while <s>vipaśyanā</s> cultivates wisdom and abandons ignorance? (Answer) For one whose mind is distracted, the mental continuum operates upon form and other [sense objects]. When this mind is being continued [in practice], it attains <s>śamatha</s>. Because of that calming, it is said '<s>śamatha</s> cultivates the mind.' From the calmed mind, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) arises. Therefore it is said '<s>vipaśyanā</s> cultivates wisdom.' After insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>) has arisen, whatever is further cultivated — all of it is called 'cultivated wisdom.' The initial wisdom is called <s>vipaśyanā</s>; the subsequent one is called <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).

body.text: yathoktaṃ sūtre- śamatho bhāvito rāgaṃ prajahātīti | idaṃ vidhnībhūtaprahāṇaṃ bhavati | kena tat jñāyate | rūpādiṣu bāhyakāmeṣu rāgo jāyate | śamathauṣadhaṃ labdhavato na punarjāyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yogī nirāmiṣāṃ prītiṃ labhamānaḥ sāmiṣāṃ prītiṃ jahāti iti | yaduktamavidyāprahāṇamiti, tadātyantikaprahāṇam | kena tat jñāyate | avidyāprahāṇāddhi rāgādayaḥ kleśāḥ prahīyante nirudhyante nāvaśiṣyante | sūtre 'pyuktam- rāgavirāgāt cetovimuktiḥ | idaṃ vighnībhūtaprahāṇaṃ bhavati | avidyāvirāgāt prajñāvimuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Śamatha</s> (tranquility), when cultivated, abandons <s>rāga</s> (passion).' This is <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment). How is this known? <s>Rāga</s> (passion) arises toward external desires such as form and so forth. For one who has obtained the medicine of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), it does not arise again. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>yogī</s>, obtaining <s>nirāmiṣā prīti</s> (non-material rapture), abandons <s>sāmiṣā prīti</s> (material rapture).' What was stated as 'the abandonment of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)' — that is <s>ātyantikaprahāṇa</s> (ultimate abandonment). How is this known? Through the abandonment of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as <s>rāga</s> (passion) and others are abandoned, ceased, and nothing remains. It is also stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Through dispassion from <s>rāga</s> (passion), there is <s>cetovimukti</s> (liberation of mind).' This is <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment). 'Through dispassion from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), there is <s>prajñāvimukti</s> (liberation through wisdom).'

body.text: idamātyantikaprahāṇam | iti | asti ca dvidhā vimuktiḥ sāmayikavimuktiḥ akopyavimuktiriti | sāmayikavimuktirvighnībhūtaprahāṇam | akopyavimuktirātyantikaprahāṇam |
body.translated_text: This is <s>ātyantikaprahāṇa</s> (ultimate abandonment). Thus, there are two kinds of <s>vimukti</s> (liberation): <s>sāmayikavimukti</s> (temporary liberation) and <s>akopyavimukti</s> (unshakeable liberation). <s>Sāmayikavimukti</s> (temporary liberation) is <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment). <s>Akopyavimukti</s> (unshakeable liberation) is <s>ātyantikaprahāṇa</s> (ultimate abandonment).

body.text: (pṛ) sāmayikī vimuktiḥ pañcavidhānāmarhatāmanāsravā vimuktiḥ | akopyā vimuktiścākopyadharmaṇo 'rhato 'nāsravā vimuktiḥ | kasmādvidhnībhūtaprahāṇamātramucyate | (u) neyamanāsravā vimuktiḥ | kasmāt | samayavimukto hi yat adhikabalena kañcitkālaṃ saṃyojanāni vighnayati nātyantaṃ prajahāti | paścātpunaḥ [saṃyojanāni]prādurbhavanti | ato nānāsravā[sā] bhavati | vimuktiriyaṃ sāmayikatṛṣṇāvimuktiḥ | kṣīṇāsravasyārhato nāsti kiñcidiṣyamāṇam | (pṛ) tathā ced nāryasyeṣyamāṇaṃ śīlam | (u) śaikṣāṇāmakṣīṇāsravatvāt ātmamatiḥ kadācitprādurbhavati | ataḥ śīle jāyata iṣṭam | nārhato 'tyantaprahīṇātmamateḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question) <s>Sāmayikī vimukti</s> (temporary liberation) is the <s>anāsravā vimukti</s> (outflow-free liberation) of the five types of <s>Arhats</s>. <s>Akopyā vimukti</s> (unshakeable liberation) is the <s>anāsravā vimukti</s> (outflow-free liberation) of the <s>Arhat</s> of unshakeable nature. Why is it called merely <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment)? (Answer) This is not <s>anāsravā vimukti</s> (outflow-free liberation). Why? Because one who is temporarily liberated, through superior strength, obstructs the <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters) for some time but does not ultimately abandon them. Afterwards, the <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters) manifest again. Therefore it is not <s>anāsravā</s> (outflow-free). This liberation is <s>sāmayika-tṛṣṇā-vimukti</s> (temporary liberation from craving). For the <s>Arhat</s> whose outflows are destroyed, there is nothing that is desired. (Question) If so, then the <s>Ārya</s> (noble one) would not desire moral conduct. (Answer) For <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners), because their outflows are not yet destroyed, the notion of self sometimes manifests. Therefore desire arises regarding moral conduct. But not for the <s>Arhat</s> whose notion of self has been ultimately abandoned.

body.text: (pṛ) godhiko 'rhan ṣaḍvāraṃ sāmayikavimukteḥ parihiṇaḥ | saptamaparihāṇabhayādasinātmānaṃ jaghāna | yadi sa āsravān vināśitavān, nātmānaṃ hanyāt | ato jñāyate samayavimukto nānāsrava ityucyate | (u) ayaṃ spṛṣṭāt saṃyojanaprahāṇātsamādheḥ parihīṇaḥ | asmātsamādheḥ ṣaṭkṛtva parihīṇaḥ | saptamavāraṃ spṛṣṭvā samādhimimaṃ ātmānaṃ hantumaicchat | tasmin samaye saṃkalpito 'rhanmārgamaspṛśat | ato māraḥ śaikṣo vivṛttakāyaskandhaṃ mṛta iti ācaturdigantaṃ tadvijñāpanāya yena bhagavān tenopasaṃkramya bhagavantametadavocat |
body.translated_text: (Question) <s>Godhika</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, fell from <s>sāmayikavimukti</s> (temporary liberation) six times. Fearing a seventh fall, he killed himself with a sword. If he had destroyed the outflows, he would not have killed himself. Therefore it is known that one who is temporarily liberated is not called <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free). (Answer) He fell from the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) through which he had attained the abandonment of <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters). Having fallen from this <s>samādhi</s> six times, upon touching it a seventh time, he wished to kill himself. At that time, having resolved, he touched the path of an <s>Arhat</s>. Therefore <s>Māra</s>, [thinking he was] a learner, [searched] in the four directions to find where the deceased body-aggregate had gone, and approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
śrāvakaste [mahāvīra maraṇaṃ maraṇābhibhūḥ |]
akāṃkṣate cetayate [tanniṣedhadyutendriya] |
body.translated_text:
'Your disciple, O <s>Mahāvīra</s> (Great Hero), overcome by death, seeks death;
he desires it and contemplates it, [you of] radiant faculties should prevent this.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān [māra iti viditvā ta]mavocat |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing [him to be <s>Māra</s>], said to him:

body.text: evaṃ hi dhīrāḥ kurvanti nākāṃkṣante [ca
body.translated_text:
'Thus indeed the wise act, they do not cling to life;
having uprooted <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) with its root, <s>Godhika</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text:
jīvitam |]
samūlāṃ tṛṣṇāmṛdgṛhya godhikaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ || iti |

(pṛ) yaḥ kṣīṇarāgaḥ sa vighnībhūtaprahāṇakaḥ | sūtra uktaṃ- rāgāccetovimuktiḥ | dveṣamohābhyāṃ prajñāvimuktiriti | kiñcāha- nandirāgaprahāṇācceto vimuktiriti | āha- kāmāsravāccittaṃ vimucyata iti | evaṃ vighnībhūtavimuktiḥ syāt na pāramārthikavimuktiḥ | (u) atrāpyuktam- avidyā prahīyata iti | ato jñāyata iyamātyantikavimuktiriti | yadi mataṃ rāgaprahāṇaṃ kadācidvidhnībhūtaprahāṇaṃ, kadācidātyantikaprahāṇamiti | anutpannatattvajñānasyedaṃ vidhnībhūtaprahāṇam | tattvajñānānusāriṇa atyantikaprahāṇam | nāsti tu kaścit [kevalaṃ] śamathaṃ spṛṣṭvā rāgamātyantikaṃ prajahātīti | tathā cet tīrthikā api rāgamātyantikaṃ prajahyuḥ | vastutastu na tathā | ato jñāyata idaṃ vighnībhūtaprahāṇamātramiti |
body.translated_text: (Question) One whose <s>rāga</s> (passion) is destroyed has <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment). The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'From <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>cetovimukti</s> (liberation of mind); from <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred) and <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>prajñāvimukti</s> (liberation through wisdom).' Moreover it says: 'Through the abandonment of <s>nandirāga</s> (delight-passion), there is liberation of mind.' It says: 'The mind is liberated from <s>kāmāsrava</s> (outflow of desire).' Thus there would be only <s>vighnībhūtavimukti</s> (obstruction-type liberation), not <s>pāramārthikavimukti</s> (ultimate liberation). (Answer) Here too it is stated: '<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is abandoned.' Therefore it is known that this is <s>ātyantikaprahāṇa</s> (ultimate abandonment). If you think that the abandonment of <s>rāga</s> is sometimes <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment) and sometimes <s>ātyantikaprahāṇa</s> (ultimate abandonment) — for one who has not generated knowledge of reality, this is <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment); for one who follows knowledge of reality, it is <s>ātyantikaprahāṇa</s> (ultimate abandonment). There is no one who, having merely attained <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), ultimately abandons <s>rāga</s> (passion). If so, even <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist practitioners) would ultimately abandon <s>rāga</s>. But in reality it is not so. Therefore it is known that this is merely <s>vighnībhūtaprahāṇa</s> (obstruction-type abandonment).

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- śamathena cittaṃ bhāvayati | vipaśyanāmupādāya vimuktiṃ spṛśati | vipaśyanayā cittaṃ bhāvayati | śamathamupādāya vimuktiṃ spṛśatīti | tat katham | (u) yogīyadi samādhiṃ pratītya kṣayamālambya prajñāmutpādayati | tadocyate śamathena cittaṃ bhāvayati | vipaśyanāmupādāya vimuktiṃ spṛśatīti | yadi vikṣiptacittena skandhadhātvāyatanādīni vikalpayati | tatpratītya kṣayamālambya śamathaṃ spṛśati | tadocyate vipaśyanayā cittaṃ bhāvayati | śamathamupādāya vimuktiṃ spṛśatīti | yadi smṛtyupasthānādīni nirvedhabhāgīyāni spṛṣṭvā cittaṃ parigṛhṇāti | tadā śabhathaṃ vipaśyanāṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvayatīti | sarve ca yogino dvāvimau dharmau niśritya cittaṃ nirudhya vimuktiṃ spṛśanti ||
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'Through <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) one cultivates the mind. Relying on <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), one touches liberation. Through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) one cultivates the mind. Relying on <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), one touches liberation.' How is this? (Answer) If the <s>yogī</s>, relying on <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), taking cessation as object, generates <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — then it is said 'through <s>śamatha</s> one cultivates the mind; relying on <s>vipaśyanā</s> one touches liberation.' If with a distracted mind one discriminates the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and so forth, and relying on that, taking cessation as object, touches <s>śamatha</s> — then it is said 'through <s>vipaśyanā</s> one cultivates the mind; relying on <s>śamatha</s> one touches liberation.' If, having touched the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) and other <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetrative) practices, one restrains the mind — then one cultivates <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> in <s>yuganaddha</s> (yoked pair). All <s>yogīs</s>, relying on these two <s>dharmas</s>, cease the mind and touch liberation.

body.text: śamathavipaśyanāvargaḥ saptāśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter on <s>Śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>Vipaśyanā</s> (insight), the one hundred and eighty-seventh.

body.text: 188 samādhibhāvanāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 188. Chapter on the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).

body.text: (pṛ) bhavānavocat- samādhiṃ bhāvayediti | samādhicittamidaṃ pratiṇakṣamutpannavināśi | tat kathaṃ bhāvayitavyaṃ bhavati | (u) pratyakṣaṃ paśyāmaḥ khalu kāyikaṃ karma pratikṣaṇavināśyapi bhāvanāvaśādvibhinnakauśalaṃ bhavati | bhāvanāvaśāt ciraṃ punaḥ punaḥ pravartyamānaṃ sat sukaraṃ bhavati | tathā vācikaṃ karmāpi | anuvihitāvṛtti āvṛttyā ca praguṇīkṛtaṃ dṛḍhībhūtañca susmaraṇaṃ bhavati yathādhyayanādi | mānasaṃ karma ca kṣaṇikamapi bhāvayitavyamiti jñātavyam | yathāgnirjanyaṃ vikārayati | āpaḥ śilā bhedayanti | vāyuḥ padārthān vidhamati | evaṃ kṣaṇikadharmāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃhatānāṃ balamasti | kleśā yathāvāsanamanuvardhante | yathā kaścit punaḥ punarmaithunacittaṃ bhāvayan bahūn kāmānabhinirvartayati | tathā dveṣamohāvapi | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo yadvastucittaṃ manasi karoti sa tatra pratipannaḥ | tadyathā sadā kāmavitarkacittamanusaran kāmāya pratipadyate | evamanyau dvau vitarkāvapi | iti | ato jñāyate cittamidaṃ kṣaṇikamapi bhāvayitavyaṃ bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: (Question) You have said 'one should cultivate <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).' This <s>samādhi</s>-mind perishes at every moment. How then is it to be cultivated? (Answer) We directly perceive that physical action, though perishing at every moment, through the power of cultivation becomes distinctly skillful. Through the power of cultivation, being practiced repeatedly over a long time, it becomes easy. Similarly with verbal action. Through repeated practice, what has been rehearsed becomes well-established, firmly fixed, and easily remembered — like studying and so forth. Mental action too, though momentary, should be understood as requiring cultivation. Just as fire transforms what it produces, water splits rocks, and wind scatters objects — thus all momentary <s>dharmas</s>, when aggregated, have power. <s>Kleśas</s> (afflictions) increase according to their habitual tendencies. Just as someone, repeatedly cultivating thoughts of sexual desire, produces many desires — so too with <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred) and <s>moha</s> (delusion). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whoever directs the mind to whatever object, he proceeds toward that. Just as one who constantly follows thoughts of desire proceeds toward desire — so too with the other two types of thought.' Therefore it is known that this mind, though momentary, is to be cultivated.

body.text: bhāvanā nāmopacayaḥ | dṛśyante dṛṣṭe sarve dharmāḥ sopacayāḥ | yathoktaṃsūtre- yogī khalu ayoniśo manasikārāt kāmādīnāsravānanutpannānutpādayati | utpannān vivardhayati | yadavarānmadhyamutpādayati | madhyāduttamamutpādayati | tadyathā bījādaṅkuramaṅkurātkāṇḍaṃ kāṇḍānnāḷaṃ nāḷāt patraṃ patrātpuṣpaṃ puṣpātphalamiti pratyakṣato hetuto 'nupūrvaṃ vivardhate | samādhisamprajanyādidharmā apyevameva syuḥ | pratyakṣato dṛṣṭaṃ khalu vāsitatilasya gandhaḥ saṃṅgkrātyā vardhata iti | ayaṃ gandhastilañca pratikṣaṇamavidyamānaṃ, tathāpi tadvāsanābalamasti | ato jñāyate kṣaṇikā dharmā api bhāvayitavyā iti |
body.translated_text: Cultivation means accumulation. It is observed that all <s>dharmas</s> in the visible world are subject to accumulation. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>yogī</s>, through improper mental attention, causes the unarisen outflows of desire and so forth to arise, and causes those that have arisen to increase. He causes what is inferior to become middling, and what is middling to become superior.' Just as from a seed comes a sprout, from a sprout a stalk, from a stalk a stem, from a stem a leaf, from a leaf a flower, from a flower a fruit — so it increases gradually through causes as directly observed. <s>Dharmas</s> such as <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>samprajanya</s> (clear comprehension) should also be just like this. It is directly observed that the fragrance of perfumed sesame increases through transmission. This fragrance and the sesame are non-existent at each moment, yet the power of that habitual imprint exists. Therefore it is known that even momentary <s>dharmas</s> are to be cultivated.

body.text: (pṛ) tilaṃ vartamānadharmaḥ | vāsito gandha āgantukaḥ | avidyamānaṃ cittaṃ kṣaṇikajñānenāgatya bhāvyate | kathaṃ dṛṣṭānto bhavet | (u) nāsti kaścidvidyamānadharmaḥ sarve ca dharmāḥ kṣaṇikā iti pūrvameva sādhitam | ato nāsti dūṣaṇama | yadi dharmā akṣaṇikāḥ, na bhāvayitavyāḥ | svarūpata eva sadāsthitasya bhāvanayā ka upakāraḥ | yadi dharmaḥ pratikṣaṇavināśi,
body.translated_text: (Question) Sesame is a presently existing <s>dharma</s>. The perfumed fragrance is adventitious. The non-existent mind is to be cultivated by momentary knowledge arriving — how can this analogy apply? (Answer) There is no existing <s>dharma</s> whatsoever; all <s>dharmas</s> are momentary — this has been established previously. Therefore there is no fault. If <s>dharmas</s> were non-momentary, they would not need cultivation. What benefit would cultivation bring to something that always exists in its own nature? If a <s>dharma</s> perishes at every moment,

body.text: [tadā] avarānmadhyaṃ madhyāduttamamiti dharmasya bhāvanā bhavet | (pṛ) kusumāni tilaṃ prāpya vāsayanti | jñānantu na cittamāpnoti | ato nāsti bhāvanā | (u) pūrvakarmadṛṣṭānte pratipāditamidam | yaduttarabhāvikarma na pūrvabhāvikarma prāpnoti | purvavacanaṃ nottarabhāvivacanamapekṣate | tathāpi kāyikavācikakarmaṇorasti ca bhāvanālakṣaṇam | ato 'prāptaṃ na bhāvyata iti tava vacanaṃ na dūṣaṇāya bhavati | pratyakṣato dṛśyate ca hetuphalayorayaugapadye 'pi bhavatyeva hetoḥ phalaṃ bhavatīti | evaṃ cittadharmasya kṣaṇikatve 'pi bhāvanāstyeva | yathā ca bījaṃ salilasiktamaṅkurādīnaprāpyāpi aṅkurādīnaṅkurayati | evaṃ prajñā pūrvacitaṃ bhāvayati tadūrdhvacittamupacitaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: then cultivation of <s>dharma</s> would be from inferior to middling, from middling to superior. (Question) Flowers, having reached the sesame, perfume it. But knowledge does not reach the mind. Therefore there is no cultivation. (Answer) This has been demonstrated by the analogy of previous action. The subsequent action does not reach the previous action. The previous speech does not depend on the subsequent speech. Yet there is the characteristic of cultivation in physical and verbal action. Therefore your statement that 'what is not reached cannot be cultivated' does not serve as a refutation. It is directly observed that even when cause and effect are not simultaneous, the effect still arises from the cause. Thus even though the mental <s>dharma</s> is momentary, cultivation still exists. Just as a seed, watered, produces sprouts and so forth without reaching them — so <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) cultivates the previously accumulated, and the mind above that becomes accumulated.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi kṣaṇikāttilāt tilāntaraṃ jāyate | kimidaṃ tilaṃ vāsitaṃ jāyate, avāsitaṃ vā | yadyavāsitaṃ jāyate, naiva bhavedvāsanāvat | yadi vāsitaṃ jāyate | punaḥ ka upayogaściravāsana [kriya]yā | (u) vāsanāhetutvāt | yathā bijātsalilasiktādaṅkuro 'ṅkurayate | evaṃ pūrvakusumayogaṃ pratītya tilāntaraṃ jāyate | idaṃ tu vāsitaṃ jāyate | bhavānavocat- ka upayogaścirakālavāsanayeti | yathā bhavatāṃ sūtra uktaṃ- agnisaṃyogādaṇuṣu kṛṣṇavarṇe niruddhe raktavarṇaṃ jāyata iti | yadyādāvagnisaṃyuktadharmasya kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ nirudhyata iti | na syātpunaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇasyotpattiḥ | yadyādāvagnisaṃyuktadharmasya raktavarṇamutpadyata iti punaḥ paścādagnisaṃyuktadharmaḥ kimartham | yadyādāvagnisaṃyogakāle kṛṣṇavarṇamutpadyate | raktavarṇaṃ naivotpadyeta | yadi dvitīyakṣaṇe raktavarṇaṃ jāyate | punaraścirakālāgnisaṃyogaḥ kimartham | yadi bhavatāmabhisandhiḥ raktavarṇaṃ kramaśo jāyata iti | cittamapyevamiti ko doṣaḥ | tathā vipariṇāmādirapi |
body.translated_text: (Question) If from a momentary sesame seed another sesame arises — does this sesame arise perfumed or unperfumed? If it arises unperfumed, then there would be no fragrance at all. If it arises perfumed, then what is the use of prolonged perfuming? (Answer) Because it is the cause of habitual imprint. Just as from a seed watered, a sprout sprouts — so relying on the previous contact with flowers, another sesame arises. And this arises perfumed. You said 'what is the use of long-duration perfuming?' — just as in your <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'Through contact with fire, when the black color in atoms ceases, red color arises.' If at first, for the <s>dharma</s> conjoined with fire, black color ceases — there should be no further arising of black color. If at first, for the <s>dharma</s> conjoined with fire, red color arises — then what need is there for further fire-conjunction? If at the first moment of fire-conjunction black color arises, red color would never arise. If at the second moment red color arises, then what is the purpose of prolonged fire-conjunction? If your intended meaning is that red color arises gradually — then the mind too is just like this; what fault is there? Similarly with transformation and the rest.

body.text: sarve dharmā sahetusapratyayā api kramaśo jāyante | yathā garbhādhānādikrameṇa śarīramabhinirvartyate | evaṃ prajñāsamādhyādayo dharmāḥ kṣaṇikā api avaramadhyottamadharmakrameṇa jāyante | bhāvanādharmaḥ sūkṣmo 'pi cittasantatimanyathayati | yathā pakṣacchadasyoṣmaṇi mṛdunyapi aṇḍaṃ kramaśo vikriyate | pāṇitalamāṃsamardanāt vāśījaṭā sūkṣmaśaḥ kṣīyate | evaṃ cittamapi | samāhitaprajñā sūkṣmetyataḥ kramaśo bhāvyate | dharmaṃ bhāvayan prāptikāle tāvat jānāti |
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s>, even though they have causes and conditions, arise gradually. Just as through the process beginning with conception, the body is produced — so <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), though momentary, arise in the sequence of inferior, middling, and superior. The <s>dharma</s> of cultivation, though subtle, transforms the mind-continuum. Just as with the gentle warmth of a wing-feather, an egg is gradually transformed; as through rubbing with the palm, the blade of an adze gradually wears down — so too with the mind. Since concentrated <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is subtle, it is cultivated gradually. One who cultivates the <s>dharma</s> knows it at the time of attainment.

body.text: yathoktaṃ gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: As stated in the verse:

body.text:
ācāryātsarvamādatte, sarva[tat] mi(mai?)trahetukam |
ātmacetanayā sarva, sarva pāke kālamapekṣate || iti |
body.translated_text:
'One receives everything from the teacher, everything is due to spiritual friends;
everything is through one's own awareness, and everything awaits the time of ripening.'
