body.text: kaścidajasramadhīyāno 'pi na pratyeti paripavkakālika iva | yathā bahubhiḥ puṣpairekasmin samaye tilaṃ vāsayati na yathā puṣpālpāni kramaśaściraṃ vāsayanti | medasā paripuṣṭiḥ jale [naukā] nimajjanaṃ bhittinirmāṇaṃ ityādirapi tathā | pratyakṣaṃ khalu [naḥ] bījāṅkurādīnāmupacayo 'tisūkṣmaḥ, naiva draṣṭuṃ śakyate | teṣāṃ dainandina upacayaḥ kleśānāṃ gaṇanā | bālakādīnāṃ śarīraṃ stanyapānādinā paripacyata itīdamapi tathā syāt | ato jñāyate dharmabhāvanā sūkṣmā praṇītā duravabodhā ceti |
body.translated_text: Someone, even though studying constantly, does not understand, like [a thing that takes its] cooking time. Just as many flowers perfume sesame all at once, not as a few flowers gradually perfume [it] over a long time. Nourishment by fat, sinking [of a boat] in water, building a wall — and so forth — are also likewise. It is indeed directly perceived [by us] that the growth of seeds, sprouts, and the like is extremely subtle and cannot even be seen. Their daily accumulation is [like] the counting of defilements. That the bodies of infants and the like are matured by breast-milk and the like — this too would be so. From this it is known that the cultivation of <s>dharma</s> is subtle, refined, and difficult to understand.

body.text: (pṛ) kadāciddharmo yugapadupacīyate | kaścitpūrvaṃ rūpamadṛṣṭvāpi taddarśanamātreṇa tatrābhiniviśate | kaścidalpakāle 'pi bahu pratisaṃvedī bhavati | kasmāducyate kramikaiva bhāvaneti | (u) sarvasyātītabhāvitvāt | ato jñāyata upacitā bhāvanā kramiketi | idaṃ pratipāditameva | na cittotpādamātreṇa yatkiñcitsādhayati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yaḥ kuśaladharmeṣu na bhāvanāyogamanuyuktaḥ kuśaladharmānanupādāya kevalaṃ praṇidadhāti āsravebhyaścittavimokam | naivāsya cintitaṃ praṇidhānādbhavati | kuśaladharmeṣu bhāvanāyogānanuyuktatvāt iti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Sometimes <s>dharma</s> accumulates all at once. Someone, even without having seen a form before, becomes absorbed in it merely from seeing it. Someone, even in a short time, becomes one who experiences much. Why is it said that cultivation is only gradual? (Answer) Because everything has the nature of having a past [cause]. From this it is known that the accumulated cultivation is gradual. This has already been demonstrated. One does not accomplish anything merely by the arising of a thought. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whoever, not devoted to the practice of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, without taking up wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, merely makes a resolve for the liberation of mind from the outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) — his aspiration does not come about from that resolve, because he is not devoted to the practice of cultivation in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: yogī yadi kuśaladharmeṣu bhāvanāyogamanuyukto bhavati | akṛtapraṇidhānasyāpi [tasya] āsravebhyaścittaṃ vimucyate | hetorhi phalaṃ jāyate na praṇidhānāt | tadyathā pakṣiṇāmaṇḍasaṃsparśa āvaśyakaḥ | na praṇidhānāt janturaṇḍānnirgacchati | na ca praṇidhānātpradīpaprakāśaḥ pariśuddho bhavati | kintu pariśuddhatailaṃ pariśuddhavartikāñcobhayamapekṣya [anya]vastusaṃsparśacāñcalyarāhitye ca tatprakāśaḥ pariśuddho bhavati | kiñca na praṇidhānamātreṇa dhānyaṃ labhyate | kintu avaśyaṃ sūkṣetrasadbījartuvṛttisamīkriyākṛṣikarmaṇāṃ sākalye tatpratilābho bhavati | nāpi ca praṇidhānamātrāt deho rūpaṃ balañca labhate | avaśyaṃ vastrauṣadhāhārapoṣaṇādipratyayena tu paripūrṇo bhavati | evaṃ na praṇidhānamātrādāsravāṇāṃ kṣayo bhavati | avaśyaṃ tatvajñānamapekṣya vimucyate | ko jñānī hetoḥ phalaṃ jāyata iti prajānan taddhetumupekṣya anyasmātphalamākāṃkṣeta |
body.translated_text: If the <s>yogī</s> is devoted to the practice of cultivation in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, even without having made a resolve, his mind is freed from the outflows (<s>āsravas</s>). For the fruit arises from the cause, not from the resolve. Just as, for birds, the contact of the egg [with warmth] is indispensable — a creature does not emerge from the egg by mere resolve. Nor does the light of a lamp become pure by mere resolve. Rather, depending on both pure oil and a pure wick, and in the absence of contact with or disturbance by other substances, its light becomes pure. Moreover, grain is not obtained merely by resolve. Rather, the obtaining of that necessarily occurs when there is a totality of [conditions such as] a good field, good seeds, seasonal weather, leveling of the ground, and plowing work. Nor does the body obtain form and strength merely by resolve. It necessarily becomes complete through the condition of clothing, medicine, food, nourishment, and the like. Thus the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) does not occur merely from resolve. It is necessarily through dependence on the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) that one is freed. What wise person, knowing that the fruit arises from the cause, would disregard that cause and hope for a fruit from something else?

body.text: dharma bhāvayan dṛṣṭa eva phalavipākaṃ paśyati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- tiṣṭhantu saptadināni mayā śāsitāḥ śrāvakā muhūrtaṃ tāvatkuśaladharmaṃ bhāvayanto 'pramāṇavarṣeṣu nityaṃ sukhāṃ vedanāṃ spṛśanti iti | bhikṣuṇyo bhadantamānandamavocan- vayaṃ smṛtyupasthāneṣu supratiṣṭhitacittā viharantyaḥ pūrveṇāparaṃ viśeṣaṃ samprajānīma iti | sūtre ca bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantryāha- aśaṭhasya māmupasaṅkramato yanmayā prātarupadiṣṭo dharmaḥ tadartha sāyaṃ vindate | yat sāyamupadiṣṭo dharmaḥ prātastaddhitaṃ vindata iti | yaccārhanmārgaṃ spṛśati na tat parapudgalaḥ prayacchati | nānanyapudgalaḥ | kevalaṃ samyagghetubhāvanātastaddhitamāpnoti | anuttaraṃ buddhamārga eva nanu kuśaladharmasyopacitabhāvanayā spṛśati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantryāha- dvau dharmau niśrityāhamanuttaraṃ mārgaṃ samāpannaḥ yat śubhābhiratāvanirvedo mārgabhāvanāyāmaklāntiśca iti | bhagavataḥ kuśaladharmāṇāṃ nāsti sīmā |
body.translated_text: One who cultivates <s>dharma</s> sees the ripening of the fruit in this very life. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Let the seven days stand — my instructed disciples (<s>śrāvakas</s>), cultivating wholesome <s>dharma</s> for even a moment, touch pleasant feeling constantly for immeasurable years.' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) said to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'We, dwelling with minds well-established in the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), discern a distinctive [improvement] from the former to the latter.' And in the <s>sūtra</s> the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'For one who approaches me without deceit, whatever <s>dharma</s> I teach in the morning — he obtains its benefit by evening. Whatever <s>dharma</s> I teach in the evening — he obtains its benefit by morning.' And the touching of the <s>Arhat</s>-path — no other person bestows it, nor does any non-other person. Only through the cultivation of right causes does one attain that benefit. It is precisely through the accumulated cultivation of wholesome <s>dharma</s> that one touches the unsurpassed path of a <s>Buddha</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: Relying on two <s>dharmas</s>, I have attained the unsurpassed path — namely, non-weariness in delighting in virtue and unwearied effort in the cultivation of the path.' There is no limit to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: bodhisattvāḥ samādhimaspṛśanto 'pi na kusīdā bhavanti | kasmāt | kuśale 'kṛte na kiñcilabhyate | kuśale kṛte 'pi nākāre parivṛttiḥ | kuśalamakurvato naiva kṣaimaṃ bhavati | idaṃ cintayitvā vīryamārabhamāṇaḥ kuśaladharmaṃ bhāvayet | vīryamārabhamāṇasya lābho vā bhavati hānirvā | akṛtavīryasya naivāsti pratyāśā | ato bhāvanāmārabheta mā parikhedo bhūditi | prājñaḥ paryavasāne 'vaśyaṃ mucyate | bhāvanāvinirmuktasya na punarastyupāyaḥ | ataḥ prājñena bhāvanārabdhavyā, mā parikhedo janayitavyaḥ | yogī sucaritacaryāyā asti phalavipāka ityanusmṛtya alabhamāno 'pi na viṣādaṃ karoti | kiñca yogī manasi kuryāt- mayā bhāvanāyāḥ phalavipāko 'nuprāpta eva | pūrvāgataiḥ sattvaiḥ sarveṣāṃ dhyānasamādhīnāṃ [phalavipākasya] anuprāptatvāt | mamedānīṃ samyagbhāvanāpi phalavipākamanuprāpsyatīti | ato na parikhidyāt |
body.translated_text: Even <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have not yet touched <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) do not become idle. Why? Without having done the wholesome, nothing is obtained. Even when the wholesome is done, there is no reversal without [further] effort. For one who does not do the wholesome, there is never well-being. Having reflected thus, the one who arouses effort should cultivate wholesome <s>dharma</s>. For one who arouses effort, there is either gain or loss; but for one who has not aroused effort, there is not even hope. Therefore one should undertake cultivation — let there be no discouragement. The wise person, at the end, is certainly liberated. For one who is not freed through cultivation, there is no other means. Therefore, the wise person should undertake cultivation and should not generate discouragement. The <s>yogī</s>, recollecting that there is a ripening of fruit from well-practiced conduct, does not despair even when not obtaining [immediate results]. Furthermore, the <s>yogī</s> should reflect: 'The ripening of the fruit of cultivation has indeed been attained by me, because beings of the past have attained the ripening of all <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). My proper cultivation too will attain the ripening of the fruit.' Therefore one should not be discouraged.

body.text: sucaritaśālini tathāgataḥ pratyakṣaṃ karoti | ahamidānīṃ samyagācarāmītyato jñānamavaśyamanuprāpsyate | ahaṃ mārgasamāpattipratyayasampannaḥ yat manuṣyadehaprāptiravikalendriyatā puṇyapāpavijñātṛtā vimuktāvapi cādhimuktatā abhyāgatasambuddhitā ityetaiḥ pratyayaiḥ samanvitaḥ kathaṃ na bhāvanāphalavipākamanuprāpsye | vīryasamācaraṇamamoghameva | ato na parikhidyate |
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> makes it directly evident to one who excels in good conduct. 'I am now practicing well' — from this, knowledge will necessarily be attained. I am endowed with the conditions for path-attainment — namely, the obtaining of a human body, intact sense-faculties, the ability to distinguish merit and demerit, faith in liberation, and the arrival of an awakened <s>Buddha</s>. Endowed with these conditions, how would I not attain the ripening of the fruit of cultivation? The undertaking of effort is never in vain. Therefore one is not discouraged.

body.text: kleśānāṃ prahāṇamatisūkṣmaṃ dūravabodhaṃ vāśījaṭāyāṃ kramaśaḥ kṣayavat | mama kleśānāmapi bhavetprahāṇam | saukṣmyātparaṃ na sambudhyate | ato jñāyate kuśalaṃ bhāvayituṃ vīryamuttamaṃ bhavatīti | alpīyasī prajñāpi kleśān vināśayati yathā alpīyān prakāśo 'ndhakāramapanayati | evamalpīyasīṃ prajñāṃ labhamānaḥ kṛtakṛtyo bhavati | ato na parikhidyate | dīrghakāye 'pi dussādhanā yat samādhisamāpattiḥ | yadi samādhiṃ samāpadyate | tadānye guṇā acireṇa bhavanti | ataḥ kṣipramalabhamāno 'pi na parikhidyate |
body.translated_text: The abandonment of defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) is extremely subtle and hard to understand, like the gradual wearing away of an adze blade. My defilements too would be abandoned. Because of [its] subtlety, another does not perceive [the progress]. From this it is known that the supreme effort for cultivating the wholesome is necessary. Even a small amount of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) destroys the defilements, just as a small light dispels darkness. Thus, even obtaining a small amount of <s>prajñā</s>, one becomes one whose task is accomplished. Therefore one is not discouraged. Even over a long period, what is difficult to accomplish is the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). But if one does attain <s>samādhi</s>, then the other qualities arise quickly. Therefore, even when not attaining quickly, one is not discouraged.

body.text: yogī samanucintayet samādhisamāpattiratikṛcchrā yathā purā bodhisattvaḥ puṇyena prajñayā ca ghaniṣṭhaḥ ṣaṭvarṣāṇi vyavasyan ante 'nuprāptaḥ | anyeṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ samādhisamāpattirapi kṛcchrā, kiṃ punarmama pṛthagjanasya mandendriyasya vegenānuprāptiriti | evamanucintya na parikhidyeta | yogibhiravaśyaṃ kartavyaṃ yat samādhibhāvanā, nāsti punaḥ karmāntaram | ato 'nanuprāptasyānuprāptaye bhāvayitavyam | bhāvayitā samādhimasamāpanno 'pi kāyapravivekalābhī bhavati | praviviktakāyasya samādhiḥ sulabho bhavati | samādhibhāvanāmārabhamāṇo bhagavadanugrahasyānṛṇo bhavati | pravivekacāritvāt yogāvacara ityākhyāmapi vindate | dīrghakālaṃ kuśalaṃ bhāvayataḥ kuśalasvabhāvaḥ sidhyati | yāvatkāyapravṛtti kuśalameva sadānupatati | ataḥ sujanaiḥ saṅgaccheta | idaṃ mahate 'rthāya bhavati | sadā kuśalasya bhāvayitā dṛṣṭa eva kāyena āsravāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ spṛśet | yadi vā maraṇakāle spṛśet yadi vā āyuṣo 'nte susthāna upapadya tadantarā spṛśet | iti yathādharmaśravaṇānuśaṃsa uktam |
body.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> should reflect: 'The attainment of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is extremely difficult. Just as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of old, though rich in merit and wisdom, strove for six years and only at the end attained [it]. The attainment of <s>samādhi</s> was difficult even for other <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) — how much more so for me, an ordinary person of dull faculties, to attain it quickly!' Having reflected thus, one should not be discouraged. What must necessarily be done by <s>yogīs</s> is the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s>; there is no other task. Therefore, for the sake of attaining what has not been attained, one should cultivate. Even one who cultivates but has not attained <s>samādhi</s> gains bodily seclusion. For one whose body is secluded, <s>samādhi</s> becomes easy to obtain. By undertaking the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s>, one repays the kindness of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Because of practicing in seclusion, one also obtains the designation '<s>yogāvacara</s>' (practitioner of meditation). For one who cultivates the wholesome for a long time, the nature of wholesomeness is established. As long as bodily activity [continues], the wholesome constantly follows. Therefore one should associate with good people. This is of great benefit. One who constantly cultivates the wholesome should, in this very life, touch with the body the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravas</s>). Or one should touch it at the time of death, or at the end of life, having been reborn in a good destination, one should touch it in the interim. Thus the benefits of hearing the <s>Dharma</s> have been stated.

body.text: yogī adhyātmaṃ cittaṃ vīralakṣaṇaṃ puraskṛtyaivaṃ cintayati ahaṃ kleśāvaraṇamaparyādāya na kadācidvṛthā pratinivarta iti | kiñca yogī mānacittamāśrityaivaṃ cintayati- śraddhādīni kuśalendriyāṇi santīti anye samādhiṃ pratipadyante | mamāpīdānīṃ santi | kimarthaṃ na samāpadya iti | yathā purā bodhisattvaḥ arāḍādibhyo munibhyo dharmaṃ śrutvaivamacintayat ime śraddhādikuśalendriyatvāt dharmamanuprāpnuvan | samāpīdānīṃ santi kasmānnānuprāpsyāmīti | yogī prajānāti- kleśā durbalāḥ prajñā balavatī | tatprahāṇaṃ kimiti duṣkaramiti | yathoktaṃ- bhikṣuḥ ṣaḍbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato mukhamārutena himavantaṃ [parvatarājamapi] pradalayet | kaḥ punarvādo avidyāmiti |
body.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s>, bringing to the fore the hero-characteristic of the mind internally, reflects thus: 'Without having completely overcome the obstruction of defilements (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>), I shall never retreat in vain.' Furthermore, the <s>yogī</s>, relying on a mind of pride, reflects thus: 'Others, because they possess wholesome faculties (<s>kuśalendriya</s>) beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), have attained <s>samādhi</s>. I too now possess them. Why should I not attain it?' Just as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of old, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from sages such as <s>Ārāḍa</s> and others, reflected: 'These [sages], because they possess wholesome faculties beginning with faith, have attained the <s>dharma</s>. I too now possess them — why should I not attain?' The <s>yogī</s> understands: 'The defilements are weak; <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is powerful. Why then should their abandonment be difficult?' As stated: 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> endowed with six <s>dharmas</s> could split even <s>Himavat</s> (the Himālaya), king of mountains, with the wind of his breath. What need to speak of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)?'

body.text: kiñca yogī cintayati- ahaṃ pūrvādhvani na samādhiṃ bhāvitavān | ata idānīṃ nānuprāpnomi | idānīṃ na prayate paścātpunarnānuprāpsyāmīti | ato bhāvanāmārabhate | sadā samādhibhāvitvāt cittamekatra pratitiṣṭhati | yathā ghaṭasya pravartanamanuparatamavaśyamekatra pratitiṣṭhati | api ca yogī cintayati- yadyahaṃ sadā vīryamārabhe yadi cānanuprāptamanuprāpnomi | tadordhvaṃmavaśyaṃ na vipratisariṣyāmīti | ataścittaikāgryeṇa samādhīn bhāvayitumārabheta ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>yogī</s> reflects: 'In the past, I did not cultivate <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore I do not attain it now. If I do not strive now, I shall not attain it later either.' Therefore he undertakes cultivation. From constantly cultivating <s>samādhi</s>, the mind comes to rest in one place. Just as the turning of a potter's wheel, when it ceases, inevitably comes to rest in one place. Moreover, the <s>yogī</s> reflects: 'If I always arouse effort, and if I attain what has not been attained, then from that point onward I shall certainly have no regret.' Therefore, with one-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgrya</s>), one should undertake the cultivation of <s>samādhis</s>.

body.text: samādhibhāvanāvargo 'ṣṭhāśītyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The Chapter on the Cultivation of <s>Samādhi</s> (Concentration), the one hundred and eighty-eighth.

body.text: 189 mārgasatyaskandhe jñānādhikāre jñānalakṣaṇavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 189. In the section on the Truth of the Path (<s>mārgasatya</s>), in the division on knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>): the Chapter on the Characteristic of Knowledge.

body.text: tattvasya prajñā jñānamityākhyāyate | tattvaṃ yat śūnyānātmatā | tasya prajñā tattvajñānaṃ bhavati | prajñāptau prajñeti saṃjñā na tu jñānam | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre- yathāsiḥ parikṛntati | āryaśrāvakāḥ prajñāsinā saṃyojanānubaddhān anuśayaparyavanaddhān sarvān kleśān samucchedayati | nānyadharmeṇeti vadanti | nātattva[jñāne] na kleśān samucchedayati iti | ato jñāyate prajñaiva tattva[jñāna]miti |
body.translated_text: The <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) regarding reality (<s>tattva</s>) is called '<s>jñāna</s>' (knowledge). Reality is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and non-self (<s>anātmatā</s>). The <s>prajñā</s> of that is the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>). In conventional designation it is called '<s>prajñā</s>' (wisdom), not '<s>jñāna</s>' (knowledge). Why? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Just as a sword cuts. The noble disciples (<s>āryaśrāvakāḥ</s>), with the sword of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), completely eradicate all defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) that are bound by the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) and enveloped by the latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>).' They say: 'It is not by any other <s>dharma</s>. Without the knowledge of reality, one does not completely eradicate the defilements.' From this it is known that <s>prajñā</s> alone is the knowledge of reality.

body.text: (pṛ) yat bhavānāha- prajñaiva kleśān samucchedayatīti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | saṃjñayāpi hi kleśān samucchedayati | yathoktaṃ sūtra- anityasaṃjñā bhāvitā [bahulīkṛtā] sarvaṃ kāmarāgaṃ paryādāti | [sarvaṃ] rūparāgaṃ [sarva]bhavarāgaṃ [sarva]masmimānaṃ [sarvā]mavidyāñca paryādāti | iti | (u) maivam | prajñayā yaḥ kleśānāṃ samucchedaḥ [sa eva] saṃjñayetyucyate |
body.translated_text: (Question) What you have said — that '<s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) alone completely eradicates the defilements' — is not sound. Why? Because <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) too completely eradicates the defilements. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The perception of impermanence (<s>anityasaṃjñā</s>), when cultivated [and made abundant], completely overcomes all passion for desires (<s>kāmarāga</s>), [all] passion for form (<s>rūparāga</s>), [all] passion for existence (<s>bhavarāga</s>), [all] the conceit "I am" (<s>asmimāna</s>), and [all] ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>).' (Answer) It is not so. The complete eradication of defilements that is [accomplished] by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is [merely] called [eradication] 'by <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception).'

body.text: asti bhagavato dvividhaṃ vacanaṃ- paramārthavacanaṃ saṃjñāvacanamiti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- maitrī vyāpādaṃ samucchedayatīti | ayaṃ maitrīdharmaḥ paramārthato na saṃyojanaṃ samucchedayati | jñānamātraṃ samucchedayati | yathoktaṃ- jñānāsiḥ sarvān kleśān samucchedayati iti | ato jñāyate maitrī saṃyojanaṃ samucchedayatīti saṃjñāvacanam | kiñcoktaṃ prajñārthasūtre- vimuktiṃ prajānātīti prajñā | kiṃ vastu vimuktiriti prajānāti | yat anityaṃ rūpaṃ anityamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | anityā vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskārā, vijñānamanityamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | iyaṃ prajñaiveti | kiñcāha- āryaśrāvakāḥ samāhitā yathābhūtaṃ prajānantīti | ato jñāyate paramārtha eva prajñeti | prajñādṛṣṭānte coktam- jñānamasiḥ prajñā iṣurityādi | dṛṣṭānto 'yaṃ sarvakleśaprahāṇamupadarśayati | tattvajñānameva kleśān samucchedayatītyataḥ prajñaiva tattva[jñāna]miti jñāyate | uktañca gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: There are two kinds of statements of the Blessed One — the statement of ultimate truth (<s>paramārthavcana</s>) and the statement of conventional designation (<s>saṃjñāvacana</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) eradicates <s>vyāpāda</s> (ill-will).' This quality of <s>maitrī</s> does not ultimately eradicate the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>). Only knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) alone eradicates [them]. As stated: 'The sword of knowledge cuts off all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).' Therefore it is known that 'loving-kindness eradicates the fetters' is a conventional designation. Moreover, it is stated in the Sūtra on the Meaning of <s>Prajñā</s>: '<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) is that which understands liberation.' What reality is it that understands liberation? That which truly understands impermanent form as 'impermanent'; which truly understands impermanent feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as 'impermanent' — this is <s>prajñā</s>. And further he says: 'The noble disciples, being concentrated, understand things as they truly are.' Therefore it is known that <s>prajñā</s> is ultimately [true knowledge]. And in the simile of <s>prajñā</s> it is said: 'Knowledge is a sword, <s>prajñā</s> is an arrow' — and so forth. This simile demonstrates the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>. Since it is knowledge of reality alone that eradicates the <s>kleśas</s>, it is known that <s>prajñā</s> is itself knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>). And it is stated in a verse —

body.text:
yogī paśyati vai loke sarve devāśca mānuṣāḥ |
tattvajñānaparibhraṣṭā nāmarūpe 'bhiniviṣṭāḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> sees in the world — all the gods and human beings, fallen from knowledge of reality, are absorbed in name-and-form.

body.text: laukikā bhūyasā tucchakaṃ nityaṃ sukhaṃ subhamityādi dṛṣṭvā tattvajñānādbhaṣṭā bhavanti | yaḥ paramārthataḥ śūnyamanātma ityādi paśyati, sa tattvajñānī bhavati | ato jñāyate prajñaiva tattva[jñāna]m iti |
body.translated_text: Worldly beings, for the most part, seeing what is empty as permanent, pleasant, auspicious, and so forth, become fallen from knowledge of reality. He who sees [things] as they ultimately are — empty, without self, and so forth — he becomes a knower of reality. Therefore it is known that <s>prajñā</s> is itself knowledge of reality.

body.text: āha ca bhagavān sūtre- yasya dhanaṃ vinaṣṭhaṃ, tasyālpīyān lābho vinaṣṭaḥ | yasya prajñā vinaṣṭā, tasya mahīyān lābho vinaṣṭa iti | kiñcāha- lābheṣu dhanamalpīyān lābhaḥ | prajñā tūttamo lābha iti | āhaca- pradyotānāṃ candrasūryapradyota alpīyān prajñāpradyoto 'gra iti | yadi prajñā na tattva[jñānaṃ], kasmādevaṃ vadet | uktañca sūtre- prajñendriyamāryasatyasaṅgṛhītamiti | āha ca- duḥkhasamudayajñānādiḥ tattva[jñāna]miti prajānīyāt | paramārthasatyālambaneyaṃ prajñā iti | āha ca- [bodhipakṣika]dharmeṣu prajñā agrā iti |
body.translated_text: And the Blessed One said in a <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one whose wealth is lost, the lesser gain is lost. For one whose <s>prajñā</s> is lost, the greater gain is lost.' And further he said: 'Among gains, wealth is the lesser gain. But <s>prajñā</s> is the supreme gain.' And he said: 'Among lights, the light of the moon and sun is the lesser; the light of <s>prajñā</s> is the foremost.' If <s>prajñā</s> were not knowledge of reality, why would he speak thus? And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The faculty of <s>prajñā</s> (<s>prajñendriya</s>) is included among the Noble Truths.' And he said: 'One should understand that knowledge of suffering, its origination, and so forth is knowledge of reality. This <s>prajñā</s> has ultimate truth as its object.' And he said: 'Among the [<s>bodhipakṣika</s>] qualities, <s>prajñā</s> is the foremost.'

body.text: kiñcāha- anuttarā samyaksambodhiḥ prajñendriyamityabhidhīyate iti | ataḥ sā tattvamiti | bhagavato daśa balāni jñānamayāni | ato jñāyate prajñā vastutaḥ paramārthālambanā bhavatīti | (pṛ) tathā sati prajñā alaukikī bhavet | (u) vastuto 'laukikī prajñā | kenedaṃ jñāyate | laukikaṃ cittaṃ prajñaptimavalambate | lokottaraṃ cittaṃ nairātmyaśūnyatāmavalambate | kasmāt | prajñaptirhi loka eva | prajñapteratikrāntaṃ lokottaram |
body.translated_text: Moreover he said: 'The unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) is called the faculty of <s>prajñā</s> (<s>prajñendriya</s>).' Therefore it [<s>prajñā</s>] is reality. The ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>) of the Blessed One consist of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). Therefore it is known that <s>prajñā</s> in reality has ultimate truth as its object. [Objection:] If so,

body.text: (pṛ) bhavaduktaṃ na yujyate | kasmāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre- kiṃ vijānāti vijñānam | yaduta rūpaśabdagandharasasparśān vijānāti | yathā skandhadhātvāyatanādīni vijñānena vijānāti | idaṃ vijñānaṃ lokottaraṃ bhavet | iti | ato laukikaṃ cittaṃ prajñaptimātramālambate na tattvamiti bhavadvacanamayuktam | manovijñānamapi tattvālambanam | vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārādyālambitvāt | kiñcāha bhagavān- dve samyak dṛṣṭī laukikī lokottareti | puṇyapāpādyastitva [samyak dṛṣṭi]laukikī yadāryaśrāvakāṇāṃ duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgānālambya anāsravasmṛtyā samprayuktā prajñā lokottarā | uktañca gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] What you have said is not tenable. Why? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'What does consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) cognize? Namely, it cognizes forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles. Just as consciousness cognizes the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), and so forth.' If this consciousness is supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>),

body.text:
laukikottamadṛṣṭīko yātāyāto 'pi saṃsṛtau |
adhvanāṃ śatasāhasraṃ na yāvaddurgatau gataḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: One who has the highest worldly view, even though he comes and goes in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), does not go to a lower realm, even for a hundred thousand lifetimes.

body.text: uktañca sūtre- mithyācāriṇaḥ susthāne janma bhavati | astya pāpakarmaṇo 'nabhinirvṛttau kuśalapratyayaḥ pūrvaṃ vipacyate | kadācinmaraṇakāle samupasthite samyak dṛṣṭisamprayuktaṃ kuśalacittamabhimukhībhavati | ataḥ susthāne jāyate | iti | daśasu kuśala[karma]patheṣvapi samyagdṛṣṭiruktā | kathaṃ bhavānāha lokottaraṃ jñānamiti | āha ca bhagavān- trividhā prajñā śrutamayī prajñā, cintāmayī prajñā, bhāvanāmayī prajñā | śrutamayī prajñā cintāmayī prajñā laukikī | bhāvanāmayī ubhayavidhā iti | kiñca bhagavān [ānāpāna]smṛtiṃ janayāmāsa | rāhulo bhikṣurapariniṣpannāṃ vimuktiprajñāmanuprāpa | āha ca pañcadharmā aparipavkaṃ vimukticittaṃ vipācayanti iti | eṣā sarvā laukikī prajñaiva | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- kecidabhiniṣkramaṇakuśalāḥ, na vipaśyanākuśalāḥ | kecidvipaśyanākuśalāḥ na santaraṇakuśalā iti | laukika jñānalābhitayā abhiniṣkramaṇakuśala ityucyate | catussatyādarśitayā na vipaśyanākuśalaḥ |
body.translated_text: And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One of wrong conduct may obtain birth in a good place. When there is non-ripening of evil <s>karma</s>, the wholesome condition ripens first. Sometimes, when the moment of death is approaching, a wholesome mind associated with right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) arises [and leads to a favorable rebirth].'

body.text: catussatyāni paśyannapi āsravakṣayālābhitayā na santaraṇakuśalaḥ | bhagavān svayamāha- dharmajñānamanvayajñāna paracittajñānañca laukikaṃ jñānamiti | kiñcāha- pūrvanivāsajñānaṃ cyutyupapattijñānaṃ sāsravamiti | api cāha- dharmāṇāṃ sthitijñānaṃ nirvāṇajñānaṃ bhavati | ityādisūtreṣūktatvāt jñātavyaṃ asti sāsravaṃ jñānamiti |
body.translated_text: Even one who sees the Four Truths, if he has not attained the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>), is not skilled in crossing over. The Blessed One himself said: 'Knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmajñāna</s>), subsequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>), and knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>) are worldly knowledge.' And further he said: 'Knowledge of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsajñāna</s>), knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapattijñāna</s>),

body.text: atra pratibrūmaḥ | yadyasti sāsravā prajñā | idānīṃ vaktavyaṃ sāsravānāsravayoḥ pravibhaktaṃ lakṣaṇam | (pṛ) yo dharmo bhave pātakaḥ sa sāsravaḥ | tadanyo 'nāsravaḥ | (u) ko dharmo bhave pātakaḥ | ko vā na bhave pātakaḥ | idaṃ prativaktavyam | apratibrūvāṇasya nāsti sāsravānāsravayorlakṣaṇam | yadbhavatoktam- asti laukikaṃ cittamaprajñaptyavalambanaṃ yadviṣayādīnāṃ vijñānamiti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | āha khalu bhagavān- pṛthagjanāḥ satataṃ prajñaptimanudhāvantīti | asyārthaḥ | sarvapṛthagjanacittaṃ prajñaptiṃ na paryādātītyataḥ sadā asmitālakṣaṇamanudhāvati | naiva tato visaṃyujyate | rūpaṃ paśyato 'pi na ghaṭādilakṣaṇādvisaṃyujyate iti | ataḥ pṛthagjana cittaṃ na tattvārthamavalambate | vedanāsaṃjñādīn dharmānavalambamāno 'pi ahaṃ mameti paśyati | ato jñāyate sarvaṃ laukikaṃ cittaṃ prajñaptimavalambata iti |
body.translated_text: To this we reply: If there is <s>prajñā</s> with outflows (<s>sāsravā prajñā</s>), then the distinguishing characteristic between [<s>prajñā</s>] with outflows and without outflows must be stated. [Objection:] That <s>dharma</s> which causes falling into [continued] existence is with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). What is other than that is without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>). [Response:] What <s>dharma</s> causes falling into existence? What is it

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhavatā- laukikī prajñā yaduta dvidhā samyagdṛṣṭirityādi iti | tatredaṃ prativaktavyam- asti cittadvaividhyaṃ mohacittaṃ jñānacittamiti | prajñaptidharmāvalambanaṃ cittaṃ mohacittam | yat śūnyā nātmarūpadharmamātrāvalambanaṃ cittaṃ jñānacittam | yathoktamavidyāvibhaṅgasūtre- avidyā katamā | yat pūrvānte 'jñānamaparānte 'jñānaṃ pūrvāntāparāntājñānaṃ karmaṇyajñānaṃ karmavipāke 'jñānaṃ pūrvāparakarmavipākājñānaṃ ityādi tatra tatra yathābhūtasyājñānamadarśanamanabhisamayaḥ tamaḥ saṃmohaḥ [avidyā]ndhakāraḥ iyamucyate 'vidyā iti | yathābhūtasyā jñānamiti yat śūnyānātmā jñānam | idaṃ pṛthagjanacittaṃ sadā prajñaptigataṃ sat prajñaptimavalambate | ato 'vidyetyākhyāyate | śūnyālambanaṃ jñānam | idānīṃ yadi sarvaṃ laukikaṃ jñānaṃ prajñaptimavalambate | prajñaptyālambanaṃ cittamavidyā bhavati | kathamucyate asti laukikī prajñā iti |
body.translated_text: As for what you have said — 'worldly <s>prajñā</s>, namely the twofold right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>)' and so forth — to this the following reply should be given: There are two kinds of mind — the mind of delusion (<s>mohacittam</s>) and the mind of knowledge (<s>jñānacittam</s>). The mind that takes conventionally designated <s>dharmas</s> (<s>prajñaptidharmāvalambana</s>) as its object is the mind of delusion. That which [takes] emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>) [as object]

body.text: (pṛ) bhavatoktavat prajñaptyālambanaṃ prajñālakṣaṇamavidyā | idānīmarhato 'vidyā bhavet | ghaṭādyālambanacittasya sattvāt | (u) arhato nāsti ghaṭādyālambanaṃ cittam | kasmāt |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] According to what you have said, <s>prajñā</s> whose characteristic is to take conventional designations as its object is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). In that case, the <s>arhat</s> would have ignorance, since a mind taking pots and so forth as its object exists [in an <s>arhat</s>]. [Response:] The <s>arhat</s> does not have a mind that takes pots and so forth as its object. Why?

body.text: prathamābhi sambodhikāla eva sarvaprajñaptilakṣaṇānāṃ vidhvastatvāt | kriyārthārya kevalamabhidadhāti | na tatra mānadṛṣṭāvabhiniviśate | santi trayo vādāḥ- (1) dṛṣṭijaḥ, (2) mānajaḥ, (3) kriyārthaja iti | tribhyaḥ kriyārtho bhavati | pṛthagjanā yadvadanti ghaṭa iti pudgala iti | ayaṃ vādo dṛṣṭijaḥ | śaikṣā ātmadṛṣṭivihīnā api samyaksmṛtipramoṣat pañcasu skandheṣu asmimānalakṣaṇena vadanti- ayaṃ pudgalaḥ ayaṃ ghaṭa iti | yathā kṣemakasūtra uktam | kriyārthaja iti yadarhataḥ | yathā mahākāśyapaḥ saṅghāṭiṃ dṛṣṭvā āha- iyaṃ mameti [yat] divyarddhau vicikitsāṃ janayati | bhagavān tadvivṛṇvannāha- ayamatyantasamuddhatamānendriyaḥ pradagdhahetupratyayaḥ kathaṃ sābhimānaḥ syāt | prajñaptyā paraṃ [tathā] vadatīti | ato jñāyate astyarhato ghaṭādicittamiti |
body.translated_text: Because at the very time of first awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodhi</s>), all characteristics of conventional designation have been destroyed. The <s>ārya</s> (noble one) speaks merely for the purpose of action (<s>kriyārtha</s>). He does not cling to [things] with the view of self-conceit (<s>mānadṛṣṭi</s>). There are three kinds of discourse: (1) that born of [wrong] view (<s>dṛṣṭija</s>), (2) that born of conceit (<s>mānaja</s>), (3) that made for the purpose of action (<s>kriyārthaja</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadyalaukikī prajñā | dve samyagdṛṣṭī ityādī sūtraṃ kathaṃ neyam | (u) idaṃ sarvaṃ saṃjñājñānamiti nāmnocyate | bhagavān dharmāṇāṃ tattvalakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī vineyasattvānanusṛtya vividhaṃ nāma sthāpayati | yathā prajñāmeva vedanādināmnopadiśati | yaduta vedakaḥ sarvadharmebhyo vimucyata iti | api cāha anityādisaṃjñā bhāvitā sarvān kleśān paribhedayatīti | āha ca- caturthamakṛṣṇamaśuklaṃ karma sarvakarmāṇi śaikṣacetanākhyāni kṣapayatīti | kiñcāha- manasā sarvānabhiviveśān prajahātīti | āha ca-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If <s>prajñā</s> is supramundane (<s>alaukikī</s>), how should the <s>sūtra</s> [passage] 'There are two kinds of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>)' and so forth be interpreted? [Response:] All this is called 'conventional knowledge' (<s>saṃjñājñāna</s>) — it is a name. The Blessed One, who perceives the reality-characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s>, following the dispositions of the beings to be guided, establishes various names.

body.text:
śraddhayā tarati ogham apramādena cārṇavam |
vīryeṇa duḥkhamatyeti prajñayā pariśudhyati || iti |
body.translated_text: By faith one crosses the flood; by diligence, the ocean. By vigor one overcomes suffering; by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) one is purified.

body.text: api cāha- cakṣū rūpadarśanāyecchati iti | cakṣuṣi vastuto 'satyāmapīcchāyāṃ cittameva darśanāyecchat cakṣurnāmnocyate |
body.translated_text: And moreover he said: 'The eye wishes to see form.' When the eye does not actually exist [as an independent reality], even in [the expression of] desire, it is the mind alone that wishes to see — [yet] it is called 'the eye.'

body.text: (pṛ) yadi laukikaṃ jñānaṃ saṃjñā | kasmāt jñānaṃ bhavati | yadi hetupratyayān vinopadiṣṭaṃ jñānam | tadā sarvāḥ saṃjñā jñānaṃ bhavetyuḥ | vaktavyā ca dvividhā saṃjñā lokaṃ pratītya satyaṃ, paramārthaṃ pratītya satyamiti | (u) maivam | saṃjñāyāḥ santi nānāvibhāgāḥ | kācit mohakāṣṭhātmikā saṃjñā yāvat laukikakuśalākuśalāni na vijānāti | kācidavaramohātmikā saṃjñā kuśalākuśalāni vivecayati | kācidalpamohātmikā saṃjñā asthisaṃjñādyālambate | prajñapti mavihāya na skandhalakṣaṇāni vidhamati | itīyaṃ saṃjñā skandhalakṣaṇaparibhedakaṃ jñānamanukūlayatītyato bhagavānupadiśati jñānamiti | iyañca saṃjñā tattvajñānasya hetuṃ karotītyato jñānami tyucyate | asti ca loke kāraṇe kāryopacāraḥ | yathā suvarṇaṃ bhuṅkte | puruṣasya pañcavṛttīrdadāti | strī śīlaṃ malinaṃ karoti | supārā jaladhārā sukhā | dharmavasanaḥ puruṣaḥ sukha iti | saptāsravasūtre ca vacanaprahāṇavṛttiprahāṇādaya āsravahetava āsravā ityucyante | āhuśca āhāro jīvitaṃ paśavastṛṇānīti | api cāhuḥ- annavasrādīni bāhyajīvitam, yat parasvāpaharaṇaṃ tadeva parajīvitāpaharaṇam iti | idaṃ sarvaṃ hetumeva phalatayā vadanti | evaṃ jñānahetureva jñānamityucyate | ato 'navadyam |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If worldly knowledge is [merely] conventional designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>), how is it [called] knowledge? If knowledge is taught without causes and conditions, then all designations would be knowledge. And [you must] state that there are two kinds of designation — truth dependent on the world (<s>lokaṃ pratītya satya</s>) and truth dependent on ultimate reality (<s>paramārthaṃ pratītya satya</s>). [Response:] It is not so. There are various divisions of designation. Some designation is of the nature of the utmost delusion, [in which one] does not discern worldly wholesome and unwholesome [states]. Some designation is of lesser delusion and discriminates wholesome from unwholesome. Some designation is of slight delusion and takes as its object the perception of bones (<s>asthisaṃjñā</s>) and the like. Without abandoning conventional designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), it does not destroy the characteristics of the aggregates (<s>skandhalakṣaṇa</s>). Since this designation is favorable to the knowledge that penetrates the characteristics of the aggregates, the Blessed One teaches it as 'knowledge.' And since this designation creates the cause of knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), it is called 'knowledge.' And in the world, there is the figurative usage of applying the [name of the] effect to the cause. Just as [one says] 'he enjoys gold' [meaning the things gold buys], or 'it gives a man five livelihoods,' or 'a woman defiles virtue,' or 'a good crossing — the stream of water is pleasant,' or 'a man clothed in <s>dharma</s> is happy.' And in the Sūtra on the Seven Outflows, the causes of outflows — abandonment of [wrong] speech, abandonment of [wrong] conduct, etc. — are called '<s>āsravas</s>' (outflows). And they say: 'Food is life, cattle are grass.' And they also say: 'Food, clothing, and the like are external life; taking another's property is itself taking another's life.' All this speaks of the cause as if it were the effect. Similarly, what is the cause of knowledge is called 'knowledge.' Therefore [our position] is blameless.

body.text: (pṛ) smṛtyupasthāneṣu uṣmādiṣu ca gataṃ cittaṃ tattvadharmamālambate | kimidamanāsravam | (u) yadanāsravaṃ cittaṃ tat prajñaptiṃ vidhamati | ato yatra prajñaptividhamanaṃ cittaṃ tadanu samāgataṃ cittamanāsravaṃ bhavati | (pṛ) kutra cittaṃ prajñaptiṃ yugapat vidhamati | (u) yatra pañcānāṃ skandhānāmudayavyayānudarśanasampanno bhavati | tadā [teṣā]manityasaṃjñāmanuprāpnoti | anityasaṃjñā ca yogino 'nātmasaṃjñāṃ sampādayati | yathoktam- āryaśrāvakāṇāmanityasaṃjñayā cittaṃ bhāvayatāmanātmasaṃjñā pratitiṣṭhati | anātmasaṃjñayā cittaṃ bhāvayatāṃ kṣipraṃ rāgadveṣamohebhyo vimucyate ityādi | kasmāt | anātmasaṃjñayā hi cittaṃ bhāvayatāṃ duḥkhasaṃjñā pratitiṣṭhati | ātmasaṃjñitvāt duḥkhamapi pratibudhyate | ato yo dharmo 'nityo 'nātmā, sa duḥkho 'pi iti prajānan akuśalānnirvidyate | ato 'nātmasaṃjñā duḥkhasaṃjñāṃ sampādayati |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] In the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the <s>ūṣmagatas</s> (warmth stage), and so forth, the mind takes the <s>dharma</s> of reality as its object. Is this [mind] without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>)? [Response:] The mind that is without outflows destroys conventional designation. Therefore, wherever there is a mind that destroys conventional designation, the mind that subsequently follows it becomes without outflows. [Objection:] Where does the mind destroy conventional designation all at once? [Response:] Where one becomes accomplished in contemplating the arising and perishing of the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). Then one attains the perception of impermanence (<s>anityasaṃjñā</s>). And the perception of impermanence, for the <s>yogin</s>, brings about the perception of non-self (<s>anātmasaṃjñā</s>). As stated: 'For noble disciples cultivating the mind with the perception of impermanence, the perception of non-self becomes established. For those cultivating the mind with the perception of non-self, the mind is quickly liberated from passion, hatred, and delusion' — and so forth. Why? For those cultivating the mind with the perception of non-self, the perception of suffering becomes established. Because of perceiving a self, suffering too is realized. Therefore, one who understands that whatever is impermanent and non-self is also suffering becomes disenchanted with the unwholesome. Thus the perception of non-self brings about the perception of suffering.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmādbhavānāha [anyathā] vidhanakramam | sūtre tūktam- yadanityaṃ tadduḥkham | yadduḥkhaṃ tadānātma iti | ato 'nityasaṃjñā duḥkhasaṃjñā sampādayati | duḥkhasaṃjñānātmasaṃjñāṃ sampādayati |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Why do you state the order of destruction differently? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is non-self.' Therefore the perception of impermanence brings about the perception of suffering, and the perception of suffering brings about the perception of non-self.

body.text: (u) sūtra uktam- anityasaṃjñābhāvitaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ cittamanātmasaṃjñāyāṃ pratitiṣṭhati iti | ato 'nityasaṃjñā anātmasaṃjñāṃ sampādayati | evaṃ vadato 'pi asti mārganayaḥ | kasmāt | ātmavādī hi paralokasādhanāyāha- ātmā nitya iti | ataḥ pañcaskandhā anityā iti paśyan anātmāna iti prajānāti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- cakṣurātmeti yo vadet | tat nopapadyate | cakṣuṣa utpādopi vyayo 'pi prajñāyate | yasya khalu punarutpādo 'pi vyayo 'pi prajñāyate | ātmā ma utpadyate vyeti cetyasyāgataṃ bhavati | iti |
body.translated_text: [Response:] It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The mind of the disciples, cultivated with the perception of impermanence, becomes established in the perception of non-self.' Therefore the perception of impermanence brings about the perception of non-self. Even though one speaks thus, there is [also] the method of the path. Why? For the proponent of a self (<s>ātmavādin</s>) says, in order to establish the other world: 'The self is permanent.' Therefore, one who sees that the five aggregates are impermanent understands 'they are non-self.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'He who says the eye is the self — that is not tenable. For the arising and perishing of the eye is perceived. And for one whose arising and perishing is perceived, it would follow that 'my self arises and perishes.''

body.text: (pṛ) sūtradvayamidaṃ kathaṃ pratisaṃvedanīyam | (u) duḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ dvividham- anityasaṃjñotthitaṃ vipariṇāmaduḥkhalakṣaṇam | anātmasaṃjñotthitaṃ saṃskāraduḥkhalakṣaṇama | ataḥ sūtradvayamapyaviruddham | (pṛ) tathā cet smṛtyupasthānoṣmādāvastyanityasaṃjñā | ayaṃ dharmo 'nāsravaḥ syāt | (u)smṛtyupasthānādau yadīyamanāsravā, ko doṣo 'sti | (pṛ) pṛthagjanānāṃ citte na syādiyamanāsravā | pṛthagjanānāṃ citte 'pyasti abhūtasmṛtyupasthānam | kathamidanāsravaṃ bhavet | (u) pudgalo 'yaṃ na vastutaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ | ayaṃ srotaāpattiphalapratipannaka ityucyate | (pṛ) ayaṃ srotaāpattiphalapratipannakaḥ satyadarśanamārge vartate | smṛtyupasthānādidharmāśca na satyadarśanā bhavanti | (u) srotaāpattiphalapratipannakaḥ sannikṛṣṭo viprakṛṣṭaśca bhavati | smṛtyupasthānādigato viprakṛṣṭaḥ pratipannakaḥ satyadarśanagatastu sannikṛṣṭaḥ | kenedaṃ jñāyate | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā vāśījaṭopamasūtre- jānataḥ paśyata āsravāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ vadāmi | kiṃ jānataḥ kiṃ paśyata āsravāṇāṃ kṣayo bhavati | iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpasya samudayaḥ | iti rūpasyāstaṅgamaḥ | iti vedanā saṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni yāvadastaṅgamaḥ | mārgamabhāvayato nāsravāṇāṃ kṣayo bhavati | bhāvayatastu bhavati | tadyathā [kukkuṭyā] aṇḍāni samyagadhiśayitāni | evameva bhāvanānuyogamanuyuktasya bhikṣornaivaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati etāvatko bata me 'dyāsravāṇāṃ kṣīṇam | etāvatko hayaḥ etāvatkaḥ paramiti | atha khalvasya kṣīṇe kṣīṇānta eva jñānaṃ bhavati | tadyathā vāśījaṭāyāṃ [dṛśyante 'ṅgulipadāni]
body.translated_text: [Objection:] How are these two <s>sūtra</s> [passages] to be reconciled? [Response:] The characteristic of suffering is twofold: the characteristic of suffering from change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkha</s>), which arises from the perception of impermanence, and the characteristic of suffering inherent in conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāraduḥkha</s>), which arises from the perception of non-self. Therefore both <s>sūtra</s> [passages] are not in conflict. [Objection:] If so, in the foundations of mindfulness, the warmth stages, and so forth, there is the perception of impermanence. This <s>dharma</s> would be without outflows. [Response:] If in the foundations of mindfulness and so forth this [perception] is without outflows, what fault is there? [Objection:] It would not exist in the mind of ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjanas</s>). [Yet] in the mind of ordinary persons too there exist inauthentic foundations of mindfulness. How could this be without outflows? [Response:] This individual is not in reality an ordinary person. He is called 'one attained to the fruit of stream-entry' (<s>srotaāpattiphalapratipannaka</s>). [Objection:] This one attained to stream-entry abides on the path of truth-seeing (<s>satyadarśanamārga</s>). But the <s>dharmas</s> of the foundations of mindfulness and so forth are not [part of] truth-seeing. [Response:] One attained to the fruit of stream-entry can be near (<s>sannikṛṣṭa</s>) or far (<s>viprakṛṣṭa</s>). One who has gone through the foundations of mindfulness and so forth is a distant attainer; one who has entered truth-seeing is a near attainer. How is this known? For the Blessed One said in the Sūtra of the Simile of the Adze-Handle: 'I declare that for one who knows and sees, there is destruction of the outflows. What does he know? What does he see? [He sees:] This is form; this is the arising of form; this is the cessation of form; this is feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — up to their cessation. Without cultivating the path, the destruction of the outflows does not occur. But for one who cultivates [it], it does occur. Just as [a hen's] eggs that are properly incubated [hatch] — so too, for a monk devoted to the practice of cultivation, the knowledge does not arise [prematurely]: "How much of my outflows has been destroyed today? How much yesterday? How much before?" Rather, when [the outflows] are destroyed, the knowledge arises precisely at the moment of their complete destruction. Just as on an adze-handle [the finger-marks are seen —'

body.text: | saptatriṃśa[vdodhya]ṅga bhāvanānuyogamanuyuktasya bhikṣoralpakṛcchreṇaiva saṃyojanāni pratipraśrabhyante | pūtikāni bhavanti | tadyathā sāmudrikayānāno[rbandhanāni] | ato jñāyate smṛtyupasthānādigato mārgāṅgabhāvanānuyogamanuktaḥ srotaāpattiphalapratipannaka iti | yadyekasmin kṣaṇe yadi vā pañcadaśasu kṣaṇeṣu na bhāvanānuyogaṃ vindate | [tadā] jñātavyamayaṃ viprakṛṣṭaḥ srotaāpattipratipannaka iti |
body.translated_text: — for a monk devoted to the practice of cultivating the thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the fetters (<s>saṃyojanas</s>) are pacified with little difficulty. They become rotten. Just as the ropes of an ocean-going vessel [rot away]. Therefore it is known that one who has gone through the foundations of mindfulness and so forth, devoted to the practice of cultivating the path-factors, is [called] 'one attained to the fruit of stream-entry.' If in a single moment, or in fifteen moments, one does not attain the practice of cultivation, then it should be known that this is a distant attainer of stream-entry.

body.text: (pṛ) iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpasya samudayaḥ iti rūpasyāstaṅgamaḥ, iti vedanā iti jñānamiti prathamamuktamādyaphalasya mārgaḥ | anantarāsrayo dṛṣṭāntāsrayāṇāṃ phalānāṃ mārgāḥ | ato nādyaphalapratipannaka ityucyate | (u) yadyaṇḍāni na samyagadhiśayitāni | tadā vinaśyanti | samyagadhiśayatāni saṃsidhyanti | evaṃ smṛtyupasthānādārabhya prathamaṃ bhāvanāmārabhate | sa yadi na sādhayati | na sa pratipannako bhavati | sādhayanstu śaikṣajano 'timātrapūtivedaka ityucyate | ataḥ smṛtyupasthānādau pūtibhūtaḥ san pṛthagjano bhavati | yaḥ saṃsiddhabhāvanaḥ sa ādyaphalapratipannako bhavati | tadyathā aṇḍāntargata | aṇḍābdahirgataḥ srotaāpanno bhavati | ato jñāyate smṛtyupasthānādigataḥ viprakṛṣṭaḥ pratipannaka ityucyate | kiñcogreṇa saṅghe nimantrite devatā upasaṅkramya ārocayanti- amuko gṛhapate arhan yāvadamuka ādyaphalapratipannaka iti | yadi sa satyadarśanamārgagataḥ | kathamārocayeyuḥ | jñātavyaṃ sa viprakṛṣṭaḥ pratipannaka iti |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'This is form, this is the arising of form, this is the cessation of form, this is feeling' — this knowledge, as first stated, is the path to the first fruit. The paths to the subsequent fruits are based on the examples [given in the simile]. Therefore he is not called 'one attained to the first fruit.' [Response:] If the eggs are not properly incubated, they are destroyed. If properly incubated, they succeed. Similarly, beginning from the foundations of mindfulness, one first commences cultivation. If one does not succeed, one does not become an attainer. But if one succeeds, one is called a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) who has fully experienced the rotting [of fetters]. Therefore, one who is in the rotting stage at the foundations of mindfulness and so forth is an ordinary person. One whose cultivation is accomplished is an attainer of the first fruit. Just as [the chick] inside the egg [is still forming] — [when it emerges] outside the egg, one becomes a stream-enterer. Therefore it is known that one who has gone through the foundations of mindfulness and so forth is called a 'distant attainer.' Moreover, when one who is stringent is invited to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, deities approach and announce: 'Such-and-such a householder is an <s>Arhat</s>, such-and-such is an attainer of the first fruit.' If he were on the path of truth-seeing, how could they announce [this]? It should be known that he is a distant attainer.

body.text: kiñcoktaṃ bhagavatā sūtre- yasya [khalu bhikṣava imāni] pañcendriyāṇi (śraddhādīni) na santi | tamahaṃ bāhyaḥ pṛthagjanapakṣe sthita iti vadāmīti | asyārthaḥ- asti bāhya ābhyantaraśca pṛthagjanaḥ | yasya nirvedhabhāgīyāni kuśalendriyāṇi na santi | sa bāhyaḥ pṛthagjana iti | yasya santi sa ābhyantara iti | ayamābhyantaraḥ pṛthagjana ārya ityupyucyate pṛthagjana ityapyucyate | bāhyaṃ pṛthagjanamupādāya āryaḥ | satyadarśanamārgamupādāya pṛthagjanaḥ | yathānandaśchannamāmantryāha- pṛthagjano nānusmarati rūpaṃ śūnyamanātmā, vedanā, saṃjñā
body.translated_text: Moreover, the Blessed One said in a <s>sūtra</s>: 'Monks, he who does not possess these five faculties (beginning with faith) — him I declare to be an outsider, standing in the class of ordinary persons.' The meaning of this is: there is an outer and an inner ordinary person. One who does not possess the wholesome faculties that belong to the penetrative stages (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) is an outer ordinary person. One who possesses them is an inner [ordinary person]. This inner ordinary person is also called a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) and also called an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). In relation to the outer ordinary person, he is noble. In relation to the path of truth-seeing, he is an ordinary person. Just as <s>Ānanda</s> addressed <s>Channa</s>: 'An ordinary person does not recollect: form is empty and non-self; feeling, perception —'

body.text: saṃskārā vijñānaṃ śūnyamanātmā | sarve saṃskārā anityāḥ | sarve dharmā anātmānaḥ | teṣāṃ nirodho nirvāṇamiti | atha ca [tatra] channasya [cittaṃ] na dharmaniyāme praskandati | nāpi pṛthagjanasyaivaṃ bhavati ityāha |
body.translated_text: '— formations, consciousness are empty and non-self. All formations are impermanent. All <s>dharmas</s> are non-self. Their cessation is <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' And yet <s>Channa's</s> mind does not leap forward into the certainty of the <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmaniyāma</s>). Nor does an ordinary person have [this experience]' — thus he says.

body.text: (pṛ) sannikṛṣṭo viprakṛṣṭo vā, ubhāvapi pratipannakau | kaḥ pravibhāgastayoḥ | (u) yo nirodhaṃ paśyati sa tattvataḥ pratipannakaḥ | yo dūrabhāgīyakuśalendriyagataḥ paśyati pañcaskandhā anityāḥ duḥkhā śūnyā anātmāna iti | na tu nirodhaṃ paśyati | sa saṃjñāpratipannakaḥ | kasmāt | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti- kathaṃ dharmaṃ paśyema iti | bhagavānāha- cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpañca cakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | tatsahabhuvo vedanāsaṃjñā cetanādayaḥ sarve [dharmā] anityā vipariṇāmadharmāṇaḥ aśraddheyāḥ | yo dharmo 'nityaḥ, tad duḥkham | duḥkhasyāsya samudayo 'pi duḥkham | sthitirapi duḥkham | punaḥ punarbhavalakṣaṇamapi duḥkham | evaṃ yāvanmano dharmā api | yadīdaṃ duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate | anyāni duḥkhāni na sambhavanti | na punaḥ santāno bhavati | yoginaścitta evaṃ bhavati- idaṃ praṇītamupaśamapadaṃ yat sarveṣāṃ mṛṣābhūtānāṃ kāmatṛṣṇānāmapagamaḥ kṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇam | yadasmin dharme cittaṃ praskandati adhimucyate neñjate na parāvartate na śocate na paritrāsate | tato nidānaṃ dharmaṃ paśyeyam iti | ato jñāyate yogī anityādyākāraiḥ pañcaskandhānavalokayan viprakṛṣṭaḥ pratipannaka ityucyate | teṣāṃ nirodhaṃ paśyan sannikṛṣṭaḥ pratipannaka iti | yathā channaḥ sthavirān prativadati- mamāpyevaṃ bhavati- rūpamanityaṃ [vijñānamanityaṃ rūpamanātmā, vijñānamanātmā, sarve saṃskārā anityāḥ, sarve dharmā anātmāna iti | atha ca punarme] sarvasaṃskārasamarthe tṛṣṇākṣaye nirodhe nirvāṇe cittaṃ na praskandati, na prasīdati, na vimucyate [paritarṣaṇā | upādānamutpadyate | pratyudāvartate mānasam | atha kastarhi ma ātmeti |] na khalvimaṃ dharmaṃ paśyato bhavati | iti |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Whether near or distant, both are attainers. What is the distinction between them? [Response:] He who sees cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is an attainer in the true sense. He who has gone through the wholesome faculties of the distant stages and sees that the five aggregates are impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self — but does not see cessation — he is an attainer by conventional designation (<s>saṃjñāpratipannaka</s>). Why? As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: The monks asked the Blessed One: 'How should we see the <s>dharma</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Dependent on the eye and form, eye-consciousness arises. Its co-arising [factors] — feeling, perception, volition, and the rest — all [these] <s>dharmas</s> are impermanent, of the nature of change, unreliable. Whatever <s>dharma</s> is impermanent, that is suffering. The arising of this suffering is also suffering. Its persistence is also suffering. The characteristic of repeated becoming is also suffering. Similarly up to the mind and <s>dharmas</s>. If this suffering ceases, other sufferings do not arise. There is no more continuity. In the mind of the <s>yogin</s> it occurs thus: This is the peaceful, excellent, tranquil state — namely, the departure of all false cravings for sensual desire, their exhaustion, dispassion, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. When the mind leaps forward, is resolved, does not waver, does not turn back, does not grieve, and does not tremble regarding this <s>dharma</s> — then by that cause I should see the <s>dharma</s>.' Therefore it is known that a <s>yogin</s> contemplating the five aggregates through the aspects of impermanence and so forth is called a 'distant attainer.' One who sees their cessation is a 'near attainer.' Just as <s>Channa</s> replied to the elders: 'I too have this [understanding]: form is impermanent, consciousness is impermanent, form is non-self, consciousness is non-self, all formations are impermanent, all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self. And yet my mind does not leap forward, is not purified, is not liberated [in relation to] <s>nirvāṇa</s> — the cessation, the exhaustion of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), the complete stilling of all formations. [Craving arises. Clinging arises. The mind turns back.] Then who is my self?' — This does not occur for one who sees the <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: kiñcāha- yogī yadasmin dharme mṛduprajñayā kṣāntiṃ śraddadhate sa śraddhā[nusārī] pratipannakaḥ | pṛthagjanamatītya dharmaniyāmamavatāryādyaphalamalabdhvā na deveṣu bhavati | yastīkṣṇaprajñayā kṣāntiṃ śraddadhate sa dharmā[nusārī] pratipannakaḥ | [yo] dharmamimaṃ paśyan
body.translated_text: Moreover he says: The <s>yogī</s> who, with gentle wisdom, places faith in patient acceptance of this <s>dharma</s>, he is a <s>śraddhānusārī</s> (faith-follower) practitioner. Having transcended the state of an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), descending into the certainty of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmaniyāma</s>), and having obtained the first fruit [of stream-entry], he is not reborn among the gods. He who, with sharp wisdom, places faith in patient acceptance, he is a <s>dharmānusārī</s> (doctrine-follower) practitioner. He who, seeing this <s>dharma</s> —

body.text: trīṇi saṃyojanāni samucchedayati | na srotaāpannaḥ yo niravaśeṣa[kṣayā]bhijñaḥ so 'rhan | ato jñāyate nirodhaṃ paśyan sannikṛṣṭaḥ pratipannako bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: — cuts off the three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>). [But he is] not [yet] a <s>srotāpanna</s> (stream-enterer). He who has the direct knowledge of the complete exhaustion [of the defilements] — he is an <s>arhat</s> (worthy one). Therefore it is known that one who sees cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) becomes a practitioner who is near [to attainment].

body.text: (pṛ) yogī kasmānnātyantaṃ nirodhaṃ paśyati | (u) sūtra uktam- dharmā nissvabhāvāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ | ayaṃ dharmaḥ paramagambhīraḥ | sarvatṛṣṇākṣaya upaśamo nirodho nirvāṇam | idaṃ padamatidurdarśam | bhagavān dvādaśanidānānāṃ nirodhaṃ dṛṣṭvā anuttaramabhisambuddho 'bhūt iti | dharmamudrāyāñcoktam- pañcaskandhānanityān vipralopān mṛṣābhūtānasārān śūnyāṃśca paśyato yogino jñānadarśanamaviśuddhaṃ bhavati iti | sūtramidamanta āha- yogina evaṃ bhavati- yanmayā dṛśyate śrūyate ājighryate rasyate spṛśyate manyate tat sarvaṃ pratītyasamutpannaṃ vijñānam | yadasya vijñānasya hetupratyayā nityā vā anityā vā iti | tadanityajñānam | anityebhyo hetupratyayebhya utpannaṃ vijñānaṃ kathaṃ nityaṃ bhavet | ataḥ sarve pañcaskandhā anityāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ kṣayalakṣaṇāḥ vipariṇāmalakṣaṇā viyogalakṣaṇā nirodhalakṣaṇā iti paśyati | tadā yogino viśuddhaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati | ātyantikanirodha ityanena viśuddhaṃ jñānadarśanamucyate | ato nirodhajñānadarśanameva āryasatyadarśanaṃ bhavati | ādau ca dharmasthititājñānamante nirvāṇajñānaṃ bhavati | ato nirodhasatyadarśanamevāryamārgalābho bhavati |
body.translated_text: (Question:) Why does the <s>yogī</s> not see cessation in its entirety? (Answer:) The <s>sūtra</s> states: '<s>Dharmas</s> are without own-nature (<s>nissvabhāva</s>), arisen through dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>).' This <s>dharma</s> is supremely profound. 'The cessation of all craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is pacification, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' This state is extremely hard to see. 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), having seen the cessation of the twelve links of dependent origination (<s>nidāna</s>), attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>abhisambodhi</s>).' And in the <s>Dharmamudrā</s> (Seal of Dharma) it is stated: 'The knowledge-and-vision of the <s>yogī</s> who sees the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as impermanent, as subject to dissolution, as false, as without essence, and as empty — is impure.' This <s>sūtra</s> states at the end: 'Thus it occurs to the <s>yogī</s>: Whatever is seen by me, heard, smelled, tasted, touched, or cognized — all that is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arisen through dependent origination. Whether the causes and conditions of this consciousness are permanent or impermanent — that is the knowledge of impermanence. How could consciousness arisen from impermanent causes and conditions be permanent?' Therefore he sees: 'All five <s>skandhas</s> are impermanent, dependently arisen, characterized by decay, characterized by transformation, characterized by separation, characterized by cessation.' Then the <s>yogī</s>'s knowledge-and-vision becomes purified. By 'ultimate cessation' (<s>ātyantikanirodha</s>), purified knowledge-and-vision is meant. Therefore, the knowledge-and-vision of cessation alone constitutes the seeing of the Noble Truths (<s>āryasatya</s>). At first there is the knowledge of the stability of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthitatā</s>), and at the end the knowledge of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore, the seeing of the Truth of Cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) alone constitutes the attainment of the Noble Path.

body.text: jñānalakṣaṇavarga ekonanavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the characteristics of knowledge (<s>jñānalakṣaṇavarga</s>), the one-hundred-and-eighty-ninth.

body.text: 190 ekasatyadarśanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 190. The chapter on the seeing of a single truth (<s>ekasatyadarśanavarga</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadbhavānāha- nirodhaṃ paśyanneva phalapratipannaka iti | tadayuktam | kasmāt | sūtre hi bhagavatoktam- caturṇāmaryasatyānāṃ yathābhūtamananubodhāt evamidaṃ dīrghamadhvānaṃ [sandhāvitaṃ] saṃsaritaṃ mama ca yuṣmākañca idānīmimāni catvāri satyānyanubaddhāni | tato nidānañca samucchinnaṃ saṃsaritam | na punaḥ kāyasya vedanā bhavati | iti | jñātavyaṃ catussatyadarśanāt phalapratipannako bhavati iti | na nirodhamātradarśanāt | kiñcāha bhagavānuttamadharmo yaduta catvāryāryasatyāni iti | ato yogī sarvāṇi [satyāni] jānīyāt paśyecca | āha ca- ye hi kecit dharmakañcukā ninditakāyāḥ samyakpravrajyāṃ śraddadhante |
body.translated_text: (Question:) What you have said — that 'one who sees cessation alone is a fruit-attaining practitioner' — is improper. Why? For in the <s>sūtra</s> the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Because of not truly awakening to the Four Noble Truths, this long road has been traversed in <s>saṃsāra</s>, both by me and by you. Now these Four Truths have been realized. Thereby the root [of <s>saṃsāra</s>] has been cut off. There will no longer be sensation of the body.' Therefore it should be known that one becomes a fruit-attaining practitioner through the seeing of the Four Truths — not through merely seeing cessation. Moreover, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The supreme <s>dharma</s> is namely the Four Noble Truths.' Therefore the <s>yogī</s> should know and see all [four] truths. And he said: 'Whatever <s>dharma</s>-clad ones with disciplined bodies place faith in correct renunciation —

body.text: sarve te caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ yathābhūtamabhisamayāya | ye hi kecit srotaāpattiṃ sakṛdāgāmitāmanāgāmitāñca lipsanti | sarve te caturṇāmāryasatyānābhisambuddhatvāt | ye hi kecit arhatāṃ pratyekabuddhatāṃ buddhamārgañca lipsanti | sarve te caturṇāmāryasatyānāmabhisambuddhatvāt | ato jñāyate na nirodhasatyadarśanamātramārgamārga iti | āha ca bhagavān- catvāryāryasatyānyanupūrveṇānuprāpnotīti | dharmacakrapravartane coktam- idaṃ duḥkhamayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipaditi paśyato mama teṣu cakṣurudapadyata jñānamudapadyata vidyodapadyata bodhirudapadyata iti, evaṃ triparivartaṃ catvāryāryasatyānyavocat | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- avadātavasane hrade prakṣipte sati rūpaṃ [yathā] vedayate | evamayaṃ puruṣa ekatra niṣaṇṇaścatvāri satyāni paśyati iti | kiñcāha pariśuddhacittaḥ samyak bhāvayati- duḥkhasatyaṃ yāvanmārgasatyam | evaṃ paśyataḥ kāmāsravāt bhavāsravādavidyāsravāt cittaṃ vimucyate | iti | yatra yatra sūtra uktamāryasatyam | tatra sarvatra catvāri satyānyuktāni | na nirodhasatyamātrama | bhagavānāha catvāri jñānāni duḥkhajñānaṃ samudayajñānaṃ nirodhajñānaṃ mārgajñānamiti | tāni caturṇāmāryasatyānāmarthāya bhavanti iti | yogī dharmaśaḥ paripaśyet catvāri satyāni | yathā bhiṣak rogaṃ jñātvā roganidānaṃ rogavināśaṃ rogavināśauṣadhañca jānīyāt | evaṃ yogī duḥkhānāṃ nissaraṇamicchan duḥkhaṃ duḥkhanidānaṃ duḥkhanirodhaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminīṃ pratipadañca jānīyāt | yadi na jānāti duḥkhaṃ kena jñāsyati duḥkhanidānaṃ duḥkhanirodhaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminīṃ pratipadañca | ato jñāyate na nirodhadarśanamātra[māryasatyam] iti |
body.translated_text: — all of them [do so] for the purpose of truly realizing the Four Noble Truths. Whatever [beings] aspire to <s>srotāpatti</s> (stream-entry), <s>sakṛdāgāmitā</s> (once-returning), and <s>anāgāmitā</s> (non-returning) — all of them [do so] because of having awakened to the Four Noble Truths. Whatever [beings] aspire to <s>arhatship</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhahood</s>, and the <s>Buddha</s>-path — all of them [do so] because of having awakened to the Four Noble Truths.' Therefore it is known that the mere seeing of the Truth of Cessation is not the path to the path. Moreover, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'One realizes the Four Noble Truths in sequence.' And in the Turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-Wheel (<s>Dharmacakrapravartana</s>) it was stated: 'Seeing thus — "This is suffering, this is the origin of suffering, this is the cessation of suffering, this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering" — the eye arose in me, knowledge arose, insight arose, awakening arose.' Thus with three turnings he proclaimed the Four Noble Truths. Moreover, it was stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Just as when a clean white cloth is cast into a lake, one perceives its form — so too this person, seated in one place, sees the Four Truths.' Moreover he says: 'One of purified mind properly cultivates the Truth of Suffering up to the Truth of the Path. For one seeing thus, the mind is liberated from the defilement of sensual desire (<s>kāmāsrava</s>), from the defilement of existence (<s>bhavāsrava</s>), and from the defilement of ignorance (<s>avidyāsrava</s>).' Wherever in the <s>sūtra</s> the Noble Truth is mentioned, in all those places the Four Truths are stated — not merely the Truth of Cessation. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There are four knowledges: knowledge of suffering, knowledge of origination, knowledge of cessation, and knowledge of the path. These serve the purpose of the Four Noble Truths.' The <s>yogī</s> should systematically contemplate the Four Truths. Just as a physician, having known the disease, should know the cause of the disease, the destruction of the disease, and the medicine for destroying the disease — so too the <s>yogī</s>, desiring escape from sufferings, should know suffering, the cause of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering. If he does not know suffering, by what will he know the cause of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Therefore it is known that not merely the seeing of cessation [constitutes the Noble Truth].

body.text: atrocyate | yat keṣāñciduktaṃ- catussatyānāṃ pratilābha iti | sarvaṃ [tat] skandhadhātvāyatanādiṣūktam- yadidaṃ rūpaṃ ityādi ayaṃ rūpasya samudaya ityādi ayaṃ rūpasya vyaya ityādi prajānata āsravāḥ kṣīyanta iti | kiñcāha bhagavān- rūpādīnāṃ skandhānāṃ yathābhūtamāsvādamādīnavaṃ nissaraṇaptaprajñāyānuttaraṃ mārgamaspṛśamiti na vadāmi | yathābhūtaṃ prajānanstu mārgamaspṛśamiti prajānāmīti | nagaropamasūtre coktam- yadā mama na jñānamabhūt- [iti] jarāmaraṇaṃ jarāmaraṇasamudayo jarāmaraṇanirodho jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminī pratipat | yāvat saṃskārāḥ saṃskārasamudayaḥ saṃskāranirodhaḥ saṃskāranirodhagāminī pratipat iti | na
body.translated_text: Here we reply: What some have said — 'the attainment of the Four Truths' — all that was stated with reference to the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and so forth: 'This is form' and so on, 'this is the arising of form' and so on, 'this is the passing away of form' and so on — 'for one who knows [thus], the defilements (<s>āsravas</s>) are exhausted.' Moreover, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'I do not say that one who does not truly know the <s>skandhas</s> beginning with form — their relishing, their danger, and the escape from them — has touched the unsurpassed path. But one who truly knows [these], I know that he has touched the path.' And in the City Simile <s>Sūtra</s> (<s>Nagaropamasūtra</s>) it was stated: 'When I did not have the knowledge: "aging-and-death, the arising of aging-and-death, the cessation of aging-and-death, the path leading to the cessation of aging-and-death; up to: the formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), the arising of formations, the cessation of formations, the path leading to the cessation of formations" — not

body.text: tadā vadāmi- adhigato mārga iti | iti | evamādi [vacanāni] dṛṣṭvā yadi [vadāmaḥ] ayameva darśanamārgādhigama iti | tadā ṣoḍaśacitta[kṣaṇā] na mārgādhigamaḥ syuḥ |
body.translated_text: then did I say: "The path has been attained."' Seeing such [statements], if [we say] 'this alone is the attainment of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>),' then the sixteen mind-moments (<s>cittakṣaṇa</s>) would not constitute the attainment of the path.

body.text: (pṛ) nāhaṃ vadāmi- ayamucyate darśanamārgādhigama iti; kintu ayaṃ sammarśana kālīna iti | (u) caturṣu satyeṣvapyevamucyate | vaktavyañcedaṃ sammarśanakālīnamiti | tathā no cet nidānaṃ vaktavyaṃ- catussatyadarśanaṃ mārgādhigamakālīnaṃ pañcaskandhādidarśanaṃ sammarśanakālīnamiti | (pṛ) kleśānāṃ prahāṇajñāṃna mārgādhigamo bhavati | pañcaskandhādīnāṃ sammarśanaṃ na kleśānāṃ prahāṇāya bhavati | (u) pūrvamevoktamasmābhiḥ- pañcaskandhādijñānamapi kleśānāṃ prahāṇāya bhavatīti | yathoktam- rūpādijñānadarśanādāsravāḥ kṣīyanta iti | āha ca- lokasamudayaṃ samanupaśyato nāstitādṛṣṭirnirudhyate | lokanirodhaṃ samanupaśyato 'stitādṛṣṭirnirudhyata iti | bhagavān svayaṃ nidānānyavalokayan mārgamadhijagāma | kiṃśuko[pama]sūtre coktā nānāmārgādhigamapratyayāḥ | kecit pañcaskandhān paśyanto mārgamadhigacchanti | kecit dvādaśāyatanāni vā aṣṭādaśadhātūn vā dvādaśanidānāni vā anyāni vā paśyanto mārgamadhigacchanti iti | ato jñāyate na catussatya[darśana]mātreṇa mārgādhima iti | yadi bhavato mataṃ satyapyasmin vacane naitaddarśanena kleśān prajahātīti | catussatyadarśanenāpi na kleśān prajahatīti vaktavyam | satya[darśane]na na mārgamadhigacchatīti avaśyaṃ vaktavyamiti | catussatyavibhaṅga uktam- jātirapi duḥkhaṃ jarāpi duḥkhaṃ vyādhirapi duḥkhaṃ maraṇamapi duḥkhaṃ vipriyasaṃyogo duḥkhaṃ priyaviyogo duḥkhaṃ yadiṣṭaṃ na labhyate tadapi duḥkhaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhamiti | kiñcāha duḥkhasamudayo yeyaṃ tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī tatra tatrābhinandinī iti | evamādidarśanena nāsravāṇāṃ kṣayaḥ syāt | idaṃ sarvaṃ lokasatyaṃ na tu paramārthasatyam |
body.translated_text: (Question:) I do not say that 'this is called the attainment of the path of seeing'; rather, [I say] 'this belongs to the time of examination (<s>sammarśana</s>).' (Answer:) The same is said regarding the Four Truths as well. And this should be stated: '[this] belongs to the time of examination.' If that is not so, then the reason should be stated: 'the seeing of the Four Truths belongs to the time of path-attainment, while the seeing of the five <s>skandhas</s> etc. belongs to the time of examination.' (Question:) The knowledge of the abandonment of the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) constitutes path-attainment. The examination of the five <s>skandhas</s> etc. does not serve to abandon the defilements. (Answer:) We have already stated earlier that the knowledge of the five <s>skandhas</s> etc. also serves to abandon the defilements. As stated: 'From the knowledge-and-vision of form etc., the defilements are exhausted.' And he said: 'For one who sees the arising of the world, the view of non-existence (<s>nāstitādṛṣṭi</s>) ceases. For one who sees the cessation of the world, the view of existence (<s>astitādṛṣṭi</s>) ceases.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, contemplating the <s>nidānas</s> (links of dependent origination), attained the path. And in the <s>Kiṃśuka</s> (Kiṃśuka-tree Simile) <s>Sūtra</s>, various causes for path-attainment are stated. Some attain the path by seeing the five <s>skandhas</s>. Some attain the path by seeing the twelve <s>āyatanas</s>, or the eighteen <s>dhātus</s>, or the twelve <s>nidānas</s>, or other [dharmas]. Therefore it is known that the path is not attained merely through the seeing of the Four Truths. If, according to your view, even in the face of this statement, 'one does not abandon the defilements through this seeing,' then it should be said that one does not abandon the defilements through the seeing of the Four Truths either. It must necessarily be said that one does not attain the path through the seeing of [the Four] Truths. In the analysis of the Four Truths (<s>Catussatyavibhaṅga</s>), it is stated: 'Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, illness is suffering, death is suffering, union with the unpleasant is suffering, separation from the pleasant is suffering, not obtaining what is wished for is suffering — in brief, the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>) are suffering.' Moreover he says: 'The origin of suffering is this craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) that leads to renewed existence, delighting here and there.' Through such seeing, there would be no exhaustion of the defilements. All this is conventional truth (<s>lokasatya</s>), but not ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) yadyapi jātimaraṇādi paśyato nāsravakṣayaḥ syāt | tathāpi pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhamityuktam | teṣāṃ parijñātuḥ kleśā bhidyante | (u) anyāni trīṇi satyāni kathaṃ bhavanti | ato jñāyate [tat] bhavataḥ svasaṃjñānusmaraṇavikalpa iti | pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhamiti paśyataścittameva vikṣipyate na mārgo 'dhigamyate | (pṛ) yadi caturbhiḥ satyaurna mārgamadhigacchati | kena dharmeṇādhigacchet | (u) ekenasatyenādhigacchati yo 'yaṃ nirodhaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- mṛṣā nāma anṛtam | satyaṃ tadviparītam | sarve saṃskṛtadharmā anṛtamṛṣāgrahā iti | ato jñāyate yogī cittata eva saṃskṛtadharme vartate na paramārthata iti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- saṃskṛtadharmā anṛtā māyopamā jvālopamā svapnopamā ṛṇopamā iti | yathoktaṃ dharmapade-
body.translated_text: (Question:) Even though seeing birth, death, etc. does not lead to the exhaustion of the defilements, still it is said that 'the five aggregates of clinging are suffering.' For one who fully comprehends them, the defilements are destroyed. (Answer:) How do the other three truths come about? Therefore it is known that [your position] is merely a conceptual elaboration following your own notion. For one seeing that 'the five aggregates of clinging are suffering,' the mind is merely agitated — the path is not attained. (Question:) If one does not attain the path through the Four Truths, through what <s>dharma</s> does one attain it? (Answer:) One attains it through a single truth — namely, this cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Mṛṣā</s> means what is false. Truth is the opposite of that. All conditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>saṃskṛtadharma</s>) are false, deceitful grasping.' Therefore it is known that the <s>yogī</s> dwells in conditioned <s>dharmas</s> only conventionally, not in ultimate reality. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Conditioned <s>dharmas</s> are false, like an illusion, like a flame, like a dream, like a debt.' As stated in the <s>Dharmapada</s> —

body.text:
abhūtabaddho loko 'yaṃ suniścitavat prabhāsate |
asat dṛṣṭaṃ sadābhāsaṃ asadvai parayā dhiyā || iti |
body.translated_text:
'This world, bound to what is unreal, shines as if with certainty;
the unreal is seen with an appearance of reality — but it is truly unreal, [seen] through supreme wisdom.'

body.text: strī puruṣa iti dharmo yathābhūtaṃ nāsti | pañcaskandhānāṃ kalāpamātre strī puruṣa iti sudṛḍhaṃ kīrtayantaḥ pṛthagjanā viparyayamugdhā vadanti | sa vastuto nāsti | iti | yogī tu ime pañcaskandhāḥ śūnyā anātmāna iti bhāvayati | ato na punastaṃ paśyati | yathoktaṃ dharmamudrāsūtre- yogī bhāvayati rūpamanityaṃ śūnyaṃ viyogalakṣaṇamiti | iti | anityamiti yat rūpaṃ svarūpato 'nityam | śūnyamiti yathā ghaṭe jale 'sati śūnyo ghaṭa iti vadanti | evaṃ pañcaskandheṣu nāstyātmā ityataḥ śūnyā bhavanti | evaṃ bhāvayitāpi śūnyaḥ | [tasya] jñānadarśanamapi aviśuddham pañcaskandhānāṃ nirodhādarśatvāt | ante tu nirodhaṃ paśyati yaduta yogina evaṃ bhavati yanmayā dṛṣṭaṃ śrutamityādi | ato jñāyate nirodhaṃ paśyata eva kleśāḥ kṣīyanta iti |
body.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> called 'woman' or 'man' does not exist as it truly is. Ordinary people (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), deluded by perversion, firmly proclaim 'woman' and 'man' regarding the mere aggregate (<s>kalāpa</s>) of the five <s>skandhas</s>, but that [designation] does not [truly] exist. The <s>yogī</s>, however, contemplates: 'These five <s>skandhas</s> are empty (<s>śūnya</s>), without self (<s>anātman</s>).' Therefore he no longer sees that [false designation]. As stated in the <s>Dharmamudrā Sūtra</s>: 'The <s>yogī</s> contemplates: form is impermanent, empty, characterized by separation.' 'Impermanent' means that form is impermanent by its own nature. 'Empty' means: just as people say 'the pot is empty' when there is no water in the pot, so the five <s>skandhas</s> are empty because there is no self (<s>ātman</s>) in them. Even the one who contemplates thus is [himself] empty. His knowledge-and-vision too is impure, because he has not yet seen the cessation of the five <s>skandhas</s>. But at the end he sees cessation — namely, 'thus it occurs to the <s>yogī</s>: whatever has been seen by me, heard' and so forth. Therefore it is known that the defilements are exhausted only for one who sees cessation.

body.text: (pṛ) kasmānnirodhaṃ paśyataḥ kleśāḥ kṣīyante nānyasatyāni | (u) yoginastasmin samaye duḥkhasaṃjñā vyavasthitā bhavati | nirodhalakṣaṇasākṣātkurvatastu saṃskṛteṣu duḥkhasaṃjñā na
body.translated_text: (Question:) Why are the defilements exhausted for one who sees cessation, and not the other truths? (Answer:) At that time, the <s>yogī</s>'s perception of suffering (<s>duḥkhasaṃjñā</s>) is established. But for one who directly realizes the characteristic of cessation (<s>nirodhalakṣaṇa</s>), the perception of suffering regarding conditioned things does not —

body.text: vyavasthitā bhavati | yathā kasyacit prathamadhyāne prītisukhamalabdhavato na pañcakāmaguṇeṣu nirvedasaṃjñā jāyate | yathā ca avitarkāvicārasamādhimalabdhvā na savitarkasavicārasamādhau doṣaṃ manyate | tathā yogyapi nirvāṇamupaśamalakṣaṇamanadhigamya na saṃskāraduḥkhamadhigacchati | ato jñātavyaṃ nirodhasatyaṃ paśyata eva duḥkhasaṃjñā sampannā bhavati | duḥkhasaṃjñāsampannatvāt tṛṣṇādīni saṃyojanāni prahīyante iti |

(pṛ) yadi nirodhasatyadarśanāt duḥkhasaṃjñā sampannā bhavati | nirodhasatyaṃ paśyet paścāt kleśāḥ prahīyeran | kasmāt | nirodhasatyaṃ dṛṣṭavat eva duḥkhasaṃjñāyāḥ sampannatvāt | (u) na paścātprahīyeran | yasmin samaye nirodhasya nirodhalakṣaṇamadhigatam, tasminneva samaye duḥkhasaṃjñā sampadyate | paścāttu abhimukhībhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yogī [yat] samudayalakṣaṇaṃ tat nirodhalakṣaṇamiti prajānan suviśuddhaṃ dharmacakṣuranuprāpnoti | iti | skandheṣu ca sadāsti ātmamatiḥ | skandhā anityā duḥkhā iti paśyannapi na nirodhamanuprāpnoti | nirodhasatyaṃ paśyatastu asallakṣaṇatvādātmamatiratyantaṃ nirudhyate | (pṛ) yadi nirodhasatyaṃ paśyata ātmamatiḥ kṣīyate | kasmāt bhagavān pudgalaḥ sukumāramatirityādi dṛṣṭvā catussatyānyudeśayati, na tu nirodhasatyamātram | (u) tatrāsti mārgānulomyena caritam | kimiti | anityasaṃjñayā anātmasaṃjñāsampannatvāt idaṃ duḥkhamiti darśanamanuprāpnoti | idaṃ mārgasya sannikṛṣṭamityato militvā vadati |
