(pṛ) mārgalābhasamaya eva yadi satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ prahīyata iti | kasmāt punarāha śīlavrataparāmarśo vicikitsā iti | (u) yogī mārgamanuprāpya dharmāḥ śūnyā anātmāna iti dṛṣṭataḥ paśyan na punarvicikitsate | na pṛthagjanānāṃ śrutacintādidarśanaiḥ samāno bhavati | mārgasatyaṃ paśyan prajānāti idamekameva tattvaṃ nānyadastīti | atastrīṇyāha | (pṛ) yadi mārgalābhakāla eva satyadarśanapraheyāḥ kleśāḥ kṣīyante | kasmāt trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāmeva kṣayamāha | (u) sarve kleśāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭimūlakāḥ | yathā bhagavān bhīkṣūn pṛcchati- kena vastunā kiṃ vastūpādāya kiṃ vastvabhiniviśya īdṛśī dṛṣṭirbhavati | asmin kāye mriyamāṇa eva īdṛśādayaḥ sarvā dṛṣṭayo nirudhyante | bhikṣava āhuḥ- bhagavanmūlā hi
no bhagavan dharmāḥ | bhagavantameva prārthayāmahe vyākaraṇāyeti | bhagavānāha- rūpe khalu sati rūpamupādāya rūpamabhiniviśya saktāyadṛṣṭirbhavati | yāvadvijñānamapyevam | iti |

ato jñātavyaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭimupādāya sarve kleśāḥ sambhavantīti | kasmāt | satyāṃ hi satkāyadṛṣṭau vadanti- ayamātmā nityo vānityo veti | nitya iti paśyataḥ śāśvatadṛṣṭiḥ | anitya iti paśyata ucchedadṛṣṭiḥ | yadyātmā nityaḥ | tadā na karma, na vipākaḥ, duḥkhavimokṣaḥ | na mārgabhāvanayā nirvāṇamanuprāpnoti | yadasyā dṛṣṭeḥ prādhānyam | sa eva dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ | [tasyā eva] yatprakarṣalābhaḥ | sa eva śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ | ātmadṛṣṭau tṛṣṇā | paradṛṣṭau dveṣaḥ | ātmana uccadarśanameva mānaḥ | yathābhūtājñānāt yatsaṃyojanānāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ | saivāvidyā | ataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭisamucchedātsatyadarśanena saṃyojanaprahāṇaṃ bhavati |

(pṛ) yadi satkāyadṛṣṭisamucchedādanyānyapi prahīyante | kasmādviśiṣyāha śīlavrataparāmarśaṃ vicikitsāñca | (u) tayoḥ prādhanyāt | dharmalakṣaṇaṃ sākṣātkurvato yogino na vicikitsā bhavati | vicikitseyamastyātmā nāstyātmeti vicikitsate | mārgo viśuddhiṃ prāpayati navetyapi vicikitsate | idānīṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ paśyata ātmadṛṣṭiḥ prahīyate | ayameva mārgo na punaranyo 'stītyapi prajānāti | ata ucyate satkāyadṛṣṭiprahāṇameva vastuto duḥkhadarśanam | śīlavratasamucchedāt mārgaṃ prayujya jñāne jñeyadharmeṣu ca na vicikitsate | yaḥ samyakjñānena jñeyadharmān prajānāti | sa eva samudayaṃ prahāya nirodhamadhigacchan catussatyasampanna ityucyate | ata eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ vacanameva nirvicikitsālakṣaṇaṃ pradarśayati | vicikitseyamātmani mārge ca bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- ādyābhisambodhilakṣaṇaṃ yaduta dharmaṃ paśyati dharmaṃ pratilabhate dharmaṃ prajānāti dharmaṃ pratisaṃvedayate | vicikitsājālaṃ vitīrya paraśāsanaṃ nānuvartate | bhagavacchāsane ca vaiśāradyabalamanuprāpya phale supratitiṣṭhati | iti ||
ekasatyadarśanavargo navatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
191 sarvālambanavargaḥ

(pṛ) kasmāt jñānaṃ sarvālambanaṃ bhavati | (u) yat jñānaṃ dhātvāyatanādigocaraṃ tat sarvālambanamityucyate | kasmāt | āyataneṣu dhātuṣu cokteṣu padārthā ālambanāni viṣayā jñeyā ityādayaḥ sarve dharmā bhavanti | [tān] yat jñānamālambate tat sarvālambanamityucyate |

(pṛ) jñānamidaṃ na samprayuktasahabhvādidharmān jānāti | (u) jānāti yadyāyatanādyālambanaṃ, tatsāmānyalakṣaṇajñānaṃ bhavati | sāmānyalakṣaṇajñānatvāt sarvamālambate | kasmāt | dvādaśāyatanānīti vadato nānyaḥ punardharmo 'sti | ato jñāyate jñānamidamapi svātmānamālambata iti | (pṛ) uktaṃ hi sūtre- dvābhyāṃ pratyayābhyāṃ vijñānamutpadyata iti | ato na svātmālambanaṃ jñānaṃ syāt | jñānānāṃ dṛṣṭāntān pratītya nāsti svātmālambanam | tadyathā- aṅgulyagraṃ nātmānaṃ spṛśati | na cakṣuḥ svātmānaṃ paśyati | (u) yat bhavānāha- dvābhyāṃ pratyayābhyāṃ vijñānamutpadyata iti | na tat niyamena bhavati | ālambanaṃ vināpi jñāmutpadyate | na hi sarvaṃ dvābhyāṃ pratyayābhyāmutpadyate | kiñcit ṣaṣṭhasya vijñānasya svakalāpe sarvathā asadālambanaṃ bhavati | dṛṣṭadharmā[lambana]tvāt | vijñānasyāsya rūpādidharmānālambanatvāt | yadyālambate andho 'pi rūpaṃ paśyet | puruṣasyāsya tasmin samaye cittacaittā atītānāgatagatāḥ | atītānāgatāśca asaddharmāḥ, kasyālambanāni syuḥ | ātmādhyavasānamātrasya pratiṣedhādevamucyate | yadi vijñānāni bhavanti | tāni sarvāṇi ābhyāṃ dvābhyāmeva bhavanti | na caturbhiḥ pratyayaiḥ | kiñcit vijñānaṃ dvau pratyayau vinotpadyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśa iti | na vastutaḥ sparśasya ṣaḍāyatanāni pratyayā bhavanti | utpadyamānaṃ na ṣaḍāyatanebhyo bhavati | saptamāyātanasya pratiṣedhāt | evaṃ caturaḥ pratyayān pratiṣidhyāha bhagavān dve āyatane iti |

atītānāgatākāśakāladigādīnāñca jñānamutpadyate | te dharmāśca na vastusantaḥ | idamevānālambanaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati | (pṛ) anenaiva hetunā atītānāgatādayoḥ dharmāḥ santaḥ syuḥ | yadyasantaḥ, kiṃ tajjñānamutpādayati | śaśaśṛṅgakūrmaromāhipadādiṣu na jātu jñānamutpadyate | (u) kāritre jñānamutpadyate | evaṃ puruṣadarśane 'tīte tadatītakālaṃ smarati | puruṣaṃ bhāṣamāṇaṃ śṛṇvan tadbhāṣaṇakālaṃ smarati | evamatītādidharmāṇāṃ nāsti kāritramityato 'yuktam | (pṛ) idānīmatīte kiṃ kṛtvā smaryate | (u) smaraṇasya nāsti ko 'pi dharmaḥ | bhavānāha- śaśaśṛṅgādi kasmānna smaratīti | yo dharma utpadya niruddhaḥ sa smaraṇīyaḥ | yaḥ prakṛtito 'san | kiṃ smaryeta yathā dharmaḥ pūrvaṃ sattvākhya idānīmatīto 'pi sattvākhyaḥ | evaṃ tasmin dharme pūrvaṃ smṛtyutpādāt tadeva cittaṃ punaḥ smaryate | na tu cittāntaram | anena puruṣeṇa pūrvaṃ taddharmanimittamupāttam | tasmin dharme niruddhe 'pi tatsaṃjñānusmaraṇamutpādya [taṃ dharmaṃ] vikalpayati | yo dharmastasya citte jāyate sa dharmo vinaṣṭaḥ | paścāt [ta]nmanovijñānaṃ tat vastu vijānāti ida[meva] nimittālambanaṃ vijñānamityākhyayate | nimittamidaṃ pāścātyanimittālambanavijñānasya pratyayaṃ karoti | śaśaśṛṅgādivijñānantu animittahetukamityato notpadyate | śaśaśṛṅgādi pratītyāpi vijñānaṃ bhavet | yadi na bhavati | kathaṃ vaktuṃ prabhavet |

(pṛ) śaśaviṣāṇasvabhāvo na vijñeyaḥ | kasmāt | tasya hrasvatvadīrghatvaśuklatvakṛṣṇatvādismṛtirhi na jātu jāyate | tathātītadharmo 'pi | kasmāt | nahyasmākamatītadharma idānīmabhimukhībhavati | yathā āryā anāgataṃ vastu jñātvā vadanti- idaṃ vastu tathā syāt, idaṃ vastu tathā na syāditi | (u) āryajñānabalaṃ hi tathā dharmamasantamapi prāk prajānāti | yathā āryāḥ pāṣaṇabhittiṃ bhittvā apratihatamunmajjanti nimajjanti ca | tathedamapi vastu asadapi jānanti | smṛtibalācca jānanti | yathā cakṣurvijñānaṃ na strīti puruṣa iti vā vikalpayati | yadi cakṣurvijñānaṃ na vikalpayati | manovijñānamapi

na vikalpayet | vastutastu manovijñānaṃ vikalpayati | tathedamapi syāt | yathā cāsmākamanubhūtaniruddhe jñānamutpadyate | tathāryāṇāmapi asati dharme jñānamutpadyate | yathā devadatta iti vacane naikaṃ vijñānaṃ catvāryakṣarāṇi vijānāti | tathāpi [tāni] vijānāti | yathā ca saṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvādayaḥ | te dharmā adṛṣṭā api [sva]vijñānamutpādayanti | yathā ca puruṣasya svarūpaṃ naikakṣaṇena parijñeyamam | nāpi pratyaṅgavijñānena | asatyapi pratyaṅgaṃ puruṣajñāne ekakṣaṇaṃ [ta]jjñāne puruṣajñānamutpadyate | idamapi tathā syāt |
body.translated_text: should not conceptualize. But in reality, mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) does conceptualize. This too would be the same. Just as for us, when a previously experienced [object] has ceased, knowledge arises — so too for the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>), knowledge arises even regarding a non-existent <s>dharma</s>. Just as when the word '<s>Devadatta</s>' is spoken, a single consciousness does not cognize the four syllables [individually], yet it does cognize them [as a whole]. And just as number, measure, separateness, conjunction, disjunction, proximity, remoteness, and so forth — those <s>dharmas</s>, though unseen, generate their own cognition. And just as the true nature of a person cannot be fully known in a single moment, nor through cognition of individual limbs — even without cognition of individual limbs, in a single moment of knowledge of that [person], knowledge of the person arises. This too would be the same.

body.text: bhavānavādīḥ- dṛṣṭāntaṃ pratītya nāsti kiñcit svātmālambanaṃ jñānamiti | tatrāsti vacanaṃ manaḥ svātmānaṃ vijānātīti | yogī cittavipaśyanāmanusarati atīte 'nāgate tu cittaṃ nāsti iti vacanāt | yathā pratyutpannacittena pratyutpannacittamālambate | no cet na jātu kaścitpratyutpannacittasamprayukta dharmaṃ vijānāti | (pṛ) sūtra uktam-
body.translated_text: You have said: 'Relying on the analogy, there is no knowledge whatsoever that takes itself as its own object.' But there is the statement: 'The mind cognizes itself.' The <s>yogī</s> follows <s>cittavipaśyanā</s> (contemplation of mind). But because of the statement: 'The mind of the past and the future does not exist.' How does the present mind take the present mind as its object? If it does not, then no one ever cognizes a <s>dharma</s> associated with the present mind. (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> —

body.text:
sarve dharmā anātmānaḥ prajñayā yadi paśyati |
atha nirvindate duḥkhe eṣa mārgo viśuddhaye || iti |
body.translated_text:
'All <s>dharmas</s> are non-self (<s>anātman</s>); if one sees this with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
then one becomes disenchanted with suffering — this is the path to purification.'

body.text: iyaṃ prajñā ātmānaṃ sahabhūdharmānanyāni sarvadharmālambanāni cāpanayati | (u) jñānamidaṃ sāsravālambanameva, natvanāsrava[ālambana]m | kasmāt | tasyāṃ hi gāthāyāmuktam- atha nirvindate duḥkha iti | ato jñāyate tat duḥkhasatyālambanameveti | ātmadṛṣṭipraṇāśāya ca
body.translated_text: This <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) removes the self (<s>ātman</s>), the <s>dharmas</s> coexistent with it, and all other objects of all <s>dharmas</s>. (Answer) This knowledge takes only what has outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) as its object, not what is without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>). Why? Because in that verse it is said: 'then one becomes disenchanted with suffering.' From this it is known that it takes only the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>) as its object. And for the destruction of the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>),

body.text: anātmabhāvanā | ātmadṛṣṭiḥ pañcopādānaskandhālambinī | jñātavyamanātma[dṛṣṭi]rapi pañcaskandhānālambata iti | pañcaskandhā anityatvādanātmānaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yadanityaṃ tadanātmā | yadānātmā tadduḥkham iti | bhagavānāha yadbhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ tatprajahata iti | bhikṣava āhuḥ- ājñaptaṃ bhagavan | bhagavānāha- kathaṃ yuṣmābhirājñaptam | rūpaṃ bhagavan [anātmā] anātmīyam | vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskārā, vijñāna[manātmā] anātmīyam | tadasmābhiḥ- prahātavya]miti | bhagavānāha- sādhu sādhu khalu bhikṣava iti | [ato] jñātavyamupādānaskandheṣveva anātmabuddhirbhavatīti | uktañca sūtre- yatkiñcit [bhikṣavo] rūpamatītamanāgataṃ pratyutpannamādhyātmikaṃ vā bahirdhā vā audārikaṃ vā sūkṣmaṃ vā [hīnaṃ vā praṇītaṃ vā] yaddūre 'ntike vā sarvaṃ jānāti nātmā nātmīyamiti | evaṃ yathābhūtaṃ samyak prajñayā paśyati iti | āha ca- rūpaṃ nātmā, vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskārā vijñānañca nātmā iti paśyati | rūpamanityaṃ tucchaṃ māyāvat bālālāpanaṃ vadhakaṃ steyakamanātmā anātmīyamiti | kiñcāha bhagavān- atra niṣaṇṇaḥ kaścinmūḍho 'vidyāṇḍagato 'vidyāndhībhūtaḥ parityajya buddhaśāsanamimāṃ mithyādṛṣṭimutpādayati- yadi rūpaṃ nātmā, vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskārā, vijñānañcanātmā | kathamanātmā karma kṛtvā ātmanā anubhavati iti | ato jñāyata upādānaskandhālambanameva nairātmyamiti | sūtre ca anātmajñānaṃ sarvadharmanālambata iti vacanasthānaṃ na kiñcanāsti | tatra tatra sarvatroktaṃ pañcaskandhānālambata iti |
body.translated_text: there is the cultivation of non-self (<s>anātmabhāvanā</s>). The view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) takes the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>) as its object. Therefore it should be known that the [knowledge of] non-self too takes the five aggregates as its object. The five aggregates are non-self because of being impermanent. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'What is impermanent is non-self. What is non-self is suffering.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s>, abandon what is yours.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: 'Understood, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'How have you understood it?' 'Form, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is non-self and not belonging to a self. Feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are non-self and not belonging to a self. This is to be abandoned by us.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Good, good indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>.' From this it should be known that the cognition of non-self (<s>anātmabuddhi</s>) pertains only to the aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>). And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whatever form, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or excellent, far or near — all of it one knows as "not self, not belonging to self." Thus one sees correctly with right <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as it truly is.' And he said: 'One sees that form is not self, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are not self. Form is impermanent, empty, illusory, childish prattle, murderous, thievish, non-self, and not belonging to self.' And further the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Here some fool, wrapped in the egg of ignorance, blinded by ignorance, abandoning the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, generates this wrong view: "If form is not self, and feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are not self, then how can a non-self perform action and a self experience [its result]?"' From this it is known that non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>) takes only the aggregates of clinging as its object. And in the <s>sūtra</s>, there is no passage stating that knowledge of non-self (<s>anātmajñāna</s>) takes all <s>dharmas</s> as its object. Everywhere, in every passage, it is stated that it takes the five aggregates as its object.

body.text: (pṛ) bhagavān svayamāha- sarvadharmā anātmāna iti | ato jñāyate saṃskṛto 'saṃskṛtaścaitajjñānasyālambanam | na tu pañcopādānaskandhamātramiti | āha ca- daśa śūnyatāḥ sarvadharmālambanā iti | yā śūnyatā tadeva nairātmyam | kiñcāha- sarve saṃskārā anityā duḥkhā, sarve dharmā anātmāna iti | yadanātmajñānaṃ tad duḥkhasatyālambanameva | kasmānnāha- sarvasaṃskārā anātmāna iti | sarve dharmā anātmāna ityuktatvāt jñātavyaṃ yat saṃskārā iti vacanaṃ tat saṃskṛtābhidhāyakam | yat dharmā iti vacanaṃ tat sarvā[bhidhāyaka]miti | āha ca- ka ekalakṣaṇadharmaṃ lakṣaṇāntaradharmañcābhimukhaṃ samprajānāti yathā vidyācakṣuṣā rūpaṃ
body.translated_text: (Question) The <s>Bhagavān</s> himself said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are non-self.' From this it is known that both the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) are the object of this knowledge, not merely the five aggregates of clinging. And he said: 'The ten emptinesses (<s>śūnyatās</s>) take all <s>dharmas</s> as their object.' Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is itself non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>). And further he said: 'All conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are impermanent and suffering; all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self.' If knowledge of non-self takes only the truth of suffering as its object, why does he not say 'all conditioned things are non-self'? Since he says 'all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self,' it should be known that the term '<s>saṃskāras</s>' (conditioned things) refers to what is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), while the term '<s>dharmas</s>' refers to everything. And he said: 'Who comprehends face-to-face the <s>dharma</s> of one characteristic and the <s>dharma</s> of another characteristic, just as one sees form with the eye of knowledge?

body.text: paśyati | kevalaṃ buddhā bhagavantaḥ samyak sambuddhā vimuktilābhina ekalakṣaṇadharmaṃ lakṣaṇāntaradharmañcābhimukhaṃ samprajānanti yathā vidyācakṣuṣā rūpaṃ paśyanti iti | anātmalakṣaṇena hi sarvadharmā ekalakṣaṇāḥ | ato jñāyate anātma[jñānaṃ] sarvadharmānālambate | na tu duḥkhamātram iti |
body.translated_text: Only the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, the perfectly and fully awakened ones, who have obtained liberation, comprehend face-to-face the <s>dharma</s> of one characteristic and the <s>dharma</s> of another characteristic, just as they see form with the eye of knowledge.' For by the characteristic of non-self, all <s>dharmas</s> are of one characteristic. From this it is known that knowledge of non-self (<s>anātmajñāna</s>) takes all <s>dharmas</s> as its object, not merely suffering alone.

body.text: ucyate | sarva[miti] dvividhaṃ sarvasaṅgrāhakamekadeśagrāhakamiti | sarvasaṅgrāhakamiti yathā bhagavānāha- aśaṃ sarvajña iti | [atra] sarvaṃ nāma dvādaśāyatanāni | ekadeśagrāhakamiti yathāha- sarvamādīptamiti | anāsravamasaṃskṛtantu nādīptamupalabhyate | yathā ca tathāgatavarge uktam- tathāgataḥ sarvatyāgī sarvajayī iti | śīlādayo dharmā na tyājyāḥ | kintu akuśaladharmānuddiśyāha- sarvatyāgīti | ajeyyā anye buddhāḥ | anyān sattvānuddiśyāparamāha- sarvajayīti | kiñcāha- katamo bhikṣuḥ sarvajñaḥ | yaḥ ṣaṭsparśāyatanānāmutpādaṃ nirodhañca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | ayamucyate sāmānyalakṣaṇajñaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ, na tu viśeṣalakṣaṇajña iti | bhagavāṃstu sāmānyaviśeṣajñaḥ sarvajña ityucyate | bhikṣurayaṃ sāmānyena sarve dharmā anityā iti prajānātītyataḥ sarvajño bhavati | tasya nāmasāmye 'pi vastuto 'sti bhedaḥ | [tat] ekadeśasaṅgrāhakaṃ nāma |
body.translated_text: It is replied: 'All' (<s>sarva</s>) is of two kinds — all-inclusive (<s>sarvasaṅgrāhaka</s>) and partial (<s>ekadeśagrāhaka</s>). 'All-inclusive' is as when the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'I am omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>).' Here 'all' means the twelve sense-bases (<s>dvādaśāyatanas</s>). 'Partial' is as when he said: 'Everything is ablaze.' But the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) are not found to be ablaze. And as stated in the <s>Tathāgata</s> chapter: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is the all-renouncer, the all-conqueror.' <s>Dharmas</s> such as moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) are not to be renounced. Rather, it is with reference to unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that he says 'the all-renouncer.' Other <s>Buddhas</s> are unconquerable. It is with reference to other beings that he further says 'the all-conqueror.' And further he said: 'Which <s>bhikṣu</s> is omniscient? He who knows as they truly are the arising and cessation of the six bases of contact (<s>ṣaṭsparśāyatana</s>).' This one is called 'a knower of the general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇajña</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>,' not a knower of the specific characteristic (<s>viśeṣalakṣaṇajña</s>). But the <s>Bhagavān</s>, being a knower of both general and specific [characteristics], is called omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>). This <s>bhikṣu</s>, because he knows generally that 'all conditioned things are impermanent,' becomes omniscient. Though having the same name, there is in reality a difference. That is what is called 'partial inclusion' (<s>ekadeśasaṅgrāhaka</s>).

body.text: āha ca bhagavān- yatsūtre 'vatarati | vinaye ca sandṛśyate | dharmatāñca na vilomayati | sa dharma upādeya iti | kiñcāha- ya āha idaṃ buddhavacanamiti | sa suvyañjanaḥ | na svarthaḥ | vidvān tatra svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ brūyāt | yenārthena bhikṣorasya vyañjanaṃ praśasyaṃ bhavati | punarasti kaścidvaktā svarthasya, na suvyañjanasya | svarthaṃ suvyañjanena prakṣipet | ityevamādisūtre bhagavān sarvaṃ tat saṃśrāvayati | asti ca nītārthaṃ neyārthañca sūtram | idantu neyārthaṃ sūtram | kasmādekasmin vastuni sarvamiti vacanaṃ bhavati | tasyābhisandhi rjñātavyāsti | laukikā api vadanti ekasmin sarvamiti | yathā vadanti- sarvatyāgaṃ karoti | sarveṣāñca bhojanaṃ prayacchati | ayaṃ sarvabhuk iti | ato jñāyate sarvamanātmeti vacane satyapi pañcopādānaskandhāna[bhisandhāya] uktaṃ, na tu sarvadharmāniti draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: And the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What accords with the <s>sūtra</s>, is seen in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and does not contradict the nature of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>) — that <s>dharma</s> is to be accepted.' And further he said: 'One who says "this is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>" — his wording is good, but not the meaning. A learned person should there state both the meaning and the good wording. By what meaning the wording of this <s>bhikṣu</s> becomes praiseworthy — furthermore there is someone who speaks the meaning but not in good wording; one should cast the meaning in good wording.' In <s>sūtras</s> such as these, the <s>Bhagavān</s> makes known all of that. And there are <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>) and <s>sūtras</s> requiring interpretation (<s>neyārtha</s>). This is a <s>sūtra</s> requiring interpretation. Why does the word 'all' occur with respect to a single entity? Its intended meaning (<s>abhisandhi</s>) must be understood. Even worldly people say 'all' regarding a single thing. As they say: 'He makes a total renunciation.' 'He gives food to everyone.' 'This one eats everything.' From this it is known that even when the statement 'all is non-self' is true, it is said with reference to the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>), not with reference to all <s>dharmas</s> — this should be understood.

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhavatā- daśa śūnyatā iti | tatrāsaṃskṛtaṃ śūnyamiti nopalabhyate |
body.translated_text: As for what you said — 'the ten emptinesses (<s>śūnyatās</s>)' — regarding them, no statement is found that 'the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) is empty.'

body.text: kasmāt | na hi kaścidasaṃskṛta ātmasaṃjñāmutpādayati | tadanyasmin śūnye 'pi na kācitkṣatiḥ | bhavānapi duḥkhajñānena śūnyaṃ saṃyojayati | ataḥ śūnyatā na sarvadharmālambinī | (pṛ) laukikī śūnyatā sarvadharmānālambate na tu anāsravaśūnyatā | (u)nāsti tu laukikī śūnyatā | sarvā śūnyatā anāsravā | (pṛ) uktaṃ hi dharmamudrāsūtre- śūnyatā laukikī śūnyateti | (u) iyaṃ lokottaraśūnyatā na tu laukikī śūnyatā | (pṛ) atroktaṃ jñānadarśanasyāviśuddhatvāt jñāyata iyaṃ laukikī śūnyateti | (u) uktantu prāgasmābhiḥ- anāsravaṃ cittaṃ prajñaptividāraṇamiti | ataḥ prajñaptividāraṇādāgatamanāsravaṃ cittam | paścānnirodhasatyaṃ dṛṣṭvā abhimānaṃ vihāya jñānadarśanaṃ viśuddhaṃ bhavati | ato na laukikī śūnyatā |
body.translated_text: Why? For no one generates the perception of self (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>) regarding the unconditioned. Even if it were empty in some other sense, there would be no harm. You yourself also conjoin emptiness with the knowledge of suffering. Therefore emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) does not take all <s>dharmas</s> as its object. (Question) Mundane (<s>laukikī</s>) emptiness takes all <s>dharmas</s> as its object, but not supramundane emptiness (<s>anāsravaśūnyatā</s>). (Answer) But there is no mundane emptiness. All emptiness is without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>). (Question) For it is stated in the <s>Dharmamudrāsūtra</s>: 'Emptiness and mundane emptiness.' (Answer) This is supramundane emptiness (<s>lokottaraśūnyatā</s>), not mundane emptiness. (Question) It is stated there: 'Because of the impurity of knowledge and vision, it is known that this is mundane emptiness.' (Answer) We have previously stated: 'The supramundane (<s>anāsrava</s>) mind is what penetrates conventional designations (<s>prajñaptividāraṇa</s>).' Therefore, from the penetration of conventional designations comes the supramundane mind. Afterwards, having seen the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) and having abandoned conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>), knowledge and vision become purified. Therefore it is not mundane emptiness.

body.text: yadbhavānāha- sarve saṃskārā anityāḥ sarve dharmā anātmāna iti | evaṃ hi syāt- yogī yadā nairātmyasaṃjñāsamanvitaḥ tadā dharmasaṃjñāsamanvitatvāt nairātmye dharma iti sa saṃjñocyate | yathoktaṃ darśanavarge- yo duḥkhaṃ na paśyati, sa ātmadarśī bhavati | yo yathābhūtaṃ duḥkhaṃ paśyati, na sa punarātmānaṃ paśyati | iti | yathābhūtamiti yadanātmadarśanam | ataḥ sarve dharmā anātmāna iti vacanaṃ duḥkhasatyamātramālambya anātmā saṃskāra ityabhidadhāti | yadbhavānavocat- buddhā [bhagavantaḥ] ekalakṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇāntarañcābhimukhaṃ paśyantīti | tadapi dhātvāyatanādīnāmekatvādekalakṣaṇamityucyate iti syāt | ko doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: As for what you said — 'All conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are impermanent; all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self' — this would be as follows: when the <s>yogī</s> is endowed with the perception of non-self (<s>nairātmyasaṃjñā</s>), at that time, because he is endowed with the perception of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasaṃjñā</s>), the non-self in <s>dharma</s> — that perception is called '<s>dharma</s>.' As stated in the Chapter on Views (<s>darśanavarga</s>): 'He who does not see suffering sees self. He who sees suffering as it truly is does not see self.' 'As it truly is' means the seeing of non-self. Therefore the statement 'all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self' refers only to the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), and 'non-self' designates conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>). As for what you said — 'the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, see face-to-face both the one characteristic and the other characteristic' — that too could be explained as follows: because of the oneness of the elements (<s>dhātus</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), and so forth, it is said to be 'of one characteristic.' What fault is there?

body.text: sarvālambanavarga ekanavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The Chapter on All Objects (<s>sarvālambanavarga</s>), the one hundred and ninety-first.

body.text: 192 āryavihāravargaḥ
body.translated_text: 192. The Chapter on Noble Abiding (<s>āryavihāravarga</s>).

body.text: asti dvividho vihāraḥ śūnyavihāra anātmavihāra iti | pañcaskandheṣu nāsti sattva iti darśanaṃ śūnyavihāraḥ | pañcaskandhā api na santīti darśanamanātmavihāraḥ | kenedaṃ jñāyate | uktaṃ hi sūtre- rūpaṃ niskhabhāvaṃ paśyati [yāvat] vedanāṃ saṃjñāṃ saṃskārān vijñānaṃ niḥskhabhāvaṃ paśyatīti | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- niḥskhabhāvamupādāya vimucyata iti | ato jñāyate rūpasvabhāvo na vastusan yāvadvedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānasvabhāvā na vastusanta iti | api
body.translated_text: There are two kinds of abiding: abiding in emptiness (<s>śūnyavihāra</s>) and abiding in non-self (<s>anātmavihāra</s>). The seeing that in the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandhas</s>) there is no being (<s>sattva</s>) is the abiding in emptiness. The seeing that even the five aggregates themselves do not exist is the abiding in non-self. How is this known? For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One sees form as without substance (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>), [and likewise] one sees feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as without substance.' And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Relying on substancelessness, one is liberated.' From this it is known that the intrinsic nature of form is not truly real, and likewise the intrinsic natures of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are not truly real. Moreover,

body.text: coktaṃ sūtre- pañcaskandhāḥ śūnyā māyāvat iti | na hi māyā vastusatīti nirvācyā | yadi māyā vastusatī, na māyeti bhavati | nāstītyapi na nirvaktuṃ sambhavati | avastutvādeva [bālā]lāpanaṃ karoti | ayañca yogī sarvaṃ śūnyaṃ paśyati | ato jñāyate pañcaskandhā na vastusanta iti | yathā ekalakṣaṇavidhamanādbhittyādireko ['pi] dharmo nāsti | tathā pañcaskandhā api, naikaḥ [tādṛśaḥ] paramārthiko dharmo 'sti |
body.translated_text: it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandhas</s>) are empty, like an illusion.' For indeed, an illusion is not to be spoken of as truly real. If an illusion were truly real, it would not be an illusion. Nor is it possible to declare it 'non-existent,' for it is precisely because of its non-substantiality that it produces childish prattle. And this <s>yogī</s> sees everything as empty. From this it is known that the five aggregates are not truly real. Just as through the method of one characteristic, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever other than walls and the like exists [as ultimately real] — so too with the five aggregates: there is not a single such ultimately real <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) yadi rūpādayo dharmā api avastusantaḥ | tadā ekaṃ lokasatyameva syāt | (u) nirodhaḥ paramārthasatyatvādasti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- mṛṣā nāma yat tucchakam | satyaṃ nāma yathābhūtamiti | nirodhaḥ sa niyataṃ yathābhūta ityataḥ paramārthasan iti | (pṛ) yadbhavatoktaṃ pañcaskandheṣu nāsti sattva iti darśanaṃ [śūnyavihāra] iti | kena hetunā pañcaskandhāḥ sattva ityucyante | [sa] kiṃ sāsrava utānāsravaḥ | (u) sāsravo 'nāsravaśca (pṛ) sūtra uktam- yaḥ sattvaṃ paśyati sa pañcopādānaskandhān paśyati iti | (u) anāsravadharmo 'pi sattvākhye vartate nāsattvākhye tarupāṣāṇādau | ato jñāyate anāsravān skandhānupādāyāpi sattva ityucyante | yadācāryo 'nāsravacittagataḥ | tasmin samaye 'pyasti cittaṃ sattva iti | ato 'nāsravacittamapi sattvo bhavati | sarve skandhā upādānaskandhā ityucyante | upādānādutpannatvāt |
body.translated_text: (Question:) If <s>dharmas</s> such as form are also non-substantial, then there would be only conventional truth (<s>lokasatya</s>). (Answer:) Cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) exists, because it is ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Mṛṣā</s> means what is worthless. Truth means what is as it truly is.' Cessation is certainly as it truly is — therefore it is [said to be] ultimately real. (Question:) You have said that the seeing that 'in the five <s>skandhas</s> there is no being (<s>sattva</s>)' is [called] the 'emptiness-abiding' (<s>śūnyavihāra</s>). For what reason are the five <s>skandhas</s> called 'a being'? Is that [designation] with defilements (<s>sāsrava</s>) or without defilements (<s>anāsrava</s>)? (Answer:) Both with and without defilements. (Question:) The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'He who sees a being sees the five aggregates of clinging.' (Answer:) Even the undefiled <s>dharma</s> operates under the designation 'being' — not under the designation 'non-being,' as with trees and stones. Therefore it is known that [aggregates] are called 'a being' even taking into account the undefiled <s>skandhas</s>. When the teacher has entered the undefiled mind, even at that time there is a mind [called] 'a being.' Therefore, even the undefiled mind constitutes a being. All <s>skandhas</s> are called 'aggregates of clinging' (<s>upādānaskandha</s>), because they arise from clinging (<s>upādāna</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) kathaṃ jñāyate sarve upādānādutpadyanta iti | (u) anāsravadharmo dānaśīlasamādhibhāvanā karmacittādutpadyate | asati tu [tasmin] notpadyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- avidyānivṛtatṛṣṇāsaṃyojanayā pratibaddho mūḍha imaṃ kāyamanuprāpnoti | evaṃ vidvānapi iti | kāya evopādānaskandhaḥ | (pṛ) yadi sarve skandhā upādānaskandhāḥ | sāsravo 'nāsrava iti skandhānāṃ pravibhāgaḥ katham | (u) sarve skandhā upādānādutpannā ityata upādānaskandhā ityucyante | naiva punarbhavamupādadata ityato 'nāsravāḥ | ityayaṃ pravibhāgaḥ | skandhā upādānaskandhaiḥ sahopādānādutpannā ityata upādānaskandhā ityabhidhīyante | idaṃ sūtraṃ na virudhyate |
body.translated_text: (Question:) How is it known that all [skandhas] arise from clinging? (Answer:) Undefiled <s>dharma</s> — generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — arises from volitional mind (<s>karmacittā</s>). Without that [volitional mind], it does not arise. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who is bound by the fetter of craving, enveloped by ignorance — that deluded one obtains this body. Even a wise person [does] likewise.' This body itself is the aggregate of clinging. (Question:) If all <s>skandhas</s> are aggregates of clinging, how is the classification of <s>skandhas</s> into 'with defilements' and 'without defilements' [possible]? (Answer:) All <s>skandhas</s> are called 'aggregates of clinging' because they arise from clinging. [But those that] do not take up renewed existence are [called] 'without defilements.' This is the classification. The <s>skandhas</s>, having arisen from clinging together with the aggregates of clinging, are therefore called 'aggregates of clinging.' This <s>sūtra</s> is not contradicted.

body.text: imau dvau vihārau yatkiñcidabhāvamālambete | yadrūpādaye dharmāḥ śūnyāḥ svabhāvaniruddhā iti | ayameva yatkiñcidabhāvaḥ | (pṛ) imau dvau pañcaskandhānālambete | uktaṃ hi sūtre- rūpaṃ paśyati śūnyamanātmā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārān vijñānañca paśyati śūnyamanātmā iti | (u)
body.translated_text: These two abodes (<s>vihāra</s>) have as their object the non-existence of anything whatsoever. That <s>dharmas</s> such as form are empty, of a nature that has ceased — this itself is 'the non-existence of anything whatsoever.' (Question:) These two have the five <s>skandhas</s> as their object. For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One sees form as empty, without self; one sees feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as empty, without self.' (Answer:)

body.text: skandhānupādāya paśyati śūnyamanātmeti | kasmāt | sattvakāraṇe sattvaśūnyaṃ paśyati | rūpādīnāṃ dharmāṇāmapi nirodhaṃ paśyati | (pṛ) evañcobhayālambanam | yadyogī skandhāṃśca śūnyānanusmarati | tadeva skandhān yatkiñcidabhāvañcālambate | (u) yogī sattvakāraṇe na sattvaṃ paśyatītyata eva śūnyacittamutpādya tataḥ śūnyaṃ paśyati | pañcaskandhānāṃ nirodhe ca na paśyati rūpasvabhāvaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānasvabhāvam | ato jñāyate imau dvau yatkiñcidabhāvālambanāviti ||
body.translated_text: One sees the <s>skandhas</s> taken up as empty and without self. Why? Because in the cause of a being, one sees the being as empty. One also sees the cessation of <s>dharmas</s> such as form. (Question:) Thus both [emptiness and cessation] serve as objects. When the <s>yogī</s> recollects the <s>skandhas</s> as empty, that very [cognition] has both the <s>skandhas</s> and the non-existence of anything whatsoever as its object. (Answer:) The <s>yogī</s>, not seeing a being in the cause of a being — from that very [realization], having generated the empty mind, then sees emptiness. And in the cessation of the five <s>skandhas</s>, he does not see the own-nature of form, nor the own-nature of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness. Therefore it is known that these two [abodes] have the non-existence of anything whatsoever as their object.

body.text: āryavihāravargo dvinavattyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the Noble Abodes (<s>āryavihāravarga</s>), the one-hundred-and-ninety-second.

body.text: 193 jñānadarśanavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 193. The chapter on knowledge and vision (<s>jñānadarśanavarga</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) samyagdarśanasya samyagjñānasya ca ko viśeṣaḥ | (u) ubhayamekātmakameva | nāsti kaścidviśeṣaḥ | samyagdarśanaṃ dvividhaṃ laukikaṃ lokottaramiti | laukikaṃ yadasti puṇyaṃ pāpamityādi | lokottaraṃ yat duḥkhādīnāṃ satyānāṃ pratisaṃvedaḥ | tathā samyak jñānamapi ||
body.translated_text: (Question:) What is the distinction between right vision (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) and right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>)? (Answer:) Both are of one and the same essence. There is no distinction whatsoever. Right vision is twofold: worldly (<s>laukika</s>) and supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>). The worldly is [the knowledge] that 'there is merit, there is sin,' and so forth. The supramundane is the direct experience of the truths such as suffering. Right knowledge is likewise.

body.text: (pṛ) bhavatoktaṃ jñānadarśanayornedṛśaṃ lakṣaṇam | kasmāt kṣāntayo darśanamātraṃ na jñānam | kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānaṃ, pañcavijñānasamprayuktā ca prajñā jñānameva ca darśanam | (u) kasmāt kṣāntayo na jñānam | (pṛ) ājñātamājñāsyāmītyata ājñāsyāmīndriyam | yadi duḥkhe dharmakṣāntirjñānam | duḥkhe dharmakṣāntirjñātaiva duḥkhe dharmajñānamājñendriyaṃ syāt | nājñāsyāmīndriyam | ato kṣāntirna jñānam | uktañca sūtre- yat dharmeṣu dharmān parīttaṃ prajñayā vipaśyati | kṣānti[riyaṃ vipaśyanā] apariniṣpannā | pariniṣpannā tu jñānam iti | yā kṣāntiḥ, apariniṣpannā vipaśyanā [sā] | prathamā cānāsravā prajñā prāthamikaṃ darśanaṃ kṣāntiḥ | na prāthamikaṃ darśanaṃ jñānaṃ bhavet | kṣāntikāle ca na viniścayo bhavati | jñānakāle tu viniścayo 'vaśyaṃ bhavati | kṣāntyutpattikāle vicikitsā punaranuvartate | ataḥ kṣāntirna jñānam | (u) yā kṣāntistadeva jñānam | kasmāt | chandaḥ abhiratiḥ kṣāntiḥ
body.translated_text: (Question:) According to what you have said, knowledge and vision do not have such [distinct] characteristics. Why then are the patient acceptances (<s>kṣānti</s>) vision only and not knowledge? And the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>), the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) associated with the five [sense-]consciousnesses — [why are they] knowledge only and not vision? (Answer:) Why are the patient acceptances not knowledge? (Question:) '<s>Ājñātamājñāsyāmī</s>' — therefore there is the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> (faculty of 'I shall come to know'). If the <s>dharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of <s>dharma</s>) regarding suffering were knowledge, then the <s>dharmakṣānti</s> regarding suffering, being already known, [and] the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of <s>dharma</s>) regarding suffering would be the <s>ājñendriya</s> (faculty of knowing), not the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>. Therefore <s>kṣānti</s> is not knowledge. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'When one with limited wisdom examines <s>dharmas</s> among <s>dharmas</s> — this <s>kṣānti</s> (<s>vipaśyanā</s>) is not brought to completion. When brought to completion, it is knowledge.' <s>Kṣānti</s> is that which is an uncompleted <s>vipaśyanā</s>. The first undefiled wisdom is the initial seeing — <s>kṣānti</s>. The initial seeing cannot be knowledge. At the time of <s>kṣānti</s>, there is no definite determination. At the time of knowledge, there is necessarily definite determination. At the time when <s>kṣānti</s> arises, doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) may recur. Therefore <s>kṣānti</s> is not knowledge. (Answer:) That which is <s>kṣānti</s> is itself knowledge. Why? Desire, delight, and patient acceptance —

body.text: sarvamekārthakam | yogī pūrvaṃ duḥkhaṃ jñātvā paścāt [tat]kṣāntāvabhiramate | yadi pūrvameva nāsti jñānam | kṣantavye kābhiratiḥ | parīttavacane ca kevalamuktaṃ vipaśyanā kṣāntiriti na jñānam | tathā cet pratipattiphalavedako jñānarahitaḥ syāt | yadi manyase yogino jñānavata eva kṣāntirbhavatīti | tadā kṣāntivedanameva jñānaṃ bhavati | uktañca sūtre- [evaṃ] jānan paśyan āsravādvimucyata iti | āha ca- jñānaṃ darśanañcaikārthakamiti | kiñca bhagavānāha- duḥkhajñānaṃ samudaya[jñānaṃ] nirodha[jñānaṃ] mārgajñānam iti | na tvāha kṣāntiriti | ato jñāyate jñānameva kṣāntiriti |
body.translated_text: — are all of the same meaning. The <s>yogī</s>, having first known suffering, afterwards delights in the patient acceptance of it. If there is no knowledge from the very first, what delight could there be in that which is to be patiently accepted? And in the statement regarding 'limited [wisdom],' it is merely said that '<s>vipaśyanā</s> is <s>kṣānti</s>' — not that it is not knowledge. If so, then the fruit-perceiving practitioner would be devoid of knowledge. If you think that <s>kṣānti</s> arises only for the <s>yogī</s> who possesses knowledge, then that very experience of <s>kṣānti</s> would be knowledge. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Knowing and seeing, one is liberated from the defilements.' And he said: 'Knowledge and vision are of one and the same meaning.' Moreover, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of origination, knowledge of cessation, knowledge of the path' — but he did not say '<s>kṣānti</s>.' Therefore it is known that <s>kṣānti</s> is itself knowledge.

body.text: bhagavān vimuktyarthamāha- yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti jñānam iti | kṣāntirapi yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti na [jñānā]danyā syāt | yadi bhavat ājñāta[mājñāsyāmī]ndriyameva kṣāntiriti | tadayuktam | na vayaṃ vadāmaḥ pūrvaṃ kṣāntiḥ paścāt jñānamiti | ekasyaiva cittasya kṣāntiḥ jñānamityākhyā bhavati | ayaṃ sūtrārtho 'siddhaḥ | bhavataḥ kathamasiddhena lakṣaṇasiddhirbhavati | bhavānāha- kṣāntipariniṣpanneti | pratyuktamidaṃ mayā yat jñānapūrvikā kṣāntiriti | [ataḥ] pariniṣpannaiva kṣāntiriti draṣṭavyam | yadi pariniṣpattiṃ na jānāti | kathaṃ kṣamate | bhavānavocat- kṣāntikāle na viniścayo 'stīti | bhavatāṃ śāsanekṣāntyā saṃyojanaṃ prajahāti | evamaniścitaṃ kiṃ saṃyojanaṃ prajahāti | bhavānavocat- kṣāntikāle vicikitsānuvartate iti | tathā cet mārgasatyadarśane 'pi vicikitsānuvartamānā bhavati | tatra jñānamutpadyamānamapi ajñānaṃ syāt | na savikalpikeyaṃ kṣāntiḥ idaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati | yathā laukikī vipaśyanā catussatyānusāriṇī kṣāntirityapyucyate jñānamityapyucyate | anāsravā kṣāntirjñānañca tathā syāt |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the purpose of liberation, said: 'One who truly knows' — this is knowledge. <s>Kṣānti</s> also 'truly knows' — therefore it should not be different from knowledge. If your view is that <s>kṣānti</s> is only the <s>ājñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s> — that is improper. We do not say that first there is <s>kṣānti</s> and afterwards knowledge. Of one and the same mind, there are the designations <s>kṣānti</s> and knowledge. This interpretation of the <s>sūtra</s> is not established [by you]. How can you establish the defining characteristic from what is unestablished? You say that '<s>kṣānti</s> is brought to completion' — I have already replied that <s>kṣānti</s> is preceded by knowledge. Therefore, <s>kṣānti</s> itself should be regarded as brought to completion. If one does not know the completion, how does one exercise patient acceptance? You said: 'At the time of <s>kṣānti</s> there is no definite determination.' [But] in your own teaching, it is through <s>kṣānti</s> that one abandons the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>). How can one abandon fetters through something so indeterminate? You said: 'At the time of <s>kṣānti</s>, doubt recurs.' If so, then even in the seeing of the Truth of the Path, doubt would be recurring. There, even knowledge arising would [then have to] be non-knowledge. This <s>kṣānti</s> is not conceptually constructed; this is knowledge. Just as worldly <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) that accords with the Four Truths is called both <s>kṣānti</s> and knowledge, so too the undefiled <s>kṣānti</s> and knowledge should be [of the same nature].

body.text: (pṛ) kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānañca jñānamātraṃ na dṛṣṭiḥ | (u) kiṃ kāraṇam | (pṛ) sūtre hi pṛthugucyate samyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyak jñānamiti | ato jñānaṃ na dṛṣṭiḥ | (u) tathā cet samyagdṛṣṭirna samyag jñānaṃ bhavati | yadi bhavato mataṃ samyag
body.translated_text: (Question:) The knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) are knowledge only, not vision (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). (Answer:) For what reason? (Question:) In the <s>sūtra</s>, right vision (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) and right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) are stated separately. Therefore knowledge is not vision. (Answer:) If so, then right vision would not be right knowledge. If your view is that right

body.text: dṛṣṭiḥ samyag jñānamiti | samyag jñānamapi samyag dṛṣṭiḥ syāt | pañcāṅgadharmakāye prajñāskandhāt pṛthaguktaṃ vimuktijñānadarśanaṃ na prajñā bhavet | tathā ca kṣayajñānamamutpādajñānamapi na prajñā bhavati | idānīṃ samyagdṛṣṭireva bhinnalakṣaṇatayā samyag jñānamityucyate | yaduta sarvakleśānāṃ kṣayo 'rhataścitte samutpadyata ityata[stata] samyag jñānamityucyate |
body.translated_text: vision is right knowledge, then right knowledge too should be right vision. The liberation-knowledge-and-vision (<s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s>), stated separately from the wisdom-aggregate (<s>prajñāskandha</s>) in the five-limbed body of <s>dharma</s> (<s>pañcāṅgadharmakāya</s>), would not be wisdom. Likewise, the knowledge of destruction and the knowledge of non-arising would also not be wisdom. Now, right vision itself, by virtue of a distinct defining characteristic, is called 'right knowledge' — namely, the exhaustion of all defilements arises in the mind of the <s>arhat</s>, and therefore it is called 'right knowledge.'

body.text: (pṛ) yadi samyag jñānameva samyagdṛṣṭiḥ | tadā arhanna daśāṅgasampannaḥ syāt | (u) ekasyaiva nāmāntaram | yathā dharmajñānaṃ duḥkhajñānamiti | āha ca- arhan aṣṭaguṇapuṇyakṣetrasampaditi | ataḥ samyag jñānameva samyagdṛṣṭiḥ | ṣaṭsu sāmīcīṣu ṣaṣṭhī sāmīcī samatādṛṣṭirityucyate | yadi bhavatoktavat bhavati | tadā kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānaṃ na sāmīcī bhavati | kiñca samyagvipaśyatīti samyagdṛṣṭiḥ | kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānañca samyagvipaśyatītyato 'pi samyagdṛṣṭiḥ |
body.translated_text: (Question:) If right knowledge is indeed right vision, then the <s>arhat</s> would not be endowed with ten factors. (Answer:) They are merely different names for one and the same [thing]. Just as '<s>dharmajñāna</s>' and 'knowledge of suffering' [refer to the same thing]. And he said: 'The <s>arhat</s> has the perfection of a field of merit with eight qualities.' Therefore right knowledge is indeed right vision. Among the six conformities (<s>sāmīcī</s>), the sixth conformity is called 'the vision of equanimity.' If it were as you have stated, then the knowledge of destruction and the knowledge of non-arising would not be conformities. Moreover, 'seeing rightly' is right vision. The knowledge of destruction and the knowledge of non-arising also 'see rightly' — therefore they too are right vision.

body.text: (pṛ) pañcavijñānasamprayuktā prajñā jñānamātraṃ na dṛṣṭiḥ | (u) kasmānna dṛṣṭiḥ | (pṛ) pañcavijñānāni nirvikalpakāni | prathamata ālambanagatatvāt | dṛṣṭirnāma sañcityopanidhyānam | pañcavijñānāni ca pratyutpannamālambante | ato na dṛṣṭiḥ | (u) tatra vitarkavicārābhāvāt na vikalpayanti | prathamata ālambanagatatvāt na dṛṣṭiriti yadi matam | tadayuktam | kasmāt | bhavatāṃ hi śāsanaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ santānālambanaṃ yathā manovijñānamiti | ato na vaktavyaṃ prathamata ālambanagatamiti | tathā cenmanovijñānamapi na dṛṣṭirbhavet | bhavān punarāha- pratyutpannālambanatvānna dṛṣṭiriti | idamapi na yuktam | paracittajñānamapi pratyutpannālambanam | idamapi na dṛṣṭiḥ syāt | pañcavijñāneṣu nāsti yathābhūtajñānam | pratipattyabhāvāt | sadā prajñaptyanuvartanācca | dṛṣṭiḥ jñānaṃ prajñā ityādi sarvaṃ nāsti | kiṃ punardṛṣṭimātraṃ nāstīti |
body.translated_text: (Question:) Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) associated with the five [sense-]consciousnesses is knowledge only, not vision. (Answer:) Why is it not vision? (Question:) The five consciousnesses are non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), because from the first they are directed toward [their] object. Vision means deliberate contemplation (<s>upanidhyāna</s>). The five consciousnesses grasp only what is present. Therefore they are not vision. (Answer:) Because conceptualization (<s>vitarka</s>) and investigation (<s>vicāra</s>) are absent therein, they do not conceptualize. If your view is that 'they are not vision because from the first they are directed toward [their] object' — that is improper. Why? For according to your own teaching, visual consciousness grasps a continuous [object] just as does mental consciousness. Therefore one should not say 'it is directed toward the object from the first.' If so, then mental consciousness too would not be vision. And you further say: 'It is not vision because it grasps what is present' — this too is improper. Knowledge of others' minds also grasps what is present; that too would then not be vision. In the five consciousnesses there is no knowledge of things as they truly are, because of the absence of realization, and because they always follow [mere] designation. Vision, knowledge, wisdom, etc. — all of these do not [truly] exist [in them]. But is it the case that not even vision alone exists?

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- cakṣurindriyaṃ dṛṣṭiriti | kathamidam | (u) na cakṣurindriyaṃ
body.translated_text: Some say: 'The eye-faculty (<s>cakṣurindriya</s>) is vision.' How is this? (Answer:) The eye-faculty is not

body.text: dṛṣṭiḥ | cakṣurvijñānaṃ [viṣayā]lambanaṃ bhavati | lokavyavahāramanusṛtya cakṣurdṛṣṭirityucyate | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- santyaṣṭadṛṣṭayo yaduta pañcamithyādṛṣṭayo laukikī samyagdṛṣṭiḥ śaikṣadṛṣṭiraśaikṣadṛṣṭiḥ | etā aṣṭadṛṣṭirvarjayitvā anyā prajñā na dṛṣṭirityucyata iti | kathamidam | (u) jñānadarśanaṃ vimuktilābhaḥ pratisaṃvedanaṃ sākṣātkāra itīdaṃ sarvamekārthakam | iyaṃ dṛṣṭiriyaṃ na dṛṣṭiriti yat vacanam | sarvaṃ tat svasaṃjñāvikalpitaṃ vacanam | (pṛ) uktaṃ nanu sūtre- jānan paśyan āsravādvimucyata iti | kathamasti pravibhāgaḥ | (u) yat jñātvā ādau prajñaptiṃ vidārayati tat jñānamityucyate | dharmasthitāyāmavataraṇaṃ darśanam | ādyavipaśyanā jñānam | [tat]pratisaṃvedanaṃ darśanam | ityevamasti pravibhāgaḥ ||
body.translated_text: vision. Visual consciousness grasps its object. Following worldly convention, the eye is called 'vision.' (Question:) Some say: 'There are eight types of vision — namely, the five wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), worldly right vision, the learner's vision (<s>śaikṣadṛṣṭi</s>), and the adept's vision (<s>aśaikṣadṛṣṭi</s>). Excluding these eight types of vision, other wisdom is not called vision.' How is this? (Answer:) Knowledge, vision, attainment of liberation, direct experience, direct realization — all these are of one and the same meaning. The statement that 'this is vision, this is not vision' — all such statements are mere conceptual elaboration of one's own notions. (Question:) Is it not stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Knowing and seeing, one is liberated from the defilements'? How is there a distinction? (Answer:) That which, by knowing, first penetrates designation — that is called knowledge. The descent into the stability of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthitatā</s>) is vision. The initial <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) is knowledge. The direct experience of that is vision. Thus there is a distinction.

body.text: jñānadarśanavargastrinavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on knowledge and vision (<s>jñānadarśanavarga</s>), the one-hundred-and-ninety-third.

body.text: 194 trividhaprajñāvargaḥ
body.translated_text: 194. The chapter on the threefold wisdom (<s>trividhaprajñāvarga</s>).

body.text: tisraḥ prajñā, śrutamayī prajñā, cintāmayī prajñā, bhāvanāmayī prajñeti | sūtrādi dvādaśāṅgapravacanādutpannā śrutamayī | idamanāsravāṃ prajñāṃ janayatīti prajñā | yathoktaṃ sūtre- rāhulo bhikṣurvimuktiprāpiṇīṃ prajñāṃ sampādayati iti | vedādīn vyāvahārikagranthān śṛṇvannapi nānāsravāṃ prajñāmutpādayatītyato na [sā] śrutamayī prajñā bhavati | yat sūtrāṇāmarthaṃ cintayati sā cintāmayī prajñā | yathocyate- yogī dharmaṃ śrutvā tadarthagatiṃ cintayati | iti | api cāha- yogī dharmaṃ śrutvā tadarthaṃ cintayan sadā pratipadamanuvartata iti | yat jñānadarśanamabhimukhībhavati sā bhāvanāmayī prajñā | yathocyate- yogī samāhitacitte pañcaskandhānutpādaniruddhān paśyatīti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yūyaṃ bhikṣavo dhyānasamādhiṃ bhāvayanto yathābhūtajñānadarśanamabhimukhaṃ labhadhve | iti | kiñcoktaṃ saptasamyagjñānasūtre- yat bhikṣu dharmaṃ prajānāti | [iyaṃ] śrutamayī prajñā | yadarthaṃ prajānāti [iyaṃ] cintāmayī prajñā | yat
body.translated_text: There are three kinds of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom): <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of learning), <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of reflection), and <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of meditation). That which arises from the twelve divisions of the teaching (<s>dvādaśāṅgapravacana</s>) beginning with the <s>sūtras</s> is <s>śrutamayī</s>. 'This produces outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) wisdom' — that is <s>prajñā</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The monk <s>Rāhula</s> develops the <s>prajñā</s> that leads to liberation.' Even one who hears worldly texts such as the <s>Vedas</s> and so forth does not produce outflow-free <s>prajñā</s>; therefore that is not <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. That which reflects on the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s> is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. As it is said: 'The <s>yogī</s>, having heard the <s>dharma</s>, reflects on its meaning.' And further he says: 'The <s>yogī</s>, having heard the <s>dharma</s>, always reflecting on its meaning, follows the practice.' That which turns toward knowledge-and-vision is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. As it is said: 'The <s>yogī</s>, with concentrated mind, sees the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as unborn and unceased.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'You monks, cultivating <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration), obtain knowledge-and-vision of reality face to face.' And further it is stated in the <s>Saptasamyagjñānasūtra</s> (Sūtra of Seven Right Knowledges): 'That a monk understands the <s>dharma</s> — [this is] <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. That he understands the meaning — [this is] <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. That

body.text: kālādīn prajānāti | iyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā | iti | yathā ca rāhulaḥ pañcopādānaskandhanikāyādīnadhīte | iyaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | yadviviktadeśe tadarthaṃ cintayati | iyaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | paścātsambodhikāle bhāvanāmayī prajñā | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- trīṇyāyudhāni śrutāyudhaṃ vivekāyudhaṃ prajñāyudhamiti | śrutāyudhaṃ nāma śrutamayī prajñā | vivekāyudhaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | prajñāyudhaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā | api coktaṃ sūtre- pañcānuśaṃsādharmaśravaṇe | katamāḥ pañca | aśrutaṃ śṛṇoti | śrutaṃ paryādāpayati | kāṃkṣāṃ vihanti | dṛṣṭiṃ ṛju karoti | cittamasya prasīdati | iti | aśrutaṃ śṛṇoti | śrutaṃ paryādāpayati itīyaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | kāṃkṣāṃ vihanti | dṛṣṭiṃ ṛjukaroti itīyaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | cittamasya prasīdati itīyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā | dharmaśravaṇānuśaṃsāyāñcoktam- śrotreṇa dharmaṃ śṛṇoti | vācā dharmamadhīte | iyaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | manasā mīmāṃsate | iyaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | paśyan abhisameti | iyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā iti | caturṣu śrotaāpattyaṅgeṣu saddharmaśravaṇaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | yoniśomanaskāraścintāmayī prajñā | dharmānudharmapratipattirbhāvanāmayī prajñā | pañcavimuktidvāreṣu [yadanyatarasmāt] gurusthānīyāt dharmaṃ śrṛṇoti | iyaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | [tasmin dharme] yadarthapratisaṃvedī bhavati | iyaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | tasya yat pramodyādi jāyate | iyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā |
body.translated_text: he understands time and so forth — this is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>.' Just as <s>Rāhula</s> studies the collections beginning with the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>) — this is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. When in a secluded place he reflects on their meaning — this is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. Afterward, at the time of his awakening — this is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are three weapons (<s>āyudha</s>): the weapon of learning (<s>śrutāyudha</s>), the weapon of seclusion (<s>vivekāyudha</s>), and the weapon of wisdom (<s>prajñāyudha</s>).' The weapon of learning is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. The weapon of seclusion is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. The weapon of wisdom is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are five benefits of hearing the <s>dharma</s>. What five? One hears what has not been heard. One masters what has been heard. One dispels doubt. One straightens one's views. One's mind becomes serene.' 'One hears what has not been heard; one masters what has been heard' — this is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. 'One dispels doubt; one straightens one's views' — this is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. 'One's mind becomes serene' — this is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. And regarding the benefits of hearing the <s>dharma</s> it is also said: 'With the ear one hears the <s>dharma</s>; with speech one recites the <s>dharma</s>' — this is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. 'With the mind one investigates' — this is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. 'Seeing, one fully realizes' — this is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. Among the four factors of stream-entry (<s>śrotaāpatti</s>), 'hearing the true <s>dharma</s>' (<s>saddharmaśravaṇa</s>) is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. 'Proper attention' (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>) is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. 'Practice in accordance with the <s>dharma</s>' (<s>dharmānudharmapratipattiḥ</s>) is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. Among the five doors to liberation (<s>vimuktidvāra</s>), [when] from a teacher or someone in a teacher's position one hears the <s>dharma</s> — this is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. [When] regarding that <s>dharma</s> one experiences its meaning — this is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. That from which joy (<s>pramudya</s>) and so forth arise for him — this is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>.

body.text: api coktaṃ sūtre- bhagavān dharmamupadiśati ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇamante kalyāṇamityādi | taṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoti satpuruṣastaruṇo vṛddho vā | śruttvā pratisañcikṣati- sambādho gṛhāvāso 'bhyavakāśā pravrajyā | nedaṃ su karamagāramadhyāvasatā [ekāntapariśuddhaṃ] saddharmaṃ caritumiti | tadaiva bhogaskandhaṃ prahāya jñātiparivṛttaṃ prahāya agārādanāgāraṃ
body.translated_text: And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) teaches the <s>dharma</s> — beautiful in the beginning, beautiful in the middle, beautiful at the end,' and so forth. A good person, young or old, hears that <s>dharma</s>. Having heard it, he reflects: 'The household life is confined; going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>) is open. It is not easy while living in a household to practice the holy life in its entirety and purity.' Then, relinquishing his mass of possessions and his circle of relatives, he goes forth from the household to homelessness

body.text: pravrajati | śīlaṃ dhatte | indriyāṇi rakṣati | iryāpatheṣu samprajanyakārī bhavati | viviktadeśe cintayati | pañca nīvaraṇāni prahāya prathamadhyānādīnupasampadya viharati | yāvadāsravakṣayamanuprāpnoti | iti | tatra yat dharmaṃ śṛṇoti taruṇo vā vṛddho vā iti | iyaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | śrutvā yat pratisañcikṣati- sambādho gṛhāvāso 'bhyavakāśā pravrajyeti | iyaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | pañca nīvaraṇāni prahāya yāvadāsravakṣayamanuprāpnoti | iyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- dvābhyāṃ pratyayābhyāṃ samyagdṛṣṭirutpadyate | [katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām] | parato dharmaśravaṇaṃ yoniśomanaskāra iti | parato dharmaśravaṇaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | yoniśomanaskāraścintāmayī prajñā | samyagdṛṣṭisamutpādo bhāvanāmayī prajñā | uktañca gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: . He maintains moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>). He guards his sense faculties (<s>indriya</s>). He acts with clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>) in his daily activities. In a secluded place he reflects. Having abandoned the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), he enters upon and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s> and so forth, until he attains the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>). Therein, 'that a good person, young or old, hears the <s>dharma</s>' — this is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. 'Having heard, he reflects: the household life is confined, going forth is open' — this is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. 'Having abandoned the five hindrances, until he attains the destruction of the outflows' — this is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) arises from two conditions. What two? Hearing the <s>dharma</s> from another (<s>parato dharmaśravaṇa</s>) and proper attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>).' 'Hearing the <s>dharma</s> from another' is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. 'Proper attention' is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. 'The arising of right view' is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. And it is said in a verse —

body.text:
niṣevya santaṃ puruṣaṃ saddharmamupaśrutya ca |
viviktadeśābhirataḥ taccittaṃ vinayetpunaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Having attended upon a good person, having heard the true <s>dharma</s>,
delighting in a secluded place, one should tame that mind again.'

body.text: tatra niṣevya santaṃ puruṣaṃ saddharmamupaśrutya cetīyaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | viviktadeśābhirata itīyaṃ cintamayī prajñā | taccittaṃ vinayetpunaritīyaṃ bhāvanāmayī prajñā | kiñca bhagavān bhikṣūnanuśāsti- yatkiñcidbhāṣamāṇairyuṣmābhiścatussatyāni bhāṣayitavyāni | yatkiñciccintayadbhiścatussatyāni cintayitavyāni iti | tatra catussatyabhāṣaṇaṃ śrutamayī prajñā | catussatyacintanaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | catussatyānāṃ lābhaḥ bhāvanāmayī prajñā | evamādinā tatra tatra sūtre bhagavān trividhāṃ prajñāmavocat |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'having attended upon a good person, having heard the true <s>dharma</s>' — this is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. 'Delighting in a secluded place' — this is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. 'One should tame that mind again' — this is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. And further the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructs the monks: 'Whatever you speak of, you should speak of the Four [Noble] Truths. Whatever you reflect upon, you should reflect upon the Four Truths.' Therein, 'speaking of the Four Truths' is <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>. 'Reflecting on the Four Truths' is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. 'The attainment of the Four Truths' is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. By such [methods] and others, in various <s>sūtras</s> the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the threefold <s>prajñā</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) tisṛṣu prajñāsu kati kāmadhātau | kati rūpadhātau | kati ārūpyadhātau bhavanti | (u) kāmadhātau sarvā bhavanti | yathā hastaka upāsako 'tapyaddeveṣūpapadya tatra dharmaṃ deśayati | dharmaṃ deśayan avaśyaṃ tadarthaṃ cintayati | ato jñāyate rūmadhātāvapyasti cintāmayī prajñeti | ārūpyadhātāvasti bhāvanāmayī prajñā | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ kāmadhātau nāsti bhāvanāmayī prajñā | rūpadhātau nāsti cintāmayī prajñeti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Among the three kinds of <s>prajñā</s>, how many exist in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm)? How many in <s>Rūpadhātu</s> (form realm)? How many in <s>Ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm)? (Answer) All [three] exist in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>. Just as the lay follower <s>Hastaka</s>, having died and been reborn among the gods, teaches the <s>dharma</s> there. One who teaches the <s>dharma</s> necessarily reflects on its meaning. Therefore it is known that <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> also exists in <s>Rūpadhātu</s>. In <s>Ārūpyadhātu</s> there is <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. (Question) Some say: 'In <s>Kāmadhātu</s> there is no <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>. In <s>Rūpadhātu</s> there is no <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>.'

body.text: kathamidam | (u) kena pratyayena kāmadhātau nāsti bhāvanāmayī prajñā | (pṛ) na kāmadhātukamārgeṇa sarvāṇi nīvaraṇāni sarvāṇi paryavasthānāni prajahāti yena kāmadhātukaparyavasthānaṃ nābhimukhībhavet | (u) bhavatāṃ śāsane nedaṃ vacanamasti yat na kāmadhātukamārgeṇa nīvaraṇāni paryavasthānāni prajahāti yena kāmadhātukaparyavasthānaṃ nābhimukhībhavediti | āha ca kāmadhātukamārgeṇa kleśāna paribhedayatīti | kimiti | kāmadhātāvasti aśubhādibhāvanā | yathoktaṃ sūtre- aśubhabhāvanāṃ bhāvayan kāmarāgaṃ samūhanti iti | tathā karuṇādāvapi | (pṛ) kāmadhātāvaśubhādibhāvanā nātyantaṃ kleśān samucchedayati | (u) rūpadhātukāśubhādibhāvanāpi nātyantaṃ kleśān samucchindyāt | (pṛ) dauṣṭhulyādyākāraiḥ kleśān prajahāti | nāśubhādinā | (u) dauṣṭhulyādinā kleśān prajahāti nāśubhādinā iti nāsti kiñcana sūtravacanam | uktaṃ hi sūtre- aśubhādinā kleśān samūhanti iti | dauṣṭhulyādīnāṃ kimasti balaṃ kleśānāṃ samucchedakam | [yat] nāstyaśubhādīnām | yadi kāmadhātau dauṣṭhulyādyākāro 'sti | anenākāreṇa kleśān samucchindyāt | yadi nāsti, vaktavyaṃ kāraṇaṃ kasmādasti aśubhādiḥ, na dauṣṭhulyādiriti | yadi sannapi na kleśān samucchedayati | rūpadhātau sannapi na samucchindyāt | atrāpi kāraṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ kasmāt kāmadhātau na samucchedayati | rūpadhātau paraṃ samucchedayatīti |
body.translated_text: How is this? (Answer) For what reason is there no <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s> in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>? (Question) The <s>Kāmadhātu</s>-path does not abandon all hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) and all secondary afflictions (<s>paryavasthāna</s>), such that the <s>Kāmadhātu</s>-secondary afflictions would not arise again. (Answer) In your teaching there is no statement that 'the <s>Kāmadhātu</s>-path does not abandon hindrances and secondary afflictions such that the <s>Kāmadhātu</s>-secondary afflictions would not arise again.' And it is said that 'through the <s>Kāmadhātu</s>-path one breaks through the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).' Why so? Because in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> there exists the cultivation of the contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubhabhāvanā</s>) and so forth. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who cultivates the contemplation of the impure eradicates sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>).' Similarly with the cultivation of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) and so forth. (Question) The contemplation of the impure and so forth in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> does not ultimately uproot the <s>kleśas</s>. (Answer) The contemplation of the impure and so forth in <s>Rūpadhātu</s> also would not ultimately uproot the <s>kleśas</s>. (Question) Through aspects such as coarseness (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) and so forth one abandons the <s>kleśas</s> — not through the contemplation of the impure and so forth. (Answer) That 'one abandons the <s>kleśas</s> through coarseness and so forth, not through the contemplation of the impure and so forth' — there is no such statement in any <s>sūtra</s>. For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Through the contemplation of the impure and so forth one eradicates the <s>kleśas</s>.' What power do [aspects such as] coarseness and so forth have to uproot the <s>kleśas</s> that the contemplation of the impure and so forth do not? If in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> the aspect of coarseness and so forth exists, one should uproot the <s>kleśas</s> through that aspect. If it does not exist, you should state the reason why the contemplation of the impure and so forth exists but not coarseness and so forth. If even though [coarseness] exists it does not uproot the <s>kleśas</s>, then even though it exists in <s>Rūpadhātu</s>, it should not uproot them either. Here too the reason must be stated: why does it not uproot them in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> but uproots them only in <s>Rūpadhātu</s>?

body.text: kāmadhātau sannapi dauṣṭhulyādirna kleśān samucchedayati | asti vikṣepadhātutvāt | vikṣiptacitto na kiñcitsamucchedayati | yayoktaṃ sūtre- cittasamādhānaṃ mārgaḥ cittavikṣepo 'mārga iti | (u) kāraṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ kasmāt kāmadhāturvikṣepadhāturiti | tatrāsti aśubhādibhāvanā yadyayaṃ vikṣepadhātuḥ | kathaṃ kaṅkālādi vilakṣaṇaṃ paśyati | rūpadhātau ca cittasamādhāne
body.translated_text: Even though [the aspect of] coarseness and so forth exists in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>, it does not uproot the <s>kleśas</s>. Why? Because [<s>Kāmadhātu</s>] is a realm of distraction. One with a distracted mind does not uproot anything. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Concentration of mind (<s>cittasamādhāna</s>) is the path; distraction of mind (<s>cittavikṣepa</s>) is not the path.' (Answer) You must state the reason why <s>Kāmadhātu</s> is a realm of distraction. Since the contemplation of the impure and so forth exists there — if it is a realm of distraction, how does one see the distinctive [meditation objects] such as skeletons (<s>kaṅkāla</s>) and so forth? And in <s>Rūpadhātu</s>, in the concentration of the mind

body.text: kasya vailakṣaṇyamasti | kāmadhāto tu nāsti | (pṛ) rūpadhātukamārgeṇa vairāgyamanuprāpya tadantarā mriyamāṇo rūpadhātāvutpadyate | yathā āṇirāṇiṃ nissārayati | (u) kiṃ nāma vairāgyam | (pṛ) kleśaprahāṇaṃ vairāgyam | rūpadhātukarmārgeṇa kleśān prajahāti | na kāmadhātukena | (u) tīrthikāḥ prahīṇasaṃyojanā api punaḥ kāmadhātau samutpadyante | ataḥ [te] prākṛtā na prahīṇasaṃyojanā ityucyante | yadi [saṃyojanāni] prahāya punarutpadyate | tadā anāsravaḥ kṣīṇasaṃyojano 'pi punarutpadyeta | tattu na sambhavati |
body.translated_text: , of what is there a distinctive vision? But not in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>. (Question) Through the path of <s>Rūpadhātu</s>, having attained dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), one who dies in the interim is reborn in <s>Rūpadhātu</s>. Just as one nail drives out another nail. (Answer) What is this dispassion? (Question) The abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> is dispassion. Through the <s>Rūpadhātu</s>-path one abandons the <s>kleśas</s> — not through the <s>Kāmadhātu</s>-path. (Answer) The non-Buddhist practitioners (<s>tīrthikas</s>), even though they have abandoned the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), are again reborn in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>. Therefore they are called 'ordinary' (<s>prākṛta</s>), not 'ones who have abandoned the fetters.' If having abandoned [the fetters] one is reborn again, then even an outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) being whose fetters are destroyed would be reborn again. But that is impossible.

body.text: api coktaṃ sūtre- kṣīṇatrisaṃyojanastrīṇi viṣāṇi samūhantīti | prākṛto na trīṇi saṃyojanāni kṣapayatītyato na vītarāgo bhavati | prākṛtasya nityamasti ātmadṛṣṭiḥ | yataḥ sa na satkāyadṛṣṭyādīn kṣapayati | yadi prākato vairāgyakuśalaḥ, sarve 'pi kleśā na syuḥ | kasmāt | sarve hi kleśāḥ pratītyasiddhāḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- pratyayebhya ātmā sidhyatīti | yadi pṛthagjanasyāsya kāmadhātukapañcaskandheṣu satkāyadṛṣṭirnodbhavati | ūrdhvadhātukaskandheṣu punarna bhavet | tadā tu pṛthagjanasya na satkāyadṛṣṭirbhavet | ityastīdṛśo doṣaḥ | evaṃ kleśairatyantakṣīṇairbhavitavyam | pṛthagjano 'yamarhan syāt | vastutastu [tasya] kleśā naikāntaṃ kṣīṇāḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dvāvimau bhikṣavaḥ aśanyā phalantyā na santrasataḥ | [katamau dvau] bhikṣuśca kṣīṇāsravo rājā ca cakravartī iti | idānīmayaṃ pṛthagjano 'pi na santraset | arhan nābhinandati jīvitaṃ, nābhisantrasati maraṇam | ayaṃ [pṛthagjano] 'pi evaṃ syāt | yathā upaseno 'rhan āśīviṣadaṣṭo jīvitānte 'virūpendriyo 'vikṛtarūpaśca babhūva | tathāyamapi syāt | arhato 'ṣṭau lokadharmā na cittamavapātayanti |
body.translated_text: And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who has destroyed the three fetters eradicates the three poisons.' An ordinary person does not destroy the three fetters; therefore he does not become dispassionate. An ordinary person always has the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>). Since he does not destroy the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and so forth, if an ordinary person were skilled in dispassion, then all <s>kleśas</s> would cease to exist. Why? Because all <s>kleśas</s> are established dependently. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The self is established through conditions.' If for this ordinary person the view of the existing body does not arise regarding the five <s>skandhas</s> of <s>Kāmadhātu</s>, then it would also not arise regarding the <s>skandhas</s> of the higher realms. In that case, the ordinary person would have no view of the existing body — and there is such a fault. Thus the <s>kleśas</s> would be completely destroyed, and this ordinary person would be an <s>arhat</s>. But in reality, his <s>kleśas</s> are not completely destroyed. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Monks, there are these two who do not tremble when the thunderbolt strikes: a monk whose outflows are destroyed (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>), and a wheel-turning monarch (<s>cakravartī</s>).' Now this ordinary person too would not tremble. An <s>arhat</s> does not delight in life nor tremble at death. This [ordinary person] too would be the same. Just as the <s>arhat</s> <s>Upasena</s>, bitten by a venomous snake at the end of his life, had undistorted faculties and unchanged appearance — so too would this [ordinary person] be. The eight worldly conditions (<s>lokadharmā</s>) do not cast down the mind of an <s>arhat</s>

body.text: tathā syādayamapi | vītarāgatvāt | vastutastu pṛthagjanasya vītarāga iti kathyamānasyāpi nedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ syāt | ato jñāyate na kṣīṇakleśo ['ya]miti |
body.translated_text: . So too would it be for this [ordinary person], on account of being dispassionate. But in reality, for an ordinary person who is said to be 'dispassionate,' these characteristics would not apply. Therefore it is known that he has not destroyed the <s>kleśas</s>.

body.text: (pṛ) pṛthagjanaḥ saṃyojanāni prahāya atrāyuṣo 'nte rūpadhātāvutpadyate | yadi saṃyojanāni na prajahāti | kathaṃ tatrotpadyeta | sūtre 'pyuktam- asti vītarāgastīrthika iti | āha ca arāḍaḥ kalāma udrako rāmaputro rūpe vītarāga ārūpya utpadyata iti | kiñcāha- rūpeṇa kāmaṃ vijahāti | arūpeṇa rūpaṃ vijahāti | nirodhena smṛtyupasthānāni vijahātīti | ato [yat]bhavatoktaṃ pṛthagjanaḥ kṣīṇakleśo 'pi punarutpadyata ityato na kṣīṇa[kleśa] iti | tanna yujyate | bhavānapyāha- pṛthagjanasya sarvāṇi vidyamānāni prahīṇānīti idaṃ vastutaḥ pratiṣiddhamityataḥ kṣīṇo vīta ityucyate | yathoktaṃ gāthāyām-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] An ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), having abandoned the fetters (<s>saṃyojanas</s>), is reborn in the form-realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) at the end of his lifespan here. If he does not abandon the fetters, how would he be reborn there? And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There exists a non-Buddhist ascetic (<s>tīrthika</s>) who is free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>).' And it is said that <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s> and <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s> were free from passion regarding form and were reborn in the formless [realm]. And further it is said: 'Through form, one abandons sensual desire; through formlessness, one abandons form; through cessation, one abandons the foundations of mindfulness.' Therefore, your statement that 'an ordinary person, even if his afflictions are exhausted, is reborn again, and therefore his [afflictions] are not exhausted' — that is untenable. You yourself also say: 'All [afflictions] that are present in an ordinary person are [said to be] abandoned' — since this is actually contradicted, [the affliction] is called 'exhausted' or 'departed.' As stated in the verse —

body.text: ahaṃ mameti yā cintā mriyamāṇo jahāti tām
body.translated_text: The thought 'I' and 'mine' — one who is dying abandons it.

body.text: ayameva vītarāgo nāma | tīrthikānāṃ prahāṇantu maraṇaprahāṇādanyat | maraṇaprahīṇo na rūpārūpyadhātāvutpadyate | yo bālaḥ svabhūmiṃ tyajati taṃ satkṛtavatāmapi nāsti mahāvipākaḥ | yadi vītarāgaṃ tīrthikaṃ satkaroti, mahāvipākaṃ vindate | vacane samāne 'pi tadarthastu vibhinnaḥ | ato jñāyate pṛthagjano vastutaḥ prahīṇa[kleśo] vīta[rāga] iti |
body.translated_text: This alone is called 'free from passion.' But the abandonment of the non-Buddhist ascetics is different from abandonment at death. One whose [afflictions] are abandoned at death is not reborn in the form or formless realm. One who is a fool and abandons his own plane — even for those who honor him, there is no great result of [his] <s>karma</s>. But if one honors a non-Buddhist ascetic who is free from passion, one obtains a great karmic result. Though the statement is the same, its meaning is different. Therefore it is known that an ordinary person has truly abandoned [the afflictions] and is free from passion.

body.text: (u) pratiṣedhe 'sti pravibhāgaḥ | yadi gabhīrakleśavyāvartakaḥ tadā rūpārūpadhātāvutpadyate | yadi satkāyadṛṣṭiṃ vyāvṛttavān tadā pūrvokto doṣaḥ | yadi kāmadhātukasatkāyadṛṣṭiṃ na vyāvṛttavān | kathaṃ rūṇarūpyadhātāvutpadyate | vyāvṛttarāgapratighamātrasya rūpadhātāvutpādaḥ | na vyāvṛttasatkāyadṛṣṭikasya | ataḥ pṛthagjano na vastutaḥ prahīṇasaṃyojana iti jñāyate | kāmadhātukasaddharmo 'pi kleśavyāvartako 'sti | ato jñāyate kāmadhātāvapi bhāvanāmayī prajñāstīti | sūtre 'pyuktam- saptaniścayānatikramya sambodhiṃ vindata iti | ato jñāyate kāmadhātuniśritaḥ samādhistattvajñānajanaka iti |
body.translated_text: [Response:] There is a distinction in the negation. If [the abandonment] removes deep afflictions, then one is reborn in the form or formless realm. If one has turned away from the view of self-identity (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), then the previously stated fault [applies]. If one has not turned away from the <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> of the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), how is one reborn in the form or formless realm? One who has merely turned away from passion and aversion is reborn in the form-realm — not one who has turned away from the view of self-identity. Therefore it is known that an ordinary person has not truly abandoned the fetters. Even wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of the desire-realm can turn away afflictions. Therefore it is known that there exists cultivation-born <s>prajñā</s> (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>) even in the desire-realm. And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Having transcended the seven stages of certainty, one attains awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>).' Therefore it is known that concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) based in the desire-realm generates knowledge of reality.

body.text: (pṛ) pugdalo 'yaṃ prathamadhyānasyāsannabhūmiṃ niścityārhanmārgamanuprāpnoti | na kāmadhātukasamādhim | (u) na yuktam | atikramya saptaniśrayāniti vacanena prathamadhyānaṃ tadāsannabhūmiścātikrāntaiva | na tatrāsti kāraṇamāsannabhūmiṃ niśrayate na kāmadhātukasamādhimiti | yadyayaṃ yogī āsannabhūmimupasannaḥ | kasmānna prathamadhyānamupasampadyate | asyāpi nāsti kāraṇam | susīmasūtre coktam- pūrvaṃ khalu dharmasthitijñānaṃ pañcānnirvāṇajñānamiti | asyārthaḥ nāvaśyaṃ dhyānasamādhiprāptipūrvaka āsravakṣayaḥ | kintu dharmasthitijñānamavaśyaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛtvā paścādāsravakṣayo bhavatīti | ato jñāyate sarvān dhyānasamādhīnatikrāmatīti | dhyānasamādhisamatikramāya sūsīmasūtramāha | yadyāsannabhūmiṃ vedayate | sa eva dhyānasamānadoṣaḥ | sūtre cāsannabhūmiriti vacanaṃ nāsti | svasaṃjñānusmaraṇavikalpo 'yam |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] This individual, having ascertained the proximate ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), attains the path of an <s>Arhat</s>. Not through desire-realm concentration. [Response:] This is not tenable. By the statement 'having transcended the seven supports,' the first <s>dhyāna</s>, its proximate ground,

body.text: (pṛ) pūrvamukto mayā āṇidṛṣṭāntaḥ | ato jñāyate anyabhūmikamārgeṇānyabhūmikasaṃyojanaṃ prajahātīti | yathā sūkṣmayāṇyā sthūlāṇiṃ nissārayati | evaṃ rūpadhātukamārgeṇa kāmadhātuṃ prajahāti | yogī yadi pūrvaṃ kāmamakuśaladharmāṃśca prajahāti | taduttaraṃ prathamadhyāne 'vatarati | ato jñāyate 'vaśyamastyāsannabhūmiḥ yayā kāmaṃ prajahāti | āha ca- rūpamupādāya kāmamatikrāmatīti | yadi nāstyāsannabhūmiḥ | kathaṃ rūpamupādadyāt | uktañca sūtre- yogī śubhaṃ pratilabhamāno 'śubhaṃ tyajati tadyathā nandaḥ apsaratṛṣṇāmupādāya pūrvatanakāmaṃ jahau iti | yaśca prathamadhyāne nopaśamarasamanuvindate, na sa pañcakāmaguṇeṣu mahāvadyamatiṃ karoti | ato jñāyate pūrvaṃ prathamadhyānasyāsannabhūmimanuprāpya kāmadhātumutsṛjatīti |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] I previously stated the simile of the peg. Therefore it is known that through the path of another plane, one abandons the fetters of another plane. Just as one drives out a thick peg with a thin one, so through the path of the form-realm, one abandons [the fetters of] the desire-realm.

body.text: ucyate | kāmadhātau śubhamanuprāpyāśubhaṃ prajahati | tadyathāha- pañcanissaraṇasvabhāvā iti | yadyāryaśrāvakaḥ kadācit pañcakāmaguṇā na prītisaumanasyajanakā ityanusmarati | tadā taccittaṃ nābhiramate sirāpakṣadāhavat | yadi [te] nissaraṇadharmā ityanusmarati | tadā cittamabhiramate | āha ca- yogino yadākuśalavitarko bhavati | tadā kuśalavitarkeṇa taṃ nirodhayati | tasmādbhavadukta āṇidṛṣṭānto 'pi kāmadhātau sambhavati | yat bhavānāha-
body.translated_text: It is said: In the desire-realm, having attained the wholesome, one abandons the unwholesome. As [the <s>sūtra</s>] states: 'Of the nature of five escapes.' If a noble disciple sometimes recollects that the five strands of sensual pleasure do not produce delight and mental happiness, then

body.text: rūpamupādāya kāmamatikrāmatīti | idaṃ caramabhavikam | yogī yadi kāmadhātukamārgeṇa kleśān prajahāti | tadanukramaśo yāvadrūpadhātukakuśaladharmān pratilabhate | tasmin samaye kāmadhātoratyantaprahāṇaṃ nāma rūpadhātukadharmapratilābhaḥ | bhavānāha- nirodhasamāpattiṃ pratilabhata iti | arhannapi samādhīn pratilabhate | kintu taccaramabhavikamityucyate | yadbhavatoktaṃ- śubhaṃ praṇītaṃ pramodamupaśamarasañca pratilabhamāna iti | tatsarvaṃ sāmānyataḥ pratyuktam |
body.translated_text: — depending on form, one transcends sensual desire. This [pertains to] one in his final existence. If a <s>yogin</s> abandons afflictions through the path of the desire-realm, then progressively, up to the point of obtaining wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of the form-realm, at that time

body.text: yadi ca kāmadhātau nāsti samādhiḥ | kathaṃ vyagracittena rūpadhātukakuśalaṃ sākṣātkaroti | (pṛ) prajñāvimuktasyārhato nāsti samādhiḥ | prajñā paramasti | (u) tatra dhyānasamādhimātrasya niṣedhaḥ | avaśyaṃ bhavitavyamalpakālaṃ samāhitacittena yāvadekaṃ kṣaṇam | yathā sūtre bhagavānāha- bhikṣūṇāṃ cīvaraṃ gṛhṇatāṃ triṣu [kleśa] viṣeṣu satsvapi cīvarāsaṅgo niruddha eveti | vyagracittasya tattvajñānamutpadyata iti na kiñcitsūtramāha | sarvathāha- samāhito yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti ||
body.translated_text: And if there is no concentration in the desire-realm, how could one with a distracted mind directly realize the wholesome [<s>dharmas</s>] of the form-realm?
