[Objection:] For an <s>Arhat</s> liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>), there is no concentration; wisdom alone is supreme. [Response:] There, the <s>dhyāna</s>-concentration

body.text: trividhaprajñāvargaścaturvanavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter 194: The Section on the Three Types of <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom)

body.text: 195 catuḥ pratisaṃvidvargaḥ
body.translated_text: Chapter 195: The Section on the Four Analytical Knowledges (<s>Pratisaṃvid</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) asti dharmasthiteḥ pratyāsannaṃ laukikaṃ jñānam | katamadidam | (u) idaṃ ūṣmādidharme prajñaptividārakaṃ jñānam | jñānamidaṃ sāṃvṛtasatyadarśana[rūpa]tvāt laukikam | āryamārgasya pratyāsannatvāt dharmasthiteḥ pratyāsannamityucyate | (pṛ) idaṃ satyadarśanamārge anāgatabhāvanādīnāṃ jñānam | (u) anāgatabhāvanādīnāṃ jñānaṃ nāstīti paścādvakṣyate | kasmāt | dharmalakṣaṇavidāraṇe hi nāsti prajñapticittam | ataḥ satyadarśanamārge na laukikaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvayati |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Is there worldly knowledge that is proximate to the establishment of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthiti</s>)? What is it? [Response:] This is the knowledge in the warmth (<s>ūṣman</s>) and other stages that destroys conventional designation (<s>prajñaptividāraka</s>). This knowledge is worldly because it has the character of seeing conventional truth (<s>sāṃvṛtasatya</s>). The noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>)

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- catasraḥ pratisaṃvida iti | katamā imāḥ | (u) akṣareṣu,
body.translated_text: [Objection:] It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>).' What are these? [Response:] In syllables/words,

body.text: yā pratisaṃvit | iyaṃ dharmapratisaṃvit | ruteṣu pratisaṃvit niruktipratisaṃvit | yaduta [nānā]digantaravyavahṛtarutaviśeṣa[jñāna]m | yathoktaṃ sūtre- janapadaniruktau nābhiniveśeta yogī iti | rutasyāprayoge 'rtho duradhigamaḥ | akṣarābhāve 'rtho na prakāśyo bhavati | iyameva niruktirakuṇṭhā akṣayā asandigdhaṃ subhāṣitamityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- santi catvāro bhāṣitadharmāḥ kiñcidbhāṣitaṃ sārthagati nākṣayakaram | kiñcidakṣayakaraṃ na sārthagati | kiñcidubhayavat iti | kiñcinnobhayavat iti | idaṃ trividhaṃ jñānaṃ niruktyupāyaḥ | nāmapadajñāne yadarthapratisaṃvedanam, iyamarthapratisaṃvit | yathāha- santi catvāro bhāṣitadharmāḥ kaścidarthopāyaḥ na vyañjanopāyaḥ | kaścidvayañjanopāyo nārthopāyaḥ | kaścidubhayopāyaḥ | kaścinnobhayopāyaḥ | ya etaccatuḥpratisaṃvitprāptaḥ sa upāyasampanno duṣpradhṛṣyo duradhigamyo dharmabhāṣaṇe | [tasya] subhāṣitamakṣaya[kara]mapi sārthagati | prajñānavasannā vacananiruktiścā pratihatā bhavati |
body.translated_text: — that analytical knowledge is the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>). The analytical knowledge in sounds/expressions is the analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>) — namely, knowledge of the particular expressions used in the speech of various regions and directions. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One should not insist on local expressions (<s>janapadaniruktau nābhiniveśa</s>).'

body.text: (pṛ) pratisaṃvidiyaṃ kathaṃ pratilabdhavyā bhavati | (u) pūrvādhvanīnakarmapratyayāt | yadi pratyadhva prajñāpratyayaṃ skandhādyupāyañca samyagbhāvayati | tadā tadbhāvanābalādihaivādhvani aśikṣitākṣarasūtrādhyayano 'pi [tatra] jñānaṃ vindate | yathā divyacakṣurabhijñādiṣu | (pṛ) katamaḥ pudgalaḥ pratilabhate | (u) āryapudgala eva pratilabhate | kecidāhuḥ- arhanneva
body.translated_text: [Objection:] How are these analytical knowledges to be obtained? [Response:] Through the condition of <s>karma</s> from past lives. If one properly cultivates in the present life the conditions of <s>prajñā</s> and the means [such as] the aggregates and so forth, then by the power of that cultivation, one obtains [them] here in this very [life].

body.text: pratilabhate | na śaikṣajanā iti | nāyaṃ tathā niyamaḥ | śaikṣā api aṣṭavimokṣān vindate | kasmānna pratilabhanta idaṃ jñānam |
body.translated_text: — not [only] learners (<s>śaikṣas</s>).' This restriction does not hold. Learners too attain the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>). Why would they not obtain this knowledge?

body.text: (pṛ) catasra imāḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ kasmin dhātau vartante | (u) kāmadhātau rūpadhātau ca sarvā bhavanti | ārūpyadhātau kevalamarthapratisaṃvidasti | pratisaṃvid dvividhā bhavati sāsravā anāsraveti | śaikṣāṇāṃ dvividhā ca bhavati | aśaikṣāṇāṃ kevalamanāsravā | pratilābhe tu sarvā yugapadvindate | striyo 'pi pratilabhante yathā dharmadinnādayo bhikṣuṇyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Objection:] In which realm do these four analytical knowledges operate? [Response:] In the desire-realm and the form-realm, all [four] exist. In the formless realm, only the analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>) exists. The analytical knowledges are of two kinds — with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) and

body.text: catuḥpratisaṃvidvargaḥ pañcanavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter 195: The Section on the Four Analytical Knowledges

body.text: 196 pañcajñānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: Chapter 196: The Section on the Five Knowledges

body.text: pañca jñānāni- dharmasthitijñānaṃ, nirvāṇajñānaṃ araṇājñānaṃ praṇidhijñānaṃ prāntakoṭikajñānamiti | tatra dharmāṇāmutpādajñānaṃ dharmasthitijñānam | yathā jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ yāvadavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā iti | asti vā tathāgato nāsti vā tathāgataḥ | eṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ sadā sthita ityato dharmasthitijñānamityucyate | eṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodho nirvāṇajñānam | yathā jātinirodhe jarāmaraṇanirodhaḥ | yāvadavidyānirodhe saṃskāranirodha iti |
body.translated_text: The five knowledges are: knowledge of the establishment of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthitijñāna</s>), knowledge of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>nirvāṇajñāna</s>), knowledge of non-enmity (<s>araṇājñāna</s>), knowledge of resolve (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), and knowledge of the ultimate limit (<s>prāntakoṭikajñāna</s>). Among these, knowledge of the arising of <s>dharmas</s> is knowledge of the establishment of <s>dharma</s>. Just as birth is the condition for old age and death —

body.text: (pṛ) tathā cet nirvāṇajñānamapi dharmasthitijñānaṃ bhavati | kasmāt | yataḥ asti vā tathāgato nāsti vā tathāgataḥ | asya svabhāvo 'pi sadā sthitaḥ | (u) dharmāṇāṃ kṣayanirodho nirvāṇamityākhyāyate | asmin kṣayanirodhe ko dharmaḥ sthitaḥ | (pṛ) nirvāṇaṃ kimadravyamasat | (u) skandhānāmaśeṣanirodho nirvāṇamiti kīrtyate | tatra kimasti [avaśiṣṭam] | (pṛ) dravyasat nirvāṇam | tat kena jñāyate | nirodhasatyaṃ hi nirvāṇam | duḥkhādīnāṃ satyānāṃ vastusattvāt nirvāṇamapi vastusat | kiñca nirvāṇasya jñānaṃ nirodhajñānaṃ bhavati | yadyasan dharmaḥ | kasya dharmasya jñānamutpadyate | sūtre ca bhagavānavocat- asti, bhikṣavaḥ kṛtako jāto bhūtaḥ saṃskṛtadharmaḥ | asti
body.translated_text: (Question) If so, the knowledge of <s>nirvāṇa</s> too would be knowledge of the stability of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthitijñāna</s>). Why? Because 'whether the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists or does not exist, the intrinsic nature of this [<s>dharma</s>] is always established.' (Answer) The complete exhaustion and cessation of <s>dharmas</s> is called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>.' In this exhaustion and cessation, what <s>dharma</s> is established? (Question) Is <s>nirvāṇa</s> without substance, non-existent? (Answer) The complete cessation without remainder of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) is called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>.' What then remains there? (Question) <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is a real substance (<s>dravyasat</s>). By what is this known? For <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>). Since the truths such as suffering are real entities (<s>vastusat</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s> too is a real entity. Moreover, the knowledge of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>). If it were a non-existent <s>dharma</s>, regarding what <s>dharma</s> would knowledge arise? And in the <s>sūtra</s> the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There is, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the made, the born, the become, the conditioned <s>dharma</s>. There is

body.text: [bhikṣavaḥ] akṛtako 'jāto 'bhūto 'saṃskṛtadharma iti | api coktam- santi dvidhaiva dharmāḥ saṃskṛto 'saṃskṛta iti | saṃskṛtadharma iti utpādasthitivyayavikṛtaḥ | asaṃskṛta anutpādasthitivyayavikṛtaḥ | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- ye vidyante saṃskṛtā vā asaṃskṛtā vā nirodho nirvāṇaṃ teṣāmagramākhyāyate iti | āha ca- rūpamanityam | rūpanirodhe nirvāṇaṃ nityam | evaṃ yāvadvijñānamapi | sūtre coktam- nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavya iti | yadyasan dharmaḥ | katamaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ | bhagavān bahudhātukasūtra āha- vidvān saṃskṛtadhātumasaṃskṛtādhātuñca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | iti | yo 'saṃskṛtadhātuḥ tadeva nirvāṇam | yathābhūtajñātaṃ kathamabhāva ityucyate | sarveṣu sūtreṣu nāsti kiñcinniyataṃ vacanaṃ nirvāṇamasaddharma iti | ato jñāyate yannirvāṇamasaditi tat bhavataḥ svasaṃjñāvikalpa eveti |
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the unmade, the unborn, the unbecome, the unconditioned <s>dharma</s>.' And moreover it is said: 'There are just two kinds of <s>dharmas</s> — conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). A conditioned <s>dharma</s> is characterized by arising, persisting, and perishing. The unconditioned is characterized by non-arising, non-persisting, and non-perishing.' And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Among whatever exists, whether conditioned or unconditioned, cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is declared the foremost among them.' And he said: 'Form is impermanent. In the cessation of form, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is permanent. So too up to consciousness.' And in the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'Cessation is to be directly realized (<s>sākṣātkartavya</s>).' If it were a non-existent <s>dharma</s>, what would be that which is to be directly realized? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said in the <s>Bahudhātuka Sūtra</s>: 'The wise one knows as it truly is both the conditioned element (<s>saṃskṛtadhātu</s>) and the unconditioned element (<s>asaṃskṛtadhātu</s>).' The unconditioned element is precisely <s>nirvāṇa</s>. How can what is known as it truly is be called 'non-existent'? In all the <s>sūtras</s> there is no definite statement that '<s>nirvāṇa</s> is a non-existent <s>dharma</s>.' From this it is known that the [claim] that '<s>nirvāṇa</s> is non-existent' is merely your own conceptual elaboration of convention (<s>saṃjñāvikalpa</s>).

body.text: ucyate | yadi skandhānāṃ viyoge 'pi punarasti dharmāntaraṃ nirvāṇamiti | tadā dharmāṇāmaśeṣanirodho nirvāṇamiti na syāt | yadi nirvāṇaṃ sat | tadā vaktavyaḥ asti svabhāvaḥ ko 'yamiti | nirvāṇālambanaḥ samādhiranimitta ityākhyāyate | yadi dharmalakṣaṇamapi sajīvam | kimasallakṣaṇaṃ bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yogī rūpalakṣaṇaṃ prahīṇaṃ paśyati yāvaddharmalakṣaṇaṃ prahīṇaṃ paśyati iti | sūtre ca tatra tatroktam- sarve dharmā anityāḥ sarve dharmā anātmānaḥ | teṣāṃ vyupaśamo nirvāṇamiti | tatrātmā sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaḥ | yat sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvādarśanam | tadā anātmadarśanaṃ bhavati | yadi nirvāṇaṃ dharmaḥ tadā nāsti svabhāva iti darśanaṃ nopalabdhuṃ śakyate | asya dharmasya nirodhābhāvāt | yathā yatra ghaṭo 'sti | na tatra ghaṭasya vināśadharmo 'sti | ghaṭe vinaṣṭe tu ghaṭo vinaṣṭa iti vaktuṃ śakyate | vṛkṣacchede 'pyevam | evaṃ saṃskārā athāpi vartante | tadā na nirvāṇamityākhyāyate | saṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhe tu nirvāṇamityākhyā bhavati |
body.translated_text: It is replied: If, even in the separation from the aggregates, there is yet another distinct <s>dharma</s> called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>' — then the statement 'the complete cessation without remainder of <s>dharmas</s> is <s>nirvāṇa</s>' would not hold. If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is existent, then its intrinsic nature must be stated — 'What is this?' The <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that takes <s>nirvāṇa</s> as its object is called '<s>animitta</s>' (signless). If even the characteristic of a <s>dharma</s> were alive [i.e. real], how could it have the characteristic of signlessness? As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>yogī</s> sees the characteristic of form as abandoned, up to the characteristic of <s>dharma</s> as abandoned.' And in the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated everywhere: 'All conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are impermanent; all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self. Their complete pacification is <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' Therein, 'self' (<s>ātman</s>) means the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. When there is the non-seeing of the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, then there is the seeing of non-self (<s>anātman</s>). If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is a [real] <s>dharma</s>, then the seeing of 'there is no intrinsic nature' cannot be obtained — because of the non-cessation of this <s>dharma</s>. Just as where a pot exists, the characteristic of the destruction of the pot does not exist. But when the pot is destroyed, one can say 'the pot is destroyed.' Similarly with the felling of a tree. Thus as long as conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) still persist, it is not called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>.' But upon the cessation of conditioned things, the designation '<s>nirvāṇa</s>' applies.

body.text: duḥkhanirodhaśca na punardharmāntaraṃ bhavati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yadidaṃ bhikṣavo duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate anyadduḥkhaṃ notpadyate na punastatsantatirasti | idaṃ sthānaṃ paramaṃ śāntaṃ śiva yaduta
body.translated_text: And the cessation of suffering is not itself another distinct <s>dharma</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s>, when this suffering ceases, other suffering does not arise — nor is there any further continuity of it. This state is supremely peaceful, auspicious — namely,

body.text: sarvapratinissargaḥ kāyikacaitasikarāgātyantavisaṃyogo nirodho nirvāṇamiti | tatredaṃ duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate | anyaddaḥkhaṃ notpadyata iti vacane ko dharmo nirvāṇādanyo bhavati | nāpyasti punaḥ pṛthak kṣayadharmaḥ | utpannamātrā tṛṣṇā nirudhyate, ajātā na jāyate | tasmin samaye kṣayo nāma | ko dharmaḥ punarasti kṣaya ityabhidhīyamānaḥ | dravyato nābhidhātuṃ śakyate |
body.translated_text: the complete relinquishment of all, the utter separation from bodily and mental passion, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' In the statement 'when this suffering ceases, other suffering does not arise' — what <s>dharma</s> is there apart from <s>nirvāṇa</s>? Nor is there a separate <s>dharma</s> of destruction. The moment craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) arises, it ceases; when unborn, it does not arise. At that time it is called 'destruction' (<s>kṣaya</s>). What <s>dharma</s> is there further that is designated as 'destruction'? It cannot be designated as a real substance (<s>dravyatas</s>).

body.text: atha sattā dharmasya nāmāntaram | pañcaskandhānāmabhāvo nirvāṇamityucyate | tatrābhāvo vidyamānaḥ san sattetyucyeta | itīdantu na sambhavati | aśeṣanirodhe nirvāṇamityabhidhīyate | tadyathā cīvarakṣayaḥ punarna dharmāntaramasti | tathā no cet cīvarakṣayādirapi pṛthak dharmaḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: Now, 'existence' (<s>sattā</s>) is another name for <s>dharma</s>. The non-existence of the five aggregates is called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>.' Therein, if non-existence were something that exists, it would be called 'existent.' But this is not possible. In the complete cessation without remainder, '<s>nirvāṇa</s>' is designated. Just as the destruction of a robe is not itself another distinct <s>dharma</s> — so too. If that were not so, then even the destruction of a robe and the like would be a separate <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: bhavānavocat- asti nirodhajñānamiti | tadapyabādhitam | tadyathā vṛkṣacchedādau [vṛkṣaccheda]jñānamutpadyate | na cāsti pṛthak chedadharmaḥ | saṃskāravaśāttatra jñānamutpadyate | yat sarvasaṃskārāṇāmabhāvaḥ | [tat] nirvāṇaṃ bhavati | yathā yatra yannāsti tatra tena śūnyamiti jñānam | (pṛ) kimidānīṃ nāsti nirvāṇam | (u) na nāsti nirvāṇamiti | kintu nāsti dravyadharma[rūpam] | yadi nāsti nirvāṇam | tadā sadā sarvatra jātimaraṇamasti | na kadācinmokṣasamayaḥ | yathā asti ghaṭabhaṅgaḥ vṛkṣasamucchedaḥ | paraṃ tu nāsti dravyato dharmāntaramastīti | [anena] anyasatyādivacanamapi pratyuktam | kasmāt | asti duḥkhanirodha ityato 'styajāto 'bhūto 'kṛtako 'saṃskṛta ityādivacanaṃ sarvamapratihatam |
body.translated_text: You have said: 'There is the knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>).' That too is not refuted. Just as from the felling of a tree and so forth, the knowledge of 'tree-felling' arises — yet there is no separate <s>dharma</s> of felling. Knowledge arises there through the force of conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>). That which is the non-existence of all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — that is <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Just as where something does not exist, the knowledge 'it is empty of that' arises. (Question) Then is <s>nirvāṇa</s> now non-existent? (Answer) It is not that <s>nirvāṇa</s> does not exist. Rather, it does not exist as a substantial <s>dharma</s>. If <s>nirvāṇa</s> did not exist, then always and everywhere there would be birth and death; there would never be a time of liberation. Just as there is the breaking of a pot and the uprooting of a tree — but there is no further separate substantial <s>dharma</s>. By this, the statements about 'other truths' and so forth are also answered. Why? Because [the statement] 'there is the cessation of suffering' — therefore 'there is the unborn, the unbecome, the unmade, the unconditioned' and other such statements are all unobstructed.

body.text: araṇājñānamiti | yena jñānena na raṇāyate pareṇa saha | idamaraṇā [jñāna]m |
body.translated_text: '<s>Araṇājñāna</s>' (knowledge without conflict) means: the knowledge by which one does not engage in conflict with another — this is <s>araṇājñāna</s>.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- maitrīcittamidamiti | maitrīcittānna sattvānupahanti | anye kecidāhuḥ- śūnyatāvihāro 'yamiti | anena śūnyatāvihāreṇa na vastunā raṇāyate | kecidvadantinirvāṇābhirucicittamidamiti | nirvāṇābhirucyā hi na raṇāspadamasti | kecidvadanti- caturthadhyānagataṃ [kiñcidida]miti | nedaṃ niyamena tathā | etajjñānabhāvitacittasyārhato nāsti [raṇāspadaṃ] kiñcit |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'This is the mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrīcitta</s>).' Through the mind of loving-kindness one does not harm beings. Others say: 'This is the abiding in emptiness (<s>śūnyatāvihāra</s>).' Through this abiding in emptiness one does not engage in conflict with real entities. Some say: 'This is the mind delighting in <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>nirvāṇābhiruci</s>).' Through the delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, there is no ground for conflict. Some say: 'This is something pertaining to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).' But this is not necessarily so. For an <s>arhat</s> whose mind has been cultivated by this knowledge, there is no ground for conflict whatsoever.

body.text: praṇidhijñānamiti | dharmeṣu apratihataṃ praṇidhijñānamityucyate | (pṛ) tathā cet bhagavato buddhasya kevalamidaṃ jñānaṃ syāt | (u) evameva | buddho bhagavānevaitajjñānasampannaḥ | anye [ta]dbalādhiṣṭhitā apratihata[jñānaṃ] vindante |
body.translated_text: '<s>Praṇidhijñāna</s>' (knowledge of resolve/aspiration) means: the unobstructed resolve-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>) regarding <s>dharmas</s> is so called. (Question) If so, this knowledge would belong solely to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. (Answer) Exactly so. Only the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, is endowed with this knowledge. Others, empowered by his power (<s>balādhiṣṭhita</s>), obtain unobstructed knowledge.

body.text: prāntakoṭikajñānamiti | yat yogī prakṛṣṭamuttamaṃ jñānaṃ sarvadhyānasamādhibhiḥ paribhāvitaṃ parivardhitaṃ pratilabhya [sva]jīvitasya bṛddhau hrāse vaśitāṃ vindate | idaṃ prāntakoṭikajñānamityucyate ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Prāntakoṭikajñāna</s>' (knowledge at the final limit) means: the <s>yogī</s>, having obtained the most excellent and supreme knowledge, cultivated and developed through all <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), obtains mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) over the increase and decrease of his own life-span. This is called '<s>prāntakoṭikajñāna</s>' (knowledge at the final limit).

body.text: pañcajñānavargaḥ ṣaṇṇavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The Chapter on the Five Knowledges (<s>pañcajñānavarga</s>), the one hundred and ninety-sixth.

body.text: 197 ṣaḍabhijñājñānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 197. The Chapter on the Knowledge of the Six Supernatural Powers (<s>ṣaḍabhijñājñānavarga</s>).

body.text: asti ṣaḍabhijñājñānam | ṣaḍabhijñāḥ- kāyarddhiḥ dviyacakṣuḥ divyaśrotraṃ paracittajñānaṃ pūrvanivāsānusmṛtirāsravakṣaya[jñāna]miti | kāyarddhiriti | yogī svakāyādapo 'gniñcāviṣkaroti | vihāyasā gacchati | āvirbhavati | tirobhavati | sūryācandramasau parāmṛśati | brahmāṇamīśvaraṃ nānānirmitāṃścādhigacchati | īdṛśaṃ karma kāyarddhiḥ | (pṛ) kathamidaṃ setsyati | (u) yogī dhyānasamādhīnāṃ samyak bhāvanayā vindate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- dhyānasamādhānasya balamacintyamiti | kecidāhuḥ- nirmāṇacittamavyākṛtamiti | idamayuktam | yadyayaṃ yogī parahitāya nānānirmitaṃ pradarśayati | kasmāttadavyākṛtaṃ bhavet | kecidāhuḥ- kāmadhātukacittena kāmadhātukanirmitaṃ karoti | rūpadhātukacittena rūpadhātukanirmitaṃ karotīti | tadapyayuktam | cakṣurādyapi evaṃ syāt | kāmadhātukavijñānena kāmadhātukarūpameva paśyedityādi | yadi rūpadhātukacittaṃ kāmadhātukacittaṃ karoti | ko doṣo 'sti | kecidāhuḥ- prathamadhyānābhijñayā brahmalokaṃ gacchati yāvaccaturthadhyānābhijñayā rūpaparyantaṃ gacchatīti | idamapyayuktam | indriyabalavaśāt yatra kutracit gacchati | yadi tīkṣṇendriyaḥ, prathamadhyānābhijñayā caturthadhyānamanuprāpnoti | mṛdvindriyo dvitiyadhyānābhijñayāpi na prathamadhyānamupayojayati | yathā mahābrahmā [sahāṃ] patiḥ dhyānasyāntaramanuprāptaḥ | na tatrāsti [tasyā]bhijñā | prathamadhyānabalena anyān brahmadevānanuprāpnoti | naiva tu prathamadhyānena brahmāvāsaṃ prajānāti | bhagavān pūrvanivāsena ārūpyamanusmarati | yathoktaṃ sūtre rūpe vā ārūpye vā pūrvatanīnamupapattyāyatanaṃ bhagavān sarvaṃ prajānāti | ato nāsti niyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: There is the knowledge of the six supernatural powers (<s>ṣaḍabhijñā</s>). The six supernatural powers are: bodily miraculous power (<s>kāyarddhi</s>), the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>), the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>), recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛti</s>), and knowledge of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>). Regarding bodily miraculous power (<s>kāyarddhi</s>): the <s>yogī</s> manifests water and fire from his own body; he travels through the sky; he appears and disappears; he touches the sun and moon with his hands; he attains <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and various magical creations. Such action is bodily miraculous power. (Question) How is this accomplished? (Answer) The <s>yogī</s> obtains it through the proper cultivation of the <s>dhyāna</s>-concentrations (<s>dhyānasamādhi</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The power of <s>dhyāna</s>-concentration is inconceivable.' Some say: 'The mind of magical creation (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>) is indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>).' This is improper. If this <s>yogī</s> displays various magical creations for the benefit of others, why should that be indeterminate? Some say: 'With a mind belonging to the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātuka</s>) one creates desire-realm creations; with a mind belonging to the form-realm (<s>rūpadhātuka</s>) one creates form-realm creations.' That too is improper. The eye and the rest would also be the same [by that logic] — with desire-realm consciousness one would see only desire-realm form, and so forth. If form-realm mind performs desire-realm activity, what fault is there? Some say: 'Through the supernatural power of the first <s>dhyāna</s> one goes to the <s>Brahma</s>-world, up to through the supernatural power of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> one goes to the limit of the form-realm.' This too is improper. By the strength of one's faculties, one goes wherever one wishes. If one has sharp faculties, through the supernatural power of the first <s>dhyāna</s> one reaches the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. If one has dull faculties, even through the supernatural power of the second <s>dhyāna</s> one may not attain the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Just as the great <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the <s>Sahā</s> [world], has reached the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> — yet there the supernatural power is not his. Through the power of the first <s>dhyāna</s> he reaches the other <s>Brahma</s>-gods. But he does not know even the <s>Brahma</s>-abode through the first <s>dhyāna</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, through recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>), recollects the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whether in the form or formless realm, the <s>Bhagavān</s> knows all the former places of rebirth.' Therefore there is no fixed rule.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- divyacakṣuḥ prajñāsvabhāvamiti | tadapyayuktam | divyacakṣurālokavaśena siddham | prajñā tu naivam | (pṛ) sūtra uktam- ālokalakṣaṇaṃ bhāvayan jñānadarśanaṃ sādhayati iti | jñānadarśanameva divyacakṣuḥ | (u) maivam | api cāha- divyaśrotraṃ na prajñāsvabhāvamiti | tat śrotramityākhyāyate iti | ato na prajñāsvabhāvam | divyacakṣuḥ pratyutpannaṃ rūpamālambate | na tathā manovijñānam | divyacakṣurvibhaṅge coktam- jñānaṃ sattvakarmavipāka[bhūta]m | cakṣurvijñānasya nāsti balamidam | kintu manovijñānasya jñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānaprayogakāle samutpadyate | ato dhyānasamādhibhya utpannaṃ rūpaṃ divyacakṣurityucyate | (pṛ) divyacakṣuṣaḥ saṃsthānaṃ kiṃ mahat kiṃ vālpam | (u) tārakāpramāṇasadṛśam | (pṛ) andhasya katham | (u) cakṣurāyatanena sahaiva bhavati | (pṛ) kiṃ divyacakṣurekaṃ uta dve | (u) dve bhavataḥ | (pṛ) yāṃ kāñciddiśamanupaśyati | (u) sarvā diśo vyāpya paśyati | (pṛ) kiṃ nirmite 'pyasti | (u) nāsti | nirmāturasti | divyaśrotravādo 'pyevam |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'The divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>) has <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as its intrinsic nature.' That too is improper. The divine eye is established through the power of light (<s>āloka</s>), but <s>prajñā</s> is not so. (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Cultivating the characteristic of light, one accomplishes knowledge-and-vision (<s>jñānadarśana</s>).' Knowledge-and-vision itself is the divine eye. (Answer) That is not so. And further he said: 'The divine ear is not of the nature of <s>prajñā</s>.' It is called 'ear' (<s>śrotra</s>). Therefore it is not of the nature of <s>prajñā</s>. The divine eye takes present form as its object, not so mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>). And in the analysis of the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣurvibhaṅga</s>) it is stated: 'Knowledge pertains to the <s>karmic</s> ripening (<s>karmavipāka</s>) of beings. Eye-consciousness does not have this power. Rather, it is the knowledge of mental consciousness that arises at the time of the operation of eye-consciousness.' Therefore, form produced through the <s>dhyāna</s>-concentrations is called 'the divine eye.' (Question) What is the size of the divine eye — is it large or small? (Answer) It is similar to the measure of a star. (Question) How [does it work] for a blind person? (Answer) It arises together with the sense-base of the eye (<s>cakṣurāyatana</s>). (Question) Is there one divine eye or two? (Answer) There are two. (Question) Does one see in any direction? (Answer) It pervades and sees all directions. (Question) Does it exist in a magical creation (<s>nirmita</s>) too? (Answer) It does not. It exists in the creator [of the magical creation]. The explanation of the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>) is likewise.

body.text: yogī tat paracittaṃ vetti | yat paracittajñānam |(pṛ) kasmānnocyate paracaitasikajñānam | (u) asmādeva kāraṇānnāsti pṛthak caitasikam | parakīyasaṃjñāvedanādīnāṃ jñānamapi paracittajñānameva | kecidāhuḥ- jñānamidaṃ sajātīyālambanam | yathā sāsraveṇa sāsravaṃ jānāti anāsraveṇa anāsravaṃ jānāti iti | tadayuktam | neme vadanti kāraṇaniyamam- anena kāraṇena sajātīyamevālambanaṃ jānātīti | kecidvadanti- pratyutpannamātrālambanamiti | tadapyayuktam | kiñcidanāgatālambanam | yathā kaścidavitarkasamādhimupasampannaḥ prajānāti asmāt samādhervyutthite evamevaṃ vitarko bhaviṣyatīti | kecidvadanti- jñānamidaṃ na mārgasatyaṃ prajānātīti | tadayuktam | yadi prajānāti | ko doṣaḥ | āha ca- pratyekabuddho mārgasatyadarśanagatatṛtīyacittaṃ jñāsyāmīti saptamaṃ cittameva paśyati | śrāvakastṛtīyacittaṃ jñāsyāmīti ṣoḍaśaṃ cittameva paśyati | kimayaṃ na mārgasatyadarśanaṃ prajānāti | kecidāhuḥ- jñānamidaṃ na prajānāti ūrdhvabhūmimūrdhva[bhūmi]pudgalamūrdhvamindriyamiti | idamapyaniyatam | devā api prajānānti bhagavataścittam | tadyathā bhagavānekadā pariṣadaṃ vihāya punargrahaṇecchāmanvasmarat | tat sarvaṃ brahmā prājānat | kiñcaikasmin samaye manasyacintayat- rājā bhūtvā
body.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> knows that other mind — that is the knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>). (Question) Why is it not called 'knowledge of others' mental factors' (<s>paracaitasikajñāna</s>)? (Answer) For the very reason that mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) do not exist separately. Even the knowledge of others' perceptions (<s>saṃjñā</s>), feelings (<s>vedanā</s>), and so forth is itself the knowledge of others' minds. Some say: 'This knowledge takes an object of the same kind — just as one with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) knows what has outflows, and one without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>) knows what is without outflows.' That is incorrect. They do not state a fixed rule of causation — namely, that 'by this cause one knows only an object of the same kind.' Some say: 'It takes only a present object.' That too is incorrect. Some [knowledge] has a future object. For example, one who has attained a concentration without examination (<s>avitarkasamādhi</s>) knows: 'When I emerge from this concentration, such-and-such examination (<s>vitarka</s>) will arise.' Some say: 'This knowledge does not know the Truth of the Path (<s>mārgasatya</s>).' That is incorrect. If it knows [it], what fault is there? And it is said: 'A <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, wishing to know the third mind-moment that has entered the seeing of the Truth of the Path, sees only the seventh mind-moment. A <s>śrāvaka</s>, wishing to know the third mind-moment, sees only the sixteenth mind-moment.' Does this one not know the seeing of the Truth of the Path? Some say: 'This knowledge does not know the higher realms, persons of the higher realms, or the higher faculties.' This too is not fixed. Even the gods know the mind of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. For example, the <s>Bhagavān</s> once, having left the assembly, recollected his wish to resume [teaching]. All of that <s>Brahmā</s> knew. And at one time he thought in his mind: 'Having become a king

body.text: yathādharmaṃ lokaṃ vineṣyāmīti | mārastadeva jñātvā samāgatyāyācata | devā api jānanti- ayamarhan yāvadayaṃ srotaāpattipratipannaka iti | bhikṣavo 'pi prajānanti bhagavataścittam | tadyathā bhagavati parinirvāṇābhimukhe sati anirūddho bhagavatopasampannān dhyānasamādhīn yathākramamajānīt | kecidāhuḥ- jñānamidaṃ nārūpyaṃ prajānātīti | ida mayuktam | bhagavān hi pūrvanivāsā[nusmṛtyā] ārūpyaṃ prajānāti | paracittajñānenāpi tathā jñāne ko doṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: I shall guide the world according to the <s>dharma</s>.' <s>Māra</s>, having known that very [thought], came and made a request. And the gods know: 'This one is an <s>arhat</s>,' and even 'this one is an attainer of the fruit of stream-entry.' The monks too know the mind of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. For example, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> was approaching <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, <s>Anuruddha</s> knew in sequence the <s>dhyānas</s> and <s>samādhis</s> that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered. Some say: 'This knowledge does not know the formless [realm] (<s>ārūpya</s>).' That is incorrect. For the <s>Bhagavān</s>, through the recollection of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛti</s>), knows the formless [realm]. If knowledge of others' minds also knows it in the same way, what fault is there?

body.text: (pṛ) kathaṃ paricittaṃ jānāti | (u) ālambane sati jānāti | yadi cittaṃ rūpāvacaraṃ, rūpālambanaṃ cittaṃ bhavati | ityādi | (pṛ) tathā cet paracittaṃ sarvadharmālambanaṃ syāt | (u) evameva [syāt] | yadi na jānātyālambanaṃ, katamat cittaṃ jānīyāt | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhavataścittamevamevamiti prajānāmi iti | idameva rūpādyālambanam |
body.translated_text: (Question) How does one know others' minds? (Answer) One knows when there is an object (<s>ālambana</s>). If the mind belongs to the form realm (<s>rūpāvacara</s>), the mind has a form-object. And so forth. (Question) If so, knowledge of others' minds would have all <s>dharmas</s> as its object. (Answer) Exactly so. If one does not know the object, which mind would one know? As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'I know that your mind is exactly thus-and-thus.' This itself is having form and so forth as its object.

body.text: paracittajñānaṃ trividham- nimittajñānaṃ, vipākapratilabdhaṃ, bhāvanāpratilabdhamiti | nimittajñānamiti yathā aṅgamantrādinā jānāti | vipākaprāptamiti yathā asurādīnām | bhāvanāpratilabdhamiti dhyānasamādhibhāvanābalapratilabdhaṃ paracittajñānam | idameva ṣaḍabhijñāsu bhāvanāpratilabdhamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Knowledge of others' minds is of three kinds: knowledge through signs (<s>nimittajñāna</s>), knowledge obtained through karmic ripening (<s>vipākapratilabdha</s>), and knowledge obtained through meditation (<s>bhāvanāpratilabdha</s>). Knowledge through signs means knowing through bodily signs, mantras, and so forth. Knowledge obtained through karmic ripening is like that of <s>asuras</s> and others. Knowledge obtained through meditation is the knowledge of others' minds obtained through the power of cultivating <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration). This alone, among the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), is said to be 'obtained through meditation.'

body.text: yadatītādhvanīskandhānāmanusmaraṇaṃ [tat] pūrvanivāsānusmaraṇam | (pṛ) keṣāṃ skandhānāmanusmaraṇaṃ karoti | (u) svaskandhān paraskandhānasattvaskandhāṃścānusmarati | jinānāṃ skandhānanuramarannapi teṣāṃ śīlādīn dharmānanusmarati | kena tat jñāyate | yathā śāriputraḥ bhagavantaṃ pratyāha- ahamatītānāgatānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ cittamajānannapi teṣāṃ dharmaṃ jānāmīti | śuddhāvāsā devāstathāgatacittaṃ jānantītyato bhagavantamupasampadyāhuḥ- atītatathāgatānāṃ bhagavan iryāpatho 'pyevamiti |
body.translated_text: That which is the recollection of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) of past time-periods — that is the recollection of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛti</s>). (Question) Whose <s>skandhas</s> does one recollect? (Answer) One recollects one's own <s>skandhas</s>, others' <s>skandhas</s>, and the <s>skandhas</s> of non-sentient [things]. Even when recollecting the <s>skandhas</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors), one recollects their qualities such as moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and so forth. How is this known? Just as <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Even though I do not know the minds of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past and future, I know their <s>dharma</s>.' The gods of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (pure abodes) know the mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; therefore they approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said: 'Bhagavān, the conduct of the past <s>Tathāgatas</s> was also just like this.'

body.text: (pṛ) pūrvanivāsā[nusmṛti]vibhaṅge kasmāduktaṃ saha nimittena saha jātyeti | (u) anusmṛtirviśadetyata evaṃ nimittasaṃjñāmavocat amukaḥ pudgalaḥ ityādi | vastuvijñānena nimittamityucyate | jātirnāma gotram | yathāhuḥ- idaṃ tava kulaṃ iyaṃ tava jātiriti | jātiṃ nimittañca militvā vadatītyato jñānadarśanaṃ viśuddham | (pṛ) kasmādviśadānusmaraṇaṃ bhavati | (u) atītadharmā niruddhā na nimittāni | athāpi tān jñātuṃ prabhavatīdamadbhutam |
body.translated_text: (Question) In the analysis of the recollection of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛtivibhaṅga</s>), why is it stated 'together with the sign (<s>nimitta</s>), together with the birth (<s>jāti</s>)'? (Answer) The recollection becomes vivid, and therefore he spoke of the sign-perception (<s>nimittasaṃjñā</s>) — such as 'such-and-such a person' and so forth. 'Sign' (<s>nimitta</s>) is called the object of knowledge through [direct] cognition of things. 'Birth' (<s>jāti</s>) means clan (<s>gotra</s>). As they say: 'This is your family, this is your birth.' Combining birth and sign, he speaks — therefore knowledge-and-vision is purified. (Question) Why does the recollection become vivid? (Answer) Past <s>dharmas</s> have ceased and are not signs. Yet one is able to recollect them — this is marvelous.

body.text: kaścinnimittābhyuhena jānan na viśadaṃ jānāti | yajjinaurasāḥ [te] 'pi punarevam | ato jātiṃ nimittaṃ militvoktam |
body.translated_text: One who knows through the approach of signs does not know vividly. But even the true sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors) [do likewise]. Therefore, combining birth and sign, it was stated.

body.text: kaścit pūrvanivāsajñānaṃ prayojayati | kadācit samārgayā cintāmayaprajñayā prajānātyatītamadhvānam | yathā saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam | anayordvayościntāmayī prajñā viśiṣyate | kasmāt | asti hi pudgalasya aṣṭamahāsahasrakalpān jānato 'pi nāstīyaṃ cintāmayī prajñā | ato mithyādṛṣṭirutpadyate | yadi ta āgataṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ bhavati | tadatītya na punarasti [iti] | samārgacintāmayaprajñasya naivāsti taccittam |
body.translated_text: Sometimes one employs the knowledge of past lives; sometimes through the <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of reflection) that accords with the path (<s>samārga</s>), one knows the past time-period. Just as [one knows] 'consciousness is conditioned by formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>).' Of these two, the <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> is superior. Why? Because even a person who knows eighty-thousand great <s>kalpas</s> may not have this <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>. Therefore wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) arise [for him]. 'If aging and death come from that [source], then beyond that there is nothing more' — [he thinks]. For one who has the <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> that accords with the path, that mind does not arise.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- jñānamidamatītaṃ kramaśo 'nusmaratīti | tadayuktam | yadi kṣaṇakrameṇānusmarati | ekasminneva kalpe vastu durvijñeyaṃ sarvataḥ | kiṃ punarapramāṇakalpe (pṛ) sūtre kasmāduktam- ahamekanavatikalpānāgatya nāpaśyaṃ [kimapi] dānamapacīyamānaṃ vinā vipākena iti | (u) bhagavānatra saptabuddhān sākṣīcakāra | dīrghāyuṣkāḥ śuddhāvāsā api buddhairna samadarśinaḥ | bhagavān yathābhūtajñānaṃ pratilabdhavānityataḥ pariśuddhaguṇaḥ | yadi satkaroti [tathāgataṃ] sa ubhayorlokayoḥ puṇyamanuprāpnoti | ata etadubhayamuktam |
body.translated_text: (Question) Some say: 'This knowledge recollects the past sequentially.' That is incorrect. If one recollects moment by moment, then even [the events] within a single <s>kalpa</s> would be difficult to know in their entirety — how much more so in immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>! (Question) Why is it stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Going back ninety-one <s>kalpas</s>, I did not see any gift that had diminished without [producing] its ripening'? (Answer) The <s>Bhagavān</s> in that [context] took seven <s>Buddhas</s> as witnesses. The gods of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (pure abodes), long-lived though they are, do not see equally with the <s>Buddhas</s>. Because the <s>Bhagavān</s> has obtained knowledge-of-things-as-they-truly-are (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>), his qualities are purified. If one reveres [the <s>Tathāgata</s>], one obtains merit in both worlds. Therefore both of these [statements] were made.

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- jñānamidaṃ nordhvabhūmiṃ prajānātīti | tadayuktam | ūrdhva[bhūmika] kāyarddhyādau pratyuktameva | (pṛ) yadi smṛtisvabhāvamidam | kuto jñānamityucyate | (u) smṛtirnimittamanusambhavati | atītaṃ na nimittam | athāpyanusmarati | prajñāviśeṣameva smṛtiriti brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'This knowledge does not know the higher realms (<s>ūrdhvabhūmi</s>).' That is incorrect. Regarding the miraculous powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>) and so forth of the higher realms, it has already been answered. (Question) If this [knowledge] has the nature of recollection (<s>smṛti</s>), why is it called 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>)? (Answer) Recollection follows upon a sign (<s>nimitta</s>). The past is not a sign. Yet one recollects it. We say that recollection is itself a special kind of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).

body.text: pūrvanivāsānusmṛtistrividhā- pūrvanivāsajñānaprayogiṇī, vipākapratilabdhā, punarātmasmṛtisañjananīti | pūrvanivāsajñānaṃ bhāvanāpratilabdham | vipākapratilabdhamiti yathāsurādīnām | punarātmasmṛtisañjananī yanmanuṣyagatau bhavati | (pṛ) kena karmaṇā punarātmasañjananī bhavati | (u) sattvānāmavihiṃsanena karmaṇā pratilabhate | kasmāt | maraṇakāla upapattikāle ca duḥkhābhihatatvānmuṣitasmṛtirbhavati | tatrāmoṣaṇaṃ durlabham | ataḥ kuśalaṃ karmāpekṣyate | kecidvadanti- idamatītaṃ saptādhvaparamamanusmaratīti | nāyaṃ niyamaḥ | kaścit pratyadhvamavihiṃsanadharmasubhāvitatvāt suciraṃ viprakṛṣṭañcānusmarati |
body.translated_text: The recollection of past lives is of three kinds: that which employs the knowledge of past lives, that obtained through karmic ripening (<s>vipākapratilabdhā</s>), and that which generates self-recollection (<s>ātmasmṛtisañjananī</s>). The knowledge of past lives is obtained through meditation (<s>bhāvanāpratilabdha</s>). That obtained through karmic ripening is like that of <s>asuras</s> and others. That which generates self-recollection occurs in the human realm. (Question) Through what <s>karma</s> does the self-recollection arise? (Answer) Through the <s>karma</s> of non-harming of beings one obtains it. Why? Because at the time of death and at the time of rebirth, due to being struck by suffering, recollection is lost. There, the non-loss [of recollection] is difficult to obtain. Therefore wholesome <s>karma</s> is required. Some say: 'This [knowledge] recollects the past for a maximum of seven time-periods.' This is not a fixed rule. Someone, because of having well-cultivated the quality of non-harming in each time-period, recollects even very distant [past lives].

body.text: āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkārābhijñeti | vajropamasamādhirayam |
body.translated_text: The superknowledge of the direct realization of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkārābhijñā</s>): this is the <s>vajropamasamādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration).

body.text: vajropamasamādhirayamāsravakṣayarūpaḥ anāvaraṇamārgaḥ | āsravakṣayaḥ aśaikṣajñānamityucyate | vajropamasamādhinā āsravāṇāṃ nirodhaḥ kṣayaḥ | [sa] āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkārābhijñetyucyate | (pṛ) anye ṛddhi[pādā] api vaktavyāḥ; kena dharmeṇa sākṣātkaroti | (u) uktameva pūrvaṃ dhyānasamādhīn gabhīraṃ bhāvayan ṛddhipādān sākṣātkarotīti | yatprayojanamanusṛtya sākṣātkāraḥ sākṣātkṛtaṃ vastu, [sa] sarva ṛddhipādaḥ |
body.translated_text: This <s>vajropamasamādhi</s>, having the nature of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>), is the unobstructed path (<s>anāvaraṇamārga</s>). The destruction of the outflows is called 'the knowledge of the adept' (<s>aśaikṣajñāna</s>). Through the <s>vajropamasamādhi</s>, the cessation of the outflows is their destruction. That is called 'the superknowledge of the direct realization of the destruction of the outflows.' (Question) The bases of miraculous power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) too should be stated. Through what <s>dharma</s> does one directly realize [them]? (Answer) It has already been stated previously — one who deeply cultivates <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhi</s> directly realizes the bases of miraculous power. That purpose for which the direct realization occurs, and that thing which is directly realized — all of that is a base of miraculous power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>).

body.text: kecidāhuḥ- sarva āryamārgā asravakṣayasyopāyāḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- tathāgate loka utpanne supuruṣā dharmaṃ śrutvā pravrajitāḥ śīlaṃ samādadānā apanītapañca nīvaraṇāḥ samādhiṃ bhāvayantaḥ satyaṃ paśyanti ityādi sarvamāsravakṣayasyopāyāḥ | kecidāhuḥ- dānādayaḥ kuśaladharmā api āsravakṣayasya nidānāni | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yogino dānaṃ kṣīṇāsravaśūnyānātmajñānaṃ sādhayatīti | idamucyate tattvata āsravakṣayasākṣātkārābhijñā iti | asyaiva dharmasya nāmāntaraṃ vajropamasamādhiriti | nimittāni samūhantīti vajratvam | tīrthikāḥ pañcābhijñā bhavanti | tairasya tattvajñānasyāpratilabdhatvāt |
body.translated_text: Some say: 'All the noble paths (<s>āryamārga</s>) are means for the destruction of the outflows.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'When a <s>Tathāgata</s> arises in the world, good people, having heard the <s>dharma</s>, go forth, maintain moral discipline, remove the five hindrances, cultivate concentration, and see the truths' — and so forth — all are means for the destruction of the outflows. Some say: 'Wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and so forth are also causes for the destruction of the outflows.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For the <s>yogī</s>, generosity accomplishes the knowledge of [things as] empty, without self, and with outflows destroyed.' This is called 'in reality, the superknowledge of the direct realization of the destruction of the outflows.' Another name for this very <s>dharma</s> is '<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>' (diamond-like concentration). It eradicates the signs (<s>nimitta</s>) — that is the diamond-nature. The non-Buddhist practitioners (<s>tīrthikas</s>) possess the five superknowledges. Because they have not obtained this knowledge of reality, [they lack the sixth].

body.text: (pṛ) anātmajñānena ātmadṛṣṭiṃ bhindyāt | kathamanena kāmapratighādi prajahāti | (u) anātmajñānena sarvāṇi nimittāni nirundhe | nimittābhāvātsarve kleśā nirudhyante | (pṛ) adyena anātmajñānena nimittāni nirundhe | dvitīyajñānādinā ka upayogaḥ (u) nimittāni niruddhānyapi punarutpadyante | ato dvitīyādyapekṣate | (pṛ) yadi niruddhaṃ punarutpadyate | tadā anavasthaṃ nimittaṃ bhavati | tathā sati nārhanmārgaḥ | (u) astyavasthā | yathā paśyāmaḥ stanyaṃ śuṣyat punaḥ prasravati | asti kaścit kālaḥ [yadā] stanyaṃ pratiruddhapayaḥprasūti bhavati | tadā avadhirbhavati | nimittamapyeyam | yathā ca tapte 'yasi kṛṣṇalakṣaṇaṃ niruddhaṃ punarutpadyate | yāvallohitalakṣaṇamutpadyate | sa samayo 'vadhirityucyate | kalalādayo dṛṣṭāntā apyevam | yasmin samaye nimittāni niruddhāni na punarutpadyante | sa samayo 'rhanmārgapratilambhaḥ | (pṛ) kimarhato 'tyantābhāvarūpāṇi nimittāni | (u) yadā asamāhitacittasthaḥ, tasmin samaye santyapi rūpādinimittāni | kintu na doṣajanakāni | yadi kiścit cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā mithyāmanaskāreṇa mithyā vikalpayati | tadā doṣājanakāni bhavanti |
body.translated_text: (Question) Through the knowledge of non-self (<s>anātmajñāna</s>) one would break the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>). How does one abandon sensual desire (<s>kāma</s>), ill-will (<s>pratigha</s>), and so forth through it? (Answer) Through the knowledge of non-self one blocks all signs (<s>nimitta</s>). Through the absence of signs, all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are blocked. (Question) If with the first knowledge of non-self one blocks the signs, what use is a second knowledge and so forth? (Answer) Even blocked signs arise again. Therefore a second [knowledge] and so forth is required. (Question) If what has been blocked arises again, then the signs would be without end. In that case there would be no path of the <s>arhat</s>. (Answer) There is an end. Just as we see: breast-milk, having dried up, flows again. [But] there is a time when the breast-milk is [permanently] stopped from flowing. Then there is a limit. The same applies to signs. And just as when iron is heated, the black coloring is blocked but arises again — until the red coloring appears. That moment is called the limit. The examples of <s>kalala</s> (embryo) and so forth are likewise. At the moment when the signs, having been blocked, no longer arise again — that moment is the attainment of the path of the <s>arhat</s>. (Question) Are the signs of an <s>arhat</s> of the nature of absolute non-existence? (Answer) When one is in an unconcentrated state of mind, at that time signs such as form and so forth do exist. But they do not generate faults. If someone, having seen forms with the eye, wrongly attends to them through false conceptualization (<s>mithyāmanaskāra</s>) — then they become fault-generating.

body.text: (pṛ) kimanātmaśūnyajñānam | (u) yadyogī pañcasu skandheṣu prajñaptaṃ sattvaṃ na paśyati | dharmaśūnyatvāt rūpakāyanirodhaṃ yāvadvijñānanirodhaṃ paśyati | idamucyate anātmaśūnyajñānam |
body.translated_text: (Question) What is the knowledge of non-self and emptiness (<s>anātmaśūnyajñāna</s>)? (Answer) When the <s>yogī</s> does not see a being conventionally designated (<s>prajñapta</s>) in the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — and because of the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaśūnyatā</s>), he sees the cessation of the form-body up to the cessation of consciousness — this is called 'the knowledge of non-self and emptiness.'

body.text: (pṛ) prajñaptikṛtā dharmā nityavartinaḥ | [teṣu] tṛṣṇādayaḥ kleśā api praheyāḥ | yathoktam- padārthā nityasthāyinaḥ | vyavasāyī tu [tatra] kāmatṛṣṇāṃ prajahāti iti | kiṃ nirodhalakṣaṇamapekṣate | (u) sūtra uktam- yatkiñcitsamudayadharma, tatsarvaṃ nirodhadharma | teṣu dharmeṣu virajo dharmacakṣuḥ pratilabhata iti | yo nirodhena prahāṇaṃ tadatyantaprahāṇam | kaścidyogī rūpeṣu vītarāgaḥ kāmapratighaṃ kṣapayati | tadarthaṃ bhāgavānīdṛśīṃ gāthāmavocat | kiñcāha- saṃskārāḥ svabhāvaśūnyā māyāvat | prākṛtā ajñā vadanti- te vastusanta iti | śaikṣāḥ punaḥ prajānanti- te tucchā riktā māyāvaditi | arhannapi māyāṃ [kiṃ] na paśyati | ato jñāyate yayā prajñayā dharmāṇāṃ nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti iyamāsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñeti ||
body.translated_text: (Question:) <s>Dharmas</s> that are merely designations (<s>prajñaptikṛta</s>) are perpetually ongoing. Among them, defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) such as craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) are also to be abandoned. As stated: 'Categories of objects are permanently abiding. But the resolute one abandons sensual craving therein.' Why does one need the characteristic of cessation? (Answer:) The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of cessation. With regard to those <s>dharmas</s>, one attains the stainless <s>dharma</s>-eye.' That abandonment which is through cessation is the ultimate abandonment. A certain <s>yogī</s>, being free from attachment to forms, exhausts sensual desire and aversion. For that purpose the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke such a verse. Moreover he says: 'Formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are empty of own-nature, like an illusion. Ordinary, ignorant persons say: "They are substantial things." But learners (<s>śaikṣas</s>) know: "They are worthless, void, like an illusion."' Does not even the <s>arhat</s> see the illusion? Therefore it is known: that wisdom by which one directly realizes the cessation of <s>dharmas</s> — this is the direct realization of the superknowledge of the exhaustion of defilements (<s>āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā</s>).

body.text: ṣaḍabhijñāvargaḥ saptanavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the six superknowledges (<s>ṣaḍabhijñāvarga</s>), the one-hundred-and-ninety-seventh.

body.text: 198 jñānakṣāntivargaḥ
body.translated_text: 198. The chapter on knowledge and patient acceptance (<s>jñānakṣāntivarga</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- yo yogī saptabhirupāyaistribhirarthāvalokanaiḥ samanvitaḥ so 'smin dharme kṣipramāsravakṣayamanuprāpnotīti | kimidaṃ jñānam | (u) saptopāyā nāma śrutamayī prajñā cintāmayī prajñā ca | kasmāt | asamāhitacitta evaṃ vicārayati- yadidaṃ rūpam, ayaṃ rūpasamudayaḥ ayaṃ rūpanirodhaḥ iyaṃ rūpanirodhagāminī pratipat, [ayaṃ] rūpāsvādaḥ, [ayaṃ] rūpādīnavaḥ idaṃ rūpanissaraṇaṃ iti | (pṛ) yadīyaṃ śrutamayī cintāmayī prajñā | kasmādāha- kṣipramāsravakṣayamanuprāpnotīti | (u) yadyapīyaṃ śrutamayī cintāmayī prajñā tathāpyevaṃ pañcaskandhān vikalpayan ātmamatiṃ vibhedayati | ata āha- kṣipramāsravakṣayamanuprāpnotīti | trividhāvalokanajñānaṃ yaduta saṃskārā anityā duḥkhā anātmāna iti | skandhadhātvāyatanamukhena saṃskārān paśyato nāstyartho hitaṃ vā | (pṛ) tathā cet pūrvamādīnava uktameva- anityā duḥkhā iti | nissaraṇe coktam- anātmāna iti | kasmātpunarucyate trividhamidamavalokanamiti | (u) trividhāḥ śikṣate- pūrvaṃ śrutamayīṃ cintāmayīṃ prajñām | paścāt bhāvanāmayīṃ prajñām | pūrvaṃ śrutamayyāṃ cintāmayyāṃ prajñāyāmuktāḥ sapta prakārāḥ | paścādbhāvanāmayyāṃ prajñāyāṃ trayaḥ prakārāḥ | kasmāt | yadanityaṃ tat duḥkhamiti lakṣaṇasya bhaṅgo
body.translated_text: (Question:) The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'The <s>yogī</s> who is endowed with seven methods (<s>upāya</s>) and three contemplations of meaning (<s>arthāvalokana</s>) quickly attains the exhaustion of defilements in this <s>dharma</s>.' What is this knowledge? (Answer:) The seven methods are wisdom born of learning (<s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>) and wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>). Why? Because with an unconcentrated mind, one investigates thus: 'This is form, this is the arising of form, this is the cessation of form, this is the path leading to the cessation of form; this is the relishing of form, this is the danger of form, this is the escape from form.' (Question:) If this is wisdom born of learning and reflection, why does he say 'one quickly attains the exhaustion of defilements'? (Answer:) Even though this is wisdom born of learning and reflection, nevertheless, by thus analyzing the five <s>skandhas</s>, one breaks apart the notion of self (<s>ātmamati</s>). Therefore he says: 'One quickly attains the exhaustion of defilements.' The knowledge of the threefold contemplation is: formations are impermanent, suffering, and without self. For one who sees formations through the gateway of <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, there is no [real] object or benefit. (Question:) If so, the danger has already been stated earlier — 'impermanent, suffering' — and regarding escape, it was said 'without self.' Why is it stated again that 'this is a threefold contemplation'? (Answer:) One trains in three [stages]: first in wisdom born of learning and reflection; afterwards in wisdom born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>). In the first — wisdom born of learning and reflection — seven aspects were stated. Afterwards, in wisdom born of cultivation, three aspects [are stated]. Why? Because 'what is impermanent is suffering' — the dissolution of the characteristic

body.text: nāma anityasya bhaṅgaḥ nānityasaṃskārāṇāṃ bhaṅgaḥ | pūrvaṃ kāmakaṣāyotsarga ukte 'pi noktaṃ kathamutsṛjatīti | paścāttābaduktaṃ trividhamarthāvalokanam |
body.translated_text: is the dissolution of impermanence — not the dissolution of impermanent formations. Earlier, the abandonment of sensual attachment was stated, but it was not stated how one abandons [it]. Afterwards, the threefold contemplation of meaning was stated.

body.text: (pṛ) katamā aṣṭa kṣāntayaḥ | (u) yatkiñcit jñānaṃ prajñaptividāraṇam, iyaṃ kṣāntirityucyate | kṣāntiriyamūṣmamurdhakṣāntilaukikāgradharmeṣva[sti] | (pṛ) yogino 'pi buddhe dharme saṅghe śīladiṣu kṣāntirasti | kasmāduktamaṣṭāviti | (u) prādhānyāduktam | prādhānyaṃ mārgapratyāsannatā | yathā duḥkhe dharmajñānāya duḥkhe dharmakṣāntirityevamādi | kasmāt | pūrvaṃ hi mārgānukūlāṃ cintāmayīṃ prajñāṃ prayujya paścātpratyakṣajñānamanuprāpnoti | yathā hastipakaḥ pūrvaṃ hastipadaṃ dṛṣṭvā tena jñānena prajānāti- atra vartata iti | paścādabhimukhīkaroti | tathā yogyapi pūrvaṃ kṣāntyānvayajñāne na nirvāṇamabhyūhya paścāt tena jñānenābhimukhīkaroti | ataḥ sūtra uktam- [evaṃ] jānan[evaṃ] paśyan āsravakṣayamanuprāpnotīti ||
body.translated_text: (Question:) What are the eight patient acceptances (<s>kṣānti</s>)? (Answer:) Whatever knowledge penetrates designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) — that is called <s>kṣānti</s>. This <s>kṣānti</s> exists in the [stages of] heat (<s>ūṣman</s>), summit (<s>murdhan</s>), patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>), and supreme worldly <s>dharma</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>). (Question:) The <s>yogī</s> also has patient acceptance regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṅgha</s>, morality (<s>śīla</s>), etc. Why is it said 'eight'? (Answer:) It is said by way of preeminence. Preeminence means proximity to the path. Just as '[there is] patient acceptance of <s>dharma</s> regarding suffering, for the sake of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding suffering' — and so forth. Why? Because having first applied wisdom born of reflection that accords with the path, one afterwards attains direct knowledge. Just as an elephant-tracker, having first seen the elephant's footprint, knows by that knowledge 'it dwells here,' and afterwards goes to face it directly. So too the <s>yogī</s>, having first inferred <s>nirvāṇa</s> through patient acceptance in the inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>), afterwards goes to face it through that knowledge. Therefore the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'Thus knowing, thus seeing, one attains the exhaustion of defilements.'

body.text: jñānakṣāntivargo 'ṣṭanavatyuttaraśatatamaḥ
body.translated_text: The chapter on knowledge and patient acceptance (<s>jñānakṣāntivarga</s>), the one-hundred-and-ninety-eighth.

body.text: 199 navajñānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 199. The chapter on the nine knowledges (<s>navajñānavarga</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) kecidābhidharmikā vadanti arhan kṣayajñānaṃ sākṣātkurvan sāṃvṛtāni nava jñānāni prāpnoti yaduta kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamavyākṛtaṃ [jñānaṃ] yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanapratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamavyākṛtaṃ [jñāna]m | kathamidam | (u) na sarvo 'rhan sarvān dhyānasamādhīn prāpnoti | kathaṃ nava jñānāni prāpnuyāt | (pṛ) sarvo 'rhan dhyānasamādhīn prāpnoti | na tu sarvaḥ samāpattimabhimukhīkaroti | (u) yadi samāpattiṃ nābhimukhīkaroti | katamā prāptirnāma | yathā kaścidāha- granthaṃ jānāmi, tadakṣaramekantu na vijānāmīti | tathedamapyasti | (pṛ) yo vītarāgaḥ san na prathamadhyānasamāpattiṃ nādyāpi pratyakṣīkṛtavān | sa āyuṣo 'nte ['pi] na tāmutpādayati | (u) sūtre tūktam- asminnantarāle samāpadya paścāttāṃ samutpādayediti | idānīṃ kathamasminnantarāle 'samāpannastāṃ samutpādayati | (pṛ) yadi
body.translated_text: (Question:) Certain <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> (Abhidharma scholars) say: 'The <s>arhat</s>, upon directly realizing the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>), attains nine conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) knowledges — namely, wholesome knowledge and indeterminate knowledge connected with the realm of desire (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), up to wholesome knowledge and indeterminate knowledge connected with the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>).' How is this? (Answer:) Not every <s>arhat</s> attains all the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). How could one attain nine knowledges? (Question:) Every <s>arhat</s> attains the <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhis</s>; but not every one enters their attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>). (Answer:) If one does not enter the attainment, what kind of 'attainment' is that? Just as someone might say: 'I know the text, but I do not understand even a single syllable of it.' This is similar. (Question:) One who, being free from attachment, has not yet directly experienced the first <s>dhyāna</s> attainment — even at the end of his lifespan, does he not produce it? (Answer:) But the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'In this interval, having entered [the attainment], one should afterwards produce it.' Now, how does one who has not entered the attainment in this interval produce it? (Question:) If

body.text: rāgādvirajyamānasyātītānāgatāni sarvāṇi dhyānāni mūlataḥ prāpnāni | tadvipākena [ta]dutpattiṃ prāpnoti | (u) anāgataṃ karma akṛtamabhūtaṃ na vipākaṃ prāpayati | atītāni dhyānāni citta utpannacarāṇi yadi vipākaṃ prayacchanti | tadā avidyamānatāhāniḥ | kiñca nānāgatakarmāṇi prāpnuyāt | yadi prāpyamiti, anāgataṃ sarvaṃ prāpyaṃ syāt | kasya pratibandhāt prāptyaprāptī staḥ |
body.translated_text: one who is becoming free from attachment obtains all past and future <s>dhyānas</s> from their root — one obtains their arising through their fruition (<s>vipāka</s>). (Answer:) Future <s>karma</s>, being unperformed and unactual, does not produce fruition. If past <s>dhyānas</s>, having arisen and passed in the mind, give fruition — then there would be the loss of [the principle of] non-existence [of the non-existent]. Moreover, one would [then] attain even future <s>karmas</s>. If [you say] 'they are attainable,' then everything future would be attainable. Due to what obstruction would there be attainment and non-attainment?

body.text: (pṛ) yadyanāgato dharmo na prāpya iti | śaikṣo nāṣṭabhiraṅgaiḥ samanvitaḥ syāt | aśaikṣo 'pi daśabhiraṅgaiḥ samanvitaḥ | kasmāt | yasya dvitīyadhyānādi niśritya samyak dharmaniyāmāvakrāntirbhavati | so 'nāgate samyaksaṅkalpaṃ prāpnoti | yadi yogī kṣayajñānamabhimuravīkaroti | tadānāgate 'dhvani samy dṛṣṭiṃ prāpnoti kaścidārūpyasamādhiṃ niśrityārhatphalaṃ prāpnoti | ayamanāgate samyaksaṅkalpaṃ samyagvācaṃ samyakkarmāntaṃ samyagājīvaṃ prāpnoti | yadi tṛtīyadhyānādi niśrityāryamārgaṃ prāpnoti | so 'nāgate prītiṃ prāpnoti | evamādayo dharmāstadā na syuḥ | ato jñāyate astyanāgato dharma iti | yadi ca nāsti anāgata[dharmaḥ] kathaṃ bhāvako phalāni dhyānasamādhyādīnanuprāpsyati | yogī yadā mārgānvayajñāne vartate | prathamaphalasaṅgṛhītāni sarvāṇi jñānāni samādhīṃśca sarvathānuprāpnoti | tathā no cet phalāni gaṇayitvā gaṇayitvānuprāpnuyāt | kasmāt | phalāni sarvāṇyabhimukhīkāle prāpnuyāditīdaṃ na sambhavati | ato jñāyate bhavedanāgate bhāvaneti |
body.translated_text: (Question:) If a future <s>dharma</s> is not attainable, then the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) would not be endowed with eight factors, nor the adept (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) with ten factors. Why? Because for one who attains the correct certainty of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmaniyāmāvakrānti</s>) by relying on the second <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond, he attains right intention (<s>samyaksaṅkalpa</s>) in the future. If the <s>yogī</s> directly realizes the knowledge of destruction, then in the future course he attains right vision. A certain one attains the <s>arhat</s>-fruit by relying on formless <s>samādhi</s>. This one attains right intention, right speech, right action, and right livelihood in the future. If one attains the Noble Path by relying on the third <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond, he attains joy (<s>prīti</s>) in the future. Such <s>dharmas</s> and the like would then not exist. Therefore it is known that a future <s>dharma</s> exists. And if no future [<s>dharma</s>] exists, how would the practitioner attain fruits, <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>samādhis</s>, etc.? When the <s>yogī</s> dwells in the inferential knowledge of the path (<s>mārgānvayajñāna</s>), he attains in every way all the knowledges and <s>samādhis</s> included in the first fruit. If not so, he would attain [them] by counting fruits one by one. Why? [Because the claim that] one attains all fruits at the time of confrontation — this is not possible. Therefore it is known that cultivation in the future exists.

body.text: ucyate | yat bhavatoktam- aṅgaiḥ samanvita iti | idamabādhitam | kasmāt | śīlādyaṅgāni kramaśaḥ prāpyante naikakālamiti brūmaḥ | ato nāsti dūṣaṇam | yaduktaṃ bhavatā keṣāñcitprāptistajjātīyātā[mapi] | yoginaḥ [kutracit] duḥkhajñānaprāptāvanyaduḥkhajñānajātiḥ prāptā bhavati | yathā manuṣyajātiḥ prāptetyato manuṣyalakṣaṇaṃ prāptaṃ bhavati | nāpi pratikṣaṇaṃ kramaśo manuṣyalakṣaṇaṃ prāptamiti | tathedamapi | (pṛ) yogino vidyamānaduḥkhādīnāṃ jñānāni kramikāṇīti sarvaṃ parihṛtameva | srotaāpattiphalasaṅgṛhītānāṃ jñānānāṃ prāptiḥ punaraikakālikī | (u) anāsravajñānāni prāptāni tu na parihīyante | (pṛ) yadi pūrvaṃ
body.translated_text: We reply: What you have said about 'being endowed with factors' — this is not damaged [by our position]. Why? Because we say that factors such as morality are attained gradually, not all at one time. Therefore there is no fault. As for what you said about the attainment of certain things [implying] their class-nature as well: for the <s>yogī</s>, when knowledge of suffering is attained, the class of other suffering-knowledge is [also considered] attained — just as when human birth is attained, human characteristics are [thereby] attained. But it is not the case that human characteristics are attained moment by moment in sequence. This is similar. (Question:) For the <s>yogī</s>, the knowledges of presently existing suffering etc. are sequential — all this has already been addressed. But the attainment of the knowledges included in the fruit of stream-entry is simultaneous. (Answer:) Undefiled knowledges, once attained, are not lost. (Question:) If once

body.text: prāptāni na parihīyante | tadā prāptiḥ prayoga iti nāsti bhedaḥ | kasmāt | prāptaphala eva yogī ityādidoṣaḥ | (u) yadi nāsti viśeṣaḥ | kimavadyaṃ bhavati | yathā sampannaphalo 'pi yogītyucyate | tathedamapi | pudgalo 'yaṃ punarviśiṣṭaṃ dharmaṃ prāpnotītyato 'sti pravibhāgaḥ | ato nāsti doṣaḥ | yathā samāpattapañcaśīlaḥ punaḥ pravrajyāsaṃvaramanuprāpnuvannapi na maulikaśīlebhyaḥ parihīyate | prāptaphalasya ca mārgādarśanādasti pravibhāgaḥ | yathā kaścidādau vastu jānannapi viśiṣṭavastu[darśanāya yatata] iti pravibhāgo 'sti | tathe damapi | ato jñāyate nāstyanāgatasya prāptiriti | kiñca yogī śūnyānātmajñāne viharati | tasmin samaye kathamanuprāpnoti laukikaṃ dharmam | ato jñāyate kṣayajñānaprāptau na laukikajñānamanuprāpnotīti |
body.translated_text: attained they are not lost, then there is no distinction between attainment and practice. Why? Because there would be the fault that the <s>yogī</s> is one who has already attained the fruit, etc. (Answer:) If there is no distinction, what harm is there? Just as one who has matured the fruit is also called a '<s>yogī</s>' — this is similar. This person further attains a distinguished <s>dharma</s> — therefore there is a classification. Therefore there is no fault. Just as one who has completed the five precepts, upon further attaining the ordination-code (<s>pravrajyāsaṃvara</s>), does not lose the original precepts. And because of the non-seeing of the path by the fruit-attainer, there is a classification. Just as someone, even while knowing a thing from the beginning, [still] strives for the seeing of a more distinguished thing — thus there is a classification. This is similar. Therefore it is known that there is no attainment of a future [dharma]. Moreover, the <s>yogī</s> abides in the knowledge of emptiness and non-self. At that time, how does he attain a worldly <s>dharma</s>? Therefore it is known that upon the attainment of the knowledge of destruction, one does not attain worldly knowledge.

body.text: (pṛ) imāni laukikajñānāni kṣayajñānena sahārhataḥ samādhisamāpattivyutthānacittakriyāṃ prāpayanti | (u) arhataścittaṃ santānena pravartamānaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ viśuddham | yadi punarnavajñānāni prāpnoti | cakṣurādi sarvaṃ punaḥ prāpyeta | tathā no cet na navajñānāni prāpnuyāt | uktañca- anāgatabhāvanāyā nāsti hetuḥ pratyayo vā iti | kasmāt | ete hi vadanti- satyadarśanamārge kevalaṃ nimittābhāsaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvayati | cintanāmārge 'pi nimittābhāsamanimittābhāsañca bhāvayati | satyadarśanamārge nordhvabhūmiṃ bhāvayati | cintanāmārge tu bhāvayati | mārgānvayajñāne na sāṃvṛtaṃ kuśalaṃ bhāvayati | anyasmin jñāne tu bhāvayati | ānantaryamārge na paracittajñānaṃ bhāvayati | śraddhāvibhukto darśanaprāptatvena parivartamānaḥ sarvasminnānantaryavimuktimārge na sāṃvṛtaṃ mārgaṃ bhāvayati | samayavimuktaḥ akopyavimuktatayā parivartamāno navānantarya[mārgeṣu] aṣṭavimokṣamārgeṣu saṃvṛtaṃ mārgaṃ na bhāvayati | navame vimuktimārge [tu] bhāvayati | sūkṣmacitte na bhāvayati sarvamanāsravam | etyevamādīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ nāsti kāraṇam | ato bhavān yadi vā samyagdyetuṃ brūyāt yadi vā śraddhāpayet | kiñca śaikṣabhāvanayā bhāvanā bhavati | ūṣma[gatā]diṣu sthitikāle uttamāni sarvāṇi kuśalamūlāni bhāvayati | sarvathā prakarṣakaraṇārthatvāt | yathā sūtramadhīyānasya sarvathā vaiśadyopakāro bhavati | ata ūṣmagatādidharmakālāt yāvat kṣayajñānaṃ sarveṣāṃ bhāvanā bhavati | tathā no cet saddheturvaktavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Question:) These worldly knowledges, together with the knowledge of destruction, enable the <s>arhat</s> to attain the function of the mind of emergence from <s>samādhi</s>-attainment. (Answer:) The mind of the <s>arhat</s>, proceeding in continuity, is pure at every moment. If he further attains nine knowledges, then the eye-faculty and all the rest would also have to be re-attained. If not so, then neither would the nine knowledges be attained. And it has been said: 'There is no cause or condition for future cultivation.' Why? For they say: 'On the path of seeing truth, one cultivates only knowledge with the appearance of signs (<s>nimittābhāsa</s>). On the path of reflection, one cultivates both sign-appearance and signless-appearance. On the path of seeing truth, one does not cultivate the higher realms. But on the path of reflection, one does cultivate them. In the inferential knowledge of the path, one does not cultivate conventional wholesome [dharma]. But in other knowledge, one does. On the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), one does not cultivate knowledge of others' minds. The faith-liberated one, turning as one who has attained seeing, does not cultivate the conventional path on any uninterrupted-liberation path. The time-liberated one, turning as one liberated by the unshakeable, does not cultivate the conventional path on nine uninterrupted paths and eight liberation paths. But on the ninth liberation path, one does cultivate. In the subtle mind, one does not cultivate anything undefiled.' For all these and others, there is no reason. Therefore, whether you state a correct reason or generate faith — furthermore, cultivation occurs through the cultivation of the learner. During the time of dwelling in the stages of heat (<s>ūṣmagatā</s>) etc., one cultivates all supreme wholesome roots. Because the purpose is to bring [them] to excellence in every way. Just as for one who studies a <s>sūtra</s>, there is assistance toward clarity in every way. Therefore, from the time of the heat-stage etc. up to the knowledge of destruction, there is cultivation of all [dharmas]. If not so, a correct reason must be stated.

body.text: navajñānavarga ekonadviśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The chapter on the nine knowledges (<s>navajñānavarga</s>), the one-hundred-and-ninety-ninth.

body.text: 200 daśajñānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 200. The chapter on the ten knowledges (<s>daśajñānavarga</s>).

body.text: daśa jñānāni- dharmajñānaṃ anvayajñānaṃ, paracittajñānaṃ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ, catvāri satyajñānāni, kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānamiti | pratyutpannadharmajñānameva dharmajñānamityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bhagavānānandamāmantryāha- asmin dharme evaṃ jñānena dṛṣṭvā evaṃ pratibudhyasva | atīte 'nāgate 'pyevaṃ jānīhīti | vaktavyaṃ pratyutpannadharmajñānamiti | idānīṃ pratyutpannamanuktvā kevalamucyate dharmajñānamiti | yathoktaṃ sūtre- bālaḥ pratyutpannaṃ dharmaṃ bahumanyate | jñānī anāgataṃ bahumanyata iti | kiñcāha- pratyutpannāḥ kāmā anāgatāḥ kāmāśca mārasenā māradheyā mārabandhanā ityādau sarvatrocyate pratyutpannavādaḥ | idaṃ saṃkṣipyavacanāt kevalaṃ dharmajñānamityucyate |
body.translated_text: The ten knowledges are: knowledge of dharma (<s>dharmajñāna</s>), inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>), knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>), conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>), the four knowledges of the truths (<s>satyajñāna</s>), knowledge of exhaustion (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>), and knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>). Knowledge of present <s>dharmas</s> alone is called '<s>dharmajñāna</s>.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Blessed One addressed <s>Ānanda</s>: Having seen with this knowledge in this <s>dharma</s>, thus awaken! Know likewise regarding the past and future.' It should be stated that this is knowledge of present <s>dharmas</s>. Now, without mentioning 'present,' it is simply called '<s>dharmajñāna</s>.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A fool esteems present <s>dharmas</s>; a wise person esteems the future.' And further he said: 'Present desires and future desires are <s>Māra's</s> army, <s>Māra's</s> retinue, <s>Māra's</s> bondage' — and so forth, everywhere the discourse concerns the present. By way of abbreviation, it is simply called '<s>dharmajñāna</s>.'

body.text: avaśiṣṭadharmajñānamanvayajñānamiti vadanti | avaśiṣṭā iti yadutātītā anāgatā dharmāḥ | pratyutpannadharmānanu paścāt jānātīti anvayajñānam | kasmāt | dṛṣṭadharmajñānapūrvakaṃ hi anvayajñānam | dharmajñānaṃ nāma dṛṣṭajñānamityucyate | etaddharmajñānamanusṛtya vitarkitaṃ jñānamanvayajñānamityucyate | (pṛ) anvayajñānamidamanāsravaṃ jñānam | anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ kathamanvayajñānaṃ bhavati | (u) loke 'pyastyanvayajñānam | kasmāt | dharmajñānamanvayajñānaṃ paracittajñānaṃ duḥkhajñānaṃ samudayajñānaṃ nirodhajñānaṃ mārgajñānañca sarvaṃ sāsravamanāsravamasti | imāni jñānāni ūṣmagatādidharmeṣu sāsravāṇi niyāmāvakrāntiprāpyāṇi anāsravāṇi |
body.translated_text: They say that knowledge of the remaining <s>dharmas</s> is inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>). 'Remaining' means past and future <s>dharmas</s>. Because one knows subsequently, following present <s>dharmas</s>, it is called '<s>anvayajñāna</s>.' Why? Because inferential knowledge is preceded by direct knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Dharmajñāna</s> is called 'direct knowledge' (<s>dṛṣṭajñāna</s>). The knowledge that follows and reflects upon this <s>dharmajñāna</s> is called '<s>anvayajñāna</s>.' [Objection:] This inferential knowledge is knowledge without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>). How can knowledge without outflows be inferential knowledge? [Response:] Even in the world there exists inferential knowledge. Why? Because <s>dharmajñāna</s>, <s>anvayajñāna</s>, knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>), knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhajñāna</s>), knowledge of origination (<s>samudayajñāna</s>), knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>), and knowledge of the path (<s>mārgajñāna</s>) — all these can be with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) or without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>). These knowledges, in the <s>dharmas</s> of the warmth stage (<s>ūṣmagata</s>) and so forth, are with outflows; upon attaining entry into certainty (<s>niyāmāvakrānti</s>), they become without outflows.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- kāma[sampratiyukteṣu] saṃskāreṣu [yadanāsravaṃ] jñānaṃ [kāmasampratiyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ] hetau [yadanāsravaṃ] jñānaṃ [kāmasampratiyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ] nirodhe [yadanāsravaṃ] jñānaṃ [kāmasampratiyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ] prahāṇāya mārge [yadanāsravaṃ] jñānam, idamucyate dharmajñānam | rūpārūpyasampratiyukteṣu saṃskāreṣu yadanāsravaṃ jñānaṃ rūpārūpyasampratiyuktānāṃ
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Some say: The outflow-free knowledge regarding formations connected with the desire-realm (<s>kāma</s>), the outflow-free knowledge regarding their cause, the outflow-free knowledge regarding their cessation, the outflow-free knowledge regarding the path to their abandonment — this is called '<s>dharmajñāna</s>.' Regarding formations connected with the form and formless realms (<s>rūpārūpya</s>), the outflow-free knowledge, [and regarding] the form and formless —

body.text: saṃskārāṇāṃ hetau yadanāsravaṃ jñānaṃ rūpārūpyasampratiyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhe yadanāsravaṃ jñānaṃ rūpārūpyasampratiyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ prahāṇāya mārge yadanāsravaṃ jñānam, idamucyate 'nvayajñānam iti | kathamidam | (u) uktaṃ hi sūtre- bhagavānānandamāmantryāha- atītae 'nāgate caivaṃ prajānīhīti | na kiñcitsūtramāha- rūpārūpyasampratiyukteṣu saṃskāreṣu jñānamanvayajñānamiti | kiñcoktaṃ sūtre- yogī anusmaret- ahamidānīṃ dṛṣṭarūpeṇopadruto bhavāmi | atīte 'pi rūpeṇopadruto 'bhavam, anāgate 'pi rūpeṇopadruto bhaviṣyāmīti | api coktaṃ sūtre- jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇam | atīte 'nāgate 'pyevaṃ syāditi | tathāvocadaśvaghoṣabodhisattvo gāthām-
body.translated_text: — formations' cause, the outflow-free knowledge, the form and formless formations' cessation, the outflow-free knowledge, and the path to the abandonment of the form and formless formations, the outflow-free knowledge — this is called 'inferential knowledge' (<s>anvayajñāna</s>). How is this? [Response:] For it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The Blessed One addressed <s>Ānanda</s>: Know likewise regarding the past and future.' No <s>sūtra</s> says: 'Knowledge regarding formations connected with the form and formless realms is inferential knowledge.' And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>yogin</s> should recollect: I am now afflicted by visible form. In the past too I was afflicted by form; in the future too I shall be afflicted by form.' And further it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Birth is the condition for old age and death. So it was in the past and shall be in the future.' And thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s> spoke this verse:

body.text:
pratyakṣamālokya ca janma duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathātītamapīti viddhi |
yathā ca tat duḥkhamidañca duḥkhaṃ tathānāgatamapyavehi |
[bījasvabhāvo hi yatheha dṛṣṭo bhūto 'pi bhavyo 'pi tathānumeyaḥ |]
patyakṣataśca jvalano yathoṣṇo bhūto 'pi bhavyo 'pi tathoṣṇa eva || iti |
body.translated_text: Seeing directly that birth is suffering, know that past [birth] too is suffering; just as that is suffering and this is suffering, so too understand the future. For just as the nature of a seed seen here [operates], so the past and future should be inferred; and just as fire is directly experienced as hot, so was it hot in the past and shall be hot in the future.

body.text: evamādi duḥkhaṃ mahāvaibhāṣikā api vadanti |
body.translated_text: Even the great <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> speak of suffering in such terms.

body.text: atītānāgatādhvanīnadharmajñānamevānvayajñānam | asya ca yuktirasti | kasmāt | yogī hi atīte 'nāgāmini pratyutpanne ca duḥkhe nirvidyate | nirveda eva eṣu dharmeṣu tattvajñānaprādurbhāvaḥ | yathā pratyutpannāḥ saṃskārā duḥkham | tathātītā anāgatāḥ saṃskārā api duḥkham | kena jñānena atītānāgatān dharmān jānāti | yadīdaṃ dharmajñānam | rūpārūpyasampratiyuktāḥ saṃskārā api santyatītā anāgatāḥ | teṣāṃ jñānamapi dharmajñānaṃ syāt | tathā ca dharmajñānameva nānvayajñānamasti | yadi rūpārūpyasampratiyukteṣu atītānāgateṣu saṃskāreṣu jñānāntaramastīti | kāmasampratiyukteṣvatītānāgateṣu saṃskāreṣu ca jñānāntaraṃ bhavet | tadarthameva ābhidharmikā āhuḥ- asti prāptiraprāptirityato 'nupūrveṇa satyaṃ paśyatīti | kāmadhātusampratisaṃyuktaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāptiḥ | rūpārūpyasampratiyuktaṃ duḥkhamaprāptiḥ | ata ekasmin samaya ubhayajñānaṃ na sambhavati | yadyaprāptirduḥkhamanvayajñānena jñāyate | idānīṃ kāmadhātāvaprāptirduḥkhamapi anvayajñānena jñāyeta |
body.translated_text: Knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to the past and future time-periods is precisely inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>). And there is reason for this. Why? For the <s>yogin</s> becomes disenchanted with suffering in the past, future, and present. This very disenchantment (<s>nirveda</s>) is the manifestation of knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) regarding these <s>dharmas</s>. Just as present formations are suffering, so too are past and future formations suffering. By what knowledge does one know past and future <s>dharmas</s>? It is this <s>dharmajñāna</s>. Formations connected with the form and formless realms also exist as past and future. Knowledge of these too would be <s>dharmajñāna</s>. Thus there is only <s>dharmajñāna</s> and no separate <s>anvayajñāna</s>. If there were a separate knowledge for formations connected with the form and formless realms in the past and future, then there would also be a separate knowledge for desire-realm formations in the past and future. For this very reason, the <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say: 'There exists attainment and non-attainment' — and accordingly one sees the truths in sequence. Suffering connected with the desire-realm is attainment (<s>prāpti</s>); suffering connected with the form and formless realms is non-attainment (<s>aprāpti</s>). Therefore, both knowledges cannot occur simultaneously.
