If suffering that is non-attainment is known by inferential knowledge, then suffering that is non-attainment in the desire-realm should also be known by inferential knowledge.

body.text: (pṛ) kena jñānena saṃyojanaprahāṇamārgo bhavati | (u) [tatra] dharmajñānamātramupayujyate | anvayajñānamupāyamārge vartate | (pṛ) kiṃ dharmajñānamupayujyate | (u) duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ nirodhe dharmajñānañcopayujyate | kasmāt | yogī anityaṃ duḥkhamiti paśyan śūnyamanātmeti paśyati | tasmin samaye saṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti | anyat jñānaṃ sarvamupāyaḥ | (pṛ) kiṃ duḥkhaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirodho bhavati | (u) vedanāḥ dukhaṃ paśyati | tatrātmamatirutpadyate | atastāsāmapi nirodhaṃ paśyati | yathoktam- adhyātmavimuktatvāt tṛṣṇāyāḥ kṣaye nirodhe svata evārhan prāpta ityucyate | iti | (pṛ) nanu sūtre kiṃ noktaṃ sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ prahāṇaṃ prahāṇalakṣaṇamiti | (u) ayaṃ yogī adhyātmanirodhaṃ sākṣātkṛrvan sarvatra nirviṇṇaḥ | kiñca yogī adhyātmanirodhamavaśyaṃ sākṣātkuryāt | nānyadavaśyaniyatam |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] By which knowledge does the path of abandoning the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) operate? [Response:] Only <s>dharmajñāna</s> alone is employed there. Inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>) operates in the preparatory path (<s>upāyamārga</s>). [Objection:] How is <s>dharmajñāna</s> employed? [Response:] <s>Dharmajñāna</s> regarding suffering and <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding cessation are employed. Why? The <s>yogin</s>, seeing [things as] impermanent and suffering, sees [them as] empty and non-self. At that time, he directly realizes the cessation of formations. All other knowledge is [merely] preparatory. [Objection:] Does cessation occur by seeing suffering? [Response:] One sees feelings as suffering. There the notion of self arises. Therefore one also sees the cessation of those [feelings]. As stated: 'Through being inwardly liberated, upon the exhaustion and cessation of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), one is called an <s>Arhat</s> who has attained [liberation] by oneself.' [Objection:] Is it not stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The abandonment of all formations is the characteristic of abandonment'? [Response:] This <s>yogin</s>, directly realizing inner cessation, becomes disenchanted with everything. Moreover, the <s>yogin</s> must necessarily directly realize inner cessation. Nothing else is necessarily determined.

body.text: (pṛ) satyeṣu kathaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati | (u) jātirduḥkhamityādi jñānaṃ bhavati | (pṛ) idamasamāhitaṃ cittam, kathaṃ jñānaṃ janayati | (u) evaṃ darśane sati skandhānāmanityatādidoṣamapi dṛṣṭvā duḥkhanātmasaṃjñāṃ janayati | yathoktaṃ sūtre- [yat] duḥkhaṃ tadanityam, yadanityaṃ tadānātma iti | kasmāt | cakṣurādīnāmindriyāṇāmutpādo 'sti vyayo 'sti | yadyayamātmā, ātmana utpādo vyayaḥ syādityato jñāyate anātmeti | idañca cakṣurādyutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati | kṛtakamastītyato 'nātmetyucyate | sūtre coktaṃ- nāsti kāraka iti | ato jñāyate yadanityaṃ tadanātmeti | evaṃ yoginaḥ samyak anityamanātma ca bhāvayataḥ kāyacittamupaśāmyati | sarvasaṃskāreṣu samutpanneṣu teṣāṃ vihiṃsāmanubhavato duḥkhasaṃjñā samutpadyate | niścarmaṇyā yathā gāva alpasparśe ['pi] vyathānubhūyate | tathā yogī anātmasaṃjñāvaśāduttamāṃ duḥkhasaṃjñāṃ sādhayati | mūḍhastu ātmasaṃjñāvaśātsatyapi mahati duḥkhe na tadupāyāsamanubhavati | idamucyate duḥkhajñānam | saṃskārāṇāmutpādadarśanaṃ hetujñānam | saṃskārāṇāṃ vyayadarśanaṃ nirodhajñānam | mārgasyāvarāgrānusaraṇaṃ mārgajñānam |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] How does knowledge arise regarding the truths? [Response:] Knowledge arises as 'birth is suffering' and so forth. [Objection:] This is an unconcentrated mind — how does it generate knowledge? [Response:] With such a view, having seen the faults of impermanence and so forth in the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), one generates the perception of suffering and non-self. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'What is suffering is impermanent; what is impermanent is non-self.' Why? Because the faculties such as the eye have arising and perishing. If this were the self, the self would have arising and perishing — therefore it is known as non-self. And these [faculties] beginning with the eye, when arising, do not come from anywhere; they are produced [by conditions] — therefore they are called 'non-self.' And it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There is no agent.' Therefore it is known that what is impermanent is non-self. Thus, for the <s>yogin</s> who properly cultivates [the contemplation of] impermanence and non-self, body and mind become pacified. When all formations arise, as one experiences their harm, the perception of suffering arises. Just as flayed cows experience pain at even slight contact, so the <s>yogin</s>, by the power of the perception of non-self, accomplishes the supreme perception of suffering. But the deluded person, by the power of the perception of self, does not experience that distress even when there is great suffering. This is called 'knowledge of suffering' (<s>duḥkhajñāna</s>). Seeing the arising of formations is 'knowledge of the cause' (<s>hetujñāna</s>). Seeing the perishing of formations is 'knowledge of cessation' (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>). Following the path from its lower to its higher [stages] is 'knowledge of the path' (<s>mārgajñāna</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) kimucyate kṣayajñānam | (u) sarvāṇi nimittāni kṣapayatīti kṣayajñānam | kasmāt | śaikṣasya nimittaṃ prahīṇaṃ punarutpadyate | idantu atyantaṃ kṣapayatīti
body.translated_text: [Objection:] What is called 'knowledge of exhaustion' (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>)? [Response:] That which exhausts all signs (<s>nimitta</s>) is <s>kṣayajñāna</s>. Why? For a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), though the signs are abandoned, they arise again. But this [knowledge] exhausts them completely —

body.text: kṣayajñānam | yathoktaṃ sūtre- abhūtanimittamidamabhūtaṃ saṃjñāmātramiti prajānato duḥkhāni kṣīyanta iti | śaikṣāḥ prajānanti | abhūtaṃ saṃjñāmātramātmeti | taccittamatyantaṃ prahīṇamiti kṣayajñānamityucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- kaścidarhan tathāgatasya purato vyākaroti- bhagavatā deśitāni na santi mama | nāhameṣu saṃyojaneṣu punarvicikitse | sadā mama samāhitaikāgrasya samyak caryāmanusmarataḥ kāmādīnyakuśalāni na cittasyāsravā bhavanti iti | tatra nimittaṃ gṛhṇātītyataḥ saṃyojanāni bhavanti | prahīṇanimittasya tu saṃyojanāni nirudhyante | śaikṣā nimitte 'nimittamiti viharanti | ata ātmamatiḥ kadācidāvirbhavati | yathā sthāṇuṃ dṛṣṭvā ayaṃ puruṣa iti saṃśerate | ato 'rhataḥ kevalaṃ nirvicikitsasya prāptiḥ | sadā animittavihāricittatvāt pūrvaṃ sattvaśūnyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā pañcasu skandheṣu na paśyatyātmānam | paścāt dharmaśūnyatvānna paśyati rūpasvabhāvaṃ yāvadvijñānasvabhāvañca | ato jñāyate sarvanimittakṣayaḥ kṣayajñānamiti |
body.translated_text: — this is <s>kṣayajñāna</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one who understands that this unreal sign is unreal, mere designation — suffering is exhausted.' Learners (<s>śaikṣas</s>) understand: 'The [notion of] self is unreal, mere designation.' The complete abandonment of that mind is called '<s>kṣayajñāna</s>.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A certain <s>Arhat</s> declares before the <s>Tathāgata</s>: The [fetters] taught by the Blessed One do not exist in me. I no longer doubt regarding these fetters. Always concentrated and one-pointed, properly recollecting my conduct, unwholesome [states] such as sensual desire do not become outflows of my mind.' There, because one grasps at signs, fetters arise. But for one whose signs are abandoned, the fetters cease. Learners dwell [seeing] signlessness in signs. Therefore the notion of self sometimes manifests. Just as upon seeing a tree-stump, one doubts 'is this a person?' — therefore only for the <s>Arhat</s>, who is completely free from doubt, is there [true] attainment. Because the mind always dwells in signlessness, having first seen the emptiness of beings, one does not see a self in the five aggregates. Subsequently, due to the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s>, one does not see the own-nature of form, up to the own-nature of consciousness. Therefore it is known that the exhaustion of all signs is <s>kṣayajñāna</s>.

body.text: sarvanimittānāmanutpādaṃ jānātītyanutpādajñānam | śaikṣasya prahīṇanimittasya punarutpādaḥ kṣīṇaḥ | aśaikṣasya nimittaṃ kṣīṇaṃ na punarutpadyate | sarvanimittānāṃ kṣaye nirodhe yatpunaranutpādaḥ tadanutpādajñānam | (pṛ) śaikṣo 'pi jānāti asti [mama] kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānamiti | yathānusmarati- parikṣīṇatrisaṃyojano na punarutpatsya iti | kasmānnāha daśāṅgasamanvita iti | (u) śaikṣo na sarvasaṃjñāḥ prajahāti | ato nāha- asti [mama] kṣayajñānamanutpādajñānamiti | yathā kaścit tatra tatra pratibaddha ekasmānmukto 'pi na vimukta ityucyate | asti cāyamarthaḥ śāriputro 'nāthapiṇḍadasya daśāṅgasamanvāgamamavocat iti | arhan vaśitābalaprāptatvāt prajānāti- kṣīṇāni [me] saṃyojanāni, na punarutpatsya iti | tathā śaikṣo 'pi | arhan aśaikṣamārgaṃ prāpto [yat] prajānāti kṣīṇā[me]jātiriti | tat kṣayajñānamityucyate | uṣitaṃ brahmacaryamiti śaikṣacaryāparityāga ucyate | kṛtaṃ karaṇīyamiti karaṇīyāni sarvāṇi kṛtvā prajānāti- asmādbhavāt nāsti bhavāntaramiti | ato jñāyate arhanneva sarveṣu karaṇīyeṣu vaśitāṃ prāptaḥ kṣayajñānenānutpādajñānena ca samanvitaḥ syāt,
body.translated_text: Knowing the non-arising of all signs is 'knowledge of non-arising' (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>). For a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), the arising again of abandoned signs has ceased. For a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), the signs have ceased and do not arise again. Upon the exhaustion and cessation of all signs, the subsequent non-arising is <s>anutpādajñāna</s>. [Objection:] A learner too knows: 'I have <s>kṣayajñāna</s> and <s>anutpādajñāna</s>.' For he recollects: 'The three fetters being exhausted, I shall not be reborn [in lower realms].' Why is it not said that [a learner] possesses the ten [knowledges]? [Response:] A learner does not abandon all perceptions. Therefore it is not said that he has <s>kṣayajñāna</s> and <s>anutpādajñāna</s>. Just as someone bound here and there, though freed from one [bond], is not called 'liberated.' And there is this meaning: <s>Śāriputra</s> spoke to <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> about the possession of the ten [qualities]. An <s>Arhat</s>, having attained mastery and power, understands: 'My fetters are exhausted; I shall not be reborn.' Likewise a learner too [understands this partially]. An <s>Arhat</s> who has attained the path of the non-learner (<s>aśaikṣamārga</s>) understands: 'Birth is exhausted for me' — this is called <s>kṣayajñāna</s>. 'The holy life has been lived' means the non-abandonment of the learner's conduct. 'What was to be done has been done' — having done all that was to be done, one understands: 'From this existence, there is no further existence.' Therefore it is known that only the <s>Arhat</s>, having attained mastery in all that is to be done, possesses both <s>kṣayajñāna</s> and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> —

body.text: na tu śaikṣā iti | yathā kaścit jvarārto[jvarā]nudgamakāle 'pi jvarītyucyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: — but not learners (<s>śaikṣas</s>). Just as someone afflicted by fever, even at the time when the fever has not fully departed, is still called 'feverish.' As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
sarvatra vihatā nandiḥ tamaskandhaḥ pradālitaḥ |
jitvā mṛtyorhi senāñca viharāmi anāsravaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: Everywhere delight has been destroyed, the mass of darkness has been shattered; having conquered the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), I dwell without outflows.

body.text: paracittajñānaṃ yathā ṣaḍabhijñāsūktam | pañcaskandhakalāpaḥ sattvaḥ | tatra jñānaṃ saṃvṛtijñānam | anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ tattvajñānam | idamanāsravābhāsaṃ jñānākhyāṃ prāpnotītyataḥ saṃvṛtijñānamiti vadanti | (pṛ) kecidāhuḥ- sarve sattvāḥ samaṃ jñānasamanvitā iti | kathamidam | (u) yo jinauraso jānāti dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpannā iti | sa prāpnoti nānyaḥ sattvaḥ | jñānākhyāyāḥ prāpitvāt | sarve sattvāḥ saṃjñāprayogamātraṃ vijānanti | yadi prāpnuvantīdaṃ jñānam | [tadā] ābhyantarapṛthagjana ityucyante |
body.translated_text: Knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>) is as stated in the section on the six supernatural powers (<s>ṣaḍabhijñā</s>). A 'being' (<s>sattva</s>) is the aggregate (<s>kalāpa</s>) of the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandha</s>). Knowledge regarding that is conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>). Knowledge without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>) is knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>). This [knowledge], being a semblance of the outflow-free (<s>anāsravābhāsa</s>), obtains the designation 'knowledge' — therefore they say it is conventional knowledge. (Question) Some say: 'All beings are equally endowed with knowledge.' How is this? (Answer) One who is a true son of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) knows that '<s>dharmas</s> are dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>).' He attains [this knowledge], not any other being — because of the attainment of the designation 'knowledge.' All beings cognize merely through the application of conventional designation (<s>saṃjñāprayoga</s>). If they attain this knowledge, then they are called 'inner ordinary persons' (<s>ābhyantarapṛthagjana</s>).

body.text: daśajñānavargo dviśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The Chapter on the Ten Knowledges (<s>daśajñānavarga</s>), the two hundredth.

body.text: 201 catuścatvāriṃśajjñānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 201. The Chapter on the Forty-Four Knowledges (<s>catuścatvāriṃśajjñānavarga</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- catuścattvāriṃśat jñānāni yaduta jarāmaraṇe jñānaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudaye jñānaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhe jñānaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhamārge jñānaṃ, jātibhavopādānatṛṣṇāvedanāsparśaṣaḍāyatananāmarūpavijñānasaṃskāreṣvapyevam | kasmādidamucyate | (u) nirvāṇe
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are forty-four knowledges — namely, knowledge regarding aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>), knowledge regarding the origination of aging-and-death, knowledge regarding the cessation of aging-and-death, knowledge regarding the path leading to the cessation of aging-and-death; likewise regarding birth (<s>jāti</s>), existence (<s>bhava</s>), clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>), name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), and formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>).' Why is this said? (Answer) Regarding <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

body.text: tattvaratne vividhairdvārairavatarati | kaścitpañcaskandhamukhenāvatarati | kaścit dhātvāyatananidānadvāraiḥ, [kaścit] satyaiḥ evamādibhirdvārairnirvāṇamanuprāpnoti | kenedaṃ jñāyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- [tadyathā] nagarasvāmī nagare niṣaṇṇaḥ syāt | [tatra] kiñcit dūtayugamekasmāt dvārādāgatyopasṛtya nagarasvāmino yathābhūtaṃ vacanaṃ niryātya [yathāgatamārgaṃ] pratipadyeta | tathā [anyadūtayugamanyebhyo] dvārebhyo 'pi | tatra nagarasvāmyupamo yogī | dvārāṇīti skandhadhātvāyatanādīnāṃ bhāvanāyā adhivacanam | dūtayugaṃ śamathavipaśyanopamam | yathābhūtaṃ vacanaṃ nirvāṇasyādhivacanam | iti | dūtā nānādvārebhya āgatā api ekameva sthānamupasarpanti | evaṃ skandhadhātvāyatanādīnāṃ bhāvanā nānādvārāṇyupāyā nirvāṇe 'vataraṇasya | yathā rāhula ekānte niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ cintayan evaṃ prajānāti- īdṛśo dharma parikīrtitaṃ nirvāṇaṃ prati anuprayātīti |
body.translated_text: one enters the jewel of reality through various doors. Some enter through the door of the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandha</s>). Some through the doors of elements (<s>dhātu</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), and dependent origination (<s>nidāna</s>); some through the truths (<s>satyas</s>) — through such various doors one reaches <s>nirvāṇa</s>. How is this known? As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Suppose a lord of a city were seated in his city. A pair of messengers, having come from one gate, approaches the city-lord, delivers the true message, and departs by the way they came. Likewise, another pair of messengers [comes] from other gates.' There the city-lord is likened to the <s>yogī</s>. 'Gates' is a designation for the cultivation of the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, and so forth. The pair of messengers is likened to <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). 'The true message' is a designation for <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Thus messengers coming from various gates all approach one and the same place. Similarly, the cultivation of the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, and so forth are the various gates, the means for entering <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Just as <s>Rāhula</s>, seated in solitude, contemplating the <s>dharma</s>, comprehends thus: 'Such a <s>dharma</s> leads toward the proclaimed <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: kiñca bhagavān dharmasyāniśaṃsāyāmāha- dharmo 'yaṃ sarvān kleśāgnīna nirodhayatīti nirodha ityucyate | yoginaścittaṃ praśamayatīti praśamaḥ | yoginaḥ samyak parijñānaṃ parāyayatīti parāyaṇam | ityādayo 'rthā nirvāṇasyāniśaṃsāḥ | brahmacaryamaṣṭāṅgamārga ucyate | aṣṭāṅgamārge ca samyagjñānamevoktam | asya samyagjñānasyaiva phalaṃ yaducyate nirvāṇamiti | bhagavatopradiṣṭaṃ śāsanaṃ sarvaṃ nirvāṇāya bhavati | ato jñāyate pañcaskandhādayo dvārāṇi nirvāṇaparāyaṇāni bhavanti |
body.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said regarding the benefits of <s>dharma</s>: 'This <s>dharma</s> extinguishes all the fires of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) — therefore it is called "cessation" (<s>nirodha</s>). It pacifies the mind of the <s>yogī</s> — therefore it is called "pacification" (<s>praśama</s>). It brings the <s>yogī</s>'s right comprehensive knowledge to the further shore — therefore it is called "the further shore" (<s>parāyaṇa</s>).' These and such meanings are the benefits of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is called the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>aṣṭāṅgamārga</s>). And in the Noble Eightfold Path, it is right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) alone that is stated. The fruit of this right knowledge alone is what is called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>.' The entire teaching proclaimed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> is for the sake of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. From this it is known that the five aggregates and so forth are gates leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s> as their destination.

body.text: (pṛ) kecidābhidharmikā āhuḥ- jarāmaraṇajñānaṃ duḥkhajñānamiti | kathamidam | (u) na [yuktam] | kasmāt | na tatrocyate duḥkhākāraḥ | ato na [tat] duḥkhajñānam | (pṛ) idaṃ kasya jñānaṃ bhavati | (u) tat jarāmaraṇasvabhāvajñānam | (pṛ) ucyate ca jarāmaraṇasamudayaḥ jarāmaraṇanirodho jarāmaraṇanirodhamārga ityādi | ato jñāyate idaṃ duḥkhajñānameva syāditi | (u) tat nidānadvāraṃ bhavati, na satyadvāram | ato na tasya duḥkhākāro vaktavyaḥ | [evaṃ] samudayādau vaktavyaḥ | lakṣaṇasāmyāt | (pṛ) atra kuto nocyate āsvādādīnavanissaraṇādīnāṃ jñānāni | (u) sarvāṇīmāni atra parigṛhītāni | kintu saṅgītikāraḥ saṃkṣipan na [vistaraśa] uvāca ||
body.translated_text: (Question) Some <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> (Abhidharma scholars) say: 'Knowledge regarding aging-and-death is knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhajñāna</s>).' How is this? (Answer) That is not correct. Why? Because the aspect of suffering (<s>duḥkhākāra</s>) is not stated there. Therefore it is not knowledge of suffering. (Question) To what kind of knowledge does this belong? (Answer) It is knowledge of the intrinsic nature of aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇasvabhāvajñāna</s>). (Question) But it is said: 'the origination of aging-and-death, the cessation of aging-and-death, the path leading to the cessation of aging-and-death' and so forth. From this it is known that this would indeed be knowledge of suffering. (Answer) That is through the door of dependent origination (<s>nidāna</s>), not through the door of the truths (<s>satya</s>). Therefore the aspect of suffering is not to be stated regarding it. Similarly with the origination and the rest — [the same] should be stated, because of the similarity of their characteristics. (Question) Why are the knowledges of relishing (<s>āsvāda</s>), danger (<s>ādīnava</s>), escape (<s>nissaraṇa</s>), and so forth not stated here? (Answer) All of these are included herein. But the compiler of the collection (<s>saṅgītikāra</s>), abridging [the material], did not state [them] in detail.

body.text: catuścatvāriṃśajjñānavarga ekottaradviśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The Chapter on the Forty-Four Knowledges (<s>catuścatvāriṃśajjñānavarga</s>), the two hundred and first.

body.text: 202 saptasaptatijñānavargaḥ
body.translated_text: 202. The Chapter on the Seventy-Seven Knowledges (<s>saptasaptatijñānavarga</s>).

body.text: (pṛ) sūtra uktam- saptasaptatijñānāni yaduta jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamiti [jñānam] | asatyāṃ jātau nāsti jarāmaraṇamiti [jñānam] | evamatīte 'nāgate 'dhvanyapi |
body.translated_text: (Question) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are seventy-seven knowledges — namely, "Birth is the condition for aging-and-death" — this is knowledge. "In the absence of birth, there is no aging-and-death" — this is knowledge. Likewise regarding the past and the future temporal periods.

body.text: yadasya dharmasthitijñānam | [tadapi] anityaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ kṛtakaṃ pratītyasamutpannaṃ kṣayadharma, vipariṇāmadharma, viyogadharma, vyayadharma iti jñānam | yāvadavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityapyevam iti | tatra kasmānnoktaṃ- jarāmaraṇasya svabhāvo nirodho mārga ityādi | (u) hitajñasya kṛta evamuktaṃ tasya dvāratvamātramaviṣkaroti | anyadapyevaṃ jñeyam |
body.translated_text: "This is the knowledge of the stability of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthitijñāna</s>)" — and further: "It is impermanent, conditioned, made, dependently arisen, of the nature of destruction, of the nature of change, of the nature of separation, of the nature of perishing" — this is knowledge. Similarly up to "ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the condition for formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>)."' Why then is it not stated there: 'the intrinsic nature of aging-and-death, its cessation, its path' and so forth? (Answer) The one who knows the beneficial (<s>hitajña</s>) has thus stated; it merely reveals that it serves as a door. Other [aspects] too should be understood in the same way.

body.text: tīrthikā bahavo nidāne bhrāntā vadanti- laukikānāṃ padārthānāṃ heturlokātmaka ityādi | ato bhagavān teṣāṃ nidānamātramāha | (pṛ) jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamityuktvā kasmātpunarāha- asatyāṃ [jātā]viti | (u) niyamārtham | yathā dānaṃ puṇyasya hetuḥ | śīlenāpi puṇyaṃ vindate | yathoktam- dhṛtaśīlo deveṣūtpadyata iti | kecinmanyante- jarā- maraṇapratyayā jātiriti | kecidahetukā jātiriti | ato niyama ucyate | (pṛ) kasmādatīte 'nāgate 'dhvani punarniyama ucyate | (u) pratyutpannamatītādhvanaḥ kadācidbhinnadharma bhavati yadutātītānāṃ sattvānāmāyurapramāṇaṃ prabhāvaśca devatulya ityevamādi | āyurādi bhinnaṃ jarāmaraṇapratyayo 'pi bhinno bhavediti janā vadeyuriti bhītyā niyama ucyate | anāgate 'pyevaṃ [vaktavyam] |
body.translated_text: The non-Buddhist ascetics (<s>tīrthikas</s>), many of whom are confused about dependent origination (<s>nidāna</s>), say: 'The cause of worldly entities is a world-soul (<s>lokātmaka</s>)' and so forth. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated for them merely the [links of] dependent origination. (Question) Having said 'birth is the condition for aging-and-death,' why does he further say 'in the absence of birth...'? (Answer) For the purpose of certainty (<s>niyamārtha</s>). Just as giving (<s>dāna</s>) is the cause of merit — yet through moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) too one obtains merit. As stated: 'One who maintains moral conduct is reborn among the gods.' Some think: 'Birth is conditioned by aging-and-death' [i.e. the reverse]. Some think: 'Birth is without cause.' Therefore the certainty is stated. (Question) Why is the certainty further stated regarding the past and future temporal periods? (Answer) Present [beings] differ from beings of the past temporal period sometimes in the nature of their <s>dharma</s> — for instance, the lifespan of beings of the past was immeasurable, and their splendor was equal to that of gods, and so forth. Since the lifespan and other [qualities] differ, people might say that the condition of aging-and-death too would be different — out of fear [of this misunderstanding], the certainty is stated. Regarding the future too, [the same] should be stated likewise.

body.text: idaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ dharmasthitijñānam | anyannāma nirvāṇajñānam | jarāmaraṇasantānakaratvāducyate- anityaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ kṛtakaṃ pratītyasamutpannam | kṣayadharma vipariṇāmadharma ityanityākāraḥ | viyogadharma iti duḥkhākāraḥ | vyayadharma iti anātmaśūnyākāraḥ |
body.translated_text: This sixfold knowledge is knowledge of the stability of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthitijñāna</s>). The other is called knowledge of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>nirvāṇajñāna</s>). Because [aging-and-death] produces the continuity of aging-and-death, it is said: 'impermanent, conditioned, made, dependently arisen.' 'Of the nature of destruction, of the nature of change' — this is the aspect of impermanence (<s>anityākāra</s>). 'Of the nature of separation' — this is the aspect of suffering (<s>duḥkhākāra</s>). 'Of the nature of perishing' — this is the aspect of non-self and emptiness (<s>anātmaśūnyākāra</s>).

body.text: kasmāt tatra rūpasya svarūpaṃ nirodhaḥ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vijñānasya ca svarūpaṃ nirodhaḥ | ayaṃ trividhavipaśyanānāmartha ityākhyāyate | yathoktaṃ sūtre- yo bhikṣavaḥ saptabhiḥ sthānopāyaiḥ tribhirvipaśyanārthaiśca samanvitaḥ sa kṣipramāsravāṇāṃ kṣayamanuprāpnoti | idameva nirvāṇajñānaṃ bhavatīti | ityādi nidānajñānāni apramāṇaśatasahasrāṇi santi yaduta
body.translated_text: Why? Because therein the intrinsic nature of form is cessation, the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is cessation. This is called the meaning of the threefold <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s>, one who is endowed with the seven grounds of investigation (<s>sthānopāya</s>) and the three insights (<s>vipaśyanā</s>) quickly reaches the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravas</s>).' This alone becomes the knowledge of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Thus the knowledges regarding dependent origination are immeasurable hundreds of thousands — namely,

body.text: cakṣurvijñānamityādi | yathoktaṃ sūtre- cakṣuṣa karma pratyayaḥ | karmaṇaḥ tṛṣṇā pratyayaḥ | tṛṣṇāyā avidyā pratyayaḥ | avidyāyā ayoniśomanaskāraḥ pratyayaḥ | ayoniśomanaskārasya cakṣūrūpaṃ pratyayaḥ | āsravāṇāmayoniśo mananaṃ pratyayaḥ | āhārāṇāṃ tṛṣṇā pratyayaḥ | pañcakāmaguṇānāṃ kabalīkārāhārādayaḥ pratyayāḥ | narakasyālpāyuṣaśca prāṇātipātādayaḥ pratyayāḥ | yadidānīntanaṃ duḥkhaṃ pūrvatanīnañca duḥkhaṃ, sarvasyābhūtasaṃjñā pratyayaḥ | abhūtasaṃjñāyāḥ kāyacittayoḥ priyāpriye pratyayaḥ | priyāpriyayoḥ kāmarāgaḥ pratyayaḥ | kāmarāgasya mithyāvitarkaḥ pratyayaḥ ityevamādipratyayānāṃ jñānamapramāṇamanavadhi svayamevonnetavyam ||
body.translated_text: eye-consciousness and so forth. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The eye's condition is <s>karma</s>. <s>Karma</s>'s condition is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). Craving's condition is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Ignorance's condition is improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>). Improper mental attention's condition is the eye and form. The condition of the outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) is improper mental engagement. The condition of nutriment (<s>āhāra</s>) is craving. The condition of the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>pañcakāmaguṇa</s>) is material nutriment (<s>kabalīkārāhāra</s>) and the rest. The condition of hell and short lifespan is killing (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>) and the rest. Whatever is present suffering and whatever is past suffering — the condition of all of it is false perception (<s>abhūtasaṃjñā</s>). The condition of false perception is the pleasant and unpleasant in body and mind. The condition of pleasant and unpleasant is sensual passion (<s>kāmarāga</s>). The condition of sensual passion is wrong deliberation (<s>mithyāvitarka</s>).' Thus the knowledge of such conditions and the like is immeasurable and boundless — one should deduce it by oneself.

body.text: saptasaptatijñānavargo dvyuttaraśatatamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The Chapter on the Seventy-Seven Knowledges (<s>saptasaptatijñānavarga</s>), the two hundred and second.

body.text: mārgasatyaskandhaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: The section on the Truth of the Path (<s>mārgasatyaskandha</s>) is completed.

body.text: śāstraṃ samāptam
body.translated_text: The treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) is completed.
